engagement_title: Kantyna Nova opening season: bring a service-night plate archive to one dark house look, build the menu, partner deck and reservations page as documents the room edits itself, and turn the printer's pairing card into a real per-guest run
vertical: Food, restaurant and beverage, an eighteen seat chef's tasting room with a private dining side, Portland, Maine
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Freelancer.com post 'Professional Photo Editor for Restaurant Brand', asking to 'improve the quality of photos for a new website for our restaurant and catering brand', naming 'improving overall image quality, sharpness, colors, lighting, and contrast' and 'consistent color grading across all materials'. The real poster is a Polish catering brand, laundered here to the fictional Kantyna Nova with a fictional owner persona. Co-anchors: the Upwork dine-in menu refresh post asking for a dark ground, hero food photography and an accent with new sections added; and the Upwork premium restaurant site post asking for a 'high-end, clean, modern-minimalist' presence with a 'Dark Mode aesthetic' that 'focuses heavily on high-quality food photography', split into home, an interactive menu and a booking section. All three want one dark house look derived from their own food photography, carried across everything a guest and a partner sees. The ledger conceded page composition was not connector work when it was written; CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) changes that, because HTML authoring now yields a native editable Express document at true millimetre page sizes and mixed canvases in one export, and a printer's press PDF can be reverse engineered into a live merge template.
client_one_liner: Our plates were photographed during service on the nights we could spare a camera, our menu changes every six weeks, and the room opens in November with a printer, a partner meeting and a reservation link all waiting on the same set of files.
client_brief:
Kantyna Nova, opening season

We are opening an eighteen seat tasting room in Portland, Maine in November. One seating a night, one menu, one wine flight. Marta runs the room and I cook. There are two of us and there will not be a third.

Our pictures. We photographed the plates ourselves, in the room, during service, one pass per dish, because a plate that sits does not go out. They are honest pictures of our food. Laid next to each other they are not one thing. Some are warmer, the light over the pass is not the light at the corner two top, and a few of the glazes came back harder than they look in the room. We need them to read as one house: dark, quiet, the food lit and the rest of the frame receding. The gloss on a sauce should still read as light falling on a sauce.

What we need built. The printed menu, two pages, the tasting on page one and the wine list on page two, at a normal European page size, because we reprint every six weeks and want to change it ourselves. A short deck for the two partners who put money in, ending on how the price is built up. The page behind the reservation link, with our hours. And a small set of posts for the opening, in the shapes the platforms want.

Then the private dining side. Our printer already made us a pairing card, one per guest, and gave us the print file. For each booking we need that card produced per guest, carrying their name, their course and the wine poured with it, with the dish picture on it. Our December bookings are in a list.

Money. The tasting is one hundred and eighty five dollars, the pairing another ninety five. Our guests are thirty to fifty five and this is their evening, not their dinner. It should feel held back and expensive without raising its voice. Price is not a feature here, so please do not treat it like one.

And a note on what you did, what type we are on, and anything you could not do.
price_band_and_audience: One hundred and eighty five dollars for the tasting, ninety five more for the pairing, eighteen covers a night, guests thirty to fifty five treating the evening as the occasion. The band is load bearing on every canvas. At this price the grounds go dark and restrained, one dish carries a page on its own, held space is generous, the specular on a glaze is protected rather than crushed, and the price sits quietly at body size in the text face with no rule, no box and no currency flourish. Push the same photographs into saturated warmth, dense tiling and prices set large in a display face and the room reads as a forty dollar bistro that has overpriced itself, which is exactly the grammar the sibling deli commission is correctly built on. Push further into black grounds and a single hairline and it becomes a three hundred dollar destination an eighteen seat Portland opening cannot fill. A posted job of this shape runs 1,800 to 4,000 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: One seating. One menu. One evening.
brand_identity.sector: An eighteen seat chef's tasting room with a private dining side, one seating a night, in Portland, Maine.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Opening November 2026, Portland, Maine. A two person house: Marta runs the room, the chef cooks, and there will not be a third.
brand_identity.about: Kantyna Nova is a single table set once a night: one tasting, one wine flight, cooked and served by the two people who built it. The room is dark and quiet by design, so the plate is the only thing lit. Nothing is rushed, nothing is upsold, and the evening is the point rather than the meal.
brand_identity.audience: Guests thirty to fifty five who book the room as their occasion, not their dinner. They value intention over abundance and read a dark, spare room as confidence rather than as coldness.
brand_identity.price_positioning: One hundred and eighty five dollars for the tasting, ninety five more for the wine pairing. Held back and expensive without raising its voice: above a neighbourhood bistro, deliberately short of a destination tasting palace an eighteen seat opening cannot fill. Price is never a feature.
brand_identity.typography: A transitional display serif for course titles and the room's name, quiet and old world, set large but never loud. A humanist text face beneath it for descriptions, hours and prices, prices sitting at body size in the same text face with no rule, box or currency flourish.
brand_identity.voice: First person plural, plain and understated, never salesy. Example line the brand would write: 'One seating a night. Sit down and let the evening happen.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No formal brand kit exists yet. The course titles and the approved copy are set, there is a single handheld photograph of the finished room, and the owners photographed every plate themselves in the room during service. The private dining printer holds the pairing card press file. The identity is being set now for the first time.
brand_identity.values: Two makers, one honest evening. Restraint as generosity, and food worth looking at.

assets_supplied.name: kantyna_plates/ (14 frames, camera scale, one dish per frame)
assets_supplied.kind: Plate photography shot by the owners in the dining room during service across roughly a month, available light plus the pass lamp, one pass per dish.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Every dish we serve, shot in the room while we were open. Some are warmer than others. They are the only pictures we have and we cannot reshoot them."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: On an unknown subset the pass lamp put the sauce gloss and the porcelain rim past the top of the file, so those brightest pixels carry nothing left to recover and a highlight move on them returns success while changing nothing visible. Separately two of the fourteen are the same dish plated on two different nights, and one course was never photographed at all, which no filename reveals.

assets_supplied.name: kantyna_pairing_card_press.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The press file the room's printer supplied for the private dining pairing card: a small landscape card carrying a guest name, a course line, a wine designation, an allergen line and a picture well.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The card our printer already makes for us. This is the file he prints from."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The printed card reads as four separate blocks but the file was set as one continuous flow, so the converted document exposes far coarser frame granularity than the printed page implies, and its wine frame is fixed at the width of the printer's own short sample text. The file also carries no bleed at all, so a press ready delivery with bleed cannot be honoured from it.

assets_supplied.name: kantyna_december_bookings.csv
assets_supplied.kind: The December private dining bookings, one row per guest: date, guest name, course, wine designation, allergen string and a picture column.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our December bookings. The wine column is what the sommelier writes on the pass sheet."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: One booking seats two guests who share a first name and the roster records them that way, so naming one file per guest by name collides and silently overwrites. The picture column names dishes rather than files, so the binding between a row and an actual photograph is the agent's to establish and can go wrong invisibly.

assets_supplied.name: kantyna_wine_list.txt
assets_supplied.kind: The wine list as the sommelier keeps it: forty two entries, each a producer, an appellation, a vintage and a glass price.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The list as she keeps it. It is ordered the way she thinks about it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is ordered by producer, not by the sequence the flight is poured in and not by colour, so splitting it by entry count rather than by meaning breaks the pairing sequence in the middle of a grower. Two appellations run long enough that a narrow measure will not hold them on one line.

assets_supplied.name: kantyna_room_reference.jpg and kantyna_copy.txt
assets_supplied.kind: A handheld picture of the finished dining room taken at handover, plus the approved copy: course titles and descriptions, hours, reservation wording and the deck's price build up.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The room as it is now, and the words as we want them. The course titles are set."

acceptance_bar: The fourteen plate frames read as one house in the sequence a menu and a deck lay them: one black point, one warmth, one sense of where the light comes from. A frame that cannot be brought to the set is named in the note, not shipped at eighty percent.
On every delivered plate the gloss on a sauce and the rim of the porcelain still read as light falling on a surface, not as a flat paper white hole.
No delivered file exceeds the pixel dimensions of the frame it came from, and no returned resize record carries an enlargement entry.

The menu is one document at a true European page size, the tasting on page one and the wine list on page two, with the list holding two columns as delivered rather than only as authored, and no entry falling off the page.
The wine list is split where it means something, by colour and pour order, not at the halfway entry.

Every text object in the menu, deck, reservations page and social set is live editable text in one licensed type system, with family and real weight declared on the element rather than inherited, and price set at body size in the text face.

The December run produces one card per guest, every card carrying that guest's own dish picture rather than one picture repeated, page count equalling row count, and per guest files identifiable without ambiguity where two guests share a name.
Every merged card is readable at trim: no guest's name, course, wine designation or allergen line is cut off at a frame edge, on the longest record as well as the shortest.
Nothing is claimed as press ready with bleed that the supplied print file cannot carry, and the shortfall is reported rather than quietly dropped.

The note records per photograph what was applied and why that frame differs from its neighbours, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and the real numeric weight, every resize any tool reported, the picture to course reconciliation, and everything that could not be delivered.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload and asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, image_adjust_highlights, image_adjust_light_portions, image_select_by_prompt with returnBbox, image_invert_selection, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize reading metadata.tradeoffs and detection_confidence
adobe_surfaces.role: Every raster decision. It fixes one dark house target off the best lit plate and brings each of the fourteen toward it one call at a time under three different service lights, confines corrections to the food by naming the material's own visual properties rather than the vessel it sits in, cuts the per guest card pictures while reading what each crop reports about its own confidence, and establishes which frames have anything left in their brightest areas.

adobe_surfaces.surface: InDesign layout and data merge
adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt including its validator pass, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout with recordRange and additionalImageFiles, document_render_layout with createSeparateFiles and resolution
adobe_surfaces.role: The private dining run, the only genuine one record per page job here. The press PDF is reverse engineered into a live merge template, offsets computed from the document's own reconstructed story text rather than the mapping readout, the graded dish pictures bound per row through a prefixed picture column, delivered as one press PDF in row order plus per guest single record files the agent names itself.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express by url, asset_search with entityScope CCAsset, asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The four pieces the room maintains itself: the two page A4 menu with the wine list as real table markup, the six slide partner deck, the reservations page with its hours table, and three social canvases at three sizes in one export. Photographs are carried as embedded image data because a reference renders as an empty grey box at full success, each root declares its own canvas, and the returned per canvas markup is the only place the importer reports what it changed.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Fonts
adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend called once per typographic role, font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: One type system across all four documents. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to land on restrained rather than rustic or luxury pastiche. Numeric weights are non standard per family, a display cut is reached by its own slug, and one unlaunderable name kills the entire kit.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as one surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search with entityScope StockAsset, a short query, a contentType filter and never orientation, asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the one frame the room does not own, a dark dining interior band for the deck's opening slide and the reservations header, IP clean, at camera scale, generative candidates excluded, then graded into the house target so it does not read as bought. The Boards half persists the selects the owners sign off from, with a partial result read as partial.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, settle which deliverable lands on which surface, and upload every asset holding each returned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Four pieces are collateral the room edits itself, which only the authoring surface composes; the December run is one record per page at volume, which only the merge surface does.
trajectory.produces: A surface plan, the confirmed tier, and a manifest keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Look at all fourteen plate frames and triage them: which service light each was shot under, which sit warm, which are off level, and which dish each actually shows against the fourteen course titles.
trajectory.judgement: The owners believe they have one picture per course. The pictures are the only place that can be settled, and reading fourteen frames against fourteen titles is not counting files.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note with the picture to course reconciliation.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Fix one dark house target off the best lit plate, then bring each of the fourteen toward it with its own call, recording the parameters applied per frame.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a set, not fourteen good pictures. One batched call applies one identical parameter set, which is exactly wrong for frames shot under three service lights.
trajectory.produces: Fourteen graded masters at source scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Confine corrections where a whole frame move goes wrong, selecting the food and the sauce by their own visual properties rather than by the vessel or the table, and protecting the glaze speculars.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the whole gate: naming the plate pulls the selection to the porcelain. At this band the specular is the difference between food that looks cooked and food that looks wet.
trajectory.produces: Confined corrections on the frames a global move would have taken grey or muddy.

trajectory.action: Search short generic queries for the dark dining interior band, filter to photography, exclude generative candidates, license at full resolution, then bring it to the house target.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose existing light can reach the target rather than the best thumbnail. Long queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns nothing.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP clean, camera scale interior frame graded into the set.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged against a one hundred and eighty five dollar room with eighteen covers. The weight cannot be inferred from a style name.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry or designer and actual weight per role.

trajectory.action: Author the two page menu at a true European page size with the wine list as real table markup, then the partner deck, the reservations page with its hours table, and the three social canvases, each root declaring its own canvas, every photograph carried as embedded image data, family and weight declared on every text element.
trajectory.judgement: The wine list split is a content decision the sommelier's producer ordering works against. A photograph left as a reference is not a photograph, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override collapses a mixed size set.
trajectory.produces: Export ready sources for all four documents, retained as durable deliverables.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export each document by uploaded URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the rendition and look at the first canvas, and read the returned per canvas markup for everything after it.
trajectory.judgement: Every change this importer makes returns success with no warning, and the rendition only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at page one is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: Native editable documents, an inspected first canvas each, and a markup audit for the rest.

trajectory.action: Convert the press PDF into a working document and export its interchange form, then read what the conversion actually exposes: how many text frames, how many picture frames, what each holds.
trajectory.judgement: What the printed card looks like says nothing about how the file was set. The mapping strategy is decided from what the document exposes, and this is where the bleed question is answered honestly.
trajectory.produces: A working template plus a frame inventory and a mapping strategy chosen from it.

trajectory.action: Reconstruct the document's true story text from the interchange file, compute every offset from that string, generate and validate the mapping, prepare the template, then re-export and confirm every expected placeholder is present.
trajectory.judgement: Validation returns valid on offsets computed from a shortened string and preparation reports success either way, so the only evidence a field landed is finding it in the re-exported document.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholders are confirmed by inspection, not by a success message.

trajectory.action: Cut the per guest card pictures from the graded plates to the picture well's ratio, reading what each crop reports about its confidence and bounds, and hold them against the bookings roster.
trajectory.judgement: The roster names dishes, not files, so the binding is the agent's to establish. A confident looking crop on a dark plate against a dark table is not evidence it contains the dish.
trajectory.produces: One card picture per booking row with its confidence recorded, and a stated binding key.

trajectory.action: Run the December bookings binding each row's own picture, deliver both branches, one press PDF in row order and per guest single record files named on download, render at print resolution, and read every page against its roster row at trim.
trajectory.judgement: One picture repeated across every card is what a naive run ships, the naming key has to survive two guests sharing a name, per record delivery must come through a route whose identity is guaranteed rather than inferred from position, and a page count equal to a row count says nothing about what is on the page.
trajectory.produces: The December run in both delivery forms plus print resolution proofs read per record.

trajectory.action: Create the selects board, add the graded set and the licensed frame within the per call placement cap, re-sending only the entries named as failed, then write the handover note.
trajectory.judgement: A partial success is reported as a success code, and the note has to let the room reprint in six weeks without calling anyone.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Which of the fourteen plates still has anything in its brightest areas. The pass lamp put the sauce gloss and the porcelain rim past the top of the file on an unknown subset, and the only way to find out is to pull the highlights down on a frame and look: the call returns success and the readout is that nothing moves, because there is nothing left there to move. The brightest region does not darken, does not gain texture and does not change value. At preview scale nothing distinguishes a bright specular that holds detail from a flat region that has none, and no tool in the family reports a channel reading.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering does not dodge it, because the information exists only after an adjustment has been applied and inspected, and no parameter prevents it or reports it in advance. Nothing states it: the brief says only that a few glazes came back harder than they look in the room. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different treatment for those frames, pulling the whole exposure down and rebuilding the mid tones so the flat region sits below paper white, or accepting the frame is unusable at menu size and saying so.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-plan the grade for the affected frames on a different route, re-derive their masters, and re-judge the whole set together, because moving their exposure moves where they sit relative to the frames already on target.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A dark menu and partner deck whose hero plates carry flat white holes where the sauce should be glossy, for a room whose entire claim at one hundred and eighty five dollars is that the food is worth looking at.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether every guest's card is readable at trim. The wine designation frame in the press file was sized around the printer's own short sample text, and it is a fixed frame: it does not grow, it does not push the following line down, and it does not spill anywhere visible. A record whose designation carries a producer, an appellation and a vintage simply stops rendering at the frame edge, mid word, on that record alone. Every gate above it passes: the merge reports success, page count equals row count, the template validates, the placeholders are present, and the page thumbnail looks like a card.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the frame's real capacity is a property of the converted document meeting this particular roster and neither is knowable from the other. Nothing states it: the brief describes the card and the bookings list without characterising either. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different construction, re-setting the designation as a shorter composed string the room agrees to, or moving that field into a frame the conversion exposed with room in it, which changes the mapping rather than repeating it.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-derive the mapping around the field that will not fit, re-prepare the template, re-run both delivery branches, and re-read the longest records at trim rather than at thumbnail scale.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Cards printed and set on the table for a private booking where a guest's wine is described as a producer name cut off mid word, on the one piece of collateral a guest holds in their hand.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the importer does to the wine list. Page two is a forty two entry list and the natural way to set a wine list on a portrait page is a flowing two column measure. The importer normalises that construct rather than honouring it, silently and at full success, and the list reflows into a single column whose overflow is clipped at the artboard edge because the canvas is fixed. The returned per canvas markup is the only channel that reports it, and the rendition resolves the first artboard only, so page two of a two page document is invisible through the one visual channel that exists.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the normalisation happens at import and the import is the last step of authoring, and getting it right first time presumes knowing which of several equally reasonable constructions survives, which nothing reports. Nothing states it: the acceptance line asking the list hold two columns as delivered is the client's requirement for the printed piece. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a genuinely different construction, two explicitly positioned fixed measure text frames side by side, which forces the agent to decide where the list breaks and so to make the content decision the sommelier's ordering was already fighting.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-author page two around two placed measures, decide and defend the split by colour and pour order rather than by entry count, re-check the longest appellation still holds in the narrower measure, re-upload, re-run the readiness check, re-export, and audit page two from the returned markup.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A printed menu whose second page is a single tall column with the last several wines missing entirely, delivered as a document that reported success at every step and whose first page looked correct in the only preview anyone opened.

deliverables.name: Kantyna Nova house plate photography
deliverables.spec: Fourteen plate masters brought to one dark house target, one black point, one warmth and one sense of where the light falls, with glaze speculars reading as light on a surface rather than as flat holes, plus one licensed camera scale dining interior frame graded into the same world. At or below source pixel dimensions, with a per frame parameter log and the picture to course reconciliation stated, including the course that has no photograph.

deliverables.name: Kantyna Nova printed menu, two pages
deliverables.spec: One native editable document at a true European page size, the tasting menu on page one and the forty two entry wine list on page two as real table markup holding two columns as delivered, split by colour and pour order rather than by entry count, every text object live and editable in one licensed type system with family and real numeric weight declared per element, prices at body size in the text face. Delivered with the self contained source, the half that guarantees the room can reprint in six weeks.

deliverables.name: Partner deck, reservations page and opening social set
deliverables.spec: A six slide partner deck at wide canvas ending on the price build up, a reservations page carrying the hours as a real table, and three opening social canvases at three sizes inside one export each keeping its own canvas, all on the same type system and the same graded photography, every image carried as embedded data. Delivered with their sources.

deliverables.spec: The printer's press card reverse engineered into a live merge template with every placeholder confirmed present by inspection of the re-exported document, then run against the December bookings: one press PDF with page count equal to row count in roster order, per guest single record files named on a key that survives two guests sharing a name, and print resolution proofs. Every card carries that guest's own graded dish picture, and every field is readable at trim on the longest record as well as the shortest.

deliverables.name: House note and selects board

Paired with a persistent shareable selects board carrying the graded set and the licensed frame with nothing silently dropped.

verifiers_human.text: On every delivered plate the sauce gloss and the porcelain rim read as light on a surface, not as a flat hole.
verifiers_human.how: View each frame at full resolution and look specifically at the brightest region of each.

verifiers_human.text: Page two of the printed menu holds two columns with every wine present, and the split falls somewhere meaningful.
verifiers_human.how: Open the exported menu in Express, look at page two, and read the break point against the sommelier's list.

verifiers_human.text: Every private dining card is fully readable at trim on the longest record as well as the shortest.
verifiers_human.how: View the proofs at trim size and read every field on every page against its roster row, starting with the longest wine designation.

verifiers_human.text: The work reads as a one hundred and eighty five dollar tasting room, not as a bistro and not as a three hundred dollar destination.
verifiers_human.how: Judge ground darkness, held space, type scale and how the price is presented against the stated band and guest.

verifiers_human.text: The note tells the owners something they did not already know, including everything that could not be delivered.
verifiers_human.how: Read the note against the run and check the reconciliation, the naming key, the bleed reality and every limitation are named.

verifiers_human.text: The type system declares a real, non-standard numeric weight for each role in every document, family and weight set per element rather than inherited, and the pairing reads as one restrained kit for a one hundred and eighty five dollar room.
verifiers_human.how: Read the returned HzHTML of each of the four documents alongside the note's type table and confirm each declared numeric weight is an actual weight the chosen Adobe Fonts family ships (cross-checked against font_styles), that family and weight are declared on every text element rather than inherited, and that the pairing reads as restrained rather than rustic or luxury pastiche.

decision_gates: Which deliverables need an authored fixed canvas document the room edits itself, and which is a genuine one record per page run at volume.
Whether the fourteen frames are one shoot. The owners believe they nearly are, and the sequence is the only place that can be settled.
How far to push the frames shot under the pass lamp before they stop being worth saving, versus naming them.
How to word the selection so a correction lands on the sauce rather than on the porcelain it sits in.
Which of fourteen frames covers which of fourteen courses, and how to say so when one course has none and one dish has two.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against an eighteen seat room at one hundred and eighty five dollars, plus the real numeric weight per family.
Where the wine list breaks, given the sommelier's ordering is by producer and the pour sequence is by colour.
How much held space each canvas carries. At this band restraint is the design, and a dense benefit led page is a correct looking wrong answer.
Whether to compute offsets from the mapping readout or from the document's own reconstructed text, when both paths report valid.
The key that identifies a per guest file when two guests share a name, and which delivery branch carries per record identity safely.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of dark restaurant food and a picture of a menu. IDENTITY: these are this kitchen's own fourteen plates shot in this room under this light, with the actual approved course titles and the sommelier's actual forty two entry list; a regenerated dish is another restaurant's dish and a regenerated wine list is a fabrication with prices on it. SPEC: the private dining run is one card per guest bound to that guest's own booking row, page count equal to row count, every field readable at trim, which a generated image neither satisfies nor can be checked for, and the menu has to be a true European page the printer accepts. EDITABILITY: the whole commission is defined by two people reprinting the menu every six weeks and rebuilding the deck for the next partner meeting with no designer, so a flat picture of a menu is worthless. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: does this frame have anything left in its highlights, does this record fit its frame at trim, did the list survive the import as two columns.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, the highlight and light-portion adjusters, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds and crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and detection_confidence are verified headless across 27 live calls; no upscaling is specced and the no-enlargement gate is checkable against the tradeoffs array. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt with its validator, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout and document_render_layout are verified fully headless and synchronous end to end, including per-row image binding through an @-prefixed CSV column plus additionalImageFiles, one record per page for PDF with page count equal to row count, per-record files in correct order via createSeparateFiles or a recordRange loop, and true 300 DPI raster. The truncation checkpoint rests on the verified facts that PDF-derived frame granularity is not under the agent's control and that no bleed can be introduced, so no bleed gate is asserted, and the reversed multi-record raster ordering trap is avoided by using only the PDF and createSeparateFiles routes. EXPRESS: a true 210 by 297 millimetre canvas at exactly 96 dpi, multi-page and mixed-canvas export in one call, and tables importing as real per-cell tables are verified, and column-count is a verified silent drop with the returned markup as the only channel and the rendition documented as page one only. Transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined photography passes the 70 KB threshold immediately. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit verified end to end, with the pairing refusal, non-standard numeric weights and all-or-nothing kit call all live findings. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed, license returned a real 7360x4912 JPEG, boards cap at 12 placements per call with 201 meaning partial. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no variable QR, no fill_text, no animate_design, no replace_image, no download_design, no upscaling, no compositing, no OCR, no text-to-image, no photo reaching Express as a URL, no batch above 20.

engagement_title: Corner & Cure counter refit: bring a phone shot food archive to one warm counter look, recover the hand painted board sign as artwork a vinyl cutter can actually use, and build the window, the wall board, the cold case labels and the daily posts off it
vertical: Food, hospitality and travel, a fast casual neighbourhood deli counter with a marketplace storefront, Brooklyn, New York
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork post from a scrappy New York style sandwich shop needing storefront art for a delivery ordering app, asking for something 'gritty, bold, and a little chaotic', 'not polished or corporate', and saying 'we have the assets, they just need to be pulled together so they look like they were shot in the same image'. The real shop is named in the post, so it is laundered to the coined fictional Corner & Cure and the marketplace is genericised. Co-anchors: the Upwork post from a family owned neighbourhood restaurant wanting static paid social creative for two recurring offers, personality stated as 'authentic, community-focused, family-oriented, warm, bold, local neighborhood favorite' and explicitly not a corporate chain, laundered to a fictional operator; and the Freelancer.com post for a fast food counter wanting a 'creative, vibrant, and appetizing' menu in a 'retro, street-food, rustic chalkboard' style with room for photography and print ready output. The ledger's verdict is REBUILD because the original concept sat almost entirely on one authoring surface. The honest fuller commission is what all three clients are really buying: one warm counter look pulled out of their own phone pictures, their own hand painted sign recovered as artwork rather than redrawn, and that material carried onto the window, the wall, the cold case and the daily posts.
client_one_liner: Everything we have was shot on a phone over the counter, the only version of our sign is painted on a board screwed to the wall, and the window guy, the label printer and the ordering app all want files from us this month.
client_brief:
Corner & Cure, counter refit

We are a deli on a corner in Brooklyn. Sandwiches, bowls, a cold case, a coffee machine, twelve to sixteen dollars, people who work nearby and come in three times a week. My father opened it and I run it now. We are refitting the front of house and every piece of paper and vinyl in the place is being replaced at once.

Our pictures. Everything we have was shot on my phone, over the counter, on the paper we wrap on, while people were waiting. There are a lot of them and they are all a bit different: some at lunch with the door open, some at four in the afternoon with just the strip light. We want them to look like one shop. Warm, loud, food up close and looking like you want to eat it now, not like a magazine.

Our sign. The name is painted on a board over the slicer. My father had it done by a sign painter twenty years ago and there is no file anywhere. The window company needs artwork they can cut vinyl from, not a photograph, and it goes on the glass at about a hand's width tall across the middle of the window. It has to still be our sign.

What we need. The board on the wall behind the counter, laid out in tiles so we can swap one when a special changes. A big poster for the window. The daily special posts, in the three shapes the platforms want, in one file we can open ourselves. A small card by the register with our hours and the loyalty thing. Labels for the cold case, one per item, printed off our item list, because the printer wants a run of them. And enough of a written basis that the next person we hire does not repaint the whole thing.

We are not fancy and we do not want to look it. But we are not cheap either, and cheap is what this stuff usually looks like.
price_band_and_audience: Twelve to sixteen dollars for a sandwich or a bowl, walk up neighbourhood trade, mostly twenty to forty five, three visits a week, decided in about eight seconds at the counter or six on a phone. The band is load bearing. At impulse pricing the food is shown warm, saturated and cropped close enough to read across a room, the boards are dense but scannable, the price is set at tile size in the display face because the price is the offer, and the whole thing carries the hand of the painted sign rather than a neutral grid. Treat the same photographs the way the sibling tasting room commission is correctly treated, dark grounds, one dish a page, price whispered at body size, and a twelve dollar sandwich shop reads as pretentious and empty. Push the other way into starbursts and four fonts and it reads as a franchise nobody trusts with a sandwich. A posted job of this shape runs 1,200 to 2,800 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: Sandwiches worth leaving the block for.
brand_identity.sector: A fast casual neighbourhood deli counter with a cold case and a marketplace storefront, on a corner in Brooklyn, New York.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Opened by the current owner's father, now run by his son, Brooklyn, New York. A single corner shop refitting its whole front of house at once.
brand_identity.about: Corner & Cure is a corner deli: sandwiches, bowls, a cold case and a coffee machine, for the people who work nearby and come in three times a week. It is loud, warm and unpretentious, run by the family that opened it. The food is made to be wanted right now, not admired later.
brand_identity.audience: Walk up trade, mostly twenty to forty five, three visits a week, deciding in about eight seconds at the counter or six on a phone. They want appetite and honesty, not polish.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Twelve to sixteen dollars for a sandwich or a bowl. Impulse priced but not cheap: the price is the offer and sits large and proud, while the whole shop works to look like a place that is worth it rather than a bargain or a franchise.
brand_identity.typography: The hand painted board sign carries the name and sets the tone. Around it, a bold condensed display face for the wall board, prices and specials, prices at tile size so they read across the room, with a plain workhorse sans for hours, loyalty rules and small print. Warm and loud, never a novelty pile.
brand_identity.voice: Plainspoken, neighbourhood, a little brash and generous. Example line the brand would write: 'Pulled together, piled high, see you at the counter.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There is no digital version of the sign: the name survives only as a board hand painted by a sign painter twenty years ago and screwed to the wall over the slicer. Everything else was shot on the owner's phone over the counter. A two page written note holds the voice, hours, loyalty rules and section names, and the label printer holds a press file.
brand_identity.values: A family corner shop, second generation. Real food for regulars, made with the hand of a place, not a chain.

assets_supplied.name: cornerandcure_counter_shots/ (18 phone frames)
assets_supplied.kind: Phone photography shot by the owner over the counter across several weeks, food on the shop's own butcher paper, mixed daylight and strip light.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Everything we have. Shot on my phone on the paper we wrap on. Some at lunch, some late afternoon."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The butcher paper sits at almost the same value as a toasted crust, so on an unknown subset of frames a one call knockout returns a clean looking complete cutout that has quietly bitten the crust edge where the two meet, and the bite is invisible until the cutout is placed on the marketplace's flat ground. The frames are also phone scale, so nothing cut from them can carry a large format window piece, and three of the eighteen are the same sandwich shot on three different days.

assets_supplied.name: cornerandcure_board_sign.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of the hand painted name board over the slicer, shot at an angle under tungsten: brush drawn letters with hairline joins, plus a small painted knife device beside the word.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only version of our sign. My father had it painted twenty years ago and there is no file."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The painted letterforms carry hairline brush joins and small counters that a trace holds comfortably at full canvas and closes at the height the window actually reproduces the mark, on the actual glass colour rather than on white. It is also a compound lockup, so a selection naming the whole sign returns the word and silently drops the knife device, and paint and aged board run close in value across the shadowed half of the board.

assets_supplied.name: cornerandcure_label_press.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The press file the label printer supplied for the cold case shelf label: a small landscape label carrying an item name, a size line, a price roundel and a dietary tag strip.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The label our printer already runs. This is his file."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The printed label reads as four separate blocks with a picture well in the roundel, but the roundel is a decorative element rather than a picture frame and the name, size and price were set as one continuous flow, so the frame inventory the conversion exposes is nothing like the printed label suggests. The file carries no bleed, so a press ready delivery with bleed cannot be honoured from it.

assets_supplied.name: cornerandcure_items.csv (38 rows)
assets_supplied.kind: The cold case item list: item name, size, price, dietary tags and a picture column.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Everything in the case. This is the list we print off."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three items were never photographed and their picture cells are simply blank, which no header reveals and which the merge will not complain about. Prices are written inconsistently across rows, and two items share a name at two different sizes, so naming one file per item by name collides and silently overwrites.

assets_supplied.name: cornerandcure_brand_note.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Two pages the owner wrote: the voice, the hours, the loyalty rules, the section names for the wall board and a note that the specials change daily.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "How we talk and what goes where. The specials change every day, so we have to be able to swap them."

acceptance_bar: The eighteen phone frames read as one shop across the wall board, the window and the posts: one warmth, one black point, one sense of how close the food sits. A frame that cannot be brought to the set is named in the note, not shipped at eighty percent.

Every marketplace item tile sits on the flat brand ground at the marketplace's tile size with clear air at every edge, and the cut edge holds where the food meets the wrapping paper when looked at close up rather than at thumbnail scale.

No delivered file exceeds the pixel dimensions of the frame it came from, and no returned resize record carries an enlargement entry. Anything printing larger than a phone frame supports comes from a source that can carry it.

The sign is placeable cutting artwork rather than a picture of a sign: a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath, the knife device present alongside the word, and every counter still open at the height it actually goes on the glass, on the glass colour rather than on white.

The wall board is laid out as tiles that can be swapped one at a time without relaying the board, and every text object is live editable text in one licensed type system with family and real weight declared on the element.
The three social canvases sit in one working document, each keeping its own canvas size, delivered with the self contained source they were built from.
Prices are set at tile size in the display face and read across the room, and the whole system carries the hand of the painted sign rather than a neutral grid.

The cold case run produces one label per item with the right item's own price and tags, page count equalling row count, per item files identifiable where two items share a name, and the three items with no picture handled deliberately rather than left as holes.
Nothing is claimed as press ready with bleed that the supplied print file cannot carry, and the shortfall is reported.

The note records per photograph what was applied and why that frame differs, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and the real numeric weight, every resize any tool reported, the sign recovery and its safe minimum height, and everything that could not be delivered.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, settle which deliverable lands on which surface, and upload every asset holding each returned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: The board, poster, register card and posts are collateral the shop edits itself, which only the authoring surface composes; the cold case labels are one record per page at volume, which only the merge surface does.
trajectory.produces: A surface plan, the confirmed tier, and a manifest keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Look at all eighteen counter frames and triage them: which lighting condition each belongs to, which are off level, how close the food sits, where food meets wrapping paper, and which item each actually shows against the thirty eight row list.
trajectory.judgement: The owner believes he has a picture of everything. The pictures are the only place that can be settled, and reading eighteen frames against thirty eight rows is not counting files.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note plus the picture to item reconciliation.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop, and phone frames have none to spare.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Fix one warm counter target off the best lit frame and bring each of the eighteen toward it with its own call, recording the parameters applied per frame.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a set, not eighteen appetising pictures. One batched call applies one identical parameter set, which is exactly wrong for frames split between open door daylight and a strip light, and at this band warmth is the brand rather than a correction.
trajectory.produces: Eighteen graded masters at source scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Cut the marketplace item tiles: knock each frame onto the flat brand ground at the marketplace's tile size with air at every edge, reading every returned tradeoff record rather than the success message.
trajectory.judgement: The tradeoff array is the only channel that reports what a tool did to a frame's dimensions and it carries no warning language. Optical centring on a stacked sandwich is not geometric centring.
trajectory.produces: Item tiles on the brand ground with their returned tradeoffs recorded.

trajectory.action: Search short generic queries for the counter or street frame the window poster needs, filter to photography, exclude generative candidates, license and download at full resolution, then bring it to the warm target.
trajectory.judgement: Nothing cut from a phone frame can carry a large format window piece, so the poster hero has to come from a source that is genuinely camera scale. Choose the frame whose light can reach the target rather than the best thumbnail.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP clean, camera scale frame graded into the set.

trajectory.action: Recover the painted sign: an ink level selection naming the paint's own visual properties rather than the board it sits on, correct polarity, a bounds crop driven by the selection's own returned bounds, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full canvas ground path removed.
trajectory.judgement: Naming the substrate pulls the selection to the board, a compound naming drops the knife device, background removal is the wrong instrument on painted letterforms with counters, and the tracer takes no options at all, so every lever is in the raster preparation.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent sign plus a colour accurate variant.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged against a twelve to sixteen dollar counter and a hand painted sign it must sit beside without competing.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry or designer and actual weight per role.

trajectory.action: Author the swappable tile wall board, the window poster at a true physical size, the register card and the three daily special canvases, each root declaring its own canvas, photographs carried as embedded image data, the recovered sign placed as inline vector inside an explicitly sized wrapper anchored top left, family and weight declared on every text element.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a reference is not a photograph, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override collapses a mixed size set. The design work is tile density, how large the price sits, and where the sign goes so a swapped special never touches it.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export each document by uploaded URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the rendition and look at the first canvas, and read the returned per canvas markup for everything after it.
trajectory.judgement: Every change this importer makes returns success with no warning, and the rendition only ever shows the first artboard.
trajectory.produces: Native editable documents, an inspected first canvas each, and a markup audit for the rest.

trajectory.action: Convert the label printer's press PDF into a working document and export its interchange form, then read what the conversion actually exposes: how many text frames, how many picture frames, what each holds.
trajectory.judgement: What the printed label looks like says nothing about how the file was set, and the picture well the printed sample implies may not be a picture frame at all. This is also where the bleed question is answered honestly.

trajectory.action: Reconstruct the document's true story text from the interchange file, compute every offset from that string, generate and validate the mapping, prepare the template, then re-export and confirm every expected placeholder is present.
trajectory.judgement: Validation returns valid on offsets computed from a shortened string and preparation reports success either way, so the only evidence a field landed is finding it in the re-exported document.

trajectory.action: Cut the label pictures from the graded masters to the label's proportion, reading what each crop reports about its confidence and bounds, and reconcile them against the item list including the rows that have nothing.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the cut edge survives where the food meets the paper it is sitting on. The shop wraps on butcher paper and photographs on it, and on an unknown subset of frames the paper sits at almost the value of a toasted crust. The knockout reports success, the returned cutout is complete and clean at thumbnail scale, and the bite only exists along the short stretch where crust and paper share luminance. Which frames it happens to is a property of each photograph's own light, not of the sandwich, and there is no confidence figure and no edge report anywhere in the response.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering does not dodge it, because the edge quality is a fact about this frame meeting this tool and exists only after the call has run and the result has been looked at on the ground it will sit on, not on white. Nothing states it: the brief says only that the food was shot on the paper they wrap on. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different chain for the affected frames, a material named selection of the wrapping paper, inverted and filled to the brand ground.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-plan the knockout route per frame, re-derive the affected tiles through the selection and fill chain, and re-inspect every tile against the marketplace's actual flat ground rather than against white.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A marketplace storefront where the hero sandwiches have a chewed edge along the crust on the frames nobody looked at closely, on the one surface where a customer decides in six seconds.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered sign is still the sign at the height it actually reproduces. The trace comes back looking correct: the word is there, the brush drawn letterforms are there, the counters are open, and at full canvas on a white page it is a faithful recovery. The window company puts it on the glass at about a hand's width tall across a dark painted band, and at that height on that ground the hairline brush joins fill in and the small counters close into solid blobs. The tracer takes no options at all, so nothing about the trace call can be tuned; the only evidence is placing the artwork at its real reproduction size on its real ground and looking.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the answer depends on the trace, the reproduction height and the ground colour being present together, and the first two are produced by the agent while the third is a property of the window. Nothing states it: the brief asks for artwork the window company can cut and says the mark has to still be their sign. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different raster preparation feeding the same tracer, a differently worded selection, a fill and flatten plate instead of a binary mask, or a bounds crop that changes what the tracer sees, since the tracer itself has no lever.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-prepare the raster on a different route, re-trace, re-inject the viewBox and strip the opaque ground path again, then re-place the result at reproduction height on the real ground and re-judge, and state a safe minimum height in the handover once one is actually known.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Vinyl cut and applied to the window in which the family name reads as a row of solid shapes, which is both the most visible piece in the refit and the one that cannot be quietly reprinted.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether each delivered label proof actually contains the record its filename claims. The natural way to give counter staff a proof per item is a multi record raster run, and the tool's own description says one output file per row and hands back a list labelled by row number. The labels are wrong: the files come back in an order that does not match the roster, and nothing in the response says so. Every gate above it passes, the count is right, each file is a valid label, and the only way to find out is to open the files and read the item name and price inside them against the row they were named for.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it and no parameter controls it, because the mislabelling is in the response itself and the response is the only thing an agent that trusts its tools would use to name the files. Nothing states it: the acceptance line about the right item's own price is the shop's requirement and the brief never characterises the delivery. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different delivery route, either a single multi page run whose page order is trustworthy or a per record run producing one file at a time so identity is guaranteed.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Abandon the multi record raster route, re-run the cold case set through a route whose record identity is guaranteed, rename every proof from what is actually inside it, and re-check the two items that share a name so the collision does not silently overwrite.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A cold case where the price under the turkey is the price of the roast beef, printed, laminated and clipped into the rail, discovered by a customer rather than by the shop.

decision_gates: Which deliverables need an authored fixed canvas document the shop edits itself, and which is a genuine one record per page run at volume.
Whether the eighteen frames are one shop, and how far to push the strip light frames before they stop being worth saving.
Knockout route per frame, between the one call route and a material named selection of the wrapping paper inverted and filled, where food and paper share value.
Where the window poster hero comes from, given nothing cut from a phone frame can carry it and enlargement is not an option.
Selection wording on the painted board: naming the board takes the substrate, naming the paint's own visual properties takes the mark, and a compound naming silently drops the knife device.
Whether the single colour cutting version or the colour accurate variant is what the window company actually needs, judged at reproduction height on the glass colour.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against an impulse band and a hand painted sign it must sit beside, plus the real numeric weight per family.
How dense the wall board can get before it stops being scannable across the room, and how large the price has to sit for the offer to survive at eight seconds.
What a label for an item with no photograph looks like, decided before the run rather than found on the printed sheet.
Which delivery route carries per record identity safely, and what key names a file when two items share a name.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns appetising pictures of sandwiches and a picture of a chalkboard. IDENTITY: these are this shop's own sandwiches on this shop's own paper, and the sign is a specific hand painted board a sign painter made twenty years ago, which has to be RECOVERED rather than reinvented, because a regenerated sign is a different family's name in a different hand and the window company cuts vinyl from paths, not from a picture. SPEC: the marketplace needs tiles at an exact size on a flat ground with a cut edge that survives close inspection, the window needs a closed path that still reads at a stated height, and the cold case needs one label per item bound to that item's own price with page count equal to row count, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the specials change daily and the shop swaps them itself, so a flat picture of a board is worthless a day after delivery. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did this cutout bite the crust, does this trace hold at hand height on green, is the price inside this file the price on this row.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, select_subject, invert_selection, fill_area, remove_background in both the transparent and backgroundColor forms, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and detection_confidence, and vectorize are verified headless across 27 live calls. The knockout checkpoint rests on documented findings: remove_background needs one coherent blob, its edge behaviour is a property of the frame, a material named selection inverted and filled is the verified alternative route, and the family reports no edge quality figure of any kind. The sign checkpoint rests on the verified facts that image_vectorize takes NO options at all so all tuning is raster preparation, that a compound mark selection silently drops elements, that naming the substrate returns the substrate, that the trace emits no viewBox, and that path index zero is always an opaque full canvas rectangle. No upscaling is specced and the no-enlargement gate is checkable against the tradeoffs array, which is why the poster hero comes from licensed Stock at camera scale. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt with its validator, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout with additionalImageFiles and document_render_layout are verified fully headless and synchronous, with one record per page for PDF and page count equal to row count; the proof-ordering checkpoint rests on the verified finding that multi-record PNG and JPEG output comes back REVERSED while the response labels it by row, with PDF, createSeparateFiles and a recordRange loop as the three verified trustworthy routes. PDF-derived frame granularity is not under the agent's control and no bleed can be introduced, so no bleed gate is asserted. EXPRESS: true physical canvases at exactly 96 dpi, mixed canvas sizes in one export, inline SVG becoming native editable vector shapes, and a genuinely editable native document findable by asset_search are verified, with the rendition documented as page one only. Transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit verified end to end. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed, license returned a real 7360x4912 JPEG, boards cap at 12 placements per call with 201 meaning partial and SVG unsupported. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no variable QR, no fill_text, no animate_design, no replace_image, no download_design, no upscaling, no compositing, no OCR, no text-to-image, no photo reaching Express as a URL, no batch above 20.

engagement_title: Lumora Laboratories national counter launch: build the store-page set, the counter-card run and the brand basis the next freelancer follows, off six bottle frames and one approved wordmark
vertical: Beauty, cosmetics and personal care, clinical dermo-cosmetic actives, direct to consumer plus a specialty chain counter rollout (Chicago, Illinois)
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the real Upwork 'premium clinical skincare brand, logo, label and packaging' launch post quoted in the ledger's grounding_note, which asks for a cohesive, credible visual identity across the product line plus explicitly 'print-ready files and editable source files', with a stated aesthetic of clean and minimalist, modern and timeless, science-driven and trustworthy, premium but not luxurious, clinical credibility, strong typography, whitespace and white-background ecommerce imagery. The real post names no client, so the line is laundered to a coined fictional brand; the ledger's placeholder token is superseded here by Lumora Laboratories, which names no real company, product or trademark. VERDICT STRENGTHEN, so the concept and the collateral set are kept and deepened. The ledger's own repositioning note conceded that from-scratch identity art and free-form composition were not connector work, but CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) changes what the honest fuller commission is: HTML authoring now yields a native editable Express document at mixed canvas sizes, a supplied press PDF converts into a live InDesign merge template, and a flat approved wordmark can be brought to placeable vector. So this is that client's actual job. They asked for a credible clinical look across a product line, print-ready files and editable source files, and all three are now genuinely producible: store-page collateral the founders can edit next season, a per-SKU counter-card run at press resolution for the chain, and a written basis their next freelancer works from.
client_one_liner: Our six products go onto a specialty chain's counters and onto our rebuilt store page in February, our photographs do not read as one line, and everything a customer sees has to change at once.
client_brief:
Lumora Laboratories, first national counter season

We are a four person clinical skincare line in Chicago. Six products, all actives led, sold for two years through our own site and two dermatology practices. In February we rebuild our store page and go onto a specialty chain's counters at the same time, so every picture and every piece of print a customer sees changes at once.

The pictures. All six bottles were photographed on the same pale sweep in the same room. Two of them were re-photographed later because the formula changed, so those files are newer. Individually they are fine. Put them in a row the way a product page puts them and they are not one line: some read cooler, and the glass shoulder disappears on a couple of them. We need them square, on clean white, the bottle centred with air at every edge and nothing invented behind it. The chain also wants versions with nothing behind them at all, because their page sits products on a coloured band of their own.

The store page. Three tiles per product: the bottle, an ingredient panel, and a specification panel with the INCI list and the concentrations as a proper table. Then the paid social set, a wide one, a square one and a tall one, in one working file we can change ourselves, because the launch date and the featured product will move.

The counter cards. The chain approved the card artwork last year and sent us the print file. We need one card per product carrying that product's name, its INCI line, its concentration and its claim, at print resolution, plus a single file the printer can run.

The basis page. Whoever we hire next needs one page that says what type we are on, what our colours are, how the mark may be used and how the ingredient story is drawn.

Our products are forty six to eighty dollars. Our customer is twenty eight to forty five and she compares ingredient lists before she reads copy. It should look like a laboratory with taste. And a note on what you did and anything we should know.
price_band_and_audience: Clinical dermo-cosmetic actives at 46 to 80 dollars per SKU, buyer 28 to 45 and ingredient literate. The band is load-bearing. At this price the range must sit on restrained near-monochrome grounds, the ingredient hierarchy has to lead with evidence (actives, concentrations, function) and the price has to sit quietly beside the specification rather than announce itself. The same six products at a 14 dollar mass band would correctly be shot warm and saturated, cropped tight to fill the tile, and sold on a benefit burst and a strike-through price, and shipping that treatment here repels the exact buyer who is reading the INCI list. Push the other way into near-black grounds, gold rules and cosmetic gloss and it becomes a 250 dollar luxury line, which misprices an 46 dollar cleanser and undercuts the clinical claim it depends on. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. A posted job of this shape runs 1,800 to 3,400 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: Clinical dermo-cosmetic actives, direct to consumer plus a specialty chain counter rollout, based in Chicago, Illinois.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2024, Chicago, Illinois. A four person actives led skincare line, six products, sold through its own site and two dermatology practices for two years.
brand_identity.about: Lumora Laboratories formulates clinical skincare around published actives at concentrations it names openly. Six products, evidence first, made for a customer who compares ingredient lists before she reads copy. In February the line rebuilds its store page and steps onto a specialty chain's counters at the same time, so everything a customer sees changes at once.
brand_identity.audience: Women twenty eight to forty five, ingredient literate, who read the INCI list before the claim and treat whitespace and evidence as signs of seriousness.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Forty six to eighty dollars per SKU. Premium but not luxurious: near monochrome grounds, evidence led hierarchy, and a price that sits quietly beside the specification. Deliberately clear of both the fourteen dollar mass aisle and the two hundred and fifty dollar luxury counter, either of which would misread the clinical claim.
brand_identity.typography: A neo-grotesque for the wordmark, product names and headings, set with real whitespace and strong hierarchy. A clear text face for INCI lines, concentrations and specification tables, where legibility of a long ingredient string matters more than character. Clinical, never spa.
brand_identity.voice: Precise and evidence first, no hyperbole. Example line the brand would write: 'Formulated around actives, at concentrations we publish.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The wordmark is approved but exists only as a flat web scale PNG of the letterforms in one deep ink on white, exported by the founders' first designer, with no vector source on hand. The six products were photographed in house on a pale sweep across two sessions. The regulatory cleared INCI lines and claims are fixed and cannot be edited, and the specialty chain has supplied its approved counter card press file.
brand_identity.values: Clinical credibility earned through disclosure. Actives and concentrations named, nothing oversold.

acceptance_bar: The six bottles read as ONE line when laid in a row the way a product page lays them: one white point, one black point, one crop logic, one product height in frame. A frame that cannot be brought to the set is named in the note, not shipped at eighty percent.

Every product tile is square at the retailer's stated tile size, the bottle optically centred with clear air at every edge, and the cut edge holds on the two frames where the glass runs close to the ground in value, inspected at full resolution and on the chain's coloured band rather than at preview scale.

No delivered file exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions and no returned tradeoff record in the run carries an upscale entry. A tile that reaches its size by being enlarged fails even if it looks acceptable.
The specification tile carries the INCI list and concentrations as a real table with per cell structure, not as a picture of a table and not as run-on text.
Every counter card carries the WHOLE of its record: the full INCI line and the full cleared claim, present at trim on the delivered file, on all six.

The counter-card run is delivered as one press file with page count equal to row count, in row order, PLUS one correctly identified file per product at genuine print resolution. A proof at screen resolution is not a proof.

Every counter card carries the record's OWN bottle, cut from the graded masters to the card's portrait picture-well proportion and bound per row, present at genuine print resolution with no placement enlarged past the pixels its source frame actually holds, and the bottle on each card is the product the record names; a frame that cannot reach the well without interpolation is named, not enlarged to fit.

The mark is placeable artwork rather than a picture of artwork: transparent ground, a real viewBox present, no opaque full-canvas rectangle riding underneath, and legible at the size it actually reproduces on the tiles and reversed on the house ground.
In every authored document the words are text that can be retyped and the mark is live vector shapes, not a flattened picture of a layout.
The store-page tiles and the three social canvases sit in ONE working file, each root keeping its own canvas size, delivered with the self-contained source it was built from.
The basis page's usage rules read as a set column of rules beside the colourways, not as a single run of text colliding with the swatches, on the delivered document rather than on the first root.
One type system across every canvas and the card run, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the actual numeric weight used.

The note states, per photograph, what was applied and why that frame differs from its neighbours, every resize any tool reported, what the counter card could not be made to do, and anything the founders should know about the mark.
