adobe_surfaces.role: The store-page tiles, the three social canvases and the basis page as native editable documents carrying roots at several canvas sizes, which is the only surface in the connector that composes free-form fixed-canvas layout. Every photograph must be pulled down and inlined as image data because a URL renders as an empty grey box at full success, the mark goes in as inline SVG so it stays vector, the specification tile is a real table, the ingredient chart is inline SVG, family and weight are declared on every text element, and the payload travels by uploaded URL because inlined photography passes the inline threshold immediately.

adobe_surfaces.surface: InDesign layout and data merge
adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt (as generator and as validator), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout (recordRange, additionalImageFiles, outputSpecs), document_render_layout (resolution, createSeparateFiles, pageRange)
adobe_surfaces.role: The counter-card run, which is genuine record-per-page variable data and belongs nowhere else. The chain's approved press PDF is reverse engineered into a live merge template, the mapping is computed against the document's true story text rather than the readout, and the run is delivered on both branches: one press file with page count equal to row count for the printer, and correctly identified per-product files at real print resolution for sign off. The card carries each record's own bottle, so the merge binds a picture per row through additionalImageFiles into the card's one genuine graphic frame, and the print-resolution render is where a plate that passed at store-tile scale is caught under-resolved and sent back to imaging.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Fonts
adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: The type system carrying every canvas and the basis page. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to land on clinical rather than spa. Numeric weights are non-standard per family and cannot be inferred from a style name, every name must be laundered into canonical PostScript form before the kit call because one bad name kills the whole kit, and the CSS must use the returned slug or the face falls back silently.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (entityScope StockAsset, SHORT query, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the one frame the founders do not have, a quiet laboratory bench band for the wide social canvas, IP-clean, at genuine camera scale and with generative-tech candidates excluded. The Boards half persists the shared selects set the founders sign off from, placed within the per-call cap, with a partial success read as partial and vector understood to be unacceptable there.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching a pixel.
trajectory.judgement: The tiles and social canvases are free-form fixed-canvas layout and only one surface composes that. The counter cards are one record per page at volume and belong on the merge surface. Putting the cards on the authoring surface would mean hand-building six near identical layouts and losing print resolution.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming surface per deliverable, plus the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline: a manifest keyed by role so that forty artefacts later the agent still knows which URL is which frame and which is the press PDF.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Preview all six bottle frames, the wordmark and the reference page, and triage: which session each frame belongs to, how each sits for warmth, where the sweep runs close to the glass in value, and what pixel dimensions each frame actually has.
trajectory.judgement: The client asserts one sweep and one room. The files are the only thing that can settle whether they are one capture at all, and reading dimensions off the manifest is faster and less reliable than looking at what the frames actually are.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note covering illuminant, tilt, capture scale and subject contrast against the ground.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level, before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes the subject and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop without invalidating it.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Fix one clinical target off the best lit frame and correct each of the six toward it with its own call, recording the parameters applied.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a set, not six good pictures. One batched call applies one identical parameter set, which is exactly wrong for frames shot months apart under different daylight; the agent has to hold one destination and reach it by different routes.
trajectory.produces: Six graded masters at source scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Work the frames where the ground and the glass run close together: recover the upper tones so the shoulder separates from the sweep, and apply masked corrections where a whole-frame move would take the amber glass green or the sweep muddy.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the whole gate on a masked correction: naming the substrate pulls the selection to the sweep, naming the material's own visual properties pulls it to the glass. Recovery is the move that decides whether the next step has an edge to cut against.
trajectory.produces: Corrected frames, with the response to each recovery call recorded rather than assumed.

trajectory.action: Knock the six out on both routes the client needs: a clean white ground for the store tiles and genuinely transparent variants for the chain's coloured band. Read every returned tradeoffs object rather than the success message.
trajectory.judgement: The tradeoffs array is the only channel that reports what a tool did to a frame's dimensions and it carries no warning language. The frames whose shoulder never separated will not behave like the others, and the route has to be decided per frame rather than for the set.
trajectory.produces: Six white-ground plates and six transparent variants, each with its returned tradeoffs recorded.

trajectory.action: Cut the square store tiles at the retailer's spec, product optically centred with clear air at every edge, checking each returned record for an upscale entry.
trajectory.judgement: Optical centring is not geometric centring on a bottle with a tall pump. The two newer files are the ones where a size demand and a source frame can quietly disagree, and the only signal is inside the response.
trajectory.produces: Six tiles at spec plus six on-colour variants, with a per file source-versus-output dimension table.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for a quiet bench band, filter to photography, exclude generative-tech results, license and download at full resolution, then bring it to the same target as the range.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose existing light can be brought to the clinical target rather than the prettiest thumbnail. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP-clean, camera-scale frame graded into the same world.

trajectory.action: Bring the approved wordmark to placeable artwork: an ink-level selection at the right polarity, a bounds crop from the selection's own returned box, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full-canvas ground path removed. Derive the house colourways from one mask with different adjustment parameters.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions the tools do not make: how to word the selection so it takes the letterforms and not the paper, which polarity to trace, and whether the knockout route is even the right instrument on disjoint lettering. The colourways are one mask and divergent parameters, not three separate archaeologies.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent mark plus its house colourways, with the parameters dialled for each recorded.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit for the whole engagement.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged against a 46 to 80 dollar clinical band and an ingredient-literate reader. The weight cannot be inferred from a style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug, not by asking for a heavier weight.
trajectory.produces: A one-kit type system with family, foundry and actual numeric weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Convert the chain's press PDF to a working document, export the interchange format, and read the real frame inventory: how many text frames the card actually became, how many graphic frames exist, and what each frame's true story text is.
trajectory.judgement: What a printed card looks like and what it converts into are unrelated. The inventory is the only thing that says whether fields can be mapped per frame or have to be placed inside one story, and that decision changes every mapping row that follows.
trajectory.produces: A frame inventory with bounds, applied type and the reconstructed story text for each frame.

trajectory.action: Build the mapping against the document's own reconstructed story text, validate it, prepare the merge template, then round-trip the interchange format again and confirm every expected field placeholder is actually present.
trajectory.judgement: A valid verdict and a completed successfully message are both cheap. The only evidence that a field landed is the field appearing in the prepared document's story, and checking that costs one extra export the tools never ask for.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholder inventory has been read back rather than trusted.

trajectory.action: Cut the counter-card bottle plates from the graded masters to the card's picture-well proportion, which is a portrait crop at print resolution rather than the retailer's square screen tile, reading every returned tradeoff record for an upscale entry and reconciling the six plates to the six rows against the copy.
trajectory.judgement: The square store tiles cannot be reused: the well is a different proportion and the card is a print piece, not a screen one, so the plates have to be re-cut to carry at 300 ppi. The two re-photographed SKUs are where a print-resolution demand and a phone-scale source quietly disagree, and reading a frame's stated dimensions is not the same as reading what the crop had to do to reach the well.
trajectory.produces: Six card-proportion bottle plates at the well's print resolution where the source allows it, each with its returned tradeoffs recorded.

trajectory.action: Merge the six records one record per page, binding each row's own bottle plate into the card's one genuine graphic frame through additionalImageFiles, deliver the press file in row order, produce correctly identified per-product files at genuine print resolution through the render step, and read each merged page at trim for its text.
trajectory.judgement: The card carries a picture, so a text-only merge ships six cards with an empty well or one bottle repeated across all six. The two branches are still not interchangeable: one file for the printer and identified files for sign off are different deliverables, and a per-record file is only a proof if it is at print resolution and if the product on it is the product the filename claims.
trajectory.produces: One press file with page count equal to row count, plus six identified per-product files at print resolution, each carrying its own bound bottle.

trajectory.action: Read each rendered per-product card's placed picture at trim: not whether a picture is present, but its effective resolution inside the well and whether the crop framing holds, checked against the row the file is named for.
trajectory.judgement: A well set to fill proportionally scales an under-pixelled plate up to fit and reports nothing, so the presence of a bottle is not evidence it is at print quality. The store-tile scale the two phone SKUs squeaked past is smaller than the card well at print size, so a plate that passed there can still be soft here, and the only signal is the placed picture's effective ppi read off the rendered file.
trajectory.produces: A per-card table of the placed picture's effective resolution and framing against its row, flagging any plate the well interpolated.

trajectory.action: For the two phone-scale SKUs whose plates the print render exposed as under the well's resolution, return to the graded masters and re-cut from the largest usable region, decide per frame whether the well can be reached without enlarging or whether the frame has to be named for a re-shoot rather than interpolated, then re-run the merge and re-render those records.
trajectory.judgement: The print render is the first place the shortfall is visible and it is a hard gate: enlarging to fill the well is the one move the acceptance bar forbids, so the answer is a tighter re-cut, a smaller placed size the layout can carry, or a named limitation, never an upscale. Re-cutting changes the plate the merge binds, so the affected records have to go back through the run.
trajectory.produces: Re-cut plates or a named re-shoot for the two affected SKUs, and a re-merged, re-rendered pair of cards carrying them.

trajectory.action: Author the store-page document: three tiles per product at the retailer's square canvas plus the wide, square and tall social roots, every photograph inlined as image data, the mark as inline SVG in an explicitly sized top-left anchored wrapper, the specification panel as a real table, family and weight on every text element, each root declaring its own canvas. Upload and hold the returned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto-sized right-anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override is what collapses a mixed-size set. The design work is how much air the clinical band takes and how quietly the price sits beside the specification.
trajectory.produces: One export-ready HTML carrying the store-page and social set, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Author the basis page at print proportions carrying the type roles, the palette, the mark colourways, the usage rules and the ingredient chart as inline SVG. Run the readiness check, export both documents, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve each document's rendition and look at root one, and parse the returned per-root markup for every other root.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition preview only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at root one is not looking at the deliverable, and the basis page is where a construction that reads as ordinary page furniture is most likely to be the one that did not survive.
trajectory.produces: Native editable documents, an inspected first root each, and a per-root markup audit for everything after it.

trajectory.action: Create the selects board, add the graded set and the licensed frame within the per-call placement cap, re-sending only the entries the response names as failed, then write the handover note.
trajectory.judgement: A partial success is reported as a success code, and the vector mark is not boardable so it belongs in the note instead. The note has to be specific enough that the next freelancer does not repeat the work.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the ground can be separated from the glass on the frames where the two run together. On two of the six the sweep was exposed past clipping exactly at the bottle's shoulder, and the recovery move on a clipped region returns a frame in which the readout is that nothing moves: the call succeeds, the parameters are accepted, the response carries no warning and the returned frame is visually indistinguishable from the one that went in. Nothing in the frame's appearance says which frames are clipped, because a clipped white sweep and a merely bright one look the same. It is only after the recovery has been run and the result looked at that the agent learns there is no tonal information there to recover, and therefore no edge for the next step to cut against.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter prevents it, because the operation is the diagnostic: recovery is the correct move to try, and its own null result is the only report that the region is clipped. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the glass shoulder disappears on a couple of the frames, which is the client describing what she sees, not a disclosure that the data is gone. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is a different route entirely: abandon transparency on those two and composite onto the house ground in a single knockout call so the ground is part of the raster, or select the sweep by its own material properties, invert and fill so the boundary is drawn rather than detected.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-plan the knockout route for the affected frames, re-derive both the white-ground plate and the coloured-band variant through the new route, and re-cut their tiles, then re-judge the whole row of six as a set because the two reworked frames now reach the target by a different path.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Two of six product tiles delivered with the bottle's shoulder bitten away against the chain's coloured band, on a line whose entire claim is precision, discovered by the chain rather than by the studio.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the chain's approved card actually is once it is a working document, and whether the field mapping computed against it is even addressing the right characters. The card prints as four separate blocks and converts into a single continuous flow, so there are no per-field frames to target and every field has to be placed by position inside one story. Worse, the readout of that story silently omits one run while keeping its line break, so the string still looks well formed and every offset past the omission is short by exactly that run's length. The validator returns a valid verdict on those wrong offsets with no warnings, and the placeholder step reports completed successfully. Nothing in any response distinguishes a template with all six fields from one with four.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering does not help: the conversion is the first possible moment the granularity exists, and the readout is the tool's own answer to the question the agent is asking. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the chain approved the artwork and sent the print file, which is the client telling the truth about provenance. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the fix is to reconstruct the true story text from the document's own interchange format, recompute every offset against that string, and re-verify by reading the prepared template's placeholders back, which is a different chain from the one that produced the first mapping.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the mapping from the reconstructed story text, re-prepare the template, re-export and grep the prepared document for every expected field, then re-merge and read the resulting pages at trim, where the two long claim records will also show whether a fixed measure block stopped rendering rather than spilled.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A counter-card run shipped to the chain's printer in which two of the six fields are silently absent on every card and two records lose the tail of a regulatory-cleared claim, with every tool response in the chain having reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the two re-photographed SKUs' bottles actually carry inside the card's picture well at print size. The card binds each record's own plate, and the well is a fixed portrait measure set to fill proportionally, so an under-pixelled plate is scaled up to fill it with no error: the merge succeeds, the render succeeds, every per-product file has a bottle in it, and at store-tile scale those same two plates passed their gate. It is only after the card is rendered at print resolution and the placed picture's effective ppi is read off it that the shortfall shows, because the well at 300 ppi asks for more pixels than a phone frame at a third of the others' dimensions can supply once it is cropped to a portrait bottle, and nothing in the merge or render response distinguishes a plate placed at native resolution from one interpolated up to fill.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it: the print-resolution well is a strictly larger demand than the screen tile, so a plate can legitimately clear the tile gate and fail here, and the render is the first moment the placed resolution exists to be read. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the two SKUs were re-photographed after the reformulation, which is the client telling the truth about provenance, not a disclosure that those frames are a third of the scale or that the card asks more of them than the store page did. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is a cross-surface return to imaging, re-cutting those two plates from the largest usable region of the master and deciding per frame between a smaller placed size the layout can carry and a named re-shoot, then re-binding and re-rendering, which is a different chain from the one that produced the first cards.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Return to Photoshop for the two affected records, re-cut the card plates from the graded masters at the largest region the source holds, decide whether the well can be reached without enlarging or the frame must be named rather than interpolated, then re-run the merge binding the corrected plates and re-render those per-product cards, reading the placed ppi back rather than trusting the second success.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Two of the six counter cards shipped to the chain's printer with a visibly soft, interpolated bottle enlarged to fill the well, on a line whose entire claim is precision, past an acceptance bar that forbids any enlarged placement, with every merge and render response having reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the construction the basis page's rules block is built on. A usage-rules column set beside the colourway swatches is the ordinary way to lay that page out, and the importer discards the multi-column construct entirely: the text reflows as one column at full success, with the gap value retained and meaningless. The returned per-root markup is the only channel that reports it, and the document's own rendition returns the first root only, so the basis page cannot be checked visually at all. Whether the rules still read as a set column beside the swatches, or run the length of the page and collide with them, is visible only after the export.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the drop happens at import and the import is the last step; and doing it right the first time presumes knowing which of several plausible constructions survives, which no response reports and no checklist enumerates. (b) Nothing states it. The acceptance line about the rules reading as a set column beside the swatches is the client's own requirement for the page, not a warning about an importer. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is to re-author the block as two explicitly measured text frames placed at chosen coordinates, which changes where the copy breaks and therefore what goes in each column, so the rules have to be re-cast rather than re-exported.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-author the basis page around explicitly placed fixed-measure frames, re-decide the copy split across them, re-upload, re-run the readiness check, re-export, and audit every root from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A basis page delivered as the document the next freelancer is supposed to work from, in which the usage rules run down the page through the colourway swatches, on the one root nobody could look at, with the export having reported success throughout.

deliverables.name: Lumora house photography, six SKUs plus the licensed bench frame
deliverables.spec: Six bottle masters brought to one clinical target (one white point, one black point, one product height in frame) plus one licensed camera-scale bench frame graded into the same world. Delivered with a per frame parameter log including one line on why each frame differs from its neighbours and what capture it actually came from.

deliverables.name: Lumora store tile set, white ground and on-colour
deliverables.spec: Six square store tiles at the retailer's tile size on clean white, product optically centred with air at every edge and a cut edge that holds under close inspection, plus six genuinely transparent variants for the chain's coloured band. Every output at or below its source frame's pixel dimensions with the returned tradeoff record for each. One set with one cut logic, not one picture at several sizes.

deliverables.name: Lumora mark, placeable artwork and house colourways
deliverables.spec: The approved wordmark brought from a flat opaque raster to placeable scalable geometry with a transparent ground: a real viewBox present, no opaque full-canvas rectangle riding underneath, legible at the size it reproduces on the tiles and reversed on the house ground. Delivered with the house colourways derived from one mask and divergent adjustment parameters, each parameter set reported.

deliverables.name: Lumora store-page and paid-social set, plus the basis page
deliverables.spec: Native editable documents carrying three product tiles per SKU at the retailer's square canvas, the wide, square and tall social roots each keeping its own canvas size, and a basis page at print proportions carrying the type roles, palette, mark colourways, usage rules and the ingredient chart as inline vector. Live editable text in one licensed type system, the mark as real vector shapes, the specification panel as a real table, and every photograph carried as embedded image data rather than a reference. Delivered with the self-contained source, which is the durable half.

deliverables.name: Lumora counter-card run
deliverables.spec: Six counter cards, one record per page, built on the chain's own approved artwork: one press file whose page count equals the row count in row order for the printer, plus one correctly identified file per product at genuine print resolution for sign off. Every card carries the whole of its record, full INCI line and full cleared claim, present at trim. Each card also carries the product's OWN bottle, cut from the graded masters to the card's portrait picture-well proportion and bound per row through the merge, present at genuine print resolution with no placement enlarged past the pixels its source frame holds; the two re-photographed phone-scale SKUs are re-cut from the largest usable region or named for a re-shoot rather than interpolated to fill the well, and the bottle on every card is the product the record names.

deliverables.name: Handover note and selects board
deliverables.spec: A written note recording per photograph what was applied and why that frame differs from its neighbours, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and the actual numeric weight, every resize any tool reported with the frame it applied to, what the counter card could not be made to do and why, and anything the founders should know about placing the mark. Paired with a persistent shareable selects board carrying the graded set and the licensed frame with nothing silently dropped.

verifiers_auto.text: Six store tiles exist, all square, all at the retailer's stated tile size, and no delivered file exceeds the pixel dimensions of the frame it derives from.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the pixel dimensions of every delivered file and compare each against its source frame per the manifest.

verifiers_auto.text: No crop or knockout tradeoff record captured in the run carries an upscale entry, and every downscale entry is transcribed in the handover note.
verifiers_auto.how: Diff the tradeoffs objects captured from every image call against the resize table in the note.

verifiers_auto.text: The six on-colour variants carry genuine alpha rather than a white rectangle.
verifiers_auto.how: Inspect each variant's alpha channel for partial-alpha pixels at the product boundary and full transparency at the frame corners.

verifiers_auto.text: The delivered mark SVG has a viewBox attribute and no full-canvas opaque background path at index zero.
verifiers_auto.how: Parse the SVG: assert a viewBox is present and assert the first path's geometry does not span the whole canvas.

verifiers_auto.text: The prepared merge template's story contains a placeholder for every field the card is supposed to carry.
verifiers_auto.how: Export the interchange format of the prepared template and grep the stories for each expected field token.

verifiers_auto.text: The press file's page count equals the CSV row count and the pages are in row order, and six per-product files exist at genuine print resolution.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the page count and per page text of the press file against the CSV, and read the pixel dimensions and density of each per-product file.

verifiers_auto.text: Each exported Express document returned the expected number of roots, each keeping its own declared canvas size.
verifiers_auto.how: Read slide_count and the per-root width and height in each export response.

verifiers_auto.text: No image in any root resolved to the importer's placeholder, the specification panel arrived as table structure, and the mark arrived as vector path shapes rather than one picture.
verifiers_auto.how: Parse the returned per-root markup for placeholder image data, for table cell structure, and count path shape elements in the mark region.

verifiers_auto.text: Every text element in every exported root carries a resolved licensed face rather than a fallback default.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the font-family attribute on every text node in the returned markup and check it against the families the kit call returned.

verifiers_auto.text: The selects board exists with the expected item count and an empty failed items list after the final call.
verifiers_auto.how: Read boardId and the addedEntityIds and failedItems arrays from the board responses.

verifiers_auto.text: Every per-product card carries the bottle of the SKU its row names, and each placed picture's native pixels meet or exceed the well's pixel demand at the render density, with no plate scaled above one hundred percent to fill.
verifiers_auto.how: Read each per-product file's placed image against the row's SKU, and compare each bound plate's native pixel dimensions against the well's dimensions at the render resolution, asserting no interpolated placement.

verifiers_human.text: Laid in a row as a product page lays them, the six bottles read as one line rather than six good photographs.
verifiers_human.how: Place the six tiles side by side at listing scale and judge white point, black point, product height in frame and crop logic as a set.

verifiers_human.text: The cut edge holds on the frames where the glass and the ground run close in value, as well as on the others.
verifiers_human.how: View each tile at full resolution against white and against the chain's coloured band, looking for a bitten shoulder or a soft rim.

verifiers_human.text: Every counter card carries the whole of its record at trim, including the two long claims.
verifiers_human.how: Read each merged page at trim against the CSV row it came from.

verifiers_human.text: The mark still reads as the same mark at the size it reproduces on the tiles and reversed on the house ground, with the colourways reading as one system.
verifiers_human.how: View the mark at reproduction size on each canvas and against each ground, not at full canvas.

verifiers_human.text: On the basis page the usage rules sit as a set column beside the colourways rather than running through them.
verifiers_human.how: Open the exported basis page in Express and look at the delivered root.

verifiers_human.text: The work reads as a 46 to 80 dollar clinical line, not as a spa and not as a discount aisle.
verifiers_human.how: Judge ground colour, styling density, type scale, evidence hierarchy and where the price sits, against the stated band and buyer.

verifiers_human.text: The note tells the founders something they did not already know, including anything that could not be delivered.
verifiers_human.how: Read the note against the run and check that every reconciliation and every limitation is named.

verifiers_human.text: Each counter card shows the correct product's bottle at print quality rather than a soft, enlarged placement, including the two re-photographed SKUs.
verifiers_human.how: View each rendered card at trim and read the bottle against the row's SKU, looking on the two phone-scale SKUs for the softness of an interpolated fill.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are raster work, which need an authored fixed canvas document, and which are genuine record-per-page variable data, given that each is the only surface that does its job.
Whether the six bottle frames are one capture at all. The client believes they nearly are; the row and the file dimensions are the only places that can settle it.
How far to push the two frames whose ground and glass run together before they stop being worth saving, versus naming them.

Knockout route per frame: the one-call route for the frames with a clean tonal boundary, versus compositing onto the house ground or drawing the boundary through a material-named selection where there is no boundary to detect.
Whether a size demand that a source frame cannot meet is answered by interpolating, by re-cutting the composition, or by telling the client the frame has to be re-shot.
Whether the knockout route is the right instrument on disjoint lettering at all, and which trace polarity gives a positive mark rather than a knocked-out box.
Whether the card's fields can be addressed per frame or have to be placed by position inside one story, and what evidence is sufficient before calling the template built.
Which branch each counter-card deliverable takes, given that the printer's file and the client's per-product proofs are different artefacts with different resolution requirements.

Where each counter card's bottle comes from, given the well is a portrait print-resolution crop and not the square screen tile, so the store-tile plates cannot serve it and a fresh cut from the graded masters is required per row.

For the two phone-scale SKUs, whether the card well is answered by a tighter re-cut from the largest usable region, by a smaller placed size the layout can carry, or by naming the frame for a re-shoot, given that enlarging to fill the well is the one move the acceptance bar forbids and the shortfall is invisible until the card is rendered.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a clinical band and an ingredient-literate reader, plus the real numeric weight per family.
How much air the store tiles carry and how quietly the price sits beside the specification. At this band restraint is the design, and a dense benefit-led tile is a correct-looking wrong answer.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of skincare bottles and a plausible page. IDENTITY: these are this line's actual six products with their actual labels, their actual INCI lines and their actual regulatory-cleared claims, and the mark is the one the founders already approved, so a regenerated mark is a different company's logo and a regenerated INCI line is a compliance incident. SPEC: the chain needs six square tiles at an exact size with nothing touching the edge and no interpolated pixels, transparent variants for their own coloured band, and a counter-card run whose page count equals the row count at print resolution, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the store-page set is defined by being editable, since the launch date and the featured product will move and a four person line cannot re-commission; the counter cards are defined by being a merge, since the chain will add SKUs, and each card binds that SKU's own graded photograph rather than a generated bottle. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did this recovery move actually change anything, does this prepared template contain all six fields, did the rules column survive the import.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and upscale_factor, fill_area, remove_background in both the transparent and backgroundColor forms, monochromatic_tint and vectorize are all verified headless across 27 live calls; alpha survives crops at png output (13,371 partial-alpha pixels preserved). The first checkpoint rests on documented behaviour: adjustments succeed silently with no warning channel, crop_and_resize interpolates up to a two times cap reporting only inside tradeoffs, and remove_background needs one coherent subject (run on a mark-on-white plate it kept 1,743 of roughly 18,000 ink pixels). INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt as generator and validator, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout and document_render_layout are verified end to end and synchronous; the second checkpoint rests on two live findings, that a continuous flow converts to exactly ONE text frame, and that textContent dropped a 17-char run while keeping its line break so every later offset was short and the validator still returned VALID while prepare reported success and 2 of 5 mappings silently vanished. PDF page count equal to row count in row order is verified, and 300 DPI raster is verified only through document_render_layout because merge outputSpecs.resolution is silently ignored. Binding each row's own picture through additionalImageFiles into a single genuine graphic frame is verified, as is reading a placed picture's effective resolution off the rendered file; the picture-resolution checkpoint rests on the verified facts that a fill-proportionally well scales an under-pixelled plate up with no warning and that the print-resolution well is a strictly larger pixel demand than the screen tile, so a plate can clear the tile gate and be interpolated here, which is caught only at render and forces a return to imaging. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export, real tables with per-cell structure, inline SVG as native editable vector and a genuine editable dcx findable by asset_search are all verified; the third checkpoint rests on column-count being DROPPED with the text reflowing as one column at success, and on the rendition preview being documented as first artboard only. Transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined photography passes the 70 KB threshold immediately. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit verified end to end including a browser proving licensed faces load. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed, license returned a real 7360x4912 JPEG, boards persist with a cap of 12 placements per call and a 201 meaning partial. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no fill_text, no animate_design, no create_firefly_board, no variable QR, no bleed promise off a PDF-derived template, no upscaling, no compositing, no OCR, no text-to-image, no photo reaching Express as a URL, no batch above 20.

engagement_title: NORTHGROVE fall capsule launch: two mornings of flat-lays and a photographed club pennant into a buyer lookbook, a poster pair, a shoppable set and a hang-tag run
vertical: Fashion and apparel, heritage workwear capsule with cast metal hardware, wholesale to independent stockists plus direct sale (Burlington, Vermont)
real_brief_anchor: Four real postings are absorbed into one commission. Primary: the Freelancer.com background-removal and apparel brief in the ledger, whose literal asks (compositing a second shirt into the scene, AI-erasing room clutter) are both on the connector's not-available list, so the job is honestly re-cast to the apparel-catalog intent the category points at and scaled from a single hero to a capsule workload; the fictional brand NORTHGROVE (olive leaf glyph plus a charcoal condensed wordmark) is that ledger's own coinage. Co-anchor: the Freelancer.com flat-lay apparel brief asking for 'a clean, consistent set of flat-lay photos' shot 'directly overhead, evenly lit' on a 'mid-gray' backdrop that 'keeps dark and light fabrics balanced on screen', plus high-resolution files and web-ready versions. Co-anchor: the Freelancer.com silver-jewellery open call asking for handheld product frames turned into a colour-accurate uniform-white set with 'accurate metal tone', 'no colour cast' and matching transparent cut-outs for layering, absorbed here as the capsule's cast metal hardware, which correctly needs a different treatment from the garments. Co-anchor: the Upwork brand-identity post for an invented amateur league, converted per the rework guidance from cricket to a Western sport, and absorbed as the capsule's collaboration with a fictional local lacrosse club whose only surviving artwork is a photographed pennant. No real company, label, league, club, retailer or trademark is named anywhere. VERDICT STRENGTHEN: the concept and collateral set are kept and deepened to standard, with the merge run added because a hang tag per SKU is genuine record-per-page work that the authoring surface cannot do at print resolution.
client_one_liner: The fall capsule ships to stockists in six weeks, we have two mornings of flat-lays that do not look like one shoot, a photograph of the club pennant we are collaborating with, and nothing a buyer can be sent.
client_brief:
NORTHGROVE, fall capsule launch

We make heritage workwear in Burlington. Ten pieces this fall, cut and sewn locally, sold to about forty independent stockists and off our own site. Six weeks from now the linesheet goes out to buyers and the campaign goes up.

The photography. We shot the whole capsule flat, overhead, on a mid-gray backdrop, over two mornings. The gray is deliberate: it keeps the charcoal pieces and the natural cotton pieces balanced on screen. Individually the frames are good. Put the range on one page and something is off between the two mornings. The dark pieces are the ones we worry about. We also need the pieces cut out with nothing behind them, because the linesheet and the hang tags put them on our own colour.

The hardware. This season we cast our own buttons, a keyring and a collar pin in pewter and silver. Those were shot separately on the bench. They need to be colour accurate, true metal tone, no cast, on near-white, and cut out to match.

The collaboration. One piece carries the crest of a lacrosse club a few streets from the workshop. The club has no artwork left. What they have is an old wool pennant on the wall with the crest stitched into it, and they let us photograph it. We need that crest as artwork we can put on a poster and a tag.

What we need made. A lookbook we send buyers, a look per page with a range grid at the back. A campaign poster, and we would like to see two genuinely different directions before we pick one. The shoppable set, wide, square and tall, in one file we can change ourselves. A linesheet page with the price grid as a real table. And a hang tag per piece carrying the name, the fabric, the make and the price, at print resolution, plus one file the printer runs.

Our overshirt is one hundred and twenty eight dollars, the henley is seventy four. Our buyer is twenty eight to forty five and cares about provenance and make more than logos. And a note on what you did and what direction you picked and why.
price_band_and_audience: Mid-premium heritage workwear at 74 to 128 dollars per piece, buyer 28 to 45, values provenance and construction over logos. The band is load-bearing. At this price the campaign wants muted grounds, full-frame quiet photography that shows cloth and seam, and copy that leads on material and make; the linesheet is a trade document that has to look sober beside a buyer's other lines. The same ten pieces at a 24 dollar fast-fashion band would correctly be a dense grid of cut-outs on white with a burst price and a discount ladder, and shipping that treatment here tells forty independent stockists that the capsule is not what the wholesale price says it is. Push the other way into editorial luxury, vast white space, a tiny mark and no price anywhere, and a buyer cannot work from it and a 74 dollar henley reads as mispriced. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. A posted job of this shape runs 2,000 to 3,800 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: Cut and sewn to outlast the season.
brand_identity.sector: Heritage workwear with cast metal hardware, wholesale to independent stockists plus direct sale, made in Burlington, Vermont.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Burlington, Vermont. A ten person workshop cutting and sewing a ten piece capsule each season, sold to around forty independent stockists and off its own site.
brand_identity.about: NORTHGROVE makes heritage workwear locally, in small seasonal capsules cut and sewn in Burlington. The fall line runs to ten pieces with hardware the workshop casts itself in pewter and silver. One piece this season carries the stitched crest of a neighbourhood lacrosse club a few streets from the bench, a local collaboration rather than a licence.
brand_identity.audience: Buyers and wearers twenty eight to forty five who value provenance and construction over logos, and who read fabric and make before they read a brand mark.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Seventy four to one hundred twenty eight dollars per piece, mid premium wholesale and direct. Muted grounds, full frame photography that shows cloth and seam, and copy that leads on material and make. Deliberately clear of both the twenty four dollar fast fashion grid and the price free editorial luxury a buyer cannot work from.
brand_identity.typography: The wordmark is a charcoal condensed lockup beside a small olive leaf glyph. A condensed grotesque display carries headers, look titles and the poster; a sturdy text face carries the season statement, fabric and make notes, and the linesheet price grid. Heritage and plain, never costume.
brand_identity.voice: Understated and maker focused, provenance before promotion. Example line the brand would write: 'Ten pieces, cut and sewn in Burlington, meant to be worn hard.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The NORTHGROVE wordmark and olive leaf glyph are set. The whole capsule was shot flat, overhead, on a mid gray backdrop across two mornings, with the cast hardware shot separately on the bench. The collaborating club has no artwork left: its crest survives only as a photograph of an old wool pennant on a wall. Last season's hang tag exists as the printer's press file, same size and stock this year.
brand_identity.values: Locally made, built to last. Provenance and construction over logos, and partnerships that stay neighbourly.

assets_supplied.name: northgrove_fw_flatlays/ (10 frames)
assets_supplied.kind: Overhead flat-lay photography of the ten capsule pieces on a mid-gray backdrop, shot across two mornings, one piece per frame.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Everything shot flat on the gray. The gray keeps the dark pieces and the natural cotton balanced on screen."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The charcoal overshirt and the dark olive henley sit at almost exactly the backdrop's luminance along the shoulder and placket, so a one-call knockout reports success and returns a plausible cut-out that has bitten into the shoulder seam and the placket edge, visible only at full resolution on a coloured ground. Separately the backdrop was re-hung between the two mornings and the second batch sits fractionally warmer, which reads as nothing in a single frame and reads as two shoots the moment the range grid puts them adjacent.

assets_supplied.name: northgrove_hardware_bench/ (4 frames)
assets_supplied.kind: Bench frames of the cast pewter and silver hardware: two button styles, a keyring and a collar pin, shot on a light bench.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The hardware we cast this season. These need true metal tone and no cast."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: One frame has a grey reference card lying in the corner of the bench, and a subject-focused crop on sparse bench art can lock onto the card or onto a specular highlight instead of the piece, returning a confident looking crop at a plausible size while reporting its uncertainty only as a numeric detection confidence and a bounding box buried in the metadata. The metal also carries a cool cast that any global warm move made for the garments pushes further from true, so the two families cannot share one grade.

assets_supplied.name: kestrel_pennant.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of the lacrosse club's wool pennant hanging on a workshop wall, the crest chain-stitched in two thread colours on felt.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only place the club's crest still exists. They let us photograph it off the wall."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is a compound stitched mark on a textile substrate, which behaves nothing like a flat scan: a prompt naming the pennant returns the felt rather than the thread, a compound prompt returns the outer ring and silently drops the inner rule and the central device while looking entirely plausible, and the knockout route on the ring returns a solid opaque disc because an enclosed interior cannot be punched. The chain-stitch texture also explodes a trace into far more paths than the mark has parts.

assets_supplied.name: northgrove_hangtag.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: Last season's hang tag as the printer's own press PDF, one tag, double sided, with a placed swatch image and a specification block.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The tag our printer ran last season. Same size and stock this year."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The tag carries no bleed and the converted document carries none either, so a press-ready with bleed promise cannot be met from this source however the render is called, and the specification block is a fixed measure frame that stops rendering rather than spilling when a record overruns it.

assets_supplied.name: northgrove_linesheet.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Ten rows: piece name, fabric, make note, colourway, wholesale and retail price, size run, and a column pointing at the cut-out for each piece.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The ten pieces as our stockists get them. The last column is meant to pull in the picture."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The image column header is written plainly and its cells hold folder-relative paths rather than bare filenames, which binds nothing at merge time while every tool response still reports success, so every tag renders carrying the template's original static swatch and looks like a finished tag.

assets_supplied.name: northgrove_copy.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text: the ten piece names, fabric and make notes, the season statement and the stockist terms.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The copy as we want it read."

acceptance_bar: The ten pieces read as ONE capsule when the range grid puts them adjacent: one ground, one white point, one warmth, one piece height in frame. A frame that cannot be brought to the set is named in the note, not shipped at eighty percent.
The hardware is colour accurate on near-white with true metal tone and no cast, and it is graded as its own family rather than dragged along with the garments.
Every cut-out is whole. The cut edge holds on the dark pieces at full resolution on our own colour, with the shoulder seam, the placket and the hem intact and nothing bitten away.
Every hardware crop contains the whole of the piece it depicts, and no reference card, bench edge or prop appears in any delivered frame.

The crest is placeable artwork rather than a picture of artwork: transparent ground, a real viewBox present, no opaque full-canvas rectangle riding underneath, and it still reads as the club's crest at the size it reproduces on the tag and on the poster.
Two campaign directions are shown and genuinely diverge in ground, crop, type scale and how much the mark carries, with the pick argued against the band and the buyer rather than asserted.
The linesheet price grid is a real table with per cell structure, not a picture of a table and not run-on text.
In every authored document the words are text a buyer's assistant can retype and the marks are live vector shapes, not a flattened picture of a layout.
The shoppable set's three canvases sit in ONE working file, each root keeping its own canvas size, delivered with the self-contained source it was built from.
The lookbook's per-look pages read as the season's muted world on the delivered document, on every page and not only the first one.

The hang-tag run is delivered as one press file with page count equal to row count, in row order, PLUS one correctly identified file per piece at genuine print resolution, each tag carrying that piece's own picture rather than the template's swatch.
One type system across lookbook, posters, shoppable set, linesheet and tag, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the actual numeric weight used.
The note records per frame what was applied, which direction was picked and why, every resize any tool reported, what the tag could not be made to do, and what the club should know about their crest.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching a pixel.
trajectory.judgement: The lookbook, posters, shoppable set and linesheet are free-form fixed-canvas layout and only one surface composes that. The hang tags are one record per page with a per-row picture at print resolution and belong on the merge surface. Hand-building ten tags on the authoring surface would lose both the resolution and the link to the data.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming surface per deliverable, plus the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline: a manifest keyed by role, including which cut-out will eventually stand for which CSV row.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Preview all ten flat-lays and all four bench frames and triage them: which morning each belongs to, how the backdrop sits between them, which pieces run close to the ground in value, which bench frames are sparse and what else is lying in each bench frame.
trajectory.judgement: The client asserts one backdrop and one setup. The frames are the only thing that can settle whether that survived two mornings, and a piece that is nearly the ground's value is a different job from one that is not.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note covering morning, ground warmth, subject contrast against the ground, and anything in frame that must not be delivered.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level, before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Overhead flat-lays that are a degree off read as sloppy in a grid, and straightening reframes the piece and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Fix the capsule target off the best lit garment frame and correct each of the ten toward it one call at a time, then hold the hardware as its own target: near-white, colour accurate, true metal tone.
trajectory.judgement: Two families, two destinations, and they must not fight where the linesheet puts them on one page. One batched call applies one identical parameter set, which is exactly wrong for two mornings under different daylight and catastrophic for metal that a warm move takes further from true.
trajectory.produces: Ten garment masters and four hardware masters at source scale, with a per frame parameter log and two declared targets.

trajectory.action: Apply masked corrections where a whole-frame move goes wrong, selecting by the material's own visual properties rather than by the surface it sits on, and set the bench crops so nothing that is not the piece survives into a delivered frame.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the whole gate: naming the bench pulls the selection to the bench. A confident looking crop on sparse bench art is not evidence, and the client will see a reference card long before a buyer does.
trajectory.produces: Corrected frames plus bench crops whose returned confidence and bounds were read rather than assumed.

trajectory.action: Cut every piece out for the linesheet and the tags, then inspect each cut edge at full resolution against the house colour rather than at preview scale.
trajectory.judgement: The tools report a successful cut whether or not there was a boundary to find. Inspection on the ground the asset will actually sit on is the only evidence, and the pieces most likely to fail are exactly the ones the client already worries about.
trajectory.produces: Cut-outs for all ten pieces and the four hardware items, each with its route and its returned tradeoffs recorded.

trajectory.action: Cut the range grid frames and the tag pictures to their destinations, and bake the season's tone into the raster wherever the look depends on it rather than leaving it to be applied downstream.
trajectory.judgement: Anything that has to survive an import is safer as pixels than as an instruction. Where the tone is baked in, the raster becomes the single source and the layout stops carrying a look it may not be able to hold.
trajectory.produces: Destination-ready rasters with the tone decision made once, upstream.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the one ground band a poster direction needs, filter to photography, exclude generative-tech results, license and download at full resolution, then create the board and add the capsule selects and both directions within the per-call placement cap.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose existing light can be brought to the capsule target rather than the prettiest thumbnail. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero. A partial placement is reported as a success code, so only the entries named as failed are re-sent.
trajectory.produces: One licensed camera-scale frame graded into the capsule world, and a persistent shareable board.

trajectory.action: Recover the club crest off the pennant: a thread-level selection naming the mark's own visual properties, correct polarity, a bounds crop from the selection's own returned box, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full-canvas ground path removed. Derive the reversed and single-colour versions from one mask.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions the tools do not make: how to word the selection so it takes the thread and not the felt, which polarity to trace, and whether the knockout route is the right instrument on an enclosed ring at all. A stitched mark also traces into far more parts than it has, which is a decision about what to keep.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent crest plus its reversed version, with what was simplified recorded for the club.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit for the whole engagement.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged against a 74 to 128 dollar heritage band and a buyer who reads make before logo. The weight cannot be inferred from a style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug rather than by asking for a heavier weight.
trajectory.produces: A one-kit type system with family, foundry and actual numeric weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Convert last season's tag PDF to a working document, export the interchange format, and read the real frame inventory: how many text frames the tag became, whether the placed swatch survived as a graphic frame, and what each frame's true story text is.
trajectory.judgement: What a printed tag looks like and what it converts into are unrelated, and whether a per-row picture is even bindable depends on a graphic frame existing. The inventory decides every mapping row that follows and it also settles what the tag can and cannot be promised to do.
trajectory.produces: A frame inventory with bounds, applied type, the graphic frame's link, and the reconstructed story text per frame.

trajectory.action: Build the mapping against the document's own reconstructed story text and against the real graphic frame, in the shape the merge actually consumes, validate it, prepare the template, then round-trip the interchange format and confirm every expected field placeholder is present.
trajectory.judgement: A valid verdict and a completed successfully message are both cheap. The picture binding in particular has a shape the data file does not currently have, and the only evidence a field landed is the field appearing in the prepared document's story.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholder inventory and picture binding have been read back rather than trusted.

trajectory.action: Merge the ten records one record per page, deliver the press file in row order, and produce correctly identified per-piece files at genuine print resolution, reading each page at trim and checking which piece is actually on which file.
trajectory.judgement: The printer's file and the buyer pack's per-piece files are different artefacts with different requirements, and a per-piece file is only useful if the piece on it is the piece the filename claims. What the response labels a file is not evidence of what is in it.
trajectory.produces: One press file with page count equal to row count, plus ten identified per-piece files at print resolution.

trajectory.action: Author the lookbook document: a look per page, the range grid at the back, the linesheet price grid as a real table, every photograph inlined as image data, the crest and the wordmark as inline SVG in explicitly sized top-left anchored wrappers, family and weight on every text element, each root declaring its own canvas. Upload and hold the returned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto-sized right-anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override is what collapses a mixed-size set. The design work is how much of the page each look is given and how sober the trade page stays beside it.
trajectory.produces: One export-ready HTML carrying the lookbook and linesheet, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Author the poster pair as two genuinely divergent directions and the shoppable set as three roots at three canvas sizes. Run the readiness check, export every document, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve each document's rendition and look at root one, and parse the returned per-root markup for every root after it.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition preview only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at root one is not looking at a lookbook, and two directions that differ only in accent colour are one direction shown twice.
trajectory.produces: Native editable documents, an inspected first root each, and a per-root markup audit for everything after it.

trajectory.action: Write the note: what was applied per frame and why, which poster direction was picked and the argument for it, every resize any tool reported, what the tag could not be made to do, and what the club should know about the recovered crest.
trajectory.judgement: The direction pick is the one thing the client explicitly asked to be argued, and the limitation the client will discover at the printer is the one that has to be named before the printer names it.
trajectory.produces: A written handover the next freelancer and the printer can both work from.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the cut-outs the whole linesheet and tag run depend on are actually whole. The backdrop was chosen precisely because it sits between the dark and the light pieces, and on the charcoal overshirt and the dark olive henley that puts cloth and ground at almost the same luminance along the shoulder and the placket. The knockout returns a clean looking RGBA cut-out with no warning and a full success, and at preview scale against white it looks correct; the bite into the shoulder seam and the placket edge only appears at full resolution against a colour. Which pieces this happens to is a property of each frame's own tonal relationship to the ground and cannot be read off the frame.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it. The knockout has to happen after the grade, and the grade is what fixes the tonal relationship; there is no parameter that reports whether a boundary was found and no read-ahead that says which pieces have one. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the gray keeps the dark and light pieces balanced on screen, which is the client explaining a sound photographic choice, and says the dark pieces are the ones she worries about, which is a worry, not a disclosure. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is a different chain for the affected pieces: select the backdrop by its own material properties, invert and fill so the boundary is drawn rather than detected, or composite onto the house colour in one call so the ground is part of the raster and there is no edge to fail.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-cut the affected pieces through the drawn-boundary route, re-inspect every cut edge at full resolution on the house colour rather than on white, and re-derive the range grid frames and the tag pictures that were already built on the first cut-outs.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A linesheet and a hang-tag run sent to forty stockists in which the two dark pieces have had their shoulder seam and placket eaten away, on a capsule sold on construction, discovered by a buyer.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the tag run actually is once it exists. Three things surface only in the returned artefacts, all at full success. The merge accepts a resolution on its own raster output and silently ignores it, returning page-sized files at screen resolution that open and print and look like proofs. The per-record raster files come back in an order that the response's own row labels contradict, so naming files by their position in the returned list attaches the wrong piece to the wrong name. And the picture column binds nothing in the shape the supplied data file uses, so every tag renders carrying the template's original static swatch and still looks like a finished tag.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and doing it right the first time presumes knowing that a documented parameter is inert, that stated labels are wrong, and that a plainly written data column is the wrong shape, none of which any response says. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for a tag per piece at print resolution carrying that piece's own picture, which is the requirement, not the diagnosis. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is a different delivery route entirely: merge to the document format and render separately for real resolution, and either render as separate files or drive one record at a time so identity is guaranteed by the call rather than inferred from a list, with the data column reshaped so the binding can happen at all.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reshape the picture column and its file references, re-prepare and re-merge, take the raster branch through the render step instead of the merge's own output, re-derive every per-piece file through a route whose identity is guaranteed, and read each delivered tag at trim against its row, where the long make notes will also show whether a fixed measure block stopped rendering rather than spilled.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Ten hang tags sent to the printer at a quarter of the resolution they need, in a buyer pack where the filenames name the wrong pieces, every one of them carrying last season's swatch instead of this season's garment, with every tool response having reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the season's world survives into the lookbook at all. The muted campaign tone over full-frame photography is naturally authored as a tonal layer sitting over the picture, and the importer discards that blending construction outright: the layer arrives as a plain opaque shape, at full success, with no warning, sitting on top of the photograph it was supposed to tint. The returned per-page markup is the only channel that reports it, and the document's own rendition returns the first page only, so a ten-look lookbook and both poster directions cannot be checked visually beyond page one. Whether each look still reads as the capsule's world, or as a flat panel covering a garment, is visible only after the export.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the drop happens at import and the import is the last step; and doing it right the first time presumes knowing which of several plausible constructions survives, which no response reports and no checklist enumerates. (b) Nothing states it. The acceptance line about the looks reading as the season's muted world on every page is the client's art direction, not a warning about an importer. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is to produce a different upstream asset, with the tone applied to the raster itself in the image pipeline so the layout carries no look it cannot hold, and then to re-judge the page because a baked tone and an overlaid tone do not sit the same way under type.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Take the affected photography back through the image pipeline with the tone applied to the raster, re-author the lookbook and the poster directions around rasters that already carry the look, re-upload, re-run the readiness check, re-export, and audit every page from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A buyer lookbook delivered in which nine of the ten looks are a flat panel sitting over a garment on the pages nobody looked at, with the export having reported success throughout.

deliverables.name: NORTHGROVE capsule photography, garments and hardware
deliverables.spec: Ten garment masters brought to one capsule target across two mornings (one ground, one white point, one warmth, one piece height in frame) plus four hardware masters held to a separate colour-accurate near-white target with true metal tone, plus one licensed camera-scale ground frame graded into the same world. Delivered with a per frame parameter log naming why each frame differs from its neighbours and which morning it came from.

deliverables.name: NORTHGROVE cut-out set
deliverables.spec: Fourteen genuine cut-outs, ten garments and four hardware pieces, whole at full resolution on the house colour with shoulder seam, placket and hem intact and no reference card, bench edge or prop surviving into any frame. Each with its route and its returned tradeoff record. One set with one cut logic, not one picture at several sizes.

deliverables.name: Kestrel Lane crest, recovered
deliverables.spec: The club's stitched crest recovered from a photograph of a wool pennant as placeable scalable geometry with a transparent ground: a real viewBox present, no opaque full-canvas rectangle riding underneath, its inner rule and central device intact, delivered as a positive and a reversed version derived from one mask, legible at the size it reproduces on the tag and on the poster. Accompanied by a statement of what the trace simplified, for the club's own records.

deliverables.name: NORTHGROVE lookbook, poster pair, shoppable set and linesheet
deliverables.spec: Native editable documents carrying a look per page with the range grid at the back, two genuinely divergent A2 poster directions, the shoppable set as three roots each keeping its own canvas size, and a linesheet page whose price grid is a real table with per cell structure. Live editable text in one licensed type system, both marks as real vector shapes, every photograph carried as embedded image data rather than a reference. Delivered with the self-contained source, which is the durable half.

deliverables.name: NORTHGROVE hang-tag run
deliverables.spec: Ten hang tags, one record per page, built on last season's approved artwork: one press file whose page count equals the row count in row order for the printer, plus one correctly identified file per piece at genuine print resolution for the buyer pack, each tag carrying that piece's own cut-out rather than the template's swatch and the whole of its make note at trim.

deliverables.name: Handover note and selects board
deliverables.spec: A written note recording per frame what was applied and why that frame differs from its neighbours, the poster direction picked and the argument for it against the band and the buyer, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and the actual numeric weight, every resize any tool reported, what the tag could not be made to do and why the printer needs to know, and what the club should know about their recovered crest. Paired with a persistent shareable board carrying the capsule selects and both directions with nothing silently dropped.
