decision_gates: Which deliverables are a record per page variable data run and which need an authored fixed canvas document, given that only one surface here composes free form layout at all.
Whether to trust the mapping readout or to reconstruct the template's true story text before computing a single offset.
What to do about a headshot column written for a photo box that turns out not to be a photo box.
How the act and stage strings are set across the whole run so that one rule keeps all twenty two records whole, rather than patching the records that happen to fail.
How far to push the two into the sun frames before they stop being worth saving, versus naming them.
Whether fourteen archive frames covers a three headliner billing, and how to say so when it does not.

Selection wording on the painted banner: naming the substrate takes the canvas, naming the paint's own visual properties takes the mark, and background removal on an enclosed ring is the wrong instrument entirely.
Which mark variant carries which canvas, judged at reproduction size on the actual ground rather than at canvas size.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a hundred and forty five dollar weekend ticket and a discovery led crowd, plus the real numeric weight per family.
Whether the three poster directions differ in the ways a director can actually choose between, or only in colour.
How much of the field the announcement set gives to the discovery stages, since the tiering is the whole commercial argument of the festival.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns a handsome picture of a folk festival poster. IDENTITY: the mark has to be RECOVERED off a photograph of the actual painted banner that has hung over the main stage since 2022, because a regenerated lantern is a different festival's logo, and the photography has to be of the acts who are actually billed. SPEC: twenty two laminates, one person per page, each carrying that person's own name, act, role, stages and days, printed at trim by a printer who cannot fix a truncated act name afterwards, plus separate single files named to the roster. A generated image satisfies none of that and cannot be checked for any of it. EDITABILITY: the client says outright that acts will move through the winter and they will be changing the announcement set themselves, so the deliverable is defined by being a document they can open and retype. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality: what the converted pass actually contains, whether the mapping the validator blessed actually landed, whether this record survived its frame, whether the mark holds at the size it reproduces.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout and document_render_layout are all verified fully headless and synchronous, with a bare press PDF reverse engineered into a live merge template end to end. One record per page is confirmed for PDF output (page count equals row count), per record files are confirmed in correct order via createSeparateFiles and via a per record range loop, and true print resolution is confirmed through document_render_layout rather than through the merge tool, whose own resolution parameter is silently ignored. The first checkpoint rests on two documented findings rather than assumptions: frame granularity from a PDF is not under the author's control and a continuous flow converted to exactly ONE text frame with ZERO graphic frames, and the mapping readout is LOSSY, dropping a run while keeping its line break so that every later offset is short while the validator still answers VALID and prepare still answers completed successfully (three of five mappings landed in the audit). The headshot column is deliberately unbindable because a converted PDF only exposes image frames when the source PDF carried placed images. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs, fill_area and vectorize are verified across 27 live calls, and the mark recovery rests on the verified substrate versus ink prompt asymmetry, the polarity trap before tracing, the solid disc failure of remove_background on an enclosed ring, the missing viewBox and the opaque path zero. EXPRESS: multi root export and mixed canvas sizes in one document are verified, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, the product is a genuine editable document findable by asset_search, and the rendition preview is documented as first artboard only, which is why verification is split between the rendition and the returned markup. Transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined photography passes the inline threshold immediately. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end including a browser proving licensed faces load, with the case sensitivity and non standard numeric weight traps live. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed, license returned a real camera scale JPEG, boards persist with a hard cap of twelve placements per call and a partial success reported as a success code. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no variable QR, no bleed claim off a converted PDF, no pdfPreset, no upscaling, no compositing, no OCR, no text to image, no photograph reaching Express as a URL, no fill_text, no animate_design, no batch above twenty.

engagement_title: Umbra Loft after dark series: bring six mismatched club nights to one noir look, recover three act wordmarks off photographed merch, and carry the series onto the gig poster run, the promoter deck and the printed season card
vertical: Arts, Culture and Music: an independent two hundred and fifty capacity basement live music room under a former textile mill in Providence, Rhode Island, programming a nine night autumn jazz and after dark series
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor, quoted verbatim in the ledger's grounding_note from the Freelancer.com "Modern Album Logo & Cover Design" post: the client is "getting ready to release a new project and need a striking album cover that also doubles as a recognisable logo for all my promo materials", wants "a clean modern aesthetic, nothing vintage or overly ornate, powered by bright, bold colours that jump off the screen and still look sharp in print", and explicitly asks for "a logo or word-mark element extracted from the main design so I can use it on merch and posters", with deliverables "supplied in layered PSD/AI, plus ready-to-post PNG and JPEG versions" and "scalable vector" artwork. Co anchor: the Freelancer.com open call from a dark aesthetic creative studio offering premium poster, banner and social creatives and cinematic, colour graded photo editing. That second posting names no client and attaches no images, so the brand is laundered to the coined fictional basement venue Umbra Loft, and the vague ask is fixed into a runnable job. Every act, person and street in this task is invented and no real venue, label, musician or trademark appears in any task facing field. The verdict is STRENGTHEN, so the concept and the collateral set stand and the depth is raised: the extracted wordmark ask from the first anchor becomes a genuine recovery off photographed merchandise rather than an extraction from artwork the agent drew itself, the cinematic grading ask from the second anchor becomes a real cross night consistency problem across six differently lit archive frames, and the series acquires the printed half a venue actually needs, because CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) confirms a record per page run can be built off the press PDF the venue's printer already returned.
client_one_liner: Nine autumn nights, six usable photographs shot on six nights under six different lighting rigs, three acts whose only artwork is a picture of a tour shirt, and the first poster has to be up in three weeks.
client_brief:
Umbra Loft, after dark autumn series

We are a two hundred and fifty capacity basement room under an old mill in Providence. Tickets run eighteen to thirty two dollars. Our crowd is twenty one to thirty five, scene literate, and they find us through friends and through what they see on their phones at eleven at night.

This autumn we are programming nine nights as one series instead of nine separate shows, and it has to look like one series.

What we have is our own archive. Six photographs from six nights, all shot in the room, all under whatever rig that act travelled with, so no two match. We would rather build the whole look out of our own pictures than buy stock, but we know one of the nine nights has nothing usable at all.

The look we want is dark and high contrast. Two colours doing the work, deep ground, a lot of grain and grit, type that is raw rather than polished. Not corporate, not clean. If it looks like a bank's jazz sponsorship we have failed.

The posters are the heart of it. Three A2 directions for the three headline nights, in one working file so we can change dates ourselves. Three of our headliners sent artwork and all three sent a photograph of a tour shirt, so their wordmarks have to come off cloth and become something we can actually place.

We also pitch the room to promoters, so we need a short deck: the room, the capacity, what a night looks like, what we charge, what we drew last season. And a per release set for socials, a square, a tall one and a four by five.

The printed half is a season card, A5, one night per card, that we hand out at the door and leave in record shops. Last season's card is attached exactly as our printer returned it. Nine nights, so nine cards, and our printer has asked about bleed.

Finally one page recording the series look so we are not rebuilding this next spring, and a note on anything you hit.
price_band_and_audience: Independent basement room. Tickets eighteen to thirty two dollars, capacity two hundred and fifty, audience twenty one to thirty five, scene literate and discovery driven, reached almost entirely on a phone late at night. The band is load bearing in both directions. Push polished and corporate, with a clean grid, a safe grotesque and evenly lit photography, and the series reads as sponsored programming rather than as a basement, which is precisely the failure the client names outright. Push the other way into cheap gig flyer chaos, with clip art textures and unreadable type over a black rectangle, and a thirty two dollar headline ticket stops being defensible and promoters stop returning calls. The correct register is dark, high contrast and deliberately made: two colours doing the work, grain that reads as film rather than as noise, raw display type at a real hierarchy, and photography that plainly comes from this room on these nights. A posted commission of this shape and scope runs 1,500 to 3,000 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: An independent two hundred and fifty capacity basement live music room programming a nine night autumn jazz and after dark series.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2021, a basement room under a former textile mill in Providence, Rhode Island, a small independent team.
brand_identity.about: Umbra Loft is a two hundred and fifty capacity basement room under an old mill in Providence, programming jazz and after dark nights for a crowd that finds us through friends and phones at eleven at night. This autumn we are running nine nights as one series rather than nine separate shows. It has to look like one thing, and it has to look like the room it actually is: dark, close and made by hand.
brand_identity.audience: A scene literate, discovery driven crowd aged twenty one to thirty five, reached almost entirely on a phone late at night, who read polish as inauthentic and reward work that plainly comes from the room.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Tickets 18 to 32 dollars, capacity 250. Independent basement scale: deliberately made and high contrast, credible at a headline ticket without ever reading as corporate or sponsored programming.
brand_identity.typography: A raw, weighty display face for act names and dates, set large and blunt, paired with a plain condensed grotesque for billing, door times and the room data tables. Two colours do the work over a deep ground, with grain that reads as film. The feel is gig poster made deliberately, not clip art chaos.
brand_identity.voice: Terse, atmospheric, unvarnished. It names the act, the night and the door and gets out of the way. Example line the brand would write: "Doors 8. Downstairs. Two sets, one room, cash on the night."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: We build the look from our own archive, six photographs shot on six nights under six touring rigs, no two matching. Three headline acts sent their wordmarks only as photographs of tour shirts and a tote, which their managers say is all that survives. There is no defined palette, type or treatment yet, and last season's printed card exists only as the press PDF our printer returned.
brand_identity.values: Everything comes from this room, on these nights, and it should never look like a bank's jazz sponsorship.

assets_supplied.name: umbra_archive_nights/ (6 frames, camera scale)
assets_supplied.kind: Six performance photographs from six different nights in the room, each shot under the touring act's own lighting rig: one tungsten wash, one hard follow spot, two heavy magenta, one near darkness, one lit mostly by the bar.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Six nights, six rigs, one room. Our whole archive. We would rather use these than buy pictures."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: On two of the six the follow spot has driven the performer's face and shirt fully into the top of the channel, so a highlight recovery move returns success while nothing in the frame changes at all, which reads as a correctly conservative result rather than as a dead end. A third frame is convincingly sharp at thumbnail scale but the trumpet bell and the player's right hand are smeared, which only becomes visible at poster scale.

assets_supplied.name: umbra_wordmarks/ (3 photographs)
assets_supplied.kind: Three headline acts' wordmarks, sent by their managers as photographs of tour shirts and a tote lying on a table, described by each manager as the only artwork they still have.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "All three sent us a picture of a shirt. They swear it is all they have."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: These are disjoint lettering photographed on cloth, so a one call knockout returns a clean looking transparent file holding only two or three letters of the wordmark while reporting complete success, and on the knitted shirt the letters are worked into the weave so a selection pitched at the ink returns the weave with it. One of the three files carries a different act's mark than its filename says, which only surfaces when the marks are read against the billing.

assets_supplied.name: umbra_seasoncard_autumn.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: Last season's A5 season card, the press PDF the printer returned, one night per card, with a date block, a billing block, a door and price line and a placed image panel.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Last season's card as the printer sent it back. Same shape, new nights. They have asked about bleed."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The card carries no bleed at all and none can be introduced downstream: the bleed switch is accepted without complaint and the export reports success while the trim and bleed boxes remain identical, so a press ready with bleed claim would be false. Its typography is inherited from the converted artwork and cannot be replaced with the series typeface on this surface, so the printed half will speak in a different type voice than the posters unless that is designed around and disclosed.

assets_supplied.name: umbra_nights_autumn.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Nine rows: date, headline act, support, door time, set time, ticket price, stage note, and a column of image filenames for the card's picture panel.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The nine nights as confirmed with the acts. Prices are final."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two of the nine rows are the same act's two night residency billed identically, so a straight row per card run ships two cards a reader cannot tell apart and a record shop stack that looks like a misprint. One row's door time carries a stray character that renders literally rather than being interpreted.

assets_supplied.name: umbra_billing_autumn.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Approved billing and copy: how each act must be credited, the support acts, the ticket tiers, the accessibility line and the room's licence line that must appear on printed matter.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Billing as agreed with the acts. The licence line is required on anything printed."

assets_supplied.name: umbra_room_specs.txt
assets_supplied.kind: The room as promoters ask about it: capacity, stage dimensions, load in, backline, PA, curfew, split terms and last season's average draw.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What every promoter asks before they will talk to us."

acceptance_bar: The six archive frames read as one series when laid together: one ground, one two colour treatment, one grain register, one contrast logic. A frame that cannot be brought to the series is named rather than shipped at eighty percent.
The night with no usable archive frame is covered by a picture that sits inside the series rather than beside it, and it is not obvious which one was bought.

All three act wordmarks are placeable artwork rather than pictures of artwork: transparent, scalable with a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle underneath, every letter of every wordmark present, and each mark attributed to the act it actually belongs to.
Three A2 poster directions in one working file, genuinely three directions rather than one layout in three colourways, with the dark high contrast register holding on every one.
The two colour treatment is actually present in the delivered layouts, on every canvas and not only the first one.
Every photograph in every delivered layout is actually present, not an empty box, on every canvas and not only the first one.
The promoter deck reads as a room worth booking: the capacity, the terms and the draw legible as data rather than as decoration, and the type retypable.
The per release social set is one working file carrying the square, the tall and the four by five, each keeping its own canvas size.
Nine season cards exist, one night per card, and no two cards are indistinguishable from each other.
Every card carries the required licence line and the correct billing exactly as approved, with nothing rendering a stray character literally.
Nothing is claimed as press ready with bleed that is not, and any divergence in type voice between the printed half and the authored half is stated rather than hidden.
One series type system across posters, deck, social and the basis page, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the actual weight used.
If it would look at home on a bank's jazz sponsorship it has failed, regardless of which gates passed.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching anything.
trajectory.judgement: Posters, deck and social are free form fixed canvases and can only be authored; the season card is a record per page printed run off artwork the client already has. The brief pins both destinations, so there is nothing here to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming a surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier that gates the exports.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset and hold each returned address against its role in a manifest.
trajectory.judgement: The nights file is consumed twice, once as merge data and once as billing to read the wordmarks and the archive against, so the manifest has to be keyed by role rather than by filename.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of upload addresses keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Preview all six archive frames, the three wordmark photographs and last season's card, and triage them: which rig each frame was shot under, where each frame's tonal trouble sits, which act each wordmark actually belongs to, and what the card is made of.
trajectory.judgement: Six frames from six rigs is not a set with a common problem, it is six different problems. The wordmarks are only identifiable by reading them against the approved billing, not by trusting the filenames the managers sent.
trajectory.produces: A per asset triage note covering illuminant, tonal state, sharpness and wordmark identity against the billing.

trajectory.action: Fix one series target off the most workable night and correct each of the six toward it with its own call, recording the parameters applied.
trajectory.judgement: One batched move applies one identical correction, which is exactly wrong across a tungsten wash, two magenta rigs and a room lit by its own bar. The target is a series, not six good pictures.
trajectory.produces: Six corrected masters at source scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Work the frames whose bright regions are furthest gone, reading the result of each recovery move rather than its status.
trajectory.judgement: A recovery move that returns success and changes nothing is not a conservative result, it is the frame telling you the information is not there. What to do next is a design decision, not a retry.
trajectory.produces: A decision per damaged frame, recorded, on whether it is recovered, re composed around the damage, or named as unusable.

trajectory.action: Lay in the two colour treatment and the grain as confined moves on the raster masters, keeping the faces and instruments readable inside the dark ground.
trajectory.judgement: The look is the deliverable, so it has to live in pixels that can be placed anywhere rather than in a layout effect. Confinement is the craft: an unconfined tint takes the performer with the room.
trajectory.produces: The series treatment applied to the raster masters, with the confinement and parameters recorded.

trajectory.action: Recover the three act wordmarks off cloth: selections worded to the lettering's own visual properties, correct polarity, bounds crops driven by each selection's returned box, traces, then viewBoxes injected and the opaque full canvas ground paths removed. Reconcile each recovered mark to the act it belongs to.
trajectory.judgement: Disjoint lettering on fabric is not a subject, and a knockout that returns a plausible transparent file is not evidence that the wordmark survived. Reading the recovered marks against the billing is the only way to catch a mislabelled file.
trajectory.produces: Three placeable, scalable, transparent wordmarks, each attributed to the correct act.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the night with no archive frame, filter to photography, exclude generative candidates, license and download at full resolution, then put it beside the treated six.
trajectory.judgement: A thumbnail is a hundredth of the picture. What matters is whether this frame's own light will take the series treatment, and that only exists once the full frame is in hand next to the set.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP clean, camera scale frame and a judgement on whether it belongs to the series.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit for the whole series.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged against an eighteen to thirty two dollar ticket and a crowd that will read polish as inauthentic. A weight cannot be inferred from a style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one kit series type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained file carrying three A2 poster roots, each declaring its own canvas, with every photograph inlined as embedded image data and each act wordmark placed as inline SVG inside an explicitly sized wrapper anchored top and left.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a reference is not a photograph, and an auto sized wrapper anchored from the right throws its contents clean off the canvas. The design work is whether the three are genuinely three directions on one series look.
trajectory.produces: An export ready source file for the poster run, retained as the durable half of the deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at the first canvas, and audit the returned per canvas markup for the other two.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning of any kind, and the rendition only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at canvas one is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: A native editable poster document, an inspected first canvas and a markup audit for the rest.

trajectory.action: Author and export the promoter deck as five roots at presentation size, carrying the room data as real tables and last season's draw as inline SVG, in the series look.
trajectory.judgement: A promoter reads capacity, terms and draw before they read art direction, so the data has to be legible as data. Tables and vector charts survive as native objects, which is what makes the deck worth handing over rather than screenshotting.
trajectory.produces: A native editable promoter deck with real tables and editable vector charting.

trajectory.action: Author and export the per release social set as one document carrying the square, the tall and the four by five at their own canvas sizes, plus the series basis page recording the palette, the treatment and the type system.
trajectory.judgement: Mixed canvas sizes in one document is the whole reason this is one working file the venue can drive itself for nine nights.
trajectory.produces: A native editable social set and a series basis page.

trajectory.action: Convert last season's card into an editable layout document, export its interchange form, reconstruct the true story text, build and verify the mapping, prepare the merge template and read the placeholder inventory back out.
trajectory.judgement: The printed card is not evidence of structure, and completed successfully is a status rather than a verification. Offsets computed from anything other than the document's true story are wrong in ways nothing complains about.
trajectory.produces: A verified merge template for the season card with its placeholder inventory reconciled.

trajectory.action: Merge the nine nights one per page with the per night picture bound through the image column, render the press file and per night files, and read every card against the billing.
trajectory.judgement: Two of the nine nights are billed identically, and a stack of cards a reader cannot tell apart is a design failure rather than a data failure. The bleed the printer asked about has to be answered honestly rather than switched on.
trajectory.produces: A press file of nine cards, per night files for the shops, and a written answer on bleed and on the card's inherited type voice.

trajectory.action: Create the selects board, add the treated set and the licensed frame within the per call placement cap, re sending only the entries the response names as failed, then write the handover note.
trajectory.judgement: A partial success is reported as a success code, and vector wordmarks are not boardable so they belong in the note instead. The note is what stops the venue rebuilding this look from scratch next spring.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover note.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the two worst lit nights can be brought into the series at all. On the frames where the follow spot drove the performer's face and shirt to the top of the channel there is nothing left to recover, and the recovery move answers that by returning success while the frame does not change: no warning, no error, no note, and a result that looks like a correctly restrained edit rather than like a dead end. Which frames are genuinely recoverable and which are not is a property of each night's own rig and exposure and cannot be read off a preview, because at preview scale a blown face and a bright face look identical against a dark room.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the answer only exists once the move has been made and the result compared against the frame it came from, and no parameter and no readout predicts it. Nothing states it either: the brief says the six were shot under six rigs and that no two match, which is true of every set of club photographs and is not a disclosure that two are damaged. And the response is not the same move again at a different strength, it is a different treatment for those frames, designing the blown region into the two colour look as a deliberate blank, re composing the poster around what survives, or replacing the frame.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Compare every recovery result against its own source rather than reading statuses, re plan the treatment for the affected nights so the damage becomes part of the look rather than a defect inside it, and re decide which night each poster direction is built on now that one candidate frame has changed character.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A poster run in which the headline performer's face is a flat white shape on two of the three directions, published as the series look and printed at A2.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the licensed frame belongs to this series. Everything visible before licensing is a small thumbnail: the true colour, the real grain structure, how much shadow detail the frame actually holds and how its light behaves once the series treatment is laid over it exist only in the full resolution file, and none of that can be judged in isolation. It is only judgeable beside the six treated archive frames, which is the last thing that happens.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot avoid it, because the comparison requires both a licensed full resolution frame and a finished treated set, and licensing is the step that produces the first. Nothing states it: the brief says one night has nothing usable and that the venue would rather not buy pictures, which is a preference, not a warning about a specific frame. And the response is not a re download, it is a fresh selection judged against a different criterion, or a decision to re target the treatment so both the archive and the bought frame can live under it.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Set the licensed frame beside the treated six at working scale, and if it reads as bought either license a different candidate chosen for its light rather than its subject, or adjust the series treatment and re apply it across all seven so one register covers them, then re judge.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Eight nights that look like the room and one night that looks like an advertisement, on a series whose entire pitch to its own audience is that it was all shot downstairs.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the construct the noir look is built on. Authored the natural way, a two colour treatment is a tinted or blended layer sitting over the photograph, and that construct does not survive: the blend is discarded and the element arrives as a plain opaque shape covering the picture underneath, at full success, with no warning of any kind. The same is true of a softening filter used to sink the ground. The returned per canvas markup is the only channel that reports it, and the document's own preview shows the first artboard only, so the second and third posters can be checked no other way.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the normalisation happens at import and the import is the last step of authoring; and doing it right first time presumes knowing which of several plausible constructions survives, which no tool reports and no checklist enumerates. Nothing states it: the brief asks for a dark high contrast two colour look and the acceptance line about the treatment actually being present is the client's own art direction, not a warning. And the response is not a re export, it is to produce a different upstream asset, the treatment baked into the raster master itself so that what the layout places is already the look, and then to re compose the canvases around a picture that now carries its own colour.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Move the two colour treatment out of the layout and into the raster masters for all seven frames, re author the poster canvases around those masters, re run the readiness check, re export, and audit all three canvases from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard, then repeat the same discipline for the deck and the social set.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A poster document delivered as the series look in which two of the three canvases are flat coloured rectangles sitting on top of the photographs, with every export having reported success.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are authored fixed canvases and which are a record per page printed run, given that only one surface composes free form layout at all.
Where the two colour treatment actually lives, in the raster masters or in the layout, and what that costs on either side.
What to do with the nights whose bright regions hold nothing: recover, design the damage into the look, or name the frame as unusable.
How confined the tint and grain moves have to be before the performers stop being readable inside the dark ground.

Selection wording on photographed cloth: naming the garment takes the shirt, naming the lettering's own visual properties takes the mark, and a one call knockout on disjoint lettering is the wrong instrument entirely.
Whether the wordmark filenames the managers sent can be trusted, and how to settle it when one cannot.
Whether the licensed frame belongs to the series or reads as bought, and whether the answer is a different frame or a different treatment.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against an eighteen to thirty two dollar ticket and a crowd that reads polish as inauthentic.
How the authored type system is chosen so that it sits beside the type voice the printed card inherits and cannot change.
How the two night residency is designed so a reader can tell the cards apart without the billing being altered.
What is said to the printer about bleed, given that the honest answer is that it cannot be introduced from this source.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns a very good imaginary jazz poster. IDENTITY: these are this room's own six nights, and the venue's entire pitch to its audience is that the series was shot downstairs, so the photographs cannot be regenerated. The three wordmarks belong to three real acts under approved billing and have to be RECOVERED off the merchandise photographs their managers sent, because a redrawn wordmark is a different act's logo and a mislabelled one is a billing error. SPEC: nine A5 cards, one night per card, each with its own date, billing, door time, price, picture and a licence line the room is required to print, delivered as a file a printer can run. A generated image satisfies none of that and cannot be checked for any of it. EDITABILITY: the venue says outright it will be changing dates itself and does not want to rebuild the look next spring, so the deliverable is defined by being documents they can open, retype and reuse. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality: did this recovery move actually change anything, does this bought frame sit with the set, did the treatment survive the import, did every letter of this wordmark survive the knockout.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. IMAGING: apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, auto_tone, monochromatic_tint, add_grain, halftone, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, fill_area, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs, remove_background and vectorize are verified headless across 27 live calls, and the mask accepting effect set is confirmed by live schema. The wordmark work rests on documented findings: remove_background on a disjoint mark kept only a few letters out of roughly eighteen thousand pixels of ink, the substrate versus ink prompt asymmetry is verified on a photographed printed surface, selection masks are strictly binary, polarity before tracing decides between a black box and a positive mark, and vectorize emits no viewBox and always an opaque path at index zero. EXPRESS: multi root export and mixed canvas sizes in one document are verified, tables import as real tables with per cell text and strokes, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, and the third checkpoint rests on the verified drops, mix blend mode is DROPPED and the element renders as a plain opaque shape and filter blur is DROPPED entirely, both at HTTP success with no warning, while the rendition preview is documented as first artboard only. Transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined photography passes the inline threshold immediately. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout and document_render_layout are verified fully headless and synchronous; one record per page is confirmed for PDF output, per record files are confirmed in correct order, and the per row image column bound genuinely different images per record through an at prefixed header plus additional image files. The card's two constraints are verified limitations rather than inventions: bleed cannot be introduced into a PDF derived template and the bleed switch is accepted while trim and bleed boxes stay identical, and there is no font file retrieval anywhere in the connector so typography control does not exist on this surface. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end including a browser proving licensed faces load, with the case sensitivity and non standard numeric weight traps live. STOCK AND BOARDS: short generic queries only, orientation never passed, the rendition is only a small thumbnail while license returned a real camera scale JPEG, and boards persist with a hard cap of twelve placements per call and a partial success reported as a success code. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no variable QR, no press ready with bleed claim, no pdfPreset, no upscaling, no compositing, no OCR, no text to image, no photograph reaching Express as a URL, no fill_text, no animate_design, no batch above twenty.

engagement_title: Marisol Cove shoulder season campaign: the page, the booking brochure, the social set, and the printed rate cards the agents hand over
vertical: Food, hospitality and travel. A fourteen room boutique clifftop hotel above a cove on the Mendocino coast, Northern California, pushing its autumn and winter shoulder season across its own page, a booking agent brochure, a social set and a printed per room rate card run.
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork post quoted in the ledger's grounding_note, a premium hospitality client asking for luxury style website hero banners with a clean, premium, modern design and, in the client's own words, the 'ability to maintain consistent brand identity across all creative assets'. The post names no property, so the line is laundered to the coined fictional hotel Marisol Cove. Only the sourcing platform is named, as provenance; the stock library, the booking agents and the printer are all generic, and no real hotel, person, agency, marketplace, software or trademark appears anywhere. The ledger's STRENGTHEN verdict keeps the concept (one campaign, one look, several destinations, everything editable) and deepens it to the current standard, because CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) changes what the honest fuller commission is. HTML authoring now returns a native editable Express document carrying mixed canvas sizes in one export, a mark photographed on a painted sign can be recovered as real vector, and a printer's press PDF plus a rates spreadsheet is a genuine one record per page merge. So the real job this client needed was never three hero banners: it was the campaign, the print run their booking agents actually hand over, and files they can keep editing without re-commissioning anyone.
client_one_liner: Our shoulder season push has to run off licensed coastal pictures brought to the light we actually have here, our lost mark has to come back off a photograph of the entrance sign, and our agents need nine printed rate cards, all of it editable by us afterwards.
client_brief:
Marisol Cove, autumn and winter push

We are a fourteen room hotel on the bluff above a cove on the Mendocino coast. Two owners, nine staff. Rooms run three hundred and forty to six hundred and twenty dollars a night. Our guests are couples and small groups, thirty to fifty five, and they come for the path down to the beach and for the dining room. There is no pool and there is no spa.

Autumn and winter are our thin months and this is the first year we are pushing them properly. Everything a guest sees changes at once: the page we send people to, the brochure our booking agents hand across a desk, and the set we post.

Where we actually are. There has been no photographer's shoot. What exists is our own room photographs, taken on two phones over two years, plus whatever we license from the stock library. Our office manager went through the thumbnails and shortlisted some coastal frames she likes. All of it has to end up looking like one place under one light: warm but never orange, quiet, the light we get here about an hour before sunset.

Our mark is a small wordmark with a wave rule under it. The file went with the designer who drew it in 2019. What we still have is a photograph of the painted sign at the entrance. We need the mark back as artwork we can place at any size on any colour.

We also need the rate cards, one card per room type, printed, for the fourteen travel agents who sell us. Our printer still had last season's card and sent the file over. The rates and what each room includes are in the spreadsheet.

The page, the brochure and the social set have to stay editable by us, because the featured room and the dates move every few weeks.

Finally a note: what you did, what type we are on, what the stock costs us, and anything about the mark or the printing we should know.
price_band_and_audience: Boutique premium coastal rooms at 340 to 620 dollars a night, guests 30 to 55, couples and small groups, experience led rather than amenity led. The band is load bearing. At this rate the campaign runs on serene full bleed photography, generous air, a small quiet mark and rates set in a plain table that the guest reads once and trusts. Push it down into a discount travel look (burst badges, stacked savings callouts, three deals a screen, a dense grid of small pictures) and the same rooms read as a 120 dollar highway motel, which repels the guest who was going to book and permanently anchors the rate lower. Push it up into black ground, foil serif, eight words a page luxury and it reads as a 1,400 dollar a night private estate, which misprices the property and reads as dishonest the moment the guest arrives at a fourteen room hotel with no spa. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,800 to 3,800 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: The quiet side of the coast.
brand_identity.sector: A fourteen room boutique hotel on the bluff above a cove, selling nights and the dining room to couples and small groups.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2014, on the Mendocino coast of Northern California, run by two owners with nine staff.
brand_identity.about: Marisol Cove is a small clifftop hotel built around a path down to a private beach and a dining room people plan a trip for. There is no pool and no spa, and the point of the place is the light, the water and being left alone. The autumn and winter shoulder season is the first the owners are pushing properly.
brand_identity.audience: Couples and small groups aged 30 to 55, experience led rather than amenity led, who book for the setting and the food and return in the quiet months.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Rooms run 340 to 620 dollars a night. Boutique premium, above a coastal inn and well below a resort or private estate. The rate is carried by the setting, not by facilities.
brand_identity.typography: A quiet high contrast serif for display, set large and given air, paired with a plain humanist sans for rates, captions and body. Coastal premium, never resort brochure and never luxury estate. Generous leading, restrained sizes.
brand_identity.voice: Calm, plain and specific. It describes what is actually there and lets the reader picture it. Example line the brand would write: An hour before sunset the light comes off the water and the whole cove goes gold. That is when to walk down.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The logo file was lost with the designer who drew it in 2019. The mark, a small caps wordmark over a hairline wave rule, survives only as the painted sign at the entrance, which the owners have photographed. Room photography is the owners' own phone frames plus licensed stock. No usable brand files remain beyond the sign photo.
brand_identity.values: One place under one light. Every guest facing piece should read as the same specific cove, honest about a fourteen room hotel rather than dressed up as something grander.

acceptance_bar: The licensed frames, the owners' room photographs and every picture in the campaign read as one place under one light when they sit next to each other: one white point, one warmth, one black point. A frame that cannot be brought to the set is named in the note, not shipped at eighty percent.

No delivered file exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions, and no crop or knockout tradeoff record in the run carries an upscale entry. A picture that reaches its box by being enlarged fails even if it looks acceptable at page scale.
No generative-tech stock frame appears anywhere in the delivered campaign, and every licensed frame is accounted for in the note with what it cost.

The mark is placeable artwork rather than a picture of artwork: transparent, scalable with a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath, and it still reads as the mark at the size it actually reproduces in the page header over the photograph, and reversed on colour.

The rate card run is one press PDF whose page count equals the true room type count after the spreadsheet is reconciled, in the room order the owners use, with every field present on every page and nothing stopping mid word at the frame edge.
Every room type has its own card and no card stands in for two rooms.

The campaign is ONE native editable Express document carrying every canvas in its own size (the page, the brochure pages, each social size, the basis canvas), delivered with the self contained source it was built from.
Every photograph in that document is embedded image data rather than a reference, and no canvas shows an empty grey box where a picture should be.
Headline copy sits legibly over the photography on every canvas, not only the first one, and the rate table is a real table with its own cells rather than a picture of a table.
One type system across every canvas and the printed cards, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the actual numeric weight used.

The note states what was applied per photograph and why any frame differs from its neighbours, every resize any tool reported, the room reconciliation, the stock licensing position, and anything about the mark or the print run the owners should know.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching a pixel.
trajectory.judgement: The page, brochure and social set are one authored fixed canvas document because the owners edit them every few weeks. The rate cards are a record per page print run and belong on the merge surface. Nothing here is ambiguous, so there is nothing to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming surface per deliverable, and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline, plus the fact that the image tools enforce their own domain whitelist, so nothing reaches them except through this route or a licensed stock URL.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Preview all eleven room photographs and the sign photograph and triage them: which are camera scale and which are already-cropped web exports, which are level, which sit under which light, and what each frame actually shows.
trajectory.judgement: The owners describe eleven room photographs. Only the pictures can settle whether that is eleven different rooms, and reading them against the room list is slower than counting files and is not the same thing.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note covering scale, tilt, illuminant and subject identity.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level, before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes the subject and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Search the coastal subjects with short generic queries, filter to photography, read the generative-tech flag on every candidate, then license and download the chosen frames at full resolution.
trajectory.judgement: The shortlist is a starting point, not a decision. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used, and the insurer's rule is enforced from the returned flag rather than from how a thumbnail looks.
trajectory.produces: Licensed, IP clean, camera scale coastal frames with their cost and their flags recorded.

trajectory.action: Fix one house target off the strongest frame and bring each licensed frame and each usable room photograph toward it with its own call, recording the parameters applied.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a campaign, not a set of good pictures. One batched call applies one identical parameter set, which is exactly wrong for two phones, two years and a stock library. The agent holds one destination and reaches it by different routes.
trajectory.produces: A graded house set at source scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Confined corrections where a whole frame move goes wrong, selecting materials by their own visual properties rather than by the object they belong to.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the whole gate. Bringing warmth into a frame globally takes the water toward green and the white bed linen toward cream, and those are the two things a guest reads first.
trajectory.produces: Corrected frames where a global move would have broken the water or the linen.

trajectory.action: Cut every picture to the box it actually fills on its destination canvas, reading the tradeoffs each call returns rather than the success message.
trajectory.judgement: The tradeoffs array is the only channel that reports an enlargement, and it carries no warning language. A web export that will not reach the brochure box is a frame to reassign or to name, not one to interpolate.
trajectory.produces: Destination sized pictures with their returned tradeoffs recorded per frame.

trajectory.action: Recover the mark off the sign: a paint level selection naming the mark's own visual properties, correct polarity, a bounds crop from the selection's own returned box, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full canvas path removed. Produce a single colour mark and a colour accurate variant.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions the tools do not make: how to word the selection so it takes the paint and not the board, which polarity to trace, and which variant is the deliverable. Background removal is the wrong instrument on disjoint painted lettering.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent mark plus a colour accurate variant.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged against a 340 to 620 dollar room and a guest who is choosing between three coastal hotels. The weight cannot be inferred from the style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Convert the printer's rate card PDF, export the IDML, and read the real frame inventory: how many text frames, what bounds, what applied type, what graphic frames exist.
trajectory.judgement: Frame granularity from a PDF is not under the agent's control, and the printed card's visual blocks are no evidence of it. Nothing can be promised about mapping until the document itself has been looked at.
trajectory.produces: A true frame inventory of the converted card, written down before any mapping is drafted.

trajectory.action: Reconcile the spreadsheet against the owners' room list, then build the field mapping against the document's true story text, validate it, prepare the merge template, and re-export the IDML to confirm every placeholder is actually present.
trajectory.judgement: Ten rows and nine rooms cannot both be right, and the reconciliation is the agent's call to make and to report. The validator answering VALID and the prepare step answering success are not evidence that a placeholder landed; only the round tripped document is.
trajectory.produces: A live merge template whose placeholders have been confirmed by inspection, plus a written room reconciliation.

trajectory.action: Merge to one press PDF at one record per page, merge again to the native format, then render per record proofs at true print resolution, and read every merged page.
trajectory.judgement: Page count equal to room count is the cheap check. Reading the pages is the real one, because a field that never landed and a line that stopped rendering both come back as a successful merge.
trajectory.produces: One press PDF for the printer, per record proofs for the owners, and a read of every page.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML carrying every canvas as its own root at its own declared size, inline every photograph as image data, place the mark as inline SVG inside an explicitly sized left and top anchored wrapper, set the rate table as a real table, declare family and weight on every text element, then upload the file and hold the returned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override is what collapses a mixed size set. The design work is how much air the page carries and how quietly the rates sit.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML carrying the whole campaign, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at the first canvas, and parse the returned per canvas markup for every canvas after it.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition preview only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at canvas one is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document, an inspected first canvas, and a per canvas markup audit for the rest.

trajectory.action: Create the selects board and add the graded house set and the licensed frames within the per call placement cap, re-sending only the entries the response names as failed.
trajectory.judgement: A 201 is partial success, and the vector mark is not boardable, so it belongs in the note instead.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped.

trajectory.action: Write the note: per photograph what was applied and why, every resize any tool reported, the room reconciliation, the stock licensing position and cost, the type system by role, and what the owners should know about the mark and about the print run.
trajectory.judgement: The note is the deliverable that survives the season. It has to be specific enough that the next freelancer does not repeat the archaeology, and honest about anything that could not be delivered.
trajectory.produces: The written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the licensed coastal frames actually are, once they are full size and sitting beside the graded set. Everything available before licensing is a 240 pixel thumbnail, which carries neither the frame's true cast nor its usable crop, and the owners' shortlist was made from exactly those thumbnails. The dusk frame the office manager likes best comes down as a cold blue grey whose warmth cannot be reached without the sand going muddy and the water going flat, and that verdict exists only in the adjacency: on its own it is a good photograph, and next to the graded room set it is a different day in a different place.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because full resolution colour does not exist until the frame is licensed and downloaded, and no parameter reveals it earlier. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that the office manager shortlisted frames she likes and that everything must end up looking like one place. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is a different search and a fresh licensing decision with a real cost attached, or a reassignment of that frame to a canvas where its cast reads as intentional.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-search the coastal subjects with different short queries, read the generative-tech flag on every new candidate, license a replacement, grade it into the house target, and re-judge it beside the set rather than on its own. Then re-cut whichever canvases had been built around the rejected frame.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A campaign whose page, brochure and social set are visibly three different coastal places, on a property whose entire pitch is that it is one specific cove, with a cold dusk hero anchoring the most expensive canvas.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the merged rate cards actually say. The printed card reads as six separate typographic blocks, but what the conversion exposes as mappable frames is not under the agent's control and can collapse to a single continuous flow, which changes the entire mapping strategy. On top of that, the structure readout of that flow drops one run while keeping its line break, so the string still looks well formed, every offset after it is short by exactly that run, the validator answers VALID with no warnings, and the prepare step answers success. Two fields then never land on any card. In the same pass, the one Includes line that is three times longer than its neighbours does not spill anywhere visible at trim, it simply stops rendering partway through a word.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it and no parameter controls it: granularity is a property of the source PDF, and both the validator and the prepare step report success on offsets computed from an incomplete readout. (b) Nothing states it: the owners say the layout is fine and only the rooms and the numbers change. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different mapping strategy computed from the document's true story text plus a copy decision on the record that will not fit.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reconstruct the true story text from the exported document rather than from the readout, recompute every offset against it, rebuild and re-verify the template by round tripping the document and confirming each placeholder is present, re-merge, and re-read every page. Then resolve the long Includes line by shortening it with the owners' wording rather than letting it stop mid word, and record that decision.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Nine printed cards handed to fourteen travel agents with the rate line and the season line silently missing from every one of them, and one room's inclusions ending mid word, after a merge that reported success at every stage.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered mark still reads as the mark at the size it actually reproduces, on the ground it actually sits on. The trace looks clean and complete at canvas size on white. In the page header it is small and it sits over a full bleed photograph, and at that size the wave rule can thin to nothing and the tight counters in the small-caps letterforms can close, so the wordmark reads as a dark smudge with the right silhouette. Which of those happens depends on the paint edge in that particular photograph of that particular weathered sign, and it is visible only after the canvas is exported and looked at at reproduction size.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) There is no ordering that avoids it and no measurement available: the connector has no ruler and no way to inspect a rendered glyph, so the only evidence is the exported canvas itself. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for artwork placeable at any size on any colour, which is the client's standing requirement, not a warning that this trace will fail small. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is a different raster preparation upstream, a tighter paint level selection or the opposite polarity or a bounds crop before tracing, and possibly a different variant carrying the header entirely.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-prepare the mark from the sign photograph through a different selection and polarity, re-trace, re-apply the viewBox and strip the opaque path again, decide whether the single colour or the colour accurate variant carries the header, re-author the canvas around whichever it is, re-run the readiness check and re-export.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A campaign whose header carries a smudge where the hotel's only surviving mark should be, delivered as an editable document that reported success throughout, with the owners told their mark had been recovered.
