decision_gates: Which deliverables go to the merge surface and which to authored canvases, given a card the mutual wants preserved and client-facing pieces whose rates will move every year.
Whether each producer is separated by knocking out to the house ground in one operation or by a bounded selection, decided per frame against the office each producer happened to stand in.
How far a self-submitted phone frame can be pushed toward the house rendering before it stops looking like the producer, under a compliance note that rejects anything reading as retouched.
Which producers can reach the card's photograph area at native scale and what to do about the ones who cannot, given that enlargement is reported only in a tradeoff record.
Whether a partner bank's signage in a producer's frame is the agent's to remove or the mutual's to rule on.

The roster: a resigned producer still in the export, two producers carrying longer state-specific disclosure language, and a photo reference pointing at a file nobody sent. What is the agent's call and what is the mutual's.
Whether to trust the mapping tool's readout of the printer's text or to reconstruct the story independently from the exported document.
Whether a success message counts as verification that the prepared template's placeholders exist.
Whether per-producer identity is established by position in a returned list or by opening the file.
The basis on which three plans quoted differently are compared at all, and where the qualification that makes that honest has to sit.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a regulated mutual at a modest premium band.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns a handsome insurance brochure with invented people on it. IDENTITY: these are fourteen named appointed producers whose faces sit on cards at bank counters, and a regenerated face is a misrepresentation a licensed carrier cannot distribute. SPEC: the run is one 4 by 6 card per active producer binding four named fields verbatim, including a state-mandated disclosure that must appear complete, plus per-producer single files each containing the producer they claim and proofs at true print resolution. EDITABILITY: the deck, the one-pager and the infographic are defined by being editable, because rates move annually and disclosure language changes when a state changes it. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did this shoulder survive separation, did this disclosure arrive whole at trim, is this the producer the card says it is.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. IMAGING: auto_tone, apply_adjustments global and masked, select_subject and select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, remove_background both transparent and with backgroundColor, crop_to_bounds and crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs, upscale_factor and detection_confidence are all verified headless. The separation checkpoint rests on documented facts rather than invention: there is no measurement anywhere in the family, selection masks come back fully binary with zero intermediate values so no feather exists, and remove_background is documented as depending on a coherent subject blob, which is exactly what a same-value shoulder against a same-value wall fails to present. crop_and_resize is documented as interpolating up to a hard 2x cap and reporting it only in the tradeoffs array, which makes the no-enlargement bar checkable rather than asserted. MERGE SPINE: building a merge template from a bare press PDF end to end headlessly is verified, one record per page is confirmed for the PDF branch, per-record files are confirmed in correct order by two routes, true 300 DPI at trim is confirmed through the render tool, the merge's own resolution parameter is documented as silently ignored so proofs must be rendered from the merged document, frame granularity from a PDF is documented as not under the agent's control, and the mapping readout's textContent is documented as lossy in a way the validator blesses. Image binding through an at-prefixed column plus additionalImageFiles is verified, with the single-record loop as the identity-guaranteed fallback. The disclosure checkpoint needs no unverified capability: a fixed-measure frame's overset behaviour is a property of the converted document, and reading it requires exactly the trim-resolution render the tool provides. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export, true mm print canvases at 96 dpi, real tables with per-cell strokes, inline SVG as native editable vector, and a genuine editable document are verified; the rendition shows page one only so verification splits between the rendition and the returned markup; the payload is routed by uploaded URL because inlined portraits pass the 70 KB threshold immediately. FONTS, STOCK and BOARDS follow the verified chains, with short queries, orientation never passed, and the twelve-per-call board cap with a partial success read as partial. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no fill_text, no animate_design, no create_firefly_board, no replace_image, no download_design, no upscaling, no object removal, no compositing, no OCR, no variable QR, no bleed or press-preset gate, no batch above 20.

engagement_title: Anvil and Oak strength studio launch: recover the mark off the painted brick, bring three evenings of member-athlete portraits to one look, rebuild the athlete cards from the barbell club's press file, and hand back the schedule poster, the membership deck and the spotlight set as documents the coaches can edit themselves
vertical: Health and fitness, an independent strength and functional training studio opening in a converted machine shop in Providence, Rhode Island
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the recurring Upwork gym-launch posting in which an owner opening a new studio asks for 'a class schedule poster for the wall, a membership deck we use at the front desk, and social posts for Instagram, all in our branding', explicitly noting that they have 'no logo file, only a photo of the sign' and that the schedule 'changes every season so we need to be able to edit it ourselves'. Co-anchor: the Freelancer.com posting from a barbell and powerlifting club needing 'individual athlete result cards, one per lifter, print ready, from the template our old designer made', with only the printed PDF surviving and a spreadsheet of names and numbers supplied alongside. Both real clients, their gyms and their coaches are laundered to the fictional Anvil and Oak. The ledger's STRENGTHEN verdict was right that the concept as banked leaned on authoring alone: the fuller commission this client genuinely has starts at a photograph of a hand-painted mark and sixteen inconsistent portraits, runs through a real record-per-page card run inherited from a printer who is gone, and only then reaches the poster, the deck and the spotlight set that all have to carry the same recovered mark identically.
client_one_liner: We have no logo file, only the mark our sign painter put on the brick, and everything we hand out has to carry that same mark at every size on our dark ground without a white box around it.
client_brief:
Anvil and Oak, opening in March

We are two coaches opening a strength studio in a converted machine shop. Before this we ran a barbell club out of a shared space for six years, and about half our members are coming with us.

We have no logo file. What we have is the mark our sign painter put on the brick wall of the new space, and a photograph of it. Everything we hand out has to carry that mark, the same mark, at every size, and it has to sit on our dark ground.

We need the wall poster first. It hangs by the door and it is the weekly class grid: eight classes across five days, with times, coach and level. That grid changes with the season so we have to be able to change it ourselves.

We need the membership deck, the one we walk a prospect through at the desk. Our philosophy, how the programming actually works, who the coaches are, what the tiers cost and how to join. The tiers need to sit side by side so somebody can compare them in about four seconds.

We need the athlete cards. We ran these at the barbell club after every meet, one per lifter, their numbers and a line from them, and people kept them on their fridges. Our printer set those up and we only have the file that went to press. We want the same run for our opening roster, a proof of each, and a separate file per athlete.

And we need the spotlight posts: square for the feed, tall for stories, and the four by five one, all from the same portraits.

We shot the portraits ourselves over three evenings in the old space. They are not consistent and we know it.

We have nothing usable of the street or the building from outside. If there is something honest for the deck opener, use it.

Memberships run a hundred and ten to a hundred and eighty five a month, drop in twenty eight. Our people are twenty five to forty five and they are here to get strong. Confident, not soft, and not a bargain gym.
price_band_and_audience: Memberships at a hundred and ten to a hundred and eighty five dollars a month with a twenty eight dollar drop in, sold to twenty five to forty five year olds who are choosing coached strength work over a commodity gym and who read programming detail as evidence of competence. The band is load-bearing in both directions. At this price the correct grammar is confident and specific: a dark ground, cinematic portraits with real modelling on the shoulders and forearms, a schedule grid that shows level and coach rather than mood words, tier cards that state exactly what is included, and heavy condensed display type held in check by a plain workhorse text face. Softened into the pale, airy, thin-serif register of a boutique wellness studio it misreads the audience completely and reads as a place where nobody lifts anything heavy. Pushed the other way into shouted percentages, burst callouts and a discount-first hierarchy it becomes a chain gym promotion, which directly undercuts a price roughly double what the chains charge and tells a prospective member the coaching is not what they are paying for. A real posted commission of this shape runs 1,200 to 2,800 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: An independent strength and functional training studio selling coached memberships and drop in sessions.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Opening March 2027 in a converted machine shop in Providence, Rhode Island, run by two coaches who ran a barbell club in a shared space for six years.
brand_identity.about: Anvil and Oak is a coach led strength studio built in an old machine shop. About half its opening members are following the two coaches from the barbell club they ran before. The offer is real programming and real coaching, not a commodity gym floor, and members read the detail of the programming as evidence the coaching is worth the price.
brand_identity.audience: People aged 25 to 45 choosing coached strength work over a commodity gym, here to get strong, who value programming detail and competence over amenities.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Memberships run 110 to 185 dollars a month with a 28 dollar drop in. Roughly double a chain gym, priced on coaching. Confident and specific, neither a soft boutique wellness studio nor a discount chain.
brand_identity.typography: Heavy condensed display type for headlines and the schedule grid, held in check by a plain workhorse sans for body, times and figures. Legible from across a room, comfortable at small sizes. Confident, unsoftened, industrial without being a novelty.
brand_identity.voice: Direct, plain and sure of itself, the way a good coach cues a lift. No hype, no percentages shouted. Example line the brand would write: Show up, do the work, add weight. We handle the programming so you can focus on the bar.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There is no logo file. The mark, an anvil silhouette inside a ring of lettering with an oak sprig crossing the anvil's horn, exists only as the sign painter's hand painted work on the studio's brick wall, which the coaches have photographed. Athlete portraits were shot by the coaches over three evenings and are not consistent. The old printer's press file is all that survives of the athlete card.
brand_identity.values: One mark, everywhere, complete and on the dark ground. The identity is the recovered wall mark used consistently, and the studio should always read as coached strength at its true price.

assets_supplied.name: wall_mark.jpg (approx 4000 x 3000)
assets_supplied.kind: A photograph of the hand-painted studio mark on the raw brick wall of the new space, shot slightly off square in evening light: an anvil silhouette, a ring of lettering around it, and an oak sprig crossing the anvil's horn.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The mark our sign painter put on the brick. It is all we have."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is a compound lockup, and a selection aimed at it comes back plausible while quietly dropping one of its three elements, most often the sprig, which is thin and crosses the anvil. The enclosed counters inside the ring lettering are interior holes rather than outside edges, so a background removal returns an opaque patch of brick where the counters should be see-through.

assets_supplied.name: athlete_portraits/ (16 frames, three evenings, mixed dimensions)
assets_supplied.kind: Portraits of the opening roster shot by the coaches themselves over three evenings in the old shared space, on a mix of a camera and a phone.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "We shot these ourselves over three evenings. They are not consistent and we know it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The three evenings sit at three different colour temperatures and two of them carry a green cast off the shared space's overhead tubes. Five frames are near-square captures that cannot reach the tall story format at native scale, and on two frames a loaded barbell crosses the subject at shoulder height so a subject selection takes it in on one frame and cuts through it on the other.

assets_supplied.name: meetcard_press.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The barbell club's flat press PDF for the post-meet athlete card, 5 by 7 inches portrait, fonts embedded, produced from a real page layout so it converts cleanly. Carries the lifter's name, three stat lines, a quote line, the club crest and a tinted panel where the printed card shows the lifter's photograph.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The card our printer set up. We only have what went to press and he is not doing this any more."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The crest and the panel behind the printed photograph were both drawn as artwork in the original layout rather than placed as images, so what the conversion exposes as addressable structure bears no relation to how the printed card is visually blocked out. Which of the printed lines are separately addressable and which share a single continuous flow cannot be inferred from looking at the card.

assets_supplied.name: roster_and_numbers.csv
assets_supplied.kind: The opening roster export from the club's spreadsheet, one row per athlete, with columns for name, three lift figures, level, coach and a quote line.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our opening roster and everyone's numbers."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three faults, none stated. One athlete asked to be left out after the export was taken and the request sits in the coaches' notes file rather than in the spreadsheet. The lift figures are a mix of kilograms and pounds with no unit column, so two athletes appear to be far stronger than they are. And two quote lines run to several times the length of the rest.

assets_supplied.name: coach_notes.txt
assets_supplied.kind: A page from the two coaches on how the programming actually works, what each class level means, and a few lines about the roster.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "How the programming works and what the levels mean."

acceptance_bar: One mark, not several. The mark on the poster, on the deck, on the cards and on every spotlight canvas is the same artwork placed identically, and it carries all three of its elements everywhere it appears.
The mark sits on the dark ground with no box, no halo and no white plate behind it, and it holds at the smallest size it is used at as well as the largest.

The sixteen portraits read as one shoot: one colour temperature, one black point, one degree of modelling on skin, one crop logic. An athlete who cannot be brought to the set is named, not shipped near it.
Any invented edge added to reach a format is indistinguishable from the frame it extends when the finished canvas is viewed at full size on the dark ground.
No delivered image exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions and no crop or resize operation's tradeoff record carries an enlargement entry.
Exactly one athlete card per rostered athlete who is in, no extra card and no missing card, and if the number shipped is not the roster count the note says which row was left out and why.
Every card's figures are true and comparable to every other card's figures, on a stated basis.

If a card cannot carry that athlete's photograph, the note says why in plain terms and the portrait is delivered somewhere the studio can actually use it, rather than the photograph being dropped in silence.
Each per-athlete file contains the athlete its filename claims, established by opening it rather than by the order files came back in.
The proofs are rendered at true print resolution at card trim rather than at screen scale.

The poster, the deck, the tier card and the spotlight set come back as one native editable document we can change times, prices and faces in, with every photograph actually visible, the schedule grid and the tier comparison as real tables, and every text element carrying its licensed face at that family's own weight.
The schedule grid reads at the distance a wall poster is read from, and the tier comparison can be understood in about four seconds.
The set reads as a coached strength studio at a hundred and ten to a hundred and eighty five a month, neither a soft wellness studio nor a discount chain.

A written note: what was applied to each portrait and why it differs, how the mark was recovered and at what size it stops holding, the type system by role, every roster row questioned and its resolution, what the press file conversion actually exposed, and every enlargement any tool reported.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including trace and edge extension
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (global and masked), image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_fill_area, image_crop_to_bounds, image_vectorize, image_generative_expand, image_crop_and_resize (reading tradeoffs and detection_confidence)
adobe_surfaces.role: Two jobs on one surface. It recovers the mark off the photographed brick, which means selecting ink rather than substrate on a compound lockup, getting polarity right before tracing, and then repairing what the tracer hands back, since the trace arrives with no scalable frame and an opaque plate underneath it. And it brings sixteen portraits shot across three evenings to one look, then derives the platform formats, extending a frame's edge only where the tall format cannot be reached any other way. There is no measurement anywhere in this family and selections come back fully binary.

adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml (twice), generate_indd_mapping_prompt (as generator and as validator), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout (application/x-indesign and application/pdf, recordRange), document_render_layout (resolution 300, createSeparateFiles, pageRange in N-N form)

The barbell club's press file becomes a live merge template, the roster becomes the data source after reconciliation, and the run yields the cards, the per-athlete single files the studio hands out, and the proofs the coaches approve. What that document actually exposes as addressable structure has to be read out of the exported interchange file rather than inferred from the printed card, the true story text reconstructed from its content runs, and the placeholder inventory confirmed by round trip rather than by a success message.

adobe_surfaces.role: The A2 schedule poster at true physical dimensions, the five-root membership deck, the tier comparison card and the mixed-canvas spotlight set, all as one native editable document so the coaches can change times, prices and faces themselves. The recovered mark is inlined as vector markup so it stays editable rather than becoming a picture, every photograph is inlined as image data, the schedule grid and the tier comparison are genuine tables, family and weight are declared per text element, and each root declares its own canvas so the square, tall and four by five spotlight canvases coexist with an A2 sheet in one export.

The pairing is the agent's own art direction against a confident, unsoftened strength band read from across a room, the numeric weight is non-standard per family so a heavy display cut cannot be reached by assuming a weight, one unlaundered name kills the whole kit, and the CSS must use the returned slug.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle the split: athlete cards to the merge surface, poster and deck and tier card and spotlight set to authored canvases, mark recovery and portraits to imaging.
trajectory.judgement: The card is record per page against a layout the coaches want kept; everything else is free-form, seasonal and must stay editable, which the merge surface structurally cannot give.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming the surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier.

trajectory.action: Upload the wall photograph, the sixteen portraits, the press PDF, the roster and the coaches' notes, holding each returned presigned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A manifest keyed by athlete and by role, because the same portrait will exist in four states and the mark in at least three.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by athlete and role.

trajectory.action: Preview the wall photograph and decide how to name the mark so a selection lands on the painted ink rather than on the brick or the wall panel it sits in.
trajectory.judgement: Naming the substrate pulls the selection to the substrate and naming the graphic's own colour, medium and form pulls it to the ink. The lockup has three separable elements and one selection may not carry all of them.
trajectory.produces: A selection strategy and the mask or masks it produced, with a note on which elements each carried.

trajectory.action: Level the wall photograph, isolate the mark, get the polarity right, crop to its own bounds and trace it.
trajectory.judgement: Tracing the wrong polarity returns a filled plate with the mark knocked out of it, and both outcomes report success. What comes back from the tracer has no scalable frame and carries a full-canvas plate underneath the artwork, neither of which any tool repairs.
trajectory.produces: A traced mark with its frame injected and its underlying plate removed, ready to place on a dark ground.

trajectory.action: Place the recovered mark on the studio's dark ground at the sizes it will actually be used at, from the poster's header down to the corner of a story canvas and the athlete card's footer, and look at each one.
trajectory.judgement: A trace that reads correctly at the size it was traced is not evidence about the size it will be reproduced at, and the ground it sits on changes what survives. This is judged by looking, not by any readout.
trajectory.produces: The mark shown at every reproduction size it will be used at, on the real ground.

trajectory.action: Preview all sixteen portraits and triage: colour temperature per evening, cast, subject separation, what crosses the subject, native dimensions and how much edge each frame has to spare against each spotlight format.
trajectory.judgement: Three evenings are three different problems, and which frames can reach the tall format at native scale is a fact about the files rather than a decision.
trajectory.produces: A per-frame triage note: session, cast, obstruction, native dimensions and edge margin per format.

trajectory.action: Fix one studio look and bring each of the sixteen toward it with its own call, recording the parameters applied.
trajectory.judgement: Three colour temperatures and two casts have to arrive at one temperature and one black point, which is sixteen routes to one destination rather than one batched move, and the dark ground the portraits will sit on is what the black point has to answer to.
trajectory.produces: Sixteen graded portraits at source scale with a per-athlete parameter log.

trajectory.action: Lay the sixteen graded portraits together as the spotlight set will run them and judge them as one shoot.
trajectory.judgement: Judging the set at the only moment the comparison exists, and deciding whether any portrait has been pushed far enough to stop belonging to the other fifteen.
trajectory.produces: A set judged as a set, with any portrait that will not join it named.

trajectory.action: Derive the square, four by five and tall spotlight crops from the graded masters, reading detection confidence and the tradeoff record on every crop, and extend the frame only where the tall format cannot otherwise be reached.
trajectory.judgement: One crop logic across sixteen athletes rather than sixteen good crops. Extending a frame is the only sanctioned way to add pixels and it is a last resort, not a default, and the tradeoffs array is the only place an enlargement toward the interpolation cap is ever reported.
trajectory.produces: Three families of spotlight crop with their tradeoff records, and a list of which frames were extended.

trajectory.surface: Data preparation and Creative Cloud storage
trajectory.action: Reconcile the roster against the coaches' notes, resolve the units question, normalise it into a merge-shaped data file and upload it.
trajectory.judgement: Real reconciliation: one athlete's withdrawal lives in the notes and not in the spreadsheet, the lift figures are two different units presented as one column, and two quotes are far longer than the rest. Which of these is the agent's call and which is the coaches' is a decision, and the client asked to be told.
trajectory.produces: The merge data file, a stated basis for the figures, and a list of roster questions.

trajectory.action: Convert the press PDF, export the interchange file, unzip it and read the real frame inventory and bounds, then reconstruct each frame's true story text from its concatenated content runs.
trajectory.judgement: What the document exposes is a property of how the club's printer built it, and every offset must be computed from the document's own text rather than from any convenience readout.
trajectory.produces: The converted document, its interchange export, a frame inventory with real ids and bounds, and a reconstructed story string.

trajectory.action: Author the mapping against the structure the document actually exposes, validate it, prepare the template, then export the interchange file from the RESULT and search for every placeholder the mapping claimed to create.
trajectory.judgement: Not accepting a success message as evidence, and ordering any rows that share a frame so their positions hold against the original text.
trajectory.produces: A prepared template whose placeholder inventory has been independently confirmed.

trajectory.action: Merge to a native document, render the athlete cards and the proofs at true print resolution from that document, and produce the per-athlete single files, naming each by opening it.
trajectory.judgement: Merging to the native document first keeps both the press branch and the per-record branch open, and identity by position in a returned list is the fast wrong answer that puts one lifter's numbers under another lifter's name.
trajectory.produces: The card run, print-resolution proofs, and per-athlete files verified by inspection.

trajectory.action: Read every rendered card against the reconciled roster at trim rather than at proof scale, line by line and figure by figure.
trajectory.judgement: A card carrying another athlete's numbers and a card whose quote stops early both look like success at the API boundary and both look fine on a screen-scale proxy.
trajectory.produces: A card-by-card reconciliation against the roster.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the honest deck opener, filter to photography, exclude generative-tech results, license and download at full resolution, then bring it toward the studio look and lay it against the graded portraits.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose blacks can live beside sixteen portraits already sitting on a dark ground rather than the moodiest thumbnail, and decide whether it joins the set or gets abandoned for a different search. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP-clean, camera-scale opener, in or out, with the reasoning recorded.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own and has to answer to a confident strength band read from across a room and to a schedule grid that must stay legible at small sizes. The weight cannot be inferred from the style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one-kit type system with family, foundry and actual numeric weight per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self-contained HTML carrying the A2 poster at true physical dimensions, the five deck roots, the tier comparison card and the three spotlight canvases, inline the recovered mark as vector markup and every photograph as image data, set the schedule grid and the tier comparison as real tables, declare family and weight per text element, then upload it and hold the URL.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, vector markup in an auto-sized right-anchored wrapper runs off the canvas edge, and a global canvas override collapses a mixed-size set. The design work is a schedule grid that survives being read from six feet away and a tier comparison a prospect resolves in four seconds.
trajectory.produces: One export-ready HTML carrying the poster, deck, tier card and spotlight set, retained as the durable source.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, verify the first canvas from the document's rendition and every other canvas from the returned per-canvas markup, then build the selects board within the placement cap and write the note.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, the rendition shows the first artboard only, and a partial board placement is reported as a success. The note has to carry the consent question, the units basis and the mark's smallest safe size.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document, an inspected first canvas, a markup audit for the rest, a persistent board and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered mark still holds where it is actually reproduced. The tracer takes no options at all, so everything about how the mark comes out is decided by the raster that goes in, and what comes back reads correctly at the size it was traced. On a hand-painted mark the ring lettering's counters and the gap between the oak sprig and the anvil's horn are narrow and irregular, and at the size the mark sits in a story canvas corner or a card footer, on the studio's dark ground rather than the pale field it was traced against, those counters can close up and the sprig can weld itself to the anvil. Nothing reports this. The artwork is valid, it places, it scales, and the failure exists only in what a person sees at reproduction size on the real ground.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot avoid it, because the mark must exist before it can be placed, and care cannot settle it, because the tracer exposes no threshold, no path simplification and no colour count, so there is no parameter to get right in advance. Nothing in the brief, the assets or the deliverables states that the mark has narrow counters or a tight gap; the client only states that the mark must hold at every size, which is their requirement rather than a disclosure. The response is not a re-run of the trace, it is a return to the raster preparation with a different bound and a different polarity, or an authored small-size variant of the mark, which is a design decision about what the mark is allowed to lose.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Go back into the raster preparation and re-isolate the mark on a bound that keeps the counters open, re-trace and re-repair the artwork, and if the counters still close at the smallest reproduction, author a deliberate small-size variant, then re-place both at every size on the dark ground and record which size the full lockup stops holding at so the studio knows where the line is.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A studio whose entire identity is one mark launches with that mark reading as a solid blob in the corner of every story post and at the foot of every athlete card, which is the one thing the client explicitly asked to be protected against and the thing every member will see most often.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether an extended frame can join the set. Five portraits are near-square captures that cannot reach the tall story format at native scale, so the only sanctioned route is to extend the frame's edges and crop into the result. What that extension actually builds is not knowable before it runs: it invents continuation from what is at the edge, and on a portrait shot in a cluttered shared space the invented edge can be a plausible wall that is nonetheless a different value and a different temperature from the graded set, or it can carry a smear where a rack upright ran off the frame. The call succeeds, returns a seed, and produces an image that looks entirely reasonable in isolation, on its own, at preview scale.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the frames that need extending are exactly the frames that cannot reach the format any other way, and enlargement is barred. Care cannot settle it either: nothing about a frame predicts what its edges will generate, and the same call on two portraits from the same evening can behave differently. Nothing in the brief or the assets says which frames are short or what sits at their edges, and the acceptance line about invented edges is the client's standing quality bar. The response is a composition decision rather than a re-run: extend from a different side, crop tighter and lose some of the athlete, or take that athlete out of the tall format and give them the square and four by five only.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Lay each extended frame against the graded set on the dark ground at full size rather than judging it alone at preview scale, and where the invented edge does not match, re-extend from a different side or accept a tighter crop, re-derive that athlete's spotlight canvases from the corrected master, and if no route works, drop that athlete from the tall format and say so rather than shipping a frame with an invented wall in it.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The studio's launch story posts go out with five athletes standing in front of a wall that does not exist, in a value and a temperature that visibly disagree with the eleven portraits beside them, which reads to a prospective member as a cheaply faked photograph and undercuts a price roughly double what a chain gym charges.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the club's card actually exposes as addressable structure. The printed card reads as four separate blocks plus a crest and a photograph, but the crest and the panel behind the photograph were drawn as artwork rather than placed as images, and the printer's text blocks may or may not have been built as separate frames. Which lines are separately addressable, which share one continuous flow, and whether any graphic frame exists at all that a per-athlete portrait could be bound to, is a property of a document nobody involved has ever opened. The conversion reports success either way and the mapping readout will happily describe a structure that is nothing like the printed page.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot avoid it, because the document has to be converted before it can be inspected, and no amount of study of the printed card predicts its internal construction. Nothing in the brief, the assets or the deliverables states how the printer built it; the client only says the printer set it up and is gone. It is not a propagation re-run, because if there is no graphic frame the portraits cannot be bound into the card at all, and the response is a re-plan of what the card is: a text-only merge run with the portraits carried into the spotlight set instead, put to the coaches as a change to what they asked for rather than decided silently.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Read the exported interchange file's real frame inventory before authoring any mapping, build the mapping against the structure that is actually there rather than the structure the printed card suggests, and if no frame can carry a per-athlete photograph, re-plan the card as a text run, deliver the portraits in a form the studio can use, and tell the coaches plainly why the card cannot hold the picture the old one appeared to hold.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The studio ships an opening-roster card run built on an imagined structure: fields mapped into frames that do not hold them, a portrait bound to nothing, and cards that come back looking like the old club card with lines missing or in the wrong place, discovered only when the coaches hand them to the members they were made for.

deliverables.name: Anvil and Oak mark, recovered as placeable scalable artwork
deliverables.spec: The studio mark recovered from a photograph of painted brick as artwork that scales, carries no plate behind it, and holds all three of its elements, delivered with whatever small-size variant the reproduction sizes turn out to require and a stated smallest safe size. It is placed identically on the poster, the deck, the tier card, the spotlight canvases and the athlete card, so the deliverable is one mark used consistently rather than several drawings of the same thing.

deliverables.name: Member-athlete portrait set, sixteen frames to one studio look plus the spotlight formats
deliverables.spec: Sixteen portraits shot across three evenings at three colour temperatures brought to one temperature, one black point and one degree of modelling, judged against the dark ground they will sit on, then derived into the square, four by five and tall formats under one crop logic. Every output at or below its source dimensions, with a per-athlete parameter log, a note of which frames had their edges extended and why, and any athlete who could not be brought to the set named.

deliverables.name: Opening roster athlete card run, press cards plus per-athlete files and proofs
deliverables.spec: One 5 by 7 card per rostered athlete who is in, card count equal to the reconciled roster, binding name, three figures on a single stated basis, level, coach and quote verbatim. Accompanied by one single-card file per athlete, named to the roster and identity-verified by opening it, and by proofs rendered at true print resolution from the merged document. why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns a handsome dark gym poster with a redrawn anvil on it. IDENTITY: the mark is a specific hand-painted sign on this studio's own wall and the whole brief is that it must be recovered rather than reinterpreted, and the athletes are named members whose faces and numbers appear on cards they will keep. SPEC: the run is one 5 by 7 card per rostered athlete binding named fields verbatim on one stated basis, plus per-athlete single files each containing the athlete they claim and proofs at true print resolution, alongside three named social formats derived without adding pixels. EDITABILITY: the poster, the deck and the tier card are defined by being editable, because the schedule changes with the season and the prices change with it. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: does this trace still hold at card-footer size on the dark ground, does this extended edge match the set, does this document expose anything that can carry a photograph.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments global and masked, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, select_subject, invert_selection, fill_area, crop_to_bounds, vectorize, generative_expand and crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and detection_confidence are all verified headless, and the extract-and-reuse chain from a photographed printed mark through to native editable vector inside an exported document is verified end to end. The mark checkpoint rests on documented facts rather than invention: vectorize takes no options at all so all tuning must happen in the raster prep, its output has no viewBox and always carries a full-canvas background rectangle as path zero, selection on a compound mark is documented as silently dropping elements, and remove_background is documented as unable to punch an enclosed interior hole. The extension checkpoint rests on generative_expand being the single sanctioned generative call, documented as adding pixels only at the edges with content that is AI generated, while crop_and_resize is documented as interpolating up to a hard 2x cap reported only in the tradeoffs array, which is what makes the no-enlargement bar checkable rather than asserted. MERGE SPINE: building a merge template from a bare press PDF end to end headlessly is verified, one record per page is confirmed for the PDF branch, per-record files are confirmed in correct order by two routes, true 300 DPI at trim is confirmed through the render tool, the merge's own resolution parameter is documented as silently ignored so proofs must be rendered from the merged document, multi-record raster URL order is documented as unreliable so identity must be established by opening files, frame granularity from a PDF is documented as not under the agent's control with a verified case collapsing to one text frame and zero graphic frames, and the mapping readout's textContent is documented as lossy in a way the validator blesses. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export, true mm print canvases at 96 dpi, real tables with per-cell strokes, inline SVG as native editable vector, and a genuine editable document are verified; the rendition shows page one only so verification splits between the rendition and the returned markup; the payload is routed by uploaded URL because inlined portraits pass the 70 KB threshold immediately. FONTS, STOCK and BOARDS follow the verified chains, with short queries, orientation never passed, and the twelve-per-call board cap with a partial success read as partial. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no fill_text, no animate_design, no create_firefly_board, no replace_image, no download_design, no upscaling, no object removal, no compositing, no OCR, no variable QR, no bleed or press-preset gate, no batch above 20.

engagement_title: Apexguard Surface Systems dealer rollout: recover the drafted master mark as real artwork, bring a two-session install bay to one look, rebuild the printer's roll label into a live merge, and hand the dealer channel one editable set
vertical: Automotive, Industrial and Agriculture: paint protection film, window tint and ceramic coating supplied to dealer groups and to independent installers who buy film by the roll (Charlotte, North Carolina)
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork rebrand brief from a client who 'supplies paint protection film (PPF), window tint, and related products' and is 'rebranding and need a designer to deliver a complete logo and identity system that works on digital channels and physical packaging (boxes, labels, stickers)', with the visual direction stated as 'Premium, modern, performance-automotive. Minimalist and confident. Not flashy, not factory-catalog, not tuner.', a required 'strong master + sub-brand naming' structure, and an explicit exclusion of 'mascots, vintage badges, heavy gradients.' Co-anchor: the Upwork logo-vectorization and brand-identity-kit brief from a client whose logo existed only as a low-resolution raster and who needed print-ready vector artwork plus print and apparel variations and a colour and type reference. Laundered to the fictional Apexguard Surface Systems; no real company, person, product or trademark appears, the mark is original geometry recovered from the client's own supplied artwork, and no craft-software brand name appears in any task-facing field. The ledger records this slot as previously sitting almost entirely on one authoring surface. LAYOUT-17 restores the commission both clients actually posted: the identity has to be recovered as usable artwork, and the point of recovering it is that a dealer deck, a counter poster, an installer social set and a printed roll label all carry it and all have to agree.
client_one_liner: A master mark we only have as a picture, three tiers that have to read as one family, a bay we shot on two different days, and a printer's roll label we cannot open, all due before the dealer meetings.
client_brief:
Apexguard Surface Systems, dealer rollout.

We supply paint protection film, window tint and ceramic coating. We sell two ways: through dealer groups who resell our installs, and direct to independent installers who buy film by the roll. We are rebranding and we want the whole rollout in one designer's hands.

We had a master mark drafted for us. What we actually hold is a picture of it and the shop card we had printed from that draft. We need it back as real artwork we can put anywhere, from the top of a dealer deck down to the end of a film box, and we need the three tier marks alongside it so the family reads as one family rather than three logos.

Our own photography is the next problem. We shoot in our own bay. Some of it happened on a Saturday and the rest later in the week, and it does not hang together. Clear film has to still look clear and tinted glass has to still look like tint, because that is what the customer is buying.

Then the pieces. A deck we take into dealer groups. A spec poster for the counter at the installer shops. A set for the installers' own feeds, at the three shapes they post at. A tier comparison our sales people can point at, because the question in every meeting is what the difference between the three tiers actually is. A page that shows the mark family and how to use it. And the roll labels: our printer built those last year off our system, one label per roll, we have their file and nothing else, and this year's widths and warranty wording have to go through it without the label changing how it looks.

Premium, modern, performance automotive. Minimalist and confident. Not flashy, not factory catalog, not tuner. No mascots, no vintage badges, no heavy gradients. A full install runs 1,800 to 6,000 dollars on a car worth sixty thousand, so it has to look like that.

Send it all back as one file we can edit ourselves, and if anything in our data looks wrong to you, say so before it prints.
price_band_and_audience: Full vehicle paint protection film installs 1,800 to 6,000 dollars; tint packages 400 to 1,200 dollars; film sold by the roll to installers at 900 to 4,200 dollars a roll. Two audiences: dealer group principals and fixed operations managers, 35 to 55, deciding whether to put Apexguard on their reconditioning line, and independent installer owners, 28 to 50, who buy film by the roll and post their own work. The vehicle owner behind both is 30 to 55 and protecting a 60,000 dollar car. The band is load-bearing. At this tier the correct artefact is precise and near technical: confident spacing, one restrained accent against a deep neutral, film performance stated as a plain table rather than as a burst, photography that is clean and even rather than dramatic. Push it toward discount tint shop grammar, starbursts, chrome bevels, percentage flashes, three exclamation colours, and a dealer principal reads it as a two hundred dollar tint job and stops believing the ten year warranty printed beside it, which is the exact failure the client describes when they say not factory catalog and not tuner. Push it the other way into moody cinematic car culture and it reads as an enthusiast page rather than a supplier a dealer group can put on its reconditioning line. A real posted job of this shape runs 2,200 to 4,500 dollars fixed, or 50 to 85 dollars an hour across 40 to 60 hours.

assets_supplied.name: master_mark_draft/ (mark_draft_2400.png plus shopcard_photo.jpg)
assets_supplied.kind: The drafted master mark supplied only as a flat 2400 px raster on a light ground, plus a phone photograph of the installer shop card that was printed from an earlier round of the same draft.
assets_supplied.visible_description: 'The mark as it was drafted for us, and the card we had printed off it. That is everything we have. No working file.'
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two faults, neither stated. The draft carries a hairline keyline around the shield and a narrow counter inside the inner chevron that survive a trace at canvas size and stop being holes at the sizes this mark actually gets used at, and nothing in the traced artwork declares that. The photographed shop card is an earlier revision whose chevron angle and wordmark tracking do not match the 2400 px file, so recovering the mark from whichever source is easier to select produces artwork that will not sit with the rest of the rollout.

assets_supplied.name: bay_frames/ (10 frames, 4600 x 3070)
assets_supplied.kind: In-house photography shot in the company's own install bay: film rolls on the rack, a car mid wrap, hood edge and door shut line close ups, tinted glass, a squeegee pull.
assets_supplied.visible_description: 'Our own bay, our own camera. Some of it on the Saturday, the rest later that week. It does not hang together.'
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The bay runs sodium overheads at one end and LED work lamps at the other, and the two sessions were shot under different mixes, so half the range carries a green cast that reads as a film tint difference rather than as a lighting difference. Separately, the matte black film rolls sit on a dark grey steel rack at almost the same value, so an isolation of a roll reports success and quietly takes a bite out of the roll's own edge where the two meet.

assets_supplied.name: rolllabel_2025_PRINT.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The print shop's flat press PDF of last season's film roll box end label, 4 by 6 inches, one SKU per label, fonts embedded, produced from the company's own system through a full print engine. Carries the tier name, a width and length line, a six row performance block, a warranty statement and a small mark.
assets_supplied.visible_description: 'What the printer sent us last year. Nobody here knows how it was built. Keep it looking exactly like this and put this year's widths and wording through it.'
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two facts nobody at Apexguard could tell you. The label was set as one continuous flowing block, so the tier name, the width line, the performance rows and the warranty statement all convert into a single story with no per field frames to map, and everything has to be driven by ordered offsets inside that one story. And the warranty block sits in a fixed measure frame sized to last season's shorter wording: a longer statement does not spill and does not flag, it simply stops rendering where the frame ends, and every response in the chain still reports success.

Tier names carry trailing spaces from the spreadsheet that exported them, the image column holds full local paths without the prefix the merge's own image contract requires, and three warranty statements rewritten by the legal reviewer run roughly four times the length of the others.

acceptance_bar: The master mark comes back as artwork that scales, sits clean and transparent on any ground including our deep neutral, and holds together at the smallest place we actually use it. If there is a size below which it must not be used, say so and give us the version that covers it.
The three tier marks read as one family with the master. A dealer looking at all four should see one brand, not three logos.
Only one revision of the mark exists in the delivered work. Every piece carries the same artwork.
All ten bay frames read as one bay on one day, judged with them laid out together rather than one at a time. Clear film still reads as clear and tinted glass still reads as tint.
Isolated film rolls are cut on their own edge, with nothing bitten out of the roll and nothing of the rack left attached.
No delivered file is larger than the frame it came from, and the note lists every picture that was resized and by how much.

Roll labels: exactly one label per live SKU, every field the 2025 label carried present on every label, every value bound verbatim from our export, and the mark on each label the delivered artwork rather than last year's.
Nothing in our export may be shortened, reworded or abbreviated to make it fit. Anything that will not fit inside the label as it stands, tell us in writing before it goes to the printer.
The press file renders at real print resolution at label trim, and there is one label file per SKU named to the SKU code, containing the SKU its name claims.

The dealer deck, the counter poster, the installer social set, the tier comparison and the mark family page come back as one working file we can edit ourselves, each at its own size, plus the source it was built from.
In that file the words are live text, the tier comparison is a real table and the marks are real artwork we can recolour, not pictures of a page.
One type system across all of it, and the note names per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the weight actually used.
Nothing flashy: no mascot, no vintage badge, no heavy gradient, no burst.

A written note: what was done to each picture and why it differs from its neighbours, which mark source you used and why, anything in our export you questioned and what you did about it, and anything the label could not carry.

trajectory.judgement: Two pictures of what the client calls the same mark are not the same mark, and choosing between them is a decision about what the whole rollout will carry. The frames also have to be read for value collision before anything is derived from them, since the client describes only a lighting problem.
trajectory.produces: A per asset triage note covering mark revision, session, level and subject to ground separation.

trajectory.action: Level the frames that are off level.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes and eats edge pixels, so it precedes every crop decision rather than following one.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed.

trajectory.action: Fix one neutral from the better lit session and correct each frame toward it with its own parameter set, recording what was dialled per frame.
trajectory.judgement: One destination held across ten frames rather than ten locally pleasing pictures. The frames shot under the other lamp mix need a materially different correction to arrive at the same neutral, and a single batched call would apply one identical set and ship half the bay green.
trajectory.produces: Ten graded masters at source scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Masked corrections so clear film still reads as clear and tinted glass still reads as tint rather than as a grey wash, and the black rolls keep their material without going flat.
trajectory.judgement: This is the client's commercial requirement rather than a cosmetic one, because clarity and tint level are what is being sold. Prompt wording is the whole gate, and a material selection on a dark roll lying on a dark rack can leak into the rack, which has to be read as leakage rather than accepted because the call succeeded.
trajectory.produces: Frames whose film and glass behaviour survives the grade, with the masked parameters recorded.

trajectory.action: Recover the master mark from the chosen source: an ink level selection naming the mark's own visual properties rather than the sheet it sits on, invert, crop to the mask's own bounds, trace to SVG, then inject a viewBox and strip the opaque full canvas path the trace always emits.
trajectory.judgement: Naming the substrate pulls the selection to the substrate and every downstream step then operates on a rectangle. The trace ships with no viewBox and an opaque background rectangle, and neither is announced, so an untouched trace is a white box on the deck's deep neutral.
trajectory.produces: A scalable transparent master mark as SVG artwork.

trajectory.action: Produce the three tier colourways from the one recovered plate using the same mask with different parameters, and record the parameters dialled per tier.
trajectory.judgement: The family has to be one piece of artwork carrying three treatments, because that is what makes the tiers read as a family. Hue movement here is an adjacent move, not a jump to a named colour, so the tier separation has to be designed within what the range actually reaches.
trajectory.produces: Three tier colourways of the master mark plus the per tier parameter record.

trajectory.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging and Adobe Express
trajectory.action: Place the master mark and the smallest tier lockup at their true reproduction sizes on the real grounds they will sit on, the deck's deep neutral and the roll label's box end, and look at them there.
trajectory.judgement: Artwork is judged where it is used, at the size it is used, on the ground it is used on. A mark inspected at canvas size on white has not been inspected.
trajectory.produces: Placement proofs of the mark and the smallest lockup at true size on the real grounds.

trajectory.action: Cut the film roll and hood edge isolations onto the studio ground for the poster and the social set, routing per frame, and check each cut edge against its source.
trajectory.judgement: A one call knockout is right for a roll standing clear of the rack and wrong where roll and rack share value, and the wrong route returns a plausible cutout with the roll's own edge bitten away. The route is a per frame decision made by looking at the frame.
trajectory.produces: Isolations on the studio ground with the route recorded per frame.

trajectory.surface: Data preparation and Creative Cloud storage
trajectory.action: Reconcile the stock export against the roll rack photography and the tier direction, normalise it into a merge shaped file with the image column in the form the merge contract requires and bare filenames in the cells, upload the label artwork and build the image map.
trajectory.judgement: Real data preparation work: superseded rows the system still emits, tier names carrying spreadsheet whitespace, and an image column that does not satisfy the contract. The agent decides which of those are its call and which are the client's, and how to say so.
trajectory.produces: The merge data file, uploaded label artwork, the image map, and a first list of export questions.

trajectory.action: Convert the 2025 label to a native document, export IDML, unzip it, and read the true frame inventory and the true story text reconstructed by concatenating the content runs.
trajectory.judgement: The mapping strategy is decided by what the client's own system happened to produce rather than by the plan, and the readout a tool hands you is not automatically the same string as the document's own.
trajectory.produces: The converted document, its IDML, a frame inventory with real ids and bounds, and the reconstructed story text.

trajectory.action: Author the mapping covering every label field plus the mark, ordering any rows that share a uid against the original text, and pass it through the validator.
trajectory.judgement: Choosing the right action for the granularity that actually came back, computing offsets from a source of truth chosen deliberately, and passing the whole mapping across as one stringified object with integer page item ids.
trajectory.produces: A validated mapping covering the label fields and the mark frame.

trajectory.action: Prepare the merge template, then export IDML from the result, unzip it and grep the story for every placeholder the mapping claimed to create.
trajectory.judgement: Not accepting a success message as evidence. Nothing instructs this and nothing warns if it is skipped, and it is the only place the mapping's real yield is visible before any label exists.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholder inventory has been independently confirmed.

trajectory.action: Merge to a native document with the mark bound, render the press file and 300 ppi proofs at label trim, produce per SKU labels named to the SKU code, and read every rendered label against its export row at true trim rather than at proof scale.
trajectory.judgement: Merging straight to raster silently drops to screen resolution whatever is asked for, and merging straight to a press file forfeits the per record branch, so the route is chosen deliberately. Naming twelve labels by the order they came back is the fast wrong answer and it is the one an installer discovers on a rack.
trajectory.produces: The press label file, 300 ppi proofs, per SKU identity verified labels, and a line by line reconciliation at true trim.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for one vehicle or road context frame, filter to photography, exclude generative results, license and download at full resolution, then grade it toward the house neutral and judge it beside the bay frames.
trajectory.judgement: A context frame at this band has to be restrained and plausible rather than dramatic. A night lit hero car is the wrong register for a supplier a dealer group is being asked to put on its reconditioning line.
trajectory.produces: One licensed camera scale context frame, graded, judged in or out.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, read the real numeric weights from the style inventories, launder every name, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own and has to read premium and near technical rather than aftermarket. Numeric weight cannot be inferred from a style name, a display cut is reached by its own slug, and one bad name kills the whole kit including the valid faces beside it.
trajectory.produces: One kit with family, foundry or designer and the actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML holding the six dealer deck roots, the A1 counter poster at true physical dimensions, the three installer social canvases, the tier comparison as a real table and the mark family basis page carrying the recovered artwork as inline vector, each root declaring its own canvas size, every photograph base64 inlined, family and weight declared on every text element. Upload by the allowed host route, run the readiness check, export, then verify the first canvas through its rendition and every other canvas through the returned markup.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition preview shows only the first canvas, so the export is unverified until the markup is read canvas by canvas. The design decisions, how much of the A1 is table and how much is photograph, whether the deck opens on the mark or on the warranty, are the actual work.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document holding every canvas, its durable source HTML, and a per canvas markup audit.

trajectory.action: Create the approval board with the recovered mark family, the graded bay and the licensed frame, within the placement cap and re-sending only entries named as failed, then write the handover.
trajectory.judgement: What to escalate versus what to fix silently. The note has to let the next freelancer rebuild the label from the same PDF without repeating the archaeology, and it has to name the warranty wording that will not fit and the export rows that were excluded, before a printer sees the file.
trajectory.produces: A persistent approval board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered mark survives at the sizes it is actually used at, on the grounds it is actually used on. The trace is clean and correct at canvas size on white: the shield keyline is a hairline, the inner chevron counter is a hole, the tier lockup's small type is separated. Placed at its true reproduction size on the deck's deep neutral and at box end size on the roll label, the counter closes into a solid, the keyline either disappears or merges with the shield edge, and the tier word thickens into a bar. Nothing in the trace, the artwork or any response reports this, because at the moment of tracing the artwork is genuinely correct. It becomes wrong only in the relationship between this particular drafted geometry, this particular reproduction size and this particular ground, none of which exist as a number anywhere.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it and care cannot either: a trace that is faithful to the draft is the correct output of the tracing step, and the tool takes no options that would change the result, so there is no first time to get right. Nothing states it, because the brief asks for artwork that holds at the smallest place it is used, which is an ordinary client requirement rather than a warning, and no asset description mentions the keyline or the counter. And the response is not a re-run: the mark has to be re-derived from a differently prepared raster, a minimum size rule has to be written that did not previously exist, and a small size variant has to be designed and then adopted across the label, the social set and the basis page.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-derive the mark from a mask prepared differently at the raster stage, since the trace itself has no lever, and judge the result again at true size on the deep neutral rather than at canvas size. Where the geometry still will not hold at label size, author a simplified small size variant, write the minimum size rule and the variant into the mark family basis page, and go back through the label mapping and the social set so both carry the variant they should be carrying rather than the master.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A rollout in which the mark is a legible piece of artwork in the deck and a dark blob on every film roll box in every installer shop, delivered to a client whose entire brief was an identity that works on digital channels and on physical packaging.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printer's label actually exposes, and then whether the merged labels carry what the export says. The label was set as one continuous flowing block, so tier name, width line, performance rows and warranty statement all convert into a single story with no per field frames, and the mapping has to be driven entirely by ordered offsets. The second fact only arrives at trim: the warranty block sits in a fixed measure frame sized to last season's shorter wording, so the three longer statements do not spill, do not reflow and do not raise an overset flag anywhere. The text simply stops at the frame edge, mid sentence, on those three labels, and the merge response, the render response and the label at proof scale all look correct.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Granularity is not a parameter, is not reported before conversion and has no read ahead, so the only route to it is to convert, export and read. The truncation is worse: a fixed frame that stops rendering produces no error, no warning and no visual alarm at proof scale, so an agent that maps carefully, validates cleanly and renders successfully still ships three wrong labels. It is not a propagation re-run either, because the answer is not to re-merge: it is to decide, with the client, what happens to wording that cannot be shortened inside a frame that cannot be resized.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Read every rendered label at true trim rather than at proof scale, against its export row, word by word through the warranty statement. Confirm the frame measure from the document rather than from the rendered page, establish which statements exceed it, and escalate in writing before the press file is committed, since the acceptance bar forbids shortening or rewording anything to make it fit. Re-plan the mark binding at the same time if the placement proof from the earlier checkpoint changed which variant the label should carry.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Twelve film roll labels printed and shipped in which three carry a warranty statement that stops mid sentence, sold to installers who resell that warranty to a vehicle owner, with every tool in the chain having reported success and the proof having looked right.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the importer actually did with the three constructs the rollout depends on: the tier comparison carried in as a real table with per cell strokes, the recovered mark family carried in as inline vector, and the installer social canvases carried in at shapes different from the deck. None of those can be confirmed by any channel other than reading the markup the import returns, and every drop this importer performs comes back as an unqualified success. The multi canvas shape compounds it, because the visual preview resolves only the first canvas, so whatever happened on the poster, the social set and the basis page is reported by the returned markup and by nothing else.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: How this importer normalises a given construct is not documented anywhere the agent can read ahead, is not a parameter, and is not signalled by the response status, so authoring more carefully does not tell you what happened. Nothing states it: the brief asks for live text, a real table and artwork that can be recoloured, which is the client's requirement for a file they can edit, and names no importer and no failure. And the response is not a re-run, because a construct that did not survive has to be re-authored in a different form, and the layout around it changes with it.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Parse the returned markup per canvas, not only the first, and check that every photograph resolved to real image data rather than the importer's placeholder, that the mark arrived as path shapes rather than one flattened element, that the comparison arrived as real cells rather than a stack of loose text, that every text element carries the intended face and the intended numeric weight rather than a silent fallback, and that no element resolves past its declared canvas width. Re-author whichever constructs did not survive, re-upload, re-run the readiness check, re-export, and inspect again rather than assuming the second export took.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A dealer deck and counter poster handed over as the client's editable file in which the tier comparison is a heap of loose text and the mark family page is empty geometry, discovered by a sales manager in front of a dealer group because the only canvas anyone looked at was the first one.

deliverables.name: Apexguard mark family: master mark plus three tier marks
deliverables.spec: The drafted master recovered from a flat raster as scalable transparent vector artwork with a real viewBox and no residual opaque background path, plus three tier treatments produced from the same recovered plate so the family is one artwork rather than three drawings. Delivered with a stated minimum size and, where the geometry will not hold below it, the small size variant that does, and with the record of which supplied source was used and why the other was rejected.

deliverables.name: Apexguard bay photography, ten frames at one look
deliverables.spec: Ten in-house frames shot under two different lighting mixes brought to one neutral, judged as a set rather than one at a time, with clear film still reading as clear and tinted glass still reading as tint. Plus one licensed context frame graded into the same neutral. Every output at or below its source pixel dimensions, with a per frame parameter log, one line per frame on why it differs from its neighbours, and every crop or resize tradeoff the tools reported transcribed.

deliverables.name: Roll and hood edge isolations on the studio ground
deliverables.spec: Film rolls and hood edge details isolated onto the agreed studio ground for the poster and the social set, cut on the product's own edge with nothing bitten away where roll and rack sit at the same value and nothing of the rack left attached. Isolation route recorded per frame, because a roll standing clear of the rack and a roll against it cannot be produced the same way.

deliverables.name: Apexguard 2027 roll labels: press file plus per SKU named labels
deliverables.spec: Four by six inch box end labels, one label per live SKU in export order, rendered at 300 ppi at trim. Every label binds tier, width, roll length, the six performance parameters, the warranty statement and the dealer price verbatim from the stock export, plus the delivered mark artwork rather than last year's. Accompanied by one single label file per SKU named to the SKU code and identity verified by opening it, and by 300 ppi proofs. Produced by reverse engineering the printer's flat PDF into a live merge template, handed back with the record of how it was derived.

deliverables.name: Dealer and installer set: deck, A1 counter poster, social set, tier comparison, mark family page
deliverables.spec: One native editable document holding the six root dealer deck, an A1 counter poster at true physical dimensions, three installer social canvases at their own shapes, the tier comparison as a genuine table with real cells, and the mark family basis page carrying the recovered artwork as live vector. Live editable text throughout in one licensed type system, every photograph carried as embedded image data. Delivered with the self contained source it was authored from, so prices and tier wording can change without a re-commission and the design survives the document's own retention.

deliverables.name: Handover note and approval board
deliverables.spec: A written note recording which mark source was used and why the other was rejected, the minimum size rule and the variant that covers it, per frame what was applied and why it differs from its neighbours, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and actual numeric weight, the explicit statement that no chosen face can reach the printed label because there is no way to put a font on that surface, what the label conversion exposed and the mapping decisions taken against it, every export row questioned and its resolution, the warranty wording that will not fit inside the label as it stands, and every resize any tool reported. Paired with a persistent approval board carrying the mark family, the graded bay and the licensed frame with nothing silently dropped.

verifiers_auto.how: Confirm the rendered press file has exactly 12 pages, one per live SKU in export order (the 14 export rows minus the 2 rows carrying a withdrawn_date, AG-G-60 and AG-GP-60), and confirm each rendered page raster measures exactly 1200 x 1800 px (4 x 6 in portrait at 300 ppi).

verifiers_auto.text: The delivered master mark is a transparent scalable file with a real viewBox and no full canvas opaque path, and every collateral piece carries the same revision.

verifiers_auto.text: No delivered file exceeds its source frame on either axis and no crop or background response carried an upscale or downscale entry that went unreported.
verifiers_auto.how: For every delivered raster confirm its pixel dimensions do not exceed its source on either axis (each bay frame and every isolation derived from it at or below 4600 x 3070 px, the recovered mark raster at or below 2400 x 2400 px, the stock context frame at or below its licensed source), and confirm every crop_and_resize / remove_background call's metadata.tradeoffs array (any upscale or downscale entry) is transcribed in the handover's resize list with matching direction and factor.

verifiers_auto.text: The exported document holds the deck roots, the A1 poster at true physical dimensions and three distinct social canvas shapes, with every photograph resolved to real image data, the mark present as path shapes and the tier comparison present as real table cells.
verifiers_auto.how: From the export response confirm the document holds the 6 dealer-deck roots, the A1 counter poster whose canvas is 594 x 841 mm (approximately 2245 x 3179 px at 96 dpi), and 3 social canvases at 3 distinct shapes; then parse each canvas's returned HzHTML markup and confirm that no photograph resolved to the importer's empty-box placeholder (every image carries real inline base64 or asset image data), the mark is present as path-type shapes rather than one flattened element, the tier comparison is present as real table cells with per-cell structure rather than a stack of loose text, and no element resolves to an x-position or width past its declared canvas width.

verifiers_auto.text: One label file exists per live SKU, each named to a SKU code, each containing the SKU its name claims.
verifiers_auto.how: Confirm there are exactly 12 single-label files, one named to each of the 12 live SKU codes (AG-G-24, AG-G-30, AG-G-36, AG-G-48, AG-GP-24, AG-GP-30, AG-GP-36, AG-GP-48, AG-GE-30, AG-GE-36, AG-GE-48, AG-GE-60), read the SKU/reference code printed inside each file and confirm it matches that file's own name rather than its position in the returned list, and confirm the two withdrawn widths (AG-G-60, AG-GP-60) produce no label file.

verifiers_auto.text: The approval board carries the full rollout set for sign-off with nothing silently dropped: the four mark-family marks, the ten graded bay frames and the one licensed context frame.
