decision_gates: Which deliverables go to the merge surface and which to authored canvases, given that the family wants the printed pieces to match 2019 and the book to stay editable.
Whether damage sits inside the picture or in the margin, and therefore whether a crop is a lawful remedy or a placement decision is the only honest answer.
What to do with the four files that are photographs of framed prints rather than scans, carrying reflection and keystone that no tool here removes.
How far to carry the 1968 run toward the house neutral before the correction stops being a correction, and what the deliberate alternative is if it will not come.
Whether the postcard reverses are treated as pictures or as documents, and how legibility is bought without turning cream card grey.
Which plates the 1200 px scans can carry, and what the book grid gives up because of it.
Which guest list rows collapse onto one card, which is a family convention rather than a data rule, and how to say so rather than deciding silently.
What to do about a relationship line that will not fit, when shortening the sister's words is not the agent's call to make.
Whether to trust the mapping tool's readout of the funeral home's own text or to reconstruct the story independently from the exported document.
Whether a success message counts as verification, when nothing instructs the agent to re-export the prepared template and search for its own placeholders.
How the heritage feel is built, given that the obvious means do not survive the import and the surviving means live one surface away.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged by mourners aged 45 to 75 reading a printed page at a service.
Whether a licensed cover frame belongs on this book at all, or whether the name alone on a plain ground is the more honest cover.
why_not_vlm: Paste this brief and this shoebox into a frontier image model and it returns beautiful restored photographs. IDENTITY: these are Walter Fernwood's actual family, his father's actual hand on the back of an actual postcard, and a regenerated face or a rebuilt torn corner is a fabrication of a dead man's life presented to the people who are burying him. The client says it outright: do not invent anything that is not in the photographs. SPEC: the family needs one A6 keepsake card per household bound to the sister's own words in full at trim, matching a 2019 press file so the two pieces sit together on a shelf, plus an A4 framed page at true print resolution with the subject whole. EDITABILITY: the book is defined by being editable, because captions change until the day before the service and there is no time and no money for a redo. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality: did this placeholder get created, does this line reach the end of the sister's sentence at trim, did this era actually arrive beside the others, did the page that cannot be previewed survive the import.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface, and the commission is scoped so that nothing depends on the heal, clone, inpaint, sharpen or object removal the connector does not have. MERGE SPINE: building a merge template from a bare press PDF end to end headlessly is verified (convert to native, export interchange, generate mapping, prepare template, with every field confirmed present by unzipping the round trip). One record per page is confirmed for the PDF branch, single record output by recordRange is confirmed, per row image binding through an at prefixed column plus an image map keyed to bare filenames is confirmed visually, and true 300 DPI at trim is confirmed through the render tool while the merge tool's own resolution parameter is confirmed to be silently ignored. The card checkpoint rests on documented frame behaviour from a converted press PDF, whose frame granularity, bounds and applied typography are properties of the source document that no tool reports in advance, and on the verified fact that convenience readouts of story text are lossy so offsets must be reconstructed from the exported interchange file. IMAGING: straighten, adjustments masked and unmasked, dark and light portion recovery, temperature, HSL within its verified moderate range, auto tone, monochromatic tint, grain, select by prompt with returnBbox, invert, fill area, crop to bounds and crop and resize with its tradeoffs are all verified headless. The era checkpoint rests on the verified finding that HSL range holds at moderate and that a near complementary swing is out of reach, so a shifted emulsion genuinely may not converge. EXPRESS: multi page and mixed canvas in one export, true absolute unit canvases, rich inline runs surviving inside one text frame, and a genuinely editable document are verified; the checkpoint on the plate construct rests on four separately verified silent drops, mix-blend-mode dropped to an opaque shape, filter blur dropped to a hard edge, multi layer box-shadow hard truncated to layer one, and the rendition preview returning PAGE 1 ONLY so later pages are knowable from the returned markup alone. FONTS: recommend once per role, mandatory style inventory for the non standard numeric weight, display cuts reached by slug rather than weight, name laundering before the kit, and the returned slug in the CSS, all verified. STOCK and BOARDS: short queries, contentType only and orientation never passed, licence and full resolution download verified, board creation and placement verified with a twelve per call cap where 201 means partial. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no upscaling, no generative fill or object removal, no compositing, no OCR (the family supplies its own transcriptions), no bleed or press preset gate, no variable QR, no fill_text, no animate_design, no batch above 20.

engagement_title: Harborline Realty weekly listing sheet run: rebuild the retired printer's sheet into a live template, bring eleven mixed source heroes to two tier targets, and hand back the week's book, the per property files and an open house set the office edits itself
vertical: Residential real estate, eight agent coastal brokerage running a mixed book from starter homes to point estates (mid coast Maine)
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork posting quoted in the ledger's grounding_note, whose client was 'seeking a talented designer to create a real estate flyer for a new listing' that 'should be visually appealing and effectively communicate the property's features and benefits'. Laundered to the fictional Harborline Realty (principal Dana Marlow, listing agent Theo Vane); no real brokerage, agent, portal or trademark is named. The ledger conceded that the raw brief implies a from scratch flyer layout, which the connector cannot compose, and that the task as first carved sat on one surface. The fuller commission that brokerage actually has is the one it runs every Monday: the whole active book as a repeatable record per page run, rebuilt out of a press file left behind by a retired printer, fed by photography arriving from two sources at two price tiers, paired with an open house set the office must be able to change itself when a price moves.
client_one_liner: We print a sheet for every active listing every Monday, our printer retired with the only working file, and the book runs from a three hundred and twenty thousand dollar starter to a four and a half million place on the point.
client_brief:
Harborline Realty, weekly sheet run

We are an eight agent office on the mid coast. Every Monday we print a listing sheet for each active property, one page per house, and the agents carry them to open houses and appointments all week. Right now the sheets get made one at a time in a program nobody here can drive properly, and last week two went out with January's prices on them.

Eleven properties are active this week. The book runs from a starter house at three twenty on a corner lot to a four and a half million place out on the point, and they cannot all look the same. The point house sells to people who walk out if it looks like a supermarket flyer. The starter house sells to people who need the price and the bed count to reach them from across the room. You are the designer, so make that difference read.

Our printer retired in the spring. All we have is the file she sent to press last year. The sheet itself is right. We just need to be able to fill it every Monday without her. We want the whole week as one file for the print shop, a separate file per property so an agent can reprint one sheet without touching the rest, and a full quality proof of the point house for me before anything runs.

The photographs come in as they come in. Some are ours off a phone at noon, some are from the photographer we hire for the expensive listings. They have to look like they came from one office.

We also post the week's open houses. That has to be something we can edit ourselves, because prices move on Thursdays and I am not paying twice.

The mark on the sheets is the one painted on our office window. That window is the only place it still exists. Whatever goes on the posts has to be that mark, not something close to it.

Tell us what you changed and what you had to ask about.
price_band_and_audience: One brokerage, two audiences in one weekly run. The point estate at 4.5 million is bought by buyers over fifty with liquid capital who read restraint as credibility: one photograph, deep margins, quiet type, a price set small. The starter at 320 thousand is bought by first time buyers under thirty five who need price, beds and the open house time to land instantly: brighter, denser, price forward. The band is load bearing because a single blanket treatment fails in both directions at once. Style the whole book like the estate and the starter sheets look empty and evasive; style it like the starter and the estate reads as volume agency work in front of a vendor paying a six figure commission. A weekly production retainer of this shape posts at 700 to 1,600 dollars a month.

brand_identity.sector: Independent residential brokerage selling coastal Maine homes, from corner lot starters to waterfront point estates, to local and out of state buyers.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2009, harbour front office on the mid coast of Maine, eight agents under principal Dana Marlow.
brand_identity.about: Harborline is a small owner run brokerage that lists the whole mid coast book, a three hundred and twenty thousand dollar starter one week and a waterfront estate the next. It runs on repeat referrals and reputation in town, and prints a fresh listing sheet for every active property each Monday. Dana Marlow built it to feel like the place it sells, not a national franchise.
brand_identity.audience: Two buyers in one weekly run: estate buyers over fifty with liquid capital who read restraint as credibility, and first time buyers under thirty five who need price, bed count and open house time to land at a glance.
brand_identity.price_positioning: One brokerage spanning a 320 thousand dollar starter to a 4.5 million dollar point estate; the sheet has to flex between the two without either register looking wrong. Weekly production retainer, roughly 700 to 1,600 dollars a month.
brand_identity.typography: A quiet transitional serif for headlines and prices, an even colour that reads calm on the estate sheets. A clean humanist sans for the beds, baths and square feet strip and the agent line. Estate sheets lean on space and small type; starter sheets carry weight and size so the price reaches across a room.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, grounded, mid coast. We describe the house, not ourselves, and never oversell. Example line the brand would write: 'Corner lot, three beds, a short walk to the harbour. Open Sunday, one to three.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The original logo artwork was lost years ago. The only surviving version of the mark, a rope ring around a lighthouse with the letters H and R, is the one painted in cream on the office window. There are no brand guidelines or type specimen; the retired printer's last press file is the sole reference for the listing sheet.
brand_identity.values: Honesty about price and condition, and one consistent office look across every listing no matter who shot the photograph.

assets_supplied.name: listingsheet_2025_press.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The retired printer's flat press PDF of the office listing sheet, US Letter portrait, fonts embedded, produced from a real page layout so it converts cleanly. Carries an address line, a headline, a three line description, a beds and baths and square feet strip, a price, an agent line, a small reference code line, and one placed hero photograph.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The sheet our printer ran last year. It is the only file we have and she has retired."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two faults, neither announced. What the conversion exposes as editable structure is a property of how she built the 2025 document: the description, the beds and baths strip, the price and the small reference code arrive inside ONE continuous flow while the address and the agent line sit alone, and the mapping readout silently omits the reference code run while keeping its line break, so every offset past it is short by that run's length and the validator still returns VALID. Separately the hero frame's real bounds are close to square rather than the letterbox the printed sheet suggests, and its fitting is a centre anchored proportional fill that is exposed in no readout at all, so the frame re crops whatever image is bound into it from its own centre regardless of how that image was prepared.

assets_supplied.name: hero_selects/ (11 frames, 3600 to 4200 px long edge)
assets_supplied.kind: One chosen hero photograph per active property, arriving from two sources: four shot by the brokerage's hired photographer for the expensive listings, seven shot by agents on phones.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "One picture per house. Some ours, some the photographer's. They need to look like one office."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The two sources do not merely differ in quality, they differ in direction: the photographer's four are late afternoon, warm and deep with the interior lights carrying; the agents' seven are flat midday with a cold cast off the ocean and a lifted black point that reads clean alone and grey the moment it sits beside a photographer's frame. Two of the agent frames sit a degree or so off level and straightening them consumes exactly the edge margin any subsequent crop wants. One agent frame is a twilight exterior whose windows are clipped to paper white with no data behind them, so a highlight recovery there returns a file identical to the one it was given.

assets_supplied.name: weekly_active.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Monday export from the office system, one row per active property, with columns for address, headline, description, beds and baths and square feet, price, agent, reference code and a photo filename.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "This week's eleven. Straight out of the system."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three faults, none stated. One property went under contract on Thursday and the office manager has not pulled it, so the export carries a row that must not print. The point estate's row was typed by the listing agent rather than exported, so its address uses a different abbreviation convention, its price carries a currency symbol the other rows do not, and its description runs roughly three times longer than anything in the 2025 book the sheet was built around. One photo cell names a file that does not match any folder name because the agent renamed the frame after exporting.

assets_supplied.name: officesign_photo.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: A photograph of the brokerage's harbour front office window, the house mark painted on the glass in cream: a rope ring enclosing a lighthouse and the letters H and R.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "That window is the only place our mark still exists. We lost the artwork years ago."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The mark traces convincingly at the size the trace comes back, and the failure is entirely one of reproduction size: the rope ring is drawn as a repeating gap and twist, and the R carries a small enclosed counter, and neither of those is a property the trace controls. Vectorize takes no options whatsoever, so nothing about the trace can be tuned after the fact. Whether the gaps and the counter survive is decided by how many pixels the mark occupied in the raster that went in, and it can only be seen at the size the mark is actually used, on the ground it is actually used on.

assets_supplied.name: principal_note.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Half a page from Dana Marlow on how the office wants to sit against the two other agencies in town, and what she means when she says a sheet looks cheap.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "How we want to look on the point and how we want to look in town."

acceptance_bar: The book contains exactly one page per property that is genuinely active, no extra page and no missing page, and any row left out is named to us with the reason.
Every field the 2025 sheet carried is present on every page, including the small reference code, and nothing ends mid sentence at trim.

The estate tier and the starter tier are visibly different pieces of design at a glance, in photograph treatment, in type weight and in how much air the page carries, and both still read as the same office.

The eleven photographs read as one office: one black point per tier, one warmth per tier, one crop logic, and any frame that cannot be brought to its tier is named rather than shipped at eighty percent.
Every hero on the printed sheet still shows the whole house it is a picture of, judged on the rendered page at trim rather than on the file that was prepared.
No delivered image exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions and no crop tradeoff record carries an upscale entry.
Each per property file contains the property its filename claims, established by opening it rather than by the order the files came back.
The point estate proof is rendered at true print resolution at sheet trim, not at screen scale.
The mark on the open house set is our own mark, recovered, and it still reads as a rope ring with a lighthouse and two letters at the size it is actually used, on the ground it is used on.

The open house set comes back as a native editable document we can change a price in, with every photograph actually visible, the schedule as a real table, and every text element carrying its licensed face at that family's own weight.
A written note: what was applied to each photograph and why the tiers differ, the type system by role, every export row questioned and how it was resolved, and every resize any tool reported.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (global and masked), image_apply_auto_tone, image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_invert_selection, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading tradeoffs, detection_confidence, upscale_factor), image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Everything photographic, and the mark recovery. It levels the off level agent frames before any crop is locked, fixes TWO tier targets rather than one and walks each of the eleven to its own tier's target one call at a time, derives the sheet heroes at native scale while reading the tradeoff record on every call, and pulls the painted window mark to an ink level selection, inverts it, crops it to its own bbox and traces it. Vectorize accepts no options at all, so every lever for the trace lives in the raster preparation done here.

adobe_surfaces.surface: InDesign layout and data merge

A dead press file becomes a live merge template, the Monday export becomes a data source after reconciliation, and the run produces the printer's book, the per property files an agent reprints from, and the principal's proof. The true story text must be rebuilt from the exported interchange file rather than trusted from the convenience readout, and the placeholder inventory confirmed by round trip rather than by a success message.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview

Every photograph carried as embedded image data because a photograph left as a URL renders as an empty grey box, each root declaring its own canvas so a global override cannot collapse the set, and the payload routed by uploaded URL because three photographs pass the inline threshold at once.

The Boards half persists the Friday selects for the principal's sign off before the print run commits, placed within the twelve per call cap with a 201 read as partial success.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable goes to which surface.
trajectory.judgement: The sheet is record per page against a layout the office wants kept, so it belongs to the merge surface; the open house set must stay editable through Thursday price moves, which the merge surface structurally cannot give.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming a surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier.

trajectory.action: Upload the eleven heroes, the press PDF, the Monday export, the window photograph and the principal's note, holding every returned presigned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A manifest keyed by property and by role, because the same frame will exist in four states before the end.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by property and role.

trajectory.action: Preview all eleven heroes and triage them: which tier each belongs to, which are level, which carry a usable black point, and how much edge margin each has to spare.
trajectory.judgement: Two sources shot at two times of day are two different problems, and the tier a property belongs to is a design decision the export does not carry.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note: tier, source, tilt, cast, black point and edge margin.

trajectory.action: Straighten the off level agent frames before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes and eats the edge margin a later crop wants, so it cannot follow the crop.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Fix an estate tier target and a starter tier target, then bring each of the eleven toward its own target with its own call, recording the parameters applied.
trajectory.judgement: The client asked for one office and two registers at once. Two targets is the design answer; one target is the safe answer that fails the brief in both directions.
trajectory.produces: Eleven graded masters at source scale with a per property parameter log and a stated target per tier.

trajectory.action: Derive the sheet heroes to the hero frame's readable aspect, reading detection confidence and the tradeoffs array on every crop.
trajectory.judgement: One crop logic across eleven houses rather than eleven good crops, and the tradeoffs array is the only signal that a crop clipped or that an output was interpolated toward the two times cap.
trajectory.produces: Eleven sheet heroes with their tradeoff records.

trajectory.action: Recover the house mark from the window photograph: select the painted mark at ink level rather than by naming the glass, invert, crop to the returned bbox, trace, then strip the opaque background path and inject a viewBox.
trajectory.judgement: Naming the substrate pulls the selection to the window instead of the paint. The trace ships an opaque full canvas rectangle and no viewBox, and neither is fixed by any tool.
trajectory.produces: A transparent, scalable SVG of the house mark.

trajectory.surface: Data preparation and Creative Cloud storage
trajectory.action: Reconcile the Monday export against the principal's note, normalise it into a merge shaped data file with an at prefixed image column holding bare filenames, upload the prepared heroes and build the image map.
trajectory.judgement: One row must not print, one row was typed rather than exported and does not match the others' conventions, and one photo cell points at a name that does not exist. What is the agent's call and what is the office's is itself a decision, and the client asked to be told.
trajectory.produces: The merge data file, the uploaded heroes, the image map and a list of questions for the office.

trajectory.action: Convert the press PDF, export the interchange file, unzip it and read the real frame inventory and bounds, then rebuild each frame's true story text by concatenating its content runs.
trajectory.judgement: The mapping strategy is a property of the retired printer's document, not of the printed sheet, and every offset must be computed from the document rather than from any convenience readout.
trajectory.produces: The converted document, its interchange export, a frame inventory with real integer ids and bounds, and a reconstructed story string.

trajectory.action: Author the mapping covering every copy field plus the hero frame, validate it, prepare the template, then export the interchange file from the RESULT and search it for every placeholder the mapping claimed to create.
trajectory.judgement: A success message is not evidence. Rows sharing one frame must be ordered so their positions hold against the original text.
trajectory.produces: A prepared template whose placeholder inventory has been independently confirmed.

trajectory.action: Merge to a native document with the per row heroes bound through the image map.
trajectory.judgement: Merging to the native document first keeps both the press branch and the per property branch open off one merge.
trajectory.produces: A merged native document carrying every reconciled row.

trajectory.action: Render the point estate proof at true print resolution at sheet trim and look at the rendered page rather than at the file that went in.
trajectory.judgement: The page is the only place the template's own behaviour becomes visible, and a proof at screen scale is not that place.
trajectory.produces: A 300 DPI proof of the flagship sheet, inspected.

trajectory.action: Render the whole book at trim and read every page against the reconciled roster, line by line and photograph by photograph.
trajectory.judgement: A missing line and a wrongly bound photograph both look like success at the API boundary and both look acceptable on a screen scale proxy.
trajectory.produces: A page by page reconciliation against the roster.

trajectory.action: Produce the per property single page files from the merged document and name each by opening it.
trajectory.judgement: Identity by position in a returned list is the fast wrong answer that puts the wrong house on an agent's reprint.
trajectory.produces: One named single sheet file per property, verified by inspection.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the establishing harbour frame the banner needs, filter to photography, exclude generative results, license and download at full resolution.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose light can live beside the graded eleven rather than the moodiest thumbnail. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP clean, camera scale establishing frame.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own and has to carry a starter tier and an estate tier without becoming two brands. Weight cannot be inferred from a style name.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual numeric weight per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML carrying the square post, the tall story and the wide banner, each root declaring its own canvas, every photograph inlined as image data, the open house schedule as a real table, the recovered mark inlined as SVG, family and weight declared per element; upload it and hold the URL.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override collapses a mixed size set.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML retained as the durable source.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, verify canvas one from the document's rendition and the remaining canvases from the returned per canvas markup, then build the selects board within the placement cap and write the note.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition shows the first artboard only. A 201 on the board is partial success.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document, an inspected first canvas, a markup audit for the rest, a persistent board and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the sheet's hero frame actually treats an image bound into it. The frame's bounds can be read out of the converted document, but its FITTING cannot: nothing in the conversion result, the mapping readout, the validator or the merge response says whether a bound image is fitted to the frame, filled from its centre, or placed at its own size. On this document it fills from the centre, so the subject aware crops prepared three steps earlier are re cropped again by the frame, and on the properties whose houses were composed off centre for good reasons the frame's centre lands on driveway and hedge and takes the roofline off the top. Every call in the chain reports success and the thumbnail of the prepared hero is still perfect.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it. Reading bounds and preparing to that aspect is exactly what a careful agent does, and it does not help, because the frame re crops a correctly shaped image from its own centre. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for sheets that look like one office and never mentions frames or fitting, and the acceptance line about the whole house still showing is the client's standing requirement, not a disclosure. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is a changed crop policy for the whole set, decided against a fitting behaviour nobody could have known.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Compare each rendered page's hero against the file that was bound, establish what the frame is doing to it, then return to the imaging surface and re derive the affected heroes with the house placed for the frame's centre rather than for the photograph, re read every tradeoff record so the re crop has not pushed anything into interpolation, rebuild the image map and merge again.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A four and a half million dollar estate goes onto a vendor's sheet with its roofline sliced off and a hedge in the middle of the frame, and seven other sheets go out mis framed in the same silent way, while every file the agent prepared looks perfect on disk.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: That one merged record does not fit and does not say so. The description frame was built by the retired printer at a fixed measure for a 2025 book whose entries were short. The point estate's description, typed by the listing agent rather than exported, is roughly three times that length. Overset text in a fixed frame does not spill and does not error: it simply stops rendering, so the page comes back looking finished with the description ending mid sentence at the trim edge. No tool reports overset anywhere in the chain, the merge returns success, and the page count is right.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it and care cannot settle it: the frame's real capacity for a specific string at that document's point size and leading is not computable from anything the connector exposes, and there is no overset readout to query. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says prices went out wrong once and asks for a clean weekly run; no asset note, deliverable or earlier step mentions copy length. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is editorial: decide which facts a four and a half million dollar listing cannot lose and which are decoration, rewrite in the office's voice, and only then merge again.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Read every rendered page at trim rather than at proof scale, identify each record that stops rather than ends, cut the offending copy to the measure the frame actually holds while keeping the estate's selling facts and the office's voice, raise the rewrite with the listing agent because it is his copy, then re normalise the data file and re run the merge and the per property branch.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The single most expensive listing in the book goes to every open house on a sheet whose description stops mid sentence, in front of the buyers the vendor's commission depends on, and the office's stated reason for hiring a designer was that the sheets keep going out wrong.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered house mark holds at the size it is actually used. The trace comes back at the size of the raster that went in, and at that size it is clean: the rope ring reads as rope, the R has a counter, the lighthouse has a door. Placed at the size a corner mark actually occupies on a square post and a tall story, and rendered on the cream ground the set uses rather than on white, the rope's gaps and the R's counter can close into solid shapes. Vectorize takes no options at all, so nothing about the trace can be tuned afterwards, and whether this particular mark survives is decided by how many pixels it occupied in the raster and by the ground it lands on.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it, because the judgement needs the mark at final size on the final ground, which exists only after the set is authored and exported. Care cannot settle it either: the trace looks correct at every scale before that one. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says only that the mark on the posts has to be the office's own mark rather than something close to it, which is a provenance requirement, not a warning that a trace can fill in. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The fix lives two surfaces back in raster preparation: re crop the window photograph so the mark occupies far more pixels, re select at ink level and trace again, which is new imaging work and a new judgement.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Inspect the exported canvases through the returned markup and the rendition rather than trusting the export, and where the mark has filled in, return to the window photograph, re crop tightly so the mark carries more pixels, re run the ink level selection and the trace, strip the background path and re inject a viewBox, then re author and re export the set and check the mark on the actual ground again.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The office's only surviving mark goes out on public posts as a solid blob with no rope and no letterform, next to printed sheets carrying the real thing, which is the precise brand drift the principal hired a designer to stop.

Delivered as one multi page press file for the print shop, as one named single page file per property verified by opening it, and as a 300 DPI proof of the point estate at sheet trim. Produced by reverse engineering a retired printer's press file into a live merge template, so the template and the record of how it was derived are handed back with it.

deliverables.spec: Eleven photographs from two sources and two times of day brought to two declared targets, one per tier, with one black point and one warmth and one crop logic inside each tier, and a stated reason for every difference between the tiers. Handed back as the office's only surviving artwork, with the reproduction size below which it should not be used.

Delivered with the self contained source it was authored from, so the office can change a price on Thursday itself.

decision_gates: Which deliverables go to the merge surface and which to authored canvases, given a sheet the office wants kept and prices that move on Thursdays.
How many targets the photography gets: one, which is safe and fails the brief in both directions, or two, which is the design answer the client described without naming.
Which tier each property belongs to, when the export carries no tier column and the boundary between them is a judgement about price, buyer and neighbourhood.
How much edge the two straightened agent frames can afford to give a crop, and whether the twilight exterior joins the set at all.
The roster: a property under contract that must not print, a hand typed estate row that matches nobody else's conventions, and a photo cell naming a file that does not exist.
Whether to trust the mapping tool's readout of the printer's text or to reconstruct the story independently from the exported document.
Whether a success message counts as verification of the prepared template's placeholders.
Whether per property identity is established by position in a returned list or by opening the file.
How the estate's over long description is cut, which facts it cannot lose, and whose call the rewrite is.
Whether the mark's trace is good enough at the size it is used, and how far back into raster preparation the fix has to go.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against two price tiers in one weekly voice.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the folders into a frontier image model and it returns a handsome picture of a flyer. IDENTITY: these are eleven actual properties at actual addresses with actual prices, and the mark is the office's own painted mark, which has to be RECOVERED from the window rather than redrawn, because a brokerage cannot put an invented house or an approximated logo in front of a vendor. SPEC: the print shop needs one page per active property, page count equal to row count, every field bound verbatim including a reference code, plus one named file per property that actually contains that property and a proof at true print resolution. EDITABILITY: the open house set is defined by being editable, because the price moves on Thursday and the office refuses to pay twice. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality: what the frame does to a bound image, whether a record stopped rather than ended, whether a trace still reads at the size it is used.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account); five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. MERGE SPINE: building a merge template from a bare press PDF end to end headlessly is verified (convert_pdf_to_indd returns a raw .indd, export_idml round trips it, generate_indd_mapping_prompt plus prepare_indd_merge_template produced live placeholders confirmed by unzipping the result); one record per page is confirmed for the PDF branch with page count equal to row count; per record files are confirmed in correct order via createSeparateFiles; true 300 DPI at trim is confirmed through document_render_layout, whose resolution parameter the merge tool silently ignores. Frame granularity from a PDF is documented as not under your control, and the mapping readout's textContent is documented as lossy in a way the validator blesses (it dropped a 17 character run while keeping its break, every later offset short by exactly 17, VALID returned, two of five mappings silently absent). Per row image binding through an at prefixed column plus additionalImageFiles is verified visually. IMAGING: straighten, apply_adjustments, auto_tone, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds and crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs, detection_confidence and upscale_factor are verified headless; crop_and_resize is documented as interpolating to a hard 2x cap and reporting it only in tradeoffs, which is what makes the no enlargement bar checkable. The mark chain is the verified extract and reuse chain: an ink level prompt returns stroke level masks with counters correctly excluded, the wrong prompt returns the substrate, vectorize takes NO options at all, path zero is always an opaque full canvas rectangle and no viewBox is emitted. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export, real tables, inline SVG becoming native editable shapes and a genuinely editable document are verified; external image URLs render as empty grey boxes so photographs must be base64 inlined; the rendition shows page one only. FONTS, STOCK and BOARDS follow the verified chains, with short queries, orientation never passed, and the twelve per call board cap with 201 meaning partial. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no upscaling, no object removal, no compositing, no OCR, no bleed or press preset gate, no variable QR, no fill_text, no batch above 20.

engagement_title: Cedarline Institute autumn cohort: decide which of two dead press files can still carry a run, recover a seal that survives only as an impression, and deliver a whole cohort at two registers plus a programme and a credential card the office can edit
vertical: Continuing professional education, independent institute running a community evening programme and an employer funded executive programme from two campus buildings (Vermont)
real_brief_anchor: The batch record carried no quoted posting for this entry, so the anchor is reconstructed from the recurring certificate merge brief that runs constantly on Upwork and Freelancer.com: a training provider with a roster spreadsheet and a certificate design nobody can edit any more, asking for every candidate's certificate personalised and print ready, one file per person for emailing, and the institution's seal and signatures reproduced exactly. Laundered to the fictional Cedarline Institute (registrar Helen Abbott, signatories Dr Miriam Voss and Callum Reyes); no real school, awarding body, person or trademark is named. The ledger's verdict was REBUILD because the entry as first carved was a single merge and nothing else. The commission a provider of this shape actually posts is bigger in three specific ways it always states out loud: the cohort is not one register but two at very different price points, the artwork is gone and survives only as a physical impression, and the ceremony needs a programme and a shareable credential the office can correct up to the morning.
client_one_liner: The autumn cohort finishes in five weeks, our print shop closed with the seal die, and two thirds of the cohort paid a hundred and eighty dollars while the rest are on a nine thousand dollar employer funded programme.
client_brief:
Cedarline Institute, autumn cohort credentials

We run continuing professional education out of two buildings in Vermont. The autumn cohort finishes in five weeks. Every candidate has to leave the ceremony with a certificate in hand and a file in their inbox the same evening.

The cohort is not one thing. About two thirds are on the community programme, a hundred and eighty dollar evening course, and that certificate is a plain honest thing that goes on a kitchen wall. The rest are on the executive programme, which costs nine thousand dollars and is bought by employers, and that credential ends up framed in an office where clients see it. Those two cannot come off the press looking identical. If the executive diploma reads like a printable freebie we will hear about it from the sponsoring firms inside a week.

The shop that printed for us closed. We have two files: last year's community certificate, and the executive diploma we have not changed since twenty nineteen. Use whichever of them still works.

We need the whole cohort as one file for the printer, a separate file for each candidate named to them so the office can send them out individually, and a full quality proof of one of each kind for me to sign before anything is printed.

The seal is the problem. The die went with the closed shop. All we have is a certificate with the seal pressed into it and a photograph of that impression. We need it back as artwork we can use anywhere, and it has to be the same seal on the printed credential and on anything digital.

We also need the ceremony programme with the full cohort listed, and something graduates can post afterwards. Both have to be editable here, because names get corrected right up to the morning.

Please flag anything in the registrar's export that looks wrong rather than printing it.
price_band_and_audience: Two credentials, one cohort, an order of magnitude apart. The community certificate at 180 dollars is earned by evening students in their twenties and thirties and is read by family: plain, warm, legible, honest about what it is. The executive credential at 9,000 dollars is bought by employers and read by that graduate's own clients on an office wall: heavier engraved register, generous margins, restrained colour, the seal given room. The band is load bearing in both directions. Give the community certificate the executive treatment and it becomes pompous about an evening course, which embarrasses the student. Give the executive credential the community treatment and a sponsoring firm sees a printable freebie in a frame, which is the specific failure the registrar says she will hear about within a week. A cohort run of this shape posts at 600 to 1,500 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: Independent continuing professional education institute running a community evening programme and an employer funded executive programme from two campus buildings.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 1978, two campus buildings in Vermont, cohort run by registrar Helen Abbott.
brand_identity.about: Cedarline teaches working adults across two very different registers: an accessible community evening course and a high cost executive programme bought by employers. Each autumn cohort finishes with a ceremony where every candidate leaves with a certificate in hand and a file in their inbox the same evening. The Institute trades on being trusted rather than flashy, and on the two credentials reading honestly for what they cost.
brand_identity.audience: Community students in their twenties and thirties whose certificate is read by family at home, and executive candidates whose employer funded credential ends up framed in an office where their own clients see it.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Two credentials an order of magnitude apart: a 180 dollar community certificate and a 9,000 dollar employer funded executive credential. Neither can come off the press looking like the other. Cohort run posts around 600 to 1,500 dollars fixed.
brand_identity.typography: An engraved, higher contrast serif for the executive register, set with generous margins and the seal given room. A warmer, plainly legible serif for the community certificate. The two share bones but never the same weight or spacing.
brand_identity.voice: Measured and earned, never boastful. We state what was completed and who signed it. Example line the brand would write: 'Completed the autumn programme in professional practice. Signed at Cedarline Institute, Vermont.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The seal die went to the printer that closed and cannot be recovered. The only surviving seal is the one blind embossed into an old certificate, plus a raking light photograph of that impression. Two dead press files remain, last year's community certificate and the 2019 executive diploma; there is no digital seal artwork.
brand_identity.values: Each credential must be honest about its price, and every candidate name spelled and accented correctly right up to the ceremony morning.

assets_supplied.name: adulted_2024_press.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: Last year's community completion certificate as a flat press PDF, A4 landscape, fonts embedded, produced from a real page layout so it converts cleanly. Carries a recipient name, a programme title, a completion date, a small letterspaced credential number, two signature lines and a seal position.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Last year's community certificate. It is what the shop printed from."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The conversion exposes the recipient name, the programme title, the completion date and the credential number inside ONE continuous flow while the two signatory lines sit alone, and the mapping readout omits the letterspaced credential number run while keeping its line break, so the string still looks well formed and every offset past it is short by that run's length. The validator returns VALID on those offsets, the prepare call reports success, and the fields past the omission are silently absent from the template.

assets_supplied.name: exec_diploma_2019_press.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The executive diploma as a flat press PDF, produced in 2019 by a different print shop from the community certificate and unchanged since.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The executive diploma. We have not touched it since twenty nineteen."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: How this document was built is nothing like how the printed page reads. Its whole face is one continuous typeset block, so the conversion yields a single text frame holding every line and no graphic frame at all, which means there is no target to bind a per record seal into and every field has to be driven by offset arithmetic inside one story. Nothing about the printed diploma suggests this, and it is not visible until the document has actually been converted and its interchange file read.

assets_supplied.name: cohort_export.csv
assets_supplied.kind: The registrar's export for the autumn cohort, one row per candidate, with columns for name, programme code, programme title, completion date, credential number and an honours field.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The full cohort straight out of the student system."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Four faults, none stated. Which register a candidate belongs to is carried only inside the programme code, so the two tiers have to be inferred rather than filtered. One candidate withdrew in week three and was never removed. Two rows carry the same credential number, a clerical duplicate that would put an identical number on two different people's credentials. And several names carry European diacritics typed in a convention the rest of the file does not use, while the honours column is empty for the entire community register even though the certificate face carries an honours line.

assets_supplied.name: seal_impression.jpg

assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The impression is colourless: relief and paper are the same cream, and the seal reads only as shadow. Where the raking light falls away along one side of the ring the relief and the stock sit at the same luminance, so a selection there has nothing to hold on to. The mask still comes back looking like a seal, the trace still succeeds, and what is missing is an arc of the rope border and part of the year, which is invisible against cream at preview scale.

assets_supplied.name: campus_frames/ (6 staff photographs)

acceptance_bar: Exactly one credential per candidate who genuinely completed, no extra and no missing, and any row not printed is named to the registrar with the reason.
The two registers are visibly different credentials at a glance, in type register, in margin and in how the seal is given room, and both are unmistakably from the same institute.
No two candidates carry the same credential number, and every name is set the way that candidate spells it, diacritics included.
Every field the printed face carries is present on every credential and nothing ends mid line at trim.
The seal is recovered whole: the rope border closes all the way round and the founding year is complete, judged on the cream ground at print resolution rather than on screen.
The seal on the printed credential and the seal on anything digital are the same artwork, not two versions of it.
Each per candidate file contains the candidate its filename claims, established by opening it rather than by the order the files came back.
Both proofs are rendered at true print resolution at credential trim, not at screen scale.
The six campus photographs read as one set, with one black point, and any frame that cannot join is named rather than shipped.
No delivered image exceeds its source dimensions and no crop tradeoff record carries an upscale entry.

The ceremony programme and the credential card come back as a native editable document the office can correct a name in on the morning, with every photograph actually visible, the cohort roster as a real table with every candidate present and legible, and every text element carrying its licensed face at that family's own weight.

A written note: which press file was used for which register and why the other was handled differently, every export row questioned and how it was resolved, what was applied to each photograph, the type system by role, and every resize any tool reported.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable goes to which surface.
trajectory.judgement: The credentials are record per page against faces the institute wants kept, so they belong to the merge surface; the programme and the card must stay correctable on the morning of the ceremony, which the merge surface structurally cannot give.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming a surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier.

trajectory.action: Upload both press files, the cohort export, the seal photograph, the six campus frames and the registrar's note, holding every returned presigned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A manifest keyed by register and by role, because the run forks in two and the same artwork will exist in several states.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by register and role.

trajectory.action: Read the export against the registrar's note and reconcile it: split the cohort into its two registers off the programme code, resolve the withdrawal, the duplicate credential number, the diacritic convention and the empty honours column.
trajectory.judgement: None of this is filtering. Which faults the agent may fix and which belong to the registrar's own record system is a judgement, and the client asked to be told rather than printed around.
trajectory.produces: Two normalised register files and a written list of questions for the registrar.

trajectory.action: Preview the seal photograph closely and plan the recovery: what the impression actually gives a selection to hold, and which element of the device to name.
trajectory.judgement: A blind embossed seal is not an object with an edge, it is a relief read as shadow, and naming the certificate or the paper pulls the selection to the substrate instead of the device.
trajectory.produces: A recovery plan naming the element to select and the fallback if it will not hold.

trajectory.action: Select the seal's relief, invert, crop to the returned bbox and trace, then strip the opaque background path and inject a viewBox.
trajectory.judgement: Polarity before tracing decides whether the result is a mark or a black box, and the trace accepts no options at all, so every lever lives in the raster preparation.
trajectory.produces: A first transparent, scalable SVG of the institutional seal.

trajectory.action: Lay the traced seal at credential size on the cream ground the stock has and read the device round the whole ring rather than glancing at it.
trajectory.judgement: The only place a recovered mark can be judged is at reproduction size on the real ground, and the whole point of a seal is that it closes.
trajectory.produces: An inspected seal at reproduction size, in or out, with the reasoning recorded.

trajectory.action: Convert BOTH press files, export the interchange file for each, unzip them and read the real frame inventories, bounds and object styles.
trajectory.judgement: The printed face says nothing about how a document was built, and the two files came from two different shops, so neither can be assumed to behave like the other.
trajectory.produces: Two converted documents, two interchange exports and a frame inventory for each with real integer ids and bounds.

trajectory.action: Rebuild each frame's true story text by concatenating its content runs, and compute every offset from that string.
trajectory.judgement: The convenience readout is not the document. Offsets taken from it are short past any run it omits, and nothing downstream complains.
trajectory.produces: A reconstructed story string per frame and an offset table computed from it.

trajectory.action: Decide the architecture for each register against what the two conversions actually exposed, and record why.
trajectory.judgement: This is the engagement's structural decision and it cannot be made before the documents have been opened. What each file can carry, and what a register loses if it is moved to the other file, is the whole question.
trajectory.produces: A stated route per register with the tradeoff each one costs.

trajectory.action: Author the mapping for each route, validate it, prepare each template, then export the interchange file from each RESULT and search it for every placeholder the mapping claimed to create.
trajectory.judgement: A success message is not evidence, and rows sharing one frame must be ordered so their positions hold against the original text.
trajectory.produces: Prepared templates whose placeholder inventories have been independently confirmed.

trajectory.action: Merge each register to a native document, binding the seal per record where a graphic frame exists to receive it.
trajectory.judgement: Merging to the native document first keeps both the press branch and the per candidate branch open off one merge.
trajectory.produces: A merged native document per register.

trajectory.action: Render one proof from each register at true print resolution at credential trim and read the whole face, seal included.
trajectory.judgement: The rendered page at trim is the only place the seal's recovery and the template's own behaviour are both visible at once.
trajectory.produces: Two 300 DPI proofs, inspected.

trajectory.action: Render both registers in full at trim and read every page against the reconciled roster, name by name and number by number.
trajectory.judgement: A missing field and a duplicated credential number both look like success at the API boundary and both look acceptable on a screen scale proxy.
trajectory.produces: A page by page reconciliation against both register files.

trajectory.action: Produce the per candidate single page files from the merged documents and name each by opening it.
trajectory.judgement: Identity by position in a returned list is the fast wrong answer that emails one graduate another graduate's credential.
trajectory.produces: One named single credential file per candidate, verified by inspection.

trajectory.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, and Adobe Stock
trajectory.action: Level the off level hall frame, bring the six campus photographs to one black point, derive the programme and card crops reading tradeoffs on every call, and license one establishing frame the institute does not own.
trajectory.judgement: Three frames look clean alone and grey beside the other three, and straightening the hall eats the edge the cover crop wants, so the order matters. Short generic queries only, and the orientation filter always returns zero.
trajectory.produces: A graded campus set with tradeoff records and one licensed camera scale frame.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own and has to hold an evening course and an employer funded credential in one institutional voice. Weight cannot be inferred from a style name.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual numeric weight per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML carrying the programme spread with the full cohort roster as a real table, plus the square credential card and the wide banner, each root declaring its own canvas, every photograph inlined as image data, the recovered seal inlined as SVG, family and weight declared per element; upload it and hold the URL.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override collapses a mixed size set. How a cohort of that size is set as a roster is a real typographic decision.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML retained as the durable source.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, then verify canvas one from the document's rendition and every other canvas from the returned per canvas markup, roster row by roster row.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition shows the first artboard only, so the markup is the only channel for anything past it.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document, an inspected first canvas and a markup audit for the rest.

trajectory.action: Build the registrar's sign off board within the placement cap, re sending only entries named as failed, then write the note.
trajectory.judgement: A 201 is partial success. The note has to name every export row questioned and every route decision, because the registrar asked to be flagged rather than printed around.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether this photograph of a blind embossed seal will give up the whole device. The impression is colourless, so relief and paper are the same cream and the seal exists only as shadow. Along the side where the raking light falls away the relief and the stock sit at the same luminance and the selection has nothing to hold, so the mask silently loses an arc of the rope border and part of the founding year. Nothing reports it: the selection succeeds, the mask thumbnail still looks like a seal, the trace succeeds, and the gap is invisible against cream at preview scale. It becomes visible only with the traced seal placed at credential size on the cream ground.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it and care cannot prevent it: the failure is a property of where the light fell on this one photograph, and there is no measurement anywhere in the family, no histogram and no eyedropper, so no read ahead exists. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says only that the die is gone and the seal must come back as usable artwork; no asset note or acceptance line discloses that part of it will not select. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is a different instrument, either compositing per element selections or abandoning the impression for the flat printed seal on the old certificate face.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Confirm the loss by reading the traced seal round the whole ring at reproduction size rather than glancing at the thumbnail, then re attack it: name the rope border and the year as their own selections and composite them with the ring, or crop far tighter so the shadowed side carries more pixels, or fall back to the seal printed on the 2024 certificate face and accept that it is a different generation of the same device, which is a provenance decision the registrar has to be told about.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Every credential in the cohort, community and executive alike, carries an institutional seal with a broken rope border and half a founding year, on a document that hangs on a wall for twenty years and whose whole function is to look unforgeable.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What each of the two press files can actually carry. The community certificate converts into a usable structure with a graphic frame that can receive a per record seal. The 2019 executive diploma, built by a different shop as one continuous typeset block, converts into a SINGLE text frame holding every line and NO graphic frame at all, so there is no target to bind a seal into and all four fields must be driven by offset arithmetic inside one story. Nothing about the printed diploma suggests this: it looks like the more carefully made of the two documents. Frame granularity from a PDF is not under anyone's control and is exposed only by converting and reading the interchange file.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it. Converting both and looking IS the correct move, and what it returns is not knowable in advance from the printed pages, the file sizes or anything the client said. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says only that there are two files and to use whichever still works, which is the client's ignorance, not a disclosure of which one fails or how. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is an architecture decision that changes what the executive register can be, how its seal is placed, and what the agent has to tell the registrar.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re plan the executive register around what its file can hold: drive its fields by offsets inside the one story, decide whether its seal can be placed at all through the merge or whether that register has to ride the community derived template at a corrected type register, weigh what a 9,000 dollar credential loses either way against the registrar's stated fear of looking like a printable freebie, then rebuild the mapping and re verify the placeholders for that register from scratch.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The executive register either merges with no seal at all, or is quietly run off the community template, and the employer funded credential arrives at the ceremony looking exactly like the 180 dollar evening certificate in front of the sponsoring firms the registrar named.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the importer does with the cohort roster once the table is taller than the artboard it sits on. A table survives as a live table, but nothing anywhere documents what happens past the canvas edge: whether rows are clipped, reflowed, hoisted or dropped. The export returns success either way with no warning of any kind, and because the roster sits on a canvas after the first, the rendition cannot show it, so the returned per canvas markup is the only channel through which the roster's actual state exists. Counting rows in the markup is the only way to learn whether the whole cohort is in the programme.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it and care cannot settle it, because how many rows the artboard holds at a chosen size and leading is not computable from anything the connector exposes, and the check itself only exists after an export. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for the programme with the full cohort listed and for it to be editable; no asset note, deliverable or earlier step says anything about roster length or canvas behaviour. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is an authoring decision about how a cohort is broken across pages and set in two registers.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Count the roster rows present in the returned markup against the reconciled register files rather than trusting slide_count, and where rows are missing, re author the programme: split the roster across additional canvases, decide where the two registers break and whether they are listed together or apart, re set the measure and leading so the names with diacritics still fit their cells, then re run the readiness check and export again and re count.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The ceremony programme handed to every family in the hall silently omits the last dozen graduates, whose relatives are sitting there, and the office finds out during the ceremony rather than before it.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the folders into a frontier image model and it returns a handsome picture of a certificate. IDENTITY: the seal is this institute's own seal and survives only as a physical impression, so it has to be RECOVERED from that impression rather than redrawn, because an invented seal on a credential is a forgery of the institute's own device; the names are real candidates spelled the way they spell them. SPEC: the printer needs one page per completing candidate across two registers, page count equal to row count, every field bound verbatim, unique credential numbers, one named file per candidate that actually contains that candidate, and proofs at true print resolution. EDITABILITY: the programme and card are defined by being correctable on the ceremony morning. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality: what each dead press file can carry, whether the seal came back whole, whether the roster is all there.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account); five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. MERGE SPINE: building a merge template from a bare press PDF end to end headlessly is verified (convert_pdf_to_indd returns a raw .indd, export_idml round trips it, generate_indd_mapping_prompt plus prepare_indd_merge_template produced live placeholders confirmed by unzipping the result); one record per page is confirmed for the PDF branch with page count equal to row count; per record files are confirmed in correct order via createSeparateFiles, with a recordRange loop as the identity guaranteed fallback; true 300 DPI at trim is confirmed through document_render_layout, whose resolution parameter the merge tool silently ignores. The two file triage rests on a documented fact rather than invention: FRAME GRANULARITY FROM A PDF IS NOT UNDER YOUR CONTROL AND CAN COLLAPSE TO ONE FRAME, verified when a continuous text flow converted to exactly one TextFrame holding all six lines and ZERO graphic frames, with the doc's own instruction to export IDML and look before promising a frame layout. The offset hazard is likewise documented: textContent dropped a 17 character run while keeping its break, the validator returned VALID, prepare reported success and two of five mappings were silently absent. Per row image binding through an at prefixed column plus additionalImageFiles is verified visually. IMAGING: select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, vectorize, straighten, apply_adjustments, auto_tone and crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and upscale_factor are verified headless; selection is documented as UNRELIABLY PARTIAL ON COMPOUND MARKS (a badge prompt silently dropped the inner rule and the central device while the mask still looked plausible), which is exactly the seal checkpoint, and compositing per element selections is the documented remedy; vectorize takes NO options, always emits an opaque path zero and no viewBox. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export, real tables rendered as per cell shapes and text, inline SVG becoming native editable shapes and a genuinely editable document are verified; external image URLs render as empty grey boxes so photographs must be base64 inlined; SUCCESS IS NOT FIDELITY and the rendition shows page one only, so a canvas after the first can only be checked through the returned markup. FONTS, STOCK and BOARDS follow the verified chains, with short queries, orientation never passed, and the twelve per call board cap with 201 meaning partial. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no upscaling, no OCR, no PDF text edit, no compositing, no bleed or press preset gate, no variable QR, no fill_text, no batch above 20.

engagement_title: Meridian Summit delegate badges: bring eighteen self-submitted portraits to one registration wall, recover the summit mark off the lectern plate, rebuild the bureau's badge into a live run, and hand back the room set editable
vertical: Events, Conferences and Promotion, an invitation-only two-day executive summit for regional transmission operators, infrastructure investors and utility policy staff (Providence, Rhode Island)
real_brief_anchor: The batch ledger carries no quoted posting for this slot, so the anchor here is the recurring posted-job shape rather than one quoted advertisement. Primary anchor: the Upwork commission repeatedly listed as 'InDesign data merge for conference name badges, roster CSV plus per-attendee headshots', posted by event organisers who hold last year's badge only as a flat print file from the venue's print bureau, have no working file and nobody who remembers how it was built, and need this year's roster, organisations, tracks and photographs put through the same badge, delivered as one ordered press file for the on-site printer plus individual files for the reprint desk. Co-anchor: the Upwork and Freelancer.com 'event collateral designer, badges plus registration signage plus closing deck' listings, which bundle the badge run with the registration-desk board, the session-room door cards and the closing slides, because organisers buy the room as one job and never the badge alone. Laundered to the fictional Meridian Council and its Meridian Summit; no real company, person, venue, sponsor or trademark appears. The ledger recorded this slot as a badge merge and nothing else, which is one surface and one deliverable class. LAYOUT-23 restores the commission the organisers actually post: eighteen portraits taken by eighteen different people have to be made into one wall before any of them binds, the summit mark has to be recovered because nobody kept the file, and the badge run, the registration board and the closing slides all have to agree with each other in a room where every delegate paid twenty-four hundred dollars to be there.
client_one_liner: Eighteen delegates, eighteen photographs taken by eighteen different people, a badge the venue bureau made last year off a file we do not have, and a registration desk that opens in five weeks.
client_brief:
Meridian Summit, delegate badges and the room set.

Meridian Council runs one closed-door executive summit a year. Two days, eighteen seats, twenty-four hundred dollars a seat, and the people in the room either run regional transmission networks or write the cheques that rebuild them. Everything they touch at the venue has to feel like it cost what they paid for it.

The badges worry me most. Last year the venue's print bureau made them from a file we no longer have and nobody here knows how it was put together. Keep the badge exactly as it looks, it is what people expect. What changes is what is on it: this year's delegate, their organisation, their track and their own photograph.

The photographs are the mess. Everybody sent their own. Some are proper studio headshots, some are cropped out of a conference photo, one is plainly a phone picture in a hotel corridor. Standing at the registration wall they have to look like they were all taken for us: same treatment, same framing, faces sitting the same way in the frame, and skin that looks like the person's actual skin rather than everybody averaged into one colour.

Names and organisations exactly as people registered them. Nothing shortened, nothing abbreviated, no post-nominals dropped. For half this room the title is the reason they are in it.

The check-in desk scans people in, so each badge needs its own code.

Our mark is on the badge. The only clean version I can find anywhere is a photograph of the brass plate on the lectern from last year. Pull it off that and use the same one on everything.

Three things we do not have at all: the board behind the registration desk, the door cards for the two session rooms, and the closing slides. Give those back as one file we can edit, because the running order moves the week before.

Send the badge run to the printer as one ordered file, plus one file per delegate for the reprint desk. And if anything in our registration export looks wrong to you, say so before it prints.
price_band_and_audience: Twenty-four hundred dollars a seat, eighteen seats, invitation only. Delegates are 40 to 65, they run regional transmission networks, sit on infrastructure funds or write utility policy, and they have been to two hundred conferences. The band is load-bearing. At this tier the correct badge is heavy, quiet and photo-forward: one restrained neutral, generous space, the name set large and calm, the organisation smaller but complete, the track carried as a small typographic distinction rather than a shouted colour block, and the portrait treated like a portrait. Push it toward the bright, playful, colour-blocked, text-only badge that a free two-hundred-person community meetup correctly uses and the delegate reads it as a name sticker, which at this price is an insult they will mention to the person who invited them. Push it the other way into a decorated or celebratory register and it reads as a gala rather than a closed-door working session. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,600 to 3,200 dollars fixed, or 45 to 75 dollars an hour across 30 to 45 hours.

brand_identity.tagline: The people who run the grid, and the people who fund it.
