adobe_surfaces.role: One licensed counter or botanical-ground frame for the shade card, which a house with a single sample bottle cannot shoot, graded to the same light as the packshot. Plus the persistent board the founder and the compliance clerk sign off nineteen shades and the recovered mark from before the press file is committed, which matters because two shades are close enough to argue about.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface.
trajectory.judgement: Nineteen labels are record per page against a layout the client owns and stockists recognise, so they belong on the merge surface. The shade card and the system page do not exist and must stay editable, so they belong on HTML authoring. The wordmark has to be real artwork before either can carry it.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming a surface per deliverable, with the confirmed account tier.

trajectory.action: Upload the eleven sample frames, the nineteen drawdown frames, the carton frame, the label press PDF and the roster, holding a manifest of presigned URLs against roles.
trajectory.judgement: Two per-row images across nineteen SKUs means the mapping between URL, SKU and role has to stay trustworthy through fifty artefacts.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by SKU and role.

trajectory.action: Preview the eleven sample frames and choose the one the launch runs on, judging the collar's form, how the frosted body separates from the marble, and how level the bottle stands.
trajectory.judgement: There is one sample and one afternoon, so this choice is not revisitable by reshooting. The frame with the most attractive collar highlight is often the frame where the bottle edge disappears into the marble, and that trade is made by looking rather than by rule.
trajectory.produces: A chosen hero frame and a chosen secondary frame, with the reasons recorded.

trajectory.action: Level the chosen frames and bring them to one counter light, fixing a white point and correcting toward it with recorded parameters.
trajectory.judgement: Window light in a kitchen is not counter light. The destination is a neutral the drawdowns can also be brought to, so it is fixed once for both sets rather than optimised for the bottle alone.
trajectory.produces: Corrected sample masters at source scale with a parameter log.

trajectory.action: Isolate the bottle, choosing the route by looking at the frame: the one-call knockout, or a material-named selection inverted and filled to the label ground.
trajectory.judgement: Frosted glass and polished metal are not one subject, and a route chosen for the body may not serve the collar. The route taken is recorded per element because the two may not be the same.
trajectory.produces: A bottle cutout per chosen frame, with the route recorded.

trajectory.action: Preview the nineteen drawdown frames and set a policy for where on each card the swatch is taken from, then hold it across all nineteen.
trajectory.judgement: Every draw runs thin to heavy, so the same shade yields two different swatches depending on where the chip is taken. The policy is a set-level decision and it is the difference between a shade card that is honest and one that is decorative.
trajectory.produces: A written swatch-derivation policy.
A written swatch-derivation policy applied consistently across all nineteen cards.

trajectory.action: Bring the drawdowns to the same light as the packshot, recover what the highlights will give, derive one swatch chip per SKU, then lay all nineteen chips out together beside the roster.
trajectory.judgement: Nineteen chips judged as a set rather than one at a time, against a roster that already warns two Atelier shades are close. Looking at them together is the only way the set-level truth appears.
trajectory.produces: Nineteen swatch chips with per-frame parameters, laid out as the shade card they are for.

trajectory.action: Recover the wordmark from the carton: select the foil by its own visual properties rather than by naming the carton, invert, fill, crop to the mark's bounds, trace, then repair the trace by injecting a viewBox and stripping the opaque full-canvas path. Derive the reversed cut from the same artwork.
trajectory.judgement: Foil flips value across a single letter, so naming the substrate returns the carton and naming a colour finds nothing to hold. A trace that returned successfully is not yet placeable artwork, and board grain picked up as letterform is a defect that only shows at size.
trajectory.produces: A repaired scalable transparent wordmark plus a reversed cut, with the recovery route recorded.

trajectory.surface: Data preparation and Creative Cloud storage
trajectory.action: Reconcile the roster against the printed reference and the pictures: normalise the three net-weight formats, clean the pasted ingredient lines without changing their content or order, decide how the may-contain clause is carried, resolve the duplicated shade name and the discontinued row, compose the per-label fields, and shape both image columns to the merge contract with bare filenames.
trajectory.judgement: Compliance text is the client's property and cleaning invisible characters is not the same as editing it, which is a line the agent has to draw and then state. The duplicated shade name across two tiers is the client's call, not the agent's.
trajectory.produces: The reconciled merge data file, uploaded packshot and swatch masters, both image maps, and a first list of roster questions.

trajectory.action: Convert the label PDF to a native document, export IDML, unzip it, read the real frame inventory with ids and bounds, and reconstruct the true story text by concatenating the content runs.
trajectory.judgement: The mapping strategy is decided by what the label printer's system emitted rather than by what the printed label suggests. Two graphic frames come back separable only by bounds and link, and deciding which is the packshot well and which the swatch chip is a judgement made against the printed reference.
trajectory.produces: The converted document, its IDML, a frame inventory, and the reconstructed story text.

trajectory.action: Author the mapping covering the shade name, the ingredient line, the net weight, the batch field and both images, ordering rows that share a frame against the original text, and pass it through the validator.
trajectory.judgement: Offsets have to be computed against a source of truth the agent has chosen deliberately, and rows sharing one frame have to be ordered so their positions still hold against the untouched text.
trajectory.produces: A validated mapping covering the text fields and both image frames.

trajectory.action: Prepare the merge template, then export IDML from the result, unzip it and grep the stories for every placeholder the mapping claimed to create.
trajectory.judgement: A success message is not evidence. Nothing instructs this check, nothing warns if it is skipped, and it is the only place the mapping's true yield is visible before a single label exists.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholder inventory has been independently confirmed.

trajectory.action: Merge the Atelier tier to a native document with both per-row images bound, render the press labels and a 300 ppi regulatory proof at true trim, and look at them.
trajectory.judgement: Merging straight to raster silently drops to screen resolution whatever was asked for, so the route is chosen rather than defaulted. This is also the first moment the bottle cutout has ever been seen on the ground it is actually used on.
trajectory.produces: Atelier press labels and a 300 ppi proof at trim.

trajectory.action: Take the Everyday tier through the same template and decide how the price difference is carried, given no frame can be moved and no element can be placed freely.
trajectory.judgement: The band is load-bearing but the layout is fixed client property, so the tier difference has to be carried by what the fields hold, how the swatch reads, which cut of the mark is used and how the photography sits, or else be escalated honestly as something this layout cannot express. Pretending one label serves both prices is the failure the client described in the brief.
trajectory.produces: The Everyday tier merged and rendered, plus a written position on how far the fixed layout can carry the band.

trajectory.action: Produce per-SKU named single label files across both tiers, identity verified by opening each file rather than by its position in a returned list.
trajectory.judgement: Naming nineteen files by the order they came back is the fast wrong answer and it is the one a filler discovers with a pallet of stock already labelled.
trajectory.produces: Nineteen identity-verified named label files.

trajectory.action: Read every rendered label at true trim against its roster row, field by field: shade name, the full ingredient line in compliance order, the may-contain clause, net weight, batch field, and both images in their own frames.
trajectory.judgement: Reading the artefact rather than the log. A field that never became a placeholder, a clause set in the wrong place and a swatch bound into the packshot well all look like success at the API boundary and plausible at proof scale.
trajectory.produces: A label-by-label reconciliation against the roster.

trajectory.action: License one counter or botanical-ground frame with short generic queries, filter to photography, exclude generative results, download at full resolution and grade it to the packshot's light. Then ask for type recommendations once per role, read the real numeric weights from the style inventories, launder every name and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The frame has to serve a house that spans 6 to 85 dollars without picking a side. The type pairing is the agent's own because the recommender refuses to pair, numeric weight cannot be inferred from a style name, and one bad name kills the whole kit including the valid faces beside it.
trajectory.produces: One licensed graded frame and one kit with family, foundry or designer and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self-contained HTML with two canvas roots (the counter shade card and the label system page), the nineteen shades as a real table, the recovered wordmark as inline vector inside an explicitly sized top-left anchored wrapper on both a light and a dark ground, every photograph carried as embedded image data, family and weight declared on every text element. Upload by the allowed-host route, run the readiness check, export, then verify the first canvas through its rendition and the second through the returned markup.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the visual channel shows the first canvas only. How the two tiers are shown side by side without flattening them into one house voice is the actual design work.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document with both canvases, its durable source HTML, and a per-canvas markup audit.

trajectory.action: Create the approval board with the nineteen swatches, the bottle on its label ground and the recovered mark in both cuts, staying inside the placement cap and re-sending only entries reported as failed. Then write the handover.
trajectory.judgement: What gets escalated versus what gets fixed quietly. Two close shades, one discontinued row, a duplicated shade name and anything the label could not hold all belong in front of the founder and the compliance clerk before a printer sees a file.
trajectory.produces: A persistent approval board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the two palest Atelier shades can be told apart at all. They were drawn thin and caught direct window light, so their swatch areas are clipped with nothing left in them, and the honest signal is the strangest one available: a highlight recovery accepts its parameters, returns success and moves nothing whatsoever. The picture that comes back is byte-for-byte as pale as the one that went in. Which shades behave this way is a property of these particular cards under that particular afternoon's light and cannot be read off the roster, off the shade names or off a single card previewed on its own, because on its own each of the two looks like a plausible pale shade. It only becomes a problem when all nineteen chips are laid out together and two SKUs are visibly sharing one near-white square.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it and care cannot either: the tool succeeds, the parameters are accepted, no warning is emitted, and the only tell is a nil result that an agent reading a success line will not notice. (b) Nothing states it. The client says two of the Atelier shades are very close to each other, which is a fact about the products and a reason for care, not a statement that two photographs are clipped and unrecoverable; nothing in the brief, the roster or the asset descriptions mentions exposure, clipping or which cards are affected. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is to change where the swatch comes from, which is a different operation on a different region of the card, and then to re-take the derivation policy across all nineteen, because two chips pulled from the heavy end of a draw will not sit with seventeen pulled from the middle unless the policy is re-decided for the whole set.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Abandon recovery on the affected cards and re-derive their chips from a denser part of the draw, then re-derive the other seventeen under the same revised policy so the set stays internally honest, and re-lay all nineteen together to judge again. Where the two shades still cannot be distinguished at chip size, escalate it to the founder in writing with both chips shown, because a shade card that implies two SKUs are the same colour is a commercial problem the client has to decide on rather than a problem the agent may quietly resolve by pushing one of them.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A counter shade card and two labels on which two separately formulated, separately priced Atelier shades appear as the same near-white square, printed for a launch, in front of the exact buyer who is paying 85 dollars to be able to tell them apart.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the label printer's file actually yields, and then whether the mapping built against it landed. Two things arrive only by running. First, the granularity: the ingredient paragraph, the net weight and the batch line all live in one continuous story with no separate frames, so everything must be driven by ordered offsets inside a single story, and the packshot well and the swatch chip are distinguishable only by bounds and link. Second, the yield: the readout of that story omits the run holding the net weight while keeping its line break, so the string still parses as well-formed and every offset past it is short by exactly that run's length. The validator returns valid on arithmetic that is internally consistent and wrong, the placeholder step reports success, and the net weight and the batch field never become placeholders at all.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it and diligence alone cannot either. Granularity is not a parameter, is not reported before the conversion and has no read-ahead. The yield failure is worse: it is produced by a convenience readout that presents as complete, so an agent that reads carefully and computes offsets diligently from the readout it was handed produces arithmetic every downstream tool agrees with. The only defence is an independent reconstruction of the same text from a different channel, which nothing prompts and whose necessity is invisible until the two disagree. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says work from last season's label and that nothing may be reworded or dropped, and the acceptance bar states the client's standing requirement that net weight and batch appear on every label, which is a regulatory fact rather than a warning. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the source of truth behind the mapping changes, from a tool readout to a reconstructed story, and the whole mapping is re-authored with re-ordered same-frame rows and re-computed positions.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reconstruct the true story by concatenating the document's content runs, recompute every offset against that string, re-order the rows sharing that frame so their positions hold against the original text, rebuild and re-validate the mapping, re-run the template preparation, and re-verify by round-tripping the template and grepping for every placeholder before a single label is merged. Settle which of the two graphic frames is the swatch chip by rendering one label and reading it against the printed reference rather than by assuming the larger frame is the packshot.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Nineteen product labels bound correctly for shade name and ingredient line while the net weight and the batch field are silently absent from every one of them, sent to a label printer for a retail launch, with every tool in the chain having reported success and a regulatory proof that looks finished.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the bottle cutout is actually clean. Along the left shoulder of the frosted body and across the top arc of the gold collar, the subject sits at the same value as the marble it was shot on, so the knockout reports success and returns something that looks immaculate on white and immaculate against a transparency checker, having quietly bitten away the shoulder edge and the top of the collar. Which parts fail is a property of this one bottle on this one kitchen counter at that hour and cannot be predicted from the frame preview, from the tool's response, or from any check performed against a light ground. The loss only becomes visible when the cutout is finally placed on the deep Atelier label ground, which does not happen until the merge template exists and a label has been rendered at trim.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it. The check that would reveal it (looking at the cutout on a dark ground at real size) is exactly the thing that does not exist until the layout surface has been built, and every check available before then, including the tool's own output preview, is performed against a ground that hides it. Choosing a better frame does not help either, because the frames that show the collar best are the frames where the shoulder disappears into the marble. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for the bottle to sit on the label ground rather than on a kitchen counter, which is an ordinary client requirement, and mentions no edge, no value match and no risk. No earlier step claims the cutout was verified, because no earlier step had the ground to verify it against. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is a different isolation strategy: routing the frosted body and the polished collar separately, selecting by material rather than by subject, and possibly moving to a different source frame entirely, which changes the hero photograph the whole launch is built on and therefore the light every other picture was matched to.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-isolate the bottle with the body and the collar routed separately, selecting each by naming its own material rather than asking for the subject, inverting and filling to the label ground so the edge is decided by the selection rather than by a detector. If no route holds the collar on the chosen frame, move to the secondary frame and re-run the light correction so the new hero still matches the swatch chips, then re-bind and re-render a label to look at it on the dark ground again rather than assuming the second attempt took.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: An 85 dollar counter serum whose label carries a photograph of its own bottle with a slice missing from the shoulder and the top of the gold collar shaved off, printed across the entire Atelier tier, on the one product where the buyer is paying for exactly that kind of care.

deliverables.name: SEVE launch photography at one counter light
deliverables.spec: The chosen sample frames and all nineteen drawdown frames brought to one light with one white point, delivered as the hero and secondary packshot plus nineteen swatch chips derived under one stated policy, with one licensed context frame graded to match. Every output at or below its source pixel dimensions, with a per-frame parameter log, the swatch-derivation policy written down, and every crop's reported detection and tradeoff metadata transcribed.

deliverables.name: Bottle isolation for the label ground
deliverables.spec: The sample bottle isolated for use on the label ground, with the frosted shoulder edge and the full top arc of the gold collar intact, judged and signed off on the dark ground it is used on rather than on white. The isolation route recorded per element, because a frosted body and a polished metal collar may not survive the same route, and the alpha carried intact through every subsequent crop.

deliverables.name: Recovered SEVE wordmark, artwork system
deliverables.spec: The wordmark lifted off the foil-blocked carton at ink level and delivered as real artwork: scalable, transparent, with a genuine viewBox, no background plate riding along and no board grain fused into the letterforms, plus the reversed cut that holds on a dark ground. Each cut's intended reproduction range stated and demonstrated at that size on the ground it prints on, with the recovery route recorded so the house is never again dependent on one carton.

deliverables.name: Launch label run: press file, per-SKU named labels and regulatory proofs
deliverables.spec: One label per current SKU at true label trim, one record per page, page count equal to the reconciled SKU count, rendered at 300 ppi with a proof label per tier for regulatory sign-off. Every label binds shade name, the complete compliance ingredient line in its written order with the may-contain clause set as the reference sets it, net weight, the batch field and both per-row images (the packshot and that SKU's own swatch chip) in their own frames. Accompanied by one named single file per SKU, identity-verified by opening it, and by the live merge template reverse-engineered from the printer's flat PDF with its derivation record and an explicit statement that no bleed can be introduced into it.

deliverables.name: Counter shade card and label system page
deliverables.spec: One native editable document holding two canvas roots: the counter shade card with all nineteen shades in a genuine table and live editable shade names, and the label system page carrying the recovered wordmark as real editable vector on both a light and a dark ground, the named type system by role, and the two tiers set side by side so the difference between an 85 dollar counter label and a 6 dollar peg label is written down rather than assumed. Delivered with the self-contained source it was authored from.

deliverables.name: Handover note and approval board
deliverables.spec: A written note recording what was applied to the sample frames and the drawdowns and why, the swatch-derivation policy, the wordmark recovery route and the sizes each cut is good for, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and actual numeric weight, the plain statement that no chosen face can reach the printed label, every roster value questioned and its resolution, the shades that could not be told apart, anything the fixed layout could not carry across the two price tiers, the bleed constraint, and every resize any tool reported. Paired with a persistent approval board carrying the nineteen swatches, the bottle on its label ground and both cuts of the mark, with nothing silently dropped.

verifiers_auto.text: The label press file has exactly one page per current SKU in roster order and renders at 300 ppi at true label trim.
verifiers_auto.how: Count pages against the reconciled SKU count and check the render call's resolution against the output raster dimensions at trim.

verifiers_auto.text: Net weight and the batch field are present on every merged label, and every expected placeholder exists in the prepared template.
verifiers_auto.how: Round-trip the prepared template to IDML and grep for every expected placeholder, then read the text off each rendered label against its roster row.

verifiers_auto.text: Every ingredient line on every label is complete and in the order compliance wrote it, with the may-contain clause set as the printed reference sets it.
verifiers_auto.how: Compare each rendered label's ingredient text character for character against its roster cell, at trim rather than at proof scale, and against the reference label's clause placement.

verifiers_auto.text: On every label the packshot is in the packshot well and that SKU's own swatch chip is in the swatch chip, with no two labels sharing a chip.
verifiers_auto.how: Read both bound images off each rendered label and compare them against the SKU's image-map entries rather than against the merge response's ordering.

verifiers_auto.text: The bottle cutout retains an unbroken shoulder edge and a complete collar top arc when composited over the dark label ground.
verifiers_auto.how: Render the cutout over the Atelier ground colour at label size and inspect the shoulder and collar boundaries against the corrected source frame.

verifiers_auto.text: The delivered wordmark carries a viewBox, carries no full-canvas background path, and its reversed cut renders correctly on a dark ground at the sizes it is used at.
verifiers_auto.how: Parse the delivered vector for a viewBox and for an opaque bounding path, and render both cuts at their stated reproduction sizes on their grounds.

verifiers_auto.text: Nineteen named single-SKU label files exist, each containing the SKU its filename claims, and no delivered picture exceeds its source frame on either axis.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the shade name and tier off each single-record file and compare with its filename, never with its position in a returned list; compare every delivered picture's dimensions against its source and inspect every tradeoffs array.

verifiers_auto.text: The exported document holds two canvases at their declared sizes, with the shade table present as real table cells, the wordmark present as path shapes on both grounds, every photograph resolved to real image data, and every text element carrying a resolved licensed face at the intended numeric weight.
verifiers_auto.how: Read slide_count and per-slide dimensions from the export response and parse each canvas's returned markup for table structure, path-type shapes, placeholder images, resolved font families and weights, and out-of-canvas resolved positions.

verifiers_human.text: Laid out together, the nineteen swatch chips read as nineteen distinct shades, and any pair that does not is named and escalated rather than quietly separated.
verifiers_human.how: View all nineteen chips as a set beside the roster and beside the drawdown cards, and check the handover for any pair the agent could not honestly distinguish.

verifiers_human.text: The bottle on the finished Atelier label looks like a photograph of that bottle, with nothing shaved off its edge.
verifiers_human.how: View the rendered label at true trim on the dark ground and compare the bottle silhouette against the corrected source frame.

verifiers_human.text: The two tiers are visibly different at their own price and recognisably the same house: the Atelier label reads restrained at a counter and the Everyday label wins at arm's length on a peg.
verifiers_human.how: Review both tiers against the price band and audience description, at their real sizes and under the light each one is sold in.

verifiers_human.text: The recovered wordmark reads as a wordmark rather than as a traced photograph of foil, at every size it is used at and on both grounds.
verifiers_human.how: View both cuts at their stated reproduction sizes and look for board grain fused into the letterforms and for counters closing at small size.

verifiers_human.text: The handover escalates rather than conceals, naming the indistinguishable shades, the discontinued row, the duplicated shade name, anything the fixed layout could not carry across the two tiers, and the bleed constraint.
verifiers_human.how: Read the handover against the triage, conversion, merge and reconciliation findings and check each is disclosed with the decision taken.

decision_gates: The surface split: nineteen labels to the merge surface because the layout is fixed client property and the run is record per page, shade card and system page to HTML authoring because they must stay editable.
Which of eleven phone frames the entire launch is built on, given there is one sample and the best collar and the safest edge are usually not the same frame.
Whether the frosted body and the polished collar are one subject or two, and therefore whether one isolation route can serve both.
Where on a drawdown card a swatch is honestly taken from, decided once for all nineteen rather than per card.
Whether a recovery that reports success and changes nothing means the shade is fine or means the data is gone.
Whether two shades that cannot be distinguished at chip size is the agent's problem to solve or the founder's to decide.
Whether the mark is selected by naming the carton or by naming the foil, where naming the substrate returns the carton and every downstream step accepts it.
Where cleaning invisible characters out of compliance text stops and editing compliance text begins, and how to say which was done.
How the may-contain clause is carried, given the reference sets it on its own line and the roster has it trailing in the run.
Whether to trust the readout of the label's own story or to reconstruct it independently from the document.
Whether a success message counts as verification of a prepared template.
Which of two indistinguishable graphic frames is the swatch chip rather than the packshot well.
How far a fixed single layout can be made to carry a 6 dollar peg product and an 85 dollar counter product, and at what point that becomes an escalation instead of a design decision.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, plus the disclosure that no chosen face can reach the printed label at all.
why_not_vlm: Paste this brief and these files into a frontier image model and it returns a beautiful invented skincare label. IDENTITY: the wordmark is this house's actual mark, blocked into a carton by a designer they have lost, and a redrawn approximation is a different brand's mark across a nineteen SKU launch; the bottle is the one physical sample that exists and a generated bottle is not the product being sold; the swatches are photographs of the real product drawn on card and a generated swatch is a false colour claim on a cosmetic label. SPEC: the client needs one label per SKU at true label trim and 300 ppi, page count equal to SKU count, every compliance ingredient line bound verbatim in its written order, net weight and batch on every label, two different per-row images bound to the right frames, and nineteen separately named files each containing the SKU their filename claims. None of that is produced or checkable by generation. EDITABILITY: two deliverables are defined by being editable, a live merge template so the next shade is a data change rather than a re-commission, and a native document with live text, a real table and real vector artwork. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality: did this placeholder get created, did this recovery move anything, is this swatch this shade, is this bottle's shoulder still there on the dark ground. That is not a generation problem.
doability_proof: Every link is verified in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account). Five surfaces, honestly counted: image_vectorize is used but declared Photoshop-family and never claimed as an Illustrator surface, and document_render_vector and document_merge_data_vector are never called because they sit on a polling helper absent from this host. MERGE SPINE: building a merge template from a bare PDF end to end headlessly is verified, one record per page is confirmed for PDF output with page-count equal to row-count, per-record named files are confirmed by two order-verified routes while multi-record raster output is documented as coming back reversed and is therefore never used for identity, and true 300 ppi at trim comes from document_render_layout because outputSpecs.resolution on the merge is documented as silently ignored. The supplied label PDF is a real font-embedding press PDF from a full engine, since thin hand-authored PDFs fail conversion opaquely. THE LOSSY-READOUT CHECKPOINT IS THE CONNECTOR'S OWN DOCUMENTED HEADLINE TRAP, reproduced live in the audit: textContent dropped a run while keeping its line break, every offset past it was short by exactly that run's length, the validator returned valid with zero warnings, prepare reported success, and only three of five mappings landed; recomputing offsets from the IDML-reconstructed story landed all of them. This asset is built to that shape (a continuous story carrying the ingredient paragraph, the net weight and the batch line, plus two placed graphics separable only by bounds and link), and it is verify-then-ship: if the omission will not reproduce on this asset, the checkpoint still stands on the granularity fact, which is verified and controllable. TWO PER-ROW IMAGES: per-row binding through an at-prefixed column plus additionalImageFiles keyed to bare filenames is verified; nineteen rows sit inside the documented file limits and the recordRange loop is carried as an explicit fallback that also guarantees per-record identity. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, single_color_saturation, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, select_subject, invert_selection, fill_area, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs array, remove_background with and without backgroundColor, and vectorize are all verified headless. The cutout checkpoint rests on documented behaviour: remove_background needs one coherent blob, its alpha is where edge softness lives, selection masks are binary with zero intermediate values, and a value-matched boundary is exactly where that fails; the fix route (material-named selection, invert, fill to the ground) is the verified variant. The mark recovery uses the verified extract-and-repair chain, including the substrate-versus-material prompt asymmetry, the mandatory polarity inversion before tracing, the missing viewBox and the opaque path-zero background. No upscaling is asserted: crop_and_resize interpolates to a hard 2x cap signalled only in tradeoffs and remove_background silently downscales oversized inputs, so the bar scores the decision and the disclosure separately. The bottle is never composited in the image editor; it is placed by the layout surface into a graphic frame, and by the authoring surface as an embedded image. BLEED is correctly declared impossible: a PDF-derived template carries zero bleed, useDocumentBleeds does not introduce it, and pdfPreset is never used because its enum is undiscoverable, so the task escalates rather than promises. EXPRESS: multi-root export with per-root canvas sizes is verified, tables survive as real tables with per-cell backgrounds and strokes, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, photographs must be base64 inlined because every external URL renders as an empty grey box, transport is routed through the text/html upload because the payload passes the inline threshold, and verification is split because the rendition preview shows the first canvas only. FONTS: the recommend, styles, find, embed chain is verified end to end and the task leans on the non-standard numeric weights, the slug-not-PostScript rule and the all-or-nothing kit call; the impossibility of getting a font file onto the InDesign surface is stated as a client-facing constraint. STOCK AND BOARDS: short generic queries only, never orientation, licensing returns genuine camera-scale files, board placements capped at twelve per call with partial success signalled by failedItems. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no variable QR, no pdfPreset, no fill_text, no animate_design or create_firefly_board, no replace_image, no download_design, no upscaling, no OCR, no compositing, no generated imagery, no photo reaching Express as a URL, and no batch above twenty files.

engagement_title: Rivermeadow Trust year end appeal: build the donor acknowledgement run properly from the giving export, recover the mark off the trailhead plaque, and give the office one system it can run itself next December
vertical: Nonprofit, religious and community, a small accredited land trust holding conservation easements in the Sedgewater valley, Litchfield County, Connecticut, four staff and a few hundred giving households
real_brief_anchor: The ledger entry for LAYOUT-29 carries an EMPTY real_brief_anchors array, so no verbatim posting is quoted here and none is invented. The rebuild is anchored instead to the standing posted archetype this entry was carved from, which recurs on Upwork and Freelancer in near identical wording every autumn: a small nonprofit with an existing printed letter and receipt, a giving export out of its donor database, and a request for a designer who can set up a personalised year end acknowledgement run in InDesign, deliver print ready files plus a separate file per donor for emailing, and hand back something the office can run itself the following year. The nearest quoted sibling in this same batch is the Upwork brief anchoring LAYOUT-30, which asks for 'Proficiency in Adobe InDesign', a 'Strong sense of typography, layout, and print design', print ready files and editable source, and it is cited here only for the shape of the deliverable list, not for its content. The verdict on this entry is REBUILD because the prior draft sat almost entirely on one surface, the merge, with the mark and the stewardship page bolted on as prose. This build re carves it as the commission the archetype client actually needs: the identity is RECOVERED off a photographed bronze plaque rather than assumed to exist, two genuinely different printed letters are reverse engineered into two live templates whose internal structure is not under the agent's control, and the one page the trust wanted for the annual meeting is authored as a native editable document instead of promised as a PDF the connector cannot produce. Client, persons and place names are coined and Western. No real charity, person or trademark is named.
client_one_liner: Every December we thank everyone who gave and send them the receipt they need for their taxes, it is done by hand one document at a time, it took our office manager three weeks last year, and two donors were missed entirely.
client_brief:
Rivermeadow Trust, year end appeal

We are a small land trust in the Sedgewater valley in Connecticut. Four staff, about nine hundred acres under easement, and a giving base of a few hundred households. Every December we thank everyone who gave that year and send the receipt they need for their taxes. It has always been done by hand, one document at a time. Last year it took our office manager three weeks and two donors were missed entirely.

This year we want it built properly, out of our giving export, so that next December it is a morning of work rather than three weeks of it.

Two letters exist and both were printed last year, so our printer still has the files. The community letter goes to most of our donors. It is warm and photographed, our meadows on it, and it carries a picture of the preserve nearest to where that donor lives. The leadership letter goes to the households who carry the campaign. No photograph on it, cream stock, quiet, personal, the sort of thing you would actually sign. The receipt is the same for everyone and the legal wording on it is not ours to change.

What we need. One print run our printer can take. A separate file for each donor as well, because a good number of them ask us to email it. Each one has to carry their own name, the way that household likes to be addressed, what they gave across the whole year, and the level that puts them in. The numbers come out of the database raw, so they will need to be made to look like money.

Our mark only survives on the bronze plaque at the Fenn Hollow trailhead. There is a photograph of it. We need it back as artwork we can actually use.

We also want one page about what this year of giving did, something we can post, email, and put on the screen at the annual meeting, and edit ourselves next year when the acreage changes.

Gifts run from twenty five dollars to twenty five thousand. The median is eighty five. Please do not make the small gift feel like a form letter, and do not make the large one feel mass produced.
price_band_and_audience: A small accredited land trust with a genuinely split base: gifts from 25 dollars to 25,000 dollars, median 85, roughly two thirds of the money arriving from under a tenth of the households. Donors are 45 to 78, local, land literate, and many are easement grantors who know the fields in the photographs by name. The band is load bearing in an unusual way here, because BOTH ends of it ship in the same run. The community register is warm, photographed, generously set, and it may read as produced, because a 60 dollar donor who receives a hand set personal note reads it as money spent on them rather than on land. The leadership register at four and five figures must read restrained and personal: no photograph, quiet rules, a signature that sits like a signature, wide margins, the gift figure set without emphasis. Ship the leadership register at community warmth and a 15,000 dollar donor feels processed. Ship the community register at leadership austerity and an 85 dollar donor feels held at arm's length by a charity that is supposed to be their neighbour. An agent that finds one house look and applies it to both has misread the commission even if every field lands correctly. A real posted job of this shape runs 900 to 2,200 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: Land held in common, kept for good
brand_identity.sector: A small accredited land trust that holds conservation easements and stewards preserves in one Connecticut valley, funded by a few hundred local giving households.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 1994, based in the Sedgewater valley, Litchfield County, Connecticut. Four staff, roughly nine hundred acres under easement, a few hundred giving households.
brand_identity.about: Rivermeadow protects the meadows, hollows and river bends of one valley by holding easements and caring for a handful of small preserves. Many of our donors granted the land we now steward, so the relationship is personal and long. We exist so the fields stay fields for the people who walk them.
brand_identity.audience: Local giving households aged 45 to 78, land literate, many of them easement grantors who know the fields by name. Gifts run from 25 dollars to 25,000, a broad community base plus a small leadership circle that carries most of the campaign.
brand_identity.price_positioning: A community land trust, not a national charity. Two registers live in one base: a warm community of small and mid gifts, and a leadership circle giving four and five figures. Every dollar should read as spent on the land, not on ourselves.
brand_identity.typography: A quiet transitional serif for headings and running text, set generously with wide margins, paired with a restrained humanist sans for labels and figures. Type should feel like a well kept letter, never like a campaign.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, grateful and specific, the voice of a neighbour rather than an institution. It names the field, not the fund. Example: We kept forty more acres in hay this year because you asked us to.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The original logo files left with our first designer and are gone. The mark now survives only on the cast bronze donor plaque at the Fenn Hollow trailhead, of which we hold one photograph. Approved letter copy, giving level names and thresholds, and the statutory receipt wording still exist as plain text.
brand_identity.values: Permanence of the land, and a personal duty of thanks to every household that gives, whatever the size of the gift.

assets_supplied.name: rivermeadow_giving_2026.csv (18 rows)
assets_supplied.kind: The year to date giving export straight out of the donor database, one row per constituent record, with name, salutation, address, year total, gift count, and a giving level column.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "This is what the database gives us. It has everything on it, we think."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two rows are one household entered twice, because a joint gift was split across both spouses at data entry, and only the identical mailing address reveals it, so the row count is not the household count and the page count gate moves with it. The giving level column is empty on the records whose December gift pushed them across a threshold after the field was last written, the year totals are raw unformatted numbers with inconsistent decimal places, and the salutation column is blank on every household record.

assets_supplied.name: rivermeadow_letter_community.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The printer's press file for last year's community letter, one page, photographed, carrying a placed preserve picture and the trust mark as printed artwork.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The warm one. Most of our donors get this."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Because it carries placed images it converts into several text frames plus real graphic frames, which is workable, but the readout of one frame's story text silently omits a styled run, so every character offset computed past that point is short by exactly that run's length while the validator still reports the mapping VALID and the placeholder step still reports completed successfully. The mappings that land are the early ones and the ones that vanish leave no trace anywhere in any tool response.

assets_supplied.name: rivermeadow_letter_leadership.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The printer's press file for last year's leadership letter, one page, cream stock, typographic, no photograph anywhere on it.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The quiet one. Our biggest supporters get this."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It looks on the printed page like a salutation block, a body, a gift acknowledgement line and a signature block set as four separate elements, but with no images anywhere in the file the whole page converts to exactly ONE continuous text frame and ZERO graphic frames, so the per frame mapping strategy that works on its sibling is not available on it at all and there is nowhere to bind the recovered mark as a graphic.

assets_supplied.name: rivermeadow_receipt.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The printer's press file for the statutory gift receipt, identical for every donor, carrying the trust's registration line and the acknowledgement wording the trust cannot alter.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Same for everyone. The legal line on it is not ours to change."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Its name and address block is a fixed measure frame, so an overset line does not spill, does not warn and does not error: it simply stops rendering at the frame edge, which at trim truncates the longest household names mid word while the page count stays exactly right and every tool in the chain reports success.

assets_supplied.name: rivermeadow_plaque_fennhollow.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of the cast bronze donor plaque at the Fenn Hollow trailhead, the mark raised in relief: a heron over a river bend, enclosed in a ring of small caps type broken by a hairline rule.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only place our mark still exists. The original file went with our first designer."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is a compound lockup in relief on a photographed metal substrate, so a prompt naming the plaque returns the plaque rather than the mark, a prompt naming the whole emblem returns the type ring and silently drops the heron and the hairline rule while looking entirely complete, and background removal on the ring returns a solid opaque disc because an enclosed interior cannot be punched. The raised bronze and its green patina also run close in value along the weathered left third of the casting.

assets_supplied.name: rivermeadow_volunteer_photos/ (9 frames)
assets_supplied.kind: Volunteer snapshots of the four preserves taken across the year, intended one per region so each donor sees the land nearest to them.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our stewardship volunteers took these. There should be one for each preserve."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three are phone captures far below the pixel scale the letter's photo frame needs at print resolution, and no filename or column says so, so they can only be brought to the frame by interpolation. Two others are the same footbridge from slightly different angles, which leaves one of the four preserves with no frame of its own at all, and one frame sits noticeably off level.

assets_supplied.name: rivermeadow_copy.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text: the approved letter copy in both registers, the giving level names and their thresholds, the executive director's sign off line, and the statutory receipt wording.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The wording as the board approved it. The receipt paragraph is fixed."

acceptance_bar: Every delivered household receives exactly one letter and exactly one receipt, and the delivered record set is reconciled and stated rather than assumed to equal the export's row count.
Page count equals the delivered record count on every run, and the pages sit in the order of the data.
Every field the letter and the receipt promise actually appears on every page. A field that is silently absent fails even if the template reported that it was built successfully.
No name, no address and no salutation is cut off at trim on any page of any run. A record that stops mid word is a failure, not a tight fit.
Year totals read as money, consistently formatted across letters and receipts, and every donor's stated giving level agrees with their total and the published thresholds.
The community register and the leadership register are visibly different in warmth, density and formality, and each is right for the gift it acknowledges.

The mark is placeable artwork rather than a picture of artwork: transparent, scalable with a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath it, and it still reads as our heron at the size it actually prints on the letterhead and on cream.
No photograph is delivered above the pixel dimensions it arrived at, and any frame that cannot fill its place honestly is named rather than enlarged to fit.
Each preserve is represented by its own picture, and no picture stands in for two preserves.
Per donor files are named to the roster and each file contains that donor and no other. A file named for one household that carries another's gift figure is the worst failure in the run.
The stewardship page arrives as a working file the office can edit next year plus the self contained source it was built from, with live text in one type system and the mark as real vector.

A written note states the money and giving level rules applied, every field that was mapped and how it was verified, every photograph that could not be used and why, and anything the office should know about using the recovered mark.

adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt (as generator and as validator), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout (recordRange and outputSpecs), document_render_layout (resolution, pageRange, createSeparateFiles)
adobe_surfaces.role: The spine of the commission. Three supplied press PDFs are reverse engineered into three live merge templates whose internal frame structure is not under the agent's control and cannot be known before conversion, mappings are built against each document's actual story text and image frames, the per region photograph and the recovered mark are bound per record, and the run is delivered twice: one press PDF per template with one record per page, and per donor single page files through the route whose record identity is guaranteed rather than the route whose labels lie.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including image_vectorize which is counted HERE and not as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_invert_selection, image_fill_area, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs, detection_confidence and upscale_factor), image_remove_background, image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Recovers the mark at ink level off a photographed bronze casting, with the polarity, the compound lockup and the vector hygiene decisions the tracing tool does not make, and derives the transparent raster of the same mark that the merge templates can actually carry. It also brings the usable volunteer frames to one target, straightens what is off level, crops each to the letter's photo frame without enlarging, and establishes which frames cannot honestly be used at all.

Photographs must be pulled down and embedded as image data because a reference renders as an empty grey box at full success, the recovered mark goes in as inline SVG so it stays vector, and the giving ladder is authored as real table and vector geometry rather than a picture of a chart.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url

The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and must land between the two registers this trust lives in rather than in either extreme. Numeric weights are non standard per family and cannot be inferred from a style name, every name must be laundered into canonical PostScript form before the kit call because one bad name kills the entire kit, and the CSS must use the returned slug or the face falls back silently.

adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (entityScope StockAsset, SHORT query, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the one wide valley frame the stewardship page needs and the volunteers never shot, IP clean and at genuine camera scale with generative tech candidates excluded, then grades it into the same world as the preserve pictures. The Boards half persists the selects the trustees actually sign off from, placed within the per call cap, with a partial success read as partial and vector understood to be unacceptable there.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching anything.
trajectory.judgement: The letters and receipts are a variable data run and belong on the merge surface because one record equals one page at volume. The stewardship page is a one off composition and belongs on the authoring surface, and it cannot be promised as a print file. The brief already pins both destinations, so there is nothing here to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming surface per deliverable, and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline: a manifest keyed by role, because three templates, nine photographs and a plaque become indistinguishable URLs within an hour.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Read the giving export against the two registers: reconcile rows to households, assign each household its tier, derive the giving level where the column is silent, and write the year totals into the form they will print in.
trajectory.judgement: The merge prints exactly what the data says. Nothing downstream can format a number, resolve a blank level or notice that two rows are one household, so all three are settled here or they ship wrong. Deriving a level from a total and a published threshold is arithmetic the agent must do and then state.
trajectory.produces: A reconciled delivered record set with formatted money, resolved levels, a household salutation on every row, and a written note of every reconciliation made.

trajectory.action: Recover the mark off the plaque photograph: an ink level selection worded by the mark's own visual properties, correct polarity, a bounds crop driven by the selection's returned bbox, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full canvas ground path removed. Derive a transparent raster of the same mark at the scale the letterhead needs.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions the tools do not make: how to word the selection so it takes the relief and not the casting, which polarity to trace, and whether the compound lockup came back whole or quietly missing its heron. Background removal is the wrong instrument on an enclosed ring and returns a plausible solid disc.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent vector mark plus the raster of it that a merge template can carry.

trajectory.action: Convert all three press PDFs to native documents, export IDML on each, and inventory what each conversion actually exposes: how many text frames, how many graphic frames, what each frame's story really contains.
trajectory.judgement: The printed page is not evidence of the document's structure. Conversion granularity is a property of how the PDF was produced and it is not controllable, so the inventory has to be looked at before anything is promised about which field goes in which frame.
trajectory.produces: A per document frame inventory with real bounds, applied type and the true story text of every text frame.

trajectory.action: Triage the three converted documents against the inventory and choose a mapping strategy for each one separately.
trajectory.judgement: A document with separated blocks can be mapped frame by frame. A document that collapsed to a single continuous flow can only be mapped by position inside one story, and it has no graphic frame to carry the mark, which forces a different answer for that letter's identity element.
trajectory.produces: Three named mapping strategies with the reason each was chosen.

trajectory.action: Build the community letter's mapping, run it through the validator, prepare the merge template, then export IDML on the prepared file and check the story for every placeholder the mapping was supposed to write.
trajectory.judgement: A successful response is not evidence that a mapping landed. The only channel that reports what the prepared template actually contains is the document itself, read back.
trajectory.produces: A prepared community template plus a read back record of which placeholders are genuinely present in its story.

trajectory.action: Do the same for the leadership letter and for the receipt, each on its own strategy, each read back the same way.
trajectory.judgement: The leadership letter has one story and no graphics, so its gift line, salutation and signature block all land by position inside a single flow and its mark cannot be bound as an image at all. The receipt shares the statutory paragraph across every record and only its name and address block varies.
trajectory.produces: Prepared leadership and receipt templates with their placeholders read back and recorded.

trajectory.action: Preview and triage the nine volunteer frames: which preserve each actually shows, which are duplicates of one another, which sits off level, and which are simply too small for the frame they are meant to fill.
trajectory.judgement: The client believes there is one picture per preserve. The pictures are the only thing that can settle whether that is true, and counting files is not the same as reading them.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note covering preserve identity, level, pixel scale and duplication.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level, bring the usable frames to one target with a call per frame, crop each to the letter's photo frame ratio, and read every returned tradeoff report rather than the success message.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes and eats edge pixels so it cannot follow a crop. One batched call would apply one identical parameter set to frames shot in four different seasons, which is exactly wrong. A frame that can only reach the required size by being enlarged is not a frame that can be used.
trajectory.produces: Graded and cropped preserve pictures with a per frame parameter log, plus a named list of frames that cannot honestly be used.

trajectory.action: Bind the per region photograph column and the mark into the community template, then merge the community run to a press PDF and check its page count against the delivered record set.
trajectory.judgement: The image column needs its prefixed header, bare filenames in the cells and file keys that match those filenames exactly. A naive binding places one static picture on every record and looks completely correct until two donors in different counties get the same meadow.
trajectory.produces: A press PDF of the community run with one record per page.

trajectory.action: Merge the leadership run and the receipt run to press PDFs the same way.
trajectory.judgement: Three runs, three page counts, all of which have to reconcile back to the delivered record set decided in step 3 rather than to the raw export.
trajectory.produces: Press PDFs for the leadership letters and for the receipts.

trajectory.action: Render the merged documents at print resolution and read every page at trim against the delivered record set, name by name and figure by figure.
trajectory.judgement: Nothing before this point shows the page as the donor receives it. Page count agreeing with record count says the run assembled, not that any given page is correct or complete.
trajectory.produces: Print resolution proofs of all three runs, read at trim.

trajectory.action: Produce the per donor named single page files through the route whose record identity is guaranteed, naming each file to the roster on download.
trajectory.judgement: There is more than one route to per record files and they do not all preserve identity. Choosing the one whose ordering is trustworthy is the whole of the decision, because a file named for one household carrying another's gift figure is the failure this client will actually notice.
trajectory.produces: One named single page letter and one named single page receipt per delivered household.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged against a land trust whose donors are older, local and land literate. The weight cannot be inferred from a style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug rather than by a heavy weight.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry or designer, and the actual numeric weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the wide valley frame, filter to photography, exclude generative tech, license and download at full resolution, grade it toward the preserve pictures, then create the trustees' selects board and add the set within the per call cap.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose existing light can be brought to the preserve pictures rather than the prettiest thumbnail. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used. A partial success on the board is partial, and the vector mark is not boardable.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the mapping that validated and prepared successfully actually wrote every placeholder into the template. The readout of the community letter's story omits one styled run while keeping its line break, so the string still looks well formed and every character offset computed past that point is short by exactly that run's length. The validator returns valid with zero warnings on those offsets and the placeholder step reports completed successfully, so the early mappings land and the later ones vanish leaving no trace in any tool response. Whether this document has a droppable run at all, and where in the story it sits, is a property of how this particular PDF was produced and cannot be known before conversion.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter prevents it, because the omission happens inside the readout the mapping must be built from. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for each donor's own name, salutation, total and level, which is a goal, and the acceptance line about every promised field appearing is the client's standing requirement rather than a disclosure that a readout is lossy. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is to rebuild offsets against a different source of truth, the document's own reconstructed story text, and then re prepare and read back again.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reconstruct the true story text from the document itself, recompute every offset from that string, rebuild the mapping, prepare the template again, read the placeholders back a second time, and apply the same discipline to the two templates not yet built.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A run that assembles cleanly with the right page count in which the gift figure and the giving level are simply missing from every community letter, discovered by the client rather than the agent, on the one mailing of the year that asks people for money.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether every donor's name and address survives onto the page. The receipt's name and address block is a fixed measure frame, so an overset line does not spill into another frame, does not warn and does not error. It stops rendering at the frame edge, which truncates the longest household salutations mid word at trim while the page count stays exactly right and every response in the chain reports success. Which records overflow depends on the frame's real measure and on the salutations written into the data in step 3, so it exists only once the data and the converted frame meet on a rendered page.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) It cannot be ordered around, because it only exists after data meets template, and it cannot be prevented by doing it right the first time without knowing a measure the document does not report until rendered. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says the receipt is the same for everyone and its wording is fixed. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is a decision about the DATA, shortening or restructuring the household salutation for the affected records, or moving the field to a frame that can carry it, followed by a re merge.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Identify every record whose block overflows, decide a salutation rule that holds for the longest households without making the shortest ones read oddly, rewrite those rows, re merge the receipt run, and read the affected pages at trim again.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Tax receipts going out with a household's name cut off mid word, which for a receipt is not only an embarrassment but a document a donor cannot use, on the exact deliverable whose wording the trust is not permitted to alter.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered mark still reads as the trust's mark where it actually reproduces. The trace is judged at canvas size, where it looks clean, but on the letterhead it prints small on cream, and a trace taken off raised bronze carries the weight of the relief edge rather than the weight of the original drawing. At true reproduction size the hairline rule can disappear into the ring and the counters inside the small caps can close up into solid marks, and on cream rather than on white the whole lockup can go heavy. None of that is visible at any stage before a page is rendered at print resolution and looked at at trim.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering shows it earlier, because the mark's reproduction size only exists once it sits in the template on a rendered page, and the tracing tool takes no options at all so there is no parameter that could have prevented it. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for the mark back as artwork we can use, which is a goal. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is a different recovery route, a differently prepared raster before the trace or the colour accurate plate instead of the two colour trace, or a decision to carry the mark larger and set the ring separately.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re prepare the plaque selection and retrace, or switch to the colour accurate plate, re derive the placement raster, rebind it into the templates, re merge and re render, then judge it again at trim on cream rather than at full canvas.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: An acknowledgement run going to the trust's entire giving base with a logo that is legible on the designer's screen and a dark blot on the paper, on the one piece of print the organisation is judged by.
