trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching a pixel.
trajectory.judgement: The tags are a variable data run at one record per page, which is a merge job; the bench cards are free form fixed canvas layout, which only the authoring surface does. The brief pins both, so there is nothing to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline: a manifest keyed by role, because the run depends on knowing which URL is which variety.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Read the season list against the photo folder and against what the client says they are stocking: row count, rows with a missing pot size, the order actually present, header hygiene, the shape of the photo column, and which photographs correspond to which variety.
trajectory.judgement: The growers' list and the stocked list are not the same list and neither is authoritative on its own. Bench order and department order are both plausible orders and only one of them fills a bench.
trajectory.produces: A reconciled, department ordered data file for the stocked list, an image column in the shape the binding actually accepts, and a written list of every change made to the client's export.

trajectory.action: Preview all eighteen frames and triage them: which week and which weather each belongs to, which are off level, how far the grower was standing, how much of the frame the plant occupies, and which frames are already tight.
trajectory.judgement: Eighteen usable snapshots and one rack are different things. Shooting distance is the variable nobody names and it governs both the crop and whether the crop is reachable at all.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note covering illuminant, tilt, subject occupancy and native frame size.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level, before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes the subject and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Fix one bench target off the best lit frame and bring each of the eighteen to it with its own call, recording the parameters applied.
trajectory.judgement: The destination is a rack, not eighteen nice pictures of plants. One batched call applies one identical parameter set, which is exactly wrong across weeks of changing weather; foliage green is also the hue that goes wrong first under a global warmth move.
trajectory.produces: Eighteen graded masters at source scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Apply confined corrections where a whole frame move goes wrong, selecting by the material's own visual properties rather than by the object it sits on.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the whole gate: naming the pot pulls the selection to the terracotta. Frames shot against wet bench timber need the foliage held while the ground moves.
trajectory.produces: Corrected frames where a whole frame move would have taken the foliage yellow or the bench muddy.

trajectory.action: Cut each frame to the hanging tag's photo frame geometry with one crop logic across the set, reading the returned tradeoff record for any upscale entry before accepting the crop.
trajectory.judgement: One crop logic across eighteen means the plant sits at one distance on every tag, which is what makes a rack read as a rack. Placement geometry comes from the printed tag and the converted document, not from what looks nice full frame.
trajectory.produces: Eighteen tag photographs at one crop logic with their tradeoff records.

trajectory.action: Recover the nursery mark off the slate sign: an ink level selection naming the paint's own visual properties, correct polarity, a bounds crop driven by the selection's own returned box, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full canvas ground path removed.
trajectory.judgement: Naming the sign takes the slate. The routed groove puts a shadow line around the mark's own edge, so what the selection takes and what the trace makes of it are two separate judgements.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent mark plus a colour accurate variant.

trajectory.action: Convert both printer PDFs to live documents, round trip each through IDML, and read what each one actually is: frame counts, real bounds, applied faces and sizes, object styles and existing links.
trajectory.judgement: Two tags that print as the same design in two sizes are not necessarily the same document, and what a printed face looks like says nothing about what the conversion exposes as addressable frames. Promising a field to a frame before looking is how a run ships half mapped.
trajectory.produces: Two written frame inventories, and a decision about which fields can live where on each format.

trajectory.action: Render a page of the converted hanging tag at high resolution, then recover the care icon row off that render at ink level and trace it into vector.
trajectory.judgement: The icons already exist in the client's own printed artwork, so recovering them is archaeology rather than invention, and rendering the converted document is the only route that produces a raster clean enough to trace.
trajectory.produces: The client's own care icon set as placeable vector artwork.

trajectory.action: Reconstruct each frame's true story text from the IDML content runs, compute every offset from that string, build the mapping with text mappings for the tag's lines plus an image mapping for the photo frame, run it back through validation, prepare the merge template, then re-export IDML and confirm every expected placeholder is actually present.
trajectory.judgement: A validator that says valid and a preparation step that says success are both reports about the request, not about the document. The only evidence a placeholder exists is finding it in the round tripped story.
trajectory.produces: A live merge template whose placeholders are confirmed present by inspection rather than by tool response.

trajectory.action: Merge the reconciled stocked list to one press file in department order, binding each variety's own photograph, and read a sample of the merged tags against the list line by line.
trajectory.judgement: A file with the right number of pages and the right names on them can still be wrong in every other field. The list is what the tag has to agree with, variety by variety.
trajectory.produces: One press file for the whole stocked season plus a line by line reading of sample records.

trajectory.action: Produce the per department subsets by record range off the same template and data, and check each subset for completeness and disjointness against the reconciled list.
trajectory.judgement: Subsetting only works because the data was put in department order first; on the growers' original order the ranges would be meaningless while still producing files that look correct.
trajectory.produces: Four department subsets, each verified complete and disjoint.

trajectory.action: Produce the sign off proofs at genuine print resolution at trim by rendering the merged document rather than by asking the merge for a raster.
trajectory.judgement: Print resolution is a property of the render stage; a page sized raster carrying a print name is the thing that gets signed off and then fails at the printer.
trajectory.produces: Proof rasters at real resolution at trim, with their dimensions recorded.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the potting bench band, filter to photography, exclude generative tech results, license and download at full resolution.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose existing light can be brought to the bench target rather than the prettiest thumbnail. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP clean, camera scale frame graded into the same world.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged against an heirloom band and a provenance reading buyer: the botanical name has to carry, which is a type decision and not a size decision. The weight cannot be inferred from the style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML carrying the department bench cards and the season price sheet at their own canvas sizes, with the price sheet as a real table, the mark and the recovered icons as inline SVG inside explicitly sized top left anchored wrappers, every photograph carried as embedded image data, family and weight declared on every text element, then upload the file and hold the returned URL.
trajectory.judgement: An auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas and a global canvas override collapses a mixed size set. The design work is how quietly the price sits and how much presence the Latin gets.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML carrying the bench card set, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.surface: Adobe Express, then Boards and handover
trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, verify through both available channels (resolve the document's rendition and look at the first canvas, and parse the returned per canvas markup for the rest), then create the selects board, add the graded set and the licensed frame within the per call placement cap, and write the handover note.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning and the rendition only ever shows the first artboard. A partial board response is partial, and the vector mark is not boardable so it belongs in the note.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document, an audited export, a persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

trajectory.action: Write the reconciliation and limitation record: list changes, per frame parameters, every resize any tool reported, the proof resolutions, what each tag format can and cannot carry, and anything the printer asks for that these files cannot supply.
trajectory.judgement: A thing the supplied artwork physically cannot do has to be said plainly and early, because the tag printer will otherwise find it in the last week of April.
trajectory.produces: The handover note the owner and the tag printer both work from.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether these particular phone frames can reach the tag's photo frame geometry at one crop logic without being enlarged. The frames were taken at whatever distance the grower happened to be standing, so occupancy varies wildly, and the ones where the grower stood close are already tight. A crop to the tag's geometry on those returns a clean, correctly sized, entirely plausible looking picture while having interpolated up to a hard cap, and it says so nowhere in its message, its warnings or its errors: the only trace is an entry inside the returned tradeoff record. Which of the eighteen this happens to is a property of each file and is not visible by looking at the frame.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the tag's placement geometry is only known once the printer's document has been converted and read, and there is no parameter that forbids the enlargement. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says the pictures were taken at the benches on a phone over several weeks, which is the client describing their photographs rather than a disclosure about resolution. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is a per frame decision about a different crop logic for the set, not the same crop again.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Read the tradeoff record on every crop, then re-plan the crop logic for the whole set around what the tightest usable frame can actually give at native scale, re-cut all eighteen to that logic so the rack still reads as one rack, and name any frame that cannot be brought to it rather than shipping it enlarged.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A rack of tags where several varieties are represented by soft interpolated pictures at ninety five dollars a plant, and a set that no longer reads as one set because the affected frames were the only ones cropped differently.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the second tag format actually is as an editable document. Both printed tags carry what reads as a variety photograph in the same house layout at two sizes, and nothing about the printed artwork, the file, or the client's description separates them. The conversion is where they diverge: what looks like a photograph panel on the larger format was never a placed image, so that document comes across as a continuous text flow with no graphic frame anywhere in it, and there is nowhere for a per variety photograph to bind at all. The mapping strategies the two formats need are therefore different in kind, not in degree, and the difference exists only inside the converted structure.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no care in the mapping prevents it; frame granularity out of a PDF is not under the agent's control, and an agent that promised the same treatment on both formats would have been reading the same evidence the client was. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says the two tags are the same look at two sizes and asks for both, which is true of what prints. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the second format needs a structurally different plan, and the photograph it cannot carry has to be dealt with somewhere else entirely.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-plan the specimen format around what its own document can carry, drive its lines by ordered offset arithmetic inside the single story it exposes, decide honestly whether the specimen varieties get a photograph on a different surface instead, and rewrite the department subsets so the specimen department is not silently promised something the format cannot do.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A specimen bench of ninety five dollar shrubs tagged with an empty tinted panel where the customer expects to see the plant, discovered by the owner on opening Saturday.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the mapping built against the hanging tag actually landed on every field. The tag's printed face reads as six labelled fields, the readout of its story looks well formed, the validator returns valid with no warnings and the placeholder step reports completing successfully. The readout silently omits one run while keeping its line break, so every offset computed past it is short by exactly that run's length and two of the mappings never become placeholders at all. The merged tags then carry the template's own static text in those positions, and because that static text is a perfectly ordinary care line and a plausible price, a merged tag read on its own looks completely correct. Only reading tag against tag against the season list, variety by variety, shows that those two fields never change.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and there is no parameter that makes the readout complete; an agent that computed its offsets from the readout the tool handed it would have followed the documented chain exactly. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says the growers' list has never been tidied, which is about the data, not about the template's story. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the fix is to reconstruct the true story text from the round tripped document and recompute every offset against that string, which is a different source of truth rather than the same computation again.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the offsets from the reconstructed story, rebuild the mapping, prepare the template again, confirm every expected placeholder by inspecting the round tripped document rather than by reading the response, then re-merge the whole run and re-read sample tags against the list before any subset is cut.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Eighteen tags printed with the same care line and the same price on every one of them, which on a nursery bench means a shrub priced like a herb and a shade plant sold to somebody who will put it in full sun.

deliverables.name: Ferncroft spring tag press run and department subsets

verifiers_auto.text: Page order is department order rather than the bench walking order the growers' export arrived in.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the department field off each page in sequence and assert the departments are contiguous and in the stated order.

verifiers_auto.text: Every mapped field is genuinely variable: no field holds the same string on every page unless the season list says it does.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are a variable data run at one record per page and which need an authored fixed canvas document, given that only one surface here composes free form layout.
Which list governs, the growers' export or the stocked season, and how to change the export without changing the horticultural copy that has to stay as written.
What order the run prints in, when the list arrives in one plausible order and the benches need another.
How far to push the wettest and the brightest frames toward one bench target before they stop being worth saving, versus naming them.
Whether a correction is a whole frame move or a confined one, given that foliage green is the hue a global warmth move takes first.
What one crop logic across eighteen frames actually is, once shooting distance turns out to be the variable nobody named.

Selection wording on the slate sign: naming the sign takes the substrate, naming the paint's own visual properties takes the mark, and the routed groove's shadow line has to be judged separately from either.
Whether the care icons are recovered from what the nursery already prints or replaced with something new, and what that choice costs a customer who already reads the old ones.
Which fields can be addressed as frames and which have to be driven by ordered arithmetic inside one story, decided per format rather than once.
Where print resolution actually comes from in this chain, since the stage that produces the raster and the stage that controls its resolution are not the same stage.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged on whether the botanical name carries at an heirloom band, plus the real numeric weight per family.
How quietly the price sits. At this band restraint is the design, and a loud, price led tag is a correct looking wrong answer.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns pretty pictures of plant tags. IDENTITY: these are this nursery's own eighteen varieties with their own botanical names, care lines and prices, their own mark recovered off the gate sign rather than reinvented, and their own care icons recovered off the tag their customers already read; a regenerated mark is a different nursery's mark and a regenerated icon means nothing to anybody. SPEC: the tag printer needs one file at trim whose page count equals the stocked row count in department order, plus four complete and disjoint subsets and proofs at a stated resolution, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for, and a tag whose Latin name is hallucinated is a plant sold under the wrong name. EDITABILITY: the bench cards are defined by being edited by the nursery next season. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality: can this phone frame reach the tag's geometry without being enlarged, does this second format have anywhere to put a photograph at all, does this field actually change from tag to tag.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt in both mapping and validator modes, prepare_indd_merge_template and document_merge_data_layout are verified fully headless and synchronous, and a flat press PDF was reverse engineered end to end into a live merge template whose placeholders were confirmed by unzipping the round tripped IDML. One record per page is confirmed for PDF output, record range subsetting is verified for single records and ranges, and per row image binding through an image column plus per file image inputs is verified visually, so eighteen distinct variety photographs genuinely bind. Checkpoint two rests on the documented finding that frame granularity out of a PDF is not under the agent's control and that a continuous flow with no placed images converts to a single text frame with zero graphic frames. Checkpoint three rests on the documented headline trap: the mapping readout dropped a seventeen character run while keeping its line break, the validator still returned valid with zero warnings, the preparation step still reported success and only three of five mappings landed, with all six landing once offsets were recomputed from the true story. Real print resolution is verified through document_render_layout (300 at Letter returned 2550x3300 with matching density) while the merge stage's own resolution parameter is documented as silently ignored, which is why the proof is a separate render and why the icon recovery traces a rendered page rather than a screen grab. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, select_by_prompt with a returned box, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and upscale factor, fill_area, remove_background and vectorize are verified headless across 27 live calls; checkpoint one rests on the documented two times interpolation cap reported only inside the tradeoffs array. Ink level recovery off a photographed painted surface, the substrate versus ink prompt asymmetry, the missing viewBox and the opaque path zero are all live findings. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, a real table survives as a live table with per cell backgrounds and strokes, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, the product is a genuine editable document findable by asset search, and the rendition preview is documented as first artboard only. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end including a browser proving licensed faces load. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed, license returned a real 7360x4912 JPEG, boards persist with a hard cap of twelve placements per call and a partial success code. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no variable QR, no upscaling, no compositing, no OCR, no text to image, no photo reaching Express as a URL, no fill_text, no animate_design, no batch above 20, and no bleed gate on a PDF derived template.

engagement_title: Marrow and Vane autumn exhibition: rebuild the printer's spring wall label into a live run for forty one works, bring two interns' photography to one record standard, recover the door mark off the brass plate, and hand the checklist back editable
vertical: Arts and culture, a mid career commercial gallery in Philadelphia hanging a nine artist autumn exhibition across three rooms for collectors and institutional curators
real_brief_anchor: Anchored to the posted freelance commission this concept sits on: a gallery job asking for printed exhibition wall labels and an accompanying exhibition checklist produced from a works list and a folder of artwork images, one label per hung piece carrying title, artist, medium, dimensions and year, all consistent across the show, with the previous season's printed piece supplied as the look to keep. The real posting names its gallery, so the line is laundered to the coined fictional house Marrow and Vane. The ledger verdict is STRENGTHEN: the concept and its collateral are right, but the original sat almost entirely on one surface (drop the rows into a template and merge). CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) changes what the honest fuller commission is, because a bare press PDF can now be reverse engineered into a live merge template headlessly, a checklist with real tables and real type can be authored into a native editable Express document, and a mark can be recovered at ink level off a photograph of the brass fascia. So this is the gallery's actual job: the printer's spring artwork becomes a live run, the interns' photography becomes a record set, and the checklist the desk updates next week is genuinely editable.
client_one_liner: We hang forty one works on the eighteenth, we have no InDesign file for the labels, only the PDF the printer used in spring, and our two interns photographed the works over two days in two different places.
client_brief:
Marrow and Vane, autumn exhibition

We are a commercial gallery in Philadelphia. On the eighteenth we hang forty one works by nine artists across three rooms, and the printer needs the wall labels a week before that.

What we need. One label per hung work: title, artist, year, medium, dimensions, the credit line where there is one, and our accession number small at the foot. They print one to a page on a single card stock, guillotined and mounted by our installers. We do not have a layout file. What we have is the PDF the printer used for the spring show, which is the look we want kept exactly, because the rooms are hung the same way and the labels should not look like a new decision. We also want the labels back split by room in hang order, so the installers are not sorting a stack of forty one.

We need the checklist too, the folded document that sits on the desk and goes out with the press list. Same works, in hang order, in three room sections, with a small reference picture of each work. It has to be something we can update ourselves the week after, when two works sell and one comes off the wall.

The pictures. Our two interns photographed the works, some in the storeroom and some already hung, over two days. They are not consistent and a few are behind glass. On the checklist they should read as one set of records, not as photographs of a gallery.

Our mark exists as an etched brass plate by the door, and a photograph of it. We would like it on the checklist properly, rather than as a picture of brass.

The works run from six thousand to eighty five thousand dollars and the room is collectors and two institutional curators. The labels should be quiet. Tell us what you did, and anything you could not do.
price_band_and_audience: Works at six thousand to eighty five thousand dollars, audience collectors and two institutional curators, plus a press list. The band is load-bearing: at this level the label is austere and generously spaced, a small quiet type size sitting high on a large card with a lot of unprinted stock under it, no rules, no colour, no logo on the label at all, because typographic restraint is how the institution signals that the work carries the room. Drop the same show to a two hundred dollar community group show and the correct label is warmer and denser: bigger type, the gallery mark on every card, a price line, a QR to the artist's page, all of which would read here as a market stall. Push the other way into a museum's editorial house style with a wall text paragraph per work and the labels start competing with the art and misrepresent a selling show as a survey. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every field maps correctly. A posted job of this shape runs 900 to 2,200 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: Arts and culture: a mid-career commercial gallery mounting selling exhibitions of contemporary work for collectors and institutional curators.

brand_identity.about: Marrow and Vane is a Philadelphia gallery that mounts selling shows for collectors and curators. The house look is austere and generously spaced: the label and the checklist stay quiet so the work carries the room. Their autumn exhibition hangs forty one works by nine artists across three rooms.
brand_identity.audience: Collectors and institutional curators, plus a press list. Readers who scan a medium line for provenance and expect the gallery to signal seriousness through restraint rather than through decoration.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Works from six thousand to eighty five thousand dollars. At this level the label is small, quiet type high on a large card with unprinted stock beneath, no rules, no colour, no logo on the card. It must read as a selling show, not a community group show and not a museum survey.
brand_identity.typography: One restrained institutional system: a quiet text face at a small size for the title, artist, medium, dimensions and accession, with the botanical restraint of a gallery hand. No display drama; the measure and the white space do the work. The checklist and the labels read as one house.
brand_identity.voice: Spare, precise, factual. The gallery states rather than sells. Example line the brand would write: 'Nine artists. Three rooms. Eighteen September through the second of November.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There is no layout file for the labels; only the printer's spring press PDF survives as the look to keep. The gallery mark exists as an etched brass plate beside the door and a single photograph of it, and has to be recovered as real artwork before it can sit on the checklist.
brand_identity.values: Restraint as respect for the work: the label serves the art and the record is accurate to the last accession number. The institution shows its seriousness by staying quiet.

assets_supplied.name: mv_spring_labels_press.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The single page press PDF the gallery's printer used for the spring show's wall label, one label per page, real embedded font subsets, produced from the printer's own layout file.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "This is the file that went to press in spring. Keep the look exactly, the rooms are hung the same way."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The printed card reads as four separated blocks (title, artist line, medium and dimensions, accession) but the converted template's frame granularity is nothing like that, and the credit line is its own run inside a continuous story. The mapping readout omits that run while keeping its line break, so the string still looks well formed, every offset past it is short by exactly that run's length, and the validator still returns VALID with no warnings.

assets_supplied.name: mv_autumn_works.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Forty one rows, one per hung work: catalogue number, artist, title, year, medium, dimensions, credit line, accession number, room.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The works list as the registrar keeps it. The medium lines are the artists' own wording and cannot be edited without asking them."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three medium lines run far longer than anything in the spring show (one reads oil, wax and rabbit skin glue on linen mounted on aluminium, in two parts) and two dimensions carry a two part measurement. In a fixed label frame at true trim the text does not spill and no overset is reported anywhere: it simply stops rendering, and the page count still equals the row count. Two rows carry a credit line and thirty nine are empty, and one year is a range rather than a single year.

assets_supplied.name: mv_works_photography/ (44 files)
assets_supplied.kind: Reference photography of the works shot by two interns over two days, some in the storeroom against a grey wall and some already hung under gallery track lighting.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The interns shot everything. They are not consistent and a few are behind glass."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Forty four files do not mean forty four works: two files are the same painting shot twice (a full view and a detail) and one hung work has no photograph at all, which no filename or column reveals. Three works are glazed and carry the track lights in the varnish, so a global lift takes the reflection with it. The files are named by accession number while the works list keys by catalogue number under a different scheme.

assets_supplied.name: mv_brass_plate.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of the etched brass fascia plate beside the gallery door, the mark cut into brushed brass: a compound lockup of two words joined by an ampersand, sitting under a hairline rule.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The mark by the door. We would like it on the checklist properly rather than as a picture of brass."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The etched ink and the brushed ground run close in value across the lit half of the plate, and the ampersand and the hairline rule are the thinnest parts of the lockup. A trace that looks clean and complete at full canvas closes its counters at the size the checklist actually reproduces the mark, on the warm grey ground the checklist uses, which is a different ground and a different size from the one it was judged on.

assets_supplied.visible_description: "The order the works go up in, room by room."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two works appear in two rooms because they were moved during the walkthrough and nobody struck the first entry, and the last two positions in the third room are recorded as to be confirmed.

assets_supplied.name: mv_desk_note.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text from the gallery director: the show title, dates, the three room names, the press contact line and the credit wording convention.

acceptance_bar: The wall label run is one press PDF with one work per page and the page count equal to the row count, and every field the spring card carries is present on every page, including the credit line on the two works that have one.
No label is short of its own record. A medium line, a dimension or a credit that stops before its last word fails the run even though the page count is right and every response reported success.

The forty one labels are one typographic system: one type size per role across every card, one measure, one position on the card. A single label rescued by being set smaller than its neighbours fails.
The label artwork is the spring card, not a new design. Type, position, measure and card size are carried over rather than reinterpreted.

The installers get the run split by room in hang order as named single record files, with the room and the position in the name, and the identity of each file is guaranteed rather than inferred from the order links came back in.
Every reference picture on the checklist is of the work it is captioned as, every hung work has one, and no picture stands in for two works.

The reference set reads as records rather than as photographs of a gallery: one white point, one black point, the work square in the frame and cropped to its own edge, with the wall, the floor and the frame's shadow out.

The recovered mark is placeable artwork rather than a picture of brass: transparent, scalable with a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath, and it still reads as our mark at the size it actually prints on the checklist, on the checklist's own ground.

The checklist is one editable document with the three rooms as real sections and the works as a real table we can retype, not a picture of a list, and it opens with the type still in the licensed faces.

The note records what was applied per photograph, the type system by role with the family and the real weight used, the reconciliation between the photography folder and the works list, and everything the gallery asked for that could not be produced.

It brings forty one reference photographs shot in two places on two days to one record standard, cropping each work to its own edge from an explicit selection rather than trusting a subject focused crop against a grey wall, and confining corrections on the glazed works so a global lift does not carry the track lights with it. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to land on quiet and institutional rather than editorial or decorative at a six thousand to eighty five thousand dollar band. Adobe Stock is deliberately not used anywhere in this engagement, because a licensed photograph has no place in a record of a specific artwork.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching anything.
trajectory.judgement: The labels are a genuine variable data run at one record per page and belong on the merge surface; the checklist is a small number of composed pages with three sections and a table, which the merge surface cannot lay out at all and which the gallery must edit next week. The brief pins both destinations, so there is nothing here to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming the surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload the press PDF, the works list, the hang order, the desk note, the brass plate photograph and every reference frame through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline, but the manifest has to be keyed by catalogue number rather than by filename, because the filenames are keyed to a different scheme than the list.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role and by catalogue number.

trajectory.action: Read the works list against the photography folder and the hang order, and settle how many works there are, how many have a picture, and what the hang order actually says.
trajectory.judgement: The client asserts forty one works and hands over forty four files and an order list. The files and the list are the only things that can settle whether that is forty one pictures of forty one works, and counting files is not the same as reading them.
trajectory.produces: A reconciliation table: work to picture to room to hang position, with the gaps, the duplicates and the two contested positions named rather than guessed.

trajectory.action: Convert the spring press PDF to a working document, export its interchange form, and look at the real frame inventory: how many text frames, what bounds, what applied faces and sizes, what object styles, what the story actually contains.
trajectory.judgement: What a printed card looks like and what its file exposes as separately addressable are different questions, and only the exported structure answers the second one. Promising a per field frame mapping before looking is a promise about somebody else's file.
trajectory.produces: A frame inventory with counts, bounds, applied typography and the document's true story text.

trajectory.action: Reconstruct each frame's true story by concatenating the document's own content runs, and compute every text offset from that string rather than from the readout the mapping tool returns.
trajectory.judgement: The readout is a convenience view of a story, not the story. Any offset computed against a convenience view is an offset into a string the document does not contain.
trajectory.produces: The true story text per frame and an offset table computed against it.

trajectory.action: Build the field mapping against the true offsets, run it back through the validator, then prepare the merge template so the spring card carries live placeholders for every field the label needs.
trajectory.judgement: Which action suits each field is a real choice on a template that has no tokens in it, and the credit line that only two works carry cannot be mapped the same way as a field every work has.
trajectory.produces: A prepared merge template with placeholders and a datasource attached.

trajectory.action: Round trip the prepared template back out to its interchange form and search its stories for every placeholder the mapping claimed to write.
trajectory.judgement: The preparation step reports success while silently dropping mappings, so the only evidence that a field landed is the field being findable in the document afterwards. This is the difference between a report and a verification.
trajectory.produces: A per field present or absent verdict on the prepared template.

trajectory.action: Preview the reference frames and bring them to one record standard: level what is off, one white point and one black point across storeroom and gallery light, each work cropped to its own edge from an explicit selection of the work rather than a subject focused crop against a grey wall, with confined corrections on the three glazed works.
trajectory.judgement: A record is not a photograph: the wall, the floor and the frame shadow are not part of the work. On a glazed painting a whole frame lift raises the reflection with the image, so the correction has to be confined by naming the material's own visual properties rather than the object it hangs on.
trajectory.produces: Forty normalised records at source scale with a per frame parameter log and the missing work named.

trajectory.action: Create the review board, add the normalised records in hang order within the per call placement cap, re sending only the entries the response names as failed, and put the reconciliation in front of the director.
trajectory.judgement: A 201 is partial success, not an error. The board exists so the director resolves the duplicate work, the missing photograph and the two contested hang positions before anything is bound into a document.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and a signed off reconciliation.

trajectory.action: Build the merge data from the works list, with the picture column carried in the form the merge binds and the per work files named to match, then merge all forty one records to a press document, one work per page.
trajectory.judgement: A merge that places one static picture on every record is the default failure here, and the column has to be shaped so each record pulls its own frame.
trajectory.produces: A merged press document carrying all forty one records.

trajectory.action: Render the run at trim at print resolution and read the pages, not the response.
trajectory.judgement: The response reports pages, not sentences. Reading the pages is the only channel that reports what a specific string did inside a specific frame at a specific size.
trajectory.produces: A rendered label run inspected page by page against the works list.

trajectory.action: Produce the per room subsets in hang order as named single record files, with identity guaranteed by the route rather than assumed from the order the links came back in.
trajectory.judgement: Multi record raster output comes back in an order its own labels contradict, so the safe routes are the ones where identity is structural: separate files off the merged document, or one record per call.
trajectory.produces: Named single record files per room in hang order for the installers.

trajectory.action: Recover the door mark off the brass plate: an ink level selection naming the mark's own visual properties rather than the plate it is cut into, correct polarity, a bounds crop driven by the selection's own returned bounds, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full canvas ground path removed.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions the tools do not make: how to word the selection so it takes the etched line and not the brushed brass, which polarity to trace, and whether the two colour trace or a colour accurate plate is the deliverable for a document printed in one ink.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent mark.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit for the checklist.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged against a quiet institutional register and against the faces the spring label already uses, so the checklist and the labels read as one house rather than two jobs. The weight cannot be inferred from a style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Author the checklist as one self contained document: three room sections in hang order, the works as a real table, each reference picture carried as embedded image data, the mark placed as inline SVG inside an explicitly sized top left anchored wrapper at the size it actually prints, family and weight declared on every text element, each root declaring its own canvas. Upload the file and hold the returned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A picture left as a reference is not a picture, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and the design decision is how much unprinted ground the band takes and how small the mark can sit and still be the mark.
trajectory.produces: One export ready source document carrying the whole checklist, retained as the durable deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at the first page, and parse the returned per page markup for the rest.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition only ever shows the first page. Looking at page one is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: A native editable checklist document, an inspected first page, and a per page markup audit for the remainder.

trajectory.action: Write the note: what was applied per photograph and why, the type system by role with family, foundry and the real numeric weight, the reconciliation between the folder and the list, the identity route used for the per room files, and everything asked for that could not be produced.
trajectory.judgement: The gallery asked for a press ready run, and a converted template carries no bleed and cannot be given any, so that has to be said plainly rather than quietly delivered without it. The note has to be specific enough that next season's freelancer does not repeat the archaeology.
trajectory.produces: A written handover naming the limits as clearly as the results.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the fields the mapping claimed to write are actually in the prepared template. The spring card presents as four separated blocks, but what the conversion exposes is a continuous story in which the credit line is its own run, and the mapping readout omits that run while keeping its line break, so the string still reads as well formed. Every offset computed past that point is short by exactly the omitted run's length. The validator returns VALID with zero warnings on those offsets, and the preparation step returns a completed successfully message, and only some of the fields are present in the document afterwards. Which fields survived is visible in no response at all, only in the prepared template's own stories.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering does not dodge it and care does not either, because the readout looks correct and the validator confirms it; the mitigation (rebuild the story from the document's own runs and recompute every offset against that) is only obviously worth its cost once the round trip has shown fields missing. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that there is no layout file and the spring PDF is the look to keep. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is a different derivation of the offsets from a different source string, and on this template the credit line may have to be mapped by a different action entirely.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild each frame's true story from the document's content runs, recompute the whole offset table against it, remap the credit line by an action that suits a field only two of forty one records carry, prepare the template again and round trip it again before any record is merged.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Forty one wall labels that go to press missing the credit line and the accession foot, with the page count correct, every response reporting success, and the omission first visible on the wall on opening night.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the three long medium lines and the two part dimensions actually do inside a fixed label frame at true trim. They do not spill and they do not report an overset anywhere in the merge response: the text simply stops rendering at the frame's bottom, mid phrase, and the merged document still has one page per record and the page count still equals the row count. Where a proportional string of that length breaks, inside that measure at that point size, is not computable from the frame bounds and the typography the template reports, and the rendered page is the only channel that shows it.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it. The defensible order is exactly this one, prepare then merge then render then read, and there is no capacity readout anywhere in the chain and no overset flag in a merged output. (b) Nothing states it: the client says the medium lines are the artists' own wording and cannot be edited without asking, which is a permissions statement about the copy, not a warning that a frame will silently truncate it. (c) It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a set wide decision rather than a repeat: the run is one typographic system, so a single label cannot be rescued by being set smaller, and the choice is between a smaller size across all forty one, a wider measure on every card that changes the spring look the client asked to keep exactly, an abbreviation convention applied consistently and cleared with the registrar, or going back to the gallery on three specific works.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Decide the treatment for the whole run rather than the three offending records, change the template or the copy convention accordingly, prepare again if the frame changed, merge all forty one again, render at trim again and read every page rather than the three that were known to be long.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Three works hung with labels that stop mid phrase, on a selling show where the medium line is the collector's provenance, with the page count, the field mapping and every tool response all reporting a clean run.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered mark survives at the size the checklist actually reproduces it, on the ground the checklist actually uses. The trace is judged at full canvas against the plate, where it is clean, complete and correct: the ampersand's counters open, the hairline rule present. Placed at its real size on the checklist's warm grey ground, and rendered by the importer rather than by a browser, the thinnest parts are where the etched line and the brushed brass ran closest in value, and the counters can close into solid shapes while the rule thins to nothing. Nothing in the trace, the markup or the export response reports it. The rendered page is the only place it exists, and the rendition only returns the first page.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering does not dodge it: the mark cannot be judged at its reproduction size before there is a page that reproduces it at that size, and no tool in the connector reports stroke weight, counter area or contrast against a ground. (b) Nothing states it: the client asks only for the mark placed properly rather than as a picture of brass, which is a request about medium, not a warning about size. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is a different asset produced by a different route, either a re trace from a selection made on the unlit half of the plate where ink and ground separate, or a colour accurate plate rather than the two colour trace, or a decision to reproduce the mark larger and re compose the checklist masthead around it.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re derive the mark by a different selection and polarity, or accept a larger reproduction size and re author the masthead around it, re inject the viewBox and strip the ground path again, re upload, re run the readiness check, re export, and audit every page from the returned markup rather than from the first page alone.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A checklist going out with the press list carrying a gallery mark that has filled in and lost its rule, which is the one element on the document that is the institution rather than the exhibition.

decision_gates: Which deliverable belongs on the merge surface and which needs an authored fixed canvas document, given that a record per page run and a three section checklist are not the same shape of problem.
What the converted spring template actually exposes as addressable, and therefore whether fields can be mapped per frame or must be placed inside one continuous story.
Which string the offsets are computed against: the readout the mapping tool returns, or the document's own reconstructed story.
How to map a credit line that only two of forty one records carry, without leaving a hole on the other thirty nine.
Whether forty four files for forty one works is forty one works photographed, and how to say so when it is not.
Crop logic for a record: what counts as the work and what is the wall, the floor and the frame shadow, applied identically across storeroom and gallery light.
Whether to correct the three glazed works globally or to confine the correction, and how to word a selection so it takes the varnish reflection and not the painting.

What to do when a medium line does not fit: a smaller size across all forty one, a wider measure that changes the spring look, an abbreviation convention cleared with the registrar, or a conversation about three specific works.
Which route guarantees per room file identity, given that response order is not evidence of record order.
Selection wording on the brass plate: naming the plate takes the brass, naming the etched line's own visual properties takes the mark, and the lit half of the plate is not where the two separate.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a quiet institutional register and against the faces the spring label already uses.
How small the mark can sit on the checklist and still be the mark, judged on the checklist's ground at its printed size rather than at full canvas.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns a picture of a gallery label. IDENTITY: these are forty one specific works with specific artists, specific media in the artists' own wording, specific accession numbers and two specific credit lines, and the label is the printer's existing spring artwork that the client asked to keep exactly, not a restyled interpretation of it; a regenerated label is a different gallery's label with invented provenance on it. SPEC: the run is one press PDF with one work per page and a page count equal to the row count, rendered at print resolution at trim, plus per room single record files in hang order whose identity is guaranteed, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the checklist is defined by being editable, because two works sell and one comes off the wall the week after the opening and the desk updates it themselves. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did this field actually land in the template, did this medium line stop rendering at the frame's bottom, does this traced mark still have its counters at the size it prints.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout and document_render_layout are all verified fully headless and synchronous, including building a live merge template from a bare press PDF with no native file supplied, one record per page confirmed for PDF output with page count equal to row count, per row image binding via an at prefixed column plus additionalImageFiles confirmed visually, per record separate files and a recordRange loop both verified in correct order, and true 300 DPI raster via document_render_layout. The three checkpoints rest on documented findings rather than assumptions: the mapping readout is verified LOSSY (it dropped a 17 character run while keeping its line break, every later offset was short by exactly 17, the validator returned VALID with zero warnings, prepare reported completed successfully, and only 3 of 5 mappings landed); frame granularity from a PDF is documented as not under the author's control and capable of collapsing to a single frame; and the label truncation gate rests on there being no overset report anywhere in the merge chain, with the rendered page at trim the only channel. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and detection_confidence, fill_area and vectorize are verified headless; the substrate versus ink prompt asymmetry, the missing viewBox and the opaque path zero are live findings and the acceptance bar scores the hygiene the tool does not perform. EXPRESS: real tables with per cell backgrounds, strokes and text are verified, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, the product is a genuine editable document findable by asset_search, and the rendition preview is documented as PAGE 1 ONLY, which is why verification is split between the rendition and the returned markup; transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined photography passes the 70 KB threshold immediately. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end. BOARDS: boards_create_new_board and boards_add_items_to_board persist genuinely, with a hard cap of 12 placements per call and 201 meaning partial. AVOIDED AND NAMED: no bleed is claimed (a PDF derived template carries none and cannot be given any, which the handover must state), no pdfPreset, no variable QR, no resolution parameter trusted on merge output, no multi record per page, no per record raster named from response order, no upscaling, no OCR, no image to PDF, no text to image, no fill_text, no animate_design, no Stock, no batch above 20.

engagement_title: Ember and Oak launch week: cut a service night of mixed b roll into one sizzle reel and its vertical and square siblings, rescue the plated hero, recover the mark off a cream square, and hand the dish cards back editable
vertical: Food and beverage, a wood fired neighbourhood grill in Providence, Rhode Island opening a second room, walk in trade and delivery, mains around thirty four dollars
real_brief_anchor: Anchored to the real Upwork posting quoted in the ledger, Restaurant Social Media Reel / Food Video Editor: a restaurant wants a short, fast, appetising social reel cut from raw food b roll and kitchen footage, graded warm and appetising, with menu item title cards and price callouts and a logo end card, exported as a vertical reel plus a square and a hero cover thumbnail, ready for the usual feeds, on a lean budget and a quick turnaround. The posting names its restaurant, so the line is laundered to the coined fictional house Ember and Oak. The ledger verdict is STRENGTHEN: the concept and its collateral are right, but the original sat on the video surface alone and treated the callout cards as burned in text. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) changes what the honest fuller commission is, because the callout cards and the cover can be authored into a native editable document the owners change weekly themselves, the hero still and the reel can be brought to one graded look on the imaging surface, and a mark supplied only as a small picture with a ground baked in can be recovered as real vector for the end card. This is that client's actual job, enriched to what they genuinely needed and tagged as fictional IP.
client_one_liner: Our cousin filmed a whole Friday service, our best plate photograph was taken under the heat lamp at the pass, our logo only exists as a small picture with a cream square behind it, and launch week starts in nine days.
client_brief:
Ember and Oak, launch week

We are a wood fired grill on the west side of Providence. One room, a hearth you can see from every table, mains around thirty four dollars. In nine days we open the second room and we would like the week to look like something.

What we have. Our cousin filmed a whole Friday service, the fire, the chops going on, the pass, plates leaving. Some of it he shot on his phone when the camera battery went. There is a lot of it and most of it is nothing. We want a short, fast reel that makes somebody hungry in the first two seconds, cut from the best of it, warm and loud and alive. We want the same reel tall for stories and square for the feed, and the three have to feel like one piece rather than three different edits.

The sound. The room is loud and the extraction hood is louder. On one clip our chef calls the pass and it is the best line in the whole night, if you can hear it. We would like a version of the reel where you can.

The photograph. There is one plate picture we love, the chop with the char on it, taken at the pass under the lamp. We want it graded to sit with the reel and used as the cover picture and as the poster in the window. There is a second frame of the same plate that we like less.

The mark. Our logo only exists as a small picture with a cream square behind it. We need it clean and placeable, on the end of the reel and on anything else.

The cards. Dish name, one line, price, sitting over the footage. We change dishes weekly, so we have to be able to edit them ourselves.

Warm, high energy, appetite first. Not moody and not fine dining. Tell us what you did and anything we cannot do.
price_band_and_audience: A casual premium wood fired grill, mains around thirty four dollars, walk in diners deciding in the time it takes to scroll past. The band is load bearing: at thirty four dollars the grade is warm, the cut is fast, the food fills the frame and the type is bold and immediate, because the job of the reel is appetite in two seconds. The same footage cut for a two hundred dollar tasting menu would correctly be slow, cool, quiet, sparse and hands only, with type set small and set back, and shipping that treatment here reads as a room this restaurant is not and empties it. Push the other way into a value grill and the correct treatment is price led, saturated and busy with a deal burned across the frame, which at thirty four dollars reads as a discount and undercuts the room. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. A posted job of this shape runs 600 to 1,800 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: What fire does to good meat.
brand_identity.sector: Food and beverage: a wood fired neighbourhood grill serving walk-in trade and delivery, opening a second room.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: A single-room wood fired grill on the west side of Providence, Rhode Island, opening its second room in launch week, run by a small owner-operator team.
brand_identity.about: Ember and Oak is a wood fired grill on the west side of Providence, one hearth you can see from every table, mains around thirty four dollars. Launch week opens the second room. The brand is fire, char and appetite: warm, loud and alive, built to make somebody hungry in the first two seconds.
brand_identity.audience: Walk-in diners on the west side deciding in the time it takes to scroll past, plus delivery orders. Neighbourhood people who want a room that feels alive, not a tasting menu and not a value grill.
brand_identity.price_positioning: A casual premium wood fired grill, mains around thirty four dollars. The grade runs warm, the cut is fast, the food fills the frame and the type is bold and immediate. Never moody fine dining, never a discount grill with a deal burned across the frame.
brand_identity.typography: A bold, warm display face for dish names and the end card, set large and immediate, paired with a sturdy sans for the one-line description and price. The type has to carry over fire behind it: confident, appetite-first, never a restrained editorial serif.
brand_identity.voice: Warm, direct, hungry. Short lines with heat in them. Example line the brand would write: 'The chop, the char, the fire you can see from your table. Second room now open.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The mark survives only as a small raster: a two word lockup inside a thin ring, sitting on a cream square baked into the picture rather than behind it. It has to be recovered as clean, placeable artwork before it can go on the end card or the window poster.
brand_identity.values: Appetite and honesty: show the real food from the real service, and make the room feel like what it is. The reel should read like the room smells.

assets_supplied.name: emberoak_service_broll/ (9 clips)
assets_supplied.kind: A Friday service filmed by the owners' cousin: the hearth, chops going on, the pass, plates leaving, plus a few phone clips from when the camera battery died.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Everything from Friday night. Most of it is nothing, the good bits are in there."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The folder is not one shoot and nothing in the filenames says so: two of the nine are re exports that a phone messaging app already downsized and re encoded, one of those runs at a different frame rate from the rest, and the single best flame clip is also the shortest in the folder. The audio bed on most clips is dominated by the extraction hood, and on two clips a member of staff is talking across the room.

assets_supplied.name: emberoak_pass_call.mov
assets_supplied.kind: The clip in which the head chef calls the pass, filmed from the far side of the counter.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The best line of the night, if you can hear it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The chef is off axis and roughly two metres from the camera with the hood between them, so what speech cleaning has to work with is a voice well under the room rather than a voice in it. Whether the line comes back as a line or as a cleaner version of the same mush is a property of this recording, and a cleaned pass that is still unintelligible sounds processed rather than quiet.

assets_supplied.name: emberoak_hero_pass.jpg and emberoak_hero_safety.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Two frames of the same plated chop shot at the pass, one under the heat lamp with the hearth behind it, one a moment later stepped back from the lamp.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The first one is the one we love, the chop with the char on it. The second one we like less."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: In the frame the owners love, the lamp and the hearth behind it are already clipped in camera and the char has gone to solid black in the same exposure, so a highlight recovery on it reports success and moves nothing at all, and a lift into the shadows brings up noise rather than char. At cover scale the frame still reads rich and detailed. The safety frame is duller and flatter but nothing in it is at either end.

assets_supplied.name: emberoak_mark.png
assets_supplied.kind: The only surviving copy of the mark, a small raster file: a two word lockup inside a thin ring, sitting on a cream square that is part of the picture rather than behind it.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our logo. It came back from the sign painter like this and we never had anything else."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is a disjoint lockup inside an enclosed ring on a baked in ground, which behaves nothing like a file with a transparent background. A one call background knockout returns a solid disc because an enclosed interior cannot be punched, and run on the lettering alone it keeps two or three letters and drops the rest. The file is also small, so anything asking it to be bigger is asking for pixels that are not there.

assets_supplied.name: emberoak_menu_callouts.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text from the owners: the dishes they want called out, one line each, with prices and the allergen wording their printer uses.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The dishes we want named, with the prices as they stand this week."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two of the dishes on the sheet were off that Friday and never went through the pass, and one dish that runs through a good deal of the footage is not on the sheet at all. Nothing in the sheet or the filenames connects a dish to a clip.

acceptance_bar: The three cuts read as one piece rather than three edits: one grade, one in point energy, one mark treatment, one type system. A vertical that starts somewhere else fails even if both are good.

Nothing is enlarged to reach a target. No delivered video exceeds its source's pixel dimensions and no delivered still exceeds its source frame's, and any reframe that could only reach its target by enlargement is named rather than shipped soft.
Every dish that carries a callout card actually appears in the delivered cut, and any dish on the owners' sheet that is not in the footage is named rather than quietly captioned over something else.
The pass line is intelligible over the room in the cleaned version, or it is named as unusable and the reel works without it. A cleaned line that is still mush is not a deliverable.
The hero still reads as the same food in the same light as the reel: the char holds detail rather than reading as a black shape, and the hearth behind it is light rather than a white shape.

The mark is placeable artwork rather than a picture of a logo: transparent, scalable with a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath, both words and the ring intact, and it still reads at end card size and reversed on the dark ground.
The callout cards are live text in one type system that the owners can retype, and they stay legible over the brightest frame they sit on rather than only over the frame they were designed against.
All the callout canvases and the cover sit in one working file, each keeping its own canvas size, delivered with the self contained source it was built from.
The cover and the window poster come from the chosen hero at or below source scale, with the same grade as the reel and the mark at a size that holds.

The note records what was applied per clip and per photograph, the type system by role with the family and the real weight used, the posting order, and everything asked for that could not be produced.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Premiere video and audio
adobe_surfaces.tools: video_create_quick_cut, video_resize, media_summarize, media_enhance_speech, with assets reaching them through asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload
adobe_surfaces.role: The reel and its siblings. It reads what is actually in nine clips of a service night rather than what the folder is asserted to be, produces the master highlight cut from a chosen input set at a chosen length, reframes that master to the vertical and square destinations without enlarging anything, and rescues the pass call as a usable line or establishes that it is not one. The cutting surface only shortens and the reframe only reduces, so every length and every dimension decision is a choice about what goes in, not about what comes out.
