adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_adjust_highlights and image_adjust_dark_portions, image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_invert_selection, image_fill_area, image_remove_background, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs and detection_confidence), image_apply_color_overlay, image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Two separate jobs. It brings the plated hero to the reel's warm target and finds out what is actually recoverable in a frame shot under a heat lamp, with confined corrections where a whole frame move would take the plate rim or the hearth with it, and it cuts the cover and the window poster from the chosen master at or below source scale. Then it recovers the mark off a baked in cream ground, which needs the route the enclosed ring and the disjoint lettering actually allow rather than the one call route, plus the vector hygiene the tracing tool does not perform.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The dish callout cards and the cover as one native editable document, which is the only surface in the connector that composes free form fixed canvas layout and the only reason the owners can change a dish next week without re commissioning. The cards sit at the video canvas sizes so they drop over the cut, every frame behind them is carried as embedded image data because a reference renders as an empty grey box at full success, the mark goes in as inline SVG so it stays vector on the end card, and family and weight are declared on every text element.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Fonts
adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: The type system for the callout cards, the end card and the window poster. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to land warm, bold and immediate at a thirty four dollar walk in band rather than on the restrained editorial serif a food brief attracts by reflex. Numeric weights are non standard per family and cannot be inferred from a style name, every name must be laundered into canonical PostScript form before the kit call because one bad name kills the whole kit, and the CSS must use the returned slug or the face falls back silently.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (entityScope StockAsset, SHORT query, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the one thing a service night could not provide, a charred oak and ember texture band for the window poster's ground, IP clean and at genuine camera scale with generative candidates excluded, graded into the same warm world as the reel so it does not read as bought. The Boards half persists the owners' sign off set, the chosen hero and the frames the cards sit over, placed within the per call cap with a partial success read as partial.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching anything.
trajectory.judgement: The cut and its reframes are video work with hard constraints; the callout cards have to be an authored fixed canvas document because the owners change dishes weekly, and burned in captions would make every weekly change a re commission. The brief pins that requirement, so there is nothing here to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming the surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload the nine clips, the pass call, both hero frames, the mark and the callout sheet through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline: a manifest keyed by role so that thirty artefacts later the agent still knows which URL is which clip.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Probe every clip for what it actually contains and what it actually is, rather than accepting the folder as one shoot.
trajectory.judgement: The client describes one Friday night. Nine files from two devices, some of them round tripped through a messaging app, are not one shoot, and the difference decides which clips can carry a vertical reframe and which cannot.
trajectory.produces: A per clip readout: content, true dimensions, frame rate, provenance and audio condition.

trajectory.action: Triage the folder into a candidate set for the cut, ordered, with the clips that cannot survive a reframe excluded from the ones that must.
trajectory.judgement: The cutting surface only shortens and the reframe only reduces, so the input set is the whole design decision: a clip that cannot reach the vertical destination without enlargement must not be the clip the vertical opens on.
trajectory.produces: A ranked candidate set with the exclusions and their reasons written down.

trajectory.action: Clean the pass call and listen to what comes back, then decide whether the line is usable at all.
trajectory.judgement: Speech cleaning raises a voice out of a room; it does not put a voice into one. A line that is still unintelligible after cleaning is worse than no line, because it sounds processed.
trajectory.produces: A cleaned pass call and a written verdict on whether it carries the reel.

trajectory.action: Produce the master highlight cut at the target length from the chosen input set.
trajectory.judgement: Length and input are the only levers, and the first two seconds are the whole brief. What goes in is chosen for what should survive.
trajectory.produces: A master sizzle cut at the target length.

trajectory.action: Watch the master cut through and write down what is actually in it, dish by dish and shot by shot, and read that against the owners' callout sheet.
trajectory.judgement: A cut is not a list of the clips that went into it. What survived, in what order and for how long, is the specification for everything downstream, and the callout sheet was written by people describing a menu rather than a video.
trajectory.produces: A shot list of the delivered cut reconciled against the callout sheet, with the mismatches named.

trajectory.action: Reframe the master to the vertical and the square destinations, reading what each reframe returns rather than the success message.
trajectory.judgement: The reframe reduces and does not enlarge, so a destination it cannot reach is a fact about the source, and the answer is a different source or a different destination size, never an enlargement.
trajectory.produces: A vertical and a square cut derived from the same master, with what each operation reported recorded.

trajectory.action: Preview both hero frames properly, level what is off, and take the frame the owners prefer toward the reel's warm target.
trajectory.judgement: The grade target is set by the cut, not by the photograph, because the cover has to read as a frame from the same night.
trajectory.produces: A graded candidate hero with the parameters recorded.

trajectory.action: Work the extremes of that frame: pull the lamp and the hearth back, open the char, confining each move to the region it belongs to by naming the material's own visual properties rather than the object it sits on.
trajectory.judgement: A whole frame move here takes the plate rim with the hearth and the sauce with the char. Prompt wording is the whole gate on a confined correction, and naming the object pulls the selection to the plate.
trajectory.produces: A hero with its recovery attempts made and their results looked at rather than assumed.

trajectory.action: Cut the cover and the window poster crops from the chosen hero at or below source scale, reading the tradeoffs every crop returns.
trajectory.judgement: The tradeoffs record is the only channel that reports what a crop did to the frame's dimensions and it carries no warning language. A poster that reaches its size by interpolation is a soft poster in a window at eye level.
trajectory.produces: Cover and poster masters with their tradeoff records captured.

trajectory.action: Recover the mark off the cream ground: an ink level selection naming the mark's own visual properties, correct polarity, a bounds crop driven by the selection's own returned bounds, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full canvas ground path removed, plus a knockout variant for the dark end card.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions the tools do not make: how to word the selection, which polarity to trace, and which variant carries the end card. The one call knockout is the wrong instrument on an enclosed ring and on disjoint lettering, and the file is small, so nothing here may ask for pixels the file does not have.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent mark and a variant for the dark ground.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the charred oak and ember band, filter to photography, exclude generative candidates, license and download at full resolution, then create the sign off board and add the hero, the poster ground and the frames the cards sit over within the per call cap.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose existing light can be brought to the warm target rather than the prettiest thumbnail. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero. A 201 is partial success, so only the entries the response names as failed are re sent.
trajectory.produces: One licensed camera scale frame graded into the same world, and a persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged against a thirty four dollar walk in room and a two second decision. The weight cannot be inferred from the style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained document carrying a callout card per dish that survived the cut at the video canvas sizes, the cover, the window poster and the end card, with every backing frame carried as embedded image data, the mark placed as inline SVG inside an explicitly sized top left anchored wrapper, and family and weight declared on every text element. Upload the file and hold the returned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A frame left as a reference is not a frame, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override is what collapses a mixed size set. The design decision is how the card holds its own against fire behind it without becoming a box that hides the food.
trajectory.produces: One export ready source document carrying the whole card set, retained as the durable deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at the first canvas, and parse the returned per canvas markup for the rest.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition only ever shows the first canvas. Looking at canvas one is not looking at the deliverable, and the cards are the deliverable the owners touch every week.
trajectory.produces: A native editable card set, an inspected first canvas, and a per canvas markup audit for the remainder.

trajectory.action: Write the note: what was applied per clip and per photograph, the type system by role with family, foundry and the real numeric weight, the posting order across the three cuts, the dish reconciliation, and everything asked for that could not be produced.
trajectory.judgement: The owners asked for things the route cannot give and are entitled to know which, in their own terms rather than in tool terms. The note has to be specific enough that next season's freelancer does not repeat the triage.
trajectory.produces: A written handover naming the limits as clearly as the results.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the highlight cut actually kept. The cutting surface only shortens and it selects its own moments: the only levers are which clips go in and how long the result is, and there is no shot list, no in point report and no way to nominate a moment. The response is a finished reel that looks entirely plausible, and the single best flame clip is also the shortest in the folder, which is exactly the kind of moment a highlight pass can pass over. Which dishes survived, in what order and for how long, is a property of this input set and this length and is visible only by watching the returned cut and writing down what is in it.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering does not dodge it and neither does care, because nothing about the input predicts the selection and no parameter constrains it; the mitigation, feeding a smaller and more deliberately ordered input set, is only obviously worth its cost once a first cut has been seen to drop something the reel is built on. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says most of the footage is nothing and asks for the best of it, which is a description of the material, not a statement about what a pass will keep. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is a different input set, sometimes a different target length, and it changes the downstream design, because a callout card can only name a dish that is in the cut.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re choose the input set and its order, re cut, watch the result and write the shot list again, then re plan which dishes get a callout card and in what order, and re reconcile that plan against the owners' sheet before a single card is authored.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A reel whose two second hook is not the fire, carrying callout cards for two dishes that never went through the pass that night and none for the dish that is on screen longest, with every response in the run having reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether there is anything left to recover in the frame the owners love. It was shot under the heat lamp with the hearth behind it, and the lamp, the hearth and the plate rim are already clipped in camera while the char has gone to solid black in the same exposure. A highlight recovery on that region reports success and moves nothing at all: the readout is that nothing changed, which is not an error and is not reported as one. A shadow lift on the char brings up noise rather than char. At cover scale the frame still reads rich and detailed, so looking at it small is not evidence. Which of the two supplied frames can actually carry the cover is a property of these two exposures and is knowable only by attempting the recovery on both and looking at the results at full size.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter prevents it: clipping is a property of the capture, no tool in the connector reads a level or reports a clipped region, and the client has already told the agent which frame they prefer. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says one frame was taken under the lamp and the other is liked less, which is a preference, not a disclosure. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is a different master, the safety frame, which is duller and flatter and therefore needs a different grade to reach the same warm target the cut is on, and the cover and the poster then have to be re cut from a frame with a different composition.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Attempt the recovery on both frames, look at each at full size rather than at cover scale, switch the hero master if the preferred frame cannot hold, build a different grade to bring the flatter frame to the cut's target, re cut the cover and the poster from the new master's composition, and tell the owners plainly why the frame they love is not the frame that shipped.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A window poster at eye level and a cover thumbnail in which the char is a black shape and the hearth is a white shape, on a restaurant whose entire proposition is what fire does to meat.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the thing the callout cards are built on. A caption that has to stay legible over fire behind it is authored the natural way as a softened panel behind the type, or as type carrying its own separation from the frame, and this importer discards a blur outright, drops a text shadow, drops a blend mode, drops a text stroke (leaving stroked type fully invisible) and truncates a layered shadow to its first layer, every one of them at a successful response with no warning of any kind. The returned per canvas markup is the only channel that reports it, and the document's rendition returns the first canvas only, so the remaining cards can be checked no other way. Whether what survives is still a legible card over the brightest frame it sits on is visible only after the export.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the normalisation happens at import and the import is the last step; and getting it right first time presumes knowing which of several plausible constructions survives, which no tool reports and no checklist enumerates. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for a dish name, a line and a price over the footage, and the legibility line in the acceptance bar is the client's own requirement, not a warning. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is a different construction, a solid or gradient panel that is a real shape rather than an effect, or a backing plate produced upstream on the imaging surface and carried in as embedded image data, and the card has to be re composed around whichever it is.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re author the cards around constructions that survive rather than around effects that do not, produce any softened ground upstream as a raster if that is the route chosen, re upload, re run the readiness check, re export, and audit every canvas from the returned markup rather than from the first one.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A card set handed over as the thing the owners edit every week in which the type sits directly on flame on every canvas after the first, unreadable at the size anyone actually sees it, with the export having reported success throughout.

deliverables.name: Ember and Oak launch reel set, master plus vertical and square
deliverables.spec: One master sizzle cut built from a chosen and defensible input set, plus a vertical and a square derived from that same master so the three read as one piece with one grade and one in point energy, none of them enlarged to reach its destination and any destination the source cannot reach named rather than shipped soft. Delivered with the cleaned pass call version where the line is intelligible, or with a written verdict that it is not, and with the shot list of what is actually in the delivered cut.

deliverables.name: Ember and Oak hero photography
deliverables.spec: The plated hero brought to the cut's warm target with the char holding detail and the hearth reading as light rather than as a white shape, plus the cover crop and the window poster crop taken from that master at or below source scale with every tradeoff record captured, plus one licensed camera scale ember texture band graded into the same world. Delivered with a parameter log and with the reason the shipped hero is the frame it is.

deliverables.name: Recovered Ember and Oak mark
deliverables.spec: The lockup recovered from a small raster with its ground baked in, as placeable scalable vector geometry with a transparent ground: a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding along, both words and the ring intact, delivered as a positive and as a variant that holds reversed on the dark end card, judged at end card size rather than at full canvas.

deliverables.name: Dish callout cards, cover and window poster as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: One native editable document carrying a callout card per dish that survived the cut at the video canvas sizes plus the cover, the end card and the window poster, each root keeping its own canvas size, with live editable text in one licensed type system, the mark as real vector shapes, every backing frame carried as embedded image data rather than a reference, and every card legible over the brightest frame it sits on. Delivered with the self contained source, which is the durable half: the owners change a dish every week and the source guarantees the design survives regardless.

deliverables.name: Handover note and sign off board
deliverables.spec: A written note recording what was applied per clip and per photograph, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and the actual numeric weight, the posting order across the three cuts, the dish to footage reconciliation including the dishes on the sheet that were not in the room that night, and everything the owners asked for that could not be produced with the reason. Paired with the persistent shareable sign off board carrying the hero, the poster ground and the frames the cards sit over, with nothing silently dropped.

verifiers_auto.text: The vertical and the square are derived from the delivered master rather than cut separately, and each is at or below the master's pixel dimensions.
verifiers_auto.how: Compare each reframe's dimensions and duration against the master's, and check the reframe operations recorded in the run against the manifest.

verifiers_auto.text: No delivered still exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions and no crop tradeoff record carries an upscale entry.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the pixel dimensions of the cover and poster masters against their source frames, and diff the captured tradeoffs objects against the resize table in the note.

verifiers_auto.text: Every callout card names a dish that appears in the delivered shot list, and no dish on the owners' sheet is captioned without appearing.
verifiers_auto.how: Diff the card set against the delivered cut's shot list and against the callout sheet.

verifiers_auto.text: The recovered mark's SVG has a viewBox attribute and no full canvas opaque background path at path index zero, and both words plus the ring are present as separate geometry.
verifiers_auto.how: Parse the delivered SVG: assert a viewBox is present, assert the first path does not span the whole canvas, and count the distinct path groups.

verifiers_auto.text: The card document exported with the expected canvas count and each canvas kept its own declared size.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the slide count and the per canvas width and height in the export response.

verifiers_auto.text: No backing frame in any canvas resolved to the importer's placeholder, and the mark arrived as vector path shapes rather than one picture.
verifiers_auto.how: Parse the returned per canvas markup for placeholder image data and count path shape elements in the end card region.

verifiers_auto.text: No card's legibility depends on a construction the importer drops, and no text element resolved to a fully transparent colour.
verifiers_auto.how: Search the returned per canvas markup for surviving panel shapes behind each caption and for any text node whose resolved colour carries zero alpha.

verifiers_auto.text: Every text element in the exported markup carries a resolved licensed PostScript face rather than a fallback default.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the font family attribute on every text node in the returned markup and check it against the families the kit call returned.

verifiers_auto.text: The sign off board exists with the expected item count and an empty failed items list after the final call.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the board id and the added entity and failed item arrays from the board responses.

verifiers_human.text: The three cuts read as one piece, and the first two seconds of each make somebody hungry.
verifiers_human.how: Watch the master, the vertical and the square back to back at the size each is posted at, and judge grade, energy and opening as a set.

verifiers_human.text: The pass line is intelligible over the room, or the note says plainly that it is not and the reel works without it.
verifiers_human.how: Listen to the cleaned version on a phone speaker at a normal volume, not on monitors.

verifiers_human.text: The hero holds at poster size: the char reads as char and the hearth reads as fire rather than as a white shape.
verifiers_human.how: View the poster master at full size rather than at cover scale, and beside a frame from the delivered cut.

verifiers_human.text: The mark still reads as the same mark at end card size and reversed on the dark ground, with the ring closed and both words legible.
verifiers_human.how: View the mark at its reproduction size on the end card and on the poster, not at full canvas.

verifiers_human.text: Every card is legible over the brightest frame it sits on, on every canvas and not only the first.
verifiers_human.how: Open the exported document and look at each canvas in Express with its backing frame behind it.

verifiers_human.text: The work reads as a thirty four dollar wood fired neighbourhood room, not as a tasting menu and not as a value grill.
verifiers_human.how: Judge cut speed, grade warmth, how much of the frame the food takes and the type scale against the stated band and audience.

verifiers_human.text: The note tells the owners something they did not already know, including everything that could not be delivered.
verifiers_human.how: Read the note against the run and check that the dish reconciliation, the hero decision and every limitation are named.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are video work and which need an authored fixed canvas document, given that the owners change a dish every week and burned in captions make each change a new commission.
Whether nine files from a service night are one shoot, and which of them can carry a vertical destination at all.
What goes into the highlight cut and how long it runs, given that input and length are the only levers on what comes out.
Whether the pass call is a line or a cleaner version of the same mush, and what to do with the reel if it is the second.
Which of the two hero frames actually ships, and how to tell the owners it is not the one they love.
Whether a correction on the hero is a whole frame move or a confined one, and how to word a selection so it takes the char and not the plate.
Which mark route the file's construction actually allows, given an enclosed ring and disjoint lettering on a baked in ground, and which variant carries the dark end card.
How the callout card holds its own against fire behind it without becoming a box that hides the food.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a two second decision at a thirty four dollar band rather than against a food brief's reflex serif.
Whether a licensed ember band joins the world the reel lives in or reads as bought.
The posting order across the three cuts, and which dish leads launch week given what the footage actually gave.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of a steak. IDENTITY: this is this restaurant's actual food, this actual Friday service, this actual chef calling this actual pass, and the mark must be RECOVERED off the only surviving copy rather than reinvented, because a regenerated mark is another restaurant's logo above their door. SPEC: the reel set is a master plus a vertical and a square derived from it, nothing enlarged, each at a destination size, with an audio version in which a specific line is intelligible, none of which a generated image or a generated clip satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the callout cards are defined by being editable, because the dishes change every week and the owners explicitly cannot re commission. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: what did the highlight pass actually keep, is there anything left in the highlights of this exposure, did the card's legibility survive the import.
doability_proof: Every link is scoped to what CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account) verifies, five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability. VIDEO AND AUDIO: the engagement uses only the sanctioned Premiere surface, video_create_quick_cut, video_resize, media_summarize and media_enhance_speech, and it is designed around their real constraints rather than around capabilities they do not have: quick cut ONLY SHORTENS and chooses its own moments, so input set and length are the only levers (which is exactly what checkpoint one rests on), and video_resize NEVER UPSCALES, so a destination a source cannot reach is a fact about the source. The task requires no trim to timestamp, no concatenation, no format conversion, no per clip assembly and no upscaling, none of which are available. Every acceptance line that must be machine checked rests on an artefact from a synchronous surface: the stills, the vector, the exported document, the returned markup and the board. IMAGING: apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, adjust_highlights, adjust_dark_portions, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, fill_area, remove_background, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and detection_confidence, and vectorize are all verified headless across 27 live calls. Checkpoint two rests on the documented absence of any measurement channel in the family (no eyedropper, no histogram, no level readout) plus the fact that a no op adjustment returns success; checkpoint three rests on verified importer behaviour, filter blur DROPPED, text shadow DROPPED, mix blend mode DROPPED, text stroke DROPPED (stroked type resolving to a fully transparent colour), multi layer shadow TRUNCATED TO LAYER ONE, all at HTTP success with no warning. VECTOR: remove_background returning a SOLID OPAQUE DISC on an enclosed ring and keeping only two or three letters of a disjoint wordmark are both live findings, as are the missing viewBox and the opaque path zero, and the acceptance bar scores the hygiene the tool does not perform. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, the product is a genuine editable document findable by asset_search, and the rendition preview is documented as PAGE 1 ONLY, which is why verification is split between the rendition and the returned markup; transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined frames pass the 70 KB threshold immediately. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed, license returned a real 7360x4912 JPEG, boards persist with a hard cap of 12 placements per call and 201 meaning partial. AVOIDED: no text to image, no generative fill, no object removal, no compositing, no OCR, no upscaling, no frame reaching Express as a URL, no fill_text, no animate_design, no create_firefly_board, no batch above 20.

engagement_title: Ironwood Kitchen high protein bowl line: bring eight bench shot bowls and one nine minute service take to a single bright house look, and carry the line onto paid social, a press line sheet and caption cards the counter can edit weekly
vertical: Food and beverage, fast casual grab and go meal prep bowls, two counters plus three office park delivery routes (Providence, Rhode Island)
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork recurring role posting for a creative partner serving meal prep and caterer businesses, quoted in the ledger grounding_note, whose listed deliverable scope was short form video ads, vertical short form and feed video content, product showcase videos and video resizing or adaptation, plus the graphic design line items paid social ads, website banners and assets, branding assets and promotional creatives, with turnaround weighted as the success metric. That posting is a retainer shaped list rather than one job, so the honest fuller commission is the launch it exists to service: one product line going live at once on the counter, on the delivery tiles, in the drivers' printed sheet and in paid social. The post names no client, so the line is laundered to the coined fictional brand Ironwood Kitchen. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) is what makes the printed half real rather than asserted: a printer's press PDF converts into a live InDesign merge template headlessly, so the client's own last season artwork becomes the template rather than something invented, and HTML authoring returns a native editable Express document at mixed canvas sizes, which is what the weekly rotating caption card actually needs.
client_one_liner: Our eight bowls were shot one at a time on the pass with a grey card in every frame, we have one long take from a service, and the whole line goes live in four weeks on the counter, on the delivery tiles and in the sheet our drivers leave at reception desks.
client_brief:
Ironwood Kitchen, High Protein Bowl line

We are a two counter grab and go kitchen in Providence. Eight bowls, twelve dollars each, built for the office lunch run: in the fridge case by half past ten, gone by two. The line launches in four weeks and everything a customer sees changes at once. The case labels, the delivery tiles, the printed sheet our drivers leave at reception desks, and the short clip we put money behind.

Our pictures. A friend shot all eight bowls on the pass, one at a time, straight down on the steel bench, with a grey card propped at the back of every frame so the colour could be set properly afterwards. They are honest photographs. Put them in a row the way the delivery app puts them and they are not one line: a couple read warmer than the rest and one sits noticeably greener. We need them to look like one kitchen on one morning. Bright, clean, food you would actually eat at your desk. Nothing invented, no sauce that is not in the bowl, and the card must not be in the delivered pictures.

We also have one long take from a service, about nine minutes, the chef building bowls, with two lines of him talking in the middle of it. We want a short cut out of that for paid social, plus the tall version and the four by five version the platforms want. Please tell us honestly what that footage can and cannot give us before you build anything on top of it.

The printed sheet. Our printer still had last season's file and sent the PDF back. It runs one bowl per page with the name, the description, the macros, the allergen line and the price. The new season's eight are in a spreadsheet with the picture names against them. We need it repopulated and press ready, plus a picture proof per bowl so the kitchen can sign each one off before it goes to print.

Last, caption cards for the case screen and the tiles, in one working file we can change ourselves, because the featured bowl rotates every week. Our logo only exists as a flat picture on white.

We are twelve dollars a bowl, not a tasting menu.
price_band_and_audience: Twelve dollar grab and go bowls, buyer 24 to 45 on an office lunch run with about eleven minutes to spend. The band is load bearing: at this price the work has to read bright, high key, clean and fast, food photographed close to how it looks in the case under fridge light, type large and plain, one claim per card. The same eight bowls at a thirty two dollar chef counter band would correctly be graded down, shot warmer and darker with negative space and small quiet type, and shipping that treatment here reads slow and expensive and empties a lunch rush. Push the other way into saturated primaries, drop shadows and burst badges and it becomes a mall food court, which contradicts the macro led claim the whole line is sold on. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. A posted job of this shape runs 900 to 2,200 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: Real lunch, in the case by half ten
brand_identity.sector: Fast casual grab and go: high protein meal prep bowls sold from a counter case and by office park delivery.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2019, Providence, Rhode Island, two counters and three office park delivery routes run by a small kitchen crew.
brand_identity.about: Ironwood Kitchen builds honest, high protein bowls for the office lunch run, in the fridge case by mid morning and gone by early afternoon. We are a working kitchen, not a tasting room. The promise is simple: food you would actually eat at your desk, twelve dollars, nothing invented and nothing dressed up.
brand_identity.audience: Office workers 24 to 45 on a weekday lunch run with roughly eleven minutes to spend, buying on macros, speed and trust rather than on spectacle.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Twelve dollars a bowl, the everyday middle of grab and go. Above a supermarket meal deal, well below a chef counter. We are not a tasting menu and never pretend to be one.
brand_identity.typography: One plain, high legibility grotesque sans carries everything, set large and tight. Names and prices sit big and quiet, one claim per card, no scripts and no display flourish. The type should read from arm's length in a fridge case.
brand_identity.voice: Direct, warm, counter honest, one thought per line. Example: "Twelve bucks, in the case by half ten, gone by two. That is the whole promise."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No brand kit survives. The wordmark exists only as a flat picture on a white ground, exported by a designer who has since left, with no vector file and no source anywhere. Everything else is a photograph or a spreadsheet.
brand_identity.values: Feed people well and tell the truth about what is in the bowl. The allergen line and the macros are not marketing, they are the deal.

acceptance_bar: The eight bowls read as ONE line when laid in a row the way the delivery tiles lay them: one white point, one black point, one brightness, one crop logic. A frame that cannot be brought to the set is named in the note, not shipped at eighty percent.
No grey card appears anywhere in a delivered picture, and no bowl is clipped by the crop that removed it.

No delivered file exceeds the pixel dimensions of the source it came from, and no returned resize record carries an enlargement entry. A file that reaches its size by being enlarged fails even if it looks acceptable.

Every platform slot is either delivered at the platform's stated size from source scale, or named as unreachable with the reason and the size actually delivered. Silently delivering short is a fail; so is enlarging to hit the number.
The press sheet carries one bowl per page, page count equals delivered row count, and the discontinued bowl is not among them.

Every page carries all five fields, name, description, macros, allergen line and price, with the allergen line present on all of them. A page whose allergen line is absent fails, and so does one where the description stops mid sentence at the frame edge.
There is one picture proof per bowl, and the picture on each proof is the bowl that proof is named for. A proof set that is complete but misattributed fails.

The caption cards arrive as ONE working file carrying all three canvas sizes, each keeping its own size, with live retypeable text and the mark as real vector shapes rather than a picture of a layout.
On every caption card the featured bowl is actually visible behind the type, and the type is readable over it, on all three canvases and not only the first one.
One type system across all three canvases, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the actual weight used.

The note states, per photograph, what was applied and why that frame differs from its neighbours, every resize any tool reported, what the footage could not give, and the reconciliation between the roster rows and the bowls that exist.

It fixes one bright house target and brings eight frames shot under two different light states to it one call at a time, confines corrections where a global move takes the greens grey, cuts the card out of frame without cutting the bowl, produces the tile and line sheet crops at source scale, and recovers the wordmark off a flat disjoint export with the vector hygiene the tracing tool does not perform for you.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching anything.
trajectory.judgement: The sheet is record per page variable data and belongs on the merge surface; the caption cards rotate weekly and have to be an authored editable document; the cut and the slots are motion work. The brief pins all three destinations, so there is nothing here to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming surface per deliverable, and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline: a manifest keyed by role, because forty artefacts later the agent still has to know which URL is which bowl.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Read what the supplied take actually is, then summarise it to locate the usable stretch of the service and the two spoken lines inside nine minutes.
trajectory.judgement: What the file is decides what the platform slots can be, and the folder name is not evidence. Establishing this before cutting is the difference between a delivery plan and a promise the footage cannot keep.
trajectory.produces: The take's real dimensions and duration, and a note of where the usable material and the speech actually sit.

trajectory.action: Shorten the take into the highlight cut, choosing a length that suits an impulse priced lunch product rather than a brand film.
trajectory.judgement: The cutting tool shortens and chooses its own moments; the agent's control is what it is handed and how long the result is asked to be. At twelve dollars the cut has to land the bowl fast.
trajectory.produces: A short highlight cut built from the usable stretch of the service.

trajectory.action: Clean the two spoken lines against the extractor hood so the claim is audible without the cut sounding processed.
trajectory.judgement: A twelve dollar lunch brand can carry room noise and cannot carry an unintelligible claim. Over cleaning reads as an advert, which is exactly the register the counter does not want.
trajectory.produces: A speech cleaned pass of the audio for the cut.

trajectory.action: Produce the tall and the four by five slots inside source scale, and name any slot that cannot be reached at the platform's stated size.
trajectory.judgement: Reframing is downscale only. A slot that cannot be reached honestly is a thing to report with the size actually delivered, not a thing to enlarge into.
trajectory.produces: The platform reframe set, plus a written statement of what the footage could not give.

trajectory.action: Look at all eight bowl frames and triage them: which blind state each belongs to, how each card is lit, whether the card sits clear of the plate or overlaps it, and which bowls run close to the steel bench in value.
trajectory.judgement: The client believes the card makes all eight frames equivalent. The pictures are the only place that can be settled, and a card lit by two sources is worse than no card because it looks authoritative.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note covering light state, card usability and card position relative to the plate.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes the subject and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop, and on a top down bench shot a half degree is visible against the bench seams.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Fix one bright house target off the cleanest card frame and bring each of the eight to it with its own call, confining the correction where a global move takes the greens grey, and recording every parameter applied.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a set, not eight good pictures. One batched call applies one identical parameter set, which is exactly wrong for frames shot under two different light states, and the frames whose cards lie have to be judged by the food instead.
trajectory.produces: Eight graded masters at source scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Cut the delivery crops: card out of frame, bowl optically centred, clear air at every edge, at the tile size and at the line sheet's picture ratio, reading every returned resize record rather than the success message.
trajectory.judgement: On the three frames where the card overlaps the plate, the crop that removes the card is a different crop from the other five, and optical centring on a bowl with a tall garnish is not geometric centring. The resize record is the only channel that reports what the tool did to the dimensions.
trajectory.produces: Delivery crops at both ratios with their returned resize records transcribed.

trajectory.action: Recover the wordmark: an ink level selection naming the letterforms' own visual properties, correct polarity, a bounds crop from the selection's own bbox, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque ground path removed.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions the tools do not make: how to word the selection so it takes the ink rather than the sheet, which polarity to trace, and the fact that a knockout is the wrong instrument entirely on disjoint lettering.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent mark.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged against a twelve dollar lunch product and an eleven minute decision. Weight cannot be inferred from a style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Convert the printer's PDF into a working document, export its interchange form, and inventory what the artwork actually exposes: how many text frames, how many picture frames, what each one really contains.
trajectory.judgement: Frame granularity is a property of the source artwork and not under anyone's control here. Promising a field to a frame before looking at the frames is the single most common way this deliverable dies.
trajectory.produces: A real frame inventory with bounds, applied type and existing links.

trajectory.action: Build the field mapping against the frames the document actually has, bind the per row product photograph through the image column, and run the mapping back through the validator.
trajectory.judgement: Five fields landing in one continuous flow is a different mapping problem from five fields in five frames, and the picture binding has to be per row or every page ships the same bowl.
trajectory.produces: A mapping covering all five text fields and the per row picture, with the validator's response recorded.

trajectory.action: Prepare the merge template, then read the prepared document itself for every expected field before merging anything.
trajectory.judgement: Two success messages and a validation pass are not evidence that a placeholder exists. The document is the only witness, and reading it costs one round trip against a print run that costs a great deal more.
trajectory.produces: A merge template plus a field by field account of which placeholders are genuinely present in it.

trajectory.action: Merge the delivered rows into one press sheet at one bowl per page, then reconcile page count against row count and both against the bowls that actually exist.
trajectory.judgement: The roster is the client's belief about their own line, and a roster row is not a bowl. Reconciling is the agent's job and saying so is part of the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: A press sheet at one bowl per page with the roster reconciliation written down.

trajectory.action: Produce one picture proof per bowl for kitchen sign off, and check each proof by looking at it against the roster rather than by the order it arrived in.
trajectory.judgement: A proof set exists to be signed off by people who know these bowls by sight. Naming files by their position in a response is an assumption, and it is the assumption this deliverable is most exposed to.
trajectory.produces: Per bowl proofs, each verified by eye against the bowl it is named for.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML carrying three roots at three canvas sizes, inline every photograph as image data, place the mark as inline SVG inside an explicitly sized top left anchored wrapper, declare family and weight on every text element, upload the file, run the readiness check and export.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override is what collapses a mixed size set. The design work is how large the bowl sits and how few words the card carries at twelve dollars.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML and a native editable Express document, with the HTML retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Verify the exported document through both channels that exist, resolve its rendition and look at the first canvas, parse the returned per canvas markup for the other two, then write the handover note.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at card one is not looking at the deliverable. The note has to be specific enough that the counter can rotate the featured bowl themselves next week.
trajectory.produces: An inspected first canvas, a per canvas markup audit for the other two, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the readout the mapping was built from actually matches the document. The line sheet's SKU block converts to one continuous flow, and the readout of that flow silently omits the allergen run while keeping its line break, so the string still reads as well formed and every offset past it is short by exactly that run's length. The validator returns VALID with no warnings on the wrong offsets and the prepare step reports completed successfully, so nothing anywhere says a field failed to land. Which run is dropped, and therefore which fields silently never arrive, is a property of this artwork and is visible only by reading the prepared document itself.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter controls it, because the readout is the only documented source of the story text and it presents itself as authoritative. (b) Nothing states it: the brief describes a sheet with five fields on it and says nothing about how the artwork is constructed, and the acceptance line about every page carrying its allergen line is the client's own printing requirement, not a disclosure that a readout lies. (c) It is not a propagation re run, because the response is to compute offsets from a different source entirely, the document's own reconstructed story text, and rebuild the mapping on that basis.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reconstruct the true story text from the prepared document, recompute every offset against it, rebuild and revalidate the mapping, prepare the template again, and read the document a second time field by field before any merge is attempted.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A press sheet that goes to the printer with the allergen line missing on all eight pages and the price absent under every bowl, having reported success at every step, for a food business where the allergen line is not optional.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the two constructs the caption card look is built on. A full bleed photograph placed as a CSS background with embedded image data is dropped entirely and the element arrives as an empty box with geometry and no picture, and the natural way to keep type readable over bright food, a darkening blend applied to a panel over the photograph, is dropped as well so the panel arrives as a flat opaque shape. Both return success with no warning of any kind, the returned per canvas markup is the only channel that reports either, and the document's rendition returns the first artboard only, so cards two and three can be checked no other way.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the normalisation happens at import and the import is the last step, and getting it right first time presumes knowing which of several equally natural full bleed constructions survives, which no tool reports and no checklist enumerates. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for cards the counter can edit with the featured bowl on them, and the acceptance line about the bowl being visible behind readable type is the client's own art direction. (c) It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a different construction, the photograph placed as a real picture element rather than as a ground, and legibility carried by an upstream raster treatment or by a solid panel rather than by a blend the importer discards.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re author the cards around a picture element and a surviving legibility route, possibly producing a differently treated raster upstream so the type has something to sit on, upload again, run the readiness check again, export again, and audit all three canvases from the returned markup rather than from the first card.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Caption cards handed to a counter that runs them weekly in which the featured bowl is simply absent behind the words on cards nobody previewed, with the export having reported success throughout, on the one deliverable whose entire purpose was to show the bowl.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the per bowl proofs are the bowls they say they are. The proof outputs come back labelled by row position, and on the raster route those labels do not correspond to the rows they name, so a complete, correctly sized, entirely plausible looking proof set can be misattributed end to end. Nothing in the response indicates it and the tool's own description asserts the opposite ordering, so the only evidence is looking at each proof and reading the bowl in it against the roster.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) A careful agent cannot avoid it by ordering, because the mislabelling is a property of the response and not of the sequence, and the documentation actively points the wrong way. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for a proof per bowl so the kitchen can sign off, which is a requirement rather than a warning. (c) It is not a propagation re run, because the fix is a different production route entirely, either single record outputs produced one at a time so identity is guaranteed, or a route whose ordering has been checked by eye, with the agent naming each file itself.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Discard the proof set, re produce the proofs through a route where each output's identity is guaranteed by construction, name each file from the roster, and confirm each one visually before it goes near a sign off sheet.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The kitchen signs off eight proofs believing each shows the bowl named on it, and the sheet goes to press with the descriptions, macros and allergen lines attached to the wrong photographs, which for the allergen line is the worst possible way to be wrong.

verifiers_human.how: Watch the cut and each platform version end to end with sound.

verifiers_human.text: The note tells the counter something they did not already know, including everything that could not be delivered and why.
verifiers_human.how: Read the note against the run and check that the footage limits, every resize and the roster reconciliation are all named.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are motion work, which are record per page variable data, and which need an authored fixed canvas document, given that only one surface here does each.
Whether the supplied take can serve the platform slots at their stated sizes at all, and what to tell the client when it cannot.
How long the cut should run for a twelve dollar impulse product, and how much of the nine minute service is actually usable.
How far to clean the spoken lines before the cut stops sounding like a kitchen and starts sounding like an advert.
Which grey cards can be trusted and which are lit by two sources, and what to neutralise against when the card lies.
Where to crop the three frames whose card overlaps the plate, given that the obvious crop takes part of the bowl with it.
Whether a roster of nine rows is nine bowls, and how to say so when it is not.
How to word the wordmark selection so it takes the ink rather than the sheet, given that a knockout is the wrong instrument on disjoint lettering.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against an eleven minute lunch decision, plus the real numeric weight per family.
How few words a caption card can carry and still rotate weekly without being redesigned, and how large the bowl has to sit at twelve dollars.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of grain bowls and a plausible looking sheet. IDENTITY: these are this kitchen's actual eight bowls with their actual macro lines, their actual cleared claims and their actual allergen declarations, and the wordmark has to be RECOVERED off a flat export rather than reinvented, because a regenerated mark is a different business's logo and a regenerated allergen line is a legal exposure. SPEC: the printer needs one bowl per page with page count equal to row count and every field present, the platform needs its slots at stated sizes from source scale with nothing enlarged, and the delivery tiles need a card free crop, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the caption cards exist to be changed weekly by the counter, so a flat picture of a card is worthless. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality: did these placeholders actually land in the document, is this proof the bowl it claims to be, did the photograph survive the import.
doability_proof: Every link is verified in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. INDESIGN is fully headless and synchronous end to end and was run live: convert_pdf_to_indd returned a raw .indd, export_idml yielded a genuine document structure inventory, generate_indd_mapping_prompt returned integer page_item_ids with bounds and typography and doubles as the validator, prepare_indd_merge_template produced live placeholders confirmed by re exported IDML, document_merge_data_layout to application/pdf returned ONE multi page file with page count equal to row count in CSV order, and per row image binding through an at prefixed column plus additionalImageFiles was visually confirmed to bind different pictures to different rows. The first checkpoint rests on the documented headline trap: textContent is LOSSY (a 17 character run dropped while its line break was kept), the validator returned VALID with zero warnings on the corrupted offsets, prepare reported completed successfully, and only 3 of 5 mappings landed. The third rests on the verified finding that multi record raster outputs come back in reversed order with lying row labels, while the PDF, createSeparateFiles and recordRange routes were each verified correct. IMAGING is fully headless across 27 live calls: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and upscale_factor (a documented silent 2x cap), fill_area, remove_background and vectorize; the disjoint wordmark collapse, the missing viewBox and the opaque path zero are all live findings. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, the product is a genuine editable dcx findable by asset_search, and the second checkpoint rests on two verified drops at HTTP success, a CSS background image with a data URI dropped entirely leaving an empty geometric box, and mix blend mode dropped to a plain opaque shape, with the rendition documented as PAGE 1 ONLY. Transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined photography passes the 70 KB threshold immediately. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit verified end to end, with the case sensitivity and non standard numeric weight traps live. VIDEO AND AUDIO: metadata, summarise, quick cut (shorten only), resize (downscale only) and enhance speech are submitted through the connector's asynchronous media path and resolve on the host's progress surface; no checkpoint and no automatic verifier in this task depends on byte inspecting a video file, and every gradeable motion criterion is either a dimension read off the delivered file or something a reviewer watches. AVOIDED: no bleed gate, no pdfPreset, no variable QR, no multiple records per page, no per artboard named export, no video trim to timestamp, no format conversion, no upscaling, no vector render or vector merge, no fill_text, no animate_design, no text to image, no compositing, no OCR, no photo reaching Express as a URL, no batch above 20.

engagement_title: Halden Greens first paid push: build one creator led ad and its platform set from five phone clips, and carry the hooks onto editable caption cards and a matched thumbnail without making any of it look expensive
vertical: Health and wellness, direct to consumer daily greens subscription, online only with a creator seeded audience (Portland, Oregon)
real_brief_anchor: GROUNDED in the real PeoplePerHour brief 'Video Ads for DTC Supplement Brand (UGC / VSL / Mashup)', quoted in the ledger grounding_note: a direct to consumer supplement brand supplies a batch of raw user generated talking head creator clips plus product b roll and wants them cut into short paid social ad variants testing DIFFERENT HOOKS, each reframed to the platform native ratios, with on brand text, captions and callout graphics added, and platform ready cuts plus a scroll stopping thumbnail delivered, conversion focused and fast. The posted brief names no client, so the line is laundered to the coined fictional brand Halden Greens. The real post treats the caption and hook layer as an afterthought bolted onto the cut; CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) is what lets this be built as the client actually needs it, because HTML authoring returns a native editable Express document at mixed canvas sizes, which turns 'we will be swapping hooks every week' from a promise into a deliverable the growth lead can operate without recommissioning anyone.
client_one_liner: We sent tubs to three creators, we have five clips filmed on their own phones and some counter footage our founder shot, and we are about to put real money behind one ad that has to look like something a friend sent you.
client_brief:
Halden Greens, first paid push

We sell a daily greens powder on subscription, fifty nine dollars a month, mostly to people between twenty five and forty who have already been burned by a supplement that promised too much. They do not trust anything that looks like an advert. That is the whole problem we are hiring you to solve.

What we have. Five clips from three creators we sent tubs to, filmed on their own phones in their own kitchens. They are not polished and we do not want them polished. Alongside them, four short clips of the tub, the scoop and the pour that our founder shot on the counter at home, and a handful of photographs the creators sent us. One creator clip is our favourite by a distance: she is funny, and she says the thing about the morning routine that everyone repeats back to us.

What we need. One short ad cut from that material that feels like something a friend sent you rather than something an agency made. It has to run in the vertical feeds, in the square feed and in the four by five slot, and we are spending real money behind it, so those versions have to be right rather than squeezed. Tell us which clip you built the cut around and why.

Captions matter more than anything here. Our growth lead wrote six hook lines. We want them as cards we can change ourselves week to week, because we will be testing and swapping them constantly and the wrong hook is the difference between this working and not. They sit over the footage, so they have to stay readable over a bright kitchen and over a dark counter. Tell us plainly which hooks you would not run, and why.

We also need one still for the thumbnail slot, matched to the ad. Our platform asks for 1280 by 720 there. And the tub cut out cleanly, because it sits on our green panel.

Our logo only exists as a flat export. Nothing here should look expensive.
price_band_and_audience: Fifty nine dollars a month on subscription, buyer 25 to 40, health literate and specifically sceptical of polish. The band is load bearing in an unusual direction: the money is real but the look must be cheap, because at subscription economics the acquisition cost is decided by whether the ad survives being recognised as an ad. Grade lightly, keep the phone framing, keep the room noise short of unintelligible, set the hooks in plain type at conversational length. The same product at a hundred and forty dollars a month would correctly be shot in a studio, graded cool and clean, with restrained type and generous space, and shipping that treatment here reads as a company pretending to be a person, which is the single most expensive mistake available on this brief. Push the other way into flashing text, countdowns and stacked badges and it reads as a fifteen dollar tub, which contradicts the subscription price. A posted job of this shape runs 700 to 1,800 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: Direct to consumer daily greens powder sold online on a monthly subscription, creator seeded.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2023, Portland, Oregon, online only, a small founder led team with a growth lead and three seeded creators.
brand_identity.about: Halden Greens is a daily greens powder people actually keep drinking, sold by subscription to buyers who have already been let down by a supplement that promised too much. We grow by putting the product in real kitchens and letting real people talk, not by looking like an advert. That distrust of polish is the brand.
brand_identity.audience: Health literate adults 25 to 40 who are specifically wary of supplement marketing and trust a friend's recommendation over a glossy campaign.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Fifty nine dollars a month on subscription. Priced as a considered daily habit, above the fifteen dollar tub and below the studio shot premium brands. The money is real, so the look must never be.
brand_identity.typography: One friendly, near neutral sans set at conversational size, plain weights only. Type should look unconsidered while being entirely considered: no countdowns, no stacked badges, no burst text. Hooks read like a caption a person typed, not a headline.
brand_identity.voice: Conversational, honest to a fault, a little self aware, never hype. Example: "We are not going to tell you it changed our life. It is greens. You drink them in the morning."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The wordmark exists only as a flat export, dark disjoint letters on white, with no vector source. The brand green panel is fixed and every cutout has to hold against it. Some earlier photography still shows a previous tub label and should not be reused.
brand_identity.values: Say only what we can stand behind. Claims live inside the category compliance sheet, and anything the sheet forbids does not run, however good the line.

assets_supplied.name: halden_creator_clips/ (5 clips, 3 creators)
assets_supplied.kind: Talking head clips filmed by creators on their own phones in their own kitchens, tub in hand, no scripts, no lighting.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Five clips, three creators. The second one from Mara is the one we love."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two of the five are horizontal with the creator hard left of frame, so a square reframe puts the tub outside the picture entirely, and the favourite clip is one of those two. One clip's audio sits at roughly half the level of the others and carries street noise through an open window, so a single levelling decision applied to the set leaves either that creator inaudible or the rest harsh.

assets_supplied.name: halden_founder_broll/ (4 counter clips)
assets_supplied.kind: Short handheld clips of the tub, the scoop and the pour, shot by the founder on the kitchen counter at home.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The product shots, filmed at my place. Use whichever help."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two of the four are the same pour from the same angle seconds apart, so a cut that uses both reads as a stutter, and one was captured at a different frame rate from the rest, which no filename shows and which cannot be reconciled here.

assets_supplied.name: halden_creator_stills/ (6 phone photographs, 4032 x 3024)
assets_supplied.kind: Photographs the creators sent alongside the clips: tub on a counter, tub in hand, a mug beside it.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Whatever they sent us. Better quality than the video, I think."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The only frame where the tub is held clearly is backlit by the window behind the counter, so the pale mint lid runs at almost the same value as the sunlit worktop and a one call knockout bites the lid edge while returning a complete looking cutout. Two of the six show the previous tub design with the older label.

assets_supplied.name: halden_thumb_hero.jpg (1080 x 1920)
assets_supplied.kind: A still the growth lead pulled out of the favourite clip and sent over as the intended thumbnail.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "This frame. This is the expression we want on the thumbnail."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is a screen grab from a vertical clip rather than a camera file, so the platform's 1280 by 720 slot cannot be reached from it without enlargement, which the crop tool will perform up to a two times cap while reporting it only inside its own tradeoff record. Cropping it to a wide ratio also clips the tub out of the frame.

assets_supplied.name: halden_wordmark.png
assets_supplied.kind: Flat export of the wordmark, dark disjoint letterforms on a white ground, no vector file.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "All we have of the logo."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Disjoint lettering collapses under a one call knockout, which returns two surviving letterforms at full success, and a trace returns geometry with no viewBox and an opaque full canvas ground path riding underneath it.

assets_supplied.name: halden_hooks.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Six hook lines written by the growth lead, plus the brand's own one page compliance sheet listing what the category cannot claim.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Six hooks. We think three of them are the strong ones."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two of the six make a comparative health claim the brand's own compliance sheet forbids, and nothing marks which. A third runs to fourteen words, which cannot hold at vertical caption size without dropping to a point size at which it stops functioning as a hook.

assets_supplied.name: halden_tone_reference.png
assets_supplied.kind: A screenshot the founder saved of an ad in an unrelated category whose register she likes, supplied as a tone reference only.

acceptance_bar: The cut reads as creator footage rather than as an agency edit: phone framing kept, grading restrained, room sound present but the speech intelligible throughout. A polished version fails this brief even if it is technically cleaner.
Every platform version keeps the product in frame for the whole time it is on screen. A reframe that centres the picture and loses the tub fails.

No delivered file, still or motion, exceeds the pixel dimensions of the source it derives from, and no returned resize record carries an enlargement entry. A thumbnail brought to size by enlargement fails even if it looks acceptable.

Where a slot cannot be reached at the platform's stated size from source scale, it is named with the reason and with the size actually delivered. Silently delivering short fails, and so does enlarging to hit the number.
Audio is levelled per clip rather than by one setting across the set, and the quietest creator is audible without the others becoming harsh.

Every hook that reaches a card is one the brand's own compliance sheet permits, and the ones that do not are named in the note with the reason. A compliant looking card carrying a forbidden claim fails.
Each hook card is readable over the footage it plays on, over the bright kitchen and over the dark counter, at the size it actually appears. A caption that is legible only at full canvas fails.

The hook cards arrive as ONE working file carrying all three canvas sizes, each keeping its own size, with live retypeable text so the growth lead can swap a hook without a designer, and the mark as real vector shapes.
The caption text is actually present and actually visible on all three canvases, not only on the first one.
The tub cutout holds its edge when placed on the brand's green panel, not only when viewed against white.

The note states which clip the cut was built around and why, which hooks were rejected and on what grounds, what the footage could not give, every resize any tool reported, and which stills show the previous tub.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Premiere video and audio
adobe_surfaces.tools: video_metadata, media_summarize, video_create_quick_cut, video_resize, media_enhance_speech
adobe_surfaces.role: The ad itself. It establishes what each of the nine supplied files actually is rather than what the folder implies, locates where each hook line lands inside the talking head material, shortens the chosen material into a mashup whose length suits a sceptical scroller, levels and cleans the creator audio clip by clip rather than by one setting, and produces the three platform slots inside source scale with the product held in frame.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including image_vectorize which is counted HERE and not as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_invert_selection, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs, detection_confidence and upscale_factor), image_fill_area, image_remove_background, image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: The still half. It brings the usable creator photographs to one restrained target that does not out polish the footage, isolates the tub for the overlay cards and for the brand panel, builds the thumbnail honestly at source scale while reading what every crop reports about its own dimensions, and recovers the wordmark off a flat disjoint export with the vector hygiene the tracing tool does not perform for you.

adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The hook cards as one native editable document carrying three canvas sizes, which is the only way the growth lead can swap a hook weekly without recommissioning anyone. Photography has to be carried as image data because a URL renders as an empty grey box at full success, the mark goes in as inline SVG so it stays vector, family and weight are declared per text element, and the payload travels by uploaded URL because inlined photography passes the inline threshold immediately.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url

The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own. Numeric weights are non standard per family and cannot be inferred from a style name, every name must be laundered into canonical PostScript form before the kit call because one bad name kills the whole kit, and the CSS must use the returned slug or it falls back silently.
