A family-name lookup returns an arbitrary style rather than the regular cut, the numeric weight is non-standard per family and cannot be inferred from a style name, one bad name kills the whole kit, and the CSS must use the returned slug or the face falls back silently.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (entityScope StockAsset, SHORT query, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the one clean surface the selects do not contain, a plain workbench ground for the end card and the spec callouts, IP-clean, at genuine camera scale, with generative-tech candidates excluded and chosen for whether it can be brought to the same target as the channel's own stills. The Boards half persists the thumbnail and card options the host and the sponsor sign off from, placed within the per-call cap, with a partial success read as partial and vector understood to be unacceptable there.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching anything.
trajectory.judgement: The cut and the reframes are motion work, the thumbnail is raster work, and the cards have to be an authored fixed canvas document because the host publishes several times a week and needs to reopen them. The brief pins the destinations, so there is nothing here to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload the master, the twelve selects, the bug and the sponsor copy through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline: a manifest keyed by role so that thirty artefacts later the agent still knows which URL is which select.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Summarise the master to establish what the episode actually contains and in what order, then read that against the host's notes.
trajectory.judgement: The notes are the host's memory of his own episode, not a record of it. Where the notes and the episode disagree, the episode wins, and saying so is part of the job rather than a correction to make silently.
trajectory.produces: A segment inventory with the verdict order and a written note of every point where the host's notes and the episode disagree.

trajectory.action: Treat the narration audio, handling the two halves either side of the mic move as two passes rather than one, and listen back across the join.
trajectory.judgement: One treatment applied across a file recorded at two mic distances resolves one half at the other's expense. Evenness is judged at the join and at the sponsor read, not on the file's average.
trajectory.produces: A treated narration bed with a per-half parameter log and a note on how the join sits.

trajectory.action: Listen to the treated result specifically at the segments where the review is about how a product sounds, and judge whether the thing the host is pointing at is still there.
trajectory.judgement: Cleaner is not the goal. The only test that matters is whether a viewer told to listen to this can hear it.
trajectory.produces: A written verdict per demonstration segment on whether the product sound survived the treatment.

trajectory.action: Build the feed short by shortening the master, then look at what came back against the segment inventory and the verdict order.
trajectory.judgement: The short is a reduction, not an assembly, and the tool decides which passages survive. A short that promotes a verdict the episode does not reach is worse than a short that runs a little long.
trajectory.produces: A feed short at the target length with a written account of which segments it holds.

trajectory.action: Reframe the short upright and square from the short itself, at or below the frame size it came back at, and check what each framing leaves in shot.
trajectory.judgement: The re-aspect ceiling is set by what the cut actually returned rather than by the 4K master, and enlarging to reach a feed's native size is not an option. Upright framing on a three way shootout decides whether the viewer can still see all three units.
trajectory.produces: An upright version and a square version, each at a size no larger than its source, with the reframing decisions recorded.

trajectory.action: Preview all twelve selects and triage them: which are duplicates, which is soft, what frame size each actually is, and which can carry a thumbnail at the destination size without being enlarged.
trajectory.judgement: The host has already chosen his thumbnail shot. Whether that select can reach the thumbnail size, and whether the wall behind it will let the subject be cut, are two different questions and neither is answered by the host's preference.
trajectory.produces: A per select triage note covering duplication, sharpness, frame size and headroom for the thumbnail crop.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level, then bring the publishable selects to one channel target with a call each, recording the parameters applied.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes and eats edge pixels so it cannot follow a crop, and the grid is what the channel is judged on, so the target is a set rather than a run of individually good frames.
trajectory.produces: A graded still set at source scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Cut the host and the unit out of the chosen holding shot and composite onto the channel accent, then inspect the result at full size along the top edge and through the carry handle rather than at preview scale.
trajectory.judgement: A knockout on a subject that shares its value with the wall behind it returns something clean, complete and wrong. The accent ground is where a bite becomes a notch, so that is where it has to be looked at.
trajectory.produces: A thumbnail cutout on the accent ground plus a transparent variant, with the edge inspected at full size.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the plain workbench ground the selects do not contain, filter to photography, exclude generative-tech results, license and download at full resolution.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the surface whose existing light can be brought to the channel target, not the most attractive thumbnail. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP-clean, camera-scale ground frame graded into the channel's world.

trajectory.action: Prepare and trace the bug: word the selection at ink level, set the polarity, crop from the selection's own returned bounds, trace, then inject a viewBox and remove the opaque full canvas ground path.
trajectory.judgement: The tracing tool takes no options at all, so every lever is in the raster preparation. Polarity is the whole difference between a mark and a black box, and both outcomes report success.
trajectory.produces: A transparent, scalable bug with a real viewBox and no opaque ground path.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, launder the sponsor's named family and every other name into canonical form and read what each name actually resolved to, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: A family-name lookup on this library hands back an arbitrary style, so the returned name has to be read rather than passed through. The pairing is the agent's own art direction, judged against a credible independent reviewer rather than a broadcast package, and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one-kit type system with family, style, foundry or designer and the actual numeric weight recorded per role, including what the sponsor's named family resolved to.

trajectory.action: Author one self-contained HTML carrying the sponsor read card, the spec callouts and the end card at their respective canvas sizes, inlining every photograph as image data, placing the bug as inline SVG inside an explicitly sized top-left anchored wrapper, declaring family and weight on every text element, and setting the card measure from the longest line rather than the shortest.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto-sized right-anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override is what collapses a mixed-size set. The disclosure line is the line the measure has to be built around, because it is the one line that cannot be shortened.
trajectory.produces: One export-ready HTML carrying the whole card set, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, upload the HTML and export by URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at card one, and parse the returned per-card markup for every other card and for the bug on each of them.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition preview only ever shows the first artboard. The bug appears on every card, so it is the element whose behaviour has to be checked on all of them rather than on the one that renders.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document, an inspected first card, and a per-card markup audit for the rest.

trajectory.action: Create the sign-off board, add the thumbnail options, the graded stills and the licensed ground within the per-call placement cap, re-sending only the entries the response names as failed, then write the handover note.
trajectory.judgement: A partial success is reported as a success, and the vector bug is not boardable so it belongs in the note instead. The note is what stops the host rebuilding this from scratch on Monday.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the speech treatment took out along with the room. Roughly a third of this episode is the host holding a microphone to a machine while a fan ramps, a relay clicks and an inverter whines, and a speech model treats every one of those as noise around the voice. The call succeeds, returns a genuinely cleaner and more professional-sounding file, and the parameters were applied exactly as asked. The loss is audible in one place only, at the moment the host says listen to this and there is nothing there, and which demonstration segments lose their evidence and which survive depends on how each machine's sound overlaps the voice, which is not knowable from the file, its properties or the tool's response.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the narration genuinely does need treatment and the demonstration segments are interleaved with it rather than separable in advance, and there is no parameter that says preserve the machine. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says the room has a fridge in it and asks not to end up sounding like a podcast, which is the client's taste, not a disclosure that a speech tool removes the review's evidence. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the answer is a different route: treat only the narration-carrying passages and leave the demonstration passages at source, which changes what the short is assembled from and forces the level match to be judged at every boundary between the two.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-plan the audio as two populations rather than one file, treat the narration passages and leave the demonstration passages untouched, re-judge evenness at every join between them, and then re-derive the short and both reframes from the rebuilt bed rather than from the first one.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A polished short in which the host repeatedly tells a sponsor-funded audience to listen to how loud these get over silence, on a channel whose credibility is the product it sells.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the thumbnail cutout actually holds its edge. The host's chosen select has a light grey chassis and a carry handle against a bright grey studio wall at almost the same value along the top edge, and a subject knockout on that frame returns a clean, complete, entirely plausible cutout with no error, no warning and no tradeoff entry. Against white or against the pale preview background it looks correct. The bite in the handle and the notch in the top corner only appear once the cutout is sitting on the channel's saturated accent colour at full size, which is the only place it will ever be seen. Whether it bites at all, and how far, is a property of that specific frame's exposure against that specific wall.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter prevents it: the only way to learn whether a subject separates from a ground it shares a value with is to cut it and put it on the ground it is going to. (b) Nothing states it: the brief names the shot the host wants and says to drop it on the accent colour, which is the client's art direction, not a warning. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different chain: select the wall by its own material properties, invert, and fill rather than asking for a subject knockout, or abandon the host's chosen select for one where the subject separates, which changes what the thumbnail is and has to be explained back to him.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-cut the thumbnail through a material-named ground selection inverted and filled instead of a subject knockout, or move to a different select and justify the change, then re-composite on the accent, re-inspect the top edge and the handle at full size, and re-derive any card that carried the same cutout.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A thumbnail published to the grid with a notch chewed out of the product's carry handle, on the one asset the channel's click-through and its sponsor renewal both depend on.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the traced bug still reads as the bug at the size it actually reproduces. The trace is clean at canvas size and inspecting it there shows the bolt, the hexagon, the hairline counter and the outer ring all intact. What cannot be known without placing it is that the counter around the bolt and the gap to the inner edge of the hexagon are thinner than they appear at full size, and at the size the bug sits on a card, on the channel's dark card ground, those counters close and the bug reads as a filled hexagon with a smudge in it. The tracing tool takes no options at all, so nothing about the call can be tuned, and the returned artwork is correct by every structural test.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter controls it, because behaviour at reproduction size against a specific ground is not a property of the trace and cannot be read off the artwork. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says the bug is always small and asks that it still look like the bug when it is small, which is the client's standing requirement, not a disclosure that this particular trace closes up. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the answer is a different chain: re-prepare the raster the trace is made from so the counters survive, since raster preparation is the only lever the tracing tool has, or place a knocked-out raster at card scale instead of vector, or reconstruct the bug's geometry directly as inline SVG at proportions that hold, each of which changes what is delivered.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Return to the raster preparation, re-derive the trace from a differently prepared plate or reconstruct the geometry, re-place it at true card size on the dark ground, re-judge it there rather than at canvas size, and re-author and re-export the card set around whichever form survives.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A card set in which the channel bug, which sits on every card the channel publishes several times a week, has quietly become a filled hexagon, with the export having reported success throughout.

deliverables.name: Voltcast E42 short with treated audio, plus upright and square
deliverables.spec: One feed short genuinely shortened from the twelve minute master, promoting the verdict the episode actually reaches, plus an upright version and a square version each reframed from that short at or below its frame size with all three units still readable. Carried on a treated audio bed in which the narration is even across the mic move and the demonstration passages still contain the product sound the host is pointing at. Delivered with a written account of what the short kept, what it dropped and what was done to the audio where.

deliverables.name: Voltcast episode still set
deliverables.spec: The publishable selects brought to one channel target (one white point, one black point, one crop logic) so the episode's stills sit in the grid as one channel, plus one licensed camera-scale ground frame graded into the same world. Duplicates and the soft frame identified rather than shipped, and a per frame parameter log with one line on why each frame differs from its neighbours.

deliverables.name: Voltcast E42 thumbnail, accent ground and transparent
deliverables.spec: The host and unit cut from the studio wall and composited on the channel accent colour at the thumbnail's destination size with no enlargement, the edge holding along the top and through the carry handle when viewed at full size on the accent rather than at preview scale, plus a genuinely transparent variant for reuse on other grounds, with the returned tradeoff record kept for each.

deliverables.name: Voltcast channel bug as placeable artwork
deliverables.spec: The bug delivered as scalable vector geometry with a transparent ground: a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding along, counters open, and reading as the bolt inside the hexagon at the size it actually sits on a card on the channel's dark ground and on the accent colour. Delivered with a stated minimum reproduction size and, where the vector will not hold, an honest alternative form for the smallest placements.

deliverables.name: Voltcast card set as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: One native editable Express document carrying the sponsor read card, the spec callouts and the end card, each root keeping its own canvas size for the long-form and vertical feeds, with live editable text in one licensed type system, the bug as real vector shapes on every card, photography carried as embedded image data rather than a reference, the sponsor's name in the intended cut of the intended family, and the disclosure line complete and legible word for word. Delivered with the self-contained source HTML, which is the durable half, since the host reopens this every episode.

deliverables.name: Delivery note and sign-off board
deliverables.spec: A written note recording what the short kept and dropped, the audio decisions per passage and per half of the mic move, every resize any tool reported with the asset it applied to, the disagreement between the host's notes and the episode as published, what the sponsor's named family actually resolved to, and the bug's minimum reproduction size with what to use below it. Paired with a persistent shareable board carrying the thumbnail options, the graded stills and the licensed ground with nothing silently dropped.

verifiers_auto.text: The feed short is shorter than the master, and the upright and square versions match the short in duration rather than being independently timed.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the duration of every delivered piece from its container metadata: assert the feed short's duration is strictly less than the master's, and assert the upright (9:16) and square (1:1) versions each equal the feed short's duration to within one frame (<= 1/24 s, the master being 24 fps), against the parent the manifest names for each.

verifiers_auto.text: No delivered video exceeds the frame size of the piece it derives from and no delivered still exceeds its source select's pixel dimensions.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the pixel frame dimensions of every delivered file from metadata and compare each against the source named in the manifest: assert no delivered still exceeds its source select's dimensions of 1920x1080, and assert each delivered video's frame size is <= the frame size of the piece it derives from (each reframe <= the feed short, the feed short <= the master).

verifiers_auto.text: No crop or knockout tradeoff record captured in the run carries an upscale entry, and every downscaled entry is transcribed in the delivery note.
verifiers_auto.how: Diff the tradeoffs objects captured from every image call against the resize table in the note: assert every tradeoffs object reports upscale_factor <= 1.0 (crop_and_resize silently interpolates up to a 2x cap and reports it only inside tradeoffs), and assert every entry whose scale factor is < 1.0 appears verbatim in the note's resize table with its source asset named.

verifiers_auto.text: The transparent thumbnail variant carries genuine alpha rather than a filled rectangle.
verifiers_auto.how: Inspect the alpha channel: assert partial-alpha pixels exist along the subject boundary and assert all four frame corners are fully transparent (alpha == 0), ruling out a filled opaque rectangle.

verifiers_auto.text: The bug's artwork carries a viewBox and has no full-canvas opaque path at index zero.
verifiers_auto.how: Parse the delivered SVG: assert a non-empty viewBox attribute is present, and assert the first path element's bounding box does not span the whole canvas (its width and height are each < 98% of the viewBox extent), ruling out the opaque full-canvas ground path image_vectorize emits at index zero.

verifiers_auto.text: The Express export returned one root per card, each keeping its own declared canvas size, and the bug is present as path shapes on every one of them.
verifiers_auto.how: Read slide_count and each root's declared width and height from the export response: assert slide_count == 3 (sponsor read card, spec callouts card, end card), assert at least two distinct canvas aspect ratios are present across the three roots (the 16:9 long-form card and the 9:16 vertical card each keeping its own size, i.e. no global canvas override collapsed the set), then parse each card's returned markup and assert its bug region contains more than one <path> shape (not a single filled rect) on every card.

verifiers_auto.text: The sponsor disclosure line appears in the returned markup complete and character for character as supplied, on the card it belongs on.
verifiers_auto.how: Extract the text content from the returned per-card markup and assert the disclosure string is present character-for-character identical (whitespace and punctuation included) to the disclosure line in voltcast_sponsor_readout.txt, in full on the sponsor read card and not split across two cards.

verifiers_auto.text: No image on any card resolved to the importer's placeholder, and every text element carries a resolved licensed PostScript face rather than a fallback default.
verifiers_auto.how: Parse the returned per-card markup: assert no <image> element resolves to the importer placeholder (the empty grey box), and assert every text node's font-family attribute matches a PostScript face returned by the kit call rather than a fallback (no bare sans-serif, serif, or importer default).

verifiers_auto.text: The face carrying the sponsor's name is the intended cut of the intended family rather than an arbitrary style returned by a name lookup.
verifiers_auto.how: Compare the resolved PostScript face on the sponsor name element ('Meridian VPN') against the Halstead Grotesk family style inventory returned by font_styles: assert it is the regular upright cut the note records as intended, not an italic, condensed, or display style of the kind a bare family-name lookup returns.

verifiers_auto.text: The sign-off board exists and carries the full sign-off asset set with nothing silently dropped and within the per-call cap.
verifiers_auto.how: Query the created board: assert it exists and holds the thumbnail options, the graded episode still set and the one licensed camera-scale ground frame; assert no single boards_add_items_to_board call placed more than 12 items (the hard per-call cap); and assert the response's failedItems list is empty for every add call, since a partial success is reported as a success and each intended item must be confirmed present rather than assumed.

verifiers_auto.text: The near-duplicate pair and the soft frame are excluded from the delivered still set and named in the note rather than shipped.
verifiers_auto.how: Against the delivered still manifest, assert the set includes at most one of the near-duplicate pair voltcast_e42_select_04.jpg / voltcast_e42_select_11.jpg and does not include the soft frame voltcast_e42_select_10.jpg; then assert the delivery note names select_10 as the soft/out-of-focus frame and names select_04 and select_11 as the duplicate pair, stating which was kept and which was dropped.

verifiers_human.text: At every point in the short where the host says to listen to something, the thing is audible.
verifiers_human.how: Listen through the short with the segment inventory in hand and mark each demonstration passage present or absent.

verifiers_human.text: The narration is even across the mic move and neither half sounds processed against the other.
verifiers_human.how: Listen across the join and across the sponsor read at normal listening level.

verifiers_human.text: The short promotes the verdict the episode actually reaches, in the order the episode reaches it.
verifiers_human.how: Watch the short against the master's segment inventory and the host's notes, and confirm the disagreement is reported rather than propagated.

verifiers_human.text: All three units remain readable in the upright and the square versions.
verifiers_human.how: View each reframe at phone scale and confirm the shootout still reads as a shootout.

verifiers_human.text: The thumbnail cutout holds its edge along the top and through the carry handle when seen at full size on the accent colour.
verifiers_human.how: View the thumbnail at full resolution on the accent ground and inspect the shared-value boundary.

verifiers_human.text: The bug still reads as the bolt inside the hexagon at the size it sits on a card, on the dark card ground, with its counters open.
verifiers_human.how: View each card at its reproduction size rather than at canvas size, and check the bug against the supplied original.

verifiers_human.text: The published stills sit in a grid as one channel rather than as a run of individually good frames.
verifiers_human.how: Lay the delivered stills out at grid scale and judge white point, black point and crop logic as a set.

verifiers_human.text: The package reads as a credible independent reviewer, not as a broadcast package and not as an advertorial.
verifiers_human.how: Judge pace, furniture density, type scale and how the products are presented, against the stated band and audience.

verifiers_human.text: The note tells the host something he did not already know, including everything that could not be delivered.
verifiers_human.how: Read the note against the run and check that every reconciliation and every limitation is named.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are motion work, which are raster work, and which need an authored fixed canvas document, given that only one surface here composes free-form layout.
Whether the audio is treated as one file or as two populations, narration and demonstration, and where evenness is judged once it is two.
How much of the mic move can be reconciled before the two halves start sounding processed against each other.
Which segments the short has to carry, given that the host's notes and the episode disagree about both the verdict order and how many segments there are, and how to raise that with him.
How to frame a three way shootout upright and square when the ceiling is set by what the cut returned rather than by the 4K master.
Whether the host's chosen thumbnail select can actually carry a thumbnail, and how to say so if it cannot.
Knockout route on the holding shot: a subject cut, or a material-named ground selection inverted and filled, decided by what the wall shares with the subject.
How the bug is prepared for tracing, since raster preparation is the only lever the tracing tool has, and what to deliver for placements below the size the vector holds.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a credible independent reviewer, plus what the sponsor's named family actually resolves to and what to do about it.
Whether the card measure is set from the short lines or from the disclosure line that cannot be shortened.
Which stills join the grid and which are named as duplicates or soft rather than shipped.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image or video model and it returns generic tech-review-looking footage, a generic thumbnail and a generic bolt logo. IDENTITY: this is this channel's actual episode with its actual host, its actual three units and its actual verdict, the thumbnail is a specific frame the host chose of himself, and the bug must be reproduced from the channel's own file rather than redrawn, because a regenerated bolt is a different channel. SPEC: the short must be a genuine reduction of a specific twelve minute master, the reframes must not be enlarged, the sponsor's disclosure line must appear word for word, and the sponsor's name must be in a specific cut of a specific family, none of which a generated piece satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the card set is defined by being editable, because the host publishes several times a week and currently rebuilds these from scratch every episode. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did the fan ramp survive the speech treatment, did the knockout bite the handle, does the bug still have counters at the size it prints.
doability_proof: Every link is drawn from CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account) and the standing DOABLE list, five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. MOTION: video_create_quick_cut only ever SHORTENS, which is why the short is a reduction rather than an assembly, video_resize never enlarges, which is why the reframe ceiling is real, and media_summarize and media_enhance_speech are the summary and speech surfaces; these run on the connector's submit-and-resolve path and no gate in this task depends on measuring a frame or a waveform, only on watching and listening to what came back. No timestamp trimming, no format conversion and no frame extraction is used anywhere, so the thumbnail comes from the supplied selects rather than from the video. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, auto_tone, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, select_subject, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and detection_confidence, fill_area, remove_background in both the transparent and backgroundColor forms, and vectorize are all verified headless across 27 live calls. The checkpoints rest on documented findings rather than assumptions: selection masks come back fully binary so any edge softness must come from remove_background's alpha, image_vectorize TAKES NO OPTIONS AT ALL so all tuning must happen in the raster prep, its output carries NO viewBox and an opaque full-canvas path at index zero, alpha survives crops at outputFileType png, and crop_and_resize will silently interpolate up to a two times cap while reporting it only inside tradeoffs. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, the product is a genuine editable dcx findable by asset_search, an inline SVG must sit in a wrapper with explicit left, top, width and height or its contents run off the canvas, and the rendition preview is documented as PAGE 1 ONLY, which is why the bug is audited from the returned per-card markup on every card. Transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined photography passes the 70 KB threshold immediately. FONTS: find_fonts FAMILY-NAME LOOKUP RETURNS AN ARBITRARY STYLE rather than the regular cut, get_fontkit_embed_url is case-sensitive and all-or-nothing, numeric weights are non-standard per family, and the CSS must use the returned slug, all verified; the sponsor's named face rides directly on those findings. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed, license returns a real camera-scale JPEG, and boards persist with a hard cap of 12 placements per call and a partial success reported as a success. AVOIDED: no animate_design, no fill_text, no video_render or video_render_frame, no vector render or vector merge, no upscaling, no compositing, no OCR, no text-to-image, no photo reaching Express as a URL, no batch above 20.

engagement_title: DAYDRIFT season four handover: pull a representative picture out of three episodes shot months apart and bring them to one channel look, recover the show name off the microphone flag, and rebuild the printer's episode card into a live nine record run
vertical: Music, film, publishing and media, independent long form interview podcast with a membership and one renewing sponsor (Portland, Oregon)
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Freelancer.com YouTube podcast post carried in the ledger, where a two person show hands over raw episode recordings and asks for episodes shaped into something watchable, for light hearted graphics that match a casual fun vibe, for the client's existing logo carried across the channel branding, and for any custom graphic assets created to be delivered separately in transparent PNG or vector form. Two literal asks in that post are not connector work and are re cast honestly rather than faked. A timeline trim of pauses and stumbles has no connector analogue, because the shortening tool works from engagement rather than from timestamps, so the short vertical pieces are produced by that route and the brief asks for short cuts rather than for a re edited episode. Motion graphics composited over the picture are also unavailable, so the caption plate and the end card are delivered as editable canvases the show drops into its own editor, and the brief asks for a plate rather than for burned in captions. Everything else in that post is now genuinely producible: CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) confirms an ink level recovery off photographed printed collateral, a merge template reverse engineered out of a flat press PDF, and a native editable Express document carrying mixed canvas sizes, which is exactly the separately delivered, client editable asset set the poster asked for and never got.
client_one_liner: Season four is recorded and edited, our channel page looks like nine different shows, and the only place our name still exists as artwork is the foam flag on the microphone.
client_brief:
DAYDRIFT, season four handover

We are a two person interview show out of Portland. Nine episodes a season, one guest, long form, recorded in our own room. A few thousand regular listeners, about two hundred paying members at eight dollars a month, and one sponsor who renews if the numbers hold.

Here is where we are. Season four is recorded and the audio is edited. What we have never had is a look. Every episode goes up with whatever still we grabbed that week, so our page reads as nine different shows stacked on top of each other. We want one look all of them can sit inside, and we want it built so we can keep using it ourselves next season without coming back to you.

The recordings. Three of the nine are the ones to work from first. They were shot months apart and the room was honestly not the same each time. Please pull a picture out of each that actually represents that conversation, and bring the three of them to one look. Warm and lived in, like a room people talk in. Not a news set.

Short vertical pieces. One short vertical cut per episode for the feeds, and the speech needs to be cleaner than it is. Nothing stretched or blown up to fit. We would rather it be smaller and sharp.

The name. Our show name only exists as artwork on the foam flag on our microphone. The friend who drew it moved away and there is no file. We need it back as something we can put on anything, at any size, on dark or on light.

The cards. We print an episode card for the merch table at live tapings and mail one to every member. Last year's card came back from our printer as a print file and we still have it. Build this season's nine cards from that same card, each with its own episode details.

Also the thumbnails, a caption plate for the verticals and an end card, all in one working file we can open and change ourselves, because guests move and dates move.

Our listeners are thirty to fifty and most of them listen at work. And a written note on what you did and how to use the name.
price_band_and_audience: Independent long form podcast, eight dollar monthly membership, one modest renewing sponsor, listeners thirty to fifty. The band is load bearing. At this level the look has to read considered and hand made: warm domestic light, real texture in the room, restrained type, the picture of two people talking rather than a set. Push it toward broadcast, with a hard lit black seamless, a hard geometric grid and a network style lockup, and it misrepresents a two person show to the exact membership that pays for it because it is not that. Push it the other way into a scrappy meme treatment, with heavy outlines, arrows and shouted type, and it reads as the wrong genre entirely for a fifty minute interview and the sponsor renewal argument collapses. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even when every technical gate passes. A real posted job of this shape runs 900 to 2,000 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: Independent long form interview podcast with a YouTube channel, one guest per episode, made and recorded in the show's own room.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Started 2021 in Portland, Oregon. A two person show: two hosts, one room, nine episodes a season.
brand_identity.about: DAYDRIFT is a slow, unhurried interview show built around one guest and one real conversation that runs the better part of an hour. It is made by two people in a room they know well, funded by a small paying membership and one renewing sponsor. The promise is intimacy: you are sitting in on a talk between people who like each other, not watching a broadcast.
brand_identity.audience: Regular listeners aged thirty to fifty, most of them listening at work through the day. About two hundred paying members at eight dollars a month, plus a few thousand free listeners who click through to the channel page.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Membership at eight dollars a month with one modest renewing sponsor. Squarely independent: above hobby, well below a network production. The look must read considered and hand made, never broadcast and never scrappy meme.
brand_identity.typography: A warm humanist serif for the show name and episode titles, paired with a quiet humanist sans for credits, dates and body. Generous spacing, restrained weights, nothing condensed or shouted. Type should feel like a good paperback, not a title card.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, warm and a little understated, the way two friends actually talk. We never oversell a guest. Example line the brand would write: "Episode eight. We sat down with her for an hour and did not want it to end."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There are no brand files left. The show name only survives as artwork on the foam flag on the microphone, drawn years ago by a friend who has since moved away and left no source file. Last season's printed episode card exists only as the print file the printer returned. Everything else has to be rebuilt from those.
brand_identity.values: Honesty and warmth over polish. The show would rather be small and real than slick, and it wants a look it can keep running itself next season without re commissioning.

assets_supplied.name: daydrift_episodes/ (three episode recordings, season four)

Episode five was recorded after a window was uncovered and carries a cold cast down the guest side only, while episode eight has a warm practical lamp burning behind the host. Episode two also came out of an older export at a smaller frame size than the other two, which no filename, folder or note reveals, so the vertical cut taken from it is bounded lower than its neighbours before any decision is made.

assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The wordmark is disjoint lettering on a soft compressible surface, so the one call knockout keeps two or three letters, drops the rest and still returns success. acceptance_bar: The three episode pictures read as one channel when they are stacked the way a channel page stacks them: one white point, one black point, one warmth, one sense of how much room is in the frame. A picture that cannot be brought to the set is named, not shipped at eighty percent.

No delivered still, card picture or vertical cut exceeds the pixel dimensions of the recording or frame it came from, and no returned resize report carries an enlargement entry. Reaching a size by interpolation fails even where it looks acceptable.
Each of the three pictures represents its own episode, not the same three seconds of two people sitting still. The guest is recognisable and present in each.

The show name comes back as placeable artwork rather than a picture of artwork: transparent, scalable with a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath it, every letter present, and it still reads as our name where it actually reproduces, on the dark band and reversed on light.
The nine cards are one press file with one record per page, page count equal to row count, every field on every card filled from its own row, and the sponsor line present and complete on all nine.
Every card is legible and complete at trim. A record whose title stops part way through is a failed card even when the merge reported success.
Where a card cannot carry what the roster promises, the gap is named in writing with what was delivered instead. Six episodes have no picture and nobody has said so yet.
The vertical cuts are shorter than their sources, carry cleaned speech, and are reframed by reduction only. Cleaning after cutting is not the same job and does not count.

All the channel canvases arrive in ONE working file, each keeping its own canvas size, with the words as text we can retype, the name as real vector shapes and every picture carried inside the file rather than pointed at. The self contained source it was built from comes with it.
The caption plate still reads as a caption plate after it has been handed over, on every canvas and not only the first one.
One type system across every canvas and the note names, per role, the family, its foundry or designer and the actual weight used.

The note states per picture what was applied and why that episode differs from its neighbours, every resize any tool reported, the roster reconciliation, and what we can and cannot do with the recovered name.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Premiere video and audio
adobe_surfaces.tools: video_metadata, video_render_frame, media_enhance_speech, video_create_quick_cut, video_resize
adobe_surfaces.role: The front and the back of the engagement. It reads what each recording actually is before anything is planned, because the roster's episode numbers say nothing about a file's frame size and the vertical delivery height is bounded by the source. It pulls the representative picture out of each of the three episodes, cleans the speech before anything is cut so the cleaning applies to the whole take rather than to three chosen fragments, produces the short vertical pieces by the engagement route rather than by timestamps, and reframes to vertical by reduction only.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including image_vectorize which is counted HERE and not as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_invert_selection, image_fill_area, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs, detection_confidence and upscale_factor), image_remove_background, image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Every raster decision. It fixes one channel target off the best lit of the three pulled pictures and corrects the other two toward it one call at a time rather than batching one parameter set across three different rooms, confines corrections where a whole frame move would take the guest's skin with the window, cuts the card pictures and the thumbnail pictures without enlarging anything, and recovers the wordmark at ink level off a photographed foam flag with the vector hygiene the tracing tool does not perform for you.

adobe_surfaces.surface: InDesign layout and data merge
adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt (as mapper and as validator), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout, document_render_layout
adobe_surfaces.role: The nine episode cards, built out of the printer's own file so the season matches last season on the merch table. The template is reverse engineered from a flat press PDF, which means the frame inventory has to be read out of the round tripped document rather than assumed from the printed page, the true story text has to be reconstructed before a single offset is computed, and the placeholders have to be re verified after preparation because the preparation step reports success either way. Delivery is one press file with one record per page plus per record proofs, and the fact that bleed cannot be introduced into a PDF derived template is disclosed rather than faked.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The thumbnails, the vertical caption plate and the end card as one native editable document carrying roots at three canvas sizes, which is the only surface here that composes free form fixed canvas layout and the only one that leaves the show something it can change itself next season. Every picture must be pulled down and carried as embedded image data because a reference renders as an empty grey box at full success, the recovered name goes in as inline vector inside an explicitly sized top left anchored wrapper, family and weight are declared on every text element, and the payload travels as an uploaded file because inlined photography passes the inline threshold immediately.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Fonts
adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: The type system carried across every canvas and recorded in the handover. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to land warm and domestic rather than broadcast. Numeric weights are non standard per family and cannot be read off a style name, a display cut is reached by its own slug rather than by a weight, every name has to be laundered into canonical form before the kit call because one bad name kills the whole kit, and the CSS has to use the returned slug or it falls back silently.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching anything.
trajectory.judgement: The cards are a record per page run and belong on the merge surface; the thumbnails, plate and end card are one off canvases the client must edit next season and only one surface here composes free form layout. The brief pins both destinations, so there is nothing to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming the surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline: a manifest keyed by role, so that forty artefacts later the agent still knows which URL is which episode.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Read what each of the three recordings actually is: frame size, duration and audio state, before any framing or delivery size is promised.
trajectory.judgement: The roster asserts three episodes of one show. Episode numbering is not evidence about a file, and the vertical delivery height is bounded by whatever the smallest source turns out to be.
trajectory.produces: A per recording note of true dimensions, duration and audio condition.

trajectory.action: Pull a representative picture out of each of the three episodes.
trajectory.judgement: Representative means the conversation, not the prettiest hundredth of a second. A frame where the guest is mid sentence and present beats a frame where both people happen to be still.
trajectory.produces: Three candidate pictures, one per episode, at each recording's own scale.

trajectory.action: Preview all three pulled pictures and triage them: where each frame's neutral actually sits, which side of the frame the light is coming from, what is off level, and how much room each has around the two people.
trajectory.judgement: The client believes it is the same room three times. The pictures are the only place that can be settled, and a cold window on one side of one frame is a different correction from a warm lamp behind the host.
trajectory.produces: A per picture triage note covering illuminant, tilt, and available room around the subjects.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level, before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop that has already been committed.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Fix one channel target off the best lit picture and correct the other two toward it with their own calls, recording the parameters applied to each.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a set of three, not three good pictures. One batched call applies one identical parameter set, which is exactly wrong for three different rooms. The destination is held constant and reached by different routes.
trajectory.produces: Three graded masters at source scale with a per picture parameter log.

trajectory.action: Confine corrections where a whole frame move goes wrong, selecting by the material's own visual properties rather than by the object it sits on.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the whole gate: naming the substrate pulls the selection to the wall. Pulling the cold window side of one frame back without taking the guest's skin with it is a confined move, not a global one.
trajectory.produces: Corrected frames where a whole frame move would have taken the skin green or the room muddy.

trajectory.action: Recover the show name off the microphone flag: an ink level selection naming the mark's own visual properties, correct polarity, a bounds crop driven by the selection's own returned box, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full canvas ground path removed.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions no tool makes: how to word the selection so it takes the ink rather than the foam, which polarity to trace, and whether the two colour trace or the colour accurate plate is the deliverable. Background removal is the wrong instrument on disjoint lettering and will hand back a few letters at full success.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent wordmark plus a colour accurate variant.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged against a warm domestic show with a thirty to fifty audience rather than against a network. The weight cannot be inferred from a style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Convert last season's press card into an editable document, round trip it back out as an interchange file, and read what the conversion actually exposed as frames before promising any mapping.
trajectory.judgement: What a printed page looks like says nothing about how many addressable frames it becomes. This has to be looked at, not assumed, because every downstream mapping decision and the picture on the card both depend on the answer.
trajectory.produces: A converted template plus a written frame inventory: how many text frames, how many picture frames, and what each one actually holds.

trajectory.action: Reconstruct the frame's true story text from the round tripped document's own runs, compute every offset from that string, build the mapping, prepare the merge template, then re export and confirm each expected placeholder is genuinely present.
trajectory.judgement: The readout that lists a frame's text is a convenience, not the document. Validation passing is not evidence that the mapping matched the document, and the preparation step reports success either way, so the only proof is the re exported story.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholders are confirmed present by inspection rather than by a success message.

trajectory.action: Merge the nine records, then render the press file and the per record proofs, and reconcile the roster against what actually exists.
trajectory.judgement: Multi record raster output order is not trustworthy, so identity is guaranteed through the press file or through per record renders rather than by position in a list. Nine rows want nine pictures and three episodes were shot as frames, which is a thing to say in writing rather than to paper over by repeating one picture.
trajectory.produces: One press file with one record per page, per record proofs, and a written roster reconciliation.

trajectory.action: Clean the speech on each of the three episodes, then produce the short vertical piece from the cleaned take, then reframe to vertical by reduction only.
trajectory.judgement: Cleaning has to precede cutting or it only touches whatever fragments survived. The shortening route works from engagement rather than from timestamps, so the ask is a short cut and not a re edit, and the vertical height is bounded by the smallest source rather than by the platform.
trajectory.produces: Three short vertical cuts with cleaned speech, each at or below its source dimensions.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML carrying the thumbnail canvases, the vertical caption plate and the end card, each root declaring its own canvas size, every picture inlined as image data, the recovered name placed as inline vector inside an explicitly sized top left anchored wrapper, and family and weight declared on every text element. Upload the file and hold the returned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A picture left as a reference is not a picture, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas edge, and a global canvas override is precisely what collapses a mixed size set. The design work is how warm and how quiet the plate is at this band, and how large the name can sit.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML carrying the whole channel set, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at the first canvas, and parse the returned per canvas markup for every canvas after it.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning of any kind, and the rendition only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at canvas one is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document, an inspected first canvas, and a per canvas markup audit for the rest.

trajectory.action: Write the note: what was applied per picture and why each episode differs from its neighbours, the type system by role, every resize any tool reported, the roster reconciliation, what could not be delivered and why, and how to use the recovered name.
trajectory.judgement: The note is the deliverable the show still has in two years. It has to be specific enough that the next freelancer does not repeat the archaeology, and honest about the six cards with no picture and about bleed.
trajectory.produces: A written handover note covering the run, the gaps and the limitations.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What last season's card actually becomes as an editable document. The printed page shows an episode number, a title, a guest credit, a date, a sponsor line and a picture window, which reads as six separately addressable blocks. The conversion's frame granularity is not under anyone's control: a continuous text flow can collapse into exactly ONE text frame holding every line, and a page whose picture is drawn rather than placed can convert with ZERO graphic frames, so there is nothing to bind a per record picture to. Nothing in the printed artwork, the file name or any tool description predicts which of those happened, and the conversion reports success in every case.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter controls it, because the granularity is decided inside the conversion and can only be read afterwards by round tripping the document and looking. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says the printer's file exists and asks for this season's cards from the same card, and the roster's picture column is the client's expectation rather than a disclosure about frames. (c) It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a different mapping strategy entirely: per frame mapping if the blocks are separate, offset based replacement inside one story if they are not, and if no picture frame exists then the picture on the card has to be re planned and renegotiated in writing rather than merged.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re plan the entire mapping approach around the frame inventory that actually came back, re decide how the per record picture is delivered if no picture frame exists, and revisit what the nine cards can honestly carry before any mapping is written.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A mapping written against blocks that do not exist, which validates, prepares and merges cleanly and produces nine cards carrying last season's text with this season's roster nowhere on them.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the readout that lists the frame's text is the frame's text. It can silently omit an entire run while keeping that run's line break, so the string it hands back still looks well formed and correctly punctuated, and every character offset past the omission is short by the exact length of the dropped run. Every downstream signal agrees with the mistake: the validator returns valid with zero warnings on the wrong offsets, and the template preparation returns completed successfully. The only place the truth exists is the document's own story runs, and the only proof the placeholders landed is re exporting after preparation and reading them.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Doing it right first time presumes knowing that this particular readout dropped this particular run on this card, which no response, warning or field reports. The defensive route of reconstructing the story by hand is the route a competent agent adopts once the mismatch is visible, and it is not free. (b) Nothing states it: the brief describes a card and a roster, and the acceptance line about every field on every card is the client's standing requirement rather than a warning that a readout lies. (c) It is not a propagation re run, because the mapping is rebuilt against a different source of truth, not resubmitted unchanged.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reconstruct the true story text from the document's own runs, recompute every offset from that string, rebuild and re prepare the mapping, then re export and confirm each placeholder individually before a single record is merged.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Nine printed cards on the merch table with the guest credit and the contractual sponsor line silently absent, delivered against a run in which the validator said valid and every tool said success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the caption plate. A plate whose whole job is to keep words legible over whatever is behind them is authored the natural way as outlined type over a softened panel, and this importer drops an outline entirely, drops a blur outright, drops a blend mode to a plain opaque shape, and truncates a layered glow to its first layer. Outlined type combined with a transparent fill arrives fully invisible. All of it returns success with no warning, the returned per canvas markup is the only channel that reports it, and the document's own rendition shows the first artboard only, so the vertical plate and the end card can be checked no other way.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) The drop happens at import, which is the last step, so no ordering precedes it, and doing it right first time presumes knowing which of several equally reasonable constructions survives, which no tool reports and no checklist enumerates. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for a caption plate and the acceptance line about it still reading as a plate is the client's own art direction. (c) It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a different construction: carry the legibility in an upstream raster, or rebuild the plate on a solid panel and re judge whether it still reads at all, then re compose the canvas around whichever answer wins.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re author the plate and the end card around constructions the importer keeps, re upload, re run the readiness check, re export, and audit every canvas from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A working file handed to the show in which the caption plate's words are invisible and the end card is a flat opaque slab, on the two canvases nobody looked at, with the export having reported success throughout.

verifiers_auto.how: Diff the tradeoff objects captured from every image and video call against the resize table in the note.
