decision_gates: Which deliverables are frame work and which need an authored fixed canvas document, given that only one surface here composes free form layout and the client must edit the result daily.
Which of the eight cards is a usable reference and which is not, and what replaces a card when it cannot be trusted.
Where the show white point sits, weighted toward a target a different editor can reach again tomorrow rather than the most flattering one available today.
Whether to reach that target by eight different routes or one, across frames shot seven hours apart under moving daylight.
Which of the two house colour values in the client's own notes governs the thumbnail, and how to justify the choice rather than picking.
Which knockout route holds this particular rim, decided on the ground the plate will actually sit on rather than against white.
Whether the missing segment is solved with a licensed frame or declared as a gap, and if licensed, which frame's existing light can be brought to the target.
How much of the day's summary belongs in the caption copy once the delivered cut is known, since a summary of the take is not a summary of the spot.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against daytime television rather than a food magazine, plus the real numeric weight per family.
What belongs in the recipe: which decisions are today's and which are the show's standing rules, because the client is buying the second kind.

How the Market Open card is handled when no frame was exported, between binding the licensed establishing frame, a deliberate no picture treatment, or a declared gap, decided before the run rather than found on the printed deck.

Which delivery route carries per segment proof identity safely, given a returned list order is not evidence of which segment is inside a file, and what names each proof from what it actually contains.

The ember mark recovery: naming the paint's own colour rather than the panel, keeping the ember with the wordmark as a compound rather than dropping it, and whether the single colour cutting version or the colour accurate variant is what the endboard and the deck need, judged at the small reproduction size on the show's own grounds, plus the safe minimum height.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns attractive pictures of a bright kitchen. IDENTITY: these are this show's own eight segments, this host, today's actual dish and the show's real house colour, and the promo has to be cut from the day's real take rather than imagined. SPEC: the frames must reach one shared white point that a different person can hit again tomorrow, the vertical must be derived downward only from a source of known dimensions, and every segment in the rundown has to be accounted for, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the caption cards are defined by being retyped daily by the producer, and the recipe is the actual product, since the client explicitly is not paying for this again on Tuesday. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did that recovery move anything, does the rim hold on the colour band, did the second and third cards survive the import, does the mark hold at the corner size, is the segment inside this proof the one on its row. RECOVERY AND MERGE: the show's on air bug survives only as a low resolution grab and has to be recovered as closed paths a cutter and the endboard can use rather than regenerated, because a generated bug is a different mark in a different hand, and the daily card deck needs one card per segment bound to that segment's own still with page count equal to the rundown, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for.
doability_proof: Every link is grounded in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), six surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability. VIDEO AND AUDIO: only video_metadata, video_create_quick_cut, video_resize, media_enhance_speech and media_summarize are used, submitted headlessly with the host's progress channel resolving them, and the task depends on none of the capabilities that are unavailable here: no trim to timestamp, no multi clip assembly, no format conversion, no upscale, with the cut only shortening and the re aspect only going down. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, highlight recovery, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, select_subject, invert_selection, fill_area, remove_background in both the transparent and solid ground forms, crop_to_bounds and crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and detection confidence are all verified headless across live calls. Checkpoint one rests on the documented absence of any anti aliased or partial readout for a clipped value range, so a recovery on fully clipped values returns an unchanged frame at success. Checkpoint two rests on the documented dependence of subject detection on local contrast and on the substrate versus material prompt asymmetry, which is exactly the route the correct answer takes. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed since it returns zero hits, licensing verified to return a genuine full resolution frame, and boards verified to persist with a hard placement cap per call and a partial result meaning partial. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export and a genuine editable document findable by asset_search are verified, the rendition preview is documented as first artboard only, and a background image carried as embedded data is a documented total drop leaving an empty box at HTTP success, which is checkpoint three. Transport goes by uploaded URL because inlined frames pass the inline threshold immediately. FONTS: find_fonts is used first because a kit request containing one unresolvable name fails outright and discards the valid names with it, and the non standard numeric weights make the style inventory step mandatory. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt with its validator pass, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout with recordRange and additionalImageFiles and document_render_layout with createSeparateFiles and resolution are verified fully headless and synchronous, with one record per page for a PDF sourced template and page count equal to row count; the reverse engineering rests on the verified fact that the printed card's apparent fields are not the frame inventory the conversion exposes, so offsets are reconstructed from the document's own story text and every placeholder re verified in the re-exported document because both the validator and the prepare step report success on a template silently missing fields; the proof identity checkpoint rests on the verified finding that multi record PNG and JPEG output comes back reversed while the response labels it by row, with PDF, createSeparateFiles and a recordRange loop as the three verified trustworthy routes, and a blank picture cell binds an empty well at success rather than raising; no bleed can be introduced from a template whose media box equals its trim. VECTOR RECOVERY: image_vectorize is verified headless and takes no options at all, so every lever is in the raster preparation, a compound mark selection silently drops elements, naming the substrate returns the substrate, the trace emits no viewBox and path index zero is always an opaque full canvas rectangle, which is the ember mark checkpoint, and the low resolution grab makes the counter close at reproduction size a genuine property of the recovery rather than of the call. AVOIDED: no animate_design, no fill_text, no create_firefly_board, no document_render_vector, no document_merge_data_vector, no OCR, no text to image, no photo reaching Express as a URL, no upscaling, no batch above twenty.

engagement_title: The Halden Diaries season two kit: bring eight differently lit episodes to one channel look, recover the wordmark off the painted desk board, cut the season recap tall and wide, and rebuild the patron postcard the printer made last year into a live eight card run
vertical: Music, Film, Publishing and Media. Independent daily vlog channel entering its first sponsored season, self shot, self edited, patron supported, based in Portland, Maine
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Freelancer.com post from a creator who films their own day to day content and needs recurring per episode post production, quoted in the ledger's grounding_note. The literal ask names basic colour correction, supporting graphics for lower thirds and end screens, 4K capture delivered as web ready 1080p, the supporting custom graphics wanted as their own deliverables, and an ongoing episode to episode collaboration rather than a one off. Two things in that post do not survive contact with the connector and are therefore re carved rather than pretended: on screen text burn in and lower third compositing do not exist here, so the supporting graphics become an authored editable end plate and caption plate set that the creator edits himself each week, which is closer to what the post actually wanted (graphics he keeps) than a burned in overlay he would have to re commission. The episode to episode consistency half of the post is the real commission and it is fully doable: one house look across eight differently lit episodes, one recovered wordmark, one recap in two aspects, and the printed patron card the post's real world equivalent creator sends out at season end. The creator handle is laundered to a fully invented persona, The Halden Diaries, wordmark HALDEN, tagline an ordinary week filmed, run by fictional creator Nate Halden. No real person, channel, sponsor or platform account is referenced.
client_one_liner: Eight episodes are locked and they do not look like one channel, my logo only exists as a painted board behind my desk, and the patron cards have to be at the printer in three weeks.
client_brief:
The Halden Diaries, season two kit

I film my own week and put out an episode every Sunday. Eight episodes are cut and locked for season two, and these are the first ones with a sponsor attached, so this is the first time the look matters to somebody other than me.

The honest state of things. I shoot in the kitchen, at the desk by the window, and out on the evening walk, and I shoot whenever the light happens to be there. Line the eight up and they do not look like one channel. Some are cold. The kitchen ones are orange. One is just brighter than everything else. I want the eight episode pictures to read as though they came off the same channel, and I want them to still look like my flat and not like a studio.

I need a short recap of the season for the top of the channel page, and the same recap again tall for the phone feed. My voiceover for it is recorded but it is rough, and there is a fridge in it somewhere.

My patrons get a set of printed cards at the end of every season, one card per episode. The printer did last year's set for me and I still have the file they printed from. I need the same card for these eight, each with its own picture, its own date and its own title.

The channel name only exists as a painted board that hangs behind my desk. I have never had a file for it. I need it as artwork, because it has to go on the cards and on the end plate.

And I need an end plate and a caption plate I can change myself every week, because the episode number moves and I am not paying somebody for that.

It should feel like an ordinary week filmed well. Warm, unhurried, a bit lived in. Not slick and not a brand.
price_band_and_audience: Sponsorship tier lifestyle vlog, patron subscriptions at 6 dollars a month with a printed card set at season end, audience 24 to 38 and loyal rather than large. The band is load bearing in both directions. Push it up and the work becomes a studio channel: crushed contrast, a cool graded look, a hard geometric plate, a logo that sits large. That look reads as an agency production, it contradicts the whole premise of one man filming his own week, and the audience that pays 6 dollars a month for intimacy reads it as the channel having been bought. Push it down and it becomes a phone edit: no consistent white point, a caption plate in a default system face, a card that looks like a home printer job, which fails the sponsor who is paying for the season and fails the patrons who paid for a physical object. The correct register is domestic warmth held to a professional standard: one white point, one black point, real licensed type, restrained plates, and a wordmark that still looks hand painted because it was. A real posted job of this shape runs 900 to 2,200 dollars fixed with a per season retainer attached.

brand_identity.sector: Independent daily vlog channel, self shot and self edited, patron supported, entering its first sponsored season.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2021, Portland, Maine, a one person channel run entirely by its creator Nate Halden.
brand_identity.about: The Halden Diaries is a self shot, self edited vlog in which Nate Halden films an ordinary week in his own flat and puts out one episode every Sunday. The channel promises intimacy over production: the same rooms, the same face, the same unhurried attention week after week. Season two is its first with a sponsor, and the whole point is that the sponsor changed nothing about how the week feels.
brand_identity.audience: Loyal rather than large, aged 24 to 38, patrons who pay 6 dollars a month for closeness and receive a printed card set at each season end. They buy the feeling of a friend filming his week, not a studio production.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Patron subscriptions at 6 dollars a month with a printed card set mailed at season end, first sponsored season attached. Sits deliberately between a phone edit and a studio channel: domestic warmth held to a professional standard.
brand_identity.typography: Display: a warm humanist serif with a hand set feel that echoes the painted board. Text: a quiet, readable humanist sans. Nothing geometric and nothing slick. The type should feel set by hand at home rather than commissioned from an agency.
brand_identity.voice: First person, plain, unhurried, a little self deprecating. He writes the way he talks to camera. Example line: 'An ordinary week, filmed. Thanks for staying with it.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No brand files have ever existed. The channel name lives only as a board Nate hand painted on limewashed pine before the first episode, one deep ink with a painted hairline rule beneath it, and it survives only as a handheld photograph. The wordmark HALDEN has to be recovered from that photograph as usable artwork. There is no logo file, no colour spec and no prior guideline.
brand_identity.values: Intimacy and honesty: one man filming his own week, kept that way even with a sponsor in the room.

acceptance_bar: Laid out in a row the way a channel page lays them, the eight episode pictures read as one channel: one white point, one black point, one warmth, one contrast handling. A picture that cannot be brought to the set is named rather than shipped at eighty percent.
The flat still reads as a flat. A treatment that turns a domestic kitchen into a studio fails even if the eight match each other perfectly.

No delivered file exceeds the pixel dimensions of the source it came from, and no crop, resize or knockout tradeoff record in the run carries an upscale entry. A picture that reaches the card's box by being enlarged fails.
The vertical recap keeps him in frame for its whole length, not only at its first second. A vertical that returns the right dimensions with the subject at the edge is not delivered.
The recap's audio reads as one person in one room. A join where the voice changes distance mid sentence fails.

The patron card set is one press ready file with one page per episode, eight pages in the order of the episode list, each page carrying its own episode's picture, title, date and standfirst, and no record standing in for another.
Every field on the card is present on every page, including the URL along the foot, and the URL reads exactly as supplied.

The wordmark is placeable artwork rather than a picture of artwork: transparent, scalable with a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath it, and it still reads as the painted board at the size it actually reproduces on the card foot and on the end plate.

The end plate and the caption plate arrive in one working file he can edit, each keeping its own canvas size, with the words as text he can retype and the wordmark as live vector shapes rather than a picture of a layout, delivered alongside the self contained source they were built from.
One type system across the plates and the card, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the actual weight used.

The note states, per episode picture, what was applied and why that one differs from its neighbours, plus every resize any tool reported, what happened to the voiceover, and anything he should know about using the recovered mark.

trajectory.action: Preview all eight episode stills and read their true pixel dimensions against what the card's picture box and the plates actually need.
trajectory.judgement: The creator says these are frame grabs. The files are the only thing that can settle whether they all are, and a picture that cannot make the box has to be found now rather than at the printer.
trajectory.produces: A per still triage note covering illuminant, tilt, subject contrast against the ground, and true dimensions against every destination.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level, before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes the subject and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Fix one channel target from the best lit still and bring each of the eight toward it with its own call, recording the parameters applied.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a set, not eight good pictures, and it has to keep the flat looking like a flat. One batched call applies one identical parameter set, which is exactly wrong for kitchen tungsten, window daylight and evening dusk. The agent holds one destination and reaches it by three different routes.
trajectory.produces: Eight graded stills at source scale with a per still parameter log.

trajectory.action: Masked corrections where a whole frame move breaks something, selecting by the material's own visual properties rather than by the object it sits on.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the entire gate. Naming the room pulls the selection to the room. The kitchen frames need the tungsten pulled without taking the skin grey, and the dusk frame needs its sky held without flattening him into it.
trajectory.produces: Corrected frames where a global move would have gone wrong.

trajectory.action: Recover the wordmark off the painted board: a paint level selection naming the lettering's own visual properties, correct polarity, a bounds crop driven by the selection's own returned box, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full canvas ground path removed.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions no tool makes: how to word the selection so it takes the paint and not the plank, which polarity to trace, and whether the flat single colour mark or a colour accurate plate is what the card wants. Background removal is the wrong instrument on lettering with enclosed counters.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent wordmark plus a colour accurate variant.

trajectory.action: Cut the card picture boxes and the plate crops, reading every returned tradeoff record rather than the success message.
trajectory.judgement: The tradeoff record is the only channel that reports what a crop did to the dimensions, and it carries no warning language of any kind.
trajectory.produces: Eight card pictures and the plate crops, each with its returned tradeoff record captured.

trajectory.action: Clean the recap voiceover, then listen to it end to end rather than to its first ten seconds.
trajectory.judgement: Cleanup normalises noise, not distance. Two sittings recorded on two microphones a room apart do not become one voice because the hum is gone, and the response says nothing about it.
trajectory.produces: A cleaned voiceover with a written note on what the cleanup did and did not reconcile.

trajectory.action: Summarise the eight episode masters to find where the season's usable moments actually sit, since the agent did not cut them and cannot scrub them.
trajectory.judgement: Eight locked cuts made by somebody else are opaque. The summaries are the only map, and they are what makes the choice of source for the recap a decision rather than a guess.
trajectory.produces: A per episode content map and a shortlist of which episodes carry the recap.

trajectory.action: Cut the wide recap with the shortening cutter, then produce the vertical from it with the resizer, which never adds pixels.
trajectory.judgement: The cutter only shortens and picks its own moments inside what it is handed, so what it is handed is the real decision. The vertical is a reframe of a wide frame, which means something in that wide frame is being thrown away, and which thing depends on where he is standing.
trajectory.produces: A wide season recap and a vertical companion, both with their returned dimensions and durations recorded.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's, judged against a 6 dollar patron tier and a lived in register rather than a studio one. The weight cannot be inferred from the style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Convert the printer's press PDF to a working document, export its interchange form, and read the real frame inventory it actually contains.
trajectory.judgement: Frame granularity from a PDF is not under anybody's control. Whether the card's front is four separate frames or one continuous flow decides whether fields are mapped per frame or by position inside a single story, and looking is the only way to find out.
trajectory.produces: A converted template plus a written inventory of its real text and picture frames with their bounds.

trajectory.action: Generate the mapping readout for the converted template, compose the field mapping for title, date, standfirst, URL and the per row picture, run it back through the validator, and prepare the merge template.
trajectory.judgement: The mapping is offset work inside somebody else's document, and the validator's verdict is a statement about the mapping's shape, not about whether it points at the right characters.
trajectory.produces: A prepared merge template and the validator's response.

trajectory.action: Merge the eight records with the per row picture binding, render the press file and the per record proofs, and read the pages.
trajectory.judgement: Page count equal to record count is necessary and not sufficient. Multi record raster output comes back in an order the labels misreport, so identity is confirmed on the page rather than from the response.
trajectory.produces: An eight page press file, per record proofs, and a page by page identity check.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML carrying the end plate and the caption plate at their own canvas sizes, embed every picture as image data, place the wordmark as inline vector inside an explicitly sized top left anchored wrapper, and declare family and weight on every text element.
trajectory.judgement: A picture left as a reference is not a picture, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override is exactly what collapses a mixed size set. The design work is how quiet the plates can be and still carry a sponsor.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at canvas one, and parse the returned per canvas markup for canvas two.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at page one is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document, an inspected first canvas, and a markup audit of the second.

trajectory.action: Write the note: per still what was applied and why it differs from its neighbours, every resize any tool reported, what the voiceover cleanup reconciled and what it did not, the card run's page by page identity, and how to use the recovered mark.
trajectory.judgement: The note is the deliverable that keeps him from re commissioning this next season, so it has to name the things that cannot be fixed as plainly as the things that were.
trajectory.produces: A written handover note.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the vertical recap still has him in it. The resizer returns exactly the requested vertical dimensions and reports success, and the first frame looks correct, because a reframe of a wide shot has to discard most of the width and the tool takes that decision itself. He is framed hard to the right of centre through the desk episodes because his window is on his left, so what the vertical keeps is the window. Nothing in the response, the dimensions or the duration reports it, and the wide recap it came from is entirely correct. It is visible only by watching the vertical through, and which stretches of it are wrong depends on which episodes the cutter chose to draw the recap from, which the agent also only learns by running the cut.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter controls it: the reframe is the last video step by necessity and the tool exposes no framing control, so a competent agent cannot do it right first time without already knowing where he stands in footage it did not shoot. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for the recap again tall for the phone feed and says nothing about where he sits in frame. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is a different route entirely: re cut the wide recap from a different set of source episodes whose framing survives a centred reframe, or accept that some episodes cannot go vertical and rebuild the vertical from the ones that can.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re read the episode content maps for framing rather than content, re cut the wide recap from a different selection of sources, re derive the vertical from that cut, and watch it through before it is called delivered.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A vertical recap delivered at exactly the right dimensions in which the creator is at the edge of frame or absent, published to the feed that carries the sponsor.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the field mapping actually points at the characters it names. The card's front is one continuous flow, and the readout that drives the mapping reports a story that silently omits one of its runs while keeping that run's line break, so the string still reads as well formed and every offset past the omission is short by exactly that run's length. The validator returns a valid verdict with no warnings on the wrong offsets, and preparing the template returns a success message while quietly dropping the mappings that no longer land. Which run is omitted, and therefore which fields survive, is a property of this specific document and is reported nowhere. It is discoverable only by round tripping the prepared template and looking for each expected placeholder in its own story text.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) A careful agent cannot dodge it by ordering or by care, because both signals it has (the validator and the prepare response) affirm the work; the only way through is to distrust a readout that nothing has flagged. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says the printer used this file and asks for the same card with new content. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is to reconstruct the document's true story text from the interchange file itself and recompute every offset against that, which is a different source of truth, not the same call again.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the offsets from the document's own reconstructed story text, re prepare the template, and re export it to confirm every expected field is present before a single record is merged.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Eight patron cards printed and mailed with the standfirst and the channel URL missing from every one of them, after every tool in the chain reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the plate the whole caption look rests on. The caption plate is a soft translucent band the words sit on so they stay readable over any frame, and the natural constructions for that are a blurred backdrop or a layered soft shadow. The importer discards a blur outright, drops a backdrop treatment to its underlying flat fill, and truncates a layered shadow to its first layer, all at a successful response with no warning of any kind. The returned per canvas markup is the only channel that reports which of those happened, and the document's own rendition returns the first artboard only, so the caption canvas can be checked no other way. Whether what survives still holds the words legible over a bright kitchen frame is visible only after the export.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Doing it right first time presumes knowing which of several equally reasonable constructions survives this importer, which no response and no checklist enumerates, and no ordering helps because the normalisation happens at import and import is the last step. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for a caption plate he can change himself, not for a particular construction. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is a different upstream asset or a different construction: bake the softness into the picture before it is embedded, or reduce the plate to the single opaque treatment the importer keeps and re judge legibility against the brightest frame.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re author the plate around whichever construction survives, re export, and audit both canvases from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard, then re check the words against the brightest episode picture.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A caption plate delivered as an editable file in which the words sit on nothing and go unreadable over the bright kitchen frames, on the canvas nobody looked at, with the export having reported success throughout.

deliverables.name: Halden season two episode pictures
deliverables.spec: Eight episode pictures brought to one channel look across kitchen tungsten, window daylight and evening dusk: one white point, one black point, one warmth, one contrast handling, with the flat still reading as a flat rather than as a studio. Every output at or below its source dimensions with the returned tradeoff record captured, and a per picture parameter log including one line on why each differs from its neighbours.

deliverables.name: Season two recap, wide and tall, with cleaned voiceover
deliverables.spec: A short wide season recap for the channel page and a vertical companion for the phone feed, the vertical keeping the creator in frame for its whole length and reaching its dimensions without a single added pixel, delivered with the recap voiceover cleaned and a written statement of what the cleanup reconciled between the two recording sittings and what it could not.

deliverables.name: Recovered HALDEN wordmark
deliverables.spec: The hand painted channel name recovered from a photograph of a limewashed pine board as placeable scalable vector geometry with a transparent ground: a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding along, its counters open and its painted hairline rule intact, delivered as both a single colour mark and a colour accurate variant, and holding at the size it actually reproduces on the card foot as well as on the end plate.

deliverables.name: Patron card run, season two
deliverables.spec: One press ready file of eight pages, one episode per page in the order of the episode list, each page carrying its own episode picture bound per record plus its own title, date and standfirst and the channel URL exactly as supplied, rebuilt from the printer's own flat artwork into a live merge template. Delivered with per record proofs whose identity is confirmed on the page rather than from the response labels.

deliverables.name: End plate and caption plate, as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: One native editable document carrying both plates at their own canvas sizes, with live editable text in one licensed type system, the wordmark as real vector shapes, every picture carried as embedded image data rather than a reference, and the caption plate holding its words legible over a bright frame. Delivered with the self contained source it was authored from, which is the durable half: he edits the document weekly and the source guarantees the design survives regardless.

deliverables.name: Handover note
deliverables.spec: A written note recording per episode picture what was applied and why it differs from its neighbours, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and the actual numeric weight, every resize any tool reported with the file it applied to, the card run's page by page identity check, what the voiceover cleanup did and did not reconcile, and anything he should know about using the recovered mark.

verifiers_auto.text: No delivered file, raster or video, exceeds the pixel dimensions of the source it derives from.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the dimensions of every delivered file and compare each against the source named for it in the manifest.

verifiers_auto.text: No crop, resize or knockout tradeoff record captured in the run carries an upscale entry, and every downscale entry is transcribed in the handover note.
verifiers_auto.how: Diff the tradeoff records captured from every image and video call against the resize table in the note.

verifiers_auto.text: The vertical recap is a true vertical aspect at or below source scale and its duration does not exceed the wide recap it derives from.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the width, height and duration of both recap files.

verifiers_auto.text: The patron card press file has exactly eight pages, one per episode, in the order of the supplied episode list.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the page count of the press file and read each page's title and date against the episode copy.

verifiers_auto.text: Every expected field placeholder is present in the prepared merge template's own story text before merging, including the standfirst and the channel URL.
verifiers_auto.how: Export the prepared template's interchange form and search its story content for each expected field token.

verifiers_auto.text: The recovered wordmark's vector file carries a viewBox attribute and no full canvas opaque background path at index zero.
verifiers_auto.how: Parse the delivered vector file: assert a viewBox is present and assert the first path's geometry does not span the whole canvas.

verifiers_auto.text: The Express export returned two canvases, each keeping its own declared size, with no picture resolved to the importer's placeholder and the wordmark arriving as vector path shapes rather than one picture.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the returned canvas count and per canvas dimensions, then search the returned per canvas markup for placeholder image data and count path shapes in the mark's region.

verifiers_auto.text: Every text element in the exported markup carries a resolved licensed face rather than a fallback default.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the font family attribute on every text node in the returned markup and check it against the families the kit call returned.

verifiers_human.text: Laid out in a row the way a channel page lays them, the eight episode pictures read as one channel rather than eight good frames from three different rooms.
verifiers_human.how: Place the eight side by side at listing scale and judge white point, black point, warmth and contrast as a set.

verifiers_human.text: The flat still reads as a flat. It has not been graded into a studio.
verifiers_human.how: View the kitchen and desk pictures at full size and judge whether the domestic register survived the correction.

verifiers_human.text: The creator stays in frame for the whole of the vertical recap, not only at its opening.
verifiers_human.how: Watch the vertical through end to end rather than sampling its first seconds.

verifiers_human.text: The recap audio reads as one person in one room, with no point where the voice changes distance.
verifiers_human.how: Listen to the cleaned voiceover end to end, paying attention to the sitting join.

verifiers_human.text: The wordmark still reads as the painted board at the size it reproduces on the card foot and on the end plate, with its counters open.
verifiers_human.how: View the mark at its actual reproduction size on each destination, not at full canvas.

verifiers_human.text: The caption plate holds its words legible over the brightest episode picture.
verifiers_human.how: Open the exported document and place the plate over the brightest frame in Express.

verifiers_human.text: The work reads as an ordinary week filmed well at a 6 dollar patron tier, not as a studio channel and not as a phone edit.
verifiers_human.how: Judge grade, type scale, plate weight and card density against the stated band and audience.

verifiers_human.text: The note tells the creator something he did not already know, including anything that could not be delivered.
verifiers_human.how: Read the note against the run and check that every limitation is named as plainly as every fix.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are raster work, which are moving, and which need an authored fixed canvas he can edit, given that only one surface here composes free form layout.
Whether the eight episodes are one channel. The creator believes they nearly are; the row is the only place that can be settled.
How far to push the kitchen tungsten frames toward the target before the room stops looking like his kitchen, versus naming one as unmatchable.
Which episodes the recap is drawn from, chosen from summaries of cuts the agent did not make, and judged on framing as well as on content.
Whether a vertical is producible from a given source at all, or whether that source has to be swapped rather than reframed.
Whether the two voiceover sittings can be reconciled, and how to say so in the note when they cannot.

Selection wording on the painted board: naming the board takes the plank, naming the paint's own visual properties takes the lettering, and background removal on enclosed counters is the wrong instrument entirely.
Which mark variant carries the card foot, judged at reproduction size on the actual stock rather than at full canvas.
Whether the converted card is mapped per frame or by position inside one story, which the document decides and not the agent.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a lived in register rather than a studio one, plus the real numeric weight per family.
How quiet the plates can be and still carry a sponsor. At this band restraint is the design, and a dense branded plate is a correct looking wrong answer.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of a young man in a kitchen. IDENTITY: these are this creator's own eight locked episodes, his own flat, his own face and his own hand painted board, and the wordmark has to be RECOVERED off that board rather than reinvented, because a regenerated wordmark is a different channel's logo and a regenerated kitchen is not his. SPEC: the patron card is a press file of exactly eight pages in the episode list's order with each record's own picture bound to it and a URL that must read character for character, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for, and the vertical recap has a hard no added pixels requirement. EDITABILITY: the two plates are defined by being editable, since the episode number moves every week and he explicitly will not pay for that. And the whole middle of this engagement is verification against material reality that only running produces: is he still in the vertical frame, did the mapping point at the right characters, did the caption plate's softness survive the import.
doability_proof: Every link is verified in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no invented one. VIDEO AND AUDIO: only the four permitted Premiere operations appear, media_summarize to read cuts the agent did not make, video_create_quick_cut which only ever shortens and is never asked to trim to a timestamp, video_resize which is never asked to enlarge, and media_enhance_speech. No on screen text burn in, no lower third compositing, no motion graphics, no format conversion and no per artboard export appear anywhere, which is exactly why the real post's overlay ask was re carved into an authored editable plate set. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, auto_tone, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and detection_confidence, fill_area and vectorize are all verified headless across 27 live calls. The crop tool DOES enlarge up to a two times cap and reports it only inside its returned tradeoffs, which is why the no enlargement bar is checked against that record rather than asserted. The mark work rests on documented findings: the substrate versus ink prompt asymmetry is verified, remove_background cannot punch enclosed counters and collapses on disjoint lettering, and vectorize emits no viewBox and an opaque full canvas path at index zero, so the hygiene the acceptance bar scores is hygiene no tool performs. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt with its validator mode, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout with a per row image column bound through additionalImageFiles, and document_render_layout are verified end to end; page count equal to row count is verified for PDF output. The mapping checkpoint rests on the verified lossy textContent finding, where a dropped run left every later offset short, the validator still returned valid, prepare still reported success, and only 3 of 5 mappings landed. Multi record raster order is documented as misreported, which is why identity is checked on the page. No variable QR, no bleed claim and no named press preset appear. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, inline vector becomes native editable shapes, images must be embedded because every external reference resolved to a placeholder, blur is dropped and layered shadow truncated to layer one at HTTP success, and the rendition preview is documented as first artboard only, which is why verification is split between the rendition and the returned markup. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end including a browser proving licensed faces load, and the non standard numeric weight per family is why font_styles is mandatory. AVOIDED: no text to image, no generative fill, no object removal, no upscaling, no OCR, no fill_text, no animate_design, no vector render or vector merge, and no batch above twenty files.

engagement_title: Anvil and Oak Strength movement library: cut six demo takes into one library, bring the poster frames to a single studio white, recover the wordmark and the certification seal off a photographed patch, and rebuild the printer's exercise card into a live six record run
vertical: Health, Wellness and Fitness. Subscription strength training app with a coached movement library, sold direct at 49 dollars a month to home gym subscribers, filmed in a converted barn gym outside Burlington, Vermont
real_brief_anchor: Adapted from the Upwork post quoted in the ledger's grounding_note, where a personal training business with a large exercise library wanted a repeatable production pipeline turning raw demo footage into short educational reference clips with reusable branding, muscle group callouts, and a clip naming and organisation convention. Two parts of that literal ask are on the connector's unavailable list and are therefore re carved rather than faked: open timeline editing to timestamps and frame by frame overlay or caption compositing do not exist here, so the callouts become a printed and authored reference card set that lives beside each clip rather than burned into it, which is what a coached library actually ships to subscribers anyway. Everything else in the post is real work and fully doable: shortening long demo takes into per movement highlights, producing the vertical companions the app's short feed needs, bringing a set of poster frames shot across two sessions to one studio white, recovering the studio's own mark and certification seal from the only surviving physical object, and turning the printer's existing exercise card into a live six record run so the library extends itself later. The business is laundered to a fully invented studio, Anvil and Oak Strength, run by fictional coaches Ruth Callaway and Dean Marchetti. No real trainer, gym, certifying body or app is referenced, and the certification seal is a coined in house mark rather than any real credential.
client_one_liner: Six movements are filmed, the takes are far too long, the poster frames were shot on two different days and do not match, and our logo only exists on a stitched patch we can photograph.
client_brief:
Anvil and Oak Strength, movement library build

We are two coaches with a subscription app. Subscribers pay monthly and the thing they use most is the movement library, which is a short reference clip per exercise with a card beside it. We are rebuilding the first six core movements and then we will add six more every quarter, so whatever you set up has to be something we can run again.

Here is what we have. Each movement was filmed as one long demo take, sometimes two or three takes, and they are far too long to put in front of anybody. There is a lot of setting up the bar at the front, and there is a rep in some of them that did not go well. We need a short landscape clip per movement that shows the movement being done properly, and a tall version of each for the short feed.

Our photographer came in and shot stills while we filmed. Those are the poster frames for each movement and they have to look like one studio. They do not right now. She was in twice and the light was not the same both times, and I think a bulb had been changed.

Dean recorded the coaching cues for each movement in one sitting. It is usable but the barn is a barn.

The cards. We had six exercise cards printed last year and the printer still has our file, which we have. We need six new cards, one per movement, each with its own poster frame, its own name, its own cue list and its own muscle group line. The cue lists are not all the same length.

Our mark and our certification seal only exist stitched onto a patch on our gym bags. We need both back as artwork, because they go on every card and on the library sheet.

And we need a library reference sheet we can update ourselves as movements get added.

We charge forty nine a month. It should look like a real coach's studio, not a gym chain and not a physiotherapy clinic.
price_band_and_audience: Coached strength subscription at 49 dollars a month, subscriber 30 to 52, home gym or garage gym, already lifting and buying instruction rather than motivation. The band is load bearing in both directions. Drop toward a 9 dollar mass fitness app and the correct treatment is high saturation, hard contrast, big shouty type, bodies as motivation imagery, cards that are mostly a photograph; ship that here and the coaching claim collapses, because the subscriber is paying for someone who knows what a hip hinge is and that person does not shout. Push up toward a clinical or rehabilitation register and it becomes cold, white, diagrammatic and medical, which reads as physiotherapy, is a different product, and is exactly the thing this studio's whole positioning is not. The correct register is a working craftsman's studio: one honest studio white, real bodies doing real work, quiet confident type, cue lists that read as instruction rather than as marketing. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,800 to 3,800 dollars fixed with a per quarter extension attached.

brand_identity.sector: Subscription strength training app with a coached movement library, sold direct to home gym subscribers.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2020, outside Burlington, Vermont, a two coach studio filmed in a converted barn gym.
brand_identity.about: Anvil and Oak Strength is a coached strength subscription run by two coaches, Ruth Callaway and Dean Marchetti, out of a converted barn gym outside Burlington. Subscribers pay monthly for a movement library: a short reference clip per exercise with a card beside it, rebuilt six movements at a time and extended every quarter. The promise is competence rather than motivation, someone who knows what a hip hinge is, teaching it plainly.
brand_identity.audience: Subscribers aged 30 to 52 with a home or garage gym, already lifting and paying for instruction rather than motivation. They can tell a coach from a cheerleader and buy the difference.
brand_identity.price_positioning: 49 dollars a month, coached strength, extended a quarter at a time. Positioned as a working coach's studio: clearly above a 9 dollar mass fitness app and deliberately clear of a clinical or rehabilitation register.
brand_identity.typography: Display: a sturdy, slightly condensed slab or grotesque with real weight and confidence. Text: a plain, legible humanist sans. The cue list is the hardest role, instruction read while someone is under a bar, so it favours clarity over character. No gym chain italics and no clinical thin weights.
brand_identity.voice: Direct, instructional and calm. Speaks like a coach giving a cue, not a brand selling one. Example line: 'Brace, hinge, drive through the floor. That is the whole lift.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The wordmark and the in house certification seal survive only as stitching on a canvas gym bag patch, held now as one handheld photograph. Both have to be recovered from that photograph as artwork before they can go on the cards and the library sheet. The seal is a compound ring lockup, type set around a central anvil glyph inside a ruled ring. There is no vector file, no colour spec and no prior guideline.
brand_identity.values: Competence and honesty: real bodies doing real work, taught by people who actually lift.

assets_supplied.name: anvil_oak_demo_takes/ (14 files across 6 movements)
assets_supplied.kind: Long single camera demo takes, two or three per movement, filmed in one session in the barn gym.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Every movement, all the takes. They are far too long and there is a lot of setting up at the front."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The takes carry their most visible motion in the setup and in the reset after a failed rep rather than in the working set, so a shortening pass driven by what is happening on screen returns a plausible, well paced clip of the wrong part of the take at exactly the requested length. Separately two of the fourteen were filmed against the mirrored end wall, so the plate reads reversed and the coach appears to be loading the bar with the wrong hand, and one movement's only usable take is a 1080p phone recording rather than the camera master.

assets_supplied.name: anvil_oak_poster_stills/ (6 frames plus alternates)
assets_supplied.kind: Studio stills shot by a photographer alongside the filming, across two separate visits a fortnight apart.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The poster frames. She was in twice and the light was not the same both times."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: A ceiling bank was replaced between the two visits, so the second session's frames carry a different illuminant that one identical correction applied across the set cannot resolve, and the difference is small enough per frame to look acceptable alone. In two frames the chrome of the loaded bar sits at almost the luminance of the barn's whitewashed wall, so a subject led cut bites the bar sleeve while returning a clean looking edge everywhere else.

assets_supplied.name: anvil_oak_cues.wav
assets_supplied.kind: Dean's spoken coaching cues for all six movements, recorded in one sitting in the gym.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The cues, one sitting, all six. It is usable but the barn is a barn."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The room's reverb sits on the sibilants rather than as broadband noise, so cleanup lifts intelligibility while leaving the tail of each cue ringing, and the ringing is audible only when a cue is heard immediately before the next one rather than in isolation.

assets_supplied.name: anvil_oak_exercise_card_2025.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The press PDF the printer used for last year's exercise card set: a portrait card with a picture box, a movement name, a muscle group line, and a fixed cue list block down the lower two thirds.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The file the printer worked from. Same card, six new movements."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The cue list block is a fixed frame that does not spill. Records whose cue list runs longer than last year's simply stop rendering at the frame's edge, mid line and without a mark, while the merge reports success and the page count still matches the record count.

assets_supplied.name: anvil_oak_patch.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of a stitched cloth patch on a canvas gym bag, carrying the studio wordmark in one thread colour and, beside it, a circular certification seal with type set around a central anvil glyph inside a ruled ring.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our mark and the seal. This patch is the only place either of them still exists."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The seal is a compound ring lockup, and a single prompt for it returns the type ring while silently dropping the inner rule and the central glyph at an entirely plausible looking result, while background removal on the ring hands back a solid opaque disc because an enclosed interior cannot be punched. The thread also raises a visible nap on the wordmark's strokes, which reads as texture at full frame and as broken edges once traced.

assets_supplied.name: anvil_oak_library.csv
assets_supplied.kind: The six movements with their names, muscle group lines, cue lists as approved by both coaches, and the clip naming convention the app expects.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The six movements and their cues. The naming convention is what our app reads."

acceptance_bar: Each of the six landscape highlights shows the movement actually being performed correctly from setup through the working set, not the bar being loaded and not a failed rep. A clip of the right length showing the wrong part of the take is not delivered.
No clip is delivered reversed. A movement in which the coach appears to work the wrong side fails outright, because subscribers copy what they see.
No delivered file, raster or video, exceeds the pixel dimensions of the source it came from, and no crop, resize or knockout tradeoff record in the run carries an upscale entry.

The six poster frames read as one studio when laid side by side: one white point, one black point, one warmth, with the whitewashed wall reading as the same wall in all six. A frame that cannot be brought to the set is named rather than shipped at eighty percent.
Where a poster frame carries a cut subject, the cut holds along the loaded bar as well as along the body.
The card set is one press ready file of six pages, one movement per page in the library order, each carrying its own poster frame, name, muscle group line and complete cue list.
Every cue list is complete on the page. A card whose cue list stops mid line at the edge of its block fails even though the page count is right.

The wordmark and the seal are placeable artwork rather than pictures of artwork: transparent, scalable with a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath, and both still readable at the size they actually reproduce on the card and on the library sheet against its deep ground, with the seal's inner rule and central glyph present and its counters open.

The library sheet arrives as one working file the coaches can extend themselves, canvases keeping their own sizes, with the words as text they can retype and the marks as live vector shapes, delivered alongside the self contained source it was built from.
The cleaned cue audio reads as one coach speaking in a good room, heard as a continuous run of cues and not only cue by cue.
One type system across the cards and the library sheet, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the actual weight used.
Every delivered clip and frame is named to the convention the app reads, and the note states per movement which take was used and why.

The summariser is how the agent reads takes it did not film, the shortening cutter is the only instrument available and it chooses its own moments inside whatever it is handed, the resizer produces the vertical without ever adding a pixel, and speech cleanup has to be judged across a run of cues rather than on one.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface, given that the library has to extend itself every quarter.
trajectory.judgement: The cards are a genuine one record per page run and belong on the merge surface precisely because the next six movements are rows; the library sheet has to be a free form canvas the coaches edit. The brief pins both, so there is nothing here to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role and against the app's naming convention.
trajectory.judgement: The naming convention is a deliverable requirement, not housekeeping, so it is applied at ingest rather than retrofitted at the end.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by movement and role.

trajectory.action: Summarise all fourteen takes to read what is actually in each one, since the agent did not film them and cannot scrub them.
trajectory.judgement: Fourteen long takes made by somebody else are opaque, and the client's own account of them (setup at the front, a bad rep in some) is a rough memory rather than a map. Which take per movement is the working one is the first real decision in the job.
trajectory.produces: A per take content map and a first choice of source take per movement.

trajectory.action: Cut each movement's landscape highlight from its chosen take with the shortening cutter, then watch each returned clip.
trajectory.judgement: The cutter only shortens and it selects its own moments inside what it is handed, so the only lever is which take it is handed and how long the result is asked to be. The response reports a duration, not a subject.
trajectory.produces: Six landscape highlights with the source take recorded for each.

trajectory.action: Produce the vertical companion for each movement from the landscape highlight, reading the returned dimensions against the source.
trajectory.judgement: The resizer never adds pixels, so a source that is not a camera master cannot reach the short feed's spec and that has to be found here rather than at delivery.
trajectory.produces: Six vertical companions with their returned dimensions recorded, and a note of any movement that could not reach spec.

trajectory.action: Clean the coaching cue recording, then listen to it as a continuous run of cues rather than cue by cue.
trajectory.judgement: A barn's reverb is not broadband noise and cleanup treats it as though it were. Each cue heard alone sounds fine; the question is what happens where one cue ends and the next begins.
trajectory.produces: A cleaned cue track with a written note on what the cleanup resolved and what it did not.

trajectory.action: Preview the six poster frames and their alternates, triaging which visit each belongs to by its own light rather than by its filename, and reading true dimensions against the card's picture box.
trajectory.judgement: The client says the light was not the same both times and thinks a bulb was changed. The frames are the only thing that can settle which is which, and the difference is small enough per frame to be invisible unless they are compared.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note covering illuminant, tilt, subject contrast against the wall, and true dimensions against every destination.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level, before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop, and a barn floor is rarely the horizon the camera thought it was.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Fix one studio white from the frame that best represents the room and bring each of the six toward it with its own call, recording the parameters applied.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a set, and a set shot under two different ceiling banks cannot be reached by one identical parameter set. The whitewashed wall is the reference surface because it is the thing that appears in all six.
trajectory.produces: Six graded poster frames at source scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Cut the poster frames where the card design needs the subject clear of its ground, selecting by the material's own visual properties, and inspect each cut edge along the bar as well as along the body.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the whole gate and a subject led cut has no contrast to work with where chrome meets whitewash. A clean edge on the body is not evidence about the bar.
trajectory.produces: Cut poster frames with their edges inspected, and a record of which needed a different route.

trajectory.action: Recover the wordmark and the seal off the patch: thread level selections naming each mark's own visual properties, correct polarity, bounds crops driven by the selections' own returned boxes, traces, then viewBoxes injected and the opaque full canvas ground paths removed.
trajectory.judgement: Four decisions no tool makes: how to word each selection so it takes thread and not canvas, whether the compound ring can be taken in one selection or has to be built from its parts, which polarity to trace, and whether the nap the stitching raises is texture worth keeping or noise to be resolved before tracing.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent wordmark and seal, plus colour accurate variants.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the plate rack and chalk texture band, filter to photography, exclude generative candidates, license and download at full resolution, and grade it into the studio white.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose existing light can be brought to the studio target rather than the strongest thumbnail. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP clean, camera scale frame graded into the set.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's, judged against a 49 dollar coached band: a working studio rather than a gym chain or a clinic. The cue list is the hardest role because it is read under load, and the weight cannot be inferred from a style name.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Convert the printer's press PDF to a working document, export its interchange form, and read the real frame inventory and the true bounds of the cue list block.
trajectory.judgement: Frame granularity from a PDF is not under anybody's control, and the bounds of the block that has to carry six different cue lists are a fact about the document rather than a design choice.
trajectory.produces: A converted template plus a written inventory of its real text and picture frames with their bounds.

trajectory.action: Generate the mapping readout, compose the field mapping for name, muscle group line, cue list and the per row poster frame against the document's own story text, validate it, and prepare the merge template.
trajectory.judgement: Offsets are computed against the document's true story rather than against a convenient summary of it, and the validator's verdict is a statement about shape, not about whether the fields land.
trajectory.produces: A prepared merge template verified to carry every expected field.

trajectory.action: Merge the six records with the per row poster frame binding, render the press file and the per record proofs, and read every page.
trajectory.judgement: Page count equal to record count is necessary and not sufficient, and multi record raster output returns in an order whose labels misreport it, so identity and completeness are confirmed on the page.
trajectory.produces: A six page press file, per record proofs, and a page by page identity and completeness check.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML carrying the library sheet at its canvas sizes, embed every frame as image data, place the wordmark and the seal as inline vector inside explicitly sized top left anchored wrappers at the size they will actually reproduce on the deep ground, and declare family and weight on every text element.
trajectory.judgement: A frame left as a reference is not a frame, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override collapses a mixed size set. The design work is how the six movements read as one library rather than six posters.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at canvas one, and parse the returned per canvas markup for the rest.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition only ever shows the first artboard.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document, an inspected first canvas, and a markup audit of the others.

trajectory.action: Create the selects board, add the graded frames and the licensed frame within the per call placement cap, re sending only the entries the response names as failed, then write the handover note and the naming manifest.
trajectory.judgement: A partial success response is partial success, and vector is not boardable so the marks belong in the note. The note has to be specific enough that the next quarter's six movements are a repeat rather than a rediscovery.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, plus the written handover and the naming manifest.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether each highlight actually shows the movement being performed. The shortening pass selects its own moments from inside the take according to what is happening on screen, and in these takes the most visible activity is the bar being loaded at the front and the reset after a rep that did not go well, not the smooth working set. What comes back is a well paced clip of exactly the requested length with a plausible beginning and end, and the response reports only a duration. Which of the fourteen takes this happens to is a property of where each take's activity sits, which is not visible in the take's length, its filename or its summary, and can be established only by cutting it and watching the result.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter controls it: the tool exposes no way to say which part of the take matters, so a competent agent cannot get it right first time except by luck, and the take it chose was chosen from a summary of content rather than of pacing. (b) Nothing states it: the client says only that there is a lot of setting up at the front and a bad rep in some of them, which is a description of the raw material, not of what a cutter will select from it. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is a different source, not the same call again: hand the cutter a different take of the same movement whose activity sits on the working set, or ask for a different target length so the selection window falls elsewhere, and re judge each result by watching it.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re read the content maps for where activity sits rather than for what is present, re cut the affected movements from different takes or at a different target length, and watch every returned clip through before any of them is named to the convention.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A movement library in which subscribers are shown a coach loading a bar or resetting after a failed rep as the reference for how the exercise is performed, on a product whose entire claim is coaching competence.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether every cue list is actually on its card. The cue block inherited from the printer's artwork is a fixed frame, and a fixed frame does not spill: a record whose cue list runs longer than the one the frame was drawn for simply stops rendering at the frame edge, mid line and without any mark that anything is missing. The merge reports success, the page count still equals the record count, and each page looks like a properly composed card. Which of the six overflow depends on the frame's true bounds against the applied type size and the actual cue text, and none of those three are knowable together until the pages exist.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Doing it right first time would require knowing the rendered depth of six different cue lists inside a frame whose bounds came from somebody else's document, which nothing reports; and no ordering helps, because the overflow only exists once the type system and the real copy meet the inherited frame. (b) Nothing states it. The client says only that the cue lists are not all the same length, which is a fact about the copy, not a disclosure that a frame silently truncates. The acceptance line about complete cue lists is the client's own requirement, not a warning. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is a design decision with consequences: change the type role's size or leading for the whole set so the longest record fits, which changes every card, or re cut the copy with the coaches, or re map the cue list into a different frame if the document has one.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Measure the longest record against the block by rendering it, re decide the cue role's size and leading for the entire set rather than for one card, re prepare and re merge, then read every page's cue list to its last line.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Six printed exercise cards where two of them stop mid cue, shipped to subscribers as the written reference for movements performed under load.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered seal survives at the size it is actually used. The trace is judged on screen at full canvas, where the ring's type, its inner rule and the anvil glyph all read cleanly. On the library sheet the seal sits small against the studio's deep ground, and at that reproduction size the thread nap the stitching raised becomes closed counters and a rule that merges into the type above it, so the mark reads as a dark blot rather than as a seal. Nothing in the trace's output, the export response or the first artboard reports it: the file is correct, its paths are all present, and at canvas size it is right. It is visible only by looking at the mark at its true reproduction size on the true ground.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the reproduction size is a property of the sheet's composition and the composition is downstream of the recovery; and getting it right first time would mean knowing how a specific stitched mark's stroke weight behaves at a size that has not been chosen yet. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that the marks go on the cards and the sheet, and the acceptance line about readability at reproduction size is the client's standing requirement, not a hint that this trace closes. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is a different upstream asset: re trace from a differently prepared raster where the nap has been resolved before tracing, or build the ring lockup from separate per element selections so the rule and the glyph carry their own weight, or reconsider the seal's size and its ground on the sheet, each of which is a different decision.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re prepare the patch raster to resolve the nap, re select the seal's elements separately rather than as one compound, re trace, re inject the viewBox and strip the ground path, then re place at reproduction size on the deep ground and look again before the sheet is called finished.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A library sheet and a card set carrying a certification seal that reads as a dark blot at every size a subscriber will ever see it, on the one element in the identity whose whole job is to signal credential.
