decision_gates: Which deliverables go to the merge surface and which to authored canvases, given six cards already hanging that cannot change and a folio the family will keep editing.
What is damage to correct and what is the age of the object to preserve, on prints where grain, paper texture and a studio retoucher's pencil work are all present.
Whether an automatic level actually moved a given picture, and how much of an album mount or a deckled border is evidence worth keeping when it did not.
Which way each faded colour print's residual cast runs, when both read identically yellowed as supplied and no measurement exists anywhere.
How far a fade recovery can be taken before the print stops looking like a print of its decade, at a band where anything that reads as enhanced fails.
One archival target for four decades and four papers, and which photograph, if any, cannot be brought to it.
The catalogue: one photograph entered twice, one date contradicted by the back of the print, one photo reference pointing at a renamed file. What is the agent's call and what is the family's.
Whether to trust the mapping tool's readout of the framer's text or to reconstruct the story independently from the document.
Whether per-photograph identity is established by position in a returned list or by opening the file.
What to do with a caption that will not fit the framer's measure, when six cards from 2019 fix the design and the family asked for a match.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a museum label voice rather than a memory book voice.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the scans into a frontier image model and it returns a beautiful old photograph of a woman who is not Ada Hollis. IDENTITY is the entire commission: a generative restore invents the eyes, the hairline, the teeth and the hand, and this family has already told us in writing what happened the last time somebody improved their grandmother. Every corrected pixel must derive from the pixels in the scan. SPEC: the family needs one A6 caption card per catalogued photograph matching six already hanging, complete at trim, with per-photograph files each containing the photograph they claim, and proofs at true print resolution. EDITABILITY: the folio is defined by being editable, because the aunt will find three more names. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did this level actually move the picture, which way does this cast run once the fade is lifted, does this caption reach the edge of the card.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments global and masked, monochromatic_tint, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, crop_to_bounds and crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs, detection_confidence and upscale_factor are all verified headless. The two imaging checkpoints rest on documented facts rather than invention: there is NO measurement anywhere in the family (no eyedropper, no histogram, no ruler, and metadata.bbox is a mask extent, not a tonal or angular reading), and image_auto_straighten takes no reference and reports no angle, so what it locked onto and whether it moved anything can only be established by comparing the returned file against the input. crop_and_resize is documented as interpolating up to a hard 2x cap and reporting it only in the tradeoffs array, which is what makes the no enlargement bar checkable rather than asserted. MERGE SPINE: building a merge template from a bare press PDF end to end headlessly is verified, one record per page is confirmed for the PDF branch, per-record files are confirmed in correct order by two routes, true 300 DPI at trim is confirmed through the render tool, the merge's own resolution parameter is documented as silently ignored (hence rendering from the merged document), frame granularity and frame bounds from a PDF are documented as not under your control, and the mapping readout's text content is documented as lossy in a way the validator blesses. The caption checkpoint needs no new capability: the converted document carries the bounds the framer drew, nothing in the chain reports overset, and text past a fixed measure is simply absent from the render while the page count stays correct. Image binding through an at prefixed column plus an image map is verified, with the single-record loop as the identity guaranteed fallback. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export, true mm print canvases at exactly 96 dpi, real tables and a genuine editable document are verified; the rendition shows PAGE 1 ONLY so verification splits between the rendition and the returned markup; payload routed by uploaded URL because inlined photographs pass 70KB immediately. FONTS, STOCK and BOARDS follow the verified chains, with short queries, orientation never passed, and the twelve per call board cap with 201 meaning partial. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no generative fill or AI restore, no healing or cloning, no sharpening, no upscaling, no OCR, no compositing, no bleed or press preset gate, no variable QR, no fill_text, no batch above 20.

engagement_title: Gable & Grove spring season kit: build an honest before and after library from five finished jobs, recover the lost mark as artwork that holds on a deep green yard sign, rebuild the retired printer's project cards, and hand back the quote pack and the social set
vertical: Home and property services: premium exterior renovation and garden build, five person firm (Litchfield Hills, Connecticut)
real_brief_anchor: Anchor: the Upwork home services branding brief in the ledger's grounding_note, from a new home services company that had a logo mark and wanted it cleaned up and rolled out consistently across trucks, uniforms, yard signs, social and print, laundered here to the fictional Gable & Grove Home Services (no real company, person or trademark appears anywhere; the brand, the crew, the jobs and all copy are invented for this benchmark). The killed spec was fake on two counts: every deliverable was a one click operation, and it asked for a trace of a photograph of printed artwork as though that were a clean input. The fuller commission this firm genuinely has is the season kit, because a before and after library is worthless without the collateral it feeds, the project card run is a real record per page job rebuildable from the press file the retired printer left, and the mark has to survive from a shirt to a yard sign or it is not artwork, it is a picture of a logo.
client_one_liner: Everything we sell we sell twice, on the site and on somebody's kitchen table, and right now we are selling it with phone snaps, a logo file the sign writer emailed us once, and project cards from a printer who has retired.
client_brief:
Gable & Grove Home Services, spring season kit

We do full exterior renovations and garden builds in the Litchfield Hills, mostly between forty five and a hundred and twenty thousand dollars a project. Everything we sell, we sell twice: once on the website, and once out of a quote pack on somebody's kitchen table.

We have five finished jobs from last season and photographs of all of them, before and after, some off my phone and some off our estimator's camera. They are a mess. The befores need to stay honest, because that is the entire point of a before, and the afters need to look like what we actually deliver. We are not an HGTV company. If the afters look like a supermarket flyer, the people we sell to will price us at eight thousand dollars and call somebody else.

We need those pairs for the site and for the quote pack, and we need the pergola from the Ridge Road job pulled out cleanly so we can put it on things. It is the best thing we have ever built.

Our mark is a problem. The sign writer who drew it is gone and all we have is a picture file he emailed once, plus a photograph of our own truck door. We need it back as proper artwork we can hand to anybody: the sign shop, the shirt printer, whoever. It has to work everywhere from a shirt to a yard sign, and our yard signs are the deep green.

We also need the project cards. Our old printer ran one per finished job for the quote packs and the showroom board. He has retired, we have the file he sent to press, and we now have more jobs than cards.

Then the quote pack itself, the before and after module for the site, and the social sizes. All of it editable by us, because prices change and I am not paying twice.

Finally, a note on what you did, and why the befores are treated differently from the afters.
price_band_and_audience: A firm charging 45,000 to 120,000 dollars a project, selling to households aged 45 to 65 with old houses and long time horizons, at a kitchen table against two other bids. The band is load-bearing and it points at restraint: at this price the afters read cool, calm and material, with real neutral stone, deep honest blacks, one photograph doing the work, generous white space in the quote pack and a mark that behaves like a maker's stamp rather than a sales badge. The same brief for an 8,000 dollar handyman outfit would correctly be brighter, warmer, more saturated, busier, with four photographs a page, a starburst price and a phone number in the biggest type on the sheet, and shipping that here loses the job on sight because it tells the buyer this firm competes on price. Pushed the other way into a black ground with gold rules it reads as a developer, which this buyer distrusts more than a flyer. A dishonestly improved before fails at any band, because it destroys the only proof the firm has. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,200 to 3,000 dollars fixed.

Everything is sold twice, once on the website and once out of a quote pack on somebody's kitchen table, so the work has to look like exactly what the firm delivers and no more. The proof is the before and after, and the before has to stay honest.
brand_identity.audience: Households aged 45 to 65 with old houses and long time horizons, choosing between two or three bids and buying on trust rather than on price.
brand_identity.price_positioning: 45,000 to 120,000 dollars a project. brand_identity.voice: Plain and confident, the voice of a builder who does not oversell. Example line the brand would write: "Full exterior renovation, Ridge Road. Limestone pergola, dry stone terrace, planting."

The project cards survive only as the retired printer's press PDF. Yard signs print in the deep Grove Green.

acceptance_bar: The afters read as ONE firm's finish across five jobs shot in different light: one white point on the stone, one black point, one degree of correction, one crop logic. A job that cannot be brought to the set is named, not shipped at eighty percent.

The befores stay honest. Any correction applied to a before is legibility only, is disclosed, and does not flatter the site. A before that has been quietly improved fails the whole library regardless of how good the after looks.
Every delivered pair is genuinely a pair: the same site, comparable framing, and no visible divergence in the colour of the same material across the two frames.

No delivered file exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions and no crop's tradeoff record carries an upscale entry. If a pair cannot reach the library size at its own resolution, we are told the size it CAN reach rather than being handed interpolated pixels.
The isolated pergola is clean at the edge where the stone meets the sky, judged on a contrasting ground rather than on a checkerboard preview.

The mark is delivered as artwork, not a picture of artwork: placeable, scalable, transparent where it should be transparent, and intact at real reproduction size on the firm's own deep green, including its counter and its hairline rule.
Both mark sources are handled on their own merits and the reasoning is stated. A route that works on one and produces a substrate shaped blob on the other is not a route.

Exactly one project card per publishable job, no duplicate card and no card for a job we are not allowed to show. If the number shipped is not the number the export implies, the note says which row was withheld and why.
Every card's photograph is the job named on the card, and the finished feature is still in the photograph after the card's own frame has had its way with it.
Each per-project file contains the job its filename claims, established by opening it rather than by the order the files came back in.
The proofs are rendered at true print resolution at card trim rather than at screen scale.

The quote pack, the before and after module, the social set and the yard sign come back as a native editable document we can change prices in, with every photograph actually visible, the scope block as a real table, and every text element carrying its licensed face at that family's own weight.
Nothing in the kit reads as a supermarket flyer or as developer marketing at our band.

A written note: what was applied to each frame, why the befores differ from the afters, how each mark source was handled, every job row questioned and its resolution, and every resize any tool reported.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle the split: project cards to the merge surface, quote pack, module, social set and yard sign to authored canvases, photography and the mark to imaging.
trajectory.judgement: The card is record per page against a layout the showroom board already locks in; the quote pack is free form and must stay editable, which the merge surface structurally cannot give.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier.

trajectory.action: Upload the fourteen job frames, both mark sources, the press PDF, the estimating export and the owner's notes, holding each returned presigned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A manifest keyed by job, by role and by state, because the same frame will exist in four states before the end.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by job and role.

trajectory.action: Preview all fourteen and pair each before with its after, noting light, apparent capture device, framing, what material dominates each pair and how much edge each frame has to spare.
trajectory.judgement: A pair is a claim about one site, so what the two frames share and where they diverge is the thing being assessed, not how good either looks alone.
trajectory.produces: A per pair triage note: job, light, framing, dominant material and edge margin.

trajectory.action: Correct the befores only as far as honesty allows, deciding and recording what honest means at this band.
trajectory.judgement: The before is the firm's only proof, so the line between making a phone snap legible and quietly improving the site is the single most consequential craft decision in the engagement and the client has already named the failure.
trajectory.produces: Legibility corrected befores with a per frame parameter log and a stated standard.

trajectory.action: Fix one finish target and bring every after toward it with its own call, recording the parameters applied.
trajectory.judgement: Five jobs shot across a season in different light have to arrive at one white point and one black point, which means five different routes to one destination rather than one batched move, and the destination is set by a band that punishes saturation.
trajectory.produces: Five graded afters at source scale with a per job parameter log.

trajectory.action: Derive the web three by two and square crops of every pair and lay each finished pair side by side at one size, reading confidence and tradeoffs on every crop.
trajectory.judgement: One crop logic across five jobs, not ten good crops, and the tradeoffs array is the only signal that a crop clipped or that an output was interpolated toward the two times cap. A pair is judged as a pair at the only moment that comparison exists.
trajectory.produces: Paired crops with their tradeoff records and a pair by pair judgement.

trajectory.action: Isolate the Ridge Road pergola for the hero and inspect the result on a contrasting ground rather than on a transparency preview.
trajectory.judgement: Which isolation instrument suits this subject is a judgement about the boundary, and the tool exposes no threshold, no matte control and no confidence, so what its detector did on this frame can only be seen by looking at the returned edge against something it contrasts with.
trajectory.produces: An isolated pergola on a plain ground plus a transparent version, inspected on a real ground.

trajectory.action: Triage the two mark sources and take each down its own route, naming the ink and its own visual properties rather than the surface it sits on.
trajectory.judgement: The emailed plate and the painted door look like the same job and are not: naming the substrate pulls a selection to the substrate, and a subject knockout on disjoint lettering collapses to a few letters while reporting success.
trajectory.produces: A clean positive plate of the mark from whichever source survives, with the reasoning for both routes recorded.

trajectory.action: Trace the prepared plate, then do the vector hygiene by hand: inject a viewBox, strip the full canvas background rectangle, and check the counter and the hairline rule.
trajectory.judgement: The trace takes no options at all, so every lever is in the raster preparation that precedes it, and an untouched trace is neither scalable nor transparent no matter how clean it looks.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent mark plus the raster prep that produced it.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the one honest non job still the quote pack needs, filter to photography, exclude generative tech results, license and download at full resolution.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose light and whose blacks can live beside five graded jobs, not the moodiest thumbnail, and declare it as stock. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP clean, camera scale still, graded toward the finish target.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's and has to read as a maker's stamp at a kitchen table against two other bids, not as a sales badge. The weight cannot be inferred from the style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry or designer and actual weight per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML carrying the quote pack at true physical dimensions, the before and after module, the square, four by five and nine by sixteen social canvases and the yard sign at its real size on the deep green, inlining every photograph as image data and the mark as SVG markup.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override collapses a mixed size set. The design work is how much air this band takes and how the mark is scaled and placed on its own ground.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML carrying the whole kit, retained as the durable source.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, then look: verify canvas one from the document's rendition and the rest from the returned per canvas markup, including how the mark resolved.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, the rendition shows the first artboard only, and a traced mark arrives as many loose shapes rather than one object.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document, an inspected first canvas and a markup audit for the rest.

trajectory.judgement: Real reconciliation: one job is entered twice under two names, one job may not be shown at all, and the photo column points at files this engagement produces. What is the agent's call and what is the owner's is a decision, and consent is not one of them.

trajectory.judgement: The mapping strategy and the photo frame's true aspect are properties of the retired printer's document, not of the printed card, and every offset must be computed from the document rather than from a convenience readout.
trajectory.produces: The converted document, its interchange export, a frame inventory with real ids and bounds, and a reconstructed story string.

trajectory.action: Author the mapping covering every copy field plus the photo frame, validate it, prepare the template, then export the interchange file from the RESULT and search for every placeholder the mapping claimed to create.

trajectory.action: Merge to a native document with the per row images bound, then render the card run and the proofs at true print resolution from that document, and produce the per-project single files, naming each by opening it.

trajectory.action: Read every rendered card at trim rather than at proof scale, checking each line and what the card's own photo frame did to the crop it was given.
trajectory.judgement: A wrongly bound photograph and a feature cropped away by the frame both look like success at the API boundary and both look plausible on a screen scale proxy.

trajectory.action: Build the sign off board of shortlisted pairs and the mark within the placement cap, re-sending only entries named as failed, then write the note.

trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the Ridge Road pair still reads as one site once both frames are finished and adjacent. The before and the after were shot months apart from slightly different standing positions in different light, and the limestone in the two runs to opposite sides of neutral. Neither frame looks wrong on its own, and neither looks wrong beside the other four jobs; the divergence only exists as a property of the pair, at one size, side by side, after both have been taken to the finish target. There is no eyedropper and no histogram anywhere in the connector, so it cannot be predicted from either frame and can only be seen once the pair is assembled.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it, because the comparison requires both frames finished and cropped, and care cannot prevent it: bringing each frame correctly to the set target is exactly what makes the divergence legible. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the befores must stay honest and the afters must look like the firm's finish, which are the client's goals; no asset note, no earlier step and no deliverable says anything about the stone or about how the two frames relate. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the responses available are a confined correction on the stone alone, a re-crop toward the framing the two frames actually share, or dropping the job from the library, and each is a different decision with different downstream consequences.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Judge the pair adjacent at one size rather than each frame alone, then either confine a correction to the stone (accepting that a binary selection cannot blend at the planting boundary and inspecting the result at full resolution), or re-derive both crops toward the framing the two genuinely share, or set that job aside and re-pick which pair leads the module and the quote pack. Any of the three re-flows into the social set and into which after is bound to that job's project card.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The firm's flagship pair goes on the website and into every quote pack showing limestone that is warm grey before and cool grey after, which a buyer at a kitchen table reads as a different house, and the before and after claim, which is the only proof this firm has, quietly stops being believed.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the isolation actually did to the pergola's edge where the stone meets the sky. The pale limestone stands against a flat overcast sky of very nearly its own luminance, and the tool exposes no threshold, no matte control, no confidence value and no warning: it succeeds, returns a cutout whose overall silhouette is right, and the transparency preview looks clean because a checkerboard behind a pale edge hides exactly this. Whether the detector took the rafter tails and the balustrade with the sky is a property of this frame and this boundary, and it becomes visible only when the cutout is put on a ground it contrasts with, at full resolution.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, and the agent cannot simply do it right first time because there is no parameter to set: the same call is the only call, and what it did is observable only afterwards. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for the pergola pulled out cleanly, which is the goal, and the acceptance line about a clean edge is the client's own standard, not a disclosure that this edge is at risk. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is a different instrument entirely, a positive selection of the structure by its own visual properties then an inverted knockout or a bounded crop, and possibly a different hero if the boundary will not give.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Inspect the cutout on a contrasting ground rather than on transparency, and where the edge has been bitten, rebuild the isolation through an explicit selection of the structure and its inversion, or fall back to a solid ground knockout that keeps the edge and gives up transparency, then re-judge the hero at the size the yard sign and the quote pack actually use it and re-place it in both.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The best thing this firm has ever built goes on a yard sign, a quote pack cover and the site with its rafter tails eaten off against a deep green ground, which is instantly legible to anybody who has looked at a pergola and reads as carelessness by the firm that built it.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered mark survives at real reproduction size on the firm's own deep green. The trace is clean at the size it was made, where the narrow counter in the initial is open and the hairline rule under the wordmark is a rule. What that same geometry does when it is placed at yard sign scale on a saturated dark ground, and how the importer resolves it into the document, is a different question: the counter can fill visually against the green and the hairline can drop below the weight at which it reads as a line rather than as an artefact. The trace tool takes no options at all, so nothing about this is adjustable at the point of tracing, and the only channel that reports what actually happened is the returned per canvas markup and the rendition.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it, because the ground, the scale and the trace all have to exist before the question exists, and care cannot settle it: a mark that is manifestly clean at canvas size gives no signal about a dark ground at sign size. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the mark has to work from a shirt to a yard sign and names the green, which is the client's requirement; nothing in the assets, the steps or the deliverables says anything about what the trace does to the counter or the rule. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the fix lives three steps back in the raster preparation, because the trace has no parameters, so the response is to re-prepare the plate and trace again, which is a different piece of work.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Look at the mark on its real ground at its real size rather than at authoring scale, and if the counter closes or the rule fails, go back to the raster preparation (a tighter or differently prompted plate, a different source between the emailed file and the painted door, a cleaner polarity) and trace again, then re-inject the viewBox, strip the background rectangle again, re-place it and re-export, and record the smallest reproduction the delivered artwork actually holds at.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The firm hands the artwork to a sign shop and a shirt printer as the definitive mark, and every yard sign in the Litchfield Hills carries a filled initial and a broken rule, which is worse than the situation the firm started in because it is now committed and paid for.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the photographs into a frontier image model and it returns a beautiful garden that nobody built. IDENTITY is the whole product: a before and after is a claim that THIS firm did THIS work at THIS house, and a generated after in a quote pack is not a design shortcut, it is fraud in front of a homeowner. The mark is the firm's actual mark, painted on its actual truck, and a redrawn approximation is a different company's logo handed to a sign shop. SPEC: the firm needs one A6 card per publishable job binding four named fields verbatim with the right job's photograph, per-project files each containing the job they claim, proofs at true print resolution, and delivered images that never exceed their sources. EDITABILITY: the quote pack is defined by being editable because prices move. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: does this pair still read as one site, did this knockout keep the rafter tails, does this counter stay open on green at sign size.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted (image_vectorize counted as Photoshop family, not as an Illustrator surface, and no dead vector or video tool anywhere), no banned capability. IMAGING: apply_adjustments global and masked, auto_tone, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, remove_background transparent and with backgroundColor, fill_area, crop_to_bounds and crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs, detection_confidence and upscale_factor, and vectorize are all verified headless, as is the full extract and reuse chain select, invert, crop to bounds, vectorize, inject viewBox, strip path 0, inline into HTML, export. The three checkpoints rest on documented facts rather than invention: there is NO measurement anywhere in the family, so a divergence between two frames of the same material can only be seen by putting them adjacent; remove_background exposes no threshold, no matte and no confidence and is documented collapsing on boundaries its detector reads as ambiguous (a solid disc on an enclosed interior, two surviving letters on disjoint lettering), so what it did to an edge is only observable against a contrasting ground; and image_vectorize TAKES NO OPTIONS AT ALL, with the documented consequence that all tuning must happen in the raster prep, which is what makes a re-trace a genuine three step return rather than a re-run. The documented prompt gate (naming the substrate selects the substrate, naming the ink's own colour, medium and form selects the ink) carries the two source triage, and both failure modes return success. MERGE SPINE: building a merge template from a bare press PDF end to end headlessly is verified, one record per page is confirmed for the PDF branch, per-record files are confirmed in correct order by two routes, true 300 DPI at trim is confirmed through the render tool, the merge's own resolution parameter is documented as silently ignored, frame granularity and bounds from a PDF are documented as not under your control, and the mapping readout's text content is documented as lossy in a way the validator blesses. Per row image binding through an at prefixed column plus an image map is verified visually. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export, true mm print canvases at exactly 96 dpi, real tables, inline SVG arriving as native editable vector shapes, and a genuine editable document are all verified; the rendition shows PAGE 1 ONLY so verification splits between the rendition and the returned markup; payload routed by uploaded URL. FONTS, STOCK and BOARDS follow the verified chains, with short queries, orientation never passed, and the twelve per call board cap with 201 meaning partial and vector unsupported there. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no fill_text or replace_image or animate_design, no text to image, no generative fill, no object removal, no upscaling, no OCR, no compositing, no bleed or press preset gate, no variable QR, no batch above 20.

engagement_title: Meridian Motors weekly intake: bring three lot bays to one showroom, cut compliant plain-ground primaries, and rebuild the window card run the printer took with him
vertical: Automotive retail, certified pre-owned dealership, six vehicle weekly intake, Portland, Maine
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the recurring Upwork and Freelancer.com dealership listing post class this ledger row was drawn from, in which a used vehicle dealer asks for each week's walk around photographs to be colour corrected to one consistent look and for the lead photograph of every vehicle to be placed on a plain background, because the marketplace carrying their traffic rejects a first image that carries any added logo, badge, border or burned in text. The posted version of that job is written as photo editing alone and priced as such, and the ledger's own verdict is that the concept therefore sat on one surface. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) changes what the honest fuller commission is: a client supplied press PDF now converts into a live InDesign merge template, so the window card this dealer hand writes every week becomes genuine record per page variable data work with a per row image bind, and HTML authoring now produces a native editable Express document at mixed canvas sizes for the collateral the marketplace rule actually permits them to brand. So this is that dealer's real job rather than the slice of it they knew how to post. No real dealership, marque, marketplace or person is named: the line is laundered to the coined Meridian Motors with coined marques (Calder, Norsted, Brookmere, Ardmoor).
client_one_liner: Six cars a week, three lot bays, and the listings look like six different dealerships; the marketplace keeps bouncing our first picture, and we hand write the window cards because the printer who made them is gone.
client_brief:
Meridian Motors, Portland, Maine. Certified pre-owned, roughly six cars a week onto the lot.

Our listings are the whole business and right now they look like six different dealerships. We photograph every car ourselves as it comes out of reconditioning. There are three bays: the open front apron, the covered wash bay, and the back row against the grey block wall. Same camera, same walk around order, wildly different pictures. Put six listings side by side and one car looks yellow, one looks blue, and one looks like it is parked in a cave. We want every car to look like it was photographed in one clean showroom.

The marketplace that carries most of our traffic has a hard rule about the first picture: the vehicle on a plain ground, nothing else in the frame, no logo, no badge, no border, no text burned into the image. They reject listings over it and they have rejected ours. So we need that plain ground picture for each car, and it has to hold up when they drop it onto their own coloured page, not only against white. Everything after the first picture is ours to design, and that is where we do want our name on it.

Second thing. Every car carries a card in the side window with the stock number, the year and model, the mileage, the price and the certification line. Our printer built those from a file nobody here can edit, so we hand write them now, and it looks exactly as bad as it sounds. We want the week's intake printed properly, one card per car, we want to see proofs before anything prints, and we want to be able to run next week ourselves.

Third, a small set of pictures for the forecourt screen and for our own social.

Our cars are twenty two to thirty eight thousand dollars. Our buyers are families replacing a ten year old car. We want to look organised and honest. Tell us what you did to each picture.
price_band_and_audience: Certified pre-owned at 22,000 to 38,000 dollars, buyers 30 to 55 replacing an ageing family car, deciding on trust before they decide on the vehicle. The band is load bearing. At this price the whole visual argument is that this operation is orderly and has nothing to hide, so the treatment must be an even, neutral, well lit showroom white with the full vehicle in frame, honest paint colour, and legible plain information. Push it into a dark dramatic studio look with rim light and a black sweep and it becomes a 180,000 dollar exotic specialist, which reads as evasive on a nine year old crossover and invites the buyer to wonder what the shadows are hiding. Push the other way into hot saturated pictures with starbursts and a price slash and it becomes a buy here pay here lot, which is exactly the reputation this dealer is spending money to escape. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. A posted job of this shape runs 900 to 2,200 dollars fixed, usually with a standing weekly retainer attached.

acceptance_bar: The six vehicles read as ONE lot when the listings are laid side by side: one showroom white, one black point, one honest paint rendition, one framing logic. A car that cannot be brought to the set is named in the note, not shipped at eighty percent.
Every marketplace primary is the vehicle on a plain ground with nothing else in the frame: no mark, no badge, no border, no burned in text, no reflection or shadow invented for it.

The cut edge on the primaries holds against the marketplace's own coloured page and not only against white, on the pale bodies as well as the dark ones, and the grille and wheel apertures do not read as filled panels.

No delivered file exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions and no crop or knockout tradeoff record in the run carries an upscale entry. A tile that reaches its size by being enlarged fails even if it looks acceptable.
The window card run produces one card per vehicle in roster order, and every field on every card is the merged value rather than last season's static text.
Every card carries the vehicle it names. A proof whose photograph belongs to the other silver Calder fails outright, whatever the response labelled it.
The price on every card is the current roster price, including the vehicle that was repriced after its photographs were taken.
The roundel appears on the forecourt and social collateral and appears nowhere in any marketplace primary.
On the collateral the roundel is live vector geometry with its inner ring open at the size it actually reproduces on the dark forecourt ground, not a small picture of a logo enlarged.

All three collateral canvases sit in ONE working file, each keeping its own canvas size, with live editable text and every photograph carried as embedded image data, and the self contained source is delivered with it.

The note records, per photograph, what was applied and why that frame differs from its neighbours, every resize any tool reported, the reconciliation of roster rows to vehicles, and anything about the roundel the dealer should know.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching a pixel.
trajectory.judgement: The listing images are raster work against a published external spec, the window cards are a record per page run that only the layout surface does, and the branded collateral needs an authored fixed canvas document because the dealer intends to reuse it weekly. The brief pins every destination, so there is nothing here to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline, but the manifest is keyed by stock number rather than by filename, because two vehicles in this intake are the same colour and shape.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by stock number and role.

trajectory.action: Preview all eighteen frames and triage them: which bay each belongs to, which illuminant it carries, which are off level, and which bodies sit close to their ground in value.
trajectory.judgement: The dealer describes three bays. The pictures are the only place that can be confirmed, and body colour against ground is a property of the individual frame, not of the bay.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note covering bay, illuminant, tilt, and body against ground.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes the vehicle and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop, and a canted car reads as a careless lot at exactly the price band that is buying carefulness.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Propose two candidate showroom whites, a cool clinical one and a slightly warm neutral, argue one against the band and the buyer, then fix the target off the cleanest bay frame and correct each vehicle toward it with its own call.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a lot, not six good pictures, and it is set once. Choose it off the covered bay's own light and the whole inventory ships warm and looks like a different dealership per car. One batched call applies one identical parameter set, which is exactly wrong for three bays.
trajectory.produces: A defended white point and six corrected vehicles at source scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Apply confined corrections where the global move goes wrong, selecting by the material's own visual properties rather than by the object it sits on.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the whole gate: naming the bay pulls the selection to the tarmac. The red Ardmoor's paint swings orange under the warm neutral and the black Brookmere's shadow side blocks up under the cool one, and neither is fixable at whole frame scale without breaking the other five.
trajectory.produces: Corrected frames where a whole frame move would have falsified the paint.

trajectory.action: Cut the plain ground primaries for all six vehicles, then inspect each result at full resolution against a coloured ground rather than reading the success message, and record every returned tradeoff.
trajectory.judgement: The marketplace rule is absolute and the plain ground has to be part of the delivered raster, not a page background. The tradeoffs array is the only channel that reports what any tool did to the frame's dimensions, and it carries no warning language.
trajectory.produces: Six plain ground primaries plus transparent variants, each with its returned tradeoffs recorded and its edge inspected.

trajectory.action: Cut the marketplace primary to the published tile spec and cut the sixteen by nine detail set, downscale only, vehicle framed with clear air at every edge.
trajectory.judgement: The published spec is a floor, not a target, and the only route back to it from a short frame is interpolation, which the crop tool performs up to a cap while reporting it solely inside its own tradeoffs.
trajectory.produces: Six compliant primaries at spec and a detail crop set.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for a covered forecourt atmosphere band, filter to photography, exclude generative tech results, license and download at full resolution.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose existing light can be brought to the showroom white, not the prettiest thumbnail. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP clean, camera scale frame, graded into the same world.

trajectory.action: Recover the roundel: an ink level selection naming the mark's own visual properties, correct polarity, a bounds crop from the selection's own returned box, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full canvas ground path removed, and finally a look at the result at the size it will actually reproduce on the dark forecourt ground.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions the tools do not make: how to word the selection so it takes the ink and not the white square, which polarity to trace, and whether what survives still reads as a compass roundel once its inner ring is at real size on a dark ground. Background removal is the wrong instrument on an enclosed ring.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent roundel judged at reproduction size, with its limits written down.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's, judged against a 22,000 to 38,000 dollar band and a family buyer who is reading a price and a mileage. The weight cannot be inferred from the style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Convert the window card PDF, export the IDML, and read the real frame inventory: how many text frames actually exist, what each story truly contains, and which wells are genuine image frames.
trajectory.judgement: Frame granularity from a PDF is not under anyone's control and the printed page is not evidence of it. Promising a per field frame mapping before looking is how a run ships half populated.
trajectory.produces: A frame inventory naming every mappable target and every field that has no frame of its own.

trajectory.action: Reconstruct each frame's true story text from the IDML story runs, compute every offset from that string, build the mapping with integer frame ids, validate it, prepare the merge template, then round trip the IDML again and grep for every expected placeholder.
trajectory.judgement: The structure readout and the validator both speak with total confidence and neither of them reads the document. The only evidence that a placeholder exists is the placeholder appearing in the story after preparation.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholder inventory has been read back from the document rather than reported.

trajectory.action: Merge the week's roster to one press PDF in roster order and bind the per row hero through the image column, then merge again to a native document and render the manager's proofs at true resolution, reading each proof against the roster by stock number, price and mileage.
trajectory.judgement: Six cards is a small enough run to check completely and two of the six are the same colour and shape, so the check has to be against the roster values on the card, not against the photograph. A card carrying the wrong car is a priced misrepresentation, not a design error.
trajectory.produces: A press PDF of the week's cards and a proof set whose identity has been read rather than assumed.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML with three roots at three canvas sizes, inline every photograph as image data, place the roundel as inline SVG inside an explicitly sized top left anchored wrapper, declare family and weight on every text element, let each root declare its own canvas, then upload the file and hold the returned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override is what collapses a mixed size set. The design work is how plain the collateral stays at this band, and the compliance work is that the roundel lives here and nowhere near a primary.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML carrying the whole collateral set, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at canvas one, and parse the returned per canvas markup for canvases two and three.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition preview only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at page one is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document, an inspected first canvas, and a per canvas markup audit for the other two.

trajectory.action: Create the week's selects board, add the graded set and the licensed frame within the per call placement cap, re-send only the entries the response names as failed, then write the handover note.
trajectory.judgement: A 201 is partial success, and the vector roundel is not boardable so it belongs in the note instead. The note has to let the sales desk run next week's intake without re-commissioning anything.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the one call plain ground knockout actually found the vehicle's edge on this particular photograph. On the white Norsted against the sun bleached apron and the silver Calder against the grey block wall, the paint runs at very nearly the ground's luminance along the roofline and the shoulder, so there is no contrast for subject detection to work from there. The call returns ordinary success and a cutout that is clean, complete and entirely convincing at preview scale and against white; the bite along the roof edge only shows at full resolution against a coloured ground. Which frames behave this way is a property of each capture's own paint, sky and wall, and cannot be read off the frame beforehand.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter controls it: the knockout has to be run before its edge can be judged, and doing it right first time would mean knowing in advance which of six vehicles has no edge contrast. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says the marketplace wants a plain ground and that it must hold on their coloured page, which is the client's standing requirement, not a disclosure that detection fails on pale paint. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is a different chain for those frames, selecting the bay surface by its own material properties, inverting, and filling to the house ground rather than asking for a subject.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Abandon the one call route for the affected vehicles, re-derive their plain ground primaries and transparent variants through a material named ground selection inverted and filled, re-inspect every edge at full resolution against a coloured ground rather than white, and re-cut the primaries that were already trimmed from the first cutouts.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Marketplace primaries whose roofline has been eaten, shipped on the exact deliverable the marketplace has already been rejecting, on a lot whose only sales argument is that it is careful.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: That the readout of the card's single text flow is not the text. It omits one run while keeping that run's line break, so the returned string still looks well formed and every character offset past the omission is short by the length of the dropped run. The validator then reports the mapping as valid with no warnings, and the preparation step reports that placeholders were created successfully, while two of the six fields never land. Nothing in any response distinguishes the mappings that took from the ones that were silently discarded, and the true story text exists only inside the exported document's own story runs.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it, because the readout is the only offset source the tools offer and the discrepancy is invisible in the readout itself; the mitigation of rebuilding the story from the document is a response to having seen placeholders go missing, not a step any tool asks for. (b) Nothing states it: neither the brief nor the deliverable list says anything about how the card's text is structured, and the client believes the card is six separate boxes. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the mapping is rebuilt from a different source of truth, not re-submitted unchanged.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Download and unpack the exported document, concatenate the story runs to recover the true text, recompute every offset against that string, rebuild and revalidate the mapping, prepare the template again, and re-export the document to confirm by inspection that all six placeholders are present before any record is merged.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A week's window cards printed and hung in six car windows with the mileage and the certification line missing or carrying last season's static text, on the one deliverable a walk up buyer reads before speaking to anyone.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the per record proof set actually corresponds to the roster the way the response says it does. The merge returns proofs labelled by row position, and the labels are not the order the files come back in, so a proof named for row one can be the last vehicle in the roster. There is no error, no warning, and the page count is correct. With two silver Calders of the same shape in the same intake, the mismatch survives a visual check entirely, and the only way to learn it is to read the merged values on each rendered card against the roster.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it: the tool's own description promises one output per row and the labels assert an order, so a competent agent following the documentation walks straight in, and the discrepancy exists only in the returned artefacts. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks to see proofs before printing, which is a client wanting to check a price, not a disclosure that identity is unreliable. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the fix is a different delivery route with identity guaranteed per call, not the same merge repeated.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Stop naming any per record file by its position in the response, re-derive the proof set either by merging to a native document and rendering separate files or by looping the merge one record at a time so identity is guaranteed per call, name each file from the roster on download, and re-read each rendered card against its stock number, price and mileage before the run is called checkable.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A manager approving six proofs in which the two silver Calders have swapped, so one car is hung with the other's price and mileage in its window, which at this band is not a design error but a misrepresented vehicle.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are raster work against an external spec, which need a record per page run, and which need an authored fixed canvas document, given that only one surface here composes free form layout.
Which showroom white to set, cool clinical or slightly warm neutral, argued against a 22,000 to 38,000 dollar family band rather than against the prettiest single frame.
Whether the three bays can all be brought to that white, and how to say so for the frame that cannot.

Knockout route per vehicle: the one call plain ground route for bodies that separate from their ground, versus a material named ground selection inverted and filled where paint and ground share luminance.

Whether the grille and wheel apertures can be left as the knockout returns them, or whether the compliant primary needs a different construction entirely, given that an enclosed interior cannot be punched.
Selection prompt wording throughout: naming the bay or the paper takes the substrate, naming the material's own visual properties takes the thing you want.
Which fields of the window card can be mapped to frames of their own and which have to be reached inside a single flow, decided from the document's real inventory rather than from the printed page.
Which delivery branch the proofs take, given that identity per output is guaranteed by some routes and asserted by others.
Where the roundel is permitted: on the collateral yes, on any marketplace primary never, and the compliance consequence of getting that backwards.
Whether the recovered roundel holds at reproduction size on a dark ground, and what to tell the dealer if it does not.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a family buyer reading a price and a mileage, plus the real numeric weight per family.
How plain the collateral stays. At this band restraint is the trust argument, and a dense, badge covered, starburst tile is a correct looking wrong answer.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of used cars. IDENTITY: each listing is a specific vehicle a buyer will walk around in person, so a generated car is a different car and the listing becomes a misrepresentation; the two silver Calders in this intake are the point, not an edge case. SPEC: the marketplace enforces a published tile size and a hard rule that the first image carries no added graphic of any kind, and a generated image satisfies neither and cannot be checked for either. EDITABILITY: the window card run has to exist as a template the dealer re-runs every week with a new roster, and the collateral has to be an editable document because the featured vehicle changes weekly, neither of which a flat render is. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did this cutout find the roofline, did these placeholders actually land in the story, is this proof the car it says it is.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, fill_area, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs, detection_confidence and upscale_factor, remove_background in both the transparent and backgroundColor forms, and vectorize are all verified headless across 27 live calls; alpha survives crops at outputFileType png. The knockout checkpoint rests on documented behaviour: subject detection needs contrast and remove_background reports nothing about edge quality, while masked and material named selections are the verified alternative route, and the enclosed interior failure (a solid opaque disc where a ring was expected) is a confirmed live finding, which is why the roundel is handled by selection and trace rather than by knockout. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt as readout and validator, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout with an @ prefixed image column plus additionalImageFiles, and document_render_layout at real resolution are all verified end to end and synchronous. The offsets checkpoint rests on the verified finding that the readout's textContent dropped a 17 character run while keeping its line break, that the validator returned VALID on the resulting wrong offsets, that preparation reported success, and that only 3 of 5 mappings landed until offsets were recomputed from the true story. The proof identity checkpoint rests on the verified finding that multi record raster output came back reversed while the response labels asserted row order, with PDF order, createSeparateFiles and a recordRange loop all verified correct as alternatives. Frame granularity from a PDF is documented as not controllable and as collapsing a continuous flow into one frame, which is why the inventory is read before any mapping is promised. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, the product is a genuine editable dcx findable by asset_search, external image URLs render as empty grey boxes so photographs are base64 inlined, and the rendition preview is documented as page one only, which is why verification splits between rendition and returned markup. Transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined photography passes the 70 KB inline threshold immediately. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end including a browser proving licensed faces load; the case sensitivity, all or nothing kit and non standard numeric weight traps are all live findings. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed, license returned a real 7360x4912 JPEG, boards persist with a hard cap of 12 placements per call and 201 meaning partial. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no variable QR, no bleed gate on a PDF derived template, no pdfPreset, no upscaling, no compositing, no OCR, no text to image, no photo reaching Express as a URL, no fill_text, no animate_design, no create_firefly_board, no batch above 20 (18 frames plus 6 roster rows).

engagement_title: OSTRA, one room across two services: a low light plate set that survives both a near black site and a white delivery card, plus the per cover menu run the old printer took with him
vertical: Food, restaurant and beverage, contemporary seasonal tasting counter, twenty two seats, coastal New England
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork post quoted in this ledger row's grounding_note, from a boutique digital studio commissioning a premium restaurant website described as high end, clean, modern minimalist, with a Dark Mode aesthetic that focuses heavily on high quality food photography, across Home, an interactive food menu and Booking, mobile responsive. The real post names no restaurant, so the room is laundered to the coined OSTRA and the client stays an unnamed studio whose own front end developer builds the site. The web build itself is out of connector scope, and the ledger's verdict is that what remained sat on one surface. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) changes what the honest fuller commission is: the studio's designer needs finished photographs rather than raw files, the same plates have to survive a delivery platform's white card as well as the room's near black page, a client supplied press PDF now converts into a live merge template so the per cover menu card the room prints nightly becomes real record per page work, and HTML authoring produces a native editable Express document at mixed canvas sizes for the entry screens and the booking graphic. So this is the photographer's half of that website job as the room actually needed it bought.
client_one_liner: Our plates were shot across two services and read as two different evenings, the delivery platforms put them on a white card next to everybody else, and we hand write the menu cards because the printer who set them up is gone.
client_brief:
OSTRA. Twenty two seats around the pass, one seasonal tasting menu at a hundred and thirty five dollars a head, four nights a week.

We are rebuilding the site with a small studio and their designer needs finished photographs from us rather than raw files. The site is dark: near black, very little on the page, one plate at a time. That is the room, so that is the site.

The pictures were shot across two services by a friend who cooks with us. First service ran early and second service ran late, and the pass lighting at nine is not the pass lighting at six. Looked at one at a time they are lovely. Scrolled one after another they are obviously two different evenings. We need them to read as one set: one temperature, one depth of shadow, gloss that still looks like gloss rather than a grey patch.

We also list on two delivery platforms for the Sunday supper box. Those platforms put every picture on a white card in a grid next to everybody else's, and ours currently vanish there.

Then the printed menu. Every guest gets a card at their seat with their name, the date, the courses and their pairing flight. Our old printer set that up and we lost him. We print about forty a night, we want to run tonight's covers ourselves each afternoon, and we want to see proofs before anything prints.

Last, the two screens in the entry and a square graphic for booking confirmations. Those are ours to design and they should feel like walking into the room rather than like an advertisement.

A hundred and thirty five dollars, guests thirty to fifty five, booking an occasion six weeks out. Quiet, dark, unhurried. Not a bistro and not a hotel restaurant. Tell us what you did to each plate and why that plate needed something different.
price_band_and_audience: A 135 dollar seasonal tasting counter, guests 30 to 55 booking six weeks ahead for an occasion. The band is load bearing and it dictates a specific grammar: a near black ground, one plate per frame, generous emptiness, restrained saturation, and speculars on sauce and glass that still read as light rather than as blown white or flattened grey. That restraint is what a guest is paying for and what makes a six week wait feel reasonable. Grade the same plates bright, warm, saturated and crowded, with two dishes per frame and a garnish filling every corner, and the room reads as a 14 dollar plate at a busy bistro, which at this cheque size does not read as friendly, it reads as a mistake the guest is about to make. Push the other way into near monochrome art photography with the food unreadable and it becomes a gallery rather than a dinner, and a guest cannot tell what they are booking. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. A posted job of this shape runs 1,400 to 3,000 dollars fixed.

Never a bright, crowded bistro look, and never near monochrome art photography in which the food cannot be read.
