A generated image satisfies none of that and cannot be checked against an inventory export. EDITABILITY: two deliverables are defined by being editable, a live merge template so next season is a data change rather than a re-commission, and a native document with live text and real vector geometry so the studio changes prices itself. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: does this placeholder exist, is the photograph on this card the piece named on it, does this cutout belong on this ground, does this trace hold its ring at card-foot size. None of that is a generation problem.
doability_proof: Every link is verified in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), the surface count is five and honestly declared, and image_vectorize is counted in the Photoshop family rather than as an Illustrator surface. MERGE SPINE: building a merge template from a bare PDF end to end headlessly is verified (convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt, prepare_indd_merge_template producing a story containing the expected placeholders), one record per page is confirmed for PDF output, per-record named files are confirmed by two order-verified routes (createSeparateFiles and a recordRange loop) while multi-record raster order is documented as reversed and is therefore never used for identity, and true 300 ppi comes from document_render_layout because outputSpecs.resolution on the merge itself is documented as silently ignored. THE CARD PDF IS BUILT TO A VERIFIED SHAPE: v3 observed that a continuous flow with no placed images collapses to one text frame with zero graphic frames, while interleaved images split it into two text frames plus two graphic frames. This card places one photograph in its own block with three copy lines running contiguously beside it and the mark flattened into the background artwork, so the expected yield is one graphic frame plus a small number of text frames, with the three contiguous lines sharing one story. The PDF must be a real font-embedding press PDF produced by a full engine, since v3 records that a thin hand-authored PDF fails conversion opaquely. The flattened-mark fact is a property of the manufactured asset and is verify-then-ship: before admission, run the conversion and confirm the mapping inventory returns exactly one graphic frame. IMAGE BINDING: per-row image merge through an at-prefixed CSV column plus additionalImageFiles keyed to bare filenames is verified at three keys; this task binds ten, so the trajectory carries the verified recordRange loop as an explicit fallback, which also guarantees per-record identity. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, fill_area, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs array, remove_background with backgroundColor and vectorize are all verified headless across 27 live calls. The enclosed-aperture failure of remove_background is a verified live finding (a solid opaque disc where a true knockout would have been transparent), as are the substrate-versus-ink prompt asymmetry, the binary non-anti-aliased mask, vectorize's missing viewBox and opaque path zero, and the explosion into loose ungrouped shapes in Express. UPSCALING IS HANDLED NOT ASSERTED: crop_and_resize interpolates to a hard 2x cap and signals it only in metadata.tradeoffs, and remove_background silently downscales oversized inputs and reports it only as a downscaled tradeoff, so the acceptance bar scores the decision and the disclosure as separable clauses. EXPRESS: multi-root export with mixed canvas sizes in one document is verified, mm canvases resolve exactly at 96 dpi, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, and the product is a genuine editable document in Creative Cloud. Transport is pinned to the upload route with media_type text/html because inlined photography passes the readiness skill's 70 KB inline threshold, which v3 warns triggers a user-facing warning. Verification is split to match the two channels that exist, since the rendition preview shows page one only. Persistence is not assumed, so the deliverable is the Express document plus the durable source HTML. FONTS: font_recommend, font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url is verified end to end including a real browser loading licensed faces, and the non-standard numeric weights, the slug-not-PostScript CSS rule and the all-or-nothing kit call are live findings the task leans on. STOCK AND BOARDS: short generic queries only (long queries return zero hits and the orientation filter is broken), asset_license_and_download_stock returns genuine camera-scale files, and boards placements are capped at twelve per call with partial success signalled by failedItems and SVG unsupported, all encoded in the trajectory and the bar. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no document_render_vector or document_merge_data_vector, no variable QR, no bleed requirement, no pdfPreset, no fill_text, no animate_design or create_firefly_board, no replace_image, no download_design, no upscaling, no OCR, no compositing, no generated imagery, no photo reaching Express as a URL, and no batch above twenty files.

engagement_title: Girdermark spring counter catalogue: pull two bench sessions of elevator and electrical parts to one technical white, rebuild the printer's data sheet into a live merge, and hand the counter and the road reps one editable set
vertical: Industrial and Manufacturing, elevator and electrical replacement parts distribution to service technicians, maintenance supervisors and electrical contractors (Cleveland, Ohio)
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork brief 'Catalog designer needed, B2B electrical/elevator parts distributor (per-SKU product data sheets)', posted by a wholesale distributor selling to service technicians, maintenance supervisors and electrical contractors, who wanted distributor-facing product material with clean product photography and complete specs and pricing for every part. Laundered to the fictional Girdermark Elevator & Electrical Supply; no real company, person, product or trademark appears. Co-anchor: the Upwork 'Packaging/Graphic Designer for Label Conversion' brief from a construction-chemicals maker wanting legacy product PDFs rebuilt into an editable, maintainable Adobe layout system, quoting 'recreate the labels based on the existing design (no new design required)' and supplying 'updated texts, product images' with the deliverable required to be 'editable, print-ready files'. The ledger records that both slots were previously repositioned down to a bench-normalisation exercise on eight frames, which is one surface and one deliverable class. PHOTO-14 restores the commission both clients actually posted: the photography has to be fixed, but the point of fixing it is that a per-SKU sheet, a counter catalogue and a road-rep set all come out of the same range and have to agree.
client_one_liner: Twelve parts, two bench sessions that do not match, a data sheet the printer built and we cannot open, and a counter catalogue that has to be on the counter for the spring service season.
client_brief:
Girdermark Elevator & Electrical Supply, spring counter catalogue.

We are a distributor. We stock replacement parts for elevator and electrical service work and we sell to the men and women who do that work: service technicians, maintenance supervisors, electrical contractors. Twelve parts go into the spring counter catalogue and the spring service season starts in six weeks.

Our photography is the first problem. We shoot parts ourselves on the bench in the back of the warehouse. We did most of them one Saturday and the rest a few weeks later, and looking at them now they do not belong in the same catalogue. Some of the parts are galvanised, some are zinc plated, some are clear anodised and some are powder coated, and a buyer specifying a finish has to be able to tell those apart in the picture. If our pictures make plated steel look brassy, an engineer stops trusting the numbers next to it, and that is the whole business.

What we need from the pictures: every part looking like it was shot the same way on the same day, a clean version of each part on a plain neutral ground for the sheets, and an in-context bench version that still matches. A grid tile per part for the catalogue index that shows the whole part, not a corner of it.

The second problem is the sheets. Our printer produced our data sheets last spring off our own system, one part per page. We have the file they sent us and nothing else, and nobody here knows how it was put together. Keep it exactly as it is, it is what our customers recognise, and put this year's parts, specs and prices through it. Send us the press file plus one sheet per part, named to the part number, because the road reps email individual sheets all day and cannot be opening files to check which one they have.

Then the pieces we do not have at all. A line card the reps can hand over at a service call, a poster for the trade counter, and a short set of slides for the two distributor meetings in March. We want all of that back as one file we can edit ourselves, because prices move and I am not commissioning this again in August.

The parts run four hundred to nine thousand dollars and the people buying them are thirty-five to sixty and have been doing this for twenty years. Flat, accurate, no styling. Make it look like the numbers can be trusted. And I am attaching our export from the system: if anything in it looks wrong to you, say so before it prints.
price_band_and_audience: Parts from 400 dollars (contactor blocks, relay sockets, restrictor brackets) to 9,000 dollars (governor sheave assembly, door operator arm assembly). Buyer 35 to 60, a working service technician, a building maintenance supervisor or an electrical contractor who has specified this class of part for twenty years and judges a supplier's credibility by whether the photography and the spec table agree. The band is load-bearing. At this tier the correct artefact is flat, even, technical: one neutral, true finish colour, the whole part in frame at consistent scale, generous spec tables set for reading, prices plain in the run of the sheet, no styling, no atmosphere, no lifestyle. Push it toward bright consumer-tool photography with shallow depth and warm light and the buyer reads it as a 15 dollar hardware brand and doubts the load ratings printed beside it, which is exactly the failure this client describes. Push it the other way into dark cinematic hero photography and it reads as marketing rather than a parts catalogue. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,800 to 3,500 dollars fixed, or 45 to 70 dollars an hour for 35 to 50 hours.

brand_identity.tagline: The number and the part agree.
brand_identity.sector: Industrial and Manufacturing, wholesale distribution of elevator and electrical replacement parts
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 1974 in Cleveland, Ohio. Family-held distributor, roughly 30 people across one warehouse, a trade counter and a small road-rep team.
brand_identity.about: Girdermark stocks replacement parts for elevator and electrical service work and sells them to the people who do that work: service technicians, maintenance supervisors and electrical contractors across northern Ohio. We are a parts house, not a marketing company. What we sell on is accuracy, availability and forty years of the counter being right when someone calls at seven in the morning with a stalled car and a building full of people.
brand_identity.audience: Working buyers aged 35 to 60 who have specified this class of part for twenty years and judge a supplier by whether the photography and the spec table say the same thing. They order by part number and hold us to the values printed beside it.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Mid to upper industrial. Parts run 400 to 9,000 dollars. The material has to read as trustworthy and technical, never as a consumer hardware brand and never as glossy marketing.
brand_identity.typography: A single clear grotesque for headings and part numbers, a plain, generously set text face for the long spec tables. Nothing decorative. Numbers must be legible at a glance and unmistakable one from another.
brand_identity.voice: Direct, factual, no adjectives we cannot stand behind. We state the number, the finish and the price and we stop. If something is wrong we say so before it prints.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: We have no working brand files and no written guidelines. Our data sheets exist only as a flat press PDF the printer sent us last spring, and nobody here knows how it was built. Keep that sheet exactly as our customers recognise it. The palette and type notes above are our best account of the look, reconstructed for you, not a formal system.
brand_identity.values: Accuracy over polish. Availability. Honesty about what we stock and what a part will do. We would rather lose a sale than print a spec we cannot certify.

assets_supplied.name: bench_sessions/ (12 frames, 4800 x 3200)
assets_supplied.kind: In-house product photography of twelve SKUs shot on the stainless bench top in the back of the warehouse under shop fluorescents, across two Saturdays.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Most of them one Saturday, the rest a few weeks later. Same bench, same camera. They do not look like the same catalogue."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two faults, neither stated. (1) A failed fluorescent tube was replaced between the sessions, so the six later frames carry a green cast that a buyer reads as a finish difference rather than a lighting difference, which is the one thing this client cannot ship. (2) Three of the SKUs are long, thin and made of the same brushed steel as the bench they are lying on: the guide rail section, the door operator arm and the traveling cable clamp. On these frames a subject-aware crop has almost no contrast to find, so it latches onto the one high-contrast feature in the frame (the painted end fitting, the yellow cable jacket) and returns a tight crop of that fitting at low detection confidence while reporting complete success. The resulting grid tile is sharp, well composed and plausible, and it shows a fragment of the part rather than the part. Nothing declares it except the confidence and bounds values buried in the response and the sight of the twelve tiles laid out as the grid they are for.

assets_supplied.name: datasheet_2025_PRINT.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The printer's flat press PDF of last spring's per-part data sheet, US Letter portrait, one part per page, fonts embedded, produced from the distributor's own system through a full print engine so it converts cleanly. Carries a fourteen-row spec table, a part photograph, a dimensional line drawing and a compliance footnote.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What the printer sent us last spring. We do not have the working file and nobody here knows how it was built. Keep it exactly as it is."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three facts nobody at Girdermark could tell you. (1) The system that generated the sheet set the entire fourteen-row spec table as ONE continuous story with tab characters between each parameter and its value, so there are no per-parameter frames to map and every value has to be driven by ordered offsets inside a single story. (2) The mapping readout of that story silently omits the run holding the compliance footnote while keeping its line break, so the string still reads as well-formed and every character offset past it is short by exactly that run's length. The validator returns valid on the resulting arithmetic, the placeholder step reports success, and the two fields that sit past the omission never become placeholders at all. (3) The two graphic frames are distinguishable only by their bounds and their link, and neither is named for what it holds.

assets_supplied.name: parts_export.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Export from the distributor's stock system, one row per SKU, with columns for part number, description, the fourteen spec parameters, list price, dealer price and an image column.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our export, straight out of the system. The spec values are ours and they are what the customer holds us to."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Thirteen rows for twelve parts: a superseded part number the system still emits, flagged only by a discontinued date column the client never mentions. Part numbers carry a leading apostrophe from the spreadsheet that exported them. The image column is a plain header holding full local paths rather than bare filenames and without the prefix the merge's own image contract requires, so a naive run binds no images at all or binds the template's original photograph to every page. And three of the descriptions are full compliance strings running four times the length of the others, written by the compliance clerk, which the client has said are held to as written.

assets_supplied.name: finishes_note.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Half a page from the sales manager describing the four finishes in the range in plain language, with no numbers and no colour values.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "How to tell them apart: galvanised is the spangled dull one, zinc plate is the bright bluish one, clear anodised is the flat grey one, powder coat is the flat black one."

assets_supplied.name: counter_2024.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Phone snap of the trade counter with last year's catalogue on it, supplied as a feel reference.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What the counter looks like. Nothing fancy."

acceptance_bar: All twelve parts read as one range: one neutral, one white point, one black point, judged with the twelve laid out as the catalogue index rather than one at a time.
The four finishes stay distinguishable from each other in the delivered pictures, and none of them has been pushed toward a colour the part is not.
Every grid tile shows the whole part at a consistent scale. A tile showing a corner or an end fitting of a part is a rejected tile even if it is sharp and well composed.
Each part has a clean version on the plain neutral ground for the sheet and an in-context bench version that still agrees with it.
No delivered file is larger than the frame it came from, and the note lists every picture that was resized and by how much.

Data sheets: exactly one page per current part, every field the 2025 sheet carried present on every page, every spec value bound verbatim from our export, and the photograph on each sheet the part named on that sheet.
Nothing in the export may be shortened, reworded or abbreviated to make it fit. Anything that will not fit inside the sheet as it stands, tell us in writing before it goes to the printer.
The press file renders at real print resolution at US Letter trim, and there is one sheet file per part named to the part number, containing the part its name claims.
The line card, the counter poster and the meeting slides come back as one working file we can edit ourselves, each at its own size, plus the source it was built from.
In that file the words are live text and the drawing is real artwork we can change, not a picture of a page.
One type system across all of it, and the note names per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the weight actually used.
A written note: what was done to each picture and why that one differs from its neighbours, anything in our export you questioned and what you did about it, and anything the sheet could not carry.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_adjust_single_color_saturation, image_select_by_prompt with returnBbox, image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize reading metadata.detection_confidence and metadata.tradeoffs, image_remove_background with backgroundColor, image_fill_area
adobe_surfaces.role: Fixes one technical white from the better session and corrects each SKU toward it with its own parameter set, because a batched call applies one identical set and half the range was shot under a replaced tube. Protects the four finishes from being neutralised into each other, which is the client's actual commercial requirement. Produces the neutral-ground cutouts for the sheets, routing per SKU because parts with through-bores and enclosed handles cannot be knocked out directly. Derives the catalogue grid tiles and the in-context bench crops, and is the only place the crop metadata that says a detection was weak can be read.

adobe_surfaces.surface: InDesign layout, merge-template authoring, data merge and print render
adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml (twice), generate_indd_mapping_prompt as generator and validator, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout (application/x-indesign and application/pdf, additionalImageFiles, recordRange), document_render_layout (resolution 300, createSeparateFiles, pageRange in N-N form)
adobe_surfaces.role: Rebuilds the printer's flat sheet into a live merge template with no working file to start from, reads the real frame inventory before promising any field map, reconstructs the true story text from the IDML content runs rather than trusting the mapping readout, binds the per-SKU photograph into the correct one of two indistinguishable graphic frames, and runs twelve parts at one record per page to a press PDF plus per-part named sheets plus 300 ppi proofs rendered from the merged document rather than requested at merge time.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search(CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The three pieces the client does not have: an A4 line card, an A1 trade-counter poster at true physical dimensions, and the March distributor slides, authored as one HTML with roots at three canvas sizes and exported as one native editable document. The spec comparison is a real table, the dimensional drawing is inline vector rather than a picture, and prices stay editable because they move.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Fonts
adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend once per role, font_styles for numeric OpenType weights, find_fonts for name laundering, get_fontkit_embed_url for one kit consumed through the returned css_stack
adobe_surfaces.role: The type system for the line card, the poster and the slides, and the specification of it in the handover. The pairing is the agent's own art direction because the recommender refuses to pair, and it has to land on a technical, flat, trustworthy register rather than a consumer one. Note that no font from this surface can reach the InDesign sheet, since there is no font file download, so the sheet's typography stays the printer's and the agent's typographic authorship exists only on the authoring surface, which is a constraint the handover has to state.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock plus Boards, counted as one surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search(entityScope StockAsset, short generic queries, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: One licensed machine-room or service-context frame for the counter poster and the opening slide, which the distributor cannot photograph inside a customer's building, plus the persistent board the sales manager and the two road reps approve the range from before the press file is committed.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface.
trajectory.judgement: The sheets are record per page against a layout the client has told you to keep, so they belong on the merge surface. The line card, poster and slides do not exist yet, need three canvas sizes and must stay editable, so they belong on HTML authoring. Authoring the sheets from scratch throws away the layout the customers recognise; trying to merge the poster discovers record per page cannot produce three canvas sizes.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier.

trajectory.action: Upload the twelve frames, the 2025 sheet PDF, the stock-system export and the reference material, holding each presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Manifest discipline: thirty artefacts later the mapping between URL and SKU has to still be trustworthy.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by SKU and role.

trajectory.action: Preview all twelve frames and triage: which session, which finish, how level, how much contrast each part actually has against the bench it is lying on, and whether the part in each frame is the part the export row claims.
trajectory.judgement: The client says same bench, same camera. Half the range disagrees. The agent also has to notice which parts are the same value as their background before it decides how to derive anything from those frames, and to read the export against the pictures rather than assuming a thirteen-row export describes twelve parts.
trajectory.produces: A per-frame triage note covering session, finish, level, subject contrast and identity.

trajectory.action: Level the frames that are off level.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes and eats edge pixels, so it precedes any crop decision.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed.

trajectory.action: Fix one technical white from the better-lit session and correct each SKU toward it with its own parameter set, recording what was dialled per frame.
trajectory.judgement: One destination held across twelve frames, not twelve locally optimised pictures. Six frames need a materially different correction to arrive at the same neutral. A single batched call would apply one identical parameter set and ship half the range green.
trajectory.produces: Twelve graded masters at source scale with a per-frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Masked corrections to protect the finishes: hold the galvanised spangle out of brass, keep clear anodised from collapsing into powder coat, keep zinc plate bright without going blue.
trajectory.judgement: This is the client's actual commercial requirement rather than a cosmetic one. Prompt wording is the gate, and a material selection on a brushed steel part lying on a brushed steel bench may leak into the bench, which has to be recognised as leakage rather than accepted because the call succeeded.
trajectory.produces: Finish-protected masters with the masked parameters recorded per SKU.

trajectory.action: Derive the catalogue grid tile and the in-context bench crop for every SKU, reading the detection confidence and the tradeoffs each crop returns rather than trusting success, then lay the twelve tiles out as the index grid they are for.
trajectory.judgement: A subject-aware crop is a guess with a confidence attached, and the confidence lives in the response rather than in the picture. Consistent subject scale across twelve tiles is a set-level decision that cannot be made one tile at a time.
trajectory.produces: Twelve grid tiles and twelve bench crops, laid out as the index, with the crop metadata transcribed.

trajectory.action: Propose two neutral grounds for the data-sheet cutouts, a paper white and a light technical grey, and pick one against an engineering readership.
trajectory.judgement: A taste decision with a defence attached, and one that has to hold for four different finishes: a ground that flatters powder coat can bury clear anodised.
trajectory.produces: Two proposed grounds and a written pick.

trajectory.action: Isolate each SKU onto the chosen ground, routing per part: coherent solid bodies through the one-call knockout, parts with through-bores, open frames and enclosed handles through a material-named selection, inverted and filled to the ground.
trajectory.judgement: A knockout fills an enclosed bore with captured bench and reports success, and a sheave with a filled bore is a part the buyer does not recognise. The route is a per-part decision made by looking at the part.
trajectory.produces: Twelve neutral-ground cutouts with the route recorded per SKU.

trajectory.surface: Data preparation and Creative Cloud storage
trajectory.action: Reconcile the stock export against the pictures and the finishes note, normalise it into a merge-shaped data file with the image column in the form the merge contract requires and bare filenames in the cells, upload the sheet masters and build the image map against them.
trajectory.judgement: Real data-prep work: a superseded row the system still emits, part numbers carrying a spreadsheet artefact, and an image column that does not satisfy the contract. The agent decides which of those are its call and which the client's, and how to say so.
trajectory.produces: The merge data file, uploaded masters, the image map, and a first list of export questions.

trajectory.action: Convert the 2025 sheet to a native document, export IDML, unzip it, and read the true frame inventory and the true story text reconstructed by concatenating the content runs.
trajectory.judgement: The mapping strategy is decided by what the client's own system happened to produce, not by the plan. Two graphic frames come back distinguishable only by bounds and link, and deciding which one holds the part photograph rather than the drawing is a judgement made against the printed reference, not a name in the response.
trajectory.produces: The converted document, its IDML, a frame inventory with real ids and bounds, and the reconstructed story text.

trajectory.action: Author the mapping covering every spec field plus the photograph, ordering any rows that share a uid against the original text, and pass it through the validator.
trajectory.judgement: Choosing the right action for the granularity that came back, computing offsets from a source of truth the agent has chosen deliberately, and passing the whole mapping across as one stringified object with integer page-item ids.
trajectory.produces: A validated mapping covering the spec fields and the image frame.

trajectory.action: Prepare the merge template, then export IDML from the RESULT, unzip it and grep the story for every placeholder the mapping claimed to create.
trajectory.judgement: Not accepting a success message as evidence. Nothing instructs this and nothing warns if it is skipped, and it is the only place the mapping's real yield is visible before pages exist.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholder inventory has been independently confirmed.

trajectory.action: Merge to a native document with the per-row photographs bound, render the press file and the proofs at 300 ppi, and produce per-part sheets named to part number, identity-verified by opening each file.
trajectory.judgement: Merging straight to raster silently drops to screen resolution whatever is asked for, and merging straight to PDF forfeits the per-record branch, so the route is chosen deliberately. Naming twelve sheets by the order they came back is the fast wrong answer and it is the one a road rep discovers in front of a customer.
trajectory.produces: The press sheet file, 300 ppi proofs and twelve identity-verified named sheets.

trajectory.action: Read every rendered sheet against the export and against the 2025 printed reference, line by line and photograph by photograph, at true trim rather than at proof scale.
trajectory.judgement: Reading the output rather than the log. A field that never became a placeholder, a compliance string that does not fit, and a photograph in the drawing's frame all look like success at the API boundary and all look plausible at proof scale.
trajectory.produces: A page-by-page reconciliation of the rendered sheets against the export.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for one service or machine-room context frame, filter to photography, exclude generative-tech results, license and download at full resolution, then grade it toward the technical neutral and judge it beside the range.
trajectory.judgement: An atmosphere frame at this band has to be flat and plausible rather than dramatic. A dark cinematic machine room is the wrong answer for a parts catalogue no matter how good it looks at thumbnail size.
trajectory.produces: One licensed camera-scale context frame, graded, judged in or out.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, read the real numeric weights from the style inventories, launder every name, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own and has to read technical rather than consumer. Numeric weight cannot be inferred from a style name, a display cut is reached by its own slug, and one bad name kills the whole kit including the valid faces beside it.
trajectory.produces: One kit with family, foundry or designer and the actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self-contained HTML with roots at three canvas sizes (A4 line card, A1 counter poster at true physical dimensions, meeting slides), the spec comparison as a real table, the dimensional drawing as inline vector inside an explicitly sized and top-left anchored wrapper, every photograph base64 inlined, family and weight declared on every text element, each root declaring its own canvas size. Upload by the allowed-host route, run the readiness check, export, then verify canvas one through its rendition and the remaining canvases through the returned markup.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, so the export is unverified until it is inspected, and the preview only shows the first canvas. The design decisions, how much of the A1 is table and how much is photograph, whether the line card leads with the range or the service promise, are the actual work.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document with all three canvas sizes, its durable source HTML, and a per-canvas markup audit.

trajectory.action: Create the approval board with the graded range and the licensed frame, within the placement cap and re-sending only the entries named as failed. Then write the handover.
trajectory.judgement: What to escalate versus what to fix silently. The note has to let the next freelancer rebuild the sheet from the same PDF without repeating the archaeology, and it has to name the compliance strings that will not fit and the export row that was excluded, before a printer sees the file.
trajectory.produces: A persistent approval board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether a subject-aware crop found the part. Three SKUs are long, thin and made of the same brushed steel as the bench beneath them, so the crop has almost no contrast to work with and latches onto the one high-contrast feature in the frame, returning a tight, sharp, well-composed crop of a painted end fitting or a yellow cable jacket, at a detection confidence well under any level worth trusting, while reporting complete success. Which frames behave that way is a property of these particular photographs (this part on this bench under this light) and cannot be predicted from the SKU list, the finishes note or the frame previews. The tile looks like a competent product tile. It is a picture of a fragment.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it and care alone does not either. The failure is produced by a detection step whose only honest signal is a confidence value and a bounds rectangle buried in a response that otherwise reads as success, and the crop that comes back is genuinely well composed, so there is no visual alarm in the artefact itself. An agent can only learn which frames are affected by running the crop on each of them and either reading the confidence or laying the twelve tiles out together and noticing that three of them are showing the wrong thing. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for a grid tile per part that shows the whole part rather than a corner of it, which is an ordinary client quality requirement, and says nothing about contrast, detection or which parts are at risk. No asset description names the three SKUs, and no earlier step reports subject contrast as a number. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is to abandon the subject-aware route for those frames and drive the crop from an explicit selection's own bounds instead, which is a different operation on a different input, and then to re-take the scale policy for the whole grid, because three tiles derived a different way will not sit at the same subject scale as the other nine unless the policy is re-decided across all twelve.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-derive the affected tiles by making an explicit selection of the part, taking its bounds, and cropping to those bounds with padding, rather than asking the crop to find the subject. Then re-lay all twelve tiles and re-decide the subject scale policy so the re-derived three sit with the nine, which in practice means re-cropping some of the nine as well. Transcribe every crop's reported metadata into the handover so the client can see which tiles were produced by which route.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A catalogue index in which three of twelve parts are represented by a sharp, confident photograph of the wrong end of the part, sent to buyers who order by looking at the picture and then reading the number beside it, from a supplier whose entire pitch is that the picture and the number agree.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printer's sheet actually exposes, and then whether the mapping built against it landed. Two things arrive only by running. First, the granularity: the fourteen-row spec table came out of the distributor's system as ONE continuous story with tab characters between parameter and value, so there are no per-parameter frames to map and everything must be driven by ordered offsets inside a single story, and the two graphic frames are distinguishable only by bounds and link. Second, the yield: the mapping readout of that story omits the run holding the compliance footnote while keeping its line break, so the string still parses as well-formed and every offset past it is short by exactly that run's length. The validator returns valid on internally consistent wrong arithmetic, the placeholder step reports success, and the two fields past the omission never become placeholders.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it and diligence alone cannot either. Granularity is not a parameter, is not reported before the conversion, and has no read-ahead: the only route to the answer is to convert, export and read. The yield failure is worse, because it is produced by a convenience readout that presents as complete, so an agent that reads carefully and computes offsets diligently from the readout it was handed produces arithmetic that is internally consistent and wrong, and every downstream tool agrees with it. The only defence is an independent reconstruction of the same text from a different channel, which nothing in any tool description prompts and whose necessity is invisible until the two disagree. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says keep the sheet exactly as it is and put this year's specs through it, and mentions no frames, fields, stories or offsets. The acceptance bar states an output requirement, that every field the 2025 sheet carried is present on every page, which is the client's standing requirement rather than a warning. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The source of truth behind the mapping changes, from a tool readout to a reconstructed story, and with it the whole mapping is re-authored with re-ordered same-uid rows. If the photograph turns out to have been mapped into the drawing's frame, the image binding is re-planned before the merge rather than after.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reconstruct the true story by concatenating the IDML content runs, recompute every offset against that string, re-order rows sharing a uid so their positions hold against the original text, rebuild and re-validate the mapping, re-run the template preparation, and re-verify by round-tripping IDML and grepping for every placeholder before a single page is merged. Settle which of the two graphic frames holds the photograph by rendering a page and reading it against the 2025 printed reference rather than by assuming the larger frame is the photograph.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Twelve data sheets that bind part number, description and most of the spec table correctly while the compliance line and the field after it are silently absent from every page, printed and put on a counter for technicians who order to those exact values, with every tool in the chain having reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the importer actually did with the two constructs the collateral depends on: the dimensional line drawing carried in as vector, and the spec comparison carried in as a real table. Neither the drawing's leader lines and dash treatment nor the table's per-cell strokes and cell backgrounds can be confirmed to have survived by any means other than reading the markup the import returns, and every drop this importer performs comes back as a success with no warning at all. The A1 poster and the slides compound it: the rendition preview shows the first canvas only, so whatever happened on the poster and the slides is reported by the returned markup and by nothing else.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it. How this importer normalises a given construct is not documented anywhere the agent can read ahead, is not a parameter, and is not signalled by the response status. Authoring the drawing more carefully does not tell you what happened to it, and the one visual channel available shows only the canvas that is least likely to be affected. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for live text and a drawing that is real artwork rather than a picture of a page, which is the client's requirement for an editable file, and it names no construct, no importer and no failure. No earlier step claims to have solved it, because no earlier step has exported anything. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is to re-author the construct itself, which means redrawing the dimensional artwork in a form that survives, or rebuilding the comparison in a different structure, and then re-running the readiness check and re-exporting, and the layout around the changed construct changes with it.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Parse the returned markup per canvas and check, for each canvas rather than only the first: that every photograph resolved to real image data rather than the importer's placeholder, that the drawing arrived as path shapes rather than one flattened element or nothing at all, that the table arrived as real cells rather than a stack of loose text, that every text element carries the intended face and weight rather than a silent fallback, and that no element's resolved position runs past its declared canvas width. Then re-author whichever constructs did not survive, re-upload, re-run the readiness check, re-export, and inspect again rather than assuming the second export took.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A counter poster and a slide set delivered as the client's editable file in which the dimensional drawing is gone or flattened, the spec comparison is a heap of loose text, and nobody notices because the only page anyone looked at was the line card.

deliverables.name: Girdermark range photography, twelve SKUs at one technical white
deliverables.spec: Twelve in-house frames from two sessions brought to one technical neutral with the four finishes still distinguishable from one another, delivered as a catalogue grid tile and an in-context bench crop per SKU at consistent subject scale, plus one licensed context frame graded into the same neutral. Every output at or below its source pixel dimensions, with a per-frame parameter log and one line per frame on why it differs from its neighbours, and every crop's reported detection and tradeoff metadata transcribed.

deliverables.name: Neutral-ground SKU cutouts for the data sheets
deliverables.spec: Twelve parts isolated onto the agreed neutral ground for the sheets, with through-bores, open frames and enclosed handles genuinely open rather than filled with captured bench, and the isolation route recorded per SKU because parts that are single coherent solids and parts that enclose voids cannot be produced the same way. True finish colour preserved through the isolation, since a buyer specifies from these pictures.

deliverables.name: Girdermark 2027 data sheets, press file plus per-part named sheets
deliverables.spec: US Letter portrait, one part per page in export order, page count equal to the current part count, rendered at 300 ppi at trim. Every page binds the fourteen spec parameters, the description, the compliance line and both prices verbatim from the stock export, plus that part's own photograph in the correct graphic frame. Accompanied by one single-page sheet per part named to the part number and identity-verified by opening it, and by 300 ppi proofs. Produced by reverse-engineering the printer's flat PDF into a live merge template, which is handed back with the record of how it was derived.

deliverables.name: Counter and road set: line card, A1 counter poster and March slides
deliverables.spec: One native editable Express document holding roots at three canvas sizes: an A4 line card, an A1 trade-counter poster at true physical dimensions, and the distributor meeting slides. Live editable text throughout in one licensed type system, the spec comparison as a genuine table, the dimensional drawing as real vector artwork, every photograph carried as embedded image data. Delivered with the self-contained source it was authored from, so prices can be changed without a re-commission and the design survives the document's own retention.

deliverables.name: Handover note and approval board
deliverables.spec: A written note recording per frame what was applied and why it differs from its neighbours, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and actual numeric weight, the explicit statement that the sheet's typography remains the printer's because no font can reach that surface, what the conversion exposed and the mapping decisions taken against it, every export row questioned and its resolution, the compliance strings that will not fit inside the sheet as it stands, and every resize any tool reported. Paired with a persistent approval board carrying the graded range and the licensed frame with nothing silently dropped.

verifiers_auto.text: The press sheet file has exactly one page per current part in export order and renders at 300 ppi at US Letter trim (2550 x 3300 px).
verifiers_auto.how: Count pages in the rendered PDF against the reconciled part count and check the render call's resolution and the output raster dimensions.

verifiers_auto.text: Every spec field, the description, the compliance line and both prices appear on every page of the merged output.
verifiers_auto.how: Round-trip the prepared template to IDML and grep for every expected placeholder, then read text off each rendered page and compare against its export row.

verifiers_auto.text: Every grid tile contains the whole part, and every crop's reported detection confidence and tradeoffs are transcribed in the handover.
verifiers_auto.how: Compare each tile's coverage against its source frame and against an explicit selection's bounds for that SKU; check the handover for the transcribed metadata per crop.

verifiers_auto.text: No delivered file exceeds its source frame on either axis and no crop response carried an upscale entry.
verifiers_auto.how: Compare delivered dimensions against source dimensions and inspect every tradeoffs array.

verifiers_auto.text: The exported Express document holds three canvases at three distinct declared sizes, with the A1 poster at true physical dimensions, every photograph resolved to real image data, the drawing present as path shapes and the comparison present as real table cells.
verifiers_auto.how: Read slide_count and per-slide dimensions from the export response and parse each canvas's returned markup for placeholder images, path-type shapes, table cell structure and out-of-canvas resolved positions.

verifiers_auto.text: Twelve per-part sheet files exist, each named to a part number, each containing the part its name claims.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the part number off each single-page file and compare with its filename, never with its position in the returned list.

verifiers_auto.text: Every text element in the exported document carries a resolved licensed face and the intended numeric weight rather than a fallback.
verifiers_auto.how: Compare the resolved font families and weights in the returned markup against the kit's families and the weights read from the style inventory.

verifiers_auto.text: The approval board exists with the expected item count, carrying the graded range and the licensed context frame, and an empty failed items list after the final call.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the board id and the added and failed arrays from the board responses, comparing addedEntityIds against the expected item count and requiring failedItems to be empty across all placement calls.

verifiers_human.text: Laid out as the catalogue index, the twelve parts read as one range shot the same way on the same day.
verifiers_human.how: View the twelve grid tiles together and judge neutral, white point, black point and subject scale as a set rather than one at a time.

verifiers_human.text: The four finishes remain distinguishable and none has been pushed toward a colour the part is not.
verifiers_human.how: Compare the delivered pictures of galvanised, zinc-plated, clear-anodised and powder-coated parts against the finishes note and against each other.

verifiers_human.text: Through-bores, open frames and enclosed handles are genuinely open in the cutouts.
verifiers_human.how: Place each cutout on a contrasting ground and look through the voids.

verifiers_human.text: The collateral reads flat, accurate and technical rather than consumer or cinematic, appropriate to a 400 to 9,000 dollar part and a twenty-year buyer.
verifiers_human.how: Review the line card, poster and slides against the price band and audience description and reject styled, warm or shallow-depth treatments.

verifiers_human.text: The handover escalates rather than conceals, naming the excluded export row, the compliance strings that will not fit, and the fact that the sheet's typography could not be changed.
verifiers_human.how: Read the handover against the triage, conversion and render findings and check each is disclosed with the decision taken.

decision_gates: The surface split: sheets to the merge surface because the layout is fixed client property and the run is record per page, counter set to HTML authoring because it needs three canvas sizes and must stay editable.
Which session sets the technical white, knowing a warm reference makes plated steel look brassy across the whole catalogue.
How far to correct the second session before the correction itself becomes a finish change the buyer can see.
Whether a subject-aware crop found the part, on frames where the part and the bench are the same metal and the response says success either way.
Subject scale policy across twelve tiles, decided as a set rather than per tile, and re-decided once any tile is derived a different way.
Isolation route per SKU: the one-call knockout is right for a solid body and wrong for a sheave with a bore, and the wrong route returns a filled bore that reports success.
Which of two indistinguishable graphic frames holds the part photograph rather than the dimensional drawing.
Whether to trust the mapping readout of the client's own spec table or to reconstruct the story independently from the document.
Whether a success message counts as verification of the prepared template.
How to honour 'nothing shortened or reworded' when three compliance strings do not fit the sheet as it stands, given no way to change a frame.
Whether to name twelve sheets by the order they came back or by opening each one.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a technical readership, plus the disclosure that no chosen face can reach the printed sheet at all.
Whether the licensed context frame reads as a plausible service environment or as marketing photography, which is the wrong register for a parts catalogue.
why_not_vlm: Paste this brief and these frames into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of machinery. IDENTITY: these are twelve specific parts with specific finishes that a technician orders and installs, and a generated part fabricates a finish, which on a page that also carries load and duty values is effectively a false spec claim. SPEC: the client needs one sheet per current part at US Letter and 300 ppi with fourteen spec values bound verbatim from their own stock export, twelve separately named sheet files each containing the part their filename claims, a grid tile per part showing the whole part, and no delivered file larger than its source. None of that can be produced or checked by generation. EDITABILITY: two deliverables are defined by being editable, a live merge template so next season's specs are a data change, and a native document with live text, a real table and real vector artwork so prices can move in March. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did this placeholder get created, did this crop find the part, is this photograph in the photograph's frame, do these four finishes still read as four finishes. That is not a generation problem.
doability_proof: Every link is verified in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account); the surface count is five and honestly declared, and image_vectorize is not claimed as an Illustrator surface (the genuine Illustrator tools are never called because document_render_vector and document_merge_data_vector sit on a polling helper that does not exist in this host). MERGE SPINE: building a merge template from a bare PDF end to end headlessly is verified, one record per page is confirmed for PDF output, per-record named files are confirmed by two order-verified routes while multi-record raster order is documented as reversed and is therefore never used for identity, and true 300 ppi at US Letter (2550 x 3300) comes from document_render_layout because outputSpecs.resolution on the merge is documented as silently ignored. THE SHEET PDF IS BUILT TO A VERIFIED SHAPE: v3 observed that placed images interleaved with text split the flow into multiple text frames plus graphic frames, and that a continuous flow collapses to a single frame; this asset carries a continuous tab-delimited spec story plus two placed images, so the expected yield is a small number of text frames plus two graphic frames whose only differentiators are bounds and link, exactly as v3 describes them. The PDF must be a real font-embedding press PDF from a full engine, since a thin hand-authored PDF fails conversion opaquely. The lossy-readout defect is verify-then-ship: before admission, run the conversion and the mapping generator and confirm the returned textContent is short by exactly one run against the IDML-reconstructed story; if it will not reproduce, the checkpoint still stands on the granularity fact, which is verified and controllable. THE CROP CHECKPOINT IS A DOCUMENTED LIVE FINDING, NOT AN ASSUMPTION: v3 records that fit extract with a prompt focus silently mis-cropped sparse art to a fragment at detection_confidence 0.459 with detection_source image_select_by_prompt while reporting success, and advises falling back to crop_to_bounds driven by an explicit selection's returnBbox below about 0.6, which is exactly the rework this task encodes. IMAGE BINDING: per-row binding through an at-prefixed column plus additionalImageFiles keyed to bare filenames is verified at three keys; this task binds twelve, so the verified recordRange loop is carried as an explicit fallback and also guarantees per-record identity. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, single_color_saturation, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, select_subject, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs array, remove_background with backgroundColor and fill_area are all verified headless; the enclosed-aperture failure of remove_background, the binary non-anti-aliased mask and the substrate-versus-material prompt asymmetry are documented findings. No upscaling is asserted: crop_and_resize interpolates to a hard 2x cap signalled only in tradeoffs and remove_background silently downscales oversized inputs, so the bar scores the decision and the disclosure separately. EXPRESS: multi-root export with mixed canvas sizes is verified, mm canvases resolve at exactly 96 dpi so A1 and A4 are true physical canvases, tables survive as real tables with per-cell backgrounds and strokes, and inline SVG becomes native editable vector; transport is routed through the text/html upload because inlined photography passes the 70 KB inline threshold, and verification is split because the rendition preview shows page one only. FONTS: the recommend, styles, find, embed chain is verified end to end, and the task leans on the non-standard numeric weights, the slug-not-PostScript rule and the all-or-nothing kit call; the impossibility of getting a font file onto the InDesign surface is stated as a client-facing constraint rather than silently ignored. STOCK AND BOARDS: short generic queries only, licensing returns genuine camera-scale files, board placements are capped at twelve per call with partial success signalled by failedItems. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no variable QR, no bleed gate, no pdfPreset, no fill_text, no animate_design or create_firefly_board, no replace_image, no download_design, no upscaling, no OCR, no compositing, no generated imagery, no photo reaching Express as a URL, and no batch above twenty files.

engagement_title: Summit & Sable marketplace relaunch: pull a field and bench mess of recovery gear to one honest look, give every SKU a compliant plain ground primary that also survives on the charcoal, introduce a second webbing colourway without a reshoot, and stand up the storefront graphics package
vertical: E-commerce and retail: a value band recovery and overlanding gear brand in Boulder, Colorado, relaunching a nine SKU range on a marketplace and on its own storefront
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork post quoted in the ledger for an ongoing e-commerce editor to make existing product photos consistent and to swap colours on specific parts of a product, with the client's own verbatim bar preserved: without ruining the original image, the lighting, shadows and textures must remain completely natural, and sloppy masking, flat colours or unrealistic edits cannot be accepted. The real post names no client, so the brand is laundered to the coined fictional label Summit & Sable and no real marketplace, retailer, person or trademark appears anywhere. Co-anchor: the Freelancer.com Modern Store Graphics Package brief, in which a small online shop refreshing its storefront asked for a hero banner sized for desktop AND mobile, product detail image assets plus iconography, and section and decoration graphics tying the pages together, with clean lines, bold but balanced colour, plenty of negative space, nothing fussy as the stated art direction, and asked explicitly for layered source files PLUS labelled optimised exports so the team can swap copy and images later. That last request is honoured literally here, because the authored source is delivered alongside the editable document rather than in place of it. The storefront platform is laundered to a generic online storefront.
client_one_liner: Our shots are half clean bench packshots and half gritty tailgate frames, the marketplace will not take a primary with anything in the frame, and we are launching a second webbing colour we are not paying to reshoot.
client_brief:
Summit & Sable, spring relaunch

We make recovery straps, soft shackles and overlanding kit. Nine SKUs, thirty five to two hundred and twenty dollars. Our buyer is somebody with a lifted truck and a budget, and he is buying because the gear looks like it works, not because it looks expensive.

Our pictures are two different jobs stapled together. Half are bench packshots on a pale sweep from the day we listed. Half are field frames a friend shot off a tailgate in low sun with dust in the air. Both look fine on their own. Side by side on a page they are two brands. Pull the whole range to one look.

The marketplace primary is the thing that keeps failing us. Nothing in the frame but the product on a plain ground: no logo, no words, no dirt, no scene. Square. Our own storefront is the opposite: there the field frames are what sells, our mark is allowed, and everything sits on our charcoal.

We also want one detail crop per SKU, wide, showing the stitching and the hardware finish, because that is the argument for paying our price instead of the cheap import.

The part we care most about. We are launching the same strap in a second webbing colour, Ridge Blue, and we are not paying to shoot the range again. We have sent a photograph of the spool so you can see the colour. This has to look like a photograph of a blue strap. If the weave goes flat, or the shadow inside the coil goes wrong, or it looks painted on, it is worse than not doing it.

Then the storefront itself: a hero for desktop and a hero for mobile, a set of small spec icons, a band that ties the sections together. Clean lines, bold but balanced, plenty of space, nothing fussy. Send the editable file and the labelled exports so we can swap copy later.

And a note saying what you did to each shot.
price_band_and_audience: Value band recovery and overlanding gear at thirty five to two hundred and twenty dollars, buyer twenty five to fifty, off-road and 4x4 owners buying on rugged credibility and price. The band is load-bearing and it cuts against the obvious instinct: the correct look here is honest, bright, hard-wearing and legible, flat daylight on the primaries and unstyled dust on the secondaries, with type that reads as workwear signage rather than as a lifestyle magazine. The same nine SKUs at a nine hundred dollar premium expedition band would correctly be shot dark and cinematic, low key, warm rim light, heavy blacks, tiny type in a lot of black space, and shipping that treatment here reads as pretending and prices the brand out of its own buyer's search results. Push the other way into hard flash, saturated orange and shouting sale-shaped graphics and it drops below its band into disposable import territory, which is exactly the comparison the detail crops exist to win. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even with every technical gate green. A posted job of this shape runs 800 to 2,000 dollars fixed, or an ongoing retainer.

brand_identity.tagline: Gear that looks like it works.
brand_identity.sector: E-commerce and retail, value-band recovery and overlanding gear
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2019 in Boulder, Colorado. Small owner-run shop, under ten people, selling on a marketplace and its own storefront.
brand_identity.about: We make recovery straps, soft shackles and overlanding kit for people with a lifted truck and a real budget. Nine SKUs from 35 to 220 dollars. Our buyer is not paying for a name, he is paying because the gear looks like it will hold when he is stuck at dusk on a fire road. The detail is the whole argument: the stitching and the hardware finish are what separate us from the cheap import sitting next to us in search results.
brand_identity.audience: Off-road and 4x4 owners aged 25 to 50, buying on rugged credibility and price. They trust flat daylight and visible workmanship and they distrust anything that looks staged or expensive.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Value band, 35 to 220 dollars. The look is bright, hard-wearing and legible, honest daylight on the plain-ground shots and unstyled dust on the field shots. Never premium-expedition cinematic, never discount-banner loud. Either extreme reads as pretending and loses the buyer.
brand_identity.typography: Type should read as workwear signage: a sturdy condensed or grotesque for headlines and spec callouts, a clean neutral text face for body and the range table. Bold but balanced, plenty of negative space, nothing magazine-like.
brand_identity.voice: Blunt and plain. We say what the gear does and what it is rated for. Certified working loads are stated as certified and never rounded or dressed up.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The only brand mark file we can find is a flat screen-size export our old developer left us, plus a photo of the same mark on a woven label. We have no scalable artwork and no written guidelines. Charcoal is our storefront ground and Ridge Blue is the new webbing colour we are introducing. Treat the notes above as direction, not a locked system.
brand_identity.values: Honesty in the picture and the spec. Durability over shine. Fair price for real capability. If an edit would make the product look like something it is not, we would rather it stayed plain.

assets_supplied.name: summit_bench_packshots/ (9 frames, 5472 x 3648)
assets_supplied.kind: Bench packshots, one SKU per frame, pale grey sweep, even studio light, shot the day the range was listed.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The clean ones. Every SKU is in here at least once."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three SKUs are soft shackles and sewn-loop straps whose eyes are genuine holes through the product, and a one-call knockout returns a cutout that looks complete while leaving those eyes filled with the captured sweep, which is invisible against a plain near-white ground and reads as a grey plug the moment the same cutout is placed on the brand's charcoal or over a field frame. The anodised shackle bodies also sit distinctly cooler than everything else on the bench.

assets_supplied.name: summit_field_frames/ (11 frames)
assets_supplied.kind: Field frames shot off a tailgate and on a trail in low sun with dust in the air, gear in use.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The ones that actually sell it. Shot by a friend, late afternoon, dusty."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two frames have the sunlit dust cloud clipped to nothing, so a highlight recovery on them returns an image in which visibly nothing has moved, at full success, and there is no signal distinguishing that from a recovery that worked. The low sun also puts a strong warm cast on the webbing specifically, so the frame-wide correction that fixes the scene pushes the strap colour away from the bench version of the same SKU.

assets_supplied.name: summit_ridge_blue_spool.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Photograph of the new webbing on the spool, sent as the colour reference for the second colourway.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "This is Ridge Blue. This is the colour it has to be."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The new colour sits close to opposite the current webbing on the colour wheel, which is a distance a hue move does not reach; the correction runs, reports success, and returns a flat, desaturated, slightly wrong blue, and pushing it further destroys the weave the client explicitly refuses to lose.

assets_supplied.name: summit_mark_export.png
assets_supplied.kind: A flat screen size export of the brand mark, a wordmark with a small ridge device, supplied as the only mark file the brand can find.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our logo. It is the file our old developer gave us."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is far below the size the desktop hero needs, so it can only be placed by being enlarged unless it is rebuilt as geometry, and what looks like a transparent file is a white card baked in behind the mark, which is invisible until it lands on the charcoal.

assets_supplied.name: summit_label_photo.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Photograph of the same mark screen printed on a woven webbing label sewn to a strap.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The same logo, on our label. Better quality than the file, we think."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Naming the label returns the label rather than the print, and the screen print sits down in the weave so the strokes break up along the warp, which does not show at the size the photograph is viewed at.

assets_supplied.name: summit_range.csv
assets_supplied.kind: One row per SKU: name, working load, webbing width and length, hardware, finish, warranty line, price, and which colourways it ships in.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The range as we list it. The working load numbers are certified, so they cannot be changed or rounded."

acceptance_bar: The client's own bar, verbatim and binding: the lighting, shadows and textures must remain completely natural, and sloppy masking, flat colours or unrealistic edits are rejected outright regardless of what else passes.

The second colourway reads as a photograph of a strap in that colour, with the weave, the shadow inside the coil and the sheen on the webbing all still present and still behaving as one light. A flat area of colour sitting where a strap used to be is a fail even if the hue is right.

Laid together the way a category page lays them, the bench sources and the field sources read as one brand: one white point, one black point, one contrast behaviour, one colour for the same webbing in both.
Every marketplace primary sits on a plain ground with nothing else in the frame at all: no mark, no words, no dirt, no scene, square, at or above the intake minimum.
Where a product has a hole through it, the hole is a hole. Cutouts are judged on the brand charcoal and over a field frame, not only on the plain ground.
No delivered file exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions and no crop record in the run carries an enlargement entry, the mark included. A mark placed at hero size by being enlarged fails.
Each SKU has one wide detail crop that actually contains the stitching and the hardware it is supposed to show, rather than a crop that merely fills the frame.

The mark used on the storefront is placeable scalable artwork with a genuinely transparent ground: a real viewBox present, no opaque full-canvas rectangle riding underneath, and no white card behind it on the charcoal.

The storefront package is one working file carrying the desktop hero, the mobile hero, the two secondary tile canvases and the section band, each keeping its own canvas size, with live retypeable text, every photograph actually present on every canvas, and the spec icons arriving as editable vector rather than as pictures.
The labelled exports are delivered alongside the editable file and the self contained source it was authored from, named so the client can tell which asset is which without opening them.
One type system across every canvas, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the actual weight used.

The note states per source what was applied and how the field treatment differed from the bench treatment, every resize any tool reported, and an honest account of what the second colourway can and cannot be made to do.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, counting image_vectorize here rather than as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_apply_preset, image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_fill_area, image_remove_background (transparent and backgroundColor routes), image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs, detection_confidence, upscale_factor), image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: The whole of the picture work: bringing two source families to one house look a frame at a time, confining the corrections that must not touch the scene, building the second colourway as a masked, region confined move that keeps the weave and the shadow, isolating nine SKUs onto a plain ground including three whose eyes are holes, cutting the square primaries and the wide detail crops without enlarging anything, and rebuilding the brand mark as geometry off the better of the two supplied sources.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The storefront graphics package as one native editable document carrying five roots at five canvas sizes, which is the only surface here that composes free-form fixed canvas layout. The spec icons are authored as inline vector so they arrive editable, every photograph is carried as image data because a reference renders as an empty box at full success, family and weight are declared per text element, and each root declares its own canvas so the desktop and mobile heroes do not collapse to one size.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Fonts
adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: One type system across the heroes, the tiles, the band and the handover. The recommender will not pair for you, so the pairing is the agent's art direction and has to land on workwear legibility at a value band rather than on expedition-brand austerity or sale-shaped shouting. Numeric weights are non-standard per family, names must be laundered into canonical form before the kit call, and the CSS has to use the returned slug or the whole page falls back silently.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock plus Adobe Boards, counted as one surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (entityScope StockAsset, short query, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the one frame the brand does not own, a dust and trail texture for the section band, IP clean and at genuine camera scale with generative-tech candidates excluded, then graded into the house look rather than dropped in as bought. The Boards half persists the selects the client signs off from, placed within the per call cap, a partial result read as partial.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching a pixel.
trajectory.judgement: Primaries, secondaries, detail crops and the colourway are raster work against a hard intake spec; the storefront package has to be authored because the client asked explicitly for a file they can swap copy in later. The brief pins both destinations.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming a surface per deliverable and the confirmed tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role and its SKU.
trajectory.judgement: Twenty sources across two families plus two mark files plus a colour reference; the manifest is what stops a field frame being treated as a bench frame twelve steps later.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by SKU and by source family.

trajectory.action: Preview all twenty frames, both mark files and the spool reference, and triage: which SKUs have both a bench and a field frame, which field frames have lost their highlight entirely, which products have holes through them, how far the new colourway sits from the current webbing, and which mark file is a flat export and which is a photograph of a print.
trajectory.judgement: The two mark files look interchangeable and need opposite treatments, and the two source families need one destination reached by two different routes. Counting files is not the same as reading them.
trajectory.produces: A per frame and per asset triage note, including a first read on how far the colourway has to travel.

trajectory.action: Straighten the field frames shot off the tailgate, before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop, and the wide detail crops have no margin to give away.
trajectory.produces: Levelled field masters, bench frames untouched.

trajectory.action: Fix one house look and bring both families to it one frame at a time, recording the parameters applied, and decide per clipped frame what to do when a recovery returns an image in which nothing has moved.
trajectory.judgement: Bench and field are two lighting worlds and one batched parameter set is exactly wrong for that. Where the highlight is genuinely gone there is nothing to recover, and the honest move is to reframe or to name the frame rather than to keep pushing.
trajectory.produces: Twenty graded masters at source scale with a per frame parameter log and a note on the frames that could not be brought all the way.

trajectory.action: Confine the corrections that break the scene when applied whole-frame, selecting the webbing and the anodised hardware by their own material properties rather than by the product they belong to.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the whole gate: naming the strap pulls the selection to the strap and naming the tailgate pulls it to the truck. The warm cast is on the webbing, not on the picture, so the correction has to be too, or the same SKU ends up two colours across the two families.
trajectory.produces: Corrected frames where a whole-frame move would have cooled the dust or flattened the scene.

trajectory.action: Build the second colourway as a region confined move on the webbing only, judged by eye against the spool photograph and against the weave and coil shadow it must not lose.
trajectory.judgement: This is the deliverable the client says is worth more than the rest of the job, and the client's bar is about naturalness rather than about hue accuracy. Confinement is not optional and neither is looking at the weave afterwards.
trajectory.produces: A second colourway per affected SKU, with the parameters applied recorded, judged beside the reference.

trajectory.action: Isolate the nine bench masters onto the marketplace's plain ground and to transparent variants for the charcoal tiles, reading every returned tradeoff record rather than the success message.
