trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching a pixel.
trajectory.judgement: The month is raster work with a hard no-enlargement rule, the motifs are vector recovery, and the drop set has to be an authored fixed-canvas document because she edits it herself every season and nothing else in the connector composes free-form layout. The piece cards are the one deliverable that is a genuine one-record-per-page run at volume, which only the merge surface does, so they are planned onto InDesign from the start rather than forced into the authored document. The brief pins the destinations, so there is nothing here to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming surface per deliverable, and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline: a manifest keyed by frame and by role, so that forty artefacts later the agent still knows which URL is which frame.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by frame and role.

trajectory.action: Preview all eighteen frames and the glaze swatch reference and triage them: which body shot each, which already carry a heavy in-camera treatment, which are shot into a window, where the subject sits inside each frame, and which frames are the same moment.
trajectory.judgement: Eighteen files is not eighteen posts, and a month shot on two bodies is at least two starting points, not one. The swatch frame is the only fixed reference for what the glazes are, so it is read before any look is chosen rather than after.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note covering source body, existing in-camera treatment, illuminant, subject placement, and moment identity.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level, before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes the subject and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop, and a shelf line or a bench edge running downhill is the loudest tell in a grid.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Set the signature look: read the available looks, try the serious candidates on the two frames that differ most (one phone morning, one camera night), judge them by eye against the glaze reference and against the band, and pick one.
trajectory.judgement: This is the taste decision the whole engagement rests on and it is made on the hardest pair, not the prettiest. A look that flatters window light and crushes the night kitchen is not a look, it is a filter. The applied look cannot be confined to a region, so any frame it cannot serve whole has to be served another way.
trajectory.produces: A chosen signature look with a written justification against the band, and a named list of frames the whole-frame route cannot carry.

trajectory.action: Take the month to that look, one call per frame, and for the frames the whole-frame route cannot carry rebuild the same destination by hand with confined corrections, recording the parameters applied per frame.
trajectory.judgement: The destination is a grid, not eighteen good pictures, so the frames that get there by a different route still have to arrive at the same place. The glazes are the constraint that stops the look running away: whatever is done, the clay has to stay where the swatch frame says it is.
trajectory.produces: The month at one look, at source scale, with a per frame parameter log and a reason line for every frame that took a different route.

trajectory.action: Settle the finishing texture, grain and warmth, at one setting across the set, and judge the whole thing as a nine-tile grid rather than frame by frame.
trajectory.judgement: Grain and warmth are what make a mixed-source month read as one hand, and they are also what tips it into filter territory. The judgement is made at grid scale because that is the only scale at which the client experiences it.
trajectory.produces: A finished look applied consistently, and a first grid read with any frame that still stands out named.

trajectory.action: Cut the square tiles and the taller post crops, reading the returned tradeoff record and detection readings on every crop.
trajectory.judgement: A confident looking crop is not evidence, and the subject of a maker's frame is often the hands or the piece rather than the person. The reference grid is a rhythm instruction, not a size instruction.
trajectory.produces: Square tiles and taller post crops with every returned tradeoff record retained.

trajectory.action: Cut the vertical crops for stories from the same masters, reading every returned tradeoff record and detection reading rather than the success message.
trajectory.judgement: A horizontal frame and a vertical destination is the widest aspect jump in the job, and where the subject sits inside each frame decides whether it can be made at all at native scale.
trajectory.produces: Vertical crops with their tradeoff records retained and any frame that could not be cut cleanly named.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the autumn texture and the one filler frame, filter to photography, exclude generative-tech results, license and download at full resolution, then put them beside the graded month.
trajectory.judgement: The choice is made off a small thumbnail, so it is made on composition and subject rather than on colour, which cannot be judged at that size. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used.
trajectory.produces: Two licensed, IP-clean, camera-scale frames placed beside the graded set.

trajectory.action: Recover the motifs off the sketchbook photograph: an ink-level selection naming the drawing's own visual properties, one motif at a time, correct polarity, a bounds crop from each selection's own returned bounds, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full-canvas ground path removed.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions the tools do not make: how to word each selection so it takes the ink and not the paper, which polarity to trace, and whether to spend three calls per motif rather than one call for the page. Background removal is the wrong instrument on a disjoint line drawing.
trajectory.produces: Three placeable, scalable, transparent motifs, each traced and cleaned.

trajectory.action: Knock three finished pieces to transparency for the partner page, checking the alpha survives the crops that follow.
trajectory.judgement: A glazed stoneware rim against a warm bench is exactly the kind of edge that goes soft, and a soft rim on the one page a brand partner reads is the wrong place to find out.
trajectory.produces: Three transparent piece cutouts with their edges inspected at full size.

trajectory.action: Cut the per-piece card pictures from the graded masters to the card's photo-well proportion, reading every returned tradeoff record, and reconcile them against the piece list including the rows that were never shot this drop.
trajectory.judgement: A blank picture cell is not an error the merge will raise, so what a card with no photograph looks like is decided here rather than found on the printed sheet, and a piece shot only inside a scene has to be cut down to itself without enlarging past the master. The cards reuse one frame across a piece's two sizes exactly as she does.
trajectory.produces: One card picture per photographed piece at or below source scale with its tradeoff record retained, and a stated treatment for the pieces with no photograph.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's, judged against a maker at a 600 to 1,500 dollar retainer and an audience that follows the person. The weight cannot be inferred from a style name, and the collaboration credit is a fixed string that has to sit somewhere without being shrunk into invisibility.
trajectory.produces: A one-kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self-contained HTML with a root per canvas: square, tall, vertical, the nine-tile grid preview and the partner page, each declaring its own canvas size, inlining every photograph as image data, placing each motif as inline SVG inside an explicitly sized top-left anchored wrapper, and setting family and weight on every text element with the captions, the date and the collaboration credit as live text.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto-sized right-anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override is what collapses a mixed-size set. The design work is where the motifs sit and how the two long captions are handled without shrinking the type on those tiles alone.
trajectory.produces: One export-ready HTML carrying the whole drop, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at the first canvas, and parse the returned per-canvas markup for the rest.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition preview only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at canvas one is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document, an inspected first canvas, and a per-canvas markup audit for the others.

trajectory.action: Convert the printer's card template PDF into a working document and export its interchange form, then read what the conversion actually exposes: how many text frames, how many graphic frames, what each holds, and whether a bleed box exists.
trajectory.judgement: What the printed card looks like says nothing about how the file was set: the round glaze dot that reads like a second picture well may be a decorative path, and the name, glaze and price may be one flowing story rather than three fields. This is also where the bleed question is answered honestly rather than claimed.
trajectory.produces: A working template plus a frame inventory, a mapping strategy chosen from it, and the stated bleed reality of the supplied file.

trajectory.action: Reconstruct the card's true story text from the interchange file, compute every field offset from that string, generate and validate the mapping, prepare the template, then re-export and confirm every expected placeholder is present, including the collaboration-credit slot.
trajectory.judgement: Validation returns valid on offsets computed from a shortened mapping readout and preparation reports success either way, so the only evidence a field landed, and in particular that the fixed collaboration credit did not fall off the end of the flowing story, is finding it in the re-exported document.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholders, credit slot included, are confirmed by inspection rather than by a success message.

trajectory.action: Run the piece list against the template binding each row's own cut picture through the prefixed picture column, render the printer's run at 300 ppi at trim with page count equal to row count, produce per-piece proofs for her, and read what each delivered proof actually contains against its own row.
trajectory.judgement: One picture repeated across every card is what a naive run ships, the naming key has to survive the two tumbler sizes that share a name, a blank picture cell must resolve to the deliberate treatment rather than a hole, and a file's position in a returned list is not evidence of which record is inside it.
trajectory.produces: The piece card run plus per-piece proofs, each verified against its row, its price and its glaze.

trajectory.action: Create the selects board, add the delivered set and the licensed frames within the per-call placement cap, re-sending only the entries the response names as failed, then write the look recipe.
trajectory.judgement: A partial success is not a success, and the vector motifs are not boardable so they belong in the recipe instead. The recipe has to be repeatable next month by someone who was not here, which is what a retainer actually buys.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable selects board with nothing silently dropped, and the written look recipe.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether a vertical can be cut from these particular frames at all without either losing the subject or building pixels. On the horizontal frames the subject sits high and hard against one edge on several of them, and where it sits is a property of how each moment was actually shot, not something readable as a problem from the frame. The crop tool answers a vertical request either by emitting a tradeoff that says the crop needs the frame extended first, or by quietly interpolating up to a two times cap and reporting it only as an upscale factor and a tradeoff entry, with a plausible looking result at a plausible size in both cases. Which frames fall into which is only visible after the crop is asked for.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the answer depends on the subject's position in each frame against the destination ratio, and there is no read-ahead and no parameter that prevents the interpolation. Cropping before grading would trade away crop choice for nothing, since the tradeoff still fires. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for the vertical for stories and the acceptance bar's no-enlargement line is a standing trade requirement, not a disclosure that the tool enlarges. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different route decided per frame: recompose the crop off centre so the subject survives at native scale, drop that frame from the vertical set and use another moment, or extend the short axis with the one sanctioned generative call and then re-judge whether the built edge carries the look, which the grading pass never touched.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Read the tradeoff record and the detection reading on every vertical rather than the response, re-plan the crop per frame, and for any frame extended rather than cropped, bring the extended master back through the look pass from the start, because the built pixels were never graded, then re-cut and re-inspect the seam at post scale.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A story set that is soft where every other post is sharp, or verticals that quietly show a shoulder and a wall where the piece used to be, on the format that carries a nine day drop announcement.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether a licensed frame actually sits with the graded month once the two are finally next to each other. Before licensing, the only readout is a 240 pixel thumbnail on a public CDN, which is enough to judge composition and subject and nothing like enough to judge the light, the warmth or how far the frame is from the look the month has just been brought to. The full resolution frame, and therefore its true colour, only exists after the license call, which is a purchase and not a preview. Whether the frame can be brought to the look without being pushed somewhere that makes it read as bought is only answerable with both sitting side by side.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering does not dodge it. Licensing earlier only moves the same purchase earlier, because the graded set has to exist before the comparison means anything, and doing it right first time would mean choosing correctly from a thumbnail that does not carry the information. The orientation filter is dead and long queries return nothing, so the candidate set cannot be narrowed on the qualities that matter either. (b) Nothing states it: the brief never mentions sourced imagery at all, and the client believes she shot the whole month. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is either a second license against a different candidate, which is a fresh cost decision, or a decision to run the partner page and the grid without a bought frame and rebalance the rhythm around what she actually has.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Place the downloaded frames beside the graded tiles at grid scale, judge them as a set rather than alone, and where a frame does not sit, either license a different candidate and repeat the comparison, or drop it and re-plan the nine-tile rhythm and the partner page around the real month, which changes which frames carry which canvases.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A grid whose one bought frame is the only thing anyone notices, on an account whose entire proposition is that it is a real person in a real studio, and a partner page built on a texture that contradicts the look it is meant to be selling.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered motifs survive at the size they actually reproduce. Traced from a photographed sketchbook page they look clean and complete at full canvas, which is the only scale at which anyone has yet seen them. These are monoline brush drawings whose strokes are a few pixels wide at page scale and whose enclosed counters, the gap inside the mug handle and the opening under the kiln arch, are narrower still, so at the size a motif actually sits on a tile the counters can close, thin strokes can merge and the drawing becomes a blob that still reads as clean artwork in any inspection at canvas size. On her warm ground rather than on white it goes further, because the contrast that was carrying the thin strokes is no longer there. Nothing in any tool response reports it.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it. Reproduction size and the real ground colour do not exist until the canvases are composed, and judging a trace at full canvas is the natural and wrong thing to do at every earlier point. There is no parameter on the trace to tune, since it takes no options at all, so it cannot simply be done better the first time. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says she wants the drawings as proper artwork she can put anywhere at any size, which is her goal, not a warning that they fail small, and the acceptance bar sets a standard rather than disclosing an outcome. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the fix is upstream and different: re-prepare the raster so each motif carries more pixels per stroke before tracing, which means a tighter bounds crop per motif rather than one crop of the page, or change the placement, giving the motif more room and less ground contrast to fight, and then re-judge it there.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Look at each motif at its actual placed size on the actual ground rather than at canvas size, re-crop and re-trace the ones that close, clean the viewBox and the opaque ground path again on every new trace, re-check that all three are present rather than two, re-author the HTML around whatever placement size survives, and re-export and re-audit the canvases from the returned markup.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Three hand-drawn marks delivered as artwork she can use anywhere, which turn into dark smudges on every tile and on every label at exactly the size she uses them, on the one deliverable that was supposed to be recognisably her own hand.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether each delivered card proof actually carries its own piece's price and glaze, and whether the fixed collaboration credit survived on the one card it belongs to. The template validates and prepares clean, the run returns success and the right page count, and every card is a valid card, but two things are only visible once the files are opened and read against the roster: the collaboration credit sits at the tail of a flowing story whose offset a mapping computed from the shortened mapping readout lands short of, so it is silently dropped from the Bench Pour-over Set card while every other field looks correct, and a multi-record raster proof route hands the files back in an order that does not match the roster while labelling them by row, so a card named for the Kiln Tumbler can hold the Tall price on the Short piece. The two tumbler sizes sharing a name also collide the instant files are named by piece name alone, and a piece whose picture cell was blank binds nothing unless the deliberate treatment was built in.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter controls it: the credit omission is a property of offsets computed against a shortened readout rather than the reconstructed story, and the proof mislabelling is in the response itself, which is the only thing a run that trusts its tools would use to name the files. Computing offsets from the reconstructed story and choosing a per-record delivery route is exactly the work, not a retry. (b) Nothing states it: the acceptance line that the credit appears verbatim and the requirement that a card carry its own price are standards, not disclosures that the merge drops the credit or reverses the order. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different route: recompute every offset from the reconstructed story so the credit slot lands, and deliver either a single trustworthy multi-page run or a per-record loop so identity is guaranteed, then re-check the two tumbler cards and the pieces with no picture.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Recompute the card's field offsets from the reconstructed story text, re-prepare and re-confirm the credit slot by inspection, abandon any raster proof route whose order cannot be trusted for a per-record or trustworthy multi-page route, rename every proof from what is actually inside it, re-check the two tumbler sizes that share a name so the collision does not overwrite, and confirm the pieces with no photograph carry the deliberate treatment rather than a hole. Where a bound picture is the wrong one or a card picture closes too tight at card scale, re-cut it in Photoshop and re-run, which is a loop back to the imaging surface.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A box of piece cards in which the pour-over set is missing the credit the coffee bar requires exactly as written, and a Kiln Tumbler card that prints the Tall price on the Short piece, discovered by a customer who paid for the piece rather than by Marlo.

deliverables.name: The autumn month at one signature look
deliverables.spec: The month brought to one look across two camera bodies and four lighting situations, with the clay and glaze colours held to the fired swatch reference, plus two licensed camera-scale frames graded into the same world. Per frame parameter log with a reason line for every frame that reached the look by a different route, a named and reasoned cut list, and a moment reconciliation so a burst counts as one post.

deliverables.name: Quill and Kiln motif set
deliverables.spec: Three hand-inked motifs recovered from a photograph of a sketchbook page as placeable scalable vector geometry with a transparent ground: a real viewBox present, no opaque full-canvas rectangle riding along, all three delivered with none quietly missing, each holding its counters and its thin strokes at the size it actually reproduces on a tile and on her warm ground. The identical artwork is reused across every placement rather than redrawn per surface.

deliverables.name: Studio piece cutouts
deliverables.spec: Three finished stoneware pieces knocked to genuine transparency with real alpha at the glazed rim, surviving downstream crops without falling back to a filled rectangle, for the partner page and for reuse on labels. Every output at or below its source pixel dimensions with its returned tradeoff record retained.

deliverables.name: The autumn drop as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: One native editable Express document carrying square, tall and vertical post canvases, the nine-tile grid preview and the partner page, each keeping its own canvas size, with the captions, the drop date and the collaboration credit as live editable text in one licensed type system, the motifs as real vector shapes, and every photograph carried as embedded image data rather than a reference. Delivered with the self-contained source HTML, which is the durable half: she edits the document every drop and the source guarantees the design survives regardless.

deliverables.name: The piece cards as a per-piece merge run
deliverables.spec: The printer's flat card template reverse-engineered into a live InDesign merge template with every placeholder, the collaboration-credit slot included, confirmed present by inspection of the re-exported document, then run against the piece list: the printer's run rendered at 300 ppi at trim with page count equal to catalogue row count in roster order, each card binding its OWN piece picture cut from the graded masters rather than one picture repeated, plus per-piece proofs named from what is actually inside them on a key that survives the two Kiln Tumbler sizes sharing a name, with the fixed collaboration credit appearing verbatim on the one card it belongs to and nowhere else, the pieces with no photograph handled deliberately rather than left as holes, and the bleed reality of the supplied card file reported rather than claimed away.

deliverables.name: Look recipe and selects board
deliverables.spec: A written recipe naming what the look is and how to reach it again next month, what was applied per frame and why that frame differed, every resize any tool reported with the frame it applied to, every frame that was extended rather than cropped, the moment reconciliation and the cut list with reasons, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and actual numeric weight, the minimum size each motif holds at, and what to shoot differently next month, plus the card run's picture-to-piece reconciliation, the pieces with no photograph and how they were handled, and the bleed reality of the supplied card file. Paired with a persistent shareable selects board with nothing silently dropped.

verifiers_auto.text: No delivered file exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions, and no crop tradeoff record in the run carries an upscale entry.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the pixel dimensions of every delivered file against the frame it derives from per the manifest, and diff the captured tradeoff objects against the resize table in the recipe.

verifiers_auto.text: Every frame whose short axis was extended rather than cropped is named in the recipe, and the extended masters were re-graded after extension.
verifiers_auto.how: Cross-check the expand calls in the run against the recipe's extension list and against the order of grading calls per frame.

verifiers_auto.text: Three motif SVGs are delivered, each with a viewBox attribute and no full-canvas opaque background path at path index zero.
verifiers_auto.how: Parse each delivered SVG: assert three files, assert a viewBox is present, and assert the first path's geometry does not span the whole canvas.

verifiers_auto.text: The piece cutouts carry genuine alpha rather than a filled rectangle.
verifiers_auto.how: Inspect the alpha channel of each cutout for partial-alpha pixels at the glazed rim and full transparency at the frame corners.

verifiers_auto.text: The Express export returned the expected number of slides, each keeping its own declared canvas size.
verifiers_auto.how: Read slide_count from the export response and assert it equals the five declared canvases (square, tall, vertical, nine-tile grid preview and partner page); then read each slide's width and height and assert the post canvases carry their own distinct declared sizes (square 1080x1080, tall 1080x1350, vertical 1080x1920, with the grid-preview and partner-page canvases at their own declared sizes) rather than one global size, confirming no canvas override collapsed the mixed-size set.

verifiers_auto.text: No photograph in any canvas resolved to the importer's placeholder, and each motif arrived as vector path shapes rather than as one picture.
verifiers_auto.how: Parse the returned per-slide markup for 1x1 placeholder image data and count path shape elements at each motif placement on each canvas.

verifiers_auto.text: The collaboration credit appears verbatim and unshortened as a text node on every canvas that carries it, and the drop date is text rather than part of an image.
verifiers_auto.how: String-match the exact collaboration-credit string "In collaboration with Fernhollow Coffee. Beans roasted on Alder Street." against the returned markup on each canvas that carries it, asserting it is present verbatim and unshortened, and locate the drop date and time as an editable text node rather than pixels baked into an image.

verifiers_auto.text: Every text element in the exported markup carries a resolved licensed PostScript face rather than a fallback default.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the font-family attribute on every text node in the returned markup and check it against the families the kit call returned.

verifiers_auto.text: The selects board exists with the expected item count and an empty failed-items list after the final call.
verifiers_auto.how: Read boardId, the addedEntityIds array and the failedItems array from the board responses; assert the total addedEntityIds count equals the number of selects the recipe lists as approved (the graded delivered posts plus the two licensed frames), that every add call carried at most 12 placements (the per-call cap) with any overflow split across additional calls, and that failedItems is empty after the final call (a 201 partial-success is read as failure, not success).

verifiers_auto.text: The card merge template's re-exported interchange file contains every expected placeholder including the collaboration-credit slot, and the printer's run page count equals the piece row count.
verifiers_auto.how: Unzip the interchange (IDML) file and grep the story files for each of the five expected field tokens (PIECE_NAME, GLAZE, PRICE, PIECE_PHOTO, COLLAB_CREDIT), including the collaboration-credit slot; then read the merged output's page count and assert it equals the 15 catalogue rows in quillandkiln_pieces.csv (one card per row).

verifiers_auto.text: Every per-piece proof file's name matches the piece name, glaze and price rendered inside it, no two files share a name, and the collaboration credit string appears in exactly one proof.
verifiers_auto.how: Extract the embedded text layer of each proof (delivered as a text-extractable PDF via the PDF / createSeparateFiles / recordRange route, so no OCR is required), match its rendered piece name, glaze and price against the proof's filename and its roster row, list filenames for collisions (in particular the two Kiln Tumbler sizes that share a name), and count occurrences of the exact collaboration-credit string across the run, asserting it appears in exactly one proof.

verifiers_auto.text: Each card's bound picture is the row's own cut picture at or below its source master's pixel dimensions, and the pieces with blank picture cells resolve to the stated treatment rather than a repeated or missing image.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the bound image on each card against the manifest and the CSV picture column, asserting each card's picture is the row's own cut master (not one image repeated) and at or below its source master's pixel dimensions; and confirm the three blank-picture-cell rows (Oat Side Plate, Ember Tumbler, Bench Spoon Rest) resolve to the recipe's stated deliberate treatment rather than a hole or a repeated image.

verifiers_human.text: Seen as nine tiles at grid scale the drop reads as one hand, and still reads as real rooms rather than as a filter pass.
verifiers_human.how: Lay the nine tiles out at grid scale and judge them as a set, then look at three individually for skin, wood and daylight believability.

verifiers_human.text: The clay and the glazes read as the fired swatch frame says they read.
verifiers_human.how: Place the swatch reference beside three graded frames carrying the same glazes and judge the colour relationship.

verifiers_human.text: The delivered posts are distinct moments and every cut frame has a stated reason.
verifiers_human.how: Read the delivered set against the eighteen submitted frames and against the cut list.

verifiers_human.text: The verticals hold their subject and show no seam or softness where a frame was extended.
verifiers_human.how: View each vertical at post scale and then at full resolution along the extended edge.

verifiers_human.text: Each motif still reads as a mug, a sprig and a kiln at the size it actually sits on a tile and on the warm ground, with its counters open.
verifiers_human.how: View each motif at its placed size on the actual ground rather than at canvas size, on tile, vertical and partner page.

verifiers_human.text: The same motif artwork appears everywhere it appears, rather than being redrawn or re-cropped per placement.
verifiers_human.how: Compare the motif at each placement across the exported canvases.

verifiers_human.text: The two long captions are handled without shrinking the type on those tiles alone or pushing text off the canvas.
verifiers_human.how: Open the exported document and look at every caption-bearing canvas in Express.

verifiers_human.text: The work reads as a maker at a 600 to 1,500 dollar retainer, warm and quiet and repeatable, not as an agency campaign and not as untreated phone photographs.
verifiers_human.how: Judge the look, the type scale, the grain and the layout density against the stated band and audience.

verifiers_human.text: The recipe is repeatable next month by someone who was not here.
verifiers_human.how: Read the recipe against the run and check that the look, the per frame reconciliations, the minimum motif size and the shooting guidance are all specific enough to act on.

verifiers_human.text: Every piece card carries its own piece's price and glaze, the collaboration credit is on the pour-over card and nowhere else, and the cards read as the same hand as the rest of the drop.
verifiers_human.how: Read each proof against its roster row starting with the two Kiln Tumbler sizes and the pieces with no photograph, then lay the cards beside the tiles and judge them as one system.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are raster work and which need an authored fixed-canvas document, given that only one surface here composes free-form layout.
Which signature look, chosen on the hardest pair of frames rather than the prettiest, and defended against a band where a heavy uniform filter costs conversion directly.
How to reach the same destination on the frames the whole-frame look cannot serve, since the applied look cannot be confined to a region.
How far the look may move before the glazes stop matching the fired swatch, which is the one thing in the job that cannot be traded.
Whether eighteen files is eighteen posts, and which of the four burst frames is the one that ships.
Which frames to cut entirely, on a client who has said she would rather post fewer, and how to justify each cut.
Crop route per frame for the vertical set: recompose off centre, drop the frame, or extend the short axis with the one sanctioned generative call and re-grade what it built.
Whether to spend three calls per motif on separate ink-level selections or one call on the page, and how to word each selection so it takes the ink and not the paper.
Where and how large the motifs sit, which is a design decision that also decides whether they survive at all.
How to handle two captions that run four times the length of the rest without shrinking the type on those tiles alone.
Whether a licensed frame joins the world the month lives in or reads as bought, judged only once both exist and once a license has already been spent.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged as a maker's hand rather than an agency deck, plus the real numeric weight per family.

Whether the piece cards are a genuine one-record-per-page merge run or another authored canvas, given the printer wants a batch and the card count must equal the catalogue with each card binding its own piece picture cut from the graded masters.

How to compute the card's field offsets, from the reconstructed story text or the shortened mapping readout, so the fixed collaboration credit is not dropped on the one card it belongs to, and which delivery route and naming key carry per-card identity when the two Kiln Tumbler sizes share a name.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the month into a frontier image model and it returns attractive pictures of pottery. IDENTITY: this is her studio, her hands, her market Saturday and her own three inked drawings, and a regenerated frame is a different maker's month; the motifs specifically have to be RECOVERED from her sketchbook rather than reinvented, because a redrawn mug is somebody else's mark. Her glazes are the product, so a generated or drifted colour is a misrepresented 38 to 90 dollar object. SPEC: the deliverable is three post ratios cut from these specific captures with no interpolated pixels, plus a nine-tile grid that has to work as a set, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for; and the piece cards are a one-record-per-page run whose page count must equal the catalogue and whose every card must bind that piece's own price, glaze and picture, which no generated sheet produces or can be verified against. EDITABILITY: the drop set is defined by being editable, because her dates always move and a retainer client cannot re-commission each time. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: can a vertical be cut from this frame at all, does this bought frame sit beside the month, do these counters stay open at the size the motif actually prints.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_preset, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, add_grain, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and detection_confidence, remove_background, generative_expand and vectorize are all verified headless across 27 live calls. The crop checkpoint rests on documented findings: crop_and_resize DOES upscale to a hard 2x cap reporting it only as metadata.upscale_factor plus a tradeoffs entry, and it auto-emits a requires_expand_chain tradeoff with pre-filled expand arguments when a cross-aspect crop would clip the subject; generative_expand is verified live (1024x1024 to 2048x1024, up to 4096 px per side, seeds accepted) and is the sole sanctioned generative call. image_apply_preset is confirmed single-image and NOT maskable, which is exactly why the frames it cannot serve need a hand-built route. The motif checkpoint rests on the verified prompt asymmetry (naming the substrate returned the paper cards at 154,926 px, naming the ink's own visual properties returned the strokes at 9,372 px), the verified partial selection on compound marks, the verified collapse of remove_background on disjoint lettering (1,743 opaque px of ~18,000), and the fact that image_vectorize TAKES NO OPTIONS AT ALL, so all tuning must happen in the raster prep. Vector hygiene is real work: traces come back with NO viewBox and an opaque full-canvas rect at path zero. Alpha survives crops at outputFileType png (13,371 partial-alpha pixels preserved). STOCK: renditionURL is confirmed a 240 px CDN thumbnail, the orientation filter always returns zero hits, long queries return nothing, and asset_license_and_download_stock returned a real 7360x4912 JPEG, which is the whole basis of the licensing checkpoint. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt with its validator, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout with additionalImageFiles and document_render_layout are verified fully headless and synchronous, with one record per page and page count equal to row count, rendered at 300 ppi at trim; the credit-omission checkpoint rests on the verified findings that generate_indd_mapping_prompt returns a SHORTENED story readout so offsets must be computed from the reconstructed story, that prepare_indd_merge_template reports success whether or not a field actually landed, and that the only evidence a placeholder is present is finding it in the re-exported interchange file; the proof-identity checkpoint rests on the verified finding that multi-record PNG and JPEG output comes back REVERSED while the response labels it by row, with PDF, createSeparateFiles and a recordRange loop as the three verified trustworthy routes. PDF-derived frame granularity is not under the agent's control and no bleed can be introduced, so no bleed gate is asserted and the shortfall is reported instead. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, the product is a genuine editable dcx findable by asset_search, and the rendition preview is documented as PAGE 1 ONLY. Transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined photography passes the 70 KB threshold at once. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end. BOARDS: persistence verified with a cap of 12 placements per call and 201 meaning partial. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no upscaling as a deliverable route, no compositing, no OCR, no text-to-image, no photograph reaching Express as a URL, no fill_text, no animate_design, no batch above 20.

engagement_title: Nordhaven direct-booking launch: one committed tone across a two-visit property shoot, amenity cut-outs that hold on the near-black booking page, fourteen room cards merged off last season's printed card, and the lookbook set handed back editable
vertical: Hospitality and travel: a fourteen-room design-led micro-hotel in a converted harbour warehouse, opening its own direct-booking channel after three years of selling only through the large travel platforms
real_brief_anchor: Ledger anchor for PHOTO-22. This id carries an EMPTY real_brief_anchors array in the ledger, so there is no marketplace grounding note to quote and none is invented here. The anchor is the ledger concept itself, quoted verbatim: one_line_ask, 'Give our micro design-hotel a distinctive, moody signature image treatment for the lookbook and social, a single stylized tone that runs across every amenity and detail shot so it looks unmistakably like us and nothing like a generic booking listing'; price_demo, 'A design-led micro-hotel at $600/night for design-literate 30-45 urban travellers who choose on aesthetic; a committed, restrained monochromatic signature is load-bearing.' The verdict is REBUILD because that concept, as banked, ended in one tinted image set plus crops of it, which is one deliverable and one surface. The fuller commission a property in this position actually buys, and the shape these jobs are posted in on the freelance marketplaces (a launch kit rather than a retouch), is the one built here: the signature committed across a shoot that happened on two different visits, the amenity objects cut out for the near-black booking page, the lookbook and social canvases handed back editable because the room list changes, and the desk room-directory cards reprinted off last season's press file against a new rate sheet. The hotel is the fictional Nordhaven, in a converted harbour warehouse; no real property, platform, brand or person is referenced.
client_one_liner: Our pictures sit in a grid next to three hundred other properties and look exactly like them, the shoot happened over two visits that do not match, and every cut-out we have tried looks fine until it goes on the dark booking page.
client_brief:
We are a fourteen-room hotel in a converted harbour warehouse and we open for direct bookings in eleven weeks. Right now every guest reaches us through the large travel platforms, where our pictures sit in a grid next to three hundred other properties and look exactly like them. That is the whole problem. People choose us because of how the building feels, and the pictures carry none of it.

I want one tone. A single committed treatment across every amenity and detail shot, so that when somebody sees three of our pictures anywhere they know they are ours before they read the name. Moody, restrained, a little cold. We are not a bright and cheerful place and I do not want to pretend we are.

There is one exception. The main room photograph on the booking page stays true colour, because a guest spending six hundred a night wants to know what the bed and the linen actually look like. Everything else can carry the tone.

The shoot happened over two visits, one in autumn and one in winter. They do not match. I am told that is normal.

Three things sit on our booking page against a near-black background: the carafe, the robe and the brass key fob. I need those cut out properly. Every attempt we have made looks perfectly fine until it goes on the dark, and then you can see exactly where it was cut.

For the lookbook I need a spread, plus a squarer social version and a full-height story version, and I want those in one file I can edit myself, because the room list changes.

Last thing, the room directory cards on the desks. I have last year's print file and a spreadsheet of the fourteen rooms with the new rates and views. Same card, new content, ready for the printer.

What I need back: the finished set, the cut-outs, the lookbook file, the room cards, a board my partner can review, and a note on what you did.
price_band_and_audience: Design-led micro-hotel, six hundred dollars a night, sold direct to design-literate 30 to 45 urban travellers who choose a property on aesthetic and book it because it looks like nowhere else. The band is load-bearing on nearly every decision in the job. At this level a committed, restrained, near-monochromatic signature is the product: the guest is buying atmosphere and a point of view, so the treatment has to be strong enough to survive being seen three pictures at a time in someone's feed. Run the same commission for a one hundred and twenty dollar highway property and every choice inverts: that booker needs bright, literal, reassuring colour and a clear picture of the bed, and this moody tint would actively lose them. The band also decides where the tone stops. The one true-colour room hero exists because a guest paying this much wants to see the actual linen, and an agent that tints it for consistency has followed the pattern and broken the commission. The same restraint governs the collateral: air, one photograph doing the work, type that does not shout, rates set quietly rather than as offers. Cheerful, saturated, discount-shaped design at this price reads as a property pretending to be something it is not. The ledger records the base treatment at 400 to 900 dollars; this full launch commission, with the cut-outs, the editable canvases and the fourteen-record card run, sits at 1,400 to 2,600 dollars fixed.

Guests choose us because the place looks like nowhere else, and everything we make has to carry that.
brand_identity.audience: Design-literate urban travellers, 30 to 45, who choose a property on aesthetic and book direct once they trust the point of view.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Six hundred dollars a night, direct only, positioned above the travel-platform grid as a design destination rather than a room count.
brand_identity.typography: A quiet high-contrast serif for display, set large and used sparingly, with a clean neutral grotesque for text. Nothing shouts, and rates sit small.
brand_identity.voice: Spare, understated, first person, no exclamation. Example line: 'Fourteen rooms on the water. We open direct booking this autumn.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: We work from a short brand note that fixes the near-black ground, the placements and the delivered sizes. There is no full guideline system yet, and the room list changes each season.

assets_supplied.name: nordhaven_property_shoot/ (16 frames, 4,200 to 5,000px long edge)
assets_supplied.kind: image
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Amenity and detail shots plus the rooms, from two visits, one in autumn and one in winter. They do not match." Bath and bedside details, the breakfast counter, the stair, the harbour window, plus one full-frame room.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two things nobody in the hotel can see. First, two of the detail frames separate their subject from their ground almost entirely by hue rather than by value (a moss-green wool throw lying on an oak-grey bench, a terracotta cup on a rust-red tray), so any single tone ramp collapses both of them into one flat field, while each still looks plausible on its own at thumbnail size. Second, the winter visit was shot after the blinds were replaced, so those six frames sit a step darker in the shadows than the autumn ones and plug solid once a tint is committed on top of an uncorrected base.

assets_supplied.name: nordhaven_amenity_objects/ (3 frames, 4,600px)
assets_supplied.kind: image
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The carafe, the folded robe and the brass key fob, shot on our own surfaces so they would look at home." One object per frame, styled on the hotel's plaster and oak.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The unglazed carafe is photographed against the hotel's own limewashed plaster and its shadow side sits at almost exactly the plaster's value, so an automatic knockout succeeds, returns a clean-looking file, and quietly bites the lip and the shoulder away on that side. The key fob is the opposite problem: its plate carries an enclosed cut-out letterform that a background removal cannot punch at all, so that route returns the hole filled with captured oak while reporting success.

assets_supplied.name: nordhaven_room_card_2025.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: document

assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two things the printed page does not reveal. The card's copy was set around the shortest room name the hotel had last year, so the name frame has very little slack at the merged type size, and InDesign does not spill an over-long merged record, it simply stops rendering it at the frame edge with no warning anywhere. And the four visual blocks on the printed card do not correspond to four converted frames: the conversion's real granularity is a property of how the PDF was drawn, not of how the card looks.

The rate column is also inconsistently typed across the rows, which is a copy decision the agent has to make rather than a defect any tool reports.

acceptance_bar: The tinted set reads as one committed treatment seen three pictures at a time, with no frame jumping against its neighbours and no frame collapsing into a flat field.
The two visits are indistinguishable in the finished set. Nothing gives away that the shoot happened twice.
The one true-colour room hero for the booking page is delivered untinted, and nothing else in the set is.

The three amenity cut-outs hold their edges on the near-black ground the booking page uses, judged on that ground and not on white, with nothing bitten out of an edge and no enclosed interior left filled.
No invented pixels anywhere. No delivered file exceeds its source dimensions, and the note lists every picture any tool resized, downscaled or extended, and by how much.
Every crop is composed for the size it is actually used at rather than scaled down from one master.
The lookbook spread, the social canvas and the story canvas sit in ONE editable file, each keeping its own canvas size, delivered with the self-contained source it was built from.
The words in that file are live text the client can retype, and every photograph in it is a real photograph rather than an empty frame.
One type system across all three canvases, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the weight actually used.
Fourteen room cards, one record per page, in the printer's order, every card carrying the correct room's photograph rather than one image repeated.
Every field on every card is fully present at trim. No name, view line or rate is cut off, and nothing that was mapped is silently missing.
Anything licensed sits with the property's own photography rather than reading as a bought picture.
The board carries the finished set with nothing silently dropped.
The note states, per frame, what was applied, and names any frame that could not be brought into the set and what happened to the placement it was carrying.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle what lands where: the pictures and the cut-outs on imaging, the three canvases on HTML authoring, the fourteen cards on the merge path.
trajectory.judgement: The temptation is to read this as a tint job with some crops attached. The real structure is that two of the five deliverables are defined by a surface they must survive (a near-black ground, a printed trim) rather than by a look.
trajectory.produces: A plan naming deliverable to surface and the confirmed tier.

trajectory.action: Upload the sixteen shoot frames, the three object frames, last season's card PDF and the room sheet, holding a manifest with source dimensions.
trajectory.judgement: Source dimensions are recorded here because every no-invented-pixels claim later is made against them.
trajectory.produces: A manifest with source dimensions and a presigned URL per file.

trajectory.action: Preview all nineteen frames and triage: which visit each came from, how each frame's subject separates from its ground, how much room sits around the subject, and which single frame is the true-colour booking hero that must be held out of the treatment.
trajectory.judgement: Identifying the exception before committing to the signature. The brief names it in one sentence in the middle of a paragraph about tone, and an agent working from the headline ask will tint all sixteen.
trajectory.produces: A per-frame triage note and the named exception.

trajectory.action: Straighten where needed and bring both visits onto one base: correct exposure, neutral and shadow depth per frame so autumn and winter start from the same place, one call per frame, recording parameters.
trajectory.judgement: A tint applied on top of two different bases produces two different results from one setting. The correction has to happen before the style, and the two halves need different corrections to arrive at the same base.
trajectory.produces: Nineteen corrected frames on one base with a per-frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Masked work where a whole-frame move is wrong: correct plaster, oak and linen separately by naming the material rather than the object sitting on it.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the entire gate here. Naming the substrate returns the substrate; naming a material's own visual properties returns the material. Plaster and oak want opposite moves that cannot both be served globally.
trajectory.produces: Corrected frames where a global move would have taken the plaster green or the oak grey.

trajectory.action: Commit the signature: choose the tint hue, the tint strength and the grain, apply across the set one frame at a time, and hold the booking hero out of it entirely.
trajectory.judgement: How far the tone goes is the design decision the whole engagement turns on, and at this band it is a question of restraint rather than of strength. Batching one identical parameter set across frames that arrived from two visits is the fast answer and it is the wrong one.
trajectory.produces: A tinted and grained master set plus one untinted true-colour hero, with applied settings recorded.

trajectory.action: Lay the tinted set out together at lookbook reproduction size and look across it rather than at each file in turn.
trajectory.judgement: Deciding to view the set as a set is the agent's own move; nothing prompts it, and every individual file looks correct.
trajectory.produces: A verdict on the set as a set.

trajectory.action: Take the three amenity objects to transparency, choosing a route per object rather than a route for the batch, and produce the near-black composited versions the booking page needs.
trajectory.judgement: The three objects look like one job and are not. An object whose plate carries an enclosed cut-out cannot be knocked out by background removal at all, and the correct route for it is to select the ground material, invert and fill, which is a different operation on a different principle.
trajectory.produces: Three transparent cut-outs plus their composited-on-black versions.

trajectory.action: Composite each cut-out onto the exact near-black ground the booking page uses and inspect the edges close up.
trajectory.judgement: This is the only place the edges can be judged. Both failure modes are invisible on white, which is precisely why every attempt the hotel made looked fine to them.
trajectory.produces: An edge verdict per object on the ground that matters.

trajectory.action: Search Stock with short generic queries for a night harbour or warehouse exterior, filter to photography, exclude generative results, license and download at full resolution, then bring it toward the committed tone and lay it beside the set.
trajectory.judgement: Under a committed single tone what decides whether a licensed frame joins is its luminance structure and its black point, not its colour, and a 240 pixel thumbnail carries evidence about neither.
trajectory.produces: One licensed camera-scale exterior, tinted to the set and judged against it.

trajectory.action: Compose the placement crops: the lookbook spread ratio, the 4:5 social and the 9:16 story, each framed for the size it is used at, reading each crop's tradeoff metadata and extending a frame at its edges rather than interpolating where a placement needs more room than the frame holds.
trajectory.judgement: A spread and a story are not one crop scaled. The tradeoffs array is the only signal that a crop interpolated, and adding edge material is the only route that does not invent detail inside the frame.
trajectory.produces: Composed crops per placement with a resize and extension record.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, read the family style inventories for real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to read at six hundred a night. Weight cannot be inferred from a style name, a display cut is reached by its own family slug, and one bad name in the kit call discards the valid ones with it.
trajectory.produces: A one-kit type system with family, foundry or designer and real weight per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self-contained HTML with three roots at three canvas sizes: the lookbook spread, the 4:5 social and the 9:16 story. Embed every photograph as image data, anchor every element from the top left with explicit sizes, and declare family and weight on every text element.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph on this importer, weight is not inherited from markup semantics, and a global canvas override collapses a mixed-size set. The design work is how much air each canvas carries at this band.
trajectory.produces: One export-ready HTML carrying all three canvases, uploaded and addressable, retained as a deliverable in its own right.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export, then verify through both channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at the first canvas, and parse the returned per-canvas markup for the other two, asserting per canvas that every photograph resolved to real image data, that the type resolved to the licensed faces, and that nothing sits beyond its declared canvas width.
trajectory.judgement: Treating a successful export as unverified. Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition only ever shows the first canvas.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document with three canvases, an inspected first canvas and a markup audit of the other two.

trajectory.action: Convert last season's card PDF to a live document, export IDML, and actually look at what came back: how many text frames exist, what each one holds, and whether the story text the mapping readout reports matches the story the document contains.
trajectory.judgement: The printed card shows four separate blocks, which is not evidence about frames. What the conversion exposes decides whether per-frame mapping is available at all or whether everything has to be done by offset inside one story, and that determines the entire mapping strategy.
trajectory.produces: A true frame inventory and a reconstructed story text.

trajectory.action: Build the mapping against the reconstructed story, validate it, prepare the merge template, then re-export IDML and confirm every expected placeholder is genuinely present rather than trusting the success message.
trajectory.judgement: Both the validator and the prepare step report success on mappings that never landed, so the only evidence that a field exists in the template is the field itself in the round-tripped document.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholders have been confirmed present.

trajectory.action: Merge all fourteen records one per page with each room's own photograph bound through the image column and the agent's own tinted frames supplied as the image files, render for the printer, and then look at every card at trim.
trajectory.judgement: Page count equals row count on a run where fields are missing and copy is cut off, so counting pages proves nothing. Looking at all fourteen rather than the first is the agent's own decision.
trajectory.produces: A fourteen-page press file plus per-record files, and a verdict on every card.

trajectory.action: Create the board and add the finished set for the client's partner, treating a partial success as partial. Then write the note: per frame what was applied, the tint hue, strength and grain, the exception held out of the treatment, the type system, anything licensed, every resize or extension reported, and any frame that could not be brought into the set.
trajectory.judgement: What to escalate rather than quietly fix. A frame dropped from the set changes which picture carries which page, and the client needs to hear that from the freelancer rather than find it.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the committed tone actually does to this particular set. A single tone ramp maps every colour in a frame onto one hue, so any frame whose subject is told apart from its ground by hue rather than by value loses that separation completely. Two of these detail frames are exactly that case (a moss-green throw on an oak-grey bench, a terracotta cup on a rust-red tray) and both collapse into one flat field. Nothing in either photograph announces it: they look like ordinary detail shots, they look correct in colour, the tint operation reports success, and each tinted file still reads as plausibly moody on its own at thumbnail size. The collapse only exists as a comparison against the rest of the set at reproduction size. The strength that carries the other frames is also the strength that kills these two, so there is no single setting that resolves it.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it and care cannot pre-empt it: which frames depend on hue for separation is a property of what was in the room that day, and it cannot be read off a colour preview, since in colour both frames separate perfectly well. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for one tone across every amenity and detail shot and names the single true-colour exception it already knows about; it says nothing about any frame failing, and no asset note or earlier step identifies these two. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is to go back before the tint and build luminance separation that was never there, by lifting or dropping one side under a mask, or to accept that these two frames are not treatable and change which frames carry which pages.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Return to the corrected base for those frames and separate subject from ground by value under a mask before re-committing the tone, then re-tint and look at the set again rather than assuming the second attempt took. Check the frames that were not flagged at the same reproduction size, since the reason to look was found on two frames and the rest have not been established as clean. If a frame will not separate without looking manipulated, drop it and re-plan the lookbook around the frames that survive.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The lookbook opens on two grey mush frames in the middle of a set that is supposed to be the property's entire point of difference, and they go out on the social canvases as well, in front of exactly the design-literate booker the direct-booking channel was built to reach.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the cut-outs hold where they are actually used. The carafe is unglazed and was styled against the hotel's own limewashed plaster, so on its shadow side the object and the ground sit at effectively the same value. The knockout succeeds, returns a clean-looking transparent file, and has quietly taken the lip and part of the shoulder with it. On white and on any pale layout that missing edge is invisible, because what is gone was pale anyway; on the near-black booking ground it reads as a bite out of the silhouette. Which of the three objects does this, and how far the bite runs, is a property of the styling in that one photograph rather than of the route chosen or the care taken, and no tool reports edge quality at all.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it: the cut-outs have to be made regardless of sequence, there is no metadata that describes an edge, and the defect does not exist in the returned file in isolation, only in relation to the ground it is composited on. (b) Nothing states it. The client says every version they tried looks fine until it goes on the dark, which is a client describing the symptom that made them hire somebody, not a statement of which object, why, or that the cause is a shared value on one side. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the fix is a different operation on a different principle, selecting the plaster as a material and inverting rather than asking for the object, and it carries a further decision about whether the object needs restyling advice back to the client rather than a cut.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-cut the affected object by naming the ground material and inverting rather than by asking for the subject, re-composite on the near-black ground and inspect the same edge again rather than assuming the second route worked, and inspect the other two objects at the same magnification, since one object having been caught is not evidence about the others. If an edge cannot be recovered, say so and propose the object be reshot on a ground that separates, rather than shipping a bitten silhouette.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The booking page, the one page the entire launch exists to convert on, carries a carafe with a chunk missing from its side, which is the precise defect the client hired someone to fix, handed back as fixed.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the fourteen merged cards are actually complete at trim. Last season's card was set around the shortest room name the hotel had, and three rooms were renamed this season with longer names and longer view lines. A merged record that exceeds its frame does not spill, does not wrap onto the card and does not raise anything: it simply stops rendering at the frame edge, so the card comes back looking like a properly composed card that happens to name a room slightly differently. Every automatic signal passes: the merge reports success, the page count equals the row count, the pages are in the printer's order and each card carries the correct room photograph. The frame's true capacity at the merged type size is not published anywhere and cannot be computed from the printed card, so the only way to know is to merge and look at all fourteen.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it and care cannot pre-empt it: capacity depends on the frame geometry the conversion produced and the type size the template carries, neither of which is knowable before the merge exists, and comparing string lengths against last year's copy gives no threshold. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the room list changes and hands over a spreadsheet with the new rates and views, which is a client describing their content, not disclosing that three records overrun. No asset note in the client's hands names the rooms and no acceptance line explains the cause. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is a decision the client has to be involved in, shorten the copy, move the long field to a frame that can hold it, or change the type treatment on the card, and each of those changes the mapping and the design rather than repeating an operation on changed input.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Identify which records are cut, decide with the copy in hand whether the fix is an editorial shortening, a re-mapping so the long field lands in a frame with slack, or a type change on the card, then rebuild the mapping, re-confirm the placeholders in the round-tripped document, re-merge and look at all fourteen again rather than only the three that were caught.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Fourteen room cards go to the printer and sit on the desks of a hotel that charges six hundred a night with three of them naming the room half way through a word, discovered by guests rather than by anyone at the hotel.
