trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching a pixel.
trajectory.judgement: The site specification is a list of destinations, and the client wants them all in one file they can return to. That is an authored fixed-canvas document, not a folder of exports, and nothing else in the connector composes free-form layout. The brief already pins it, so there is nothing here to stall on. The grocer shelf cards are the opposite shape, one printed card per store at volume off a spreadsheet, which is a one record per page merge rather than authored layout and lands on a different surface entirely.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming the surface per deliverable, the split between the authored family and the merged shelf-talker run, and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload the two packshots, the shortlist screengrab, the brand note, the copy, the site specification, the card printer's shelf-talker press PDF and the stockist list through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline, plus a manifest that will later have to carry licensed frames alongside supplied ones because the co-packer has to be shown where every picture came from, and the press PDF and the stockist list are the raw material of the shelf-talker merge that comes later.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role, opened as the licensing record.

trajectory.action: Preview the two packshots and read the brand note against them, reconcile the copy's three flavours against the two photographs, and read the stockist list's featured-flavour column against the same two photographs.
trajectory.judgement: The note points at a swatch card nobody sent, so the only statement of the house green left standing is the label in these two files, and these two files have already been retouched by someone else. The third flavour is the one the founders want featured and it does not exist as a photograph, which is a limitation to name now rather than to paper over later, and several stockists lead with exactly that flavour, so the merge will demand a card for a can that was never shot.
trajectory.produces: A written position on where the house green actually lives, a note on the crushed sweep, and the flavour-to-photograph reconciliation across both the copy and the stockist list.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for summer lifestyle candidates, filter to photography, read isGenTech and true dimensions on every result, and build a shortlist wider than the founders' six.
trajectory.judgement: Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used. The founders' six are thumbnails and two of them are machine generated, which their own instruction excludes, so the shortlist has to be rebuilt on evidence the thumbnails do not carry.
trajectory.produces: A candidate list with asset id, true camera-scale dimensions and generative status per frame.

trajectory.action: License and download the shortlist at full resolution immediately, then look at the actual frames properly against the two packshots.
trajectory.judgement: The download link expires within the hour, so pulling at once is the only safe order. Re-calling the licence tool refreshes the link without consuming a second licence, which is what makes a later revision affordable.
trajectory.produces: Full resolution licensed frames on disk with their licence state recorded, and a first honest look at what was actually bought.

trajectory.action: Fix one warm daylight target off the strongest licensed frame and bring the rest of the family toward it with a call per frame, recording the parameters applied.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a set, not a stack of good pictures, and it has to be reachable by both a licensed outdoor frame and a studio packshot on white without either one having to be pushed somewhere it cannot go. One batched call applies one parameter set, which is exactly wrong for frames shot on different days under different skies.
trajectory.produces: A graded family at source scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Confined corrections where a global move would take the label green with it, selecting by the material's own colour rather than by the object it sits on.
trajectory.judgement: The house green is the one colour in the package that cannot drift, and it lives on a small painted surface inside frames whose surroundings need the very moves that would shift it. Naming the can pulls the mask onto the can and the table; naming the printed colour and finish takes the label.
trajectory.produces: Corrected frames where a whole-frame move would have taken the brand colour off its own statement.

trajectory.action: Knock the cans out: genuine transparency for the sign up spot and the banner, plus a house-ground variant, reading every returned tradeoffs object and inspecting each cutout on a colour rather than on white.
trajectory.judgement: White ground hides exactly the failure this packshot is set up for, because the sweep was crushed before the file arrived and the base rim has nothing left to separate it. The inspection ground has to be the destination's, not the studio's.
trajectory.produces: Transparent can cutouts and house-ground variants with their returned tradeoffs recorded.

trajectory.action: Cut every destination in the site specification, subject aware, reading detection confidence and every tradeoff entry, and never letting a crop reach its size by enlargement.
trajectory.judgement: Two narrow section headers, a square, a tall and a banner are five different ways of losing the subject. The crop tool will interpolate up to a cap while saying so only inside its own tradeoffs, so the response has to be read rather than the success line.
trajectory.produces: Destination crops at spec, each at or below its source scale, with the tradeoff record per cut.

trajectory.action: Handle the home page band, which is far wider than any frame can be cut to: make the single sanctioned generative call with a recorded seed to build new edge on the chosen side, then re-cut the band from the expanded frame.
trajectory.judgement: Which side to grow, and how far, is a picture decision rather than a parameter, and it is the only generative call available in the whole engagement, so it has to be spent where nothing else reaches. The manufactured edge has to be able to hold the same daylight as the rest of the frame.
trajectory.produces: An expanded master with its seed recorded, and the home page band cut from it.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical PostScript form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged against a three dollar fifty craft band and a natural grocer shopper rather than against a wellness brand or a mass soda. The weight cannot be inferred from a style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one-kit type system with family, foundry and actual numeric weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self-contained HTML with a root per destination at its own canvas size, inline every photograph and every cutout as image data, declare family and weight on every text element, and keep the featured flavour in its own swappable position.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, a global canvas override is what collapses a mixed-size set, and the design work is how much air a restrained craft band takes at a wide band, a narrow header and a tall social frame, which are three genuinely different problems.
trajectory.produces: One export-ready HTML carrying the whole family, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Upload the HTML, run the readiness check, export by URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at canvas one, and parse the returned per-canvas markup for every other canvas.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition preview only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at the home page band is not looking at the section headers.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document, an inspected first canvas, and a per-canvas markup audit for the rest.

trajectory.action: Convert the card printer's flat shelf-talker press PDF into a working document and export its interchange form, then read what the conversion actually exposes: how many text frames, how many picture frames, what each holds, and whether a bleed box exists at all.
trajectory.judgement: What the printed card looks like says nothing about how it was set. The five tidy stacked fields may be one flowing story sitting beside a decorative tag, the amber price flag may not be a field at all, and the single picture frame at the top is the only place a can can bind. This is also where the bleed question is answered honestly rather than assumed.
trajectory.produces: A working template plus a frame inventory, a mapping strategy chosen from it, and a stated bleed finding.

trajectory.action: Reconstruct the document's true story text from the interchange file, compute every field offset from that string, generate and validate the mapping for STORE_NAME, TOWN, FEATURED_FLAVOUR, SHELF_PRICE and the CAN_IMAGE frame, prepare the template, then re-export and confirm every expected placeholder is actually present.
trajectory.judgement: Validation returns valid on offsets computed from whatever string it was handed and preparation reports success either way, so the only evidence a field landed is finding it in the re-exported document. The price has to resolve to its own small story rather than to the decorative flag, and the flavour mapping has to survive the row that spells it with the word and.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholders are confirmed by inspection rather than by a success message.

trajectory.action: Loop back to imaging to cut the featured-flavour can pictures from the graded can cutouts to the card's own picture-frame proportion, one per flavour that has a photograph, and settle what the spruce-tip stores' cards carry given no packshot exists for that flavour.
trajectory.judgement: The card's picture well is a different proportion from the sign up spot and the banner, so the cutouts cannot simply be reused, and cutting them here rather than letting the merge fit them is what keeps the base rim intact on the card's cream ground. The spruce tip has no photograph and inventing one is not available, so its stores' cards are a deliberate photograph-less variant named as such rather than a blank the merge will silently fill with the row above.
trajectory.produces: Per-flavour card pictures at the picture-frame proportion, and a stated treatment for the spruce-tip stores that have none.

trajectory.action: Run the stockist list against the template binding each row's own featured-flavour can, produce the printer's run and per-store proofs at 300 ppi at trim, and read what each delivered proof actually contains against its own row.
trajectory.judgement: One can repeated across every card is what a naive run ships, a blank picture cell silently rides the previous row's can into a spruce-tip store, the naming key has to survive two stores sharing a name, and a file's position in a returned raster list is not evidence of which store is inside it.
trajectory.produces: The stockist shelf-talker run plus per-store proofs, each verified against its row.

trajectory.action: Create the shortlist board, add the licensed frames and the graded heroes within the per-call placement cap, re-sending only the entries the response names as failed.
trajectory.judgement: A partial success comes back as a success code, so the failed list is the only part of the response worth reading, and vector is not boardable so anything vector belongs in the note instead.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board the two founders can sign off from, with nothing silently dropped.

trajectory.action: Write the style reference and the licensing manifest: colours as they actually exist on the delivered artwork, type by role with family, foundry and real weight, the grading recipe per picture, every licensed asset id with its licence state and its generative status, the shelf-talker merge template with its per-store naming key and its no-bleed shortfall, the treatment of the spruce-tip stores that have no can, and everything that could not be delivered.
trajectory.judgement: This is the deliverable the client asked for by name and the one that keeps the family cohesive after the freelancer leaves. It has to be specific enough to hire against, including the flavour with no photograph and any edge that was manufactured rather than shot, and it has to tell the card printer what the shelf-talker file can and cannot carry to press.
trajectory.produces: The written style reference and the source manifest the co-packer can be shown.

trajectory.action: Package the whole family: the graded set, the cutouts, the editable document, the source HTML, the stockist shelf-talker run and the reference, checked once against the site specification destination by destination and the stockist run store by store.
trajectory.judgement: The specification is a list and the family is a family, and the last honest act is to confirm that every destination has an asset at its stated size, that every store has a card carrying its own row, and that the set still reads as one piece of work when all of it is laid out together.
trajectory.produces: The delivered package with a destination-by-destination and store-by-store check recorded.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether a licensed frame actually sits with the graded set. Everything supplied about the candidates is a 240 pixel content-delivery thumbnail, which is a re-encode small enough that light direction, cast and the real behaviour of a scene's colour are not present in it. A frame whose thumbnail reads as even warm daylight can turn out at full size to be carrying a heavy foliage bounce that lays green over skin, cloth and tabletop alike, and reconciling that to the warm daylight target takes exactly the moves that also pull the house green off the label. Whether any particular licensed frame can be brought to the set at all only exists as a fact once it has been licensed, downloaded at full resolution, graded and put next to the two packshots.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the full resolution file is only obtainable by licensing and the thumbnail is the only thing that exists beforehand. Doing it right first time presumes being able to read a cast off a 240 pixel re-encode, which is not a skill any tool provides and not information the search response carries. Nothing states it: the founders supply their six as a preference, and the acceptance line about one afternoon is their art direction rather than a disclosure. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a fresh search, a different licence and a different frame, not the same chain again.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-search with different short queries, license and pull replacement candidates at full resolution, re-grade the family around whichever frames can actually reach the target, re-cut every destination that depended on a rejected frame, and record in the manifest which frames were licensed and rejected and why.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A summer family in which the hero is quietly green under the warmth, the cans in it no longer match the cans in the sign up spot, and the one colour the brand actually owns is different on two adjacent pieces of the same page.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the sky in the chosen lifestyle frame will actually do. A summer outdoor frame commonly arrives with the bright band already at the top of its range from the original capture, and the natural response is highlight recovery. What comes back is a successful call and a picture that is, where it matters, identical: the readout is that nothing moves, because there is nothing left in that band to move. There is no warning, no error and no diagnostic that distinguishes this from a correction that simply was not strong enough, so the obvious next reaction is to push the same control further and get the same nothing while dragging the rest of the frame down with it. Whether this frame is recoverable, or whether the bright band has to be composed around instead, is only knowable by making the call and looking.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the frame has to be graded before anything can be said about it and no parameter reports headroom. Doing it right first time presumes knowing in advance which of the licensed candidates lost that band at capture, which nothing in the search response, the thumbnail or the file discloses. Nothing states it: the brief asks for sun lit and warm. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a compositional decision, re-framing every crop so the dead band falls outside it, or replacing the frame, rather than repeating the same call.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Stop pushing the control, re-plan the crops for every destination so the unrecoverable band sits outside the frame, which collides directly with the home page band's ratio and may force a different expansion side or a different frame entirely, then re-grade and re-cut and record the limitation in the recipe.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A hero band and two section headers carrying a flat white void where the summer sky should be, with the rest of the frame dragged dull by repeated attempts to fix it, on a brand whose entire premium rests on looking like real daylight.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the device that makes the section headers read as one family with the hero. Two narrow headers sitting over photography with type on them need the brand colour carried across the picture, and the natural authoring construction for that is a colour layer set to blend with the image beneath it. The importer discards the blend entirely and renders the element as a plain opaque shape, which means the colour layer stops sitting in the photograph and starts sitting on top of it, covering it, at full success with no warning of any kind. The document's own rendition returns the first artboard only, so the home page band looks correct in the only picture available and the section headers, the sign up spot and the social canvases can be checked through no channel other than the returned per-canvas markup.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the normalisation happens at import and the import is the last step. Doing it right first time presumes knowing which of several equally standard constructions survives, which nothing reports and no checklist enumerates. Nothing states it: the brief asks for one cohesive family and the acceptance line about the colour surviving onto every canvas is the client's requirement, not a warning. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different construction, carrying the colour in the raster itself, or rebuilding the header as a solid panel beside the photograph rather than over it, and then re-composing each canvas around whichever it is.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Move the colour treatment upstream into the graded rasters or re-cast the headers so the colour and the photograph do not overlap, re-author the HTML around that decision, re-upload, re-run the readiness check, re-export, and audit every canvas from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A site family delivered as an editable file in which the two section headers and the sign up spot are flat blocks of green with the photography completely hidden underneath them, on canvases nobody looked at, with the export having reported success throughout.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether each delivered shelf-talker proof actually contains the store its filename claims and the right flavour's can. The natural way to hand the card printer and the founders a proof per store is a multi-record raster run, and the tool's own description says one output file per row and hands back a list labelled by row number. The labels are not trustworthy: the raster files come back in an order that does not match the roster, the two Hollow Root Market rows at two different towns collide the moment a file is named by store, and a spruce-tip store whose picture cell is blank silently carries the previous row's elderflower or rhubarb can. Every gate above passes, the count is right and each file is a valid card, and the only way to find out is to open the files and read the store, the town, the flavour and the price inside them against the row they were named for.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it and no parameter controls it, because the mislabelling is in the response and the sticky can is in the raster, and the response is the only thing an agent that trusts its tools would use to name and check the files. Nothing states it: the acceptance line about the right store's own price and can is the founders' requirement and the brief never characterises the delivery. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different delivery route, either a single multi-page PDF whose page order is trustworthy or a per-record loop producing one file at a time so identity is guaranteed, with the blank cells handled as deliberate photograph-less cards rather than left for the merge to fill.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Abandon the multi-record raster route, re-run the stockist set through a route whose record identity is guaranteed, rename every proof from what is actually inside it, re-check the two stores that share a name so the collision does not silently overwrite, and re-place the spruce-tip cards so none of them ships a can that belongs to a different flavour.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A shelf rail of cards where the price under one grocer's cans is another grocer's intro price, a spruce-tip card carries an elderflower can the brand does not even photograph, and the two stores of the same name overwrote each other, printed and clipped to the rail before the founders ever saw them.

deliverables.name: Fennhollow summer campaign photography, licensed and inherited
deliverables.spec: One warm daylight family reading as taken on the same afternoon: the licensed lifestyle frames at genuine camera scale, the two inherited packshots brought to the same target despite arriving crushed to paper white, and the house green holding on the label through every correction. Per picture parameter log including which licensed frames were rejected and why, and any place where the frame's own capture limited what could be recovered.

deliverables.name: Fennhollow can cutout set
deliverables.spec: The cans knocked out for the sign up spot and the banner: genuinely transparent, complete, with the base rim intact where the previous freelancer's retouching destroyed its separation from the ground, plus house-ground variants. Judged on the destination's own colour rather than on white. Every output at or below its source pixel dimensions with the returned tradeoff record for each.

deliverables.name: Fennhollow site and social family as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: One native editable Express document carrying a root per destination at its own canvas size across the home page band, two section headers, the sign up spot, the ad banner and the tall and square social frames, with live editable text in one licensed type system, every photograph and cutout carried as embedded image data rather than a reference, the featured flavour held in a position the founders can swap themselves, and the colour treatment reading on every canvas. Delivered with the self-contained source HTML, which is the durable half: they edit the document in August and the source guarantees the design survives regardless.

deliverables.name: Fennhollow style reference and source manifest
deliverables.spec: The written reference the client asked for by name: the colours as they actually exist on the delivered artwork rather than as a swatch card nobody sent, the type by role with family, foundry or designer and the actual numeric weight, the grading recipe per picture, and the flavour-to-photograph reconciliation naming the flavour that has none. Paired with a licensing manifest carrying every licensed asset id, its licence state and its generative status so the co-packer can be shown where each picture came from, a disclosure of any manufactured edge with its seed, and a persistent shareable shortlist board the two founders sign off from.

deliverables.name: Fennhollow summer stockist shelf-talker run
deliverables.spec: The card printer's flat shelf-talker press file reverse engineered into a live merge template with every placeholder confirmed present by inspection of the re-exported document, then run against the summer stockist list: one shelf-talker per store, page count equal to row count, rendered at 300 ppi at trim, each row binding its featured flavour's own can cutout re-cut to the card's picture-frame proportion, the stores leading with the spruce tip that has no packshot handled deliberately rather than left to inherit the previous row's can, per-store proofs named from what is actually inside them on a key that survives two stores sharing a name, and the no-bleed reality of the supplied press file reported rather than claimed away.

verifiers_auto.text: No image on any canvas resolved to the importer's placeholder.
verifiers_auto.how: Parse the returned per-slide markup for 1x1 placeholder image data on every canvas, not only the first.

verifiers_auto.text: Every text element in the exported markup carries a resolved licensed PostScript face rather than a fallback default.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are raster exports and which need an authored fixed-canvas document, given that the client wants to return to the file themselves in August.
Where the house green actually lives, given that the swatch card was never sent and the only surviving statement of it is inside two files someone else has already retouched.
Whether the founders' six saved thumbnails are a brief or a preference, and how to rebuild a shortlist on evidence a thumbnail does not carry.
How many frames to license, knowing that a rejected frame is a real cost and that an unlicensed thumbnail cannot be judged.
What the one warm daylight target actually is, given it has to be reachable by both an outdoor licensed frame and a studio packshot on white without pushing either somewhere it cannot go.
Which corrections have to be confined to the label so the one colour the brand owns does not drift, and how to word a selection so it takes the printed colour rather than the can and the table.
Knockout route for a packshot whose ground separation was destroyed before it arrived, and which ground to inspect the result against.
Where to spend the single sanctioned generative call, which side to grow, and whether the manufactured edge is honest enough to ship.
How to represent the flavour that has no photograph, given that the founders want it featured and inventing one is not available.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a natural grocer shopper rather than against a wellness brand or a mass soda aisle.
How much air each destination takes, since a wide band, a narrow header and a tall social frame are three different design problems and the restrained band is the design.
Where the colour treatment lives, in the raster or in the layout, which is a craft decision with a technical consequence at import.
Whether the summer stockist shelf-talker run is authored layout or a genuine one record per page merge, and which delivery route carries per-store identity safely when two stores share a name.
What a shelf-talker looks like for a store leading with the spruce tip that has no photograph, decided before the run rather than found on the printed sheet.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of a soda can in the sun. IDENTITY: this is a real can with a real printed label and a co-packer-cleared claim line that cannot be reworded, and a regenerated can is a different company's product with a different green on it. LEGALITY: the client's explicit requirement is photography they can prove the provenance of to their co-packer, with anything machine generated excluded by name, which is the exact opposite of what a generated image gives them and is not something a generated image can be given. SPEC: the destinations are a fixed list of pixel sizes and one of them cannot be reached by cropping at all, plus a transparent cutout complete to the base rim, none of which a generated picture satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the family is defined by being editable, because the featured flavour changes in August and the founders explicitly cannot re-commission. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: does this licensed frame actually sit with the set at full size, is there anything left in that sky to recover, did the colour survive the import onto the canvases nobody can preview. MERGE: the grocer run is one printed card per store bound to that store's own name, town, price and featured-flavour can with page count equal to row count, which a generated picture neither produces nor can be checked for, and the stores leading with the flavour that has no photograph have to be handled honestly rather than filled with a can that does not exist.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. STOCK AND BOARDS: asset_search on StockAsset is headless and returns id, renditionURL, true width and height, contentType, pricing and isGenTech, and asset_license_and_download_stock is fully headless with no prompt and no widget, verified returning state just_purchased and a real presigned link to a 7360x4912 JPEG. Checkpoint one rests on two documented findings: renditionURL is only a 240 pixel thumbnail and is explicitly not usable for editing, so the real frame does not exist until licensed, and the download link carries a one hour expiry while re-calling the licence tool refreshes it without consuming a second licence, which is what makes the rework affordable. Short generic queries are mandatory (a four word query returned 0 hits where a one word query returned 834) and the orientation filter is broken and always returns 0, both of which the trajectory respects. Boards persist genuinely with a hard cap of 12 placements per call and 201 meaning partial. IMAGING: apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, adjust_highlights, auto_tone, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, select_subject, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs, detection_confidence and upscale_factor, fill_area, remove_background in both forms, and generative_expand are all verified headless across 27 live calls. Checkpoint two is a property of the material rather than of a tool and is scored on the agent's response to a no-op readout; the connector provides no measurement tool of any kind, which is exactly why it has to be judged by eye. crop_and_resize DOES interpolate up to a hard 2x cap while reporting it only inside the tradeoffs array, and it auto-emits a requires_expand_chain tradeoff with pre-filled arguments when a cross-aspect crop would clip the subject, which is the documented route to the home page band. image_generative_expand is verified live (1024x1024 to 2048x1024, up to 4096 px per side, accepts seeds and returns the seed used) and is the sole sanctioned generative call. Alpha survives both crop tools at outputFileType png (13,371 partial-alpha px preserved). EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, the product is a genuine editable document findable by asset_search, and the rendition preview is documented as PAGE 1 ONLY, which is why verification is split between the rendition and the returned markup. Checkpoint three rests on a verified drop: mix-blend-mode is discarded and the element renders as a plain opaque shape, at HTTP success with no warning. External image URLs are documented to render as empty grey boxes even from allowlisted Adobe hosts, so every photograph is inlined, and transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined photography passes the 70 KB threshold immediately. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end including a browser proving licensed faces load, and the recommender is documented as refusing to pair, which is what makes the pairing the agent's own work. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt with its validator, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout with additionalImageFiles and document_render_layout are verified fully headless and synchronous, with one record per page for a PDF-derived template and page count equal to row count, and document_render_layout is verified at resolution 300 at trim. The proof-identity checkpoint rests on the verified finding that multi-record PNG and JPEG output comes back REVERSED while the response labels it by row, with PDF, createSeparateFiles and a recordRange loop as the three verified trustworthy routes, and on the verified behaviour that a blank picture cell leaves the prior row's bound image in place rather than clearing it, which is what rides a can into a spruce-tip store. PDF-derived frame granularity is not under the agent's control and no bleed box can be introduced, so the no-bleed shortfall is reported rather than fixed. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no upscaling, no compositing, no object removal, no background replace by prompt, no OCR, no text-to-image, no photo reaching Express as a URL, no fill_text, no animate_design, no batch above 20.

engagement_title: Verda Reformer Studio opens on Calloway Row: bring two dusk phone frames of the new room and a licensed movement set to one calm daylight look, recover the mark from the only file the last designer left, and rebuild the founding member passes from the file that went to press
vertical: Health, wellness and fitness, a boutique reformer pilates studio opening a second location, plus a printed founding member pass run carrying instructor portraits (North American city, Calloway Row)
real_brief_anchor: The reconciled ledger carries NO verbatim posted brief for this row, and this task states that rather than inventing a quotation. It is anchored instead to the recurring shape that Upwork and Freelancer.com carry continuously in the small studio and wellness category: an owner opening or relaunching a space, with a logo file inherited from a departed designer, one or two phone photographs of their own room, no shoot budget, and a request to 'source some stock that fits our vibe and make our photos match it'. That request is exactly what the killed original modelled, and it is why the ledger's own triage recorded PHOTO-28 as sitting on two surfaces with no decision density: sourcing and match grading, on their own, are the first afternoon of the job. The fuller commission the studio actually has is the opening itself. The same owner who cannot afford a shoot also has a wordmark that exists only as a small web export, a printed founding member pass her printer ran last year from a file she does not hold, six instructors who sent their own portraits, and an opening date that has already moved once. The brand is coined for this benchmark; no real studio, person or trademark is named anywhere.
client_one_liner: We open on Calloway Row in eleven weeks, our own two pictures of the room were taken at dusk and look nothing like the photography we want, our logo is one small web file, and the founding member passes have to be printed.
client_brief:
Verda Reformer Studio, Calloway Row opening

We are Marit and Dana. We have run one reformer studio for four years and we open a second on Calloway Row in eleven weeks. An intro pack is a hundred and eighty dollars, membership is two hundred and twenty a month, and our clients are mostly between twenty eight and forty eight. They are considered buyers. Most of them visit three studios before they choose one.

We have no shoot budget. What we have is two photographs of the new room, taken on our phones on the late afternoon the fit out finished, and a clear feeling about what the campaign should look like. Calm. Daylight. Room to breathe. Nothing that looks like a chain gym: no orange skin, no black rubber floor, nothing shouting.

We would like you to find a small number of genuine movement and wellness photographs we can license, chosen the way a designer chooses rather than the way a search engine ranks, and then make everything we use look as though it came from one afternoon in one room. Our own two pictures included. That last part is the actual job. If our room reads as a different brand from the campaign photography, we have wasted the money and the visit.

We need the campaign at the sizes we run: one wide picture for the top of the page, and square, tall and vertical versions for the feed and the stories.

Our logo has one file. The designer who drew it has gone and what she left is a small web export with a white square behind it. We need it usable, on the sage panel, on a printed card, at any size.

Founding members get a printed pass with their instructor on it. Our printer ran the passes last year and holds only the file that went to press. Six instructors this time, new class names, new prices. We want the whole run, a proof of each, and a file per instructor.

The launch page and the social set should stay ours to edit, because the opening date has already moved once.

And a note on what you did, and anything we should know about using the logo.
price_band_and_audience: Intro pack 180 dollars, membership 220 dollars a month, clients 28 to 48, mostly women in professional work who audition three studios before committing to one. The band is load bearing and it is a restraint band. At 220 a month the buyer is paying for calm, attention and space, so the campaign has to read as soft daylight, generous air, one body in one room, muted sage and oak, and type that is quiet. Push it down toward a 39 dollar high volume gym and the correct treatment inverts: bright, saturated, crowded, many bodies, heavy condensed type, price on the hero. Push it up into wellness luxury and it becomes near monochrome, editorial, almost empty, which at 220 a month reads as pretension and prices the studio out of its own neighbourhood. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission, and the owners have already named the failure themselves: a room that reads as a different brand from the campaign photography. A posted job of this shape runs 900 to 2,200 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: Boutique reformer pilates studio
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2022, first studio run for four years; opening a second location on Calloway Row in a North American city. Owner led by Marit and Dana, with six instructors. Small, independent, growing to two rooms.
brand_identity.about: Verda is a boutique reformer pilates studio built on calm. One body, one room, generous air, and unhurried attention. Marit and Dana have run a single studio for four years and are now opening a second on Calloway Row. The studio is deliberately the opposite of a chain gym: no crowding, no shouting, no gloss of the everyday. What clients pay for is space, focus and a considered environment they return to.
brand_identity.audience: Considered buyers, mostly women in professional work, aged 28 to 48. They typically audition three studios before committing to one, and they are paying for calm, attention and space rather than volume or intensity.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Premium neighborhood, not luxury. Intro pack 180 dollars, membership 220 a month. Positioned above a high volume budget gym and below wellness luxury: the tone is soft daylight and quiet confidence, never pretension and never a discount.
brand_identity.typography: Quiet and editorial. A light, humanist serif for headlines paired with a restrained sans for body and labels. Generous spacing, small type, nothing condensed, bold or promotional.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, warm and unhurried. Speaks to one person rather than a crowd. Confident without hype, and honest about what the room actually is.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No brand guidelines were ever written. The wordmark was drawn by a designer who has since left, and the only surviving file is a small low resolution web export she handed over. There is no master artwork, no color specification and no font list on record, so the freelancer inherits the studio look from this brief and from the room itself.
brand_identity.values: Calm, attention, generous space, and honesty about the room a client will actually walk into.

acceptance_bar: Everything the campaign uses reads as one afternoon in one room. One daylight white point, one black point, one warmth in the oak, one crop logic across the studio frames and the licensed frames alike.
The studio's own room is present in the campaign, not merely credited. If a studio frame could not carry the placement it was chosen for, the note says which one, why, and what carries it instead.
Nothing is cooked toward a chain gym look: no orange skin, no crushed blacks, no saturated floor. A frame taken far enough to stop looking like this room fails even if it looks impressive.

No delivered file exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions and no crop's tradeoff record carries an upscale entry. Where a placement could not be reached by cropping, the note says what was done to that frame.
Every licensed frame is genuine photography with generative tech candidates excluded, and every licensed asset id appears in the source manifest.

The mark is placeable artwork rather than a picture of artwork: transparent, scalable with a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath, both counters open, and it still reads at the size the printed pass reproduces it and reversed on the sage panel.
Exactly one printed pass per current instructor, no extra pass and no missing pass. If the number shipped is not six, the note says which row was left out and why.
Every pass carries all the lines last year's pass carried, and every class name and every price on every pass is the new figure named the way the studio names it to clients, not the scheduling code.
Each per instructor file contains the pass its filename claims, established by opening it rather than by the order the files came back in, and each pass carries its own instructor's portrait.
The proofs are rendered at true print resolution at pass trim rather than at screen scale.

The launch page and the social canvases come back as one native editable document at their own canvas sizes, with every photograph actually visible, the mark as live vector shapes rather than a flattened picture, and every text element carrying its licensed face at that family's own numeric weight.

A written note: what was applied to each frame and why the studio's room and the licensed frames needed different corrections to arrive at the same place, the type system by role, every roster row questioned and its resolution, every resize any tool reported, and anything the owners should know about using the recovered mark.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle the split: founding member passes to the merge surface, launch page and social canvases to authored roots, photography and mark recovery to imaging.
trajectory.judgement: The passes are record per page against a layout the printer already owns; the launch page must stay editable because the opening date moves, which the merge surface structurally cannot give.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier.

trajectory.action: Upload the two studio frames, the logo export, the six instructor portraits, the press PDF, the roster export and the owner's note, holding each presigned URL.

trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Preview everything and triage: what light each studio frame is actually under, which portraits have a separable subject and which do not, what the logo export really is at pixel level, and what native aspect each frame can reach.
trajectory.judgement: The owners describe dusk, which is a time rather than a diagnosis. Two illuminants in one room, a portrait whose subject and wall share a value, and an artefact ring around a wordmark are three different problems needing three different instruments.
trajectory.produces: A triage note per asset: illuminant, separability, native scale and boundary type.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level, then set a calm daylight base on the two studio frames, using confined corrections where the sage upholstery and the oak floor pull opposite ways under the mixed light.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes and eats edge pixels before any crop is locked. Naming a material's own visual properties confines the correction; naming the object it sits in takes the whole room with it.
trajectory.produces: Levelled studio masters at a calm daylight base with the applied parameters recorded per frame.

trajectory.action: Work the front window in the wide composing studio frame, since the daylight the campaign is about is the light coming through it.
trajectory.judgement: Whether there is anything under that window to bring back is a property of one phone exposure at dusk, and there is no measurement available anywhere to establish it in advance.
trajectory.produces: An attempted recovery on the wide studio frame and an honest look at the result.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries, filter to photography, exclude generative tech candidates, and build two defensible shortlists as two moods rather than one pile, then argue the pick against the band.
trajectory.judgement: Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used. The choice is art direction: which light could plausibly be this room, not which thumbnail is prettiest.
trajectory.produces: Two shortlists, a defended pick, and the reasoning recorded.

trajectory.action: License the chosen frames and download each at full resolution immediately, recording asset ids and the generative tech flag.
trajectory.judgement: The download link is short lived and re licensing only refreshes the URL. Camera scale matters because every later placement can only crop down.
trajectory.produces: Licensed camera scale frames on disk with a source manifest.

trajectory.action: Grade the licensed frames toward the calm daylight target and lay them beside the graded studio frames exactly as the launch page will lay them.
trajectory.judgement: This is the first moment the licensed photography and the studio's own room are adjacent, and it is the only moment the question the owners actually asked can be answered.
trajectory.produces: A campaign contact set judged as one set, with the reasoning recorded.

trajectory.action: Recover the wordmark from the web export: an ink level selection naming the letterforms' own visual properties, correct polarity, a bounds crop from the selection's own bbox, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full canvas ground path removed, plus a reversed variant for the sage panel.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions no tool makes: how to word the selection so it takes ink rather than the white plate, which polarity to trace, and whether the two enclosed counters came back open or came back filled and plausible. Background removal is the wrong instrument on an enclosed counter.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent wordmark plus a reversed variant.

trajectory.action: Prepare the six instructor portraits to one pass treatment: subject aware crops that never enlarge, then the knockout onto the studio's solid ground, reading confidence and tradeoffs on every call.
trajectory.judgement: A portrait below the pass's own reproduction scale cannot be rescued and has to be handled as a client conversation rather than a tool call. Where subject and wall share a luminance, the knockout is where the craft is.
trajectory.produces: Six prepared portraits on the studio ground, plus a note on any that could not reach pass scale.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the front window in the wide composing studio frame has anything left in it. The recovery move runs, reports success, and returns an image in which the readout is that nothing has moved: the window is clipped in every channel, so there is no detail under it to lift and the tool has nothing to do. Every later move toward the calm daylight target then pushes the rest of the room while that rectangle stays flat white, and it gets worse rather than better as the room around it comes down to a daylight value. There is no histogram, no eyedropper and no measurement anywhere in the connector, so whether a phone exposure at dusk held the window is unknowable until the attempt is made and the result is looked at.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no care prevents it, because the only channel that reports on this exposure is the attempt itself, and the frame that composes best wide is the frame with the window in it. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the two pictures were taken on phones on a late afternoon, which is the owners' account of when they were taken, and asks for calm daylight, which is the requirement. Neither is a disclosure that a channel is clipped. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the answer changes what the campaign's lead picture is a picture of.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re frame that studio master so the window falls outside the wide hero, which changes what the room's wide picture is about and therefore the crop logic for the whole set, or demote it and let a licensed frame lead, which changes how much of the campaign is the studio's own room and forces the calm daylight target to be re fixed off licensed photography rather than off the client's room, with every frame already corrected toward the old target re corrected afterwards.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The launch page ships with a flat white rectangle where the studio's daylight window should be, on the single picture a considered buyer looks at while deciding between three studios, and the effect grows more obvious the more correctly the rest of the room is graded.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the licensed frame can actually join this room. The search surface returns a 240 px thumbnail plus true dimensions and nothing else about the light, so a frame that reads on the thumbnail as soft north light can turn out at full resolution to be lit by a large warm practical off frame, laying an amber ramp across the far wall and a warm cast into the skin. Brought toward the calm daylight target globally, the skin goes cold before the wall gives up its amber; confined to the wall, the wall's new neutral changes what the sage reformer beside it reads as. Whether the frame joins at all only becomes a question at the moment it is downloaded at full resolution and laid beside the graded studio frames, which is the first time the two have ever been adjacent.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot produce that adjacency earlier, because it requires both the licence and the grade, and the pre licence readout is a 240 px proxy with no colour information worth trusting. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for frames chosen the way a designer chooses and for everything to look like one afternoon, which is the requirement rather than the finding. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is to license a different asset, which is a new shortlist, a new defence and a different lead picture.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Return to the search with what the failure taught about which lights can honestly join this room, license a replacement, grade it toward the target, re judge the whole set adjacent, and if no candidate joins, re fix the target on what the studio's own room can honestly be and re correct the licensed frames toward that instead, recording in the note why the studio frames and the licensed frames needed different corrections to arrive at the same place.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The campaign's most prominent photograph carries warm practical light and warm skin against a cool sage room, which is exactly the different brand from the campaign photography that the owners said in writing would waste the money.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printer's press card actually converts to. The printed pass plainly shows a portrait and the studio mark as two placed pictures and four separate blocks of copy, so the obvious plan binds a per row portrait to one graphic frame and the mark to the other and maps four fields to four frames. The converted document exposes one graphic frame and one continuous text story, because the mark was flattened into the background artwork before the file went to press and the copy was set as a single flow. Frame granularity is a property of how a retired printer built the document, it is announced nowhere, and the printed card is actively misleading about it. Any mapping row aimed at the second graphic frame is silently filtered out for naming an id that does not exist, the validator returns valid on what remains, and the preparation step reports success.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it, because the inventory does not exist until the conversion has run, and the only visible evidence beforehand is the printed page, which contradicts it. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that the printer holds the file that went to press. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the mapping strategy changes from per frame binding to offset arithmetic inside one story with same uid rows ordered so their positions hold, the mark can no longer be swapped per card and has to be carried some other way, and the portrait's aspect is now set by the single surviving graphic frame rather than by the two the plan assumed, which sends the portrait preparation back to the imaging surface.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Recompute every copy offset against the story text reconstructed from the exported document, re author the mapping inside one flow with same uid rows in descending position order, re prepare the six portraits to the aspect the surviving graphic frame actually has, decide and state how the recovered mark reaches the pass given that the old one is baked into the background, and verify by exporting the interchange file from the prepared template and searching for every placeholder before any pass is merged.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The founding member passes print with each instructor's portrait squeezed to the wrong shape in the only frame that exists, two copy fields never replaced so every pass carries last year's class name and price, and the studio mark stuck at whatever the printer flattened in a year ago.

decision_gates: Which deliverables go to the merge surface and which to authored canvases, given a pass the printer already owns and an opening date that keeps moving.
Whether the mixed dusk light in the room is one problem or two, since the sage upholstery and the oak floor pull opposite ways toward one white point.
Whether the wide composing studio frame can carry the wide hero at all once the window is worked, and what leads the campaign if it cannot.
Which two moods to shortlist from Stock and which to defend, at a band where the wrong light is not merely different but off brand.
Whether a licensed frame that will not join the room is the frame's problem or the target's, and therefore whether the target moves.

Selection prompt wording on the logo export: naming the plate takes the white square, naming the letterforms' own visual properties takes the ink, and background removal on an enclosed counter is the wrong instrument entirely.
Whether the recovered wordmark came back with open counters or came back filled and plausible, which only shows when it is placed small on the pass.
How the portrait below pass scale is handled, given that nothing can enlarge it and the client expects six passes.
The roster: a departed instructor still on the export, internal codes where client facing class names belong, and filenames that do not match the files. What is the agent's call and what is Marit's.
Whether to trust the printed card's apparent structure or the converted document's real frame inventory, and whether a success message counts as verification.
Whether per instructor identity is established by position in a returned list or by opening the file.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against restraint at 220 a month rather than against gym energy or luxury signalling.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns lovely pictures of a pilates studio. IDENTITY: the campaign has to contain the actual Calloway Row room that a considered buyer will walk into after visiting two competitors, and the owners have named the mismatch between room and campaign as the failure that wastes the money; a regenerated studio is a misrepresentation. The six instructors are six real people whose faces go on a printed pass, and the wordmark is a specific drawing that must be RECOVERED from the only surviving file, not reinvented into a different studio's mark. LICENSING: the sourced photography has to be genuinely licensed, provenance clear and free of generative tech candidates, because it runs in paid placement. SPEC: the printed run needs one 89 x 51 mm pass per current instructor binding class and price verbatim, per instructor files each containing the pass they claim, and proofs at true print resolution. EDITABILITY: the launch set is defined by being editable, because the opening date has already moved once. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: whether a dusk exposure held its window, whether a licensed frame's real light can join this room, whether a placeholder was ever created.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. IMAGING: straighten, apply_adjustments global and masked, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and 2x upscale cap, remove_background in both transparent and backgroundColor forms, fill_area and vectorize are verified headless across 27 live calls. The window checkpoint rests on there being NO measurement anywhere in the family (no eyedropper, no histogram, no ruler; metadata.bbox is a mask extent only), so recovery is an eye judgement and a null result is indistinguishable from a success at the API boundary. The portrait checkpoint rests on the verified alpha behaviour of remove_background (118,823 opaque and 13,371 genuinely feathered partial alpha px preserved through both crop tools at outputFileType png) and on the verified silent downscale of oversized inputs reported only through a tradeoffs entry. The mark recovery rests on the verified substrate versus ink prompt asymmetry (naming the card selected the card at 154,926 px; naming the ink's own colour and medium selected the strokes at 9,372 px), the verified polarity trap before vectorize, the verified solid disc failure of remove_background on an enclosed interior, image_vectorize TAKING NO OPTIONS AT ALL so raster preparation is the only lever, and the missing viewBox plus opaque path zero that the acceptance bar scores. MERGE SPINE: building a merge template from a bare press PDF end to end headlessly is verified; one record per page is confirmed for the PDF branch; per record files are confirmed in correct order by two routes (createSeparateFiles and a recordRange loop) while multi record PNG or JPEG URLs are verified to come back REVERSED, which is why identity is established by opening the file; true 300 DPI at trim is confirmed through document_render_layout while the merge's own resolution parameter is documented as silently ignored; per row image binding through an at prefixed CSV column plus additionalImageFiles is verified visually. The frame granularity checkpoint rests on two verified findings: FRAME GRANULARITY FROM A PDF IS NOT UNDER YOUR CONTROL AND CAN COLLAPSE TO ONE FRAME (a continuous flow converted to exactly one TextFrame and zero graphic frames), and a mapping row whose uid does not resolve is DROPPED FROM filteredMappings while prepare_indd_merge_template still returns Create Placeholder completed successfully. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export, inline SVG becoming native editable vector, and a genuine editable document are verified; the rendition shows PAGE 1 ONLY so verification splits between rendition and returned markup; every external image URL resolves to a placeholder grey box so photographs must be base64 inlined, and the payload is routed by uploaded URL because inlined photography passes the 70 KB threshold. FONTS follow the verified chain with find_fonts laundering names, font_styles supplying non standard numeric weights, and css_stack slugs in the CSS. STOCK and BOARDS follow the verified chain with short queries, orientation never passed, isGenTech exposed for exclusion, and the twelve per call board cap where 201 means partial. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no upscaling, no object removal, no compositing, no OCR, no bleed or press preset gate, no variable QR, no fill_text, no animate_design, no replace_image, no photo reaching Express as a URL, no batch above 20.

engagement_title: Cape Marren Coast Alliance shoulder season campaign: bring six member submitted photographs and a licensed coastal set to one warm October look, rebuild the member trail cards from the file that went to press, and hand the board a launch set it can edit when the dates move
vertical: Regional destination marketing, a coastal visitor alliance of independent member businesses pushing shoulder season visits, plus a printed member trail card run displayed in member windows (Atlantic seaboard, North America)
real_brief_anchor: The reconciled ledger carries NO verbatim posted brief for this row, and this task says so rather than fabricating a quotation. It is anchored instead to the shape that recurs continuously on Upwork and Freelancer.com under regional tourism and destination marketing: a small visitor board or business alliance with a thin photo library, member submitted photographs of wildly mixed quality, a printed piece a previous printer produced whose working file nobody holds, and a request to 'license some shots and make them all look like one campaign'. That request is precisely what the killed original modelled, and it is why the ledger's own triage recorded PHOTO-29 as two surfaces with no decision density: sourcing plus a shared grade is the first day of a destination campaign, not the campaign. The fuller commission a board of this size actually carries is the shoulder season push itself: the member businesses have to be in it or they will not fund it, the trail card has to be reprinted with this year's members and this year's opening months, and the opening months move, which is why the board's own coordinator has to be able to edit the launch set without coming back. Cape Marren, the alliance and every member business are coined for this benchmark; no real place, board, business or trademark is named anywhere.
client_one_liner: We are pushing October to April, our members sent us whatever photographs they had, the trail cards have to be reprinted with this year's members, and our opening months change often enough that we cannot keep coming back to you.
client_brief:
Cape Marren Coast Alliance, shoulder season campaign

I am Nell, the coordinator. We are twenty two independent businesses along the Cape Marren coast and our problem is the calendar. Summer takes care of itself. October to April is when our members either make a living or do not, and the visitor who comes then is a different visitor: a couple or a pair of friends, thirty to sixty, driving up for two or three nights and spending two hundred to six hundred dollars across a weekend on rooms, meals, cider and a walk.

We want the campaign to feel like that season honestly. Warm, low light, weather, wool, quiet. What we do not want is a summer campaign with the saturation turned up, because people arrive in November and find the sea is grey and the cafe shuts at four, and then they write about it. We also do not want it so bleak and literal that nobody books.

Our own library is thin. Six of our members sent us photographs they had. Please use them, because members who cannot see themselves in the campaign do not renew, and fill the gaps with a small number of coastal photographs we can license, chosen the way a designer chooses. Then make the whole thing look like one campaign rather than a pile of pictures from different weekends.

We need a wide picture for the top of the site, and square, tall and vertical versions for the feed and the stories.

Every member displays a trail card in their window. Our old printer ran them and holds only the file that went to press. This year's list is different, the opening months are different, and each card carries something of that member's own. We want the run, a proof of each and a file per member.

The campaign page and the social set have to stay ours to edit, because our members change their opening months more or less monthly.

And a note on what you did and what we should watch.
price_band_and_audience: Discretionary spend of 200 to 600 dollars per visitor party across a two or three night shoulder season weekend, travellers 30 to 60, driving from within four hours, mostly couples and pairs of friends rather than families. The band is load bearing in both directions. At this spend the campaign has to promise a real place in real weather: warm low sun, wool, wet stone, a lit window at four in the afternoon, quiet compositions with one or two people, and type that reads as editorial rather than promotional. Pushed up toward a 1,500 dollar luxury coastal weekend it would go near monochrome and near empty, which strands the cider barn and the bakery that fund the alliance and misrepresents what the coast actually offers. Pushed down into a peak summer treatment, saturated blue water, hard sun, crowded harbour, it sets an expectation November cannot meet, and the coordinator has already named that failure in writing: visitors who arrive to a grey sea and a cafe shut at four write about it. Either extreme costs the board member renewals, which is the money that pays for this. A posted job of this shape runs 1,200 to 3,000 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: Regional destination marketing, an alliance of independent coastal member businesses
brand_identity.founded_place_size: A visitor alliance of twenty two independent member businesses along the Cape Marren coast on the North American Atlantic seaboard. Coordinated by Nell on behalf of the members. Small, member funded, regional in reach.
brand_identity.about: Cape Marren Coast Alliance markets a stretch of independent coast to shoulder season visitors. Summer sells itself; the work is October to April, when a harbour seafood room, a cider barn, a point light, a bookshop, a bakery and an oyster landing either make a living or do not. The campaign has to feel like that season honestly: warm low sun, weather, wool, wet stone, a lit window at four in the afternoon, quiet compositions with one or two people. Members have to see themselves in it, because members who cannot see themselves do not renew.
brand_identity.audience: Travellers aged 30 to 60, driving from within four hours, mostly couples and pairs of friends rather than families. They spend 200 to 600 dollars per party across a two or three night shoulder season weekend on rooms, meals, cider and a walk.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Mid range and real. Positioned above a peak summer holiday treatment (which would oversell blue water and hard sun) and below a 1,500 dollar luxury coastal weekend (which would go near monochrome and strand the bakery and the cider barn). Editorial rather than promotional, and never promising a season the coast cannot deliver in November.
brand_identity.typography: Editorial, not promotional. A quiet serif for headlines with a plain sans for captions, trail numbers and opening months. Restrained weights, comfortable spacing, nothing that reads as a sale.
brand_identity.voice: Grounded and truthful. Warm about the place without overselling it, and specific about what a visitor will actually find when they arrive out of season.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No written brand guidelines exist. The only brand file on hand is the alliance mark left by the previous agency, supplied as a single vector file with nothing else: no color system, no type list and no usage notes. Members submit their own photographs and object shots, and the campaign look is set by this brief rather than by any existing kit.
brand_identity.values: Honesty about the season, keeping every member visible, and supporting the independent businesses that fund the alliance.

assets_supplied.name: member_photos/ (6 frames, 1400 to 5200 px, mixed provenance)
assets_supplied.kind: One photograph from each of six member businesses: a harbour seafood room, a cider barn, the point light, a bookshop, a bakery counter and an oyster landing. Shot by the members themselves over two seasons on phones and one compact camera.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Six of our members sent us what they had. They are all different and I know it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three were taken on the same flat overcast morning where the sea and the sky sit within a hair of each other in value, so a warm move that lifts the whole field carries the water with it and the horizon simply stops existing. One is a phone panorama with a stitch seam running through the harbour wall, and one is 1400 px on the long edge, which no wide placement in the set can carry and nothing can enlarge.

assets_supplied.name: member_objects/ (6 object photographs, approx 3000 px)
assets_supplied.kind: One signature object per member, shot on whatever surface was to hand: a cider press wheel, a lobster creel, the point light's lamp, a stack of secondhand books, a proving basket and an oyster knife.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Each member picked one thing that is theirs. They are meant to go on the cards."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three of the six have enclosed interiors, the creel's weave, the lamp's railing and the basket's open mouth, and a single knockout returns them as solid blobs with the interior filled by whatever was behind them while reporting success. The oyster knife was shot lying on brushed steel, so its blade and its ground are the same material and the edge is where any cutout will bite.

assets_supplied.kind: The printer's flat press PDF for last year's member trail card, 105 x 148 mm portrait, fonts embedded, produced from a real page layout so it converts cleanly. Carries the member name, the trail number, a one line description, the opening months, a contact line and a placed object photograph.

assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The readout of the card's copy silently omits the run carrying the opening months line while keeping its line break, so the string still reads as well formed prose and every character offset after it is short by exactly that run's length. The validator returns valid on the resulting arithmetic and the placeholder step reports success, while two of the fields never become placeholders.

assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Seven rows for six cards, because a business that closed in February is still on the list. Two members appear under their registered trading names rather than the names the board uses in campaign copy, and the photograph column's filenames carry an extension that does not match the files supplied.

assets_supplied.kind: The alliance's mark as the previous agency left it, a vector file of the Cape Marren compass and lettering.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our mark. The agency that made it sent us this file and nothing else."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The file carries the mark inside a full canvas white rectangle at path index zero and declares no viewBox, so it boxes out whatever ground it is placed on and will not scale in an authored page until both are fixed by hand. Its lettering also sits at a weight that begins closing up at the size the trail card actually reproduces it.

assets_supplied.name: board_note.txt
assets_supplied.kind: A page from Nell: the six members and what each is for, how the board talks about the season, what the campaign must not promise, and the two names the board writes differently from the spreadsheet.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The members, the season, and what we must not promise people."

acceptance_bar: Every frame in the campaign reads as one shoulder season rather than as a pile of weekends: one warm target, one black point, one crop logic across member submitted and licensed photography alike.

The member photographs are genuinely in the campaign, not quietly replaced by licensed frames. If a member frame could not carry the placement it was chosen for, the note names the member, the reason and what carries it instead.

Nothing promises a season the coast cannot deliver. No water is a colour that water is not in November, no sky is invented, and any frame taken far enough to read as July fails even if it looks better.
Sea and sky remain readable as two things wherever they meet. A horizon that has stopped existing is a failed frame regardless of how warm it looks.

No delivered file exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions and no crop's tradeoff record carries an upscale entry. Where a placement could not be reached by cropping, the note says what was done to that frame.
Every licensed frame is genuine photography with generative tech candidates excluded, and every licensed asset id appears in the source manifest.
The six member objects come back on one campaign ground as a set: enclosed interiors actually open rather than filled and plausible, and the edge holding where object and ground share a material.
Exactly one printed card per current member, no extra card and no missing card. If the number shipped is not the number asked for, the note says which row was left out and why.

Every card carries all the lines last year's card carried, including the opening months, and every opening months line and every description is this year's text with members named the way the board names them in copy.
Each per member file contains the card its filename claims, established by opening it rather than by the order the files came back in, and each card carries its own member's object.
The proofs are rendered at true print resolution at card trim rather than at screen scale.

The campaign page and the social canvases come back as one native editable document at their own canvas sizes, with every photograph actually visible, the alliance mark as live vector shapes on a transparent ground rather than a white box, and every text element carrying its licensed face at that family's own numeric weight.

A written note: what was applied to each frame and why the member submitted and licensed photography needed different corrections to arrive at the same place, the type system by role, every membership row questioned and its resolution, every resize any tool reported, and what the board should watch when it edits the launch set itself.
