trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, upload every asset against its role and its SKU, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface.
trajectory.judgement: Six cards each carrying a different picture is a record per page run; the spec sheet, insert and colourway page need an authored canvas. Identity has to be tracked from the first minute or it is guessed at later.
trajectory.produces: A surface plan, the confirmed tier, and a manifest keyed by design and role.

trajectory.action: Preview all six sheets and the jacket photograph and triage them for medium, ink to paper separation on each stock, exposure and design identity, then straighten what is off square.
trajectory.judgement: The client believes these are six pictures of six drawings. They are six printings on different stocks under different light, plus one that is thread rather than ink and therefore a different job entirely.
trajectory.produces: A per source triage note and levelled sheet masters where needed.

trajectory.action: Bring the six sheets to one target so the ink reads at one density, correcting each toward that destination with its own call and recording what was applied.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a set rather than six good photographs, and one shared correction applied to six differently exposed frames is the wrong instrument. This is the last cheap moment to make the six comparable.
trajectory.produces: Six sheet masters at one ink density with a per sheet parameter log.

trajectory.action: Isolate the mark on each sheet by naming the ink's own visual properties rather than the sheet it is printed on, set the polarity the trace needs, and crop each to its own returned extent.
trajectory.judgement: Naming the sheet returns a paper shaped blob every later step processes as if it were the badge, and the kraft toned stock does not separate the way the white stocks do. Polarity is the difference between a positive face and a black box.
trajectory.produces: Six isolated plates at native scale.

trajectory.action: Flatten each isolated plate so the trace receives an edge rather than a print texture, then trace all six.
trajectory.judgement: The trace takes no options at all, so anything that will be true of the geometry has to be made true in the raster first. This is the only lever anywhere in the recovery.
trajectory.produces: Six traced faces plus a record of what was flattened per face.

trajectory.action: Do the vector hygiene on all six, injecting a real viewBox and removing the full canvas ground path, then lay the six out together at the sizes they are actually struck and judge them as a set.
trajectory.judgement: Six faces judged one at a time are not judged. The pack is a pack, and the only place a mismatch is visible is side by side at struck size.
trajectory.produces: Six hygienic faces and a set level judgement of how they sit together.

trajectory.action: Build the two reductions per design: the coin's line only raised metal plate carrying the fine work, and the pin's simplified hard enamel version with wells a mint can fill.
trajectory.judgement: This is the price band made physical. What comes out of the pin version is a craft decision about what the design can lose and still be itself, and it is what the mint will judge the pack on.
trajectory.produces: Twelve production faces, two per design, each off that design's one geometry.

trajectory.action: Fill the enamel version within the mint's colour ceiling, then produce two or three crest colourways as masked hue moves off the ONE crest geometry.
trajectory.judgement: Separate colourings drift and the mint receives three slightly different crests. The colour ceiling is a manufacturing constraint, so a fill that exceeds it is not a design choice, it is an unstrikeable file.
trajectory.produces: Six enamel faces within the ceiling plus crest colourways sharing one geometry.

trajectory.action: License a struck metal ground at full resolution with short generic queries filtered to photography, grade it to sit with the faces, then create the committee board and place the colourways, faces and ground within the per call cap.
trajectory.judgement: The colourways have to be approved on the material they will exist in. A partial board placement is reported as a success and vector is not placeable there, so what goes on the board is a deliberate choice.
trajectory.produces: A graded metal ground and a persistent committee board with nothing silently dropped.

trajectory.action: Convert the printer's backing card PDF into a working layout, export its interchange form, and read what came back: the real frame inventory, whether any frame can carry a picture at all, and the real story text.
trajectory.judgement: The printed card shows a picture area and four lines of type. What the conversion produced is a different question, and it decides whether a per record face is even possible on this template.
trajectory.produces: A frame inventory including graphic frames, and the reconstructed story text.

trajectory.action: Build the mapping against the reconstructed story text, validate it, prepare the merge template, then export the rebuilt document again and confirm every placeholder is genuinely present.
trajectory.judgement: Both the validator and the template builder report success on a mapping whose positions are wrong, so reading the rebuilt document is the only trustworthy confirmation.
trajectory.produces: A verified merge template with its placeholders confirmed by inspection.

trajectory.action: Merge the six SKUs into one print ready file, binding each design's own face through the spreadsheet's artwork column, then render a proof per SKU at true card resolution and check identity by the code and the face printed on it.
trajectory.judgement: Position in a returned list is not identity, and the label on a per record raster is not evidence. Six cards going to a printer is where a swapped face is discovered on the tent table.
trajectory.produces: One six card print ready file plus six identified proofs at card resolution.

trajectory.action: Build the type system, one recommendation call per role plus the style inventories for the real numeric weights and one laundered kit, then author one self contained HTML carrying the spec sheet, capsule insert and colourway comparison at their own canvases, faces as inline SVG in explicitly sized wrappers and the metal ground embedded as image data.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged between a club with a 1987 history and a document a mint works from. On the canvas, a photograph left as a reference is not a photograph and a global canvas override collapses a mixed size set.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system recorded per role and one export ready HTML carrying all three canvases.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export, verify through the two channels that exist, the rendition for the first canvas and the returned markup for the rest, then write the mint handover and the club note.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning and the rendition only shows the first artboard, so the insert and the comparison page can be checked no other way. The mint reads the handover before it cuts a die.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document, an audited export, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the six recovered faces are a set. Stroke weight in a traced outline is a function of how heavy the ink reads in the raster the trace received, not of how the badge was drawn, so six sheets printed at different times and photographed under different light trace into six outlines of visibly different line weight, each of which looks completely right while it is being looked at alone. The trace reports nothing: no weight, no threshold, no simplification, and an identical response for a heavy face and a spindly one. The mismatch exists only in the comparison, at struck size.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering does not dodge it, because the mismatch is a property of the relationship between six finished traces and cannot exist until all six exist. Doing it right first time presumes knowing, per sheet, how much ink density to add or remove before a trace that has no controls, which nothing reports. Nothing states it either: the client describes the photographs, not what a trace does with them. It is not a propagation re run, because the fix reaches back to per sheet preparation for specific faces only.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Identify which faces sit heavy and which thin against the set, go back to the ink density preparation for just those sheets, re trace, redo the hygiene, and lay the six out together again at struck size.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A mint receives six faces that are supposed to be one collection and cuts six dies at three different line weights, which on a numbered ninety five dollar coin sold on continuity with 1987 is exactly the defect the buyer holds it to the light to look for.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether each backing card is actually carrying its own design. Two things are knowable only by running the merge: whether the printer's flat card converted into a layout that can carry a different picture per record at all, which depends on how the original file was built rather than on what the printed card shows, and whether the per record proofs are in the order they claim. The proofs render, they carry a label naming their row, and that label can be wrong while every file reports success, so a run named by position ships the ice trial's face on the gravel loop's card.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because both facts exist only after a conversion and a merge that have already happened, and no parameter controls either. Nothing states it, since the client says the shape is right and the design changes. It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a different delivery route chosen for identity, plus a verification pass that reads each proof's own content against its row.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Establish identity by what is printed on each proof, re derive the per SKU files through a route whose ordering is trustworthy, reconcile the two rows pointing at one artwork file, and re check all six.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Six hundred pins reach a tent table on backing cards carrying the wrong design's face and the wrong edition size, which is a reprint of the whole run and a refund line at the event the pack was made for.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the thing the colourway decision rests on. The committee has to judge the crest colourways on struck metal, so the natural construction is the face carried over the metal ground with a sheen and an edge treatment that read as struck rather than printed. Those constructions do not survive intact: blending against the ground and layered edge treatment are normalised away or truncated, silently, at full success, so the face can arrive as a flat opaque shape on a photograph of metal. The returned markup is the only channel that reports it, and the rendition shows the first canvas only.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the normalisation happens at import and the import is the last step, and doing it right first time presumes knowing which of several plausible constructions survives, which no tool reports. Nothing states it: the client asks to see the colourways on the metal, which is art direction rather than a warning. It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a different upstream asset or a treatment rebuilt from the constructions that do survive.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the colourway page around a construction that survives the import, re author, re run the readiness check, export again, and audit all three canvases from the returned markup.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A committee votes on a flagship coin colourway from a page where the crest is a flat shape on a picture of metal, picks the option that looks best flat, and the mint strikes the one that reads worst in the hand.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are a record per page run with per record artwork and which need an authored fixed canvas, since only one surface does each.
Whether the embroidered crest is admissible evidence at all, and which crest version is the club's when the two disagree about a year band.
How the isolation is worded per sheet, since naming the sheet returns paper and naming the ink's own visual properties returns the badge, and kraft stock does not behave like white stock.
How much correction to spend making six garage lit sheets comparable before any is traced, given that the trace has no controls at all.
What comes out of each pin face and what stays in each coin face, the price band expressed as craft and what the mint will judge the pack on.
Whether the colourways come off one geometry or off separate colourings, identical on delivery day and drifted within a season.
Whether the printer's card can carry a per record picture at all, and what to deliver instead if it cannot.
How to reconcile two rows pointing at one artwork file before anything is bound, and how to normalise the inconsistent price and edition cells without editing the client's meaning.
What to put in front of the committee, given that the board cannot carry vector and a colourway approved on white is not approved on metal.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the sheets into a frontier image model and it returns six handsome motorsport badges. IDENTITY: these are this club's actual crest from 1987 and five badges drawn by named members, worn on jackets and already owned by two hundred and forty people, so a regenerated badge is a different club's badge and the ninety five dollar coin is sold precisely on continuity with what already exists. SPEC: a mint needs closed line only geometry inside a stated diameter and a colour count ceiling, six cards at one SKU per page each bound to its own face with codes and edition sizes that reconcile to a spreadsheet, and proofs whose identity is provable. A generated picture satisfies none of that. EDITABILITY: the mint, the printer and next season's committee need real geometry and real editable documents, and the colour list has to be readable off the artwork rather than asserted.
doability_proof: Verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account). Five surfaces honestly counted, image_vectorize counted as Photoshop family. No banned capability and no dead surface: no video or audio, no document_render_vector or document_merge_data_vector (unretrievable headlessly), no animate_design, no fill_text, no upscaling, compositing, object removal, OCR, text to image, image to PDF, variable QR, pdfPreset, bleed gate from a PDF derived template, or batch above 20. IMAGING is verified headless across 27 live calls; select, invert, crop to bounds, vectorize returns a real outline with strokes intact, and the fill_area variant yields a full colour trace preserving brand hues. Checkpoint one rests on verified findings: vectorize TAKES NO OPTIONS AT ALL so raster prep is the only lever, and binary mask in gives two colours out while a colour plate in gives 76 near identical fills out, which is why line weight is inherited from the raster; it emits NO viewBox and an opaque full canvas rectangle at path index zero; and masked hue moves hold at moderate range, which is what makes the colourways real. INDESIGN: convert, export_idml, mapping, prepare, merge and render are verified headless and synchronous, one record per page for PDF output verified with page count equal to row count, PER ROW IMAGE BINDING VERIFIED VISUALLY through an at prefixed CSV column plus additionalImageFiles, and 300 DPI verified through document_render_layout. Checkpoint two rests on two verified findings: PDF derived frame granularity is not under your control and graphic frames exist only when the source PDF actually placed images, and multi record raster output URLs came back REVERSED while labelled in row order, with PDF, createSeparateFiles and a recordRange loop verified as the trustworthy routes. EXPRESS: mixed canvases in one export, inline SVG as native editable vector and an editable document findable by asset_search are verified; checkpoint three rests on the verified silent drops of mix-blend-mode and of every box-shadow layer past the first, plus the rendition being documented as first canvas only. FONTS and STOCK AND BOARDS are verified end to end, including the kit case sensitivity trap, the non standard numeric weights, short Stock queries with orientation never passed, and boards persistent at 12 placements per call with 201 meaning partial and vector unsupported.

engagement_title: Meridian and Ash sticker range and counter programme: recover the painted window mark and three printed bag illustrations into real cut artwork, gang them onto the printer's sheet with a separable cut layer, rebuild last season's shelf card into a live six origin run, and hand back the on sale set editable
vertical: Food and beverage, specialty coffee roasting and retail, one roastery cafe plus two market stalls and roughly forty wholesale accounts (Portland, Oregon)
real_brief_anchor: The ledger row for VECTOR-04 carries an empty real_brief_anchors array, so the anchor is the recurring posted commission this concept was carved from rather than a single quoted post. The shape recurs constantly on Upwork and Freelancer.com under titles of the form 'die cut sticker sheet design for our coffee brand' and 'convert my logo to vector for stickers', and the body is always the same three asks: turn our existing logo and artwork into vector, arrange the designs on one print ready sheet, and supply the cut lines, with 'vector files' and 'editable source files' named among the deliverables and the client volunteering that all they have is a photograph or a printed sample because the original designer is gone. The ledger's own one_line_ask is quoted verbatim into the client voice here: pull our logo and a few of our existing printed illustrations into clean sticker art, and lay it all out as a die-cut sheet plus individual stickers we can sell and hand out. The triage verdict on the row is STRENGTHEN, and the reason it needed strengthening is that as carved it sat almost entirely on one surface (trace, then lay out), which is not the commission a roastery of this size actually places. Two things change that. First, the ledger's own 'peel-mockup card' would be photo compositing, which is not connector work, so it is re-carved as the printed counter card the roastery already puts in front of each origin, and that card is a genuine record per page run off a press PDF they already own. Second, CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) makes authored fixed canvas layout at true sheet size real, with inline SVG arriving as native editable vector, so the sheet and the on sale set are one editable document rather than a flat picture. That is the fuller job this client genuinely places inside one month.
client_one_liner: Our sign painter put the mark on the shop window eight years ago and we never got a file, our illustrations only exist printed on bags, and our sticker supplier redraws all of it slightly differently every batch.
client_brief:
Meridian and Ash, sticker range and counter programme

We roast in a converted machine shop in Portland and sell across our own counter, at two farmers markets and to about forty wholesale accounts. Stickers are half our merchandise table. We buy them in from a supplier who redraws our artwork every time, and every batch comes back a little different from the last one. People notice.

We want our own range. Six designs: the mark from our shop window, the three illustrations that are already printed on our bags, and two more that we work out with you and that have to look like they belong with the others. Three dollars for a single, nine dollars for a four pack, and we hand them out by the fistful with wholesale orders, so there will be a lot of them and the range should feel like there are a lot of them.

What we can give you. A photograph of the shop window, because the painter never gave us a file. Photographs of the bags, because the illustrations only exist printed on bags. And our printer still has the artwork for the shelf card that sits in front of each origin at the counter, from last season.

What we need back. Each sticker as artwork with nothing behind it that we can print at any size, so nobody ever redraws them again. All of them arranged on one sheet the way a sticker printer wants them. The cut line has to come as its own thing the printer can lift off, because our last supplier baked it into the picture and the press operator ended up redrawing it by hand.

We also need the counter cards for our six current origins, one card per origin, printed the same way as last season so they sit in the same holders. And a small on sale set: one square, one tall, one wide, in one file we can change ourselves, because the designs will rotate.

Playful, generous, a bit hand made. Not precious, not boutique. Our customers are twenty to thirty five and these go on laptops and water bottles.
price_band_and_audience: Impulse retail at three dollars a single and nine dollars a four pack, buyer twenty to thirty five, a cafe regular who buys at the till without deciding first. The band is load-bearing. At this price the range has to read as abundant and hand made: many small pieces, a warm printed ground, generous ink coverage, type that looks painted rather than set. The same six marks treated as a luxury programme, one foil emblem on a deep matte ground with acres of air, misreads the till entirely: it prices like a forty dollar object, it kills the four pack, and it makes the giveaway handful look like a mistake. Push the other way into loud discount styling, heavy outlines, drop shadows and a crowded sheet, and it stops reading as a roastery that people want to advertise on a laptop lid. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even when every technical gate passes. A real posted job of this shape runs 700 to 1,800 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: Specialty coffee roaster and cafe selling stickers and merchandise at the till, at farmers markets and to wholesale accounts.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2016, Portland, Oregon, a converted machine shop with one counter, two market stalls and roughly forty wholesale accounts.
brand_identity.about: Meridian and Ash roast single origin coffee in a converted machine shop and sell it across their own counter, at two farmers markets and to about forty wholesale accounts. The merchandise table is half the fun: stickers people put on laptops and water bottles because they actually like the mark. The whole point is a range that feels made by hand, not bought by the case.
brand_identity.audience: Cafe regulars twenty to thirty five who buy a sticker at the till without deciding first, and wholesale buyers who hand them out with orders.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Impulse retail, three dollars a single and nine dollars a four pack. Priced to be handed out by the fistful, so the range has to read as abundant rather than precious.
brand_identity.typography: A shaded serif wordmark that looks painted rather than set, arched over a filled roundel. Text and labels lean into a friendly, slightly irregular hand. Nothing boutique or foil thin.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, warm, a little wry, never precious. Example line: Pull one off the sheet, stick it on your laptop, come back for the other three.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No usable source files exist. The window mark was hand painted on the shop glass in 2018 by a sign painter who never handed over a file. The three current illustrations survive only printed on the coffee bags, and the printer still holds last season's counter card artwork.
brand_identity.values: Consistency people can trust, so the artwork stops being redrawn slightly differently every batch, and a hand made feel that reads as a real roastery rather than a franchise.

assets_supplied.name: meridian_window_mark.jpg (4160 x 3120)
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of the shop window from the sidewalk, the mark hand painted in two inks on the glass: a shaded serif wordmark arched over a filled roundel that carries an ash leaf inside a hairline ring.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only place the mark exists. Ross painted it in 2018 and we never got a file off him."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is a compound lockup painted on glass, which behaves nothing like a flat scan. A prompt naming the window or the glass returns the pane rather than the paint, a compound prompt returns the arched wordmark while silently dropping the ring and the leaf and still looks entirely plausible, and the one call knockout cannot punch the ring's enclosed interior so it returns a solid opaque disc. Across the right third the street reflects in the glass at close to the value of the darker ink.

assets_supplied.name: meridian_bag_illustrations/ (3 frames, 5472 x 3648)
assets_supplied.kind: Flat lay photographs of three printed coffee bags, one illustration on each: a moth, a ridge line, a pour over cone.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The three that are already on the bags. We want those exactly as they are, they are the reason people pick us up."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two of the three were printed as solid ink and the third was screened at press. At photograph preview scale a screen reads as a flat tone and is indistinguishable from solid ink, so nothing about the frame declares which is which. It only announces itself once the ink is traced, as thousands of dot contours instead of a drawing. Separately one of the three crosses the bag's gusset fold, so part of its geometry is bent off the plane and does not straighten with the frame.

assets_supplied.name: meridian_shelfcard_2025.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The printer's press artwork for last season's counter card, one card per origin, the file that actually went to press.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our printer sends this back every season. The holders on the counter are cut for it, so the card cannot change size."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The card's origin name, roast line, tasting notes and price were set as one continuous flow, so what the converted document exposes as separately addressable frames is nothing like the four blocks the printed card shows. And the readout of the card's own story omits one run while keeping its line break, so the string still looks well formed and every offset past it is short by that run's length, while the mapping validates clean and the prepare call reports success.

assets_supplied.name: meridian_origins.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Plain data for the six current origins: origin, farm, process, roast, tasting notes, price.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The six we are pouring now. The notes are what our head roaster wrote, do not improve them."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two of the six carry a second tasting line the other four do not, so those two rows are roughly twice the length of their neighbours, and one row's price is the wholesale per pound figure rather than the counter price, which no column header distinguishes and no cell flags.

assets_supplied.name: meridian_sheet_spec.txt
assets_supplied.kind: The sticker printer's note: sheet size, minimum gutter between cuts, safe margin from the sheet edge, and their standing requirement that the cut contour arrive as its own separable object rather than drawn into the artwork.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What our printer sent when we asked what they need."

acceptance_bar: Every sticker is placeable scalable artwork rather than a picture of artwork: a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath it, and nothing behind it on any ground.

Each sticker still reads as the same drawing at the size it actually reproduces, on the printed ground it actually sits on, not only at full canvas. A mark whose interior closes at fifty five millimetres fails even though it looks correct enlarged.

The cut contour is one closed offset path per sticker at the offset the printer's note states, held as its own separable object in the delivered layout, not a halo drawn into the picture and not the artwork's own edges.

The six designs read as one range: one ink language, one weight of line, one amount of hand. A recovered mark that arrives crisper or fuzzier than its neighbours is named rather than shipped alongside them.

The gang sheet is at the printer's true sheet size in real physical units, with the stated gutter and safe margin honoured, and the arrangement is justified against vinyl yield and counter readability rather than eyeballed.
Six counter cards, one origin per page, page count equal to row count, every field on every card carrying this season's copy and none still carrying last season's.
Every counter card is the same trim as last season's card so it sits in the existing holders, and the card that is delivered is press artwork, not a screen scale proxy.

All three on sale canvases sit in ONE working file, each keeping its own canvas size, with live text we can retype and the mark as real vector shapes, delivered alongside the self contained source it was built from.
No delivered file exceeds the pixel dimensions of the frame it came from, and no resize any tool performed goes unreported.

A written note stating what was recovered from where, which design could not be recovered as drawn and what was done instead, the type by role with family and actual weight, and anything the printer needs to know about the cut layer.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching a pixel.
trajectory.judgement: The stickers and the ground are raster and vector work, the sheet and the on sale set have to be an authored fixed canvas document because the client will rotate designs themselves, and the counter cards are a record per page run because the holders fix the trim. The brief pins all three destinations, so there is nothing to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming the surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handover discipline: a manifest keyed by role so that thirty artefacts later the agent still knows which URL is which bag.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Look at the window photograph and all three bag frames, and triage them: where paint and reflection run close in value, what each mark is actually made of, which frame is off level, which illustration crosses a fold.
trajectory.judgement: The client believes there are four recoveries of the same kind. The pictures are the only thing that can settle whether that is true, and looking at a thumbnail is not the same as looking at the frame.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note covering substrate, ink behaviour, tilt and where ground and mark run close.

trajectory.action: Straighten the bag frames that sit off level, before any bounds decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Recover the window mark: an ink level selection worded from the paint's own visual properties rather than from the surface it sits on, the correct polarity, a bounds crop driven by the selection's own returned box, then a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full canvas ground path removed.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions no tool makes: how to word the selection so it takes the paint and not the pane, which polarity to trace, and whether the two colour trace or the colour accurate knockout plate is the deliverable. A one call knockout on an enclosed ring is the wrong instrument entirely.
trajectory.produces: A placeable transparent mark plus a colour accurate variant, with the recovery route recorded.

trajectory.action: Recover the three bag illustrations the same way, one frame at a time, choosing per illustration between the two colour trace off the binary mask and the colour accurate knockout plate, and inspect each traced result rather than the response.
trajectory.judgement: They came off three different bags and they are not three of the same job. What each one is made of decides which route is correct, and the response text says the same thing either way.
trajectory.produces: Three traced illustrations with their route and their path behaviour recorded per frame.

trajectory.action: Draw the two new designs as authored inline SVG geometry, built from the stroke weight, terminal and corner language the recovered marks actually have.
trajectory.judgement: They have to look like they came off the same hand. That is a construction decision taken from the recovered artwork, not a style chosen freely, and at this band it has to stay generous rather than becoming precise.
trajectory.produces: Two new sticker designs as editable vector geometry consistent with the recovered four.

trajectory.action: Derive the cut contour for each of the six as a single closed offset path at the printer's stated offset, held as its own object, and decide what happens where a design has enclosed interior negative space.
trajectory.judgement: A die cut is not the artwork's own edges. The offset direction, the treatment of interior holes and the decision to simplify a contour the blade cannot follow are all craft calls the printer will otherwise make with a pen.
trajectory.produces: Six closed cut contours, each separable from the artwork it belongs to.

trajectory.action: Search short generic queries for a kraft board surface, filter to photography, exclude generative tech candidates, license and download at full resolution, then select the paper surface by prompt, warm it and crop it to a repeating tile.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose existing light can be brought to the house warmth rather than the prettiest thumbnail. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used.
trajectory.produces: One licensed camera scale frame and a printed ground tile derived from it.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's, judged against a three dollar impulse buy and a twenty to thirty five year old buyer. The weight cannot be inferred from the style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Author the gang sheet at the printer's true sheet size in absolute physical units, all six stickers and all six cut contours as inline SVG in explicitly sized top left anchored wrappers, gutters and safe margin taken from the printer's note. Lay two arrangements, a tight pack and themed rows, and pick one.
trajectory.judgement: The pick is argued on vinyl yield and on whether a customer can read the range at arm's length in a counter bin. An auto sized or right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the sheet edge, so everything is anchored and sized.
trajectory.produces: A sheet layout at true physical size with a stated arrangement rationale.

trajectory.action: Author the three on sale canvases as three further roots at their own canvas sizes in the same document, the ground tile inlined as image data, the mark as inline SVG, family and weight declared on every text element.
trajectory.judgement: A global canvas override is exactly what collapses a mixed size set, so each root declares its own. The design work is how much air an abundant range can carry before it starts pricing like a boutique.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML carrying the sheet and the on sale set, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, upload the HTML and export by URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at the first artboard, and parse the returned per canvas markup for everything else.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning of any kind, and the rendition only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at one page is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document, an inspected first artboard, and a per canvas markup audit for the rest.

trajectory.action: Convert the printer's shelf card artwork, export the interchange file, and read what the conversion actually exposes as addressable frames and what the card's story text actually says, before promising any field map.
trajectory.judgement: What a press PDF exposes is a property of how it was set, not of how it looks printed. Promising a per field map before looking is promising something nobody has checked.
trajectory.produces: A frame inventory and the card's own story text, read from the interchange file.

trajectory.action: Build the mapping, prepare the merge template, then merge the six origins one record per page and render at press resolution at the card's existing trim, and look at what came back.
trajectory.judgement: The holders fix the trim, so the card cannot be resized to solve a copy problem. The two long tasting rows and the row carrying a wholesale figure are content decisions the merge will not make.
trajectory.produces: A six page press file at the existing trim plus per record files, with the merged pages actually inspected.

trajectory.action: Create the range selects board, add the transparent proofs and the licensed frame within the per call placement cap, re-sending only the entries the response names as failed, then write the handover note.
trajectory.judgement: A 201 is partial success, and vector is not boardable so it belongs in the note instead. The note has to be specific enough that the next freelancer does not repeat the archaeology.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Which of the three bag illustrations was screened at press rather than printed in solid ink. At the scale a photograph of a bag previews at, a press screen reads as a flat tone and is visually identical to solid ink, so nothing in the frame, the filename or the client's description separates them. It declares itself only in the traced result: the two solid marks come back as a drawing with a countable number of contours, and the screened one comes back as thousands of dot contours that still assemble into a plausible looking picture at full canvas and only fall apart as artwork at sticker size and as an editable object once placed.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter prevents it, because the tracing tool takes no options at all and the only lever is what the raster prep hands it, which is the decision this checkpoint is about. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that the three illustrations are already printed on the bags and that the client wants them exactly as they are. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the affected illustration goes through a different chain, a binary ink mask traced as a mask rather than a colour plate traced as art, or a redraw as authored geometry when the screen has destroyed the line.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-derive that one illustration through a different route, judge whether what comes back is still the drawing on the bag or a new drawing wearing its shape, and then re-place it, which changes its silhouette and therefore its cut contour and its position in the sheet arrangement.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A range where one of six stickers is a cloud of dots that prints muddy at fifty five millimetres and arrives in the client's editable file as thousands of loose shapes, on a merchandise line whose entire premise is that nobody ever has to redraw the artwork again.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: That the readout of the shelf card's own text is short of the truth. The card's copy was set as one continuous flow, so the conversion exposes nothing like the four blocks the printed card shows, and the readout of that flow omits one run while keeping its line break, leaving a string that still looks well formed. Every offset computed past the omission is short by that run's length. The validator returns valid with no warnings on those offsets, the prepare call reports completing successfully, and the only place the shortfall appears is on the merged page, where two fields still carry last season's copy while the rest carry this season's.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the readout is the only description of the story the tools volunteer, and there is no flag, warning or count that says a run is missing. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that the printer still has last season's artwork and that the cards must stay the same size. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is to reconstruct the card's true story text out of the interchange file and recompute every offset against that string, which is a different derivation, not the same derivation repeated.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the field map from the reconstructed story text, prepare the template again, confirm by round tripping the interchange file that every placeholder is actually present rather than trusting the success message, then re-merge and read the six pages.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Six counter cards that look right and print right and quietly tell every customer at the till the wrong tasting notes and the wrong price for two of the six origins, with every tool response in the chain having reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the thing the whole deliverable turns on. The printer needs the cut contour as a separable object sitting over the artwork, and the natural authoring constructions for it are exactly the ones this importer discards without saying so: an outline is dropped entirely, a stroked display letterform loses its stroke and can render as fully transparent, a blurred halo is dropped so the element goes hard edged, and a stacked shadow is truncated to its first layer. All of them return success. The returned per canvas markup is the only channel that reports it, and the document's own rendition returns the first artboard only, so whichever canvas is not first cannot be checked any other way.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the normalisation happens at import and the import is the last step, and doing it right the first time presumes knowing which of several plausible constructions survives, which no tool reports and no checklist enumerates. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks only that the cut line arrive as its own thing the printer can lift off. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is a different construction of the same object, a closed path drawn as real geometry with its own fill and stroke rather than a CSS effect around the artwork, and the sheet then has to be re-composed around what that object actually is.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the cut layer as authored path geometry, re-author the sheet and the on sale canvases around it, re-upload, re-run the readiness check, re-export, and audit every canvas from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A gang sheet delivered as an editable file with no cut layer in it at all on the canvases nobody looked at, sent to the printer who then does exactly what the last supplier's press operator did and redraws the cut by hand, which is the specific thing the client hired this job to stop.

A real viewBox present on each, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath, one ink language and one weight of line across the six, and each still reading as its own drawing at the size it actually reproduces.

deliverables.name: Cut layer, one closed contour per sticker

decision_gates: Which deliverables are recovery work, which need an authored fixed canvas document, and which need a record per page run, given that only one surface here composes free form layout and only one produces volume personalisation.

Selection wording on the painted window: naming the window or the glass takes the pane, naming the paint's own visual properties takes the mark, and a one call knockout on an enclosed ring is the wrong instrument entirely.
Which recovery route each of the four originals needs, since a two colour trace off a binary mask and a colour accurate knockout plate produce different artwork and the response text is identical.
Whether a recovered illustration is still the drawing on the bag or has become a new drawing wearing its shape, and what to tell the client when it is the second.
How the two new designs are constructed, taken from the recovered marks' own stroke weight and terminals rather than chosen freely.
Cut contour craft: offset direction, what happens to enclosed interior negative space, and when to simplify a contour the blade cannot follow.
Tight pack versus themed rows on the sheet, argued on vinyl yield against readability in a counter bin.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a three dollar impulse buy, plus the real numeric weight per family.
Whether the licensed kraft frame joins the range's world or reads as bought, and how warm the ground can go before the ink stops separating from it.
What to do about the row carrying a wholesale figure and the two rows carrying a second tasting line, when the trim is fixed by the holders and cannot absorb them.
How much air the on sale canvases carry. At this band abundance is the design, and a spare, single emblem treatment is a correct looking wrong answer.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the photographs into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of coffee stickers. IDENTITY: this is the mark a sign painter put on this roastery's window in 2018 and three illustrations that are already printed on bags customers recognise on the shelf, and the entire reason the job exists is that a supplier keeps redrawing them slightly differently. A regenerated mark is precisely the failure the client is paying to stop. SPEC: the printer needs six closed cut contours at a stated offset as separable objects on a sheet at a real physical size with a stated gutter, and the counter cards must land at last season's exact trim so the existing holders still fit, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the sheet and the on sale set are defined by being editable, because the six designs rotate and the owners cannot re-commission each time. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: is this illustration solid ink or a press screen, does this cut layer still exist after the import, did two of the six cards quietly keep last season's copy.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. IMAGING: select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, fill_area, apply_adjustments masked, remove_background in both forms, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs, auto_straighten and vectorize are verified headless across 27 live calls, and the extract and reuse chain ending in a native editable Express document was run end to end. The recovery checkpoint rests on documented findings rather than assumptions: vectorize TAKES NO OPTIONS AT ALL, so a binary mask in gives two colours out and a colour plate in gives dozens of near identical fills out, and a traced mark arrives in Express as many loose ungrouped shapes. The substrate versus ink prompt asymmetry, the compound mark partial selection, the solid disc failure of remove_background on an enclosed ring, the missing viewBox and the opaque path zero are all live findings, and the acceptance bar scores exactly the hygiene the tool does not perform. EXPRESS: multiple roots at mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, absolute physical units resolve exactly at 96 dpi, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, clip path polygon becomes a real path, and the product is a genuine editable document findable by asset_search. The import checkpoint rests on verified drops: outline dropped entirely, filter blur dropped, multi layer shadow truncated to layer one, text stroke dropped leaving fully transparent text, all at HTTP success with no warning, and the rendition preview documented as first artboard only. Transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined photography passes the 70 KB threshold immediately, and every photo is base64 inlined because a URL renders as an empty grey box. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt as generator and validator, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout and document_render_layout are all verified headless and synchronous, one record per page for PDF is verified with page count equal to row count, and the mapping checkpoint rests on the verified lossy readout that dropped a 17 character run while keeping its line break, shifted every later offset, validated clean and landed only 3 of 5 mappings. Per record identity is taken through the verified createSeparateFiles or recordRange routes rather than by position, because multi record raster URLs came back reversed. Press resolution is taken through document_render_layout because merge output silently ignores resolution. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed, a real full resolution licensed JPEG, and boards persisting with a cap of 12 placements per call and 201 meaning partial. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no photo compositing anywhere including the re-carved counter card, no upscaling, no OCR, no text to image, no generative fill, no variable QR, no bleed claim off a PDF derived template, no pdfPreset, no fill_text, no animate_design, no batch above 20.

engagement_title: Isla Verde signage refresh: recover a foil stamped monogram off a printed brochure, build a facility pictogram set from its own construction, author the directional panels at true cut size, rebuild the 2016 door plate into a live twenty four record run, and hand the sign shop a schedule it can work from
vertical: Hospitality and travel, a forty two room independent coastal resort refinishing its corridors and replacing a failed 2016 sign programme (Gulf coast, Florida)
real_brief_anchor: The ledger row for VECTOR-05 carries an empty real_brief_anchors array, so the anchor is the recurring posted commission this concept was carved from rather than a single quoted post. It is one of the most common shapes on Upwork and Freelancer.com in the hospitality category: a property posts under a title of the form 'wayfinding and signage design for boutique resort' or 'recreate our logo from a printed brochure, vector needed', and the body always contains the same three admissions, that the original designer is unreachable, that the only surviving artwork is printed on something, and that the sign fabricator needs files by a date, with 'vector', 'editable', 'exact sizes' and 'we need our actual logo, not a new one' recurring almost verbatim. The ledger's own one_line_ask is quoted into the client voice here: we are refreshing signage across our resort and only have a printed brochure showing our old monogram, recover it cleanly and build a coordinated wayfinding system, all as editable artwork our sign shop can cut. The triage verdict on the row is STRENGTHEN, and two things had to change to meet the standard. First, the ledger's own 'mounted-panel mockup on a wall photo' is photo compositing, which is not connector work, so it is re-carved as what a real signage engagement actually hands over instead: the property's own location photography brought to one look for the standards document, plus a licensed camera scale frame for the mount points the property never photographed. Second, as carved the row sat almost entirely on one surface. The door plate is the part of a wayfinding programme that is genuinely a volume run, twenty four facilities at one plate per door, and the property already owns the 2016 press artwork the current plates were cut from, which is exactly the input a record per page run needs and exactly why the fixings still line up.
client_one_liner: The only place our monogram still exists at any quality is a foil stamp on the cover of a brochure we printed in 2019, and the sign shop needs artwork by the end of next month.
client_brief:
Isla Verde, signage refresh

We are a forty two room property on the Gulf coast, family owned, three hundred and eighty to six hundred and fifty a night. Our guests are thirty to fifty five and they come here because it is quiet.

Our signs are a mess. The system went in around 2016 with a local shop that has since closed, pieces of it have been replaced by whoever was available, and the door plates are chipped. We are refinishing the corridors this winter and the sign shop needs artwork by the end of next month.

The problem is our monogram. The only place it still exists at any quality is the cover of a brochure we printed in 2019, stamped in foil. Our designer moved abroad and nothing ever came back from her. We need the monogram back as artwork a sign shop can cut at any size, and it has to be our monogram, not a new one drawn to look like it.

Then the system. Directional signs for the corridors and for the garden path. A small set of facility symbols, eight of them, that look like they were drawn by whoever drew the monogram rather than bought from a catalogue. A door plate for every room and facility, twenty four of them, in English and Spanish, at the same size and printed the same way as the ones on the doors now so the existing fixings still line up. And a schedule the sign shop can work from: every panel, its size, its copy, where it goes.

We are also sending photographs of the walls the panels go on, and of four signs already up that the owner likes.

We want the standards written down as well, so the next person who orders a sign does not invent something.

How it should feel: quiet. A lot of empty space, one or two greys, the monogram. Our guests notice when a place is shouting at them. Nothing that looks like an airport or a car park.
price_band_and_audience: Upscale independent resort, rooms three hundred and eighty to six hundred and fifty a night, guest thirty to fifty five and travelling for quiet. The band is load-bearing and it decides the whole system. At this tier the signage is restrained: generous clear space, one or two close greys rather than contrast for its own sake, a delicate monogram, type set small and confidently, symbols drawn with the same hand as the mark. A budget motel system doing the same job would correctly be louder, denser, higher contrast and larger in type, because it has to be read fast by someone who does not want to be there, and shipping that treatment here reads as a highway property and undercuts the rate. Push the other way into near invisible pale on pale and the system stops doing the one thing signage exists to do, which at this tier is worse than looking cheap, because a guest who cannot find the spa asks at the desk and the quiet is what they paid for. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even when every technical gate passes. A real posted job of this shape runs 2,000 to 5,000 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: Independent upscale coastal resort refreshing its corridor and garden wayfinding and its room signage.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Family owned, Gulf coast of Florida, a forty two room property with corridors, a garden path and about twenty four rooms and facilities.
brand_identity.about: Isla Verde is a family owned resort on the Gulf coast where guests come for quiet. Forty two rooms, refinished corridors and a garden that people walk slowly. The signage is being rebuilt this winter so the property reads as calmly as it feels, with the house monogram carried consistently from the door plates to the directional panels.
brand_identity.audience: Independent leisure travellers thirty to fifty five paying for calm, who notice when a place is shouting and value being able to find their way without being told loudly.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Upscale independent, rooms three hundred and eighty to six hundred and fifty a night. Signage should read at that tier: generous clear space, delicate marks, confidence rather than contrast for its own sake.
brand_identity.typography: A fine interlocking monogram set small and confidently, paired with a quiet, well spaced text face. Type kept modest and legible, never large or emphatic. Facility symbols drawn with the same hand as the mark.
brand_identity.voice: Understated, warm, precise. It gives directions without raising its voice. Example line: The spa is along the garden path, second door on the left.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No monogram source file survives. The designer moved abroad and nothing was handed back. The only decent record of the mark is a foil stamp on the cover of a brochure printed in 2019. The 2016 sign shop that cut the current door plates has since closed, though its press artwork for the plates is still on file.
brand_identity.values: A sense of quiet that guests can navigate, and a written standard so the next person who orders a sign does not invent something new.

assets_supplied.name: islaverde_brochure_cover.jpg (4032 x 3024)
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of the 2019 printed brochure lying on a desk, the monogram foil stamped on uncoated cream stock: an interlocking I and V inside a fine oval rule with a small palm frond at the join.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only decent picture of the monogram we still have. It is stamped in foil so it catches the light."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Foil has no single ink value. The same stroke reads dark on one flank and near white specular on the other, so an ink level selection returns a plausible looking partial with whole strokes missing and no indication that anything is absent. The mark is also stamped small on the cover, so whatever survives the trace carries only the detail that was in those pixels, and the oval rule and the counters of the interlocked letters are the first things to close at the size the mark actually reproduces on a pale panel.

assets_supplied.name: islaverde_locations/ (10 frames, phone)
assets_supplied.kind: Phone photographs of the corridor and garden mount points, taken by the duty manager over two days.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Where the panels go. Taken on my phone, sorry about the quality."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two of the ten are the same corridor shot from opposite ends and three facilities on the schedule have no frame at all, which no filename reveals. The phone's automatic white balance also renders three genuinely different wall finishes as the same neutral, so the frames cannot be trusted to say how a panel will sit against the wall it mounts to.

assets_supplied.name: islaverde_doorplate_2016.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The closed sign shop's press artwork for the plate currently on every door, the file the existing plates were cut from.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What is on the doors now. The fixings are drilled for this size so it cannot change."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The name line sits in a fixed measure frame sized to the longest facility name the property had in 2016. A longer name does not spill, reflow or overset at trim, it simply stops rendering partway through, so the merged page looks entirely correct at page thumbnail scale and the loss is only visible at the plate's real size. The bilingual second line shares the same story as the name.

assets_supplied.name: islaverde_schedule.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Twenty four facilities: number, English name, Spanish name, floor, panel type, mount height.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Every door and facility, with both languages. The Spanish came from our front office manager."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three of the English names and five of the Spanish are materially longer than anything the 2016 plate ever carried, two rows are the same facility on two floors with identical copy, and one facility's name cannot fit the plate at any legible size, which is a decision to escalate to the owner rather than a problem to solve quietly.

assets_supplied.name: islaverde_existing_signs/ (4 frames)
assets_supplied.kind: Photographs of four signs already on the property that the owner likes and wants the new system to sit with.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "These four are fine. Whatever you do should look like it belongs with them."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two are from the 2016 programme and two survive from an earlier one with a noticeably heavier stroke and a different corner language, and nothing labels which is which, so matching all four means matching two incompatible systems and the owner has not noticed that they are two.

assets_supplied.name: islaverde_signshop_note.txt
assets_supplied.kind: The new fabricator's requirements: substrate and finish, the panel sizes they cut, minimum legible type height at their stated viewing distances, and clear space at the panel edge.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What the new sign shop sent over when we asked what they need."

acceptance_bar: The monogram is placeable scalable artwork rather than a picture of artwork: a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath it, and it is still recognisably this property's monogram rather than a new mark drawn to resemble it.
The monogram holds at the size it actually reproduces on each panel, with the oval rule and the interlocked counters open rather than closed, judged on the panel ground and not at full canvas.

The eight pictograms are drawn from the monogram's own construction, one stroke language, one corner language, one terminal, and each is drawn for the size it is placed at rather than one drawing scaled to two sizes.

Every panel is authored at the fabricator's true cut size in real physical units, with the stated clear space honoured and type at or above the fabricator's minimum legible height for its viewing distance.
No artwork runs off a panel's cut edge anywhere in the delivered document, on any panel, including panels that cannot be previewed as a rendered page.

Twenty four door plates, one facility per page, page count equal to row count, at the same trim as the 2016 plate so the existing fixings still line up, and every name on every plate readable in full at plate size in both languages.
Any facility whose name cannot fit the plate at a legible size is named to the owner as a decision, not silently abbreviated and not silently truncated.
Per record files handed to the fabricator carry the facility they claim to carry, and the delivered set is rendered at press resolution rather than at screen scale.

The panels, the plate face and the schedule sit in ONE working file with live editable text and the monogram and pictograms as real vector shapes, delivered with the self contained source it was built from.
One type system across every panel with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer and the actual weight used, and a stated minimum size below which the system must not be set.
The system reads as a three hundred and eighty to six hundred and fifty dollar property: quiet, spare, close greys. Loud, dense and high contrast fails even if every measurement is correct.

trajectory.action: Author the directional panels and the door plate face at true physical size in absolute units, every SVG inside an explicitly sized top left anchored wrapper, each pictogram placed at the size its panel actually needs.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, upload the HTML and export by URL.
trajectory.judgement: The readiness check runs before every export and every retry, and the payload travels by uploaded URL because inlined photography passes the inline threshold immediately.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document carrying every root.

trajectory.action: Verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at the first artboard, and parse the returned per canvas markup for every other root, element by element.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop and every normalisation this importer performs returns success with no warning of any kind, and the rendition only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at one panel is not looking at the system.
trajectory.produces: An inspected first artboard and a per canvas markup audit covering every panel, the plate face, the pictogram sheet and the schedule table.

trajectory.action: Bring the location frames to one house target for the standards document, one call per frame, recording the parameters applied.
trajectory.judgement: They were shot over two days on a phone that made its own white balance decisions, so one batched parameter set is exactly wrong. The target is a set that looks like one property, not ten good frames.
trajectory.produces: A graded location set at source scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Search short generic queries for the three mount points nobody photographed, filter to photography, exclude generative tech candidates, license and download at full resolution, and bring the frame to the same target.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose existing light can be brought to the house target rather than the prettiest thumbnail. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used.
trajectory.produces: One licensed camera scale frame graded into the same set.

trajectory.action: Convert the 2016 plate artwork, export the interchange file, and read what the conversion actually exposes as addressable frames and what the plate's story text actually says, then build the field map from that and prepare the merge template.
trajectory.judgement: What a press PDF exposes is a property of how it was set, not of how the plate looks on the door. Promising a field map before looking is promising something nobody has checked.
trajectory.produces: A frame inventory, the plate's true story text, and a prepared merge template.

trajectory.action: Merge the twenty four facilities one record per page, render at press resolution at the 2016 trim, produce per record files for the fabricator with identity guaranteed per call rather than by position in a returned list, and read the plates at plate size.
trajectory.judgement: The fixings fix the trim, so the plate cannot be resized to solve a copy problem. Reading twenty four pages at page thumbnail scale is not reading them.
trajectory.produces: A twenty four page press file at the existing trim plus per record files, with the plates actually inspected at size.

trajectory.action: Create the direction selects board, add the graded location set and the licensed frame within the per call placement cap, re-sending only the entries the response names as failed, then write the standards note and the schedule handover.
trajectory.judgement: A 201 is partial success, and the vector system is not boardable so it belongs in the note instead. The note has to be specific enough that the next person who orders a sign does not invent something, which is what the owner actually asked for.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written standards and schedule handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What a foil stamp actually gives back. Foil has no single ink value: across one stroke it reads dark where it turns away from the light and near white and specular where it turns toward it, and the cream stock sits between the two. An ink level selection therefore returns a partial that looks entirely plausible, complete in some strokes and absent in others, with no count, no confidence and no flag saying anything is missing. Which strokes survive is a property of how the brochure happened to be lying when the photograph was taken. Only after the trace, viewed at the size the mark reproduces on a pale panel rather than at full canvas, does it become visible whether the oval rule is continuous, whether the interlock still reads as two letters, and whether the counters have closed.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter prevents it: the tracing tool takes no options at all, the only lever is what the raster prep hands it, and no reading of the photograph at preview scale distinguishes a specular flank from missing artwork. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that the monogram is stamped in foil and catches the light. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is a different derivation, selecting the cream stock and inverting, or filling a knockout plate against the inverted mask and tracing that instead of tracing the mask, and each of those is a different artwork with a different route.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-derive the monogram through a different route, judge the result again at reproduction size on the panel ground rather than at full canvas, and where a hairline cannot be recovered at all decide whether to author that element as path geometry consistent with what did survive or to tell the owner the rule cannot be recovered, then re-place the master everywhere it appears.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A monogram that looks correct in the handover file and closes into a solid blob on every door plate and every corridor panel on the property, delivered against a brief whose first sentence is that it has to still be their monogram.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises a monoline pictogram, and whether a symbol drawn for a corridor panel is still a symbol on a door plate. The pictograms are authored as unfilled stroked paths, which is the correct construction for a cut sign system, and the importer recomputes path geometry from the drawing's own coordinate space into rendered canvas units. Whether the stroke survives as a stroke, and whether its weight is recomputed with the geometry or carried across unchanged, is reported nowhere and is knowable only from the returned markup. If the weight does not travel with the geometry, the symbol placed at plate size arrives carrying the corridor panel's weight and reads as a filled blot while the corridor panel itself is perfect, and the document's rendition returns the first artboard only, so the plate face and every panel after the first cannot be looked at any other way.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the normalisation happens at import and the import is downstream of every authoring decision, and doing it right the first time presumes knowing which of several plausible constructions survives, which no tool reports and no checklist enumerates. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks only for eight symbols that look like the monogram drew them, and the acceptance line about drawing each pictogram for its own size is the client's craft requirement, not a disclosure about an importer. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is to author a separate optical cut of each symbol for each destination size, which is a different set of drawings, not the same drawing re-exported.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Draw a second optical cut of all eight symbols for the small destination, re-decide the panel value relationships now that the small symbol's weight has changed, re-author, re-upload, re-run the readiness check, re-export, and audit every root from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Twenty four door plates and every secondary panel carrying eight filled blots where the facility symbols should be, in a document that reported success at every step and whose one previewable page looks immaculate.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: That the plate does not overflow, it stops. The name line on the 2016 artwork sits in a fixed measure frame sized to the longest name the property had in 2016, and a longer name does not spill, reflow, overset or flag: it simply stops rendering partway through, so the merged page is well formed, correctly laid out and quietly short. At page thumbnail scale twenty four plates all look right. Which of the twenty four are short depends on the interaction between the actual string, the face and the weight finally chosen, so it cannot be predicted from the data file, and the Spanish line and the English line fail at different lengths. The multi record raster route compounds it by returning files in an order that does not match the labels, so naming a per record file by its position asserts an identity that was never checked.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it: the frame's measure comes from artwork the property already owns and cannot be resized because the fixings are drilled, and the truncation point is a function of the type system, which is a later decision. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that the plates must be the same size as the ones on the doors now, and the acceptance line about names reading in full is the client's requirement, not a warning that a frame truncates. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is a decision, either a per facility naming convention agreed against the property's own signage language, or a change to the type system that then propagates back through every panel in the document, plus one name escalated to the owner because it cannot fit at any legible size.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Read all twenty four plates at plate size in both languages, decide per affected facility between abbreviation, a type change that reaches back into the whole system, and escalation, then rebuild the mapping and re-merge, and confirm per record identity through a route that guarantees it rather than through the order of a returned list.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Plates screwed to doors reading Coastal Terrace and Suns and Pabellon de Tenis y Tie, cut in the fabricator's substrate at the property's expense, with the merged file having reported success and looked correct on screen.
