decision_gates: Which deliverables need an authored fixed canvas document at true cut sizes and which need a record per page run, given that only one surface composes free form layout and only one produces volume personalisation.
Selection wording on the foil stamp: naming the brochure or the stock takes the board, naming the stamp's own visual properties takes the mark, and neither route reports what it left behind.
Which recovery route the monogram needs, and what to do about an element the photograph simply does not contain: author it consistently, or tell the owner it cannot be recovered.
Whether the four existing signs are one family or two, and which of the two the new system should sit with, when the owner has not noticed they are two.
Monoline construction versus solid glyph for the pictograms, argued against the monogram's own construction rather than chosen freely.
How much contrast the panels carry. At this band restraint is the design and a guest who cannot find the spa is the worse failure, so where that line sits is the central call.
Whether a symbol drawn for a corridor panel can be the same drawing on a door plate, or whether the small destination needs its own optical cut.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a quiet upscale property and a fabricator's minimum legible height, plus the real numeric weight per family.
What to do with three facilities that have no photograph and two frames that are the same wall, when the schedule asserts ten mount points.
Per facility naming when the plate's measure is fixed by fixings already drilled: abbreviate to a convention, change the type system and propagate it back through every panel, or escalate.
How per record identity is guaranteed for the fabricator, given that the order of a returned list is not evidence of what a file contains.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the photographs into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of resort signs. IDENTITY: this is the monogram a designer made for this property and stamped on a 2019 brochure, and the client's own sentence is that it has to be their monogram and not a new one drawn to look like it, which is exactly what a generated mark is. SPEC: the fabricator cuts to a fixed size list with a stated clear space and a minimum legible type height, the door plates must land at the 2016 trim because the fixings are already drilled, and there are twenty four of them with two languages each, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the property will order signs from this system for years and explicitly asked for standards so the next person does not invent something, so a flat picture of a sign is the opposite of the deliverable. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did the foil actually give the oval rule back, is the symbol on the plate still a symbol, does this plate say Coastal Terrace or Coastal Terrace and Suns.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. IMAGING: select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, fill_area, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs, auto_straighten and vectorize are verified headless across 27 live calls, and an ink level mark was recovered off a photographed printed surface with counters correctly excluded. The recovery checkpoint rests on documented findings rather than assumptions: the substrate versus ink prompt asymmetry (the same photograph returning either a 154,926 pixel object mask or a 9,372 pixel ink mask depending only on wording), the silent partial selection on compound marks that drops elements while succeeding, the missing viewBox, and the opaque full canvas path at index zero. EXPRESS: multiple roots at mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, absolute physical units resolve exactly at 96 dpi (210mm by 297mm to 794 by 1123 px, with mm child coordinates converted), a table survives as a real table with per cell text and strokes, and inline SVG becomes native editable vector with path data recomputed from the drawing's coordinate space into rendered pixels, which is the exact mechanism the pictogram checkpoint turns on. The rendition preview is documented as first artboard only, which is why verification is split between the rendition and the returned per canvas markup, and the right anchored auto sized wrapper collapse is a verified failure that the acceptance bar scores. Transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined photography passes the 70 KB threshold immediately. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt as generator and validator, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout and document_render_layout are all verified headless and synchronous, one record per page for PDF is verified with page count equal to row count, frame granularity from a PDF is verified as not under the author's control, per record identity is taken through the verified createSeparateFiles or recordRange routes because multi record raster URLs came back reversed, and press resolution is taken through document_render_layout because merge output silently ignores resolution. No bleed is claimed, since a PDF derived template carries none, and pdfPreset is never passed. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end, including the non standard numeric weights and the display cut reached by its own slug. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed, a real full resolution licensed JPEG, and boards persisting with a cap of 12 placements per call and 201 meaning partial. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no photo compositing of any kind including the re-carved wall mockup, no upscaling, no OCR, no text to image, no generative fill, no variable QR, no fill_text, no animate_design, no batch above 20.

engagement_title: Ridgeway Rovers kit refresh: recover a crest that survives only as stitching, rebuild the club's hand drawn numbering as cuttable artwork, and carry both onto twenty four signed off back of shirt sheets, a supplier spec and a committee board
vertical: Sports and recreation, grassroots amateur football, a village club near Cirencester in the English Cotswolds with two senior sides, a veterans XI and four junior age groups, printing through one local kit supplier
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork jersey numbering brief (cand_46, db_i 823), in which a custom football kit shop asks for its signature numbering rebuilt as clean, print ready vector artwork with consistent stroke widths and even spacing for heat transfer and flock production, worked up from photographed reference sheets as original geometry rather than lifted from a proprietary font file. The shop is laundered to a fictional village club, Ridgeway Rovers FC; no real club, competition, player, supplier or typeface is named. Co-anchor: the Freelancer.com brief 'Realistic Textile Embroidery Design', quoted verbatim in the ledger ('a skilled embroidery designer to create a realistic logo. Requirements: Realism style, Medium size (3-6 inches)'), which pins the crest to an embroidered artefact at a small physical reproduction size rather than a flat scan, plus the companion candidate 'Premium Heritage Apparel Identity System & Factory-Ready Vector Engineering', whose framing is to translate an existing concept into factory ready vector engineering. The STRENGTHEN verdict keeps that concept and deliverable set; what the v3 audit adds is reach, since an ink level selection recovers a mark off a stitched surface, the supplier's own press PDF converts into a live merge template, and HTML authoring gives the spec and board as one native editable document.
client_one_liner: Our crest exists nowhere except stitched on last year's shirts, our numbers and letters were drawn by hand in the nineties on two sheets of graph paper, and the supplier needs everything by the end of the month.
client_brief:
Ridgeway Rovers FC, kit refresh for the coming season

We are a village club near Cirencester. Two senior sides, a veterans XI and four junior age groups. Everything we print goes through one local kit supplier, and this year we change shirts for the first time since 2019.

The crest. It exists on the shirts and nowhere else. When our old kit secretary moved away he took the artwork with him, and what we have is a photograph one of the parents took of the crest stitched on last season's home shirt. We need it back as proper artwork we can hand to any supplier: the crest as it is, a single ink version for the shirt breast and the training tops, and a version that works on the navy away shirt.

The numbering. Our numbers and letters were drawn by hand by a founding member in the nineties and they are genuinely ours, nobody else has them. Two sheets survive, one of the alphabet and one of the digits, both in marker on graph paper, both photographed on someone's kitchen table. We want them rebuilt as clean artwork with even, consistent strokes so the supplier can cut them.

The squad. Twenty four players. We need a back of shirt sheet per player showing their name and number, laid out the way the supplier's own sheet does it, one player per page, because the parents sign each one off before anything is cut. Last year's sheet from the supplier is attached and that is the format they want back.

We also need a sheet for the supplier showing the colours, the sizes and where things sit on the shirt, and a board showing the home and the away shirt with the crest on them, so the committee can see it before we commit the money.

Shirts are twenty eight to forty five dollars and the buyers are players and parents. It should look like a proper club, not a franchise and not a school project. And a note telling us anything we ought to know.
price_band_and_audience: Grassroots kit at 28 to 45 dollars a shirt, bought by players and by parents paying for a child's fourth kit in five years. The band is load bearing in the artwork itself: at this price the supplier cuts numbering as one robust spot colour in heat press vinyl or flock, so the glyphs must reduce to a single solid generously weighted closed geometry with no thin joins, no inline, no outline and no second colour. A pro tier sublimated number with a keyline and a gradient is not merely expensive here, it is uncuttable and the supplier bounces it. Push the other way into clip art blockiness and a club whose crest has been stitched on shirts since 1974 looks supermarket rebranded. The same tension runs through the crest, since holding as one ink at shirt breast size is a different drawing decision from a full colour crest that only appears large. A real posted job of this shape runs 700 to 1,600 dollars fixed.

acceptance_bar: The crest is placeable artwork rather than a picture of a crest: scalable, a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle underneath, delivered as the crest, a single ink version and a version that holds on navy.
Every element that is on the shirt is on the recovered crest. A crest that is recognisable but missing an interior element is not the crest.
The crest still reads at the size it reproduces on the shirt breast, not only at full canvas.
Thirty six glyphs are delivered, and the letters and the digits read as ONE set when a name sits above a number at back of shirt proportion.
No glyph carries the graph rule, a stray blue path or an unclosed counter, and every glyph is a single closed spot colour shape the supplier can cut.
Anything the drawn sheets cannot supply for this squad is named in writing rather than substituted silently.
Twenty four back of shirt pages exist, one player per page, with every field the supplier's sheet carries populated on every page.
Each player's full name renders complete on their own page. A name that stops at the frame edge fails even though the page count is right.
The proof that carries a player's name is that player's proof. A proof named for one player showing another is a rejected sheet, not a filing error.
No delivered raster exceeds the pixel dimensions of the frame it derives from.

The spec and both boards arrive as ONE editable file, each keeping its own canvas size, crest as live vector shapes, words as retypable text, delivered with the self contained source it was built from.
On BOTH the home and away board the applied number reads as printed on the shirt rather than as a flat shape laid over a photograph.
One type system across the spec and both boards, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer and the actual weight used.
The note states what was recovered, what was rebuilt, every reconciliation against the squad list, and anything the club should know before handing this to a second supplier.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and decide which deliverable belongs on which surface.
trajectory.judgement: Twenty four sheets in the supplier's format at one player per page is a record per page run; the spec and boards are collateral the club must edit later, which only authored fixed canvas layout gives. The brief pins both, so there is nothing to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A surface plan per deliverable and the confirmed account tier.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline: a manifest keyed by role, so that forty artefacts later the agent still knows which URL is which sheet.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Look at everything before deciding anything: the crest frame, both drawn sheets, both blank shirt frames, and the squad list read against what the sheets actually contain.
trajectory.judgement: The client asserts an alphabet and a set of digits. Only the sheets can settle whether the squad's names are spellable from them, and counting cells is not reading them. The two blanks must be judged against each other, not each alone.
trajectory.produces: A triage note on crest condition, sheet character, blank illuminants and a first name to glyph reconciliation.

trajectory.action: Straighten the two drawn sheets and the crest frame where they sit off level, before any crop or bounds decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes and eats edge pixels so it cannot follow a crop, and a glyph traced off a rotated sheet carries the rotation into the cut file.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Select the crest off the shirt by naming the stitching's own visual properties rather than the garment, set polarity for tracing, and crop to the selection's returned bounds.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the entire gate: naming the shirt pulls the selection to the cloth. The fold shadow side has almost no separation, so the right of the crest is not guaranteed to behave like the left, and background removal is the wrong instrument on an enclosed ring.
trajectory.produces: A crest plate at native scale with its selection bounds recorded.

trajectory.action: Trace the crest plate, inject a viewBox, remove the opaque full canvas ground path, and derive the single ink and reversed variants.
trajectory.judgement: Tracing takes no options at all, so everything is decided in the raster prep. The single ink version is a different drawing decision from a reduction, because elements that survive by colour separation alone stop working at shirt breast size in one colour.
trajectory.produces: A crest as scalable transparent geometry plus single ink and reversed derivatives.

trajectory.action: Separate the drawn marker strokes on each sheet from the printed graph rule, one sheet at a time, and prepare each raster so the strokes are solid and closed.
trajectory.judgement: The graph rule is dark enough to become geometry. Selecting the ink by its own colour and medium rather than by the paper keeps the grid out, and the raster prep is the only lever the trace responds to.
trajectory.produces: Two clean glyph rasters carrying strokes and nothing else.

trajectory.action: Trace both sheets, hygiene each glyph, and lay a sample name above a sample number at back of shirt proportion to judge the set as a set.
trajectory.judgement: Thirty six glyphs that each look right individually are not a set. A set is judged only where a name sits above a number at the proportion the shirt uses, which is also where a cutter's tolerance is judged.
trajectory.produces: A thirty six glyph vector set with a proportion test of the pairing.

trajectory.action: Reconcile the finished glyph set against every surname and initial the squad list needs, and write down what the sheets cannot supply.
trajectory.judgement: The club believes it has an alphabet; what it has is what was drawn. Naming a gap in writing is a deliverable, inventing a glyph in the founder's hand is not the commission and is not honest.
trajectory.produces: A reconciliation of squad names against available glyphs, with gaps named.

trajectory.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, and Adobe Stock
trajectory.action: Bring the two blank shirt frames toward one target with masked corrections, then license one camera scale garment frame using short generic queries with photography filtered and generative candidates excluded.
trajectory.judgement: Two evenings under a warm domestic light is not one shoot, and hue moves hold only at moderate range, so there is a real limit on how far purple returns to navy. The licensed frame is clean and large but is not the club's shirt, and that trade must be decided rather than defaulted.
trajectory.produces: Two corrected blank plates with a parameter log, and one licensed frame used or rejected with a reason.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged against a village club at this band, and it must stay subordinate to the club's drawn numbering. Weight cannot be inferred from a style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight per role.

trajectory.action: Convert the supplier's press PDF, export the round tripped structure, and read the real frame inventory and true story text out of it rather than out of any summary.
trajectory.judgement: What a converted PDF exposes as editable frames is not under anyone's control and is not what the printed page implies, so the inventory must be read before any mapping is promised.
trajectory.produces: A frame inventory with bounds and applied type, and the story text as it actually is.

trajectory.action: Build the field mapping, validate it, build the merge template, then round trip the result and confirm every expected placeholder is genuinely present in the story.
trajectory.judgement: A validator reporting valid and a build reporting success are statements about the request, not about the document. The only evidence a field landed is finding it in the rebuilt document.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholder inventory was confirmed by inspection, not by response text.

trajectory.action: Merge all twenty four records one to a page and produce the per player proofs the parents sign off from, naming each file to its player.
trajectory.judgement: Page count equal to row count is necessary and weak. Identity per page is what the parents are signing, and the route that guarantees identity is not the cheapest route.
trajectory.produces: A twenty four page press ready set and twenty four named per player proofs.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML carrying the supplier spec and the home and away boards at their own canvas sizes, inlining every photograph as image data, placing crest and glyph specimen as inline SVG in explicitly sized top left anchored wrappers, declaring family and weight on every text element.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override collapses a mixed size set. The design work is making the placement heights read as instructions to a cutter rather than as decoration.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML carrying the spec and both boards, retained as the durable source.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by uploaded URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the rendition and look at canvas one, and parse the returned per canvas markup for the rest.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition only ever renders the first artboard. Looking at page one is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document, an inspected first canvas, and a markup audit for the rest.

trajectory.action: Create the sign off board, add the crest proofs, glyph specimen, shirt plates and licensed frame within the per call placement cap, re sending only what the response names as failed, then write the handover note.
trajectory.judgement: A 201 is partial success, and vector artwork is not boardable, so the crest goes to the board as a proof and to the club as a file. The note must be specific enough that a second supplier does not repeat the archaeology.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the selection that fed the trace actually contained the whole crest. A selection naming a compound stitched lockup as one thing returns a mask that is clean, binary and crest shaped, and can silently omit interior elements: here the ring and the shield outline come back while the hairline rule and the ram's head do not. Nothing in the response says anything is missing, the mask has no soft edge to give it away because these masks carry no intermediate values at all, and the trace of it is a competent looking crest. Which elements survive is a property of this photograph's own local contrast, including the fold shadow across the right third, and cannot be read off the frame beforehand.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it and no parameter controls it, because the omission happens inside one selection call whose only input is a phrase, and selecting four elements separately as an opening move is speculative spend against a possibility nobody has raised. Nothing states it: the brief says only that the crest is stitched on a shirt. It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a different chain, per element selections composited and re traced.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re select ring, rule, shield and ram's head as separate masks each named by its own visual properties, handle the fold shadow side separately, composite, re trace, re do the hygiene, and re derive both variants before any of them reach the merge template or the boards.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A club whose crest has been on its shirts since 1974 is handed a crest with its centre motif missing, stamped onto twenty four sheets, the supplier spec and both boards, having passed every response check on the way.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the fields the mapping asked for actually landed in the merge template. The readout of the converted supplier PDF's editable text is lossy: it omits one run while keeping that run's line break, so the returned string still reads as well formed prose with no sign of a gap, and every offset computed from it past that point is short by exactly the omitted run's length. The validator then reports the mapping valid with zero warnings and the placeholder build reports completed successfully, while two of the five fields are simply absent. No response in the chain says so, and the only way to learn it is to round trip the built template and look inside its stories for the placeholders you asked for.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering does not dodge it, because the lossy readout is the only readout the mapping tool offers and the offsets must come from somewhere; doing it right first time presumes knowing that this document's summary drops a run, which no response, warning or schema states. Nothing states it: the brief only describes a supplier sheet format. It is not a propagation re run, because the response derives offsets from a different source, the document's own reconstructed story text.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reconstruct each frame's true story text from its own content runs, recompute every offset against that string, rebuild the mapping and the template, and re inspect for all five placeholders before merging a single record.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Twenty four sheets that pass a page count check and go to the parents with two fields blank on every page, so the sign off the exercise exists to obtain is worthless and the supplier cuts from an incomplete instruction.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the one construct the committee boards depend on. The club has to see the number as it will sit on the shirt, which authored the natural way means letting the flat number take the cloth's folds through a blending mode, or softening its contact edge. The importer discards a blending mode entirely and renders the element as a plain opaque shape, and discards a blur filter outright, both at full success with no warning of any kind. The returned per canvas markup is the only channel that reports it, and the rendition returns the first artboard only, so the away board can be checked no other way.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the drop happens at import and the import is the last step, and doing it right first time presumes knowing which of several plausible constructions survives, which no tool reports and no checklist enumerates. Nothing states it: the brief asks for a board the committee can judge. It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a DIFFERENT upstream asset, the number carried into the raster on the garment plate, or a board recomposed onto flat cloth.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the garment plates so the number is part of the raster, or recompose both boards around the flat cloth, re author the HTML, re upload, re run the readiness check, re export, and audit both boards from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A committee approves a kit off a board where the number floats as a flat sticker on the home shirt and, on the away board nobody opened, may not read at all, with the export having reported success throughout.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are a record per page run and which need an authored fixed canvas document, given only one surface composes free form layout and only one produces one record per page.

Selection wording on the crest: naming the garment takes the cloth, naming the stitching's own visual properties takes the mark, and background removal on an enclosed ring is the wrong instrument entirely.
Whether the single ink crest is a reduction of the full crest or a different drawing, judged at shirt breast size rather than at full canvas.
How to keep a printed graph rule out of a trace when tracing takes no options and raster prep is the only lever.
Whether two sheets drawn a decade apart with different pens can be brought to one set by re preparing a raster, or whether one has to be re drawn in geometry.
What to do about glyphs the squad needs and the sheets do not have, including an apostrophe that was never drawn, when inventing one is not the commission.
Whether the duplicated shirt number and the repeated surname are the client's problem to settle or the deliverable's to encode, and how the supplier's naming rule decides it.
Which route guarantees that a proof named for a player is that player's proof, when the cheapest route does not.
Whether the club's own badly lit shirt photographs or a licensed camera scale frame carries the board, given hue moves hold only at moderate range.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a village club at this band and kept subordinate to the club's drawn numbering.
How much the supplier spec should read as an instruction sheet rather than a designed page, given its reader is a person with a cutter and a heat press.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns a handsome football crest and a handsome set of numbers. IDENTITY: this crest has been stitched on this club's shirts since 1974 and this alphabet was drawn by a named founding member, so a regenerated crest is a different club's badge and a regenerated alphabet is somebody else's numbering, which is exactly what the original commission forbids by asking for original geometry rebuilt from the reference sheets. SPEC: the supplier needs cuttable single colour closed geometry, thirty six glyphs, and twenty four sheets in its own page format at one player per page with proofs whose identity can be checked against a roster, none of which a generated image is or can be verified to be. EDITABILITY: the spec and boards are defined by being editable, because the squad changes every season and a village club cannot re commission. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did the selection contain the whole crest, did the placeholders actually land, did the number survive the import as something that reads as printed.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. IMAGING: auto_straighten, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with tradeoffs, fill_area, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, remove_background and vectorize are verified headless across 27 live calls, including extracting ink level graphics off a photographed surface with counters correctly excluded. The crest checkpoint rests on the documented finding that selection is unreliably partial on compound marks (a circular badge prompt returned the type ring and outer arcs and silently dropped the inner circle rule and the central leaf, succeeding and looking plausible), plus the solid disc failure of remove_background on an enclosed ring, the substrate versus ink prompt asymmetry, and masks being fully binary with zero intermediate values. Vector hygiene is real work because vectorize emits no viewBox, always writes an opaque full canvas rect at path zero, and takes no options at all. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt as readout and validator, prepare_indd_merge_template and document_merge_data_layout are verified end to end from a bare press PDF, with one record per page confirmed for PDF output. The mapping checkpoint is the documented headline trap: textContent dropped a 17 character run while keeping its line break, the validator returned VALID with zero warnings, prepare returned completed successfully, and only 3 of 5 mappings landed, invisible until the merged output. Per record identity is producible via createSeparateFiles or a recordRange loop, and multi record raster URLs are documented as returning reversed with lying labels, which is why the bar gates identity rather than position. No bleed is claimed. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, the product is a genuine editable dcx findable by asset_search, mix-blend-mode and filter blur are both documented as dropped at HTTP success, and the rendition preview is PAGE 1 ONLY. Transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined photography passes 70 KB immediately, and photographs must be base64 inlined because every external URL renders as an empty grey box. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end, with the non standard numeric weight trap and the all or nothing kit call both live. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed, license returned a real 7360x4912 JPEG, boards cap at 12 placements per call, 201 means partial, vector unsupported. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no upscaling, no compositing, no OCR, no text-to-image, no variable QR, no fill_text, no animate_design, no create_firefly_board, no photo reaching Express as a URL, no batch above 20.

engagement_title: Wharfside Folk Festival twentieth year: take one approved painting to a four ink hand pulled screen programme, recover a wordmark that exists only as paint on a harbour shed, and carry the same separations onto a poster, a handbill, a two ink tee and fourteen act cards
vertical: Arts, culture and music, a three night independent folk festival on the working harbour at Fairhaven, Maine, printed since 2006 by a two person hand screen shop two streets away
real_brief_anchor: Anchored to the Upwork commemorative poster brief quoted in the ledger: a story driven twentieth anniversary poster in a 'festival posters, folk-art illustration, screenprint aesthetics' style, weaving landmarks and community traditions into one cohesive composition. The real client is a named school in Louisiana and is fully laundered here: no real institution, denomination, figure, place or person appears anywhere in this spec. The REBUILD verdict is taken literally, because the original concept sat almost entirely on one surface, a poster comp. The commission that brief actually implies, once the artwork is approved, is the production engineering that follows it, which is what a screen shop needs and what the original spec never delivered. So it is re carved as the separation programme: the approved illustration becomes something a hand press can pull at four inks plus the paper, in a registration order, reused across a poster, a handbill, a two ink shirt and a per act card run, with the festival's hand painted wordmark recovered off the shed it has lived on since 2006. That is a far larger job than composing a poster, it lands on five real connector surfaces, and it is the kind of multi part rollout actually posted on freelance marketplaces.
client_one_liner: The painting is approved and the committee loves it, but the shop that has printed us since the beginning pulls by hand with four inks plus the paper, and everything we print this year has to come off that press.
client_brief:
Wharfside Folk Festival, twentieth year

We run three nights of folk music on the old working harbour at Fairhaven every September. This is our twentieth year and we want the print to feel like it.

We commissioned an illustration from a painter who lives here: the harbour, the shed, the crowd on the quay, the hills behind. It is approved, it is scanned, and the committee loves it. It is a painting.

The problem is how we print. Everything goes through a screen shop two streets away who have printed this festival since the beginning. They pull by hand, on a press that runs four inks plus the colour of the paper. That limit is not a compromise we are making, it is why our posters look the way they do and why people frame them. So the artwork has to become something they can actually pull: separate layers, one per ink, in an order they can register, on the stock we use.

We need the poster at the size we really print it, the big one that goes on the shed and in shop windows. We need a handbill of the same thing for the tables and the tourist office. We need the key part of the picture reduced far enough that the shop can pull it on a shirt, where they can only give us two inks. And we need a sheet for the shop listing the inks, the order they go down in and the marks they register to.

Our wordmark has been hand painted on the harbour shed since 2006 and that painted lettering is the wordmark. There is no file and there never was one. We need it back as artwork.

We also print a card for each act, one per act, fourteen this year, in the same house style, from the shop's own card format. Last year's card is attached.

Tickets are thirty five to sixty dollars and the posters sell afterwards as twenty dollar keepsakes.
price_band_and_audience: A community festival at 35 to 60 dollar tickets, with posters sold afterwards as 20 dollar framed keepsakes to an audience that already owns the last five years of them. The band points the opposite way from most price logic: the visible, slightly imperfect, hand pulled limited ink look IS the product here, so flat opaque ink, visible registration, the paper colour doing real work and a coarse tone screen are value rather than defects to design out. A slick full process reproduction would be cheaper to make, would read as corporate, would stop being worth twenty dollars on a wall, and would break continuity with nineteen years hanging in local kitchens. Push the other way into deliberate crudeness, three ink grunge and distressed edges, and it reads as a pastiche of a folk festival rather than one that has run since 2006. The judgement is which four inks buy the most of the painting, and that judgement is the commission. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,400 to 3,000 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: Independent three night folk music festival producing a screen printed poster programme and act cards for its twentieth year.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2006, on the working harbour at Fairhaven, Maine, a three night festival printed by a two person hand screen shop two streets away.
brand_identity.about: Wharfside is a three night folk festival on the working harbour at Fairhaven, in its twentieth year. Everything it prints comes off a two person hand screen shop that has printed the festival since the beginning, on a press that runs four inks plus the colour of the paper. The visible, hand pulled look is the festival's signature, and people frame the posters every year.
brand_identity.audience: Festival goers and locals at thirty five to sixty dollar tickets, many of whom already own the last five years of posters and buy the new one as a twenty dollar framed keepsake.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Community festival pricing, tickets thirty five to sixty dollars and posters sold afterwards at twenty dollars. The slightly imperfect hand pulled screen look is the value, not a corner cut.
brand_identity.typography: The wordmark is the hand painted lettering that has been on the harbour shed since 2006. Supporting type sits beside that painted hand without imitating it, set for flat opaque ink and visible registration. Coarse tone screens carry the sky and water.
brand_identity.voice: Warm, plainspoken, of the place. Example line: Three nights of folk on the old harbour, twenty years and counting.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The wordmark exists only as white paint on the weathered timber of the harbour shed, photographed from the quay, with no file and none ever made. The approved twentieth year illustration exists as a single flattened scan of a gouache and watercolour painting, no layers. The screen shop's own act card from last year is on file as the format.
brand_identity.values: Keeping the hand pulled, limited ink look that makes the posters worth framing, and staying continuous with nineteen years already hanging in local kitchens.

assets_supplied.name: wharfside_artwork_master.png (4200 x 5900)

assets_supplied.hidden_defect: What reads as a handful of flat areas is a wash with hundreds of intermediate values, and two fields that look separate, the rust of the shed roofs and the ochre of the hillside behind them, run to nearly the same value where they meet along the ridge, so a selection naming either comes back as a clean, plausible, binary mask that has quietly swallowed the other. acceptance_bar: The poster resolves to four inks plus the colour of the paper. Not four plus a fifth that crept in, and not three because two of them merged.
Every plate is a plate: one ink, its own layer, separable, in a stated order the shop can register, with registration marks common to all of them.
No area of the painting is missing from the separation and none appears on two plates where the shop cannot trap it. A set that reassembles into a picture the committee would not recognise fails.
The teal in the water either has an ink of its own or is consciously and explicitly given up. It is not allowed to disappear without a decision being recorded.
The tone in the sky and water survives as a screen the shop can pull, and it reads AS A SCREEN at both the poster's true printed size and the handbill's.
The handbill is the same design, not a different one, and it is judged at its own true printed size rather than as a scaled picture of the poster.
The shirt version reduces to two inks and still reads as this festival's motif at chest size on cloth, with no line finer than the shop's stated minimum.

The wordmark is placeable artwork rather than a picture of a wall: scalable, a real viewBox, no opaque full canvas rectangle underneath, counters open, camera taper corrected, every letter present including those in the roof shadow.
Fourteen act cards exist, one act per page, every field the shop's card carries populated on every page, and every act name rendering complete at true measure.
The portraits are handled as one decision rather than fourteen, and any act that cannot be given one is named rather than left blank.
No delivered raster exceeds the pixel dimensions of the frame it derives from.

Poster, handbill, shirt canvas and shop spec arrive as ONE editable file, each keeping its own canvas size, wordmark as live vector shapes, words as retypable text, delivered with the self contained source it was built from.
One type system across everything, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer and the actual weight used.
The spec sheet is written for the person at the press: inks, the order they go down in, what registers to what, and what to do where two plates meet.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and decide which deliverable belongs on which surface before touching the painting.
trajectory.judgement: Fourteen cards at one act per page is a record per page run; poster, handbill, shirt and spec are fixed physical canvases and only authored layout gives them at true size. The brief pins both, so there is nothing to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A surface plan per deliverable and the confirmed account tier.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline, and it matters more here because a separation run generates more intermediate plates than anything else in the job.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Read the painting before carving it: what the actual colour fields are, where they meet, what is wash and what is flat, and what four inks plus the paper have to buy.
trajectory.judgement: Four inks is not four colours in the picture, it is four decisions about which four buy the most of it. The paper is one of the five, and using it as a colour rather than a background is the difference between a screen print and a reproduction.
trajectory.produces: A written ink plan naming each proposed ink, what it carries and what it gives up.

trajectory.action: Carve the first pass of plates: select each field by its own material and colour rather than by the object carrying it, set polarity deliberately, and fill each selection to its plate ink.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the entire gate and selections come back fully binary, so there is no soft edge to warn that a field took more than it should. Polarity before any fill or trace decides whether a plate is the field or its inverse.
trajectory.produces: A first plate set, one file per proposed ink, recorded against the ink plan.

trajectory.action: Lay the plates beside one another and against the painting, and judge whether the set reassembles into the picture the committee approved.
trajectory.judgement: A plate is judged as part of a set, never alone. The question is whether the fields together account for the painting without overlap the shop cannot trap and without a gap the paper was not meant to fill.
trajectory.produces: A reassembly proof of the plate set against the approved painting.

trajectory.action: Convert the wash in the sky and water into a screen the press can pull, choosing a coarseness against the poster's true printed size.
trajectory.judgement: The screen has one lever, its coarseness, and no frequency control at all, so the whole decision is a single number judged by eye against a physical size. Colour rosettes are not a duotone, so a monochrome screen is the only honest route to a tonal plate.
trajectory.produces: A tone plate at a stated coarseness with the reasoning recorded.

trajectory.action: Recover the wordmark off the shed: select the paint by its own visual properties rather than the sign or the timber, correct polarity, crop to the returned bounds, trace, inject a viewBox and remove the opaque ground path.
trajectory.judgement: Naming the sign takes the plank. Disjoint lettering defeats a subject led knockout and enclosed counters cannot be punched by background removal at all. The camera taper and the roof shadow across the last letters are properties of this photograph, not of the wordmark.
trajectory.produces: The wordmark as scalable transparent geometry with its counters open.

trajectory.action: Reduce the key motif to two inks for the shirt, judged at chest size on cloth rather than at canvas size on screen.
trajectory.judgement: Two inks on cloth is a different drawing from four inks on paper, not a subset of it. The shop's stated minimum line weight is the hard floor, and detail that survives on stock closes up on a shirt.
trajectory.produces: A two ink shirt reduction with line weights judged against the shop's floor.

trajectory.action: License one camera scale frame of the paper stock with short generic queries and generative candidates excluded, then ask for font recommendations once per role, pull the style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The comp has to show ink on this stock, because at this band the paper is one of the five colours. The pairing is the agent's own and has to sit beside hand painted lettering without imitating it; weight cannot be inferred from a style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: One licensed IP clean stock frame and a one kit type system with family, foundry and weight per role.

trajectory.action: Author the poster and the shop spec at their true physical dimensions, inlining the plates as image data, placing wordmark and registration marks as inline SVG in explicitly sized top left anchored wrappers, and building the ink list as a real table.
trajectory.judgement: Absolute units resolve at a fixed density so a poster is genuinely poster sized rather than a large picture. A plate left as a URL is not a plate, and an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas. The spec's reader is the person at the press, not the committee.
trajectory.produces: A poster comp at true size and a spec sheet, both inside one authored document.

trajectory.action: Add the handbill and the shirt canvas as further roots at their own true sizes, reusing the same separations and type system, letting each root declare its own canvas.
trajectory.judgement: The client asked for the same design, not a second one, so the discipline is reuse. A global canvas override is exactly what collapses a mixed size set, so the sizes have to live in the document.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML carrying four canvases at four true physical sizes.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by uploaded URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the rendition and look at canvas one, and parse the returned per canvas markup for the rest.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition only ever renders the first artboard. Looking at the poster is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document, an inspected first canvas, and a markup audit for the other three.

trajectory.action: Normalise the eleven act portraits toward one family and reconcile them against the fourteen acts, deciding one treatment rather than eleven.
trajectory.judgement: A studio frame and a phone photograph in a bar do not reach one family by the same route, three frames are too small to reach card size without either a softer placement or a tighter crop than the panel implies, and two files are the same act.
trajectory.produces: A normalised portrait family with a parameter log and a reconciliation against the act list.

trajectory.action: Convert the shop's card PDF, export the round tripped structure, and read the real frame inventory and true story text out of it rather than out of any summary.
trajectory.judgement: What a converted PDF exposes as editable frames is not under anyone's control and is not what the printed page implies, so the inventory must be read before any mapping is promised.
trajectory.produces: A frame inventory with bounds and applied type, and the story text as it actually is.

trajectory.action: Build the mapping against that inventory, validate it, build the merge template, then round trip the result and confirm every expected placeholder is genuinely present before merging anything.
trajectory.judgement: A validator reporting valid and a build reporting success are statements about the request, not about the document. The only evidence a field landed is finding it in the rebuilt document.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholder inventory was confirmed by inspection.

trajectory.action: Merge all fourteen acts one to a page and render the shop's proof set, naming each file to its act.
trajectory.judgement: Page count equal to row count is necessary and weak. Identity per page is what the shop burns film from, and the route that guarantees identity is not the cheapest route.
trajectory.produces: A fourteen page press ready card set and fourteen named per act proofs.

trajectory.action: Create the plate proof board, add every plate, the reassembly proof, the tone plate, the shirt reduction and the wordmark proof within the per call placement cap, re sending only what the response names as failed, then write the shop facing note.
trajectory.judgement: A 201 is partial success, and vector artwork is not boardable, so the wordmark goes to the board as a proof and to the shop as a file. The note is written for the person at the press.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable plate proof board with nothing silently dropped, and the handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the painting actually separates into the fields the eye reads in it. Two fields that look distinct, the rust of the shed roofs and the ochre of the hillside behind them, run to nearly the same value along the ridge where they meet, so a selection naming either comes back as a clean, complete looking, fully binary mask that has quietly taken both. There is no soft edge to give it away because these masks carry no intermediate values at all, the call reports success, and the plate looks correct on its own. It becomes visible only when the plates are laid together and reassembled against the painting, at which point one ink is doing two jobs and the ridge has vanished.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it and no parameter controls it: selection by material is the only route to a field, its output is binary, and the tool exposes no confidence about what it took, so selecting every field twice with different phrasings as an opening move is speculative spend. Nothing states it: the brief says the press runs four inks plus the paper and nothing about the painting's values. It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a different carving strategy that changes the ink plan itself.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re open the ink plan, re carve the affected fields through a different selection strategy and polarity, re fill and re proof every plate touching the ridge, and re run the reassembly before anything downstream reuses the separations, since poster, handbill and shirt all inherit them.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A poster pulled in what the shop believes is four inks, in which the ridge line separating the town from the hills does not exist, printed on the shed and in every shop window and sold as a twentieth year keepsake beside nineteen years that do have it.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the tone plate reads as a screen at BOTH printed sizes. The screen has exactly one control, its coarseness, and no frequency parameter of any kind, so what it does is fixed in the raster and cannot be re specified per output. A coarseness chosen against the poster's true printed size, where it reads as an open hand pulled screen, is the same raster reproduced at roughly a third of that on the handbill, where the dots close into one another and the sky becomes a flat field, losing the tone the plate exists to carry. Both exports report success, both plates are correct in isolation, and the difference exists only as the relationship between one raster and two physical sizes.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the coarseness must be chosen before the plate exists and its adequacy is a function of a size that only exists once the layout does; doing it right first time presumes knowing where one raster stops reading across a three to one reduction, which no tool reports and no parameter expresses. Nothing states it: the brief asks for a handbill of the same thing. It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a SECOND tone plate at a different coarseness, so the handbill is no longer the same separation set as the poster.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Generate a second tone plate judged against the handbill's own printed size, decide whether the shirt needs a third, re author the affected canvases, re upload, re run the readiness check, re export, audit from the returned markup, and rewrite the spec so the press knows which screen belongs to which piece.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Handbills whose sky and water print as two flat slabs of ink where the poster has weather, handed out at the tourist office all season as the festival's own advertisement, with every export having reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the shop's card actually is underneath. The printed page shows act name, stage, set time and a portrait panel as four visibly separate blocks, so it reads as a four frame layout with a picture box. What the conversion exposes is not under anyone's control: this card's text was set as one continuous flow and its portrait panel was drawn rather than placed, so the document arrives as a single story with no graphic frame at all. There is nothing to bind a per act portrait to and the four fields cannot be addressed as four frames. Nothing in the conversion response says any of this, the document converts cleanly, and the only way to learn it is to export the round tripped structure and read the actual frame inventory.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it and nothing about the PDF predicts it, because frame granularity is a property of how the original was set, invisible in the printed page and in the file's appearance, so doing it right first time presumes knowing the answer before inspecting. Nothing states it: the brief says only that the shop's card format is attached. It is not a propagation re run, because the response changes both the mapping strategy and the deliverable shape.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Compute offset based mappings against the reconstructed story text rather than per frame bindings, decide whether the portraits leave the merge and become a separately delivered plate set the shop places by hand or whether the card is re cast as text only, tell the festival which it is, and rebuild and re verify the template before merging any of the fourteen.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Fourteen cards that merge, page for act, with the names and times landing wherever the offsets happened to point and the portrait panel showing last year's opening act on every single one.

verifiers_human.how: View the poster and the handbill each at their own true printed size, not at matched screen scale.

verifiers_human.text: The shirt reduction still reads as this festival's motif at chest size on cloth, with nothing finer than the shop's minimum.
verifiers_human.how: View the two ink reduction at chest size and check its thinnest line against the shop's stated floor.

verifiers_human.text: The recovered wordmark is the lettering on the shed, taper corrected and complete, not a tidy typeface that resembles it.
verifiers_human.how: Place the recovered wordmark beside the photograph at matched size and check letter for letter.

verifiers_human.text: The act portraits read as one family on the card set despite arriving from eleven different photographers.
verifiers_human.how: Lay the fourteen cards out together and judge the portraits as a set.

verifiers_human.text: The spec sheet is usable by the person at the press without asking a question.
verifiers_human.how: Read it as a printer would: can the inks, the order, the registration and the overlaps be worked from it alone.

verifiers_human.text: The work reads as a festival that has run since 2006 and sells 20 dollar keepsakes, not as a corporate reproduction and not as a pastiche of a folk poster.
verifiers_human.how: Judge ink choice, paper use, type and screen character against the stated band and audience.

decision_gates: Which four inks plus the paper buy the most of this painting, and what is consciously given up to stay inside the press.
Whether the paper is treated as a background or worked as one of the five colours, which is the difference between a screen print and a reproduction at this band.
How each field is named for selection, given that naming the object rather than the material pulls the mask elsewhere and the result is binary with no edge to warn you.
What happens to the fifth colour in the water: its own ink, folded into a neighbour, or explicitly surrendered and recorded.
The screen's coarseness, which is one number with no frequency control, judged against a physical printed size rather than against the file.
Whether the shirt is a reduction of the poster or its own drawing, given two inks, cloth and a stated minimum line weight.
Selection wording on the shed: naming the sign takes the plank, disjoint lettering defeats a subject led knockout, and enclosed counters cannot be punched by background removal at all.
One treatment for eleven portraits from eleven photographers, and what to do about the three acts with no portrait and the two files that are the same act.
Whether the act portraits belong inside the merged card at all, once the card's real structure is known.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged to sit beside hand painted lettering without imitating it, plus the real numeric weight per family.
Who the spec sheet is written for, since a sheet that pleases the committee and puzzles the press has failed.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the painting into a frontier image model and it returns a handsome folk festival poster. IDENTITY: the painting is a commissioned, approved, signed off work by a named local painter and nothing about it changes, so a regenerated poster is a different picture and the commission is void; the wordmark has been painted on the shed since 2006 and must be recovered rather than redrawn, because a redrawn wordmark is a rebrand nobody asked for. SPEC: the deliverable is not a picture at all, it is a set of separable single ink plates in a registration order a two person hand press can actually pull inside four inks plus the paper, plus fourteen cards at one act per page whose identity can be checked against a roster, none of which a generated image is or can be. EDITABILITY: poster, handbill, shirt and spec are defined by being editable, because the act list moves until the week of the festival. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality: did that mask take one field or two, does the screen still read at handbill size, does the shop's card actually have a picture box in it.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. IMAGING: select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, fill_area, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, halftone with a mask and with blackAndWhite true, monochromatic_tint, add_grain, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize, auto_straighten, remove_background and vectorize are verified headless across 27 live calls, and the spot plate route is listed explicitly as unlocked collateral: mask the mark, invert, halftone the art field at a chosen radius while the lettering stays crisp, then vectorize the lettering only plate, verified end to end with the polarity decision named as the craft. Material and texture selection by prompt is verified (a weathered painted wood plank surface returned a clean 672,398 pixel mask), which is what makes both the field carving and the shed recovery real. The first checkpoint rests on documented behaviour: masks are fully binary with zero intermediate values so there is no softness to warn you, and selection is documented as unreliably partial and plausible looking on compound subjects. The second rests on halftone having radius as its only lever with no LPI or frequency parameter, and on blackAndWhite false producing colour rosettes rather than a duotone. Vector hygiene is real work because vectorize emits no viewBox, always writes an opaque full canvas rect at path zero, and takes no options. EXPRESS: exact print canvases via absolute units are verified (297x420mm resolved to exactly 1123x1587 px at 96 dpi), mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, tables import as real tables with per cell strokes, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, and the rendition preview is PAGE 1 ONLY. Plates must be base64 inlined because every external URL renders as an empty grey box at full success, and transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined rasters pass 70 KB immediately. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt and prepare_indd_merge_template are verified end to end from a bare press PDF, with one record per page confirmed for PDF output. The third checkpoint is the documented frame granularity finding: a continuous text flow converted to exactly ONE TextFrame holding all six lines and ZERO graphic frames, with the doc stating plainly that you cannot spec mapping fields to distinct frames unless the source PDF's visual blocks are actually separated, and that you must export IDML and look first. Per record identity is producible via createSeparateFiles or a recordRange loop, multi record raster URLs are documented as reversed with lying labels, and no bleed is claimed. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end with the non standard numeric weight trap and the all or nothing kit call both live. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed, license returned a real 7360x4912 JPEG, boards cap at 12 placements per call, 201 means partial, vector unsupported. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no upscaling, no compositing, no OCR, no text-to-image, no generative fill or expand, no variable QR, no fill_text, no animate_design, no create_firefly_board, no photo reaching Express as a URL, no batch above 20.

engagement_title: Coble & Vane cask release: reduce a full-colour illustrated mark to a one-ink system that survives wax, stencil and cap, rebuild the printer's die sheet into a live twelve-cask run, and hand back the supplier sheet editable
vertical: Spirits & Craft Manufacturing (two-person coastal distillery, Northumberland, England, shop-direct plus roughly forty independent merchants)
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork product-packaging brief behind this ledger slot, a trading firm launching its first private-label line that needed an approved master logo extended into a working variant system, swappable per-SKU labels and single-colour cartons built as data-driven templates, plus a digital asset pack for suppliers. Laundered to a fictional coined brand, Coble & Vane; no real company, product, person or trademark is named. The ledger verdict was REBUILD, because as banked the concept sat on one surface: trace the logo, hand back four SVGs. A supplier-facing mark system is judged on the stamped and printed objects it lands on, and the client who commissions one almost always has a packaging run in flight and a printer holding the only copy of last year's artwork. VECTOR-08 restores that commission: a colour illustration that has to become one ink, a die sheet nobody at the distillery has opened, twelve cask releases needing labels, and a supplier sheet that has to stay editable.
client_one_liner: Twelve cask releases, one mark that only exists in full colour, and almost nothing we print is in colour, so the mark, the labels and the sheet that tells suppliers what to do all have to come back from one person before bottling starts.
client_brief:
Coble & Vane, cask release: the mark in one ink, this year's release labels, and a sheet that tells a supplier how to use them.

We are a two-person distillery on the Northumberland coast. Iris runs the still, I run everything else. Twelve cask releases a year, sold from the shop and through about forty independent merchants, bottles fifty-five to a hundred and twenty dollars.

Our mark was drawn for us six years ago by an illustrator who has since moved abroad. It is beautiful, it is in full colour, and it is very little use to us, because almost nothing we print is in colour. The wax on the bottle neck is one ink. The crate stencil is one ink. The cap is one ink. The shoulder emboss is not ink at all. Every time a supplier asks for a single-colour version, somebody here opens the colour file, does something to it and sends whatever comes out. No two have ever matched.

So, first: give us our mark in one ink, in whatever versions it genuinely needs to exist in, and a sheet a supplier can work from. Which version goes where, how much space to leave around it, what not to do to it. We want to hand that sheet to a wax supplier we have never met and never speak to them again. Keep it editable, because the release list changes every season.

Second: the release labels. Our printer has last year's file. We do not, and we never did. Keep the label as it is, change everything on it for this year's twelve casks, and send back something the printer can run, plus one file per cask, named so the bottling hall can pull the right one without opening it.

We have three phone photographs of our own packaging you can use, and if you need one more picture we will pay for it.

On tone: our bottles sit next to bottles at twelve dollars. Restrained, plenty of air, one ink doing the work. If anything in our own list looks wrong to you, say so before you make it.
price_band_and_audience: Bottles 55 to 120 dollars (standard gin 55, cask-strength single malt 95 to 120). Buyer 30 to 55 buying a gift or a considered bottle, plus the merchant deciding whether the bottle earns its shelf facing. The band is load-bearing: at this tier the one-ink treatments read as restraint and heritage, a single deep ink, generous clear space, emboss and wax finishes carrying the value, and a supplier sheet written as instruction rather than advertisement. A twelve-dollar brand would take the opposite answer, louder and higher-contrast, and would not care whether the stencil and foil versions were different drawings. An agent that ships a loud, dense set has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,800 to 3,500 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: A two-person coastal distillery making small-batch gin and cask-strength single malt, sold shop-direct and through independent merchants.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2020, on the Northumberland coast, England. A two-person distillery: Iris runs the still, her partner runs everything else.
brand_identity.about: Coble & Vane is a working distillery on a stretch of the North Sea coast, named for the flat-bottomed fishing boat that once beached below the still house. We release twelve casks a year and nothing we cannot stand behind. The bottle is meant to earn its place on a shelf and in a hand, not to shout across the shop.
brand_identity.audience: Buyers aged 30 to 55 choosing a gift or a considered bottle, and the independent merchant deciding whether the bottle earns its shelf facing. People who read a label closely and reward restraint.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Bottles 55 to 120 dollars: standard gin at 55, cask-strength single malt from 95 to 120. Upper-craft tier, sitting deliberately apart from the twelve-dollar shelf. Value is carried by finish, emboss and wax rather than by loud print.
brand_identity.typography: Display in an engraved-feeling serif with real weight in the caps, set with generous letter spacing. Text in a quiet humanist sans for supplier and label copy. The type stays out of the way and lets a single ink do the work.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, dry, unhurried. Written as instruction, not advertisement. Example line: "One ink, plenty of air, and nothing shiny. If our own list looks wrong to you, say so before you make it."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The house mark was drawn six years ago by an illustrator who has since moved abroad and cannot be reached. It survives only as a full-colour illustration flattened to a single PNG. There are no vector files, no one-ink versions, and no supplier guidance sheet. Every single-colour version a supplier has ever received was improvised from that one file, and no two have matched.
brand_identity.values: Restraint and honesty. One deep ink, generous clear space, and finishes that carry the value instead of the print. Say plainly what a version can and cannot do.

assets_supplied.name: house_mark_colour.png (3600 x 3600)
assets_supplied.kind: The distillery's only surviving copy of its mark: a full-colour engraved-style illustration of a beached coble under a rope ring carrying the two family names, flattened to PNG.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our mark as she drew it. This file is all we have and there is nobody to ask for anything else."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two faults, neither stated. Hull, sail and water are shaded with fine engraved cross-hatch and the rope ring is two interleaved strands in two closely related inks, so the mark's weight comes from tone rather than line and reducing it to one ink is a decision about what stops existing rather than a trace. It was also composited over a warm laid-paper texture and flattened, so any preparation separating ink from ground by lightness takes part of the paper with it.

assets_supplied.name: cask_labels_2025_PRINT.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The printer's flat press PDF for last season's cask release labels, from a real page layout with embedded font subsets, one page, 210 x 148 mm.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What Redgate ran for us last year. We have never opened it. Keep the label as it is."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two structural facts nobody at the distillery could tell you and nothing in the PDF announces. The page is not a label, it is the die sheet: front and back labels sit side by side because that is how the cutter is set, so one cask is one sheet carrying two dissimilar labels. And the back label's whole copy block came across as one continuous story rather than addressable lines, with the mapping readout silently omitting one run so every offset past it is short while the validator still reports the mapping valid.

assets_supplied.name: cask_release_2026.csv
assets_supplied.kind: The cask book export, one row per release: cask number, expression name, strength, filling date, bottling date, outturn, volume, distilled-at line, photo filename.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "This year's twelve, straight out of the cask book. Iris writes the expression names herself and they go on the label as written."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two faults, neither stated. Three casks were re-numbered after a re-racking last autumn and the photo column still carries their old numbers, so three rows bind a photograph of the wrong cask while every filename resolves. And the filling and bottling dates are transposed on two adjacent rows, settleable only by reading them against the strength and outturn rather than by validating the file.

assets_supplied.name: packaging_shots/ (3 frames, 4032 x 3024)
assets_supplied.kind: Phone photographs the founders took of their own packaging: a wax seal over a bottle neck, a stencilled crate end, and a cap from above.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our own wax, our own crate, our own cap. Use these on the sheet so a supplier can see what we mean."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two faults, neither stated. Wax and cap were shot indoors under a warm work lamp and the crate outdoors in flat daylight, so the three will not sit together without different corrections. And the wax seal is deep oxblood on near-black glass, so its shadowed lower rim and the glass share luminance and a subject knockout returns success while quietly eating the bottom of the seal.

assets_supplied.name: supplier_emails.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Four forwarded messages from a wax supplier, a stencil cutter, a closure maker and the printer, each saying what they need and what went wrong last time.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What the four of them have actually asked us for. This is the mess we want to stop having."

assets_supplied.name: house_words.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Half a page of tone and colour language from Iris, with no hex values and no measurements.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "How we talk about the work. Salt, iron, cold light, nothing shiny."

acceptance_bar: The mark comes back as artwork a supplier can place at any size, transparent, with nothing behind it, and no white or black box appears on a coloured ground.
Whatever ground and size a variant is specified for, it still reads as our mark there. A version that closes up, breaks up or blobs at its specified size is a rejected file.
A version claimed as one ink is genuinely one ink, not a family of near-identical inks.
Enclosed shapes stay enclosed. A filled rope ring, a closed sail gap or a closed letter counter is a rejected file.
The variants read as versions of ONE mark laid out together, not four different drawings of a boat.
No file is larger than the frame it came from, and the note lists every picture resized and by how much.

The three packaging photographs read as one set on one sheet: one white point, one warmth, one black point. A frame that cannot be brought to the set is named to us rather than shipped at eighty percent.
Nothing is cut out sloppily. A seal or cap with a bitten edge is rejected on sight.

Release labels: one sheet per cask in cask-book order, every line last year's artwork carried present on every sheet, the photograph on each sheet the cask named on it, at real print resolution at the sheet's true trim.
One label file per cask, named so the bottling hall can pull the right one without opening it, and its contents are what its name claims.

The supplier sheet is one working file we can edit ourselves, every canvas at its own size, mark as real artwork and words as live text, plus the source it was built from, in one type system whose family, foundry and weight you name per role.

A written note: what was done to each picture, which version is for which supplier and why, anything in our own list you questioned, and anything you could not do inside the printer's file, told to us before it reaches Redgate.
