adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset upload with media_type text/html for transport, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search(CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The mark sheet: a documentation page, an icon and favicon board, a lockup page and a dark booth panel in one export, each root carrying its own canvas size, native and editable with live text and every mark as real vector shapes. This is where the three marks are finally adjacent at one size in one document.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Fonts
adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend once per role, font_styles for numeric OpenType weights, find_fonts to launder names into canonical PostScript form, get_fontkit_embed_url for one kit consumed through the returned kebab css_stack
adobe_surfaces.role: The wordmark lockups and the sheet. Nothing in the connector reads a typeface off a picture, so the face beside the mark is chosen art direction that must be disclosed as chosen, and the recommender refuses to pair. Numeric weight is non-standard per family, a display cut is reached by its own slug, and one unresolvable name kills the entire kit.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock plus Boards, counted as one surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search(entityScope StockAsset, short generic queries, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: One licensed operations frame for the booth panel, which an eleven-person company cannot shoot before the conference and which is the only IP-clean way to introduce a photograph nobody there took, plus the selects board the founder and printer sign off from before the press file is committed.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook before writing markup, settle which half of the commission lands on which surface, and upload every asset through initialize, PUT and finalize.
trajectory.judgement: The split is the first real decision and the brief never states it. Exhibitor cards are record per page against artwork the client wants preserved; the mark sheet needs several canvas sizes and must stay editable when a fourth product lands.
trajectory.produces: A plan naming surface per deliverable, the confirmed tier, and a manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Look at all three marks at full size and triage them: what each is made of, what is artwork and what is glow, what each sits on, and where each encloses negative space.
trajectory.judgement: These look like three versions of one problem and they are not. A mark on transparency, a mark flattened onto an off-white plate and a mark built around an enclosed ring need three different preparations, and choosing one route for the folder is the failure.
trajectory.produces: A per-mark triage note covering ground, enclosure and what belongs to the artwork.

trajectory.action: Prepare and trace each mark by its own route: ink-level selections worded against the artwork's visual properties rather than its substrate, the correct polarity, crops to the selection's bounds, trace, then inject a viewBox, strip the opaque full-canvas path, clear stray glow fragments and build the one-ink and reversed colourways.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions per mark the tools do not make: wording, polarity, and whether to trace the binary plate or the colour-accurate plate. The colour route is where the founder's gradient question gets its real answer, since a trace of a gradient is not a gradient. A mark surrounded by halo debris is not production artwork whatever it looks like at thumbnail size.
trajectory.produces: Three cleaned marks with on-light, on-dark and one-ink colourways, route and polarity recorded per mark.

trajectory.action: Place the master mark large and then at browser-tab size, and look at the geometry as geometry rather than as a picture.
trajectory.judgement: The first moment the artwork is real rather than soft, and the first moment its construction can be judged at all. The agent must be willing to conclude that the client's own mark is not built the way the client believes, and decide whether that is reportable, correctable by a different preparation, or outside scope.
trajectory.produces: A written finding on the master mark's construction at both extremes of size.

trajectory.action: Derive the icon, favicon and lockup-scale artwork from the cleaned masters, reading the confidence and tradeoff metadata each crop returns rather than trusting success.
trajectory.judgement: The tradeoff array is the only signal that a crop clipped, that a detection was weak, or that an output was interpolated upward toward the cap. A favicon made by shrinking a mark never designed to shrink is a decision rather than an export.
trajectory.produces: Icon and favicon artwork with a no-enlargement record drawn from what each call reported.

trajectory.action: Triage the eleven photographs on light, level, sitter tightness, true source scale and isolation risk, then level what needs it and bring every frame toward one house treatment with its own parameter set, masking where a whole-frame grade would blow a window or grey a skin tone.
trajectory.judgement: Self-submitted portraits are eleven separate problems wearing one folder name, and one batched call would apply one identical parameter set to all eleven. Prompt wording is the whole gate on the masks.
trajectory.produces: A per-frame triage note and eleven graded portraits at their true source scale with a parameter log.

trajectory.action: Cut each portrait to the card crop, choosing the isolation route per frame, and inspect each edge at card reproduction size rather than at full frame.
trajectory.judgement: A subject knockout is right where the sitter separates from the ground and wrong where a shoulder and a blown window share luminance, and the wrong route returns success. Route is a per-frame decision made by looking.
trajectory.produces: Eleven card-crop portraits with the route recorded per frame.

trajectory.surface: Data preparation and Creative Cloud storage
trajectory.action: Reconcile the roster against the photographs and the mark set, normalise it into a merge-shaped data file with an image column of bare filenames under the required prefix, upload the graded card masters and build the image map against them.
trajectory.judgement: A photo column keyed on surname is fine until two people share one, and a product line with no artwork behind it is a question for the client rather than a field to leave blank. The client asked to be told, so resolving either silently is not the same act as resolving it and saying so.
trajectory.produces: The merge data file, uploaded masters, the image map, and a first list of questions for the handover.

trajectory.action: Convert the card PDF, export IDML, unzip it, and read what came across: frame counts, object styles, real integer page-item ids and bounds, and the true story text reconstructed by concatenating the content runs.
trajectory.judgement: The mapping strategy is decided here and the answer is a property of the client's PDF, not of the plan. There must be a real addressable frame for everything already promised, since the whole per-row binding depends on there being a frame to bind to.
trajectory.produces: The converted document, its IDML, a frame inventory with real ids and bounds, and the reconstructed story text.

trajectory.action: Author the mapping against what the conversion exposed, including the per-record binding the card's code block appears to offer, validate it, prepare the merge template, then export IDML from the RESULT, unzip it and grep the story for every placeholder the mapping claimed to create.
trajectory.judgement: Not accepting a success message as evidence. Nothing instructs this verification and nothing warns if it is skipped, and it is the only place the mapping's real yield is visible before pages exist.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholder inventory has been independently confirmed.

trajectory.action: Merge to a native document with per-row images bound, render the press file and proofs at 300 ppi, then produce the per-person single-page files and name each to its person, verifying identity by opening each file rather than by its position in the returned list.
trajectory.judgement: Merging straight to raster silently drops to screen resolution whatever is asked for, and merging straight to PDF forfeits the per-record branch. Naming eleven files by return order is the fast wrong answer, and it is the failure somebody discovers at a booth.
trajectory.produces: The press card file, 300 ppi proofs, and eleven identity-verified named single cards.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the booth panel frame, filter to photography, exclude generative results, license and download at full resolution, then grade it toward the house treatment and lay it beside the portrait set.
trajectory.judgement: Choosing a frame whose light can be brought to the house treatment rather than the prettiest thumbnail, and a subject a technical audience will not read as stock filler. Both are cheap to get wrong at 240 pixels.
trajectory.produces: One licensed camera-scale frame, graded, judged in or out with the reasoning recorded.

trajectory.surface: Adobe Fonts and Adobe Express, HTML authoring
trajectory.action: Build one kit (recommend per role, pull style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name), then author one self-contained HTML with four roots at four canvas sizes, base64-inline every photograph, place every mark as inline vector in an explicitly sized top-left anchored wrapper, declare family and weight on every text element, upload by the allowed-host route, run the readiness check and export. Verify through both channels: resolve the rendition and look at canvas one, and parse the returned per-canvas markup for the rest.
trajectory.judgement: Nothing here reads the face the generator drew, so the wordmark type is the agent's own choice and must be presented as a choice; numeric weight cannot be inferred from a style name and one unresolvable name kills the kit. In the export, a URL photograph is not a photograph, weight is not inherited from markup semantics, a right-anchored auto-sized wrapper collapses off the artboard, and every drop returns success while the preview shows only the first canvas.
trajectory.produces: One kit with family, foundry and numeric weight per role plus the chosen-face disclosure, a native editable Express document holding every canvas, its durable source HTML, and a per-canvas markup audit.

trajectory.action: Create the selects board and add the graded portrait set, the licensed frame and the card proofs within the per-call cap, treating a partial success as partial and re-sending only the entries named as failed. Then write the handover.
trajectory.judgement: What to escalate versus what to fix silently. The founder asked to be told honestly about her gradient, the roster raised a question the mark set cannot answer, and the card carries a request that must be met differently from how it was asked. All three belong in writing before the printer sees anything.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable selects board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover the acceptance bar requires.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What is actually inside these three generative exports, legible only once they are real geometry. The master's two supposedly matching arms were drawn freehand and differ in width and corner angle, which a 1400 pixel soft-edged export hides completely; at trace, seen large, the mark is visibly lopsided. The outer glow belongs to the artwork rather than a background, so a preparation that separates by lightness carries a fringe through as a ring of stray shapes. And the two sub-brand marks, made months apart, come back with materially different stroke mass from each other and from the master even where every preparation succeeded. Nothing reports any of it: every selection returns a plausible mask, the tracer takes no options, and each mark inspected alone at thumbnail size looks finished.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: There is no parameter to reason about and no read-ahead: the tracer has no options, so the only way to learn what a preparation yields is to make it, trace it and look at it large. Nothing states it, since the brief says only that the exports are soft and that the sub marks have never felt like family, the client's complaint rather than a description of the geometry. And the response is not a re-run but a different preparation per mark, a decision about whether a construction fault in the client's own mark is correctable here or reportable, and usually a change to which mark carries which application.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-prepare each mark on a different route, a selection worded for the structural edge rather than the luminous field, or the colour-plate route instead of the binary route, then re-trace, re-strip the opaque path, re-clear the halo debris and re-place large and at tab size. Decide explicitly what to do about the asymmetry and the gradient, since neither can be redrawn here, and re-take the icon and favicon derivation, because a mark that only holds above a certain size needs different small artwork rather than a smaller copy.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A brand system shipped to a printer, a fabricator and an app store in which the company's primary mark is visibly lopsided at every size it is now sharp enough to show it, ringed by halo fragments, with two sub marks that still do not belong to it, delivered as the production-clean artwork the client paid for.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printer's card exposes and what it will actually carry. The name, role, product line, email and booking link came across as one continuous story rather than five addressable frames, and the mapping readout omits one of those runs, so every offset computed past it is short while the validator reports the mapping valid, the prepare call reports the placeholders created successfully, and only some of the fields land. And the card's code block converts to an ordinary graphic frame that accepts a per-record code mapping, passes validation and is reported created, while no code is ever produced on any rendered page. The client asked in good faith for each card to point at that person's own link, because last year's card did.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Frame granularity is a property of a document made by a printer nobody has spoken to, and the code binding is documented and accepted by every tool in the chain right up to the render, so no ordering and no amount of care reaches either fact earlier. Nothing states it: the brief states the goal, that each card points at that person's own booking link, a client requirement rather than a description of what the tooling will do. And it is not a propagation re-run, because the mapping changes shape to offset arithmetic against an independently reconstructed story, and the per-person code must be re-planned into a different deliverable.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reconstruct the true story from the IDML content runs, recompute every offset from that string, re-validate, re-prepare and re-verify by grepping the round-tripped IDML for every placeholder before any page is merged. Then take the code decision explicitly: bind the single booth code the client already supplied to every card and set each person's own link as live text, or ask the client for eleven exported code images so they bind through the per-row image column, and say in writing which was done and why.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A press run of eleven exhibitor cards on which the booking link is silently missing from every card and the code block is last year's flat placeholder pointing nowhere, handed to a printer six weeks before a conference, with every tool having reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the licensed frame belongs with this set, a question that exists only once the two are adjacent. Stock search returns a 240 pixel thumbnail and true dimensions and says nothing about the light, so the frame's real colour temperature, contrast and grain arrive only with the full-resolution download, and the comparison it must survive is against eleven phone portraits just pulled to one house treatment. A frame that looked crisp and neutral as a thumbnail can land warm, soft and evidently lit by somebody else, and the failure is not that it is a bad photograph but that it reads as bought the moment it sits beside the team.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: The judgement requires both halves to exist and the graded portrait set is the second half, so ordering cannot bring it forward. Care cannot dodge it either, because nothing in the search response describes the light and the thumbnail is too small to read it. Nothing states it: the brief never mentions a photograph at all, and the panel is the agent's own proposal. And it is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different frame, a materially harder grade, or a panel re-composed around type and the marks.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Lay the downloaded frame beside the graded portraits at panel size and judge it there rather than alone. Then either search again on the light rather than the subject and license a replacement, or push this frame with masked corrections until it sits with the set, or drop it and re-author the booth panel without a photograph, which changes the panel's composition, its type hierarchy and which mark variant carries it.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A booth panel standing next to eleven cards at a developer conference in which the hero photograph is visibly lit by a different person on a different day in a different colour from every face beside it, in front of the exact audience the brief says reads fuss as sloppiness.

deliverables.name: Halcyon Grid production mark family
deliverables.spec: Three marks rebuilt from generative rasters as placeable, scalable artwork with real viewBoxes, no opaque ground paths, no halo debris and enclosed shapes genuinely enclosed, in on-light, on-dark and one-ink colourways, plus horizontal and stacked wordmark lockups, an app icon and a favicon. The three must hold together as one family laid out at one size, with the preparation route recorded per mark and the gradient decision argued rather than asserted.

deliverables.name: Exhibitor cards, press file plus per-person named cards
deliverables.spec: 89 x 51 mm, one person per card in roster order, page count equal to roster count, rendered at 300 ppi at trim, binding name, role, product line, email and booking link verbatim from the roster plus that person's own photograph. With one single-page file per person, named to them and identity-verified by opening it, and 300 ppi proofs. Produced by reverse-engineering the printer's flat PDF into a live merge template, handed back with a record of how it was derived and of what the card could not be made to carry.

deliverables.name: Team portrait set at one house treatment
deliverables.spec: Eleven self-submitted phone frames shot under no common direction brought to one credible house treatment (one white point, one warmth, one black point) plus one licensed camera-scale frame graded into the same set, every output at or below its true source pixel dimensions, with a per-frame log of corrections and of every resize any tool reported.

deliverables.name: Card-crop portrait cutouts
deliverables.spec: Eleven portraits cut to the card crop, with the isolation route recorded per frame because a sitter against a plain wall and a sitter against a blown office window are not the same problem. Shoulder lines and hairlines inspected at card reproduction size rather than at full frame, with transparent versions for layering on the sheet.

deliverables.name: Brand mark sheet as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: One native editable Express document holding every canvas at its own size: a documentation page, an icon and favicon board, a lockup page and a dark booth panel. Live editable text in one licensed type system, every mark as real vector shapes, every photograph carried as embedded image data. Delivered with the self-contained source it was authored from, so a fourth product can be added next quarter without a re-commission.

deliverables.name: Handover note and selects board
deliverables.spec: A written note recording the preparation route and finding per mark, what happened to the gradient and why, what was done to each photograph, the type system by role with family, foundry and actual numeric weight together with the plain statement that the wordmark face is chosen rather than matched, what the card conversion exposed, how the per-person link request was answered, every roster row questioned, and every resize any tool reported. Paired with a persistent shareable selects board with nothing silently dropped.

verifiers_auto.text: The press card file has exactly one page per roster row in roster order and renders at 300 ppi at 89 x 51 mm trim.
verifiers_auto.how: Count pages in the rendered press PDF against the reconciled roster count and check the render resolution and output dimensions at trim.

verifiers_auto.text: Every one of the five card fields appears on every page of the merged output.
verifiers_auto.how: Grep the round-tripped IDML story for all five placeholders, then read text off each rendered page against its roster row.

verifiers_auto.text: Every delivered mark carries a viewBox, no full-canvas opaque background path, and no stray fragments outside the mark's own geometry.
verifiers_auto.how: Parse each delivered SVG for a viewBox, inspect path index zero for a full-extent rectangle, and count disconnected sub-paths outside the mark's principal bounding region.

verifiers_auto.text: Each version claimed as one ink resolves to a single fill value rather than a family of near-identical fills.
verifiers_auto.how: Enumerate distinct fill attributes across the paths of each such version and reject any carrying more than one.

verifiers_auto.text: No delivered image exceeds its true source frame on either axis, and no crop call reported an upscale entry the handover fails to transcribe.
verifiers_auto.how: Compare every delivered file's dimensions against its true source frame, including the web-copy portrait, and check every crop response's tradeoffs array for upscale entries.

verifiers_auto.text: The exported Express document holds every declared canvas at its own distinct size, every mark appears as vector paths rather than a single image, and every photograph resolved to real image data.
verifiers_auto.how: Read slide_count and per-slide width and height from the export response, and parse each canvas's markup for path-type shapes at each mark position, placeholder image data, and elements resolving beyond their declared canvas width.

verifiers_auto.text: Eleven per-person card files exist, each named to a person and containing the person its name claims, and the selects board carries the expected item count with no unre-sent failures.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the name field off each single-page file and compare with its filename, never relying on returned order; compare addedEntityIds against the expected count and require failedItems empty.

verifiers_human.text: The three marks read as one family laid out together at one size, matched on weight, corner treatment and proportion.
verifiers_human.how: View all three adjacent at one size and judge stroke mass and construction as a set, then compare against the supplied exports to confirm each is still the client's own mark.

verifiers_human.text: The master mark holds at browser-tab size and at banner size, with enclosed shapes open and no halo debris around it.
verifiers_human.how: View the delivered artwork at both extremes on light and dark grounds and look for closed enclosures, stray fragments and visible asymmetry.

verifiers_human.text: The eleven portraits read as one set when the cards are laid out in a row.
verifiers_human.how: View the delivered card set side by side at card size and judge white point, warmth, black point and subject scale as a set.

verifiers_human.text: No portrait cutout reads as bitten, particularly the two shot against bright windows.
verifiers_human.how: View each cutout at card reproduction size and zoom the shoulder line and hairline against the delivered ground.

verifiers_human.text: The design answers a technical buyer at 20 to 60 dollars a seat: sharp, plain, restrained, documentation rather than marketing.
verifiers_human.how: Review the mark sheet canvases and card proofs against the price band and audience, and reject a glossy, decorative or aspirational answer.

verifiers_human.text: The handover escalates rather than conceals: the gradient answer, the mark construction finding, the roster question, the chosen wordmark face and the per-person link answer are all named in writing.
verifiers_human.how: Read the handover against the triage and conversion findings and check each is disclosed with the decision taken.

decision_gates: The surface split: exhibitor cards to the merge surface because they are record per page against artwork the client wants preserved, mark sheet to HTML authoring because it needs several canvas sizes and must stay editable.
Whether three superficially similar generative exports are one problem or three, when one sits on transparency, one on an off-white plate and one encloses a ring.
Selection wording per mark: whether the prompt takes the artwork or the plate it was flattened onto.
Which polarity to hand a tracer that takes no options, and whether to trace the binary plate or the colour-accurate plate.
What honestly happens to the founder's gradient, and whether to say so or to quietly ship whatever the trace returned.
Whether a construction fault in the client's own mark is correctable inside this engagement, reportable, or both.
Whether to strip the opaque ground path and clear the halo debris, which nothing in the chain does and nothing warns about.
Isolation route per portrait, when a subject knockout is right against a plain wall and wrong against a blown window.

Whether to bind the client's own surname-keyed photo references or rebuild the image map against the agent's graded masters, and whether repointing a client's data silently is the same act as repointing it and saying so.
What to do with a roster row naming a product the mark set cannot answer.
Whether to trust the mapping readout of the client's text or to reconstruct the story independently from the document.
Whether a success message counts as verification, when nothing instructs a re-export and grep of the prepared template.
How to answer a per-record request the client made in good faith once it is clear the chain reports it done and produces nothing.
Whether to name eleven per-person card files by the order they came back or by opening each one.
Whether the licensed frame joins the set or reads as bought, and if bought, whether to push it, replace it or compose the panel without it.
why_not_vlm: Paste this brief and these assets into a frontier image model and it returns three nice logos. It fails all three gates. IDENTITY: the commission is that these three specific marks, which the founder made and the company has used for two years, must survive being rebuilt rather than be replaced; a regenerated mark is a different company's logo, and the printer, the fabricator and the app store listing all receive it. The eleven faces are eleven real colleagues standing at a booth, not eleven plausible portraits. SPEC: one card per person in roster order at 89 x 51 mm and 300 ppi with five named fields bound verbatim from their own roster, eleven separately named card files each containing the person their filename claims, artwork with real viewBoxes and no opaque ground paths, and no delivered file larger than its true source. A generated image satisfies none of that and cannot be checked against a roster. EDITABILITY: two deliverables are defined by being editable, a live merge template so next year is a data change, and a native document with live text and real vector so a fourth product can be added without a re-commission. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality: is this arm the same as that one, does this placeholder exist, does this code ever appear, is this face the person named beside it.
doability_proof: All verified in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account); five surfaces, honestly counted, with image_vectorize in the Photoshop family rather than as an Illustrator surface. MERGE SPINE: building a merge template from a bare PDF end to end headlessly is verified (convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt, prepare_indd_merge_template producing a story containing the expected placeholders). One record per page is confirmed for PDF output; per-record named files are confirmed by two order-verified routes (createSeparateFiles and a recordRange loop) while multi-record raster order is documented as reversed and is therefore never used for identity; true 300 ppi comes from document_render_layout because outputSpecs.resolution on the merge is silently ignored. THE CARD PDF IS BUILT TO A VERIFIED SHAPE: a PDF with two placed image blocks converts to an .indd exposing two graphic frames plus split text frames, and a contiguous copy flow collapses into a single story, which is exactly a portrait plus a code block with a five-line copy column beside them; it must be a real font-embedding press PDF from a full engine, since a thin hand-authored PDF fails conversion opaquely. THE VARIABLE CODE IS A VERIFIED FALSE POSITIVE, NOT AN INVENTION: qr_mappings was tested twice, alone and alongside an image merge, and in both cases the validator accepted it, prepare_indd_merge_template returned success, and the rendered page still showed the original flat placeholder with the round-tripped IDML carrying zero code markers. The task never requires a variable code to be produced; it requires the request to be answered, and the client-supplied single code image binds through the ordinary image route. The lossy textContent readout and the validator returning VALID on the resulting wrong offsets are likewise verified. Per-row image merge through an at-prefixed CSV column plus additionalImageFiles keyed to bare filenames is verified; eleven rows here, so the recordRange loop is carried as an explicit fallback. IMAGING: select_by_prompt with returnBbox, select_subject, invert_selection, fill_area, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs array, masked apply_adjustments, auto_tone, auto_straighten, remove_background on both routes and vectorize are verified headless across 27 live calls, as are the substrate-versus-ink prompt asymmetry, the enclosed-aperture failure of remove_background returning a solid opaque disc while reporting success, the binary mask, the mandatory polarity flip before tracing, vectorize taking no options at all, its missing viewBox and opaque path zero, its dozens of near-identical fills from a colour plate, and its explosion into loose ungrouped shapes in Express. Upscaling is handled not asserted: crop_and_resize interpolates to a hard 2x cap and signals it only in metadata.tradeoffs, which makes the 1200 pixel web-copy portrait a scored decision. EXPRESS: multi-root export with mixed canvas sizes is verified, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, and the right-anchored auto-sized wrapper collapse is a verified defect; transport is pinned to the upload route with media_type text/html; verification is split because the rendition preview shows page one only; persistence is not assumed, so the deliverable is the document plus the source HTML. FONTS: the chain is verified end to end, no font identification from an image exists anywhere in the connector (which is why the wordmark face must be disclosed as chosen), and the non-standard numeric weights, the slug-not-PostScript CSS rule and the all-or-nothing kit call are live findings. STOCK AND BOARDS: short generic queries only, the orientation filter is broken and never used, the 240 pixel rendition is not editable which is what makes the frame's true light a download-time discovery, licensed downloads are genuine camera scale, and board placements cap at twelve per call with failedItems signalling partial success. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no document_render_vector or document_merge_data_vector, no bleed, no pdfPreset, no fill_text, no animate_design or create_firefly_board, no replace_image, no download_design, no upscaling, no OCR, no compositing, no generated imagery, no photo reaching Express as a URL, no batch above twenty files.

engagement_title: Evergreen Provisions first apparel capsule: recover six hand painted crest panels into per ink plate art, prove them at the width they actually print on the garments the shop actually stocks, and hand the decorator a live spec run
vertical: Cannabis retail and dispensary lifestyle merchandise, two owned storefronts, Bend, Oregon, short run counter sold apparel capsule
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork apparel capsule post quoted in this line's ledger grounding_note, from a vertically integrated cannabis retailer asking for 'a production-ready apparel design system for a branded retail capsule' that 'hands cleanly to manufacturers and decorators (vectors, tech packs)', in an 'elevated streetwear' direction, on palette with no rework. The real post names no client, so the line is laundered to the coined fictional dispensary Evergreen Provisions (a generic dictionary pairing, no trademark collision), and the post's stated purple and black palette is dropped along with its from scratch garment art and embroidery digitising, which the ledger's own triage concedes are not connector work. What survives is the half that client genuinely needed and could not get: a decorator will not quote from a photograph, so the commission is recovery of the artwork that already exists into per ink plate art, plus the spec the shop floor actually works from. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) is what makes that the honest fuller commission rather than a thin one, because an ink level trace off photographed painted collateral recovers real artwork, HTML authoring produces a native editable Express document at mixed canvas sizes for the separation sheets and the teaser set, and the InDesign convert and merge chain turns the decorator's own last season spec card PDF into a live per design run. Verdict STRENGTHEN honoured: the concept and the six item collateral set are kept intact and the depth is raised from what sat on one vector surface to five honestly counted ones.
client_one_liner: We had six crest panels hand painted for our shop walls, the painter moved away and left us nothing but photographs of them, and our screen printer will not quote a tee run off a photograph.
client_brief:
Evergreen Provisions, first apparel capsule

We run two dispensary shops in Bend, Oregon. Two years ago we paid a local sign painter to hand paint six crest panels for the walls, one for each of our house strain families. Customers photograph them constantly and ask where they can buy them. So we want a small capsule off the back of that: three tees and two hoodies, short run, sold over our own counters.

Where we are. The painter finished the panels, was paid, and moved to Montana. We do not have her sketches and there is no file of any kind. What we have is a set of photographs of the finished panels sitting on our bench, taken over two visits, and photographs of the actual blank tees and hoodies we stock, shot on the counter under our shop lights.

What we need. Our screen printer will not quote from a photograph. He needs proper artwork, one piece of art per ink, so he can burn screens off it. He also needs to know how many inks each design costs him and in what order they lay down. Last season he sent us a spec card for a different job and asked us to use the same card again so his floor recognises it, and we still have that PDF. We have a sheet listing the designs, which garment and colour each goes on, where it sits and how wide it prints.

We want to see it before we commit. A board showing each design on the actual garment colour it goes on, at the size it actually prints, plus a set of square posts for our socials that we can edit ourselves when the drop date moves.

The look. These are hand painted panels and that is the entire reason anyone wants them. Keep the brush in it. Do not turn them into flat corporate logos. Tees are thirty two dollars, hoodies seventy, and our buyer is twenty five to forty five and buys craft.

And tell us plainly what came back and what did not.
price_band_and_audience: Craft dispensary lifestyle capsule at 32 dollars a tee and 70 dollars a hoodie, buyer 25 to 45, bought at the counter on the strength of the wall panels they already photograph. The band is load bearing. At this price the painted origin is the product, so the plates have to retain brush edge, dry brush breakup and a halftoned paint field, and the palette stays earthy and limited to the inks the decorator already keeps on his shelf. Flatten those crests into clean geometric marks with a mass retail two ink treatment and the capsule reads as gas station merch, which will not hold 70 dollars. Push the other way into a foiled, sparse, monogrammed designer drop look and it misprices a counter sold 32 dollar tee and stops looking like the panels on the wall, which is the only reason the customer walked over. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every plate separates correctly. A real posted job of this shape runs 900 to 2,200 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: A vertically integrated cannabis retailer running two dispensary storefronts, launching a short-run counter-sold apparel capsule.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2019, Bend, Oregon. Two owned dispensary shops, owner-run, with a small counter-retail apparel line.
brand_identity.about: Evergreen Provisions runs two dispensary shops in Bend, built around six house strain families. Two years ago the owners paid a local sign painter to hand-paint a crest panel for each family onto the shop walls. Customers photograph them constantly and ask where they can buy them, and the first apparel capsule exists to answer that question without losing the hand that made the panels.
brand_identity.audience: Craft-minded dispensary customers aged 25 to 45 who buy at the counter on the strength of the wall panels they already photograph. People who pay for the painted origin, not for a logo.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Tees at 32 dollars, hoodies at 70 dollars, short-run and counter-sold. Elevated streetwear priced above gas-station merch and below a designer drop. The painted texture is the product, so the value sits in the brush surviving, not in gloss or foil.
brand_identity.typography: Display in a painted or brushed-character face that echoes the sign painter's hand, kept legible. Support and spec type in a plain workhorse sans so the plates and sheets read cleanly. Type never competes with the painted crest.
brand_identity.voice: Warm, plain-spoken, shop-floor honest. No luxury posturing and no carnival hype. Example line: "These are hand painted panels and that is the entire reason anyone wants them. Keep the brush in it, and tell us plainly what came back and what did not."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The six crest panels were hand-painted by a local sign painter who has since moved to Montana and left no sketches or files. The only surviving artwork is a set of bench photographs of the finished panels, shot over two visits under mixed light. There is no vector art and no separation art, which is exactly why the screen printer cannot quote a run.
brand_identity.values: Craft and honesty. Keep the painted hand, hold the palette to the inks the decorator already stocks, and say plainly what the paintings can and cannot give a screen.

assets_supplied.name: evergreen_crest_panels/ (6 frames, roughly 4200 x 4200)
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photographs of six hand painted crest panels on primed board, taken on the shop bench across two separate visits under mixed daylight and counter light.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The six panels as they hang on the wall. Two were shot on a different day so they sit a little different."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two of the six are compound lockups, a ring of painted lettering around a central sprig, and a single compound selection returns the ring and the outer arcs while silently dropping the sprig at full success. One panel is painted in a deep aubergine that sits within a hair of the stained board behind it, so an ink level selection there has almost no contrast to work with, and the dry brush hairlines and the small painted caps are barely open in the paint itself, so whether they survive a trace is a property of each panel rather than of the tracing.

assets_supplied.name: evergreen_garment_blanks/ (5 frames)
assets_supplied.kind: Photographs of the actual blanks the shop stocks: three tees (bone, heather olive, black) and two hoodies (black, oat), laid on the counter.

assets_supplied.hidden_defect: They were shot under warm counter lights, so the black hoodie photographs brown and the heather olive reads yellow, which makes every judgement about ink contrast on those grounds wrong until the frames are corrected. One of the five was shot on a hanger rather than flat and sits noticeably off level.

The mapping readout also omits one run while keeping its line break, so the string still looks well formed, every offset past it is short, and the validator still reports the mapping valid.

acceptance_bar: Every plate is a separate piece of single ink geometry that a decorator could burn a screen from. A sheet showing a picture of a separation is not a separation.
Every delivered vector carries a real viewBox and no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath it, and drops onto a coloured garment ground without a box behind it.

At the print width the schedule states, on the garment colour that design actually prints on, each crest keeps its hairlines and its counters stay open. Judged at reproduction size on the real ground, never at canvas scale.
The one colour reductions for the dark garments are a genuine redraw of value, not the colour art with its colour taken away.
The six panels read as one capsule palette, not as six paintings shot on two different days. A panel that cannot be brought to the set is named rather than shipped at eighty percent.
The blanks are corrected to their honest colours before any ink contrast decision is made against them, and the correction is stated.
No delivered file exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions, and no returned tradeoff record in the run carries an upscale entry.

The design list is reconciled before anything is counted: the spec card run has one card per real design, every declared field lands on every card, and the reconciliation is stated rather than assumed.
On the separation sheets every plate is separately readable, including where plates overlap. A sheet where the top plate hides the ones beneath it fails even if it exported successfully.
The mockup board shows each design at true relative scale on its blank, not scaled to fill the garment.
The teaser set and the sheets arrive as one working file we can edit ourselves, each canvas keeping its own size, delivered with the self contained source it was built from.

The note names, per design, the ink count as separated rather than as guessed, the plate order, anything that could not be recovered from the paintings, and anything the print process cannot be given.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching a pixel.
trajectory.judgement: The plates and reductions are raster and vector work with a production spec, the spec cards are a genuine record per page run against a template the client actually supplied, and the sheets and teasers need an authored fixed canvas document because the shop edits them next drop. Nothing else in the connector composes free form layout.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming a surface per deliverable, and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline: a manifest keyed by role so that forty artefacts later the agent still knows which URL is which panel, which blank and which schedule row.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Preview all six panels and all five blanks and triage them: which panels are single element crests and which are compound lockups, which paint runs close in value to its board, which blank is off level, and which capture belongs to which visit.
trajectory.judgement: The photographs are the only thing that can settle what each crest is actually made of. Reading the schedule tells you what the shop calls them, which is not the same question and is answered slower.
trajectory.produces: A per asset triage note covering crest structure, paint against board contrast, illuminant and tilt.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level, before any crop or bounds decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Correct the five blanks so the garment colours are honest, recording the parameters applied.
trajectory.judgement: Every later decision about whether an ink reads on a ground is made against these frames. Judging contrast against a black hoodie that photographs brown is judging against a garment that does not exist.
trajectory.produces: Five corrected blank masters with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Bring the six panel captures to one capsule palette, correcting each toward one target with its own call rather than one batched pass.
trajectory.judgement: One batched call applies one identical parameter set, which is exactly wrong for frames shot on two visits under two lights. The target is a set of paintings that look like one hand, not six good photographs.
trajectory.produces: Six panel masters on one palette with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Pull each crest at ink level, naming the paint's own visual properties rather than the panel it sits on, and taking compound lockups element by element rather than in one prompt.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the whole gate: naming the substrate returns the board. A compound prompt returns a plausible looking mask that has quietly lost an element, and the aubergine panel has almost nothing for a selection to hold on to.
trajectory.produces: Per crest ink level masks, composited per element where the lockup is compound, each with its returned bounding box.

trajectory.action: Set polarity, crop to each mask's own returned bounds with a little padding, and trace.
trajectory.judgement: Tracing the raw mask returns a black box with the art knocked out of it, and tracing the inverted one returns the positive. Both report success, so the polarity decision is the whole difference.
trajectory.produces: One raw traced SVG per crest.

trajectory.action: Perform the vector hygiene the tracer does not: inject a viewBox and remove the opaque full canvas ground path on every trace.
trajectory.judgement: A trace with no viewBox does not scale and a trace with its ground path intact drops a white box onto a black hoodie. Neither is reported anywhere.
trajectory.produces: Placeable, scalable, transparent crest vectors.

trajectory.action: Build the separations: mask each ink and flatten the rest away so each plate carries one ink only, choose which crest carries a halftoned paint field and at what radius, then trace each plate.
trajectory.judgement: Separating after the trace gives a mess of near identical fills. The craft is deciding, per design, how many inks the painting is actually worth on a 32 dollar tee, and which parts of the brush are worth a halftone rather than an extra screen.
trajectory.produces: Per design plate sets, one piece of art per ink, plus the halftoned paint field plates.

trajectory.action: Build the one colour reductions for the dark garments as a value redraw rather than a desaturation, then knock the blanks to the house ground the mockup board needs.
trajectory.judgement: A desaturated colour separation collapses two inks of similar value into one grey mush. Deciding what survives when only one ink is left is the reduction.
trajectory.produces: One colour cuts per design and cut out blanks on the house ground.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged against a craft counter capsule at 32 and 70 dollars. The weight cannot be inferred from the style name, and a display cut is reached by its own slug rather than by a heavy weight.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML carrying the separation sheets, the mockup board and the square teaser roots, each root declaring its own canvas size, every photograph inlined as image data, every crest and plate placed as inline SVG in an explicitly sized top left anchored wrapper, family and weight declared on every text element, then upload the file and hold the returned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the artboard, and a global canvas override is what collapses a mixed size set. The design work is how a separation sheet shows overlapping inks so a decorator can read the trap between them.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML carrying the whole capsule set, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at canvas one, and parse the returned per canvas markup for every canvas after it.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning of any kind, and the rendition preview only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at page one is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document, an inspected first canvas, and a per canvas markup audit for the rest.

trajectory.action: Convert the decorator's spec card PDF, export the IDML, and read what the conversion actually exposes as editable frames and what each frame's true story text actually contains, before promising any field to any frame.
trajectory.judgement: What a printed card looks like and what its PDF converts into are unrelated questions, and the readout the mapping tool hands back is not the document. Promising a mapping before looking is promising something nobody has checked.
trajectory.produces: A real frame inventory with bounds and typography, and the reconstructed true story text per frame.

trajectory.action: Reconcile the schedule into a real design list, prepare the merge template, confirm by round trip that every field placeholder is actually present, then merge one record per page and render proofs at real print resolution.
trajectory.judgement: Two rows naming one crest on two garment colours is one design and two plate sets. A success message from the prepare step is not evidence a field landed, and the merge step ignores resolution entirely, so proofs have to come off the render.
trajectory.produces: A live merge template, a press PDF whose page count equals the reconciled design count, and print resolution proofs.

trajectory.action: License the counter surface frame, grade it into the capsule world, create the selects board and add the capsule set within the per call placement cap re sending only the entries the response names as failed, then write the handover note.
trajectory.judgement: A 201 is partial success, and the vector plates are not boardable so they belong in the note instead. The note has to be specific enough that the decorator does not phone back.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether these particular traces still hold at the width they actually print, on the garment colour they actually print on. The paintings carry dry brush hairlines and small painted caps whose counters are barely open in the paint itself, and the tracer takes no options at all, so the only lever is the raster prep upstream. At canvas scale every trace looks clean and complete. The sleeve hit prints at a fraction of the chest widths, and whether its counters close and its hairlines drop out at that size, against olive or against black rather than against white, is a property of that one painting meeting that one reproduction size and is not reported by anything.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the answer does not exist until the plate has been traced and laid down at its true width on the corrected garment ground, and there is no tracer parameter that would have prevented it. Nothing in the brief or the schedule states it: the schedule gives print widths because a decorator needs print widths, not as a warning about counters. It is not a propagation re run either, because the response is a different route for that design, either rebuilding the plate as a masked and flattened solid before tracing so the stroke carries weight, or accepting a coarser reduction for that placement and saying so.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Return to the raster prep for the affected designs, rebuild those plates through a mask and flatten route rather than tracing the painterly stroke directly, re trace, redo the vector hygiene, and re judge every affected design at its stated width on its stated ground before any of it reaches a sheet.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A capsule where the sleeve design prints as a plugged blob and the small painted caps close up on press, discovered by the decorator after screens are burned, on a capsule whose entire premise is that the brush survived.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the construct the separation sheets are built on. A separation sheet shows each ink as its own layer sitting over the ones beneath it so the decorator can read the overlap and the trap. Authored the natural way that is a blended or partially transparent stack, and the importer discards the blend outright and returns a plain opaque shape, at full success and with no warning of any kind. The returned per canvas markup is the only channel that reports it, and the document's own rendition returns the first artboard only, so every sheet after the first can be checked no other way.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the normalisation happens at import and the import is the last step of the authoring, and doing it right first time presumes knowing which of several plausible constructions survives, which no tool reports and no checklist enumerates. Nothing states it: the brief asks for one piece of art per ink and says nothing about how a sheet is drawn. It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a different construction, either separating the plates spatially into registered panels with a printed offset key, or baking the overlap into a raster upstream so the trap is part of the picture rather than of the layout.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re author the separation roots around whichever construction survives, re upload, re run the readiness check, re export, and audit every sheet from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Separation sheets handed to a decorator on which the top plate covers the ones beneath it, so every design appears to be a one ink job, with the export having reported success throughout.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the decorator's spec card actually is once converted, as opposed to what its printed face suggests. Its four blocks read as separate on paper, but the conversion decides the frame granularity and can collapse a continuous flow into a single frame, so there may be no separate name frame and ink frame to map fields to at all. Compounding it, the readout the mapping tool returns omits a run while keeping its line break, so the string still looks well formed, every offset past the omission is short by exactly that run's length, and the validator returns valid with no warnings on offsets that are wrong.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: There is no ordering that avoids it and no parameter that controls it, because the granularity is a property of how that PDF was made and the readout's omission is invisible in the readout. Nothing states it: the client says only that the printer wants the same card again. It is not a propagation re run, because the correct response is a different mapping strategy computed from a different source of truth, the reconstructed story text from the round tripped document rather than the tool's own readout, plus a decision about which fields the exposed frames can carry at all.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Recompute every offset from the reconstructed story text, re prepare the template, verify by a second round trip that each field placeholder is genuinely present rather than trusting the success message, re merge, and where two blocks collapsed into one frame decide which fields move into the note instead.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A spec card run that reports success, renders the right number of pages, and reaches the decorator's floor with the ink list and the plate order silently missing from every card.
